NATIONAL AERONAUTICS AND SPACE ADMINISTRATION  
NASA SHARED SERVICES CENTER 
 
RECOMMENDATION AND DETERMINATION TO SOLICIT FROM ONE SOURCE   
OR BRAND NAME 
 
PICK ONE 
 
Sole Source: 
☒I recommend that NASA, NASA Shared Services Center negotiate with m+p International, Inc. only for 
m + p International Software Purchase. The total estimated cost of this effort is and the 
estimated period of performance or lead-time for delivery is 30 Days ARO. 
 
OR 
 
Brand Name Justification: 
☐I recommend that NASA, NASA Shared Services Center negotiate with only with vendors who can 
provide the subject brand name from Manufacture Name for Enter Supply or Service to be procured. The 
total estimated cost of this effort is Enter Dollar amount and the estimated period of performance or lead-
time for delivery is Date. 
 
 
This recommendation is for the acquisition of supplies or services determined to be reasonably available 
from only one source/only one manufacture. Competition is impractical for the following reasons (please 
answer the questions below): 
 
1. What are the reasons for soliciting only the suggested source/suggested brand name? Please provide 
the unique characteristics of the items or services along with the supporting rationale and the market 
research performed to substantiate your reason for the suggested source/brand name. 
    
m+p International is the only authorized reseller of m+p software. D206 and D314 currently uses m+p 
hardware. The m+p International software used for this application is proprietary and requires compatible 
m+p International DAQ hardware to function correctly. Due to this hardware -software dependency, it is 
essential that m+p is the source of the software being purchased to ensure full operational capability, 
maintain system compatibility, and support required testing and data acquisition activities . 
 
2. What is the impact to the government if another vendor/brand is used? Include any dollar, schedule, 
or compatibility impacts if possible. 
 
Use of another vendor/brand software would have limited compatibility with the existing data acquisition 
(DAQ) infrastructure currently deployed at NASA Langley Research Center (LaRC) and other NASA 
centers with similar acoustic testing facilities. More importantly, an alternative vendor/brand software 
cannot effectively leverage the DAQ equipment currently assigned to LaRC D206, which is planned for 
near term utilization by LaRC D314. Implementing an alternative vendor/brand software would therefore 
require the procurement of additional compatible hardware to achieve operational capability, resulting in 
increased acquisition costs, added integration and learning curve efforts, and reduced interoperability 
with existing agency assets.

Last Updated:  July 26, 2026 
 Overview 
In this section we will be covering Water Management content found in the center of the webpage 
between the header and footer.  We will be organizing our content the same for each district while 
keeping unique elements for speciﬁc district needs.   This will help stakeholders, upper management, 
and neighboring districts ﬁnd information that they need easily.  We will organize everything in two parts 
a sidebar on the left “Water Management Data System Menu” and content oﬀ to the right.  For our 
landing page, we will have a partial hero banner across the center with a Water management label as 
seen below (The image will be unique to your district).    
 
 
For support we have a list of Division Lead for each region.  If you have a general question, you can reach 
out to one of them or the National PDT lead (a full list can be found below).  If you have a question on a 
speciﬁc topic such as reports, plots, or migration, there are specialists that you can reach out for that.   
 
 
   Formal Website Layout for Water Management - District Level Content

Section One – Sidebar Organization  
 
We will be dividing the content into three areas, Mission Essential, Unique to each district, and 
Contact/Links to Other Districts as seen below.  Mission essentials covers the content that is fairly 
standard across the board, Reports and data.  Many districts have situation maps of their region 
(dashboards).  If you do not have one of these, you can simply omit this from that section.  To customize 
the site for your district’s needs, we have a section below mission essentials for this content, “Unique to 
Each District”.  These items include DCP Monitor, Snow Melt, forecasts, and anything that does not ﬁt in 
the ﬁrst category.  At the end of the list on the sidebar we have contacts and Water Management 
districts.  If you currently have contact information on your sites, you would use this link for that content.  
Some districts do not have this on the current site and may choose not to use this.  The “Water 
Management Districts link” We will be providing this page for you.  It will be a link to all of the other 
district sites as a georeferenced layout (District map).

Last Updated:  July 26, 2026

This section has the critical items that have a higher priority, reports, data, information for our projects, 
and status map of our system.  We will be placing these items at the top of the list in the sidebar.  If you 
do not use one of the items listed, you can omit that one and move to the next.  To make it easy to 
locate information, we will keep the naming convention and order the same as listed below.  If your 
content does not ﬁt this standard, let one of the district leads know and we will help ﬁnd a solution for 
it.  Multiple reports or datasets can be listed in a dropdown menu.  An example is listed in the following 
section.

5 
Last Updated:  July 26, 2026 
Section Two - Header (global level content) 
The Header will be standard for all districts.  The left-hand side will be dedicated to A2W content as seen 
below.  A Search option for the district website will be placed on the right (this is a 21st Century 
requirement).  This will search the pages made by the district only, A2W content will not be included.   
The oﬃcial government banner will be at the top.  The Gray section will include the districts name with 
the “US Army Corps of Engineers” as seen below.  While we are migrating over to the new site, place a 
banner below the gray section indicating changes are being made.   
 
 
Section Three - Footer (global level content) 
The footer will be standard for all districts with two areas to customize “Our Mission” and “About this 
Website”.  Fill these in as your district sees ﬁt.  The links on the right-hand side will be customized by the 
district, omit what you do not need.  Keep in mind Facebook, X, and YouTube are unique to each district, 
so make sure they are for your area if you decide to use them.  Having this area blank is also an option 
for the districts. 
 


   
 
 
6 
Last Updated:  July 26, 2026 
Section Four – Supplementing Large Amounts of Information  
 
For water management reports or date, you will have the option to use drop down arrows to consolidate 
your content.  This will be for any area on the website that has more than one item.  This will keep the 
information organized without overwhelming the sidebar. 
 
 
Figure 1: Drop-Down Arrow for Additional Content 
Another option if you choose to use it, will be a page of links to pertinent information/regions.  The 
example below is the list of items for Fort Worths “Project Information”.  What you chose to put here is 
subject to your locality’s needs and requirements.

Last Updated:  July 26, 2026

8 
Last Updated:  July 26, 2026 
If you have 5-10 items, consider creating tiles to better ﬁll the space, as seen in Figure 3 
    Figure 3: Medium tiles used to link to reports  
Third option, if you have a page that has a lot of information and needs the real estate, you can use a 
there and back function.   For this one, you can omit the sidebar and add a home icon/button at the top 
left corner to return to the home page with breadcrumbs.      
 
 
If this guidance does not work for your district’s needs, contact your Division Lead for support.  We can 
also set up a working session to go through your site and help with organization.  You may run into 
areas that may not ﬁt the requirements above, so feel free to reach out.   
 


   
 
 
9 
Last Updated:  July 26, 2026 
Section Five - Suggested Steps to Organize Your Content   
 
Step one – Inventory Status and Reduction:  
Take inventory of your current pages, see what ﬁts into the mission essential items and what is unique to 
your district.  This is a good time to ﬁnd redundancies and outdated content that needs to be removed.  
If you have Google analytics, use that to determine areas that do not get much traﬃc.  For this initial 
migration, we will be taking what we currently have.  There is no need to create new content to ﬁt into 
this format.        
 
Step Two – Data Layout and Display:  
Once you have your content organized determine how you would like it displayed.  If you have a lot of 
links for one subject like reports, WM data, or pertinent information, determine if you would like to have 
a drop-down arrow on the sidebar for the content (good for 3-7 items) or a page with additional links 
(too large to ﬁt in a dropdown).  The other option would be a there and back page that omits the side 
bare to open up additional real estate (this is good for interactive maps and other intricate items). 
 
Step Three – Using Components to Build Out Your Site: 
When developing your site, the National Team will have components that are already built for the 
sidebar.  You will omit the items that do not ﬁt your website and append items that are not listed above 
to the “Unique to Each District” section.  If you have question on any of these items reach out to one of 
the Team Leads for support.   
For a list of currently available DISPLAY components see Groundwork: 
https://usace.github.io/groundwork/#/ 
For a list of currently available DATA components see Groundwork-WATER: 
https://usace-watermanagement.github.io/groundwork-water/ 
Step Four - Transfer your content to the new site:   
 There will be many components already built in React to start this process.  If something has not been 
developed by another district, you will want to be consistent with the USACE branding.  Charles Graham 
oversees Migration and Branding; he can assist with how this should be put together.  The National Team 
will also be hosting webinars on commonly used items.  
 
Step Five - Ensuring the content is what the end user needs:   
We will continue periodic checks with PAO to ensure content is user friendly.  We can provide a scan for 
compliance as needed (request this through your Team Lead).  This should be done before launching the 
site.  
 

   
 
 
10 
Last Updated:  July 26, 2026 
  Once we get the foundation set up, we will be inviting the public to test out our new sites.  This 
is expected to start by next April (2025).  
 
 We will overlap our sites for at least 6 months to get stakeholders, public, HQ, ancd other interested 
parties time to acclimate to the new content. (May-October 2025) During this time, you will add links to 
your current page (www.<dis>-wc.usace.army.mil) to the new one (water.usace.army.mil/<dis>) and add 
banners stating the upcoming changes.   
 
 
 We will create various webinar to help assist in the cutover process to the new site. s Consider sending  
out an email to let stakeholders and other third party contacts  know we will be making changes to our 
websites and transitioning to a new domain.  
 
During this process, if you have any questions or need help with anything, reach out to your team lead 
for help.  You are also welcome to request a workshop on any specific topic. Email Diana Hanbali, 
National Web PDT Lead with any concerns to request.

Section A - Solicitation/Contract Form Instrument Name: TPSS III IDIQ MATOC Product Service Code : J059

OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this acquisition includes: (1) providing quality oversight and management of cybersecurity projects; (2) developing criteria for how to implement cybersecurity across multiple agencies; (3) and performing inventories of Facility-Related Control Systems (FRCS) to include medical systems. There are no Architect-Engineer elements included in this requirement.

CONTRACT TYPE: A Firm Fixed Priced, Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ), Multiple award task order contract for Technical and Programmatic Support Services (TPSS) in support to the Department of the Army, Department of War (DoW) and non-DoW Agencies. The work will be performed at diverse locations throughout the United States, including Alaska and Hawaii, outlying areas (as defined by Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) 2.101), and U.

S. Territorial waters (as defined in 46 United States Code (U.S.C.) 70054(2)). The foreign locations include: , Germany, Italy, Japan, Netherlands, Kwajalein, and South Korea. Other foreign jurisdictions may be added to the geographic scope of the base MATOC contracts.

CONTRACT TERMS: The total shared capacity for the MATOC is $92 Million, which includes the base period and all planned options. The overall contract capacity and total estimated value will be shared amongst all MATOC holders. This effort is anticipated to be a total of 5-years, which will consist of a base ordering period of 60 months. The resultant contracts will also include RFO 52.217-8, Option to Extend Services, allowing for a potential extension of up to an additional six months. This option is not factored into the planned performance timeline, as it is reserved solely for mitigating unforeseen disruptions to services and minimizing start-up time, effort, learning curves, and procurement costs during transition periods. Price or cost will be a factor in the selection for each order placed under the IDC.

MINIMUM GUARANTEE & BASE CLINS: The Government's minimum guarantee of

$1,500.00 extends throughout the entire period of performance of the IDIQ. Funding for this minimum guarantee is obligated on the first TO and is the minimum ordering amount; not a minimum payment. Payment under the subsequent TO award(s) in an amount meeting/exceeding the minimum guarantee satisfies the minimum guarantee. The initial task order is then deobligated and closed out.

The Base CLIN establishes the maximum total capacity for the entire contract. Due to the indefinite nature of when needs arise, the total capacity is initially placed on the Base Period CLIN. Upon the exercise of any subsequent option period, the remaining unawarded capacity will be administratively transferred from the Base CLIN to the newly exercised Option CLIN. This process ensures the active CLIN accurately reflects the available capacity for task order awards during that period, while the overall maximum contract capacity remains unchanged

DORMANT STATUS: Due to extenuating circumstances (not related to performance), contractors can request to be placed in a dormant status. Contractors in dormant status cannot compete in new TO solicitations; however, they may continue to work on awarded TOs. Dormant status is granted for a defined finite time period, after which it will lift, and the contractor will be expected to compete.

CONTRACT AUTHORIZATION: The only authorized ordering office is the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Huntsville Engineering and Support Center. Other agencies may be delegated this authority, in which case, an advance written notice will be given to the contractor. In addition to, or in lieu of mailing an order, the Contracting Officer may issue an order orally, by facsimile or by electronic commerce methods, at his/her discretion.

Only a warranted Contracting Officer acting within their delegated limits, has the authority to issue modifications or otherwise change the terms and conditions of this contract. If an individual other than the Contracting Officer attempts to make changes to the terms and conditions of this contract you shall not proceed with the change and shall immediately notify the Contracting Officer.

A.7 SOLICITATION REQUIREMENTS/INFORMATION: In accordance with 10 U.S.C. (S) 3206(c)

and RFO 15.104(b)(1)(ii), the Government intends to award contracts to all qualifying offerors. Therefore, price or cost is not an evaluation factor for the award of the master Indefinite Delivery Contracts (IDC). Proposal submission shall be submitted per the instructions within this document. There will be no preproposal conference or site visits for this acquisition; however, questions relative to this solicitation shall be submitted in accordance with (IAW) with the instructions in this document. Competition for inclusion in the MATOC suite will be sought, promoted, and sustained by querying the System for Award Management (SAM), synopsizing proposed actions, and posting the solicitation in the Government-wide point of entry website (https://sam.gov/). Offerors must be registered in SAM to be eligible for award IAW RFO 52.204-7. In the event there are staggered awards during the MATOC award, later awarded contracts, will have an initial period of performance that will be less than the full base period in duration and will end on the same date as all other MATOC awardees.

Scope of Work 
For PMA/Maintenance Services 
CY2026 
 
General:  
This scope of work (SOW) describes the requirements for a full maintenance agreement for the 
network server which provides subscriber and dependent coverage for claims status, submission 
of 837 claims for Medicare and Private insurance payers and inquiry/correction of pending 
claims. 
Background:  
IHS is an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and is responsible 
for providing federal health services to American Indians and Alaska Natives. The provision of 
health services to members of federally recognized tribes grew out of the special government to 
government relationship between the federal government and Indian tribes. The IHS is the 
principal federal health care provider and health advocate for the Indian people. The goal is to 
assure that comprehensive, culturally acceptable personal and public health services are available 
and accessible to American Indians and Alaska Natives. The IHS currently provides health 
services to approximately 1.5 million American Indians and Alaska Natives who belong to more 
than 557 federally recognized tribes in 34 states. 
Navajo Area Indian Health Service (NAIHS) administers health centers and hospitals providing 
health care to approximately 201,583 members of the Navajo Nation. The Navajo Nation is the 
largest Indian tribe in the United States and has the largest reservation, which encompasses more 
than 25,516 square miles in northern Arizona, western New Mexico, and southern Utah, with 
three satellite communities in central New Mexico. The NAIHS is the primary provider of 
inpatient, ambulatory care, preventive and community health, and environmental health services 
for members of the Navajo Nation and the San Juan Southern Paiute Tribe. 
Scope:  
The Contractor shall provide Full Preventive Maintenance services for existing Internet Server 
for 837 claims processing at Chinle Comprehensive Health Care Facility.   
Location:  
Duties and responsibilities will encompass full maintenance service for the network server 
located at the Chinle Comprehensive Health Care Facility, Chinle, Arizona. Contractor shall 
provide monthly service. 
Place of Performance:  
Services are to be performed at the Chinle Comprehensive Health Care Facility, Chinle, Arizona. 
Period of Performance:  

December 12, 2025 to December 31, 2026. Will be flexible and, where feasible, include 
intermittent support to meet unplanned needs that develop on a frequent basis. 
Major Duties and Responsibility Requirements: 
 - Patient Access 
 - Ability to verify multiple commercial and government payers. Results into faster/more    
 reimbursement for the facility. 
 - Identify additional billable insurance coverage for patients. 
 Billing 
 - Electronic claims submission for Medica re, Medicaid, Veteran Administration and  
 Private Insurance. 
 - Provides 277 and 999 reports for elect ronic claims submitted to Medicare. 
 - Dashboard of Private In surance rejection session. 
 - Ability to run reports for denials. 
 - Capability to correct claims, obtain de nial reasons and resubmit claims to payers 
 FISS/DDE 
 - Securely connect to Medica re Direct Data Entry (DDE) 
 - Support for multip le submitted IDs 
 - Complete visibility to Medicare claim submissions 
 - On-line claim corrections and ability to obtain denial reasons 
 - Medicare Eligibility verifications 
 - Built in EDI tracking capability 
 
Definitions 
Acceptance: Constitutes acknowledgement that the network services conform to the applicable 
contract quality and quantity requirements, except as provided in FAR subpart 46.5 and subject 
to other terms and conditions of the contract. 
Approval: Acknowledgment by the designated Government official that submittals, deliverables, 
or administrative documents (e.g., insurance certificates, installation schedules, planned utility 
interruptions, etc.) conform to the contractual requirements. Government approval does not 
relieve the Contractor from responsibility for compliance with contract requirements. 
Area: A defined geographical region for Indian Health Service administrative purposes.               
Each Area Office may administer several Service Units. 
Contracting Officer (CO): A Government employee with the authority to enter into, administer, 
and/or terminate contracts and make related determinations and findings. 
Contractor: The individual awarded a legal binding contract to provide supplies and services. 
Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) or Project Officer (PO): A federal employee who 
assists the ordering/issuing activity contracting officer in the administration of task orders issued 
under this contract. The COR is primarily responsible for the technical assistance and day-to-day 

program management of the ordering activity's task orders. Ordering activities may have 
different designators for this employee (e.g. GTR – Government Technical Representative, 
COTR-Contracting Officer's Technical Representative, or PO - Project Officer). 
Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR): The FAR is the primary regulation for use by all Federal 
Executive agencies in their acquisition of supplies and services with appropriated funds. 
Ordering Activity Contracting Officer: A Government employee of IHS authorized and 
warranted to issue requests for services and to make modification(s) under this contract. The 
Ordering Activity CO has the authority to make initial determinations on all matters of 
maintenance services. 
Requirements:  
The Contractor shall provide full network server services in the delivery of IT server services to 
CCHCF, an IHS provider. Specific tasks include the following: 
Requirements: The Contractor shall maintain full network services for the delivery of IT services 
to CCHCF. 
The contractor shall provide training to CCHCF users. 
The contractor shall limit the amount of downtime with continuous operations. 
Submission of Invoices: The contractor will submit invoices in accordance with FAR 52.212-
4(g) on a monthly basis beginning December 12, 2025 to December 31, 2026, to the Chinle 
Comprehensive Health Care, Facility, 
Attention: Business Office, P.O. Drawer PH, Chinle, Arizona 86503. Telephone: 928-674-7030; 
Fax: 928-674-7705. 
Contractor Qualification Requirements: 
Experience. The Contractor shall possess basic knowledge, skills and abilities to maintain and 
provide network services on a monthly basis.  
The Contractor shall be in full compliant with Health Insurance Portability and Accountability 
Act of 1996 (HIPAA). 
The contractor shall define license and all relative documents. 
Government Furnished Information, Property and Services: 
 Inspection: all services rendered will be inspected, reviewed, and monitored by Patrick 
 Yazzie, BOM. 
 Contracting Officer Represen tative (COR): Michael Lampert 
 Department Point of Contact: Patrick Yazzie 

52.249-12 Termination: The Government may terminate this contract at any time upon at least-
15 days' written notice by the Contracting Officer to the Contractor. The Contractor, with the 
written consent of the Contracting Officer, may terminate this contract upon at least 15 days' 
written notice to the Contracting Officer. 
The contractor will comply with the following listed regulations: 
- Privacy Act, 5 U.S.C. 552a - Office of Privacy and Civil Liberties | Privacy Act of 1974 
- Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) - eCFR :: 45 CFR Part 164 -- 
Security and Privacy 
- CFR 42 Part 2 - eCFR :: 42 CFR Part 2 -- Confidentiality of Substance Use Disorder Patient 
Records

related to indemnification and filing deadlines are hereby waived, and shall not apply except to

determined under the Federal Tort Claims Act, or other governing federal authority. Federal 
statute of limitations provisions shall apply to any breach or claim.

hereby deleted. The TOS and this amendment shall be governed by and interpreted and enforced 
in accordance with the laws of the United States of America without reference to conflict of 
laws. To the extent permitted by federal law, the laws of the State of XXXXX will apply in the 
absence of applicable federal law.

Solicitation # 75FCMC26R0063 
National Provider Directory (NPD) Data Sourcing, Aggregation, and Quality Assurance Services 
Instructions 
 
 1 
INSTRUCTIONS TO OFFERORS 
 
1. This solicitation does not commit the Government to pay any cost for the preparation or 
submission of the quotation. This solicitation is not a contract nor a promise to contract in 
the future.  
 
2. This procurement is subject to the future availability of funds.  
 
3. The response should be prepared in a format capable of being viewed using Microsoft 
Office or Adobe Acrobat. 
 
4. Digital submissions should be formatted for print using letter-sized (8-1/2 X 11”) pages, 
single-spaced, with one inch (1”) margins. 
 
5. This solicitation may limit the number of pages associated with a given element of the 
offerors’ response. Within that context, one page equals one side of a sheet of paper. Use of 
landscape layout for certain pages when appropriate is acceptable and counts as one page. 
Number the pages consecutively. Any pages in excess of any page limitations cited herein 
will not be considered. Any page limitations set forth herein do not include
 any “front matter” 
information such as a cover letter, table of contents, and definitions or acronyms. Any 
technical or pricing information submitted within the “front matter” will not be considered. 
 
6. Responses should be 12-point font size. Smaller font not less than nine (9) point font size 
and single spacing is acceptable for any tables, graphics, illustrations, headers, and footers; 
however, offerors should not submit an abundance of information in chart format. 
 
7. Tables used throughout the narrative portions of the response should be formatted in such a 
way as to allow for the search and find functions in MS Office and Adobe Acrobat to 
discover text embedded in such tables. Offerors should avoid pasting images of such tables 
into the response, as the government wants to avoid situations where the search and find 
functions are not effective because words or numbers are embedded in the response as 
pictures/images rather than text. 
 
8. If sending electronic mail, CMS recommends keeping attachment size below 25MB to 
reduce risk of the e-mail not being delivered. 
 
9. If a Contractor Teaming Agreement (CTA) is being proposed, the proposal should indicate 
this is the case and identify all team members. Proposals must be consistent from the first 
phase to the last regarding identified CTA arrangements. The negotiation of CTAs will not 
involve the Government and are the responsibility of the offerors. The terms of any CTA 
must provide that the offeror providing the proposal will be identified as the contractor, such 
that the FPDS-NG record created for the contract reflects the offeror providing the proposal 
as the contractor. Furthermore, CMS will make payment only to the contractor identified on 
the contract; any further distribution of payment between teammates is the responsibility of 
the offeror identified in the contract. The contractor identified on the contract must be the 
CTA teammate expected to realize the most revenue under the contract, based on the data 
included in the cost/price volume.

SUBMISSION OF WRITTEN QUESTIONS 
 
All questions regarding this solicitation shall be submitted via electronic mail (e-mail) no later 
than 12:00 pm Eastern Time (ET) on 03 August 2026, to the Ordering Agency POC noted 
above.  Questions received after this date and time may not be answered prior to the closing 
date/time for receipt of responses. For each question, please include a reference to the specific 
section(s) of the RFP to which the question applies following the format below (i.e., the format 
below assumes a table with columns associated with each element). Contractors should use a 
file format that will facilitate CMS merging questions from multiple offerors into a single file. At its 
unilateral discretion, CMS may elect not to answer one (1) or more questions or to conduct one 
(1) or more live question-and-answer sessions. The questions and any CMS response thereto 
may be shared with all contract holders on a non-attribution basis as to the name of the 
contractor that asked the question. In the event of any conflict between an answer provided by 
CMS and the terms and conditions of the solicitation, as amended, the solicitation will control. 
 
In the event this solicitation includes more than one (1) phase, offerors have the opportunity to 
ask questions regarding each phase subsequent to the first. Any such questions are due no 
later than 12:00 pm ET on the third business day following distribution of the Contracting 
Officer's notification.

EVALUATION FACTORS FOR AWARD 
 
1. EVALUATION FACTORS FOR AWARD – GENERAL PROCEDURES 
A. The Government will evaluate proposals using a tradeoff process to determine which 
offerors represent the Best Value to the Government, as defined in FAR 2.101 and 
described in FAR 52.212-2. The Government may award to other than the lowest priced 
offeror or to other than the proposal assessed the most non-price merit. The relative 
importance considering all evaluation factors is provided as follows: all evaluation factors 
other than cost or price, when combined, are significantly more important than cost or 
price. 
 
B. The Government estimates one (1) single award to be made under this solicitation. This 
estimate in no way prohibits the Government from making either fewer or more awards 
than estimated based upon the offers received and a determination of the best interests 
of the Government. 
 
C. The Government may award without discussions with Offerors in accordance with FAR 
52.215-1. Therefore, the Offeror’s initial proposal should contain the Offerors’ best terms 
from a technical and price standpoint. The Government reserves the right to conduct 
discussions if deemed necessary. 
 
2. EVALUATION FACTORS FOR AWARD – EVALUATION PROCESS 
In addition to price, the following factors will be considered when determining best value: Factor 
1: Corporate Experience (Mission Focused), Factor 2: Performance Work Statement (PWS) & 
Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP), and Factor 3: Oral Presentations (Interview 
Style). For these factors, the Government will assess a confidence level (e.g., high, some, or 
low confidence) that the Offeror understands the requirement, proposes a sound approach, and 
will be successful in performing the contract with little or no Government intervention.  These 
non-price factors are listed in descending order of importance.   
In addition, CMS will evaluate Conflict of Interest (COI) and 508 VPAT submissions for 
compliance and acceptability for the apparent successful offeror. The evaluation of the COI and 
508 Volume will not be considered in terms of best value.  
Proposal submission and CMS’ evaluation thereof will occur in two phases, as follows: 
Two-Phase: Proposals will be submitted and evaluated in phases. The intent of the two-phase 
procurement is to minimize proposal development and presentation costs for those offerors with 
little or no chance of receiving an award, as well as to minimize evaluation time and effort on the 
agency’s part. In between each phase, CMS will make an advisory down-select and notify each 
offeror of CMS’s determination of whether the offeror should participate in the next phase. The 
Government will determine the appropriate number of offerors that is most beneficial to the

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT 
For 
AI-Powered Data Aggregation and Visualization Tool for Minuteman III 
Prepared For: 
Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center (AFNWC/NIM) 
Hill Air Force Base, Utah 
Date: [Current Date] 
 
TABLE OF CONTENTS 
SECTION I: DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES 
1.0 BACKGROUND 
2.0 SCOPE 
3.0 TASKS/REQUIREMENTS 
4.0 PROGRAM MANAGEMENT 
5.0 SECURITY REQUIREMENTS 
6.0 DELIVERABLES 
SECTION II: SERVICE SUMMARY 
SECTION III: GOVERNMENT-FURNISHED INFORMATION 
 
SECTION I: DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES 
1.0 BACKGROUND 
The Minuteman III (MMIII) Systems Directorate currently manages critical data across 
approximately 60 disparate and disconnected systems, including databases, local hard 
drives, and shared networks. This fragmented data environment necessitates signiﬁcant 
manual labor to compile information, assess weapon system risks (both for parts attrition 
and functional age-out), and maintain overall situational awareness. Past efforts to 
establish a uniﬁed Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) digital ecosystem have not come 
to fruition due to a range of challenges. While separate tools, including AIMM3 (Analytics 
Intelligence for MMIII), are successfully used for ﬂeet health metrics, critical gaps remain in 
centralized data access, querying, and visualization. This Performance Work Statement 
(PWS) establishes the requirement for a contractor to develop an Artiﬁcial Intelligence (AI) 
tool to address these speciﬁc gaps. 

2.0 SCOPE 
The contractor shall design, develop, test, and implement an AI-powered software tool to 
provide a centralized data query and assessment capability for the MMIII program. The 
primary objective is to bridge the existing gaps in data accessibility and technical data 
assessment. The tool shall provide a single, uniﬁed interface for users to query and retrieve 
information from the various MMIII data sources without needing to access each source 
system individually. It shall provide enhanced query capability based on user-deﬁned 
questions.  It shall also provide enhanced visualization capabilities for technical ﬁles such 
as 2D/3D drawings and functional diagrams.   This effort will complement, not replace, the 
existing AIMM3 metrics tool. 
3.0 TASKS/REQUIREMENTS 
The contractor shall perform the tasks detailed below: 
3.1 Centralized Data Querying 
The contractor shall develop a feature that provides a uniﬁed search and retrieval 
capability. 
• 3.1.1 The system shall be able to connect to and pull data from the various MMIII 
data sources as speciﬁed in the Government-Furnished Information (GFI). These 
sources include, but are not limited to: MMIII Health of the Fleet metrics, drawings, 
speciﬁcations, interface control documents, MMIII supply data, MMIII maintenance 
data, and the JIRA Weapon System Risk Repository. 
• 3.1.2 The tool shall provide a single user interface for querying the connected data 
sources. It shall not serve as the Authoritative Source of Truth (ASOT) but must have 
the ability to pull data from the respective ASOTs in near real-time. 
3.2 Enhanced Data Visualization 
The contractor shall develop a feature to query, access, and visualize complex technical 
data. 
• 3.2.1 The system shall provide an intuitive way to navigate and view technical data, 
including 2D drawings, 3D models, functional ﬂow diagrams, and other ﬁgures. 
• 3.2.2 This capability should be designed to improve the ease of training for new 
personnel and aid in the navigation of complex system architectures. 
3.3 System Performance and Risk Mitigation 
• 3.3.1 Performance: The tool shall be designed for efficiency, aiming to reduce the 
time and manual effort currently required for data compilation tasks by a 

measurable amount, to be deﬁned and agreed upon during the ﬁrst Program 
Management Review (PMR). 
• 3.3.2 Risk Mitigation: The contractor shall implement safeguards and continuous 
validation checks to ensure the accuracy and integrity of the data presented by the 
tool. The system must accurately reﬂect the data from the source systems. 
4.0 PROGRAM MANAGEMENT 
• 4.1 Project Management Plan: The contractor shall deliver a comprehensive Project 
Management Plan within 30 days of contract award. This plan will outline the 
contractor's approach to managing the project, including timelines, milestones, and 
a software development lifecycle methodology. 
• 4.2 Program Management Reviews (PMRs): The contractor shall conduct quarterly 
PMRs with government stakeholders. These reviews will cover project status, 
progress against milestones, risks, and a demonstration of completed work. 
• 4.3 Reporting: The contractor shall provide Monthly Status Reports detailing 
activities completed, upcoming work, and any issues or risks encountered. 
5.0 SECURITY REQUIREMENTS 
• 5.1 Data Handling: The contractor shall handle all data in accordance with DoD 
regulations. The initial phase of the project will involve accessibility for Controlled 
Unclassiﬁed Information (CUI) at Impact Level 5 (IL5). Future efforts may include 
work with Secret data at Impact Level 6 (IL6). 
• 5.2 Personnel: Contractor personnel requiring access to government systems or 
data will be required to have the appropriate security clearances as speciﬁed by the 
government. 
6.0 DELIVERABLES 
The contractor shall provide the following deliverables to the Government in accordance 
with the speciﬁed schedule:

B.1  BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES  
 
To modernize communication channels and support Federal Occupation Health (FOH)’s digital 
transformation, FOH requires a secure, FedRAMP‑authorized, cloud‑based electronic fax (eFax) service 
capable of supporting enterprise‑wide Health Insurance Portability & Accountability Act 
(HIPAA)‑compliant digital inbound and outbound faxing. The eFax solution is essential for enabling FOH 
program areas to exchange sensitive documents rapidly, reliably, and in alignment with federal 
cybersecurity, privacy, and interoperability standards. 
 
B.2  TYPE OF CONTRACT  
 
The Government intends to award a Fixed Price contract. 
 
B.3  SEVERABLE SERVICES  
 
The services acquired under this contract are severable services.  Funds are only available for use for the 
contract line item (CLIN) to which they are obligated.  Unused funds from one CLIN may not rollover 
for use in other periods.

Statement Work (SOW) 
 
1. Background 
 
The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is responsible for protecting the public health by ensuring the 
safety, efficacy, and security of human and veterinary drugs, biological products, and medical devices; and 
by ensuring the safety of our nation's food s upply, cosmetics, and products that emit radiation. The FDA 
also has responsibility for regulating the manufacturing, marketing, and distribution of tobacco products to 
protect the public health and to reduce tobacco use by minors. Additionally, the FDA is  responsible for 
advancing the public health by helping to speed innovations that make medical products more effective, 
safer, and more affordable and by helping the public get the accurate, science-based information they need 
to use medical products and foods to maintain and improve their health.  
 
The organization sponsoring and supporting this requirement is the Office of Computational Science (OCS) in 
the (super) Office of Translational Sciences (OTS) under the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research 
(CDER).  
 
The Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER) performs an essential public health task by making 
sure that safe and effective drugs are available to improve the health of people in the United States. As part 
of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), CDER regulates over the counter and prescription drugs, 
including biological therapeutics and generic drugs.   
 
The Office of Translational Sciences empowers a collaborative and high performing workforce to champion 
innovation and advance global human drug development. The vision of this super office is to drive 
advancements in human health through scientific and regulatory innovation. A summary of current work 
being done includes: 
• Promoting scientific collaboration and innovation in drug regulatory review across CDER 
• Assuring the validity of clinical trial design and analysis in regulatory decision making 
• Developing and applying quantitative and statistical approaches to decision making in regulatory 
review process 
• Ensuring alignment with CDER goals 
• Serving the CDER scientific community in establishing technology transfer agreements that are vital 
to collaboration with the broader scientific community 
• Maintaining knowledge management databases that can be the basis of improvements in the 
regulatory review process 
• Overseeing bioequivalence inspections to ensure the availability of safe and effective generic 
equivalents of investigational drugs 
 
The mission of the Office of Scientific Computing  is to provide CDER reviewers innovative and reliable 
solutions that improve and strengthen the scientific review process by integrating data, tools, and training. 
The focus of OCS’s current efforts include:  
• Building solutions that drive New Drug Modernization, promote access to quality data, and optimize 
data analysis capabilities  
• Processing Study Data for rapid use 
• Delivering effective tools, technologies, services, and training to meet CDER’s mission  
• Delivering solutions that streamline Bioresearch Monitoring (BIMO)  workflow for reviewers and 
inspectors  
• Spearheading the CDER Innovation Board to harness subject matter expertise across FDA 
• Offering cloud-enabled innovation space for tools, technologies, and data exploration  
• Connecting CDER staff to the scientific computing resources and technology needed to drive 
efficient analysis and cost-effective solutions  

 info@JohnSnowLabs.com © John Snow Labs, Inc. 2022  (302) 768-5227 
 
 
• Collaborating with industry, academia, and other external partners through our work with PHUSE, 
CDISC and BioCelerate  
 
Currently, the CDER process to identify submissions containing standard data is labor intensive: the Office 
of Business Informatics reviews all new submissions and performs an assessment on a few relevant files to 
determine if the submission appears to be SDTM (Study Data Tabulation Model) compliant. The DataFit 
system automatically and systematically checks submission and validates conformance of study data to 
CDISC Standards (e.g. SDTM, ADaM [Analysis Data Model], SEND [Standard for Exchange of Nonclinical 
Data]). This automated systematic approach will allow CDER to successfully transition to a more advanced 
regulatory process which takes full advantage of the benefits of high-quality standardized data improving the 
ability for Food and Drug Administration (FDA) reviewers to make science based regulatory decisions faster. 
 
2. Project Scope 
 
The objective is to install, update, support, and develop enhancements and to maintain DataFit, the CDER’s 
data standards validation platform. DataFit supports multiple FDA needs for analyses of clinical trial data and 
non-clinical data and it integrates with existing systems to provide data standards validation. 
The scope includes all the activities necessary to support regulatory review operations, to maintain and 
provide enhancements to DataFit, which include necessary management functions such as Project 
Management, and Release Management. The majority of the D ataFit capabilities are delivered through 
Pinnacle21 Enterprise, which is based on the open source CDISC clinical trial data standards compliance 
software and is licensed for use by FDA employees. DataFit extends the P21 Enterprise capability to functions 
unique to the FDA, such as implementing FDA business rules, FDA tools specific rules and interfacing with 
existing FDA systems.  
 
There is a need to have a platform that is flexible and can integrate and coordinate a variety of checking 
methods/procedures/programs in connection with a database.  
 
The scope includes: 
• Install/support/maintain DataFit by providing Steady State Activities described in SOW including 
software, interface, and configuration installation and updates in development, test and production 
environments.  
• Provide Pinnacle 21 enterprise license, or equal to solution to FDA. 
• Provide technical and customer support. 
• Participate in Change Control process and document lessons learned.  
• Develop iterative release schedule using agile methodology for minor and major releases informed 
by CoreDF assessment for current baselined codebase and DataFit platform upgrades and identified 
bugs.  
• Conduct project management tasks including CPIC required activities. 
• Provide technical support to troubleshoot and help resolve user, tool interface, system integration, or 
system operational problems. 
• Generate metrics reporting on validation results as needed 
• Create and maintain accurate documentation in accordance with DHHS’s / FDA’s Enterprise 
Performance Life Cycle (EPLC) for IT systems for O&M releases, O&M and DME change requests, 
and other development activities documents identified in future DME orders issued against this 
contract.  
 
3. Requirement Description 
  
The FDA requires software licenses, configuration management, training, and professional support services 
to fulfill this requirement: 
 

 info@JohnSnowLabs.com © John Snow Labs, Inc. 2022  (302) 768-5227 
 
 
3.1. DataFit Enterprise / FDA Specific Version, or equal to 
 
Pinnacle 21 and DataFit provide unique/salient solutions by providing: 
• Exclusive FDA -integrated functionality that extends beyond standard Enterprise capabilities  to 
include: 
o Deep regulatory alignment, backed by years of partnership and direct influence on CDISC 
and industry standards. 
o End-to-end validation and submission readiness support grounded in FDA -specific 
workflows, specifically supporting 
 Clinical CoreDF Reports already in operation 
 Nonclinical CoreDF Reports already in operation 
 BIMO CoreDF Reports already in operation 
 Modified reports tailored to existing OOD requirements already in operation 
 Modified reports tailored to existing OCP requirements already in operation 
o Advanced automation and integration, reducing submission review timelines and improving 
data quality. 
o A proven, validated platform operating at scale within FDA’s critical drug review operations. 
 
Pinnacle 21 has been a long -time partner to FDA/CDER/OTS, providing the DataFit platform and expert 
services that ensure standardized, high -quality clinical and nonclinical data are ready to support timely, 
science-based regulatory decision- making. P21 is a Certara company, and supports CDISC standards 
compliance, clinical data quality, and regulatory submission readiness.  Their mission also directly aligns 
with FDA’s public health priorities and include improving the quality of clinical data and advance p atient 
safety. 
 
FDA-Specific Technical Requirements - Integration with FDA Systems 
- Existing integrations with EDR, CTR, Data Central, and iPortal must continue without modification  
and without disruption to current daily operations 
- Automated submission intake workflows must remain operational for: 
o Clinical CoreDF Reports 
o Nonclinical CoreDF Reports 
o BIMO CoreDF Reports 
o Modified reports tailored to existing OOD requirements already in operation 
o Modified reports tailored to existing OCP requirements already in operation 
- Reviewer-facing reporting systems must maintain current functionality 
 
Any proposed "equal" solution must demonstrate: 
 
a. Existing implementation of FDA's complete 3-tier validation rule architecture (TRC + Business 
Rules + Validator Rules) without requiring re-engineering 
 
b. Proven ability to process ts.xpt -based study classification logic as documented in FDA's Study 
Data Technical Conformance Guide 
 
c. Existing publicly available sponsor -side validation tool that mirrors FDA's internal validation 
engine (equivalent to Pinnacle 21 Community's "FDA engine") 
 
d. Current integration with FDA's EDR, CTR, Data Central, and iPortal systems without requiring 
system modifications 
 
e. Ability to import and execute existing FDA Business Rules (v1.5) and Validator Rules (v1.6) 
without translation or re-engineering 
 

 info@JohnSnowLabs.com © John Snow Labs, Inc. 2022  (302) 768-5227 
 
 
Offerors proposing an "equal" solution must provide: 
a) Detailed technical documentation demonstrating each capability 
b) Transition plan with timeline and cost estimate 
c) Risk mitigation strategy for industry-facing validation ecosystem disruption 
d) References from other regulatory agencies using equivalent FDA-specific configurations 
 
History with FDA/CDER 
Pinnacle 21 has collaborated with FDA since 2011 and has successfully delivered DataFit Support Services, 
including full implementation, operational support, and enhancements to CDER’s data validation ecosystem. 
This work has established DataFit as a core capability for modernized regulatory review. Past performance 
highlights include: 
• Deployment of Pinnacle 21 Enterprise and DataFit across development, test, pilot, and production 
environments. 
• Seamless integration with FDA systems including EDR, CTR, Data Central, and OCP’s iPortal. 
• Delivery of complete validation documentation (User/Functional Requirements, Validation Plan, 
IQ/OQ/PQ testing, User Manuals, and Release Notes). 
• Development and maintenance of FDA -specific clinical and nonclinical business rules and 
automation of daily Core DataFitness (CoreDF) assessments. 
• Support for standardized data flow into critical reviewer systems, enabling faster, more consistent 
evaluation of submissions. 
 
Salient Capabilities Tailored for CDER’s Mission 
Pinnacle 21 provides comprehensive support across the full lifecycle of CDISC standardized data 
submissions: 
• DataFit Operations & Maintenance: system updates, performance tuning, production support, user 
access integration, and real-time data validation. 
• CDISC Submission Processing: tracking, data -fitness checks, conformance assessments, and CTR 
loading verification. 
• Standards Integration & Enhancements: incorporation of evolving CDISC and FDA rule sets, SEND 
Explorer-based rules, and ADaM FDA business rules. 
• Reviewer-Focused Reporting: CoreDF reports for BIMO, OCP, OOD, clinical and nonclinical 
disciplines; KickStart/JumpStart early-assessment reporting; Data Quality Report enhancements for 
OCS tools. 
• Future-Ready Technical Support: Dataset -JSON 1.1, eCTD validation, expanded API capabilities, 
and integration with additional reviewer tools. 
 
Pinnacle 21 provides FDA-exclusive and unique capabilities that define DataFit’s value: 
• FDA-embedded business rules for both clinical and nonclinical data. 
• Daily automated CoreDF assessments of all original submissions. 
• Deep integration with existing CDER review systems and workflows. 
• A global community of 50,000+ users, ensuring unmatched maturity, stability, and standards 
expertise.

Section C - Description/Specifications/Statement of Work
Performance Work Statement
DSpace Institutional Repository Support Services
Dudley Knox Library
Naval Postgraduate School
 
1.0          Background/Introduction:
The Naval Postgraduate School (NPS), located in Monterey, California, supports the U.S. Navy, other military branches, and 
foreign military services with postgraduate education for their personnel. Additionally, NPS provides significant research 
capabilities to the Department of Defense, Department of Homeland Security, and others. Dudley Knox Library (DKL) is the 
academic library at NPS and provides research scholarly content relevant to NPS instructional and research needs. Some of this 
content is housed and delivered via Calhoun, a centralized repository for the NPS scholarly record and archival materials.
 
The Naval Postgraduate School's Dudley Knox Library requires a Registered Duraspace Service Provider to provide software 
upgrades, customizations and maintenance for its DSpace-based institutional repository, Calhoun. (https://calhoun.nps.edu). 
Calhoun is built on DSpace open-source software loaded on internal NPS servers. Calhoun runs DSpace v.7.6 with 
customizations and integration with 3rd party services including handle server and backup of content into Internet Archive and 
AWS cloud storage. DKL has a second server that mirrors Calhoun for the purpose of testing batch ingests before they enter the 
Calhoun repository. Calhoun uses extended Dublin Core metadata, contains over 71,000 records; ingests at least 2,500 records 
per year; and has a history of 99.7% annual up time.
 
2.0          Scope:
The scope of this contract includes DSpace upgrades, configuration and dependency management, customizations, delivered 
and maintained modules, and technical support and monitoring.
 
3.0          Tasks:
3.1 Upgrades      
The contractor shall support the ongoing lifecycle of the NPS DSpace-based institutional repository (Calhoun), ensuring that the      
platform remains secure, supported, and aligned with community best practices to    include:
-         Planning and execution of scheduled platform upgrades
-         Coordination of upgrade activities across test and production environments
-         Validation of repository functionality following     upgrades
-         Documentation and administrative handoff
-         Upgrade readiness assessments, including dependency analysis and evaluation of impacts to existing        
customizations and reusable platform features prior to committing to a target release.
-         Upgrade to the latest stable DSpace 9 Long-Term Support (LTS) release in            2027
-         A subsequent major upgrade in or around 2029, version determination to be based on platform stability,            
community adoption, and NPS requirements.
During periods between major platform upgrades, the contractor shall support platform stability, configuration updates, 
dependency maintenance, and incremental improvements, as well as activities that reduce future upgrade risk and support            
evolving NPS priorities.

Ongoing configuration management to ensure compatibility with supported versions of underlying software components to          
include:
-         Application configuration updates
-         Dependency upgrades (e.g., Java, Tomcat, PostgreSQL,      Solr)
-         Security patching and configuration hardening.
3.3 Customizations      
This task covers customizations and enhancements developed specifically for NPS workflows, policies, and repository use cases.         
3.3.1 Repository Architecture and Data        Modeling
Support for the evolution and maintenance of the repository's organizational structure and metadata model to i          
nclude:
-         Maintenance and refinement of DSpace entity-based modeling
-         Ongoing support for repository reorganization strategies
-         Metadata schema adjustments and governance support.
3.3.2 Identity and                            Branding
Support for NPS-specific user experience and access requirements to include:       
-         Maintenance of NPS branding and theming
-         Integration with NPS authentication and single sign-on (SSO) systems
3.3.3 Ingest, Submission, and Workflow                               Enhancements
Support for NPS-defined ingest, submission, and content management processes to include:        
-         Maintenance of batch ingest workflows (e.g., CSV + ZIP)
-         Support for custom submission workflows and input forms
-         Support for curation tasks and automated processing
-         Workflow improvements driven by NPS operational      need
3.3.4 Selective     Exports
Search-based metadata and citation export functionality implemented as an NPS-specific customization to         include:
-         Search-driven export workflows
-         Support for multiple output formats
3.3.5 Advanced Replication Task Suite        (RTS)
Support for backup, replication, and restore of DSpace items implemented as an NPS-specific customization to            include:
-         Versioned replication of items and     bitstreams
-         Restore and recovery capabilities.

 PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS

The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is undergoing a significant technology transformation, migrating all unified communications and contact center operations. As part of this transition, the VA must preserve, manage, and provide compliant access to hundreds of millions of legacy call recordings currently stored across three on-premise platforms: Calabrio One, Avaya, and Verint. These recordings must be retained in accordance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) mandates, with variable retention policies by call type — including crisis, benefits, and healthcare interactions.

The VA needs a solution that extracts, decrypts, and standardizes its legacy recordings into an open format, consolidates them into a single compliant archive, and allows the decommissioning of these platforms once the contact center migration is complete.

ITEM 1 SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS

1.11	Source Systems

The VA's legacy recording environment consists of the following systems:

Calabrio One v11.5 (Main Production) — Single-tenant, Azure Cloud storage. Confirmed file count: approximately 227,381,000 files (January 2018 – present).

Calabrio One v11.5 (Legacy System) — Single-tenant, actively purging. Confirmed file count: approximately 1,860,000 files. Count will decrease over time.

Avaya / Verint 15.2 — Thales KMS (2 KMS instances). Azure Blob storage. File count: approximately 42,618,159 files. 

Total confirmed 458,811,000 files. 

1.12 Deliverables

Extraction of all call recordings and associated metadata from Calabrio (main and legacy) and Avaya/Verint environments.

Decryption of all encrypted files, leveraging the VA's existing Thales KMS credentials.

Conversion to open-standard WAV format with associated metadata, stored in a VA-designated location (on-premise, Azure Blob, or AWS S3).

Deployment and configuration of Continuity Replay within the VA's approved hosting environment (on-premise or FedRAMP-certified AWS).

Configuration of NARA-compliant retention policies by call type (crisis, benefits, healthcare, etc.).

Professional services including project management, installation, and training.

1.13 Continuity Replay

The chosen solution shall provide Continuity Replay.  Continuity Replay shall be configured at deployment to enforce NARA retention requirements across the VA's diverse call types. The system shall apply retention periods based on metadata attributes — such as call type, department, or location — ensuring that crisis calls, benefits interactions, and healthcare recordings are each held for the appropriate duration and automatically purged upon expiry. Legal hold capabilities will allow the VA to pause purge on specific files flagged for audit, compliance review, or litigation support.

Core Capabilities

Dashboard: Real-time visibility into interactions under legal hold, files scheduled for purge in the next 30 days, and total archive metrics by year.

Advanced Search & Replay: Intuitive filter interface by date range, user, interaction ID, group, department, call type, and custom tags. Playback of any archived audio directly in-browser.

On-Demand Transcription: Any archived call can be transcribed within the platform, regardless of whether it was transcribed by the original recording system. Useful for the VA's ad hoc transcription workflows.

NARA Retention Engine: Configurable retention policies by metadata attribute. Automatic purge scheduling with pre-purge notification. Legal hold to override purge for specific interactions.

Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Granular permissions by user, group, or department. Full audit trail of all access, downloads, legal holds, and replay events.

Bulk Export: Export interactions and metadata in bulk for audit response, litigation support, or downstream processing.

Multi-Interaction Support: Supports audio calls, email, chat, screen recordings, and more — future-proofed for all interaction types the VA may need to archive.

1.14 Salient Technical Specifications

NOTICE OF THE FEDERAL ACCESSIBILITY LAW AFFECTING ALL INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY (ICT) PROCUREMENTS (SECTION 508)

On January 18, 2017, the Access Board issued a final rule that updated accessibility requirements covered by Section 508 and refreshed guidelines for telecommunications equipment subject to Section 255 of the Communications Act.  The final rule went into effect on January 18, 2018.  The revisions and updates to the Section 508-based standards and Section 255-based guidelines are intended to ensure that information and communication technology (ICT) covered by the respective statutes is accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities.

SECTION 508 – INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY (ICT) STANDARDS

The Section 508 standards established by the Access Board are incorporated into, and made part of all VA orders, solicitations and purchase orders developed to procure ICT.  These standards are found in their entirety at: Revised 508 Standards and 255 Guidelines (access-board.gov).  A single PDF file version of the Revised Section 508 Standards and 255 Guidelines will be supplied upon request, or can be obtained from the Access Board website.  Federal agencies must comply with the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as amended. 

The Contractor shall comply with “508 Chapter 2: Scoping Requirements” for all electronic ICT and content delivered under this contract. Specifically, as appropriate for the technology and its functionality, the Contractor shall comply with the technical standards marked here: 

	E205 Electronic Content – (Accessibility Standard -WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA Guidelines)

	E204 Functional Performance Criteria

	E206 Hardware Requirements

	E207 Software Requirements

	E208 Support Documentation and Services Requirements

COMPATABILITY WITH ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY

The standards do not require installation of specific accessibility-related software or attachment of an assistive technology device. Section 508 requires that ICT be compatible with such software and devices so that ICT can be accessible to and usable by individuals using assistive technology, including but not limited to screen readers, screen magnifiers, and speech recognition software.

ACCEPTANCE AND ACCEPTANCE TESTING

Deliverables resulting from this solicitation will be accepted based in part on satisfaction of the Section 508 Chapter 2: Scoping Requirements standards identified above.

The Government reserves the right to test for Section 508 Compliance before delivery.  The Contractor shall be able to demonstrate Section 508 Compliance upon delivery.

Question and Responses 
Updated B.2 Price Schedule CLINs 
 
 
1. Incumbent Solution and Current Contract 
The Price/Cost Schedule (CLIN 0001AA) and PWS §17 both refer to “Imagex” software and 
“Imagex software and associated modules” already deployed at VISN 16 facilities, but Section 5 
(Brand Name or Equal salients) does not name a specific brand. The questions below are 
intended to clarify the incumbent environment and how it relates to the brand-name-or-equal 
structure of this solicitation. 
1. Please confirm the identity of the incumbent contractor and the specific product/brand 
(e.g., is “Imagex” the brand name being used to establish the salient characteristics in 
PWS §5, or is it a generic label used only in the CLIN structure)?  
Response: The incumbent is Medicom Technologies, Inc., under Contract 36C25622P1530; the 
current product/system in use is Medicom’s Imagex. In this solicitation, “Imagex” is used strictly 
as a brand‑name‑or‑equal reference. Equal products are acceptable if they meet all salient 
characteristics in PWS section 5. Evaluation will be based only on the salient characteristics 
stated in PWS. 
2. What is the current contract number, award date, period of performance, and expiration 
date for the existing DICOM image sharing/Imagex solution at VISN 16?  
Response: Please see Response #1 for the contract number. The award date, period of 
performance, and expiration date are publicly available in SAM.gov under the Contract Awards 
domain (note: FPDS public functionality has been fully transitioned to SAM.gov). 
3. What is the current annual contract value (software licensing + AMS) under the 
incumbent contract, and is that contract a sole-source, competed, or FSS award?  
Response: Please see Response #1 for the contract number. The annual value and the 
award/competition method are publicly available in SAM.gov under the Contract Awards 
domain (FPDS public functionality has been fully transitioned to SAM.gov). 
4. Which of the eight (8) VISN 16 facilities currently have an image sharing solution 
deployed today, and which vendor/product is in place at each site? Are all eight on the 
same platform, or is this a mixed environment? 
Response: All facilities within VISN 16 have the same Medicom system in place.  
5. How many community care partners are currently onboarded/connected under the 
incumbent solution at each facility, and how many existing site-to-site (S2S) connections, 
MOUs, ISAs, and BAAs are in place that a new awardee would need to assume or 
replicate? 

Response: there are approximately 53 care in the community partners across the VISN and 195 
VA connections established. 
6. If a new contractor is awarded, will the incumbent be required to support a 
transition/parallel-run period, and who is responsible for data migration, historical audit 
log retention, and cutover of existing community partner connections? 
Response: Incumbent has no obligation to perform after their period of performance ends. There 
is no data to migrate. The existing community connections belong to the incumbent and would 
not be cutover. The new awardee will be responsible for establishing new connection at each 
existing facility and every new facility requested during the period of performance.  
7. Will the Government share the incumbent's current performance data (query turnaround 
times, matching accuracy, uptime, exchange volumes) to help offerors size their technical 
and pricing approach? 
Response: Incumbent performance data will not be released. Offerors should size their technical 
and pricing approach to the published requirements in the PWS/Solicitation; evaluation will be 
based only on stated requirements. 
8. Is the incumbent contractor eligible to compete on this solicitation, and if so, does the 
Government anticipate any organizational conflict of interest (OCI) considerations?  
Response: Yes, incumbent is eligible to compete on this solicitation. Any organizational 
conflicts of interest (OCI) concerns will be evaluated/addressed under FAR Subpart 9.5.

specific brand-name product against which “equal” conformance will be judged, per FAR 
52.211-6, or is any commercially available solution meeting the salients acceptable 
regardless of brand?  
Response: Any commercially available solution that meets the PWS/Solicitation salient 
physical, functional, and performance characteristics is acceptable; no specific brand will be 
identified. 
1. For the required “literature and salients crosswalk” (Section E.1¶4), is there a required 
format or template, and does it count against the 15-page Technical volume limit?  
 
Response: The Literature & Salients Crosswalk shall be included within Volume I – Technical 
and counts toward the 15‑page Technical limit. No specific template is required; submit in a 
clear table or matrix pursuant to FAR 52.212‑1. 

2. PWS §5(e) references the VISN 16 enterprise PACS as “currently Philips/Carestream 
Vue, version as deployed.” Can the Government confirm the specific version(s) in use at 
each of the eight facilities? 
Response: The specific version of PACS does not matter for image exchange since the DICOM 
standard is the same. However, the current version of Vue PACS is 12.2.0.x but the sites are in 
transition to 12.2.8.x. The image exchange will occur from any DICOM source at the facility that 
is configured to the destination and vice versa. 
3. Scope, Technical Requirements, and Cerner Migration 
1. What is the current monthly/annual volume of DICOM studies and reports exchanged (or

Response: As of Dec 2025, the average quarterly inbound volume is 12k/qtr, outbound volume 
is 7k/qtr,  
2. What is the anticipated timeline for VA's Cerner deployment at these eight VISN 16 sites, 
and how should offerors account for a mid-contract EHR platform migration within the 
12-month base plus four 1-year option structure? 
Response: Offerors must plan for both VistA and Oracle Health interoperability. The current

3. PWS §5(h) states there are “approximately 25 to 30 partners per site” of community care

compensation? 
Response: Consider 25–30 partners indicative only; design a solution that scales with growth. 
The current system is capable of exchange with all VA and DoW partners established within the 
system in addition to community partners. As of FY26 Q1 ending Dec 2025, there were 
approximately 195 VA connections and 53 community partners setup. 
4. For the 60-day onboarding SLA, what portion of that timeline is the contractor

Response: The 60-day SLA applies to contractor-controlled work and starts after VA completes

5. Are the VistA Imaging Importer, DICOM router, and PACS interface configurations

Response: In general, the VistA, DICOM router, Radiology PACS are the same. There may be
