Attachment 0001 Memorials DevSecOps Application Systems Product List

The Memorial Benefits and Services (MBS) Products provide technology solutions to support National Cemetery Administration (NCA) programs and services. They deliver digitization, modernization, automation, and interoperability solutions to provide Veterans and their families with efficient and timely services and benefits. 

 System Acronym  | System Name  | System Description 

VA-EISS | VA- Enterprise Interment Services System (EISS) | 
VA-EISS supports a broad range of NCA business functions, including but not limited to:
Processing pre-need burial eligibility applications and state cemetery eligibility requests;
Generating pre-need determination correspondence;
Supporting time-of-need burial and memorial benefit processing;
Recording and tracking family preference;
Scheduling green burials and other specialized interment services;
Managing plaque, urn, and memorial benefits requests;
Creating, updating, and maintaining burial and interment records;
Managing subsequent interment requests and remains locations updates;
Creating and maintaining marker templates;
Scheduling, approving, and certifying interment services;
Ordering headstones, markers, and niche covers;
Performing quality assurance activities on decedent records; and
Administering system functions, including user account management, resource configuration, marker order maintenance, email template management, and cemetery settings administration.
The VA-EISS application is developed using Microsoft technologies, including C#, .NET, and the Blazor framework, and integrates with Geographic Information System (GIS) capabilities to support cemetery mapping and operational functions

MBMS | Memorial Benefits and Management System | The first major area of NCA operations to use MBMS is the National Cemetery Scheduling Office (NCSO), the central call center for anyone scheduling a burial, interment, or inurnment at a National Cemetery. The Case Management, Eligibility, and Outreach (CaMEO) module uses the Salesforce COTS platform, which brings case management functionality and automated workflow processes into one integrated system. 
A companion module, Cemetery Regulations, Reports and Testing (CeRRT), allows individual cemeteries to indicate, on a calendar-type form, the hours and capacity for services. This information is displayed to NCSO to enable accurate and consistent scheduling for Veterans and their families. Additionally, MBMS automates all business processes associated with tracking orders and delivery of monuments. It provides a complete historical record for each monument application and automates all manual, paper-intensive record keeping and information and forms processing associated with over 135,000 yearly interments. Finally, using one system, MBMS enables NCA end-users to perform eligibility, benefits, and cemetery management functions.


MEL | Memorial Enterprise Letters | The Memorial Enterprise Letters (MEL) application allows the NCA to build new letter templates to generate letters related to suspending or denying an application for a government headstone, marker, or medallion. The NCA Case Managers use these templates to create letters to the next of kin or cemetery explaining why their application for the government headstone, marker, or medallion has been suspended or denied. The MEL application also supports the print vendor, which prints and mails letters to the recipients. The current MEL custom solution will be replaced with a configurable lightweight correspondence engine, allowing NCA to build new letter templates and automate business rules for template approval. This eliminates NCA's dependency on Information Technology (IT) support for letter template management.

VLM | Veteran Legacy Memorial | The Veterans Legacy Memorial (VLM) is an interactive online memorialization platform designed to honor the service and sacrifice of the nation’s Veterans. The digital memorialization platform enables visitors to honor and pay their respects to Veterans interred at VA national cemeteries by allowing public contributions to Veterans’ pages. VLM’s online portal includes digital pictures of headstones and markers, and burial records that family members, survivors, and friends can view. VLM has incorporated architecture and functionality specializing in Cloud infrastructure, principles and protocols of user experience (UX), and human-centered design. The project is the latest from VA’s IT and Digital Modernization program and aligns with the President’s Management Agenda.
The public can search the site for Veterans, find out which of the National Cemetery they are buried, and read summary details of their lives and service. Future capabilities will allow families, survivors, fellow Veterans, and others to add historical photos, view gravesite photographs, view gravesites on a map, get directions to a gravesite, and share memories on a deceased Veteran’s memorial page. Such capabilities will include provisions that allow NCA to manage the site in a manner that maintains the same level of decorum that customers experience in VA’s National Cemeteries.
As a digital, Cloud-based, and internet-enabled platform, VLM enhances the Veterans Legacy Program concept. It includes more than 4.5 million Veterans currently laid to rest in National Cemeteries. Most importantly, VLM allows the American public to share in NCA’s mission to “honor all Veterans in perpetuity.”

BINCA | Business Intelligence National Cemetery Administration | NCA has implemented a business intelligence system using an enterprise Tableau Server. Tableau is the platform for BINCA to achieve true self-service capabilities for NCA analytics. It creates visualizations to manage and understand data, provides a method to share data among users, and exposes patterns and trends in a secure environment. The NCA Leadership team uses the output of BINCA on their dashboard for decision-making purposes.

BOSS-E | Burial Operations Support System - Enterprise | BOSS-E is a system comprising 10 VA legacy sub-systems that will be part of a future decommissioning effort. The multi-year goal is to transition users from these legacy systems by leveraging MBMS, VA systems, and COTS solutions. VA will migrate the functionality of the following mission-critical IT systems into MBMS and then decommission these systems as part of BOSS-E:
Burial Operations Support System (BOSS)
Automated Monument Application System (AMAS)
Eligibility Office Automation System (EOAS)
Nationwide Gravesite Locator (NGL)
Presidential Memorial Certificate (WebPMC)
Daily Burial Schedule (DBS)
National Gravesite Locator (NGL)
National Cemetery Kiosk (KGL)
Gravesite Assessment Reporting (GAR) Management 
Memorials Administration Decision Support System (MADSS)

BOSS | Burial Operations Support System | BOSS automates all the manual, paper-intensive record keeping and information and forms processing associated with over 150,000 yearly interments from National and State Veterans, Arlington National Cemetery, post/military, Department of Army, and Department of Interior cemeteries. BOSS creates and maintains a complete historical record for each interment and is considered an NCA mission critical system.

AMAS | Automated Monument Application System | AMAS automates all business processes associated with monument ordering, delivering, and tracking. It provides for creating and maintaining a complete historical record for each monument application. AMAS receives, processes, and tracks over 335,000 applications each year for government-furnished monuments (i.e., headstones, markers, niche covers) for graves of Veterans and beneficiaries buried in National, State, Arlington National Cemetery, post/military, Department of Army, Department of Interior, and private cemeteries. AMAS is considered an NCA Mission critical system.

EOAS | Eligibility Office Automation System | EOAS provides case processing functionality, case tracking, productivity reporting, and tracking reports for pre-need request submissions for the Eligibility Office (EO). 

NGL | Nationwide Gravesite Locator | NGL is a system designed to assist the public with locating a gravesite for which a government marker was provided. The NGL receives a data feed from both BOSS and AMAS databases and is kept constantly up to date. NGL is considered an NCA mission critical system.

WebPMC | Presidential Memorial Certificates | A PMC is an engraved paper certificate bearing the signature of the current President. It honors the memory of Veterans who have been honorably discharged from the Armed Forces of the United States. The WebPMC application provides case processing functionality, case tracking, productivity reporting, and document tracking reports for the PMC program.

DBS | Daily Burial Schedule | DBS is an online application developed to improve customer service and public access to information about those interred at any of the 135 national, state, and tribal cemeteries. DBS provides burial schedule information up to a year from the day the user searches within the application. After the day of the interment, the information no longer appears in DBS; the decedent’s burial location will be updated in the Nationwide Gravesite Locator, which can also be found online. DBS information is updated hourly, so visitors are encouraged to check back close to the date and time of the service to ensure information did not change. 

KGL | National Cemetery Kiosk
 | Over 90 kiosks are installed in National Cemeteries. Kiosks provide cemetery visitors current gravesite information and a printed map so they may easily and quickly locate the gravesite of decedents at the cemetery. Kiosks also provide visitors with the most frequently sought information including floral regulations, cemetery hours of operation, upcoming events, military honors policy, burial eligibility requirements, historical cemetery information, and NCA rules and regulations. Kiosks receive a data feed from the BOSS system nightly to ensure visitors receive current decedent information. Kiosks are considered an NCA Mission critical system.

GAR | Gravesite Assessment Reporting (GAR) Management | The Gravesite Assessment Reporting (GAR) application operates/functions within the BOSS environment. The GAR application delivers the semi-annual and fiscal year Gravesite Assessment reports. The reports collect information about the cleanliness, height and alignment of headstones/markers at National Cemeteries. The assessment is based on a random sampling of gravesites inspected by cemetery staff in April and October each year.

MADSS | Memorials Administration Decision Support System (MADSS) | The NCA Management and Decision Support System (MADSS) is an electronic system of tracking cemetery workload and administrative data. MADSS was developed to improve the accuracy and consistency of data received from the national cemeteries. MADSS is a menu driven on-line data entry system. Cemetery personnel can enter current month or quarterly data and correct current month or quarterly data within the current fiscal year. The system also gives NCA Central Office, Memorial Service Network (MSN) and national cemetery staff the ability to generate and print reports.

Description of Requirements 
Statement of Work 
IMT Hydromet Modernization Software Support 
 
1.0 Background 
The contractor shall provide 99 hours of on-demand technical support over one base year and an 
additional 99 on-demand hours in one option year. 
2.0 Scope 
These support hours will be allocated for contractor services related to the OpenVMS toolset (vxrt), the 
Fortran migration tool (FPT), and integration efforts with designated OpenVMS applications. 
3.0 Objectives 
The applications supported under this modernization effort are mission-critical.  Timely access to 
contractor expertise may be required to resolve issues affecting system performance and reliability. 
4.0 Tasks 
• Investigate potential bugs or software issues. 
• Assist with real-time software debugging. 
• Update and modify code as needed to resolve identified issues. 
• Connect government-issued equipment to the VPN at least once every 30 days to ensure 
account information remains active and to receive required automatic updates. 
5.0 Delivery 
Support services will be provided on an annual basis.  Technical support will be available Monday 
through Friday during normal business hours.  The contactor shall provide an initial response within four 
hours of receiving a support request.  All support requests will be initiated by the Systems 
Administrator. 
Contact Information: 
Daren Critelli 
daren_Critelli@ios.doi.gov 
2021 4th Avenue North 
Billings, MT 59101 
 
6.0 Government-Furnished Property 
The government has provided two government-issued laptops under a previous modernization contract. 
7.0 Security 
Contractor personnel have completed background investigations and hold active PIV credentials valid 
through February 2031. 

8.0 Place of Performance 
All work will be performed at the contractor’s facility. 
9.0 Period of Performance 
The period of performance is one base year, from December 3, 2026, through December 2, 2027, and 
one option year, from December 3, 2027, through December 2, 2028. 
6/9/2026

ACWS Call for Solutions Official Questions and Responses from Industry Day, Post-Industry Day, and Final CFS SAM.gov Posting 
 
 
Page 1 of 7 
Questions Responses 
Will this presentation be made available to industry post-presentation? Yes 
The Call mentions the MVP architecture. Can you tell us more about the history of the MVP architecture, its 
characteristics, and your pain points? 
Current MVP architecture as mentioned, is on the Appian platform leveraging the CON-IT baseline as the starting 
point in mid-2023 and adding on selected unique Army capability over the past 3 years.  Along with developing 
Army unique capability, the program also leverages code-sharing with services and imported development done 
by the Air Force/Navy. 
Current pain points seen are how the platform works with respect to code-sharing.  Merging code-baseline is time-
consuming and can lead to issues where work must be redone or bugs introduced. Other pain points are AI 
limitations within the platform, as well as how to integrate it with enterprise AI modules seamlessly. 
What is the rationale for emphasizing industry low-code/no-code solutions if the end product will still be a custom 
solution? Is the expectation that the government will be able to modify and maintain the low-code/no-code 
components directly, or that vendors will develop reusable modular components that can be leveraged across future 
efforts to reduce cost and implementation time? More broadly, what specific advantage is low-code/no-code intended 
to provide over a conventionally developed custom industry solution? 
LC/NC is an Army CIO initiative preferred due to is speed and ease of development.  While the development 
currently a custom solution, the underlying platform is LC/NC and is open for integration with COTS solution either 
in the LC/NC platform or externally. Reusable module components are preferred as these are shared across the 
services; however, there is an expectation that the government will be able to modify and maintain the low-
code/no-code components directly as needed to meet requirements. 
Will IL5 and IL6 be hosted on different platforms? Yes, currently IL5 is hosted in DLA PIEE; whereas IL6 will be a separate instance hosted in cArmy.  As far as the 
underlying platform, Army prefers that the platforms/baseline be the same, only modified for IL6 restrictions. 
Is VCE on a different hosting platform than ACWS? If yes, is the vision to have them operate on the same hosting 
platform? 
Yes, VCE is currently hosted cArmy, while ACWS is hosted in DLA PIEE. The vision is to have both systems operate 
on the same hosting platform. 
Will the incoming contractor have to perform any PADDS file migration? The PADDS data migration is scheduled to be completed by 04NOV. No file migration tasks are expected from the 
contractor. 
Are the Epics in priority order? Generally, yes, but we have embraced Agile and we are open to re-prioritizing based on what makes most sense to 
include level of effort estimates. 
For the IL-6 requirement, must the offeror already possess an IL-6-authorized solution and the required facility and 
personnel clearances at proposal submission, or may the offeror propose a defined approach, schedule, and 
Government-supported path to achieve IL-6 authorization after award? 
Offeror may propose a defined approach, schedule, and Government-supported path to achieve IL-6 
authorization; however, it must align with the schedule outlined earlier by the government. It’s important to note 
that the Government may request personnel clearance validation at the time of award. 
Teams may require more than two pages for all the member certifications. Would the government be willing to increase 
the page limit (i.e. two pages per team member)? 
The government will take this request under consideration. 
Can you explain the contractor’s role in Tier-2 service desk? The contractor will not have a role in Tier-2 support. The Functional Sponsor has lead for Tier-2 support. 

ACWS Call for Solutions Official Questions and Responses from Industry Day, Post-Industry Day, and Final CFS SAM.gov Posting 
 
 
Page 2 of 7 
Questions Responses 
Will industry day participants be shared afterward to help facilitate teaming discussions. Yes, a list of vendor registration for Industry Day will be posted to SAM.gov 
Is it the Government’s intent to only award this to a single large systems integrator? The expectation to meet all 
requirements under one submission precludes engagement from specialized commercial firms that specialize in specific 
capabilities. 
The Government’s objective is that all requirements be met, either by a single vendor or by a team under a single 
submission. As stated in Section 5.2, the Army places no restrictions on how Primes/Teams are organized. 
Is this event recorded, and will the recording as well as the slides be available after the event? If so, where can we 
access the materials? 
Yes, this event is being recorded. The link to the recording, along with the presentation will be posted to SAM.gov. 
Will there be a right seat/left seat transition with the incumbent contractor? If so, how long? Yes, a 30-day transition period with the incumbent is planned-- if necessary. 
Given the hosting requirements, is SaaS not allowed? The Army is exploring the best way to resolve the technical debt from the current MVP architecture and deliver a 
modern LCNC solution. Per Section 7.1, we will evaluate the Technical Merit of all proposed solutions, whether 
they optimize the existing platform or propose a compelling alternative. 
Will the IL6 deployment be in the PIEE IL6 environment or will it be hosted in cARMY? The government currently anticipates that the IL6 ACWS environment will be hosted in cArmy enclave. 
Questions and answer 4 seems to imply that SaaS options are not being considered, can you validate this? SaaS offerings will be considered, provided they meet the capability requirement described throughout, including 
ability to be implemented at IL6.  Since SaaS offerings vary significantly in scope, the Government requests offerors 
to clearly state whether a SaaS offering meets all requested criteria today or if additional work is required to fully 
satisfy capability requested, and timeline and cost needed to complete this work. 
Expression has an operational phase III ready SBIR solution, sponsored by ASA(ALT) that is available today to meet this 
exact requirement. can we demo this for you? 
Government cannot accept any demo at this stage, but contractors may cite the SBIR solution and operational 
status in their proposal, and if elected government may request a technical demostration during Phase 2. 
Section 3 states ACWS currently holds an ATO for DLA PIEE hosting, and that solutions requiring a new ATO must supply 
a timeline and milestones. Given the Phase 1 due date of 25 August and anticipated award of 4 November, does the 
Government have a required date for initial operational capability that would constrain how much ATO risk it can 
accept? 
And relatedly, would a solution that remediates technical debt within the existing accredited platform be evaluated as 
equally responsive to Requirement 1’s modernization objective as a solution proposing migration to a different LCNC 
platform? 
The Government does not have a specific requried date for IOC capability that would drive ATO risk tolerance; 
instead, the Government requires that there must be no disruption of service to the existing operational 
environments currently supporting our Warfighters. Government is unwilling to accept the risk of an unaccredited 
system. 
A proposal that remediates technical debt within the existing accredited platform will be viewed as equally 
responsive to Requirement 1’s Modernization objective.  The Government is not intending to dictate the technical 
solution and is open to remaining on the existing platform if industry partners believe this is the most 
appropropriate course of action. 
For the “Service Desk Support: Tier 2 and 3,” is ACWS looking for these technical support offerings to be provided 
24x7x365, or a model supporting business days (Ex, during the workweek 0800-1700)? 
The contractor will not provide Tier 2 support. Tier 3 support is 8 hours for the Business Day with core hours 0800-
1700ET. Additional support may be required in the 4th quarter of each Fiscal Year, with peak in September.

ATTACHMENT A

Red Hat Professional Services

Ansible Automation Platform Integration

for: 

Abacus Visual Playbook Builder and Automation Orchestrator

Department of Veterans Affairs

Veterans Health Administration (VHA)

Veterans Integrated Service Network 23 (VISN 23)

Healthcare Technology Management / Biomedical Engineering

Document Purpose

This document serves as Attachment A to the Performance Work Statement (PWS) for the Abacus Visual Playbook Builder and Automation Orchestrator acquisition. It defines the scope and requirements for Red Hat Professional Services engagement.

This document covers the interconnected technical areas requiring Red Hat expertise:

VM Provisioning and VLAN Management — API-driven infrastructure automation across multiple Nutanix sites

Windows Certificate Authentication — Secure, scalable authentication for managing Windows hosts

Certificate Management Workflows — Git-based certificate lifecycle management with four (4) distinct workflows

Presigned URL Workflow — S3 asset retrieval for playbook execution without direct AWS credentials

Real-Time Job Output Streaming — WebSocket integration for live job status in external UI

AAP Infrastructure and Self-Management — Operational best practices for running AAP

Abacus: The Orchestration Application

Abacus is the external application that orchestrates all user interaction and workflow coordination. Understanding Abacus's role is essential context for the AAP integration design.

Abacus Responsibilities

User interface for all VM provisioning and configuration requests

Determines which AAP job templates to invoke based on user actions and site context

Specifies which playbooks to execute (via Git commit reference)

Manages S3 asset references and coordinates presigned URL workflow

Handles user authentication and authorization before calling AAP APIs

Displays real-time job execution output streamed from AAP

Retrieves workstation onboarding script from Git

AAP's Role

AAP serves as the automation backend — it does not provide user-facing interfaces for end users. All user interaction happens in Abacus; Abacus calls AAP APIs; AAP runs playbooks against target infrastructure.

VM Provisioning and VLAN Management

This section describes the requirements for automating Windows VM provisioning and network management across multiple Nutanix sites.

Multi-Site Architecture

The Government has eight (8) geographically distributed sites, each with its own Nutanix Prism Element cluster. A single AAP installation serves all sites with strict security boundaries between them.

Multi-Site Security Model

The primary security requirement is strict site isolation. Users at Site A shall not have access to, view, or modify resources at Site B — even through misconfiguration.

Implementation approach:

One (1) AAP Organization per site (e.g., Minneapolis, Omaha, Fargo)

Organization-scoped Nutanix credentials (each credential can only access its site's cluster)

AD group to AAP Team mapping for RBAC

Site-specific VLAN configuration files in Git (vars/sites/{site}_vlans.yml)

Physical Sites:

Fort Meade, Fargo, Sioux Falls, Saint Cloud, Minneapolis, Omaha, Iowa City, Central Iowa

Logical Site:

VISN23 (administrative; no dedicated cluster; staff can work across all physical sites)

Each physical site has its own Prism Element cluster and AD security groups. VISN23 staff are granted cross-site access via AD group membership.

VLAN/Network Configuration Support

VLAN and network configuration management requirements are specified in Category LV [LV1-LV22]. The implementation mechanism (Abacus-native functionality, AAP workflows, dedicated service, or equivalent) is at Contractor discretion.

Red Hat Scope for VLAN-Related Work:

Red Hat's involvement in VLAN management is limited to technical guidance and integration support if the Contractor selects an AAP-based implementation approach:

API-Driven VM Provisioning

VM creation is triggered by Abacus via AAP's REST API — not through AAP's self-service portal. Abacus specifies the site, and the appropriate job template is invoked.

API Design:

One (1) Job Template per site (eight (8) total): minneapolis-vm-create, omaha-vm-create, etc.

Abacus determines which endpoint to call based on user's site

Site identifier implicit in endpoint (not passed as parameter)

VM Creation Parameters:

VM Creation Workflow Steps

The VM creation workflow shall execute the following steps:

Load VLAN configuration from Git for the target site

Perform "subnet math" to determine which VLAN the IP address belongs to

Validate IP is within usable range (not gateway, broadcast, etc.)

Check for IP conflicts (query existing VMs in Nutanix)

Create VM in Nutanix using specified template

Configure disks and CD-ROMs

Configure Windows hostname and network settings (mechanism at Contractor discretion per [L25])

Power on VM

Onboard VM for Windows authentication (see Section 3.6)

Add host to AAP inventory based on site, project, and group

Return result to Abacus

Automated VM Onboarding

After a VM is created and powered on, it must be onboarded into the Windows certificate authentication system before it can be managed by Ansible. This onboarding is an extension of the VM creation workflow.

Workflow continuation after VM power-on:

Wait for VM to complete initial Windows setup (sysprep completion)

Execute onboarding configuration (either via sysprep or initial connection)

Validate WinRM connectivity using certificate authentication

Add host to AAP inventory with correct Organization, Inventory, environment group, and component group memberships

Tag host with appropriate metadata (creation date, template used, etc.)

DRY Architecture Requirement

All eight (8) sites shall use identical playbook code — a single Git repository with no per-site playbook copies. Site-specific differences shall be handled via:

Organization-scoped credentials

Job Template extra variables (site_name, nutanix_cluster)

Site-specific variable files in Git (vars/sites/{site}_vlans.yml)

Benefit: Update playbook logic once; all eight (8) sites automatically receive the update.

VM Template Registry (Admin-Only)

Infrastructure administrators need the ability to register new Windows VM templates so they become available for VM provisioning. This shall be restricted to admin AD groups only.

Windows Certificate Authentication

This section describes the certificate-based authentication design for managing Windows hosts with Ansible.

Problem Statement

The Government needs to manage a mixed environment of Windows machines where some are domain-joined and others exist in workgroups. Several critical constraints eliminate traditional authentication methods.

Why Traditional Methods Do Not Work:

Solution: Two-Certificate Architecture

The solution is a certificate-based authentication system where Ansible uses WinRM over HTTPS with client certificate authentication. This approach uses two (2) separate certificates with distinct purposes.

Certificate 1: Windows Host Server Certificate

Purpose: Encrypts the WinRM communication channel (like HTTPS for a website)

Location: Each Windows host generates its own self-signed certificate

Private key: Never leaves the Windows host; never shared with Ansible

Validation: Ansible ignores validation (ansible_winrm_server_cert_validation: ignore)

Certificate 2: Ansible Client Certificate

Purpose: Proves Ansible's identity; replaces username/password authentication

Location: Single CA-signed certificate from Venafi on Ansible controller

Private key: Stored on Ansible controller only

Public key: Distributed to all Windows hosts (Trusted People store)

Mapping: Windows hosts map this certificate to local ansible_admin user

Git Repository for Platform Configuration

All certificate materials, root CAs, and generated scripts are stored in a dedicated Git repository. This design provides several benefits:

No TLS trust dependency: Git access via SSH requires no TLS certificate validation

Version history: All changes are tracked with full audit trail

Single source of truth: One authoritative location for all certificate-related materials

Resilience: If S3 or other infrastructure becomes untrusted due to CA rotation, Git remains accessible

Certificate Management Workflows Overview

Certificate management is divided into four (4) distinct workflows, each with a specific purpose and scope:

Initial Host Onboarding Workflow

When adding a new Windows host to Ansible management, an administrator performs an initial RDP session to execute a PowerShell setup script. This is the "moment of physical presence" to establish trust relationships.

The onboarding script performs these steps:

Generate self-signed certificate and configure WinRM HTTPS listener on port 5986

Import the root CA certificate that signed the Ansible controller certificate into Trusted Root store

Read Ansible controller certificate thumbprint

Create local ansible_admin user account with strong random password (generated locally, never transmitted)

Create certificate mapping: "when this certificate is presented, authenticate as ansible_admin"

After onboarding, Ansible can connect using certificate authentication without passwords transmitted over the network.

Workflow 1: Certificate Preparation and Staging

This workflow extracts certificate materials from a Venafi export, stages them in Git, and generates the onboarding script. It is a "safe" operation that does not touch any Windows hosts.

Trigger:

Admin uploads venafi-export.pfx (or ZIP containing PFX) to controller-certificate/ folder in Git, then runs the job template with the decryption password.

Steps:

Pull latest from Git repository

Detect file format (PFX directly, or ZIP containing PEM files, etc.)

Decrypt/extract using provided password: Private key → Store in AAP credential storage; Public certificate → Write to controller-certificate/public-cert.pem; Thumbprint → Extract and write to controller-certificate/thumbprint.txt; Signing root CA → If not already in root-ca/ folder, add it

Render onboarding-workstation.ps1 from Jinja2 template, embedding the root CA, thumbprint, public certificate, and logic for local user creation and certificate mapping

Write rendered script to generated/onboarding-workstation.ps1

Commit and push all changes to Git

Job completes successfully

Workflow 2: Certificate Rotation to Existing Hosts

This workflow pushes the new certificate to all managed Windows hosts. It requires careful design for reliability and rollback safety.

Pre-Conditions:

Workflow 1 has completed — all materials staged in Git

The old certificate is still valid (running 45-60 days before expiration)

AAP currently authenticates to Windows hosts using the old certificate

Both old and new credentials are available to AAP

Safety Mechanism: Scheduled Task Rollback

Before changing anything on a host:

Create a Windows scheduled task that will restore the old certificate mapping

Task triggers either on system reboot OR after a timeout (e.g., 10-15 minutes)

Then make the change:

Apply new certificate mapping (new thumbprint → ansible_admin)

Validate immediately:

Attempt to connect using the NEW certificate

Based on result:

Success: Delete the scheduled task (disarm the rollback), mark host as rotated

Failure: Leave scheduled task in place, mark host as failed — the host will auto-recover when the task fires or on next reboot

Workflow 3: Root CA Distribution to Windows Hosts

This workflow pushes all root CA certificates from the Git repository to all managed Windows hosts. It is idempotent — Windows handles "already present" gracefully.

Purpose:

Ensure Windows hosts trust all internal root CAs. This is needed for presigned URL downloads from Nutanix Objects S3 endpoint and any other internal HTTPS services Windows hosts may need to access.

Trigger:

Admin runs job template after adding new CA to root-ca/ folder in Git.

Steps:

Pull latest from Git repository

Read all .crt files from root-ca/ folder

For each managed Windows host: Push all CA certificates to Trusted Root Certification Authorities store (Windows handles idempotency natively)

Track per-host status: success, failed, unreachable

Persist state so re-runs can target only incomplete hosts

Report summary

Workflow 4: Execution Environment CA Trust Update

This workflow updates the AAP Execution Environment's CA trust store without requiring a container image rebuild.

Purpose:

Ensure the Execution Environment trusts all internal root CAs. This is required for amazon.aws.aws_s3 collection connecting to Nutanix Objects (presigned URL generation) and any other collections/modules that connect to internal TLS endpoints.

Desired Outcome:

Pull latest from Git repository

Read all .crt files from root-ca/ folder

Transform to format required by EE (Red Hat to recommend appropriate format)

Update the EE's CA trust source via the recommended mechanism

Result: Collections use system CA trust, which now includes new CAs — without rebuilding the EE image

Administrator Certificate Renewal Workflow

The annual certificate renewal should be as simple as possible for the administrator.

Desired admin experience:

Admin requests new certificate from Venafi portal, downloads the export (typically a ZIP containing an encrypted PFX)

Admin uploads the raw Venafi export (unmodified) to the Git repository (controller-certificate/ folder) via the Git web interface

Admin triggers Workflow 1 through AAP

Admin provides the PFX decryption password when prompted (this password shall be treated as sensitive data and not persisted after the workflow completes)

Admin reviews the generated onboarding script and staged materials

Admin triggers Workflow 2 to rotate existing hosts

If a new root CA was added, admin triggers Workflow 3 and Workflow 4 (or these may be automatically chained)

Key requirement:

The administrator should not need access to Linux command-line tools, OpenSSL, or manual file manipulation. The goal is that an administrator can complete annual certificate renewal by performing two (2) primary actions: uploading a file and providing a password.

CA Certificate Updates

When a new internal root CA is issued (for example, when the certificate authority used to sign the Nutanix Objects TLS certificate rotates), the administrator commits the new CA certificate file to root-ca/ in the Git repository.

Required propagation:

Workflow 3: Push new CA to all existing managed Windows workstations

Workflow 4: Update Execution Environment CA trust via ConfigMap/Secret

Workflow 1 (if re-run): Regenerate onboarding script (though new hosts only need the controller certificate's signing CA)

Question: Site access forms. We have the SECNAV 5512/1 from the solicitation 
attachments. Please conﬁrm the submission deadline and the correct recipients. Because 
the completed form is CUI and contains Privacy Act information, please also advise 
whether you prefer encrypted email, a DoD SAFE drop, or another method rather than 
standard email.  
Answer:  You can send encrypted or through DoD Safe drop, whichever is convenient, to 
Romaine Davenport & Emily Maguire. See Section L of solicitation for contact info. 
Question: Sponsor veriﬁcation. Please conﬁrm the process for sending sponsor 
veriﬁcation to NAS Oceana Pass and ID, and who we should follow up with to verify it has 
been received. We plan to obtain passes on 10 August, the day prior.  
Answer: Submission and veriﬁcation of 5512 and Visitor Access Letter to Romaine 
Davenport & Emily Maguire.  
Question: Roof access. The requirement includes rooftop donor antennas and weather-
rated mounting. To quote accurately we need to see the roof during the survey. Please 
conﬁrm whether roof access can be arranged, who will escort, and whether fall protection, 
speciﬁc PPE, or a lift will be required or provided.  
Answer: Roof access will be arranged. Escort will be provided at time of check-in. No PPE 
necessary. No lift required.  
Question: Photographs and site documentation. We understand photographs, drawings, 
and retained site details require prior written approval. We are requesting approval to take 
photographs and measurements of the existing repeater equipment, antenna locations, 
cable pathways, and roof conditions, solely for the purpose of preparing our quotation.   
Answer: Photographs can be taken, provided that at the conclusion of the site visit, all 
pictures will be reviewed and veriﬁed to ensure no sensitive information has been 
captured. The 2210/2 form (attached) will also need to be completed. 
Question: Test equipment. We intend to bring RF signal measurement equipment to take 
pre-installation readings. Please advise whether this needs to be declared in advance or is 
subject to any restriction.  
Answer: 2210/4 form PED (attached) submission & approval required prior to visit; 
veriﬁcation of device day of check-in. 
Question: Vehicle access. Our personnel will arrive in a company-owned vehicle.   
Answer: Vehicle registration, proof of insurance, and driver’s license is required when you 
report to Pass & ID for Access Pass. 

Question: Can you provide a drawing of these 2 buildings for design purposes and to create 
a BOM? 
Answer: Drawings are not being provided but vendors will have the opportunity to see the 
area on the site survey day to assist with pricing. See Section L of the solicitation for details. 
Question: Floor Plans: Are ﬂoor plans for Buildings 522 and 523 available? If so, could they 
be provided to prospective offerors? 
Answer: No ﬂoor plans are being provided but vendors will have the opportunity to see the 
area on the site survey day to assist with pricing. See Section L of the solicitation for details. 
Question: Site Visit and RF Site Survey: Will prospective offerors be permitted to visit the 
site to inspect the existing repeater systems and conduct an RF site survey before 
submitting quotations? If so, please provide the registration process and any site-access 
requirements. 
Answer: No ﬂoor plans are being provided but vendors will have the opportunity to see the 
area on the site survey day to assist with pricing. Site visit instructions are included in the 
solicitation section L.

␟26-SIMACQ-E30-0034_Cell_Phone_Repeater_Questions_Answers_V2_8072026.pdf␞

Building Information: What are the approximate square footage and number of ﬂoors for 
each building? 
Answer: Bldg. 522 – 2 Floors, approx. 12,200 SF each, 24,400 SF total Bldg. 523 – 1 Floor, 
approx. 12,100 SF 
 
Existing Repeater Systems: Can the Government provide any available information 
regarding the existing repeater systems, including the equipment currently installed, 
system conﬁguration, and any available documentation? 
Answer: Bldg. 522 uses a NODE A; Bldgs. 523 uses SureCall Force5  
 
Site Visit and RF Site Survey: Will prospective oƯerors be permitted to visit the site to 
inspect the existing repeater systems and conduct an RF site survey before submitting 
quotations? If so, please provide the registration process and any site-access 
requirements. 
Answer: Site visit instructions are already included in the solicitation section L. 
 
Coverage and Acceptance Requirements: Beyond the post-installation functional test 
described in the Statement of Work, are there speciﬁc coverage or performance 
requirements that the completed system must meet? If so, please identify the required 
commercial cellular carriers and any applicable signal-strength, coverage, testing, or 
acceptance criteria. 
Answer: AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile and support all other carrier services. Require suƯicient 
signal to provide consistent and reliable voice and data service. 
 
How many ﬂoors are in each building? 
Answer: See answer to question 9. 
 
What are the building types and primary construction materials that may aƯect cellular 
signal propagation? 
Answer: Cinder block construction 

Which areas within Buildings 522 and 523 are required to receive cellular coverage? 
Answer: Complete coverage in all spaces. 
 
Are there any speciﬁc acceptance criteria or RF coverage performance requirements that 
the completed system must meet? 
Answer: Require suƯicient 4G/5G signal to provide consistent and reliable voice and data 
service for the following Cellular carriers.  AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile and support all other 
carrier services.  
 
Is Cyber Maturity Model Certiﬁcation (CMMC) required?   
Answer: Yes.  See Section M of the Solicitation for details.

B.2  GOVERNING LAW CLAUSE

Federal law and regulations, including the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR), shall govern this Contract/Order. Commercial license agreements may be made a part of this Contract/Order but only if both parties expressly make them an addendum hereto. If the commercial license agreement is not made an addendum, it shall not apply, govern, be a part of or have any effect whatsoever on the Contract/Order; this includes, but is not limited to, any agreement embedded in the computer software (clickwrap), any agreement that is otherwise delivered with or provided to the Government with the commercial computer software or documentation (shrinkwrap), or any other license agreement otherwise referred to in any document. If a commercial license agreement is made an addendum, only those provisions addressing data rights regarding the Government’s use, duplication and disclosure of data (e.g., restricted computer software) are included and made a part of this Contract/Order, and only to the extent that those provisions are not duplicative or inconsistent with Federal law, Federal regulation, the incorporated FAR clauses and the provisions of this Contract/Order; those provisions in the commercial license agreement that do not address data rights regarding the Government’s use, duplication and disclosure of data shall not be included or made a part of the Contract/Order. In the event of conflict between this clause and any provision in the Contract/Order or the commercial license agreement or elsewhere, the terms of this clause shall prevail. The Contractor shall deliver to the Government all data first produced under this Contract/Order with unlimited rights as defined by FAR 52.227-14, this includes any custom code developed for the purpose of performing under this contract. Claims of patent or copyright infringement brought against the Government as a party shall be defended by the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) in accordance with 28 U.S.C. § 516; at the discretion of DOJ, the Contractor may be allowed reasonable participation in the defense of the litigation. Any additional changes to the Contract/Order must be made by modification (Standard Form 30) and shall only be made by a warranted Contracting Officer. Nothing in this Contract/Order or any commercial license agreement shall be construed as a waiver of sovereign immunity.

Any resulting contract will be awarded on a firm-fixed-price basis as defined by Federal Acquisition Regulation Subpart 16.202. B.4    PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Orlando VA Health Care System (OVAHCS), has a requirement to provide a 10ft height by 6ft wide Transparent Digital LED Film display. The Transparent LED Film will assess suitability, performance, visibility, and operational impact of transparent LED display technology for the veteran’s creative arts festival, informational messaging, digital signage and patient engagement use cases at the OVAHCS. Exploring innovative digital display technologies to enhance communication with patients, visitors, and staff. Transparent LED displays offer high-brightness digital content while maintaining line-of-sight visibility, making them suitable for healthcare environments where openness and aesthetics are critical. This effort will include installation of transparent digital LED film, power, and data. This shall provide a turnkey Transparent Digital LED Film display solution, including hardware, any electrical/data installation needed, delivery, and technical specifications as outlined below at location determined by OVAHCS point of contact (POC).

C. STATEMENT OF WORK 
C.1 OVERVIEW 
 
The National Library Service for the Blind and Print-Disabled (NLS), Library of Congress (Library), is 
seeking a contractor to provide RealSAM Dialog Licenses and technical-support services for legacy 
RealSAM Dialog Licenses.  Each license (legacy or new) shall include the cost of services needed to 
operate and maintain NLS’s My Talking Books (an Amazon Alexa skill) in production. 
 
My Talking Books is an Amazon Alexa skill that enables NLS patrons to search the NLS collection, browse 
the NLS collection, retrieve/manage the patron’s Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) Wishlist, 
stream NLS talking books, and manage the patron’s Bookshelf using a voice-only interface available on 
Alexa-enabled commercial smart-speaker platforms. 
 
The Contractor shall be responsible for providing RealSAM Dialog licenses and services required to 
operate the system in production, while meeting all IT information-system security requirements as 
required by the Library of Congress.  
 
C.2 BACKGROUND 
 
NLS administers a free program that loans audio and braille books and magazines, music scores in braille 
and large print, and specially designed audio-playback and refreshable-braille-display equipment to 
residents of the United States who are unable to read or use standard print materials due to visual or 
physical impairment. 
 
NLS administers the program nationally, while direct service to eligible individuals and institutions is the 
responsibility of cooperating network libraries in the various states, the District of Columbia, Puerto 
Rico, Guam, and the U. S. Virgin Islands.  This service is also extended to eligible American citizens 
residing abroad. 
 
C.3 SCOPE 
 
The contractor shall provide the Library with RealSAM Dialog licenses and services needed to operate 
and maintain NLS’s My Talking Books (an Amazon Alexa skill) in production.  My Talking Books is an 
Alexa skill that enables NLS patrons with Alexa-enabled smart-speaker devices to use a voice-only user 
interface to search the NLS Catalog, manage their Wishlist, access BARD Lists, and stream audio content 
from NLS’s Talking Book Collection.  
 
C.4 REQUIREMENTS 
 
The contractor shall provide the following: 
 
C.4.1 RealSAM Dialog License – New Licenses (including operational support) 
 
The contractor shall provide the Library with RealSAM Dialog License blocks for purchase at a firm-fixed 
price on an annual basis.  The license fee shall cover all services provided by the vendor to enable the 
use of the My Talking Books skill in production by a licensed user.  These licenses are required for the 
Library to add additional new users to the My Talking Books skill. 

 
 
C.4.2 RealSAM Dialog License – Legacy License Support (existing 5,000 Perpetual User Licenses) 
 
The contractor shall provide the Library with legacy RealSAM Dialog license support services at a firm-
fixed price on an annual basis.  This support service shall ensure that users with legacy RealSAM Dialog 
licenses can use the My Talking Books skill in production. 
 
C.4.3 License Cost Models 
 
The Contractor shall provide the Library with a pricing chart (Attachment J3 - Pricing Chart.xlsx) for C.4.1 
and C.4.2 based on the following scenarios: 
 
A. Smart Speaker’s Auth Proxy service is hosted by the Library. 
B. Smart Speaker’s Auth Proxy and Streaming Server services are hosted by the Library. 
C. Smart Speaker’s Auth Proxy, Streaming Server, and Dialog Engine (Binary Blob) services are hosted 
by the Library. 
D. Vendor hosts all required non-GFE services to support Smart Speaker (My Taking Books skill) in 
production.  Reference Attachment J2 - My Talking Books (RealSAM) Components.docx for Library 
managed and vendor managed components of the system. 
 
C.4.4 Technical Support 
 
A. With each RealSAM Dialog Licence (new and legacy), the contractor shall provide technical-support 
service to assist with answering technical questions and providing end-user support to resolve My 
Talking Books issues.  Performance metrics for the delivery of technical-support service shall be in 
compliance with Attachment J1 - SLA for My Talking Books (RealSAM).xlsx 
B. The contractor’s technical-support resources are required to have a deep knowledge of My Talking 
Books and its infrastructure to sufficiently provide this service. 
C. The contractor shall make a good-faith effort to resolve technical-support requests within 72 
business hours of submission.  If a support request cannot be resolved within 72 hours, the 
contractor shall provide a written explanation to the COR as to the reason for the delay and provide 
an estimated completion date for when the issue is expected to be resolved. 
D. The contractor shall provide a written monthly Technical Support Status Report to the COR detailing 
technical support requests, actions taken, and their current status. 
 
C.4.5 Post-Award Conference 
 
A. Relevant Library and contractor personnel shall hold a kick-off meeting/post-award conference to 
review and clarify the project’s objectives, expectations from the Government, and address any 
questions the contractor may have.  The contractor shall provide and collaborate with the COR on 
an agenda for this meeting.  Discussion topics shall include, but not be limited to, the following: (1) 
introduction of the contractor and Government Staff; (2) understanding of the specific tasks and 
subtasks; (3) project-management expectations; (4) agreement on meeting schedules; and (5) 
agreement on initial delivery dates. 
B. The kick-off meeting/post-award conference shall occur within 10 business days from contract 
award and will be scheduled by the contracting officer. This conference may be held virtually. 
 
C.4.6 Status Reports 

 
 
The contractor shall provide monthly status reports on the progress made in fulfilling technical-support 
requests and other contract deliverables.  The format shall be determined by the COR. 
 
C.4.7 Status Meeting 
 
The contractor shall be responsible for keeping the COR informed about contractor progress throughout 
this contract’s POP and ensuring that the contractor’s activities are aligned with the Library's objectives.  
At a minimum, the contractor shall review the status and results of contractor performance with the 
COR monthly via Library-approved digital conferencing means (e.g., MS Teams). The contractor shall be 
available for discussion regarding any potential problems within two (2) business days of request. 
 
C.5 CONTRACT PERFORMANCE  
 
C.5.1  Contract Administration 
Specific requirements and delivery schedules will be identified in each Task Order. The contractor shall

As a Legislative Branch agency, the Library of Congress (Library) is subject to the competition and advertising requirements of 41 
U.S.C. § 6101. Like the Competition in Contracting Act and the FAR, 41 U.S.C. § 6101 does not require competition when a 
contracting officer certifies that only one source or brand-name item is available, when dictated by public exigency, or when otherwise 
authorized by law.  
 
This document sets forth the justification and approval for award of a contract or order by means providing for other-than-full-and-
open competition, per 41 U.S.C. § 6101, LCR 7-210, and, as applicable, FAR 6.302, FAR 13.106-1, FAR 8.405, and FAR 16.505. 
Contracting without competition shall not be justified on the basis of a lack of advance planning or concerns related to availability of 
funds.

(a) Definition. "Customs territory of the United States" means the States, the District of Columbia, and Puerto

3   V12 APR 2026 
 
(c) Except as provided in paragraph (d) of this clause or elsewhere in this contract, the following procedures 
apply to supplies not identified in the Schedule to be accorded duty-free entry: 
 
(1) The Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer in writing of any purchase of foreign supplies 
(including, without limitation, raw materials, components, and intermediate assemblies) in excess of 
$20,000 that are to be imported into the customs territory of the United States for delivery to the 
Government under this contract, either as end products or for incorporation into end products. The 
Contractor shall furnish the notice to the Contracting Officer at least 20 calendar days before the 
importation. The notice shall identify the- 
 
(i) Foreign supplies; 
(ii) Estimated amount of duty; and 
(iii) Country of origin. 
 
(2) The Contracting Officer will determine whether any of these supplies should be accorded duty-free 
entry and will notify the Contractor within 10 calendar days after receipt of the Contractor’s notification. 
 
(3) Except as otherwise approved by the Contracting Officer, the contract price shall be reduced by (or 
the allowable cost shall not include) the amount of duty that would be payable if the supplies were not 
entered duty-free. 
 
(d) The Contractor is not required to provide the notification under paragraph (c) of this clause for purchases of 
foreign supplies if- 
 
(1) The supplies are identical in nature to items purchased by the Contractor or any subcontractor in 
connection with its commercial business; and 
 
(2) Segregation of these supplies to ensure use only on Government contracts containing duty-free entry 
provisions is not economical or feasible. 
 
(e) The Contractor shall claim duty-free entry only for supplies to be delivered to the Government under this 
contract, either as end products or incorporated into end products, and shall pay duty on supplies, or any portion 
of them, other than scrap, salvage, or competitive sale authorized by the Contracting Officer, diverted to 
nongovernmental use. 
 
(f) The Government will execute any required duty-free entry certificates for supplies to be accorded duty-free 
entry and will assist the Contractor in obtaining duty-free entry for these supplies. 
 
(g) Shipping documents for supplies to be accorded duty-free entry shall consign the shipments to the 
contracting agency in care of the Contractor and shall include the- 
 
(1) Delivery address of the Contractor (or contracting agency, if appropriate); 
 
(2) Government prime contract number; 
 
(3) Identification of carrier;

shipping weight); and 
 
(6) Estimated value in United States dollars. 
 
(h) The Contractor shall instruct the foreign supplier to- 
 
(1) Consign the shipment as specified in paragraph (g) of this clause; 
 
(2) Mark all packages with the words "UNITED STATES GOVERNMENT" and the title of the

Request for Information 
Version 2.0 
 
Introduction 
 
This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for the purpose of conducting market 
research. Accordingly, this RFI constitutes neither a Request for Proposal (RFP) nor a 
guarantee that one will be issued by the Government in the future. Furthermore, it does 
not commit the Government to contract for any services described herein. Do not submit 
a Proposal. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is not, at this time, seeking 
proposals or quotes, and therefore, will not accept, review, or evaluate unsolicited 
proposals or quotes received in response hereto. This notice is not to be construed as a 
commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor does the 
Government intend to pay for any information submitted as a result of this request. The 
Government does not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with submission 
of the information being requested or, reimburse expenses incurred for responses to 
this RFI. The information provided may be used by VA in developing its acquisition 
strategy and Product Description/Performance Work Statement. Any information 
submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary; however, any information 
received shall become the property of the Government and will not be returned to the 
respondent. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, 
restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response. This is a 
request for information and does not obligate the Government in any way, nor does it 
commit the Government to any specific course of action. 
 
Background/Scope: 
 
In 2017, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Office of the Chief Technology Officer 
(OCTO) partnered with VA Central Office and all three VA Administrations to identify a 
vision statement for enhancing VA’s digital presence for Veterans. That vision is known 
as the Digital Modernization Vision and is supported by a group of VA executives known 
as the Digital Modernization Council. This council is chaired by the CTO. 
 
VA Digital Modernization Vision defined in July 2017: 
 
VA will deliver self-service tools on par with top private sector companies and will 
have the best online experience in the Federal Government. Every digital service 
will be customized to the individual using it. Interacting with VA digital services 
will feel like navigating TurboTax, not filling out a form. 
 
The work directly supports benefits claims and data intake on Veteran-facing digital 
platforms. The overarching goals of this work are: 
 
1. Reduce the average time to completion of benefits claims 
2. Increase customer satisfaction 
3. Increase the quality and reliability of VA services 

VA's Benefits Portfolio encompasses a complex ecosystem of digital products that serve 
Veterans, Caregivers, Service members, their dependents, and survivors throughout the 
entirety of their benefits lifecycle—from initial application, through claim status tracking, 
to decision review and ongoing benefits management. While VA has made significant 
progress in digitizing these experiences, VA seeks to make substantial improvements in 
three areas: (1) forms updates and usability improvements, (2) benefits data intake and 
automation, and (3) document services (real-time data validation and third-party 
routing). The work encompassed in this requirement covers existing products and 
potential new modernization initiatives. 
 
NO MARKETING MATERIALS ARE ALLOWED AS PART OF THIS RFI.  See 
attached DRAFT PWS and Addendum for specific requirements. 
 
SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS 
 
Vendor Responses: 
 
Please provide the following information by 3:00 PM Eastern Time on August 10, 
2026 via email to Contract Specialist (CS) James Morgan, at james.morgan10@va.gov 
and Contracting Officer (CO) John Fields, at john.fields3@va.gov. Please note “RFI 
36C10B26Q0708 in the subject line of your response. Mark your response as 
“Proprietary Information” if the information is considered business sensitive. VA 
reserves the right to respond to any, all, or no respondents. All VA current requirements 
identified herein are subject to change at any time. If you have any questions 
concerning this announcement, please contact the CS and CO. VA appreciates your 
time and anticipated response.  
 
Please provide the following in your response:  
 
• Vendor name and POC information  
• SAM Unique Entity ID 
• Business size standard under NAICS Code **541519 (Large, Small, SDVOSB, 
WOSB, etc.) **NOTE: If you don’t think the assigned NAICS code is appropriate 
for this requirement, please provide your suggested NAICS code and rationale 
for using it.  
• List any federal contracts in which you are a prime contract holder and this effort 
is within scope of (e.g. GSA, NASA, SEWP, etc.)  
• Provide your suggestion for the best contract vehicle for this effort.  
 
In addition, please provide the following information, limited to 10 pages: 
 
 
1. Draft PWS Sufficiency. Has the draft PWS provided sufficient detail to describe 
the technical requirements that are detailed in the PWS.  If “NO”, please provide 
your technical comments/recommendations on elements of the draft PWS that 

may contribute to a more accurate proposal submission and efficient, cost 
effective effort. 
 
2. Firm Fixed Pricing and Payment Milestones. Work under this contract is 
priced as firm-fixed-price (FFP) for outcomes or deliverables tied, as much as 
practicable, to meeting the performance expectations and objectives defined in 
the PWS, rather than priced by iteration. The Contractor proposes a schedule of 
payment milestones to break the outcomes or deliverables into incremental 
payments. How would you recommend structuring payment milestones per 
period of performance? What basis for those milestones (for example, time-
based, performance-based, deliverable-based, or a combination) would best 
balance predictable cash flow for the Contractor with meaningful accountability 
for the Government? Please see PWS Addendum A and B for draft milestones 
for the Base Period. 
 
3. Optional Task Milestone Pricing. Optional tasks are priced on a firm-fixed-price 
lot basis, with milestone plans and pricing proposed by the Contractor and 
negotiated with the Government at the time of task activation rather than at 
contract award. For optional tasks, how would you recommend structuring 
milestones and milestone payments to fairly balance risk between the 
Government and the Contractor? What information would you need from the 
Government at the time of task activation to develop accurate milestone pricing 
efficiently? 
 
4. SLO Penalty Structure. Given the scope of the PWS, how might a payment 
reduction mechanism be used to ensure accountability to service-level objectives 
under a FFP for outcomes, milestone-payment structure? What kind of payment 
reduction schedule might be applied when the Contractor fails to meet defined 
SLOs (examples such as service reachability, availability, and added latency), 
assessed against milestone payments. What feedback do you have on this 
approach? Would you recommend an alternative mechanism for ensuring 
accountability to service-level objectives under a lot-based, milestone-payment 
structure? 
 
5. AI and Team Efficiency. What assumptions about AI-driven productivity should 
the Government consider when evaluating staffing plans and pricing for this 
effort? How is your organization currently using AI tools in software delivery and 
what measurable effect has this had on team output or composition? How would 
you recommend the Government distinguish between proposals reflecting 
genuine AI-enabled efficiency and proposals that understate the staffing required 
to operate a system of this scale and criticality? 
 
6. Evaluation Approach. The Government intends to evaluate this using a coding 
challenge. What feedback do you have on the use of a coding challenge as an 
evaluation method for this type of effort? Are there other show-me-don’t-tell-me 
approaches the Government should consider for this procurement? 

 
7. Human-Centered Design. Describe one project where user research changed 
the direction of a digital service — specifically, what did you plan to build, what 
did you learn from users that changed it, and what did you build instead? Include 
the research method used and roughly how many participants. 
 
8. Human-Centered Design. Describe a time your research or usability findings 
conflicted with what the government program office wanted to build. What did you 
do? 
 
9. Human-Centered Design. How do you recruit research participants to ensure 
you're capturing people with low digital literacy, limited English proficiency, or 
disabilities and how has that changed a design decision? How do you approach 
user research with people who use disabilities differently from studies that don't 
include this audience? 
 
10. Human-Centered Design. Who conducts your user research (in-house 
researchers vs. designers doing double duty vs. subcontracted), and how many 
research hours were budgeted on your two most recent projects of similar size to 
this one? 
 
11. Human-Centered Design. Describe your company's relevant experience and 
qualifications in designing digital products or services for complex, non-linear 
user journeys (e.g., helping users track status through a multi-step process). 
Include a link or screenshot of a research artifact (e.g., a journey map, service 
blueprint, findings report, or usability test summary) from a completed project that 
demonstrates this experience, redacted as needed for confidentiality. 
 
12. Understanding Users. Describe your general approach to improving user 
understanding and transparency in a complex, multi-stage process such as 
claims or benefits status tracking. 
 
13. Stakeholder Management. Describe your general approach to stakeholder 
management when balancing new development with maintenance and 
improvement of existing products. 
 
14. Web Applications and Architectural Patterns. Describe your firm's experience 
designing, developing, deploying, and sustaining modern web applications using 
technologies and architectural patterns relevant to the VA.gov platform. Include 
experience with Ruby on Rails, React, JavaScript/TypeScript, RESTful APIs, VA 
Design System (VADS), Kafka or other event-driven architectures, AWS, CI/CD, 
automated testing, and observability. Also describe experience integrating with 
enterprise platform services, implementing reusable platform capabilities, 
working with structured data, and developing scalable, high-volume public-facing 
applications. Provide illustrative examples. 
 

15. Team. Describe your general approach to staffing and team composition for a 
project of this nature, including how you typically incorporate research and 
design functions alongside engineering delivery. 
 
16. Additional Questions and Considerations. Please share any additional 
feedback, questions, risks, or recommendations regarding the draft PWS, the 
proposed contract structure, or the acquisition approach that would help the 
Government refine its requirements and strategy prior to solicitation.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
Part 1: General Information 
1.1 Overview & Background 
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Learning Center requires an enterprise-wide, 
modernized, and secure cloud-based Learning Management System (LMS) to deliver, track, 
manage, and report on training. The USACE Learning Center currently utilizes Microsoft Teams 
(MS Teams) for course collaboration and an antiquated, internally developed database known 
as the Training Management Information System (TMIS) to track registrations and completions. 
This fragmented environment is obsolete and requires severe manual administrative 
workarounds. 
This Performance Work Statement (PWS) outlines the requirements for deploying, configuring, 
and supporting a commercially available, cloud-based Cornerstone Learning Management 
Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) subscription (specifically utilizing the Cornerstone Learn 
application module). This modernization effort will consolidate USACE’s training tracking and 
records into a single, integrated, and secure FedRAMP Moderate Authorized cloud environment 
for approximately 36,000 active military and civilian users worldwide. 
1.2 Scope of Work 
The Contractor shall provide all commercial software licensing, cloud hosting, data migration 
from TMIS, implementation, system configuration, functional training, and helpdesk support 
services necessary to deliver a turnkey, fully operational FedRAMP Moderate LMS SaaS 
solution. 
1.3 Period of Performance (PoP) 
The Period of Performance shall consist of a twelve (12) month Base Period and four (4) 
consecutive twelve (12) month Option Periods: 
Performance Period Start Date End Date 
Base Period 1 October 2026 30 September 2027 
Option Period 1 (Year 2) 1 October 2027 30 September 2028 
Option Period 2 (Year 3) 1 October 2028 30 September 2029 
Option Period 3 (Year 4) 1 October 2029 30 September 2030 
Option Period 4 (Year 5) 1 October 2030 30 September 2031 
 
 1.4 Place of Performance & Hours of Operation 
The primary place of performance shall be at the Contractor’s facility (remote support). Any 
required coordination meetings or administrative enablement sessions will be conducted 
virtually. Operational support hours shall be 0800 to 1700 EST, Monday through Friday, 
excluding federal holidays. 
1.5 Level of Effort 

2 
 
In accordance with standard federal commercial acquisition guidelines, the level of effort is 
considered inherent to the Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) of the COTS SaaS subscriptions and 
associated services required to meet the performance standards outlined in this PWS. No 
specific labor hours are mandated to complete the core configurations. 
1.6 Quality Control & Quality Assurance 
1.6.1 Quality Control Plan (QCP): The Contractor shall develop, implement, and maintain a 
comprehensive Quality Control Plan (QCP) to ensure all services, software provisioning, and 
database migrations conform to the requirements of this contract. The QCP shall be submitted 
to the COR for review within thirty (30) days of contract award. The plan shall detail the 
Contractor's internal self-inspection procedures, database verification tools for the TMIS 
migration, and reporting methods for system uptime. 
1.6.2 Government Quality Assurance: The Government will monitor the Contractor’s 
performance under this contract utilizing a Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP). The 
COR will perform random inspections of helpdesk ticket logs, review monthly hosting uptime 
reports, and verify migrated TMIS records to ensure the Contractor is maintaining the 
Acceptable Quality Levels (AQLs) defined in the Performance Requirements Summary (PRS).

Part 4: Contractor Furnished Items and Services 
Except for those items specifically identified in Part 3, the Contractor shall furnish everything 
required to perform this contract, including: 
• Fully authorized Cornerstone Learning Management SaaS subscriptions compliant with 
FedRAMP Moderate security standards. 
• Secure commercial hosting infrastructure. 
• Data migration utility engines and data mapping templates. 
• Preferred Customer Success Package (PCSP) and Tier 1 Helpdesk services. 
Part 5: Specific Tasks & Technical Requirements 
The Contractor shall execute the following core technical tasks: 
Task 5.1: Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) Subscriptions & Scalability 
SaaS Subscriptions: The Contractor shall provision and maintain one (1) production instance 
and one (1) sandbox/testing instance of the Cornerstone Learning Management SaaS 
application, authorized at a FedRAMP Moderate baseline. 
Subscription Scale: The SaaS subscription model must support the enterprise-wide footprint of 
approximately 36,000 active civilian, military, and external user accounts. 
Platform Scalability: The Contractor shall provide a standard, pre-priced mechanism that allows 
the Government to procure additional user licenses or add-on software modules (e.g., additional 
compliance connectors) at any point during the period of performance via a bilateral contract 
modification. 
Task 5.2: System Configuration & SSO Integration 
Single Sign-On (SSO): The Contractor shall integrate standard DoD Common Access Card 
(CAC) and Personal Identity Verification (PIV) multi-factor authentication via SAML 2.0 to ensure 
secure user authentication and automated user provisioning. 
Role Configuration: Configure user roles, administrative permissions, reporting groups, and 
custom dashboards matching the organizational workflows of the USACE Learning Center. 
Task 5.3: Legacy Data Migration (TMIS to SaaS) 
Migration Plan: The Contractor shall draft a comprehensive Master Data Migration Plan detailing 
the database mapping, cleansing, and verification strategies to transition records out of TMIS. 

4 
 
Data Transfer: Execute the secure extraction, mapping, cleansing, and ingestion of historical 
training records, active course curricula, and completion histories from the legacy TMIS 
database into the new Cornerstone SaaS application, ensuring 100% record accuracy and zero 
data loss. 
Task 5.4: Course Design & Instructional Design Templates 
Instructional Design Templates: To accelerate training delivery, the Contractor shall design and 
deliver three (3) custom, reusable "Ready-Made Course Templates" within the LMS. These 
templates must be Section 508 compliant and configured to support rapid, standardized course 
authoring by USACE curriculum creators. 
Task 5.5: Training and Technical Support Services 
Functional Training: Conduct virtual, instructor-led system administration training for designated 
USACE training managers, covering database management, course uploading, and custom 
reporting. 
eSkillz Tier 1 Helpdesk Integration: The Contractor shall provide a 24/7/365 end-user helpdesk 
support service (utilizing the integrated eSkillz helpdesk package) to resolve login issues, 
password resets, and user navigation questions. This is a new service being introduced to 
USACE under this contract to support user onboarding and platform adoption. 
Consulting Services: Provide 1,040 hours of pre-purchased consulting support per year. These 
hours shall be utilized for routine system tuning, specialized reporting layouts, custom API 
connections, and ad hoc administrative support. Unused hours do not carry over to subsequent 
option periods and expire at the end of each performance period. 
Part 6: Security & Cybersecurity Requirements 
6.1 FedRAMP Moderate Compliance 
The Contractor shall maintain a valid FedRAMP Moderate baseline authorization for the 
Cornerstone Learning Management SaaS application throughout the entire contract 
performance period. 
6.2 Data Safeguarding & Privacy 
The Contractor shall handle all user records and PII in accordance with the Privacy Act of 
1974, DFARS 252.204-7012 (Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident 
Reporting), and DFARS 252.239-7010 (Cloud Computing Services). No Controlled Unclassified 
Information (CUI) will be processed or stored on this platform. 
6.3 Contractor Qualifications 
The Contractor shall be the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), licensor, or an authorized 
sole-source reseller holding all proprietary data and configuration rights, capable of 
guaranteeing software compliance throughout the contract lifecycle.
