Request for Information (RFI) 
 
Joint Targeting Toolbox (JTT) Capabilities Package (CP) 
Continued Sustainment 
 
THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. This notice is for information and 
planning purposes only. In accordance with Part 10 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation, the 
Government is conducting market research to determine the availability and adequacy of 
potential business sources in developing the software identified below that meets the 
Government's requirements. While industry sources are requested to provide full and 
comprehensive responses to this request, they are reminded that all information is voluntary. 
This Request for Information (RFI) does not constitute a solicitation for bids or proposals, and it 
is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government. The information herein is subject to 
change and in no way binds the Government to solicit for or award a competitive contract. No 
award will be made under this Request for Information (RFI). Proprietary information will be 
accepted, safeguarded, and handled appropriately. Responders should indicate which portions 
of their responses are proprietary and should mark them accordingly. The Government shall not 
be liable for damages related to proprietary information that is not properly identified. 
The Government reserves the right to cancel this RFI before the closing date. Respondents are 
advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs 
incurred in response to this RFI; all costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at 
the interested party’s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any 
future solicitation, if any is issued. The Air Force reserves the right to use any non-proprietary 
technical information in any resultant solicitation(s). Any submissions in response to this RFI 
constitute consent for that submission to be reviewed by Government personnel, Federally 
Funded Research and Development Center (FFRDC) Contractor employees, and Advisory & 
Assistance Services (A&AS) Contractor employees supporting Joint Targeting Toolbox (JTT) 
program and/or AFLCMC/C3C (Kessel Run) --unless the respondent clearly objects in writing to 
the release of this information to FFRDC and/or A&AS Contractor employee supporting 
AFLCMC/C3C in a cover letter accompanying the respondent's submission. All Government and 
Department of War (DoW) contractor personnel reviewing RFI responses understand their 
responsibility for proper use and protection from unauthorized disclosure of proprietary 
information. 
This RFI is from the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Kessel Run Division 
(C3C), located at 11 Barksdale Street, Hanscom AFB, MA 01731. 

2 of 8 
 
1. Program Background: 
Joint Targeting Toolbox (JTT) is an Air Combat Command (ACC)-sponsored software 
capability which provides standardized, secure, automated decision support for joint and allied 
commanders worldwide. The system is deployed at Command and Control (C2) nodes at the 
national, force, and component elements in support of decision-makers and will include targeting 
capabilities compatible within the force/theater-level common operating environments (plan, 
execute, and assess). 
JTT supports joint/coalition combat operations which include integrated air, ground, naval, and 
cyber targeting functions throughout the joint targeting cycle to include objectives, target 
development, capabilities analysis, force assignment, force execution and assessment working 
seamlessly between multiple security domains. JTT gives the targeting community the ability to 
be interoperable and collaborative across the joint enterprise. JTT allows end-to-end target 
planning, via host/core service and joint C2 systems, by targeteers and target specialists at all 
planning levels and nodes. 
The JTT PMO is seeking information on how interested parties could provide sustainment 
services for the JTT software application. The contractor may perform the work at its facility, 
remotely, and/or locally within the Hanscom AFB, MA and/or Langley AFB, VA area, as well as 
remote and in-person training and helpdesk support at locations both CONUS and OCONUS. 
The contractor must have the knowledge, processes, and tools required to sustain and maintain 
separate deployable software baselines, using agile software methodologies. JTT-CP utilizes 
Jakarta Enterprise Beans (formerly Enterprise JavaBeans) and both SOAP and REST API’s that 
require a unique software coding skillset. The contractor must also have the facilities available to 
host UNCLASSIFIED, Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), SECRET, and TOP SECRET 
classified information with 24/7 on-demand access within a virtualized environment. The 
contractor must be able to provide a helpdesk to support user engagement. Additionally, 
contractor personnel must have the ability to travel within austere environments to provide 
support to fielded systems. 
• Planned Start Date: 20 June 2027 
• Delivery Period: Two years (One-year base period, one six-month option period, and one six-
month Extension of Services period) 
• Limitations: All employees involved in the project must be U.S. Citizens and access to the 
project, tools, repositories, and data must be controlled in a way that would prevent any non-
citizens from accessing. 
• Security Requirements: All key personnel must be able to obtain Top Secret clearance and 
SCI eligible. 
• Total Estimated Contract Value: $5 - $10M 
 

3 of 8 
 
2. Program Objective: 
The JTT Program Management Office (PMO) is currently sustaining the legacy system (JTT-CP 
5.x) codebase until it is replaced and sunset. The next acquisition seeks to continue sustainment 
of JTT-CP with the following potential objectives: 
Enterprise Scalability 
• Ability to deploy to various security domains and networks (NIPRNet, SIPRNet, AFSCI (Air 
Force Sensitive Compartmentalized Information) Network, DoD Agency, Joint Services, & 
Coalition Interoperability 
• Cross-domain solutions 
• Denied, degraded, intermittent, and limited (DDIL) environment support 
Integration/Interoperability 
• Integration and automation with legacy and modernized applications within Air Force Air 
Operations Centers (AOCs) 
• Integration with other enterprise targeting applications 
• Integration with legacy and modernized enterprise intelligence databases 
Fielding/Training 
• Support cloud/on-premises installation and deployment of JTT within U.S. Armed Forces, 
U.S. Intelligence Community (IC), Coalition, and Allied partner locations 
• Remote-based and in-person administrator and user training at Contiguous United States 
(CONUS) and Outside Contiguous United States (OCONUS) locations 
Operations Support 
• Bug fixes 
• Cybersecurity patches 
• Minor improvements 
Helpdesk/Exercise Support 
• Ability to support on call, up to 24/7/365 when necessary 
• CONUS/OCONUS in-person exercise support 
New Capability Development 
1) Minimal, as required by Government to maintain fielded system 
 
 

4 of 8 
 
3. Market Research Approach: 
Through responses provided to this RFI and subsequent Market Research engagements, the 
Government intends to obtain the following: 
• Industry’s input and suggestions on refining requirements and technical approach 
• Recommendations on the Government’s acquisition and contracting approach 
• Information on industry’s capabilities to meet the JTT requirement 
Respondents to this RFI may be invited to participate in further market research activities, 
including Virtual One-on-One activities and Question-and-Answer sessions. 
Note to Respondents: The JTT PMO is an agile organization, and we welcome and encourage 
innovative inputs. 
 
4. Instructions for RFI Responses: 
Interested parties are requested to respond to this RFI with a white paper. 
Responses to this RFI are to be submitted in the stated format either by e-mail to the Contracting 
Officer, Ms. Annie Kazi at annie.kazi@us.af.mil and Contract Specialist, Ms. Diamont Daniel-
Malsch at diamont.daniel-malsch@us.af.mil or through the DoD Secure Access File Exchange 
(SAFE) website (https://safe.apps.mil/) to the same email addresses no later than (NLT) 
5:00pm EDT on 07 September 2026. Marketing materials are not requested nor desired. 
Please note that the government is still determining the acquisition strategy and best path 
forward. Therefore, this RFI is solely for market research and market intelligence. Do not 
include information such as rates within your RFI response. Responses shall be 12-point font 
typed with at least 1” margins. Each page of your package shall be legible when printed on 8 ½” 
x 11” paper. Please include a cover page, although title pages, glossaries and tables of contents 
are not required. Responses should be provided in Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF) 
format. The government anticipates responses to be between 3-5 pages, excluding a cover 
page. Responses should provide feedback/answers to Government’s questions in this RFI. 
Submissions that do not at least directly address the questions in this RFI may be 
considered nonresponsive. 
Responses shall include the following information on the cover page: 
• Company/Institute Name 
• Address

• A list of any Governmentwide Acquisition Contract (GWAC) contract vehicle(s) (i.e. GSA

Please answer the following questions for Industry: 
1. Provide your recommendations for acquisition strategies, source selection/down select

3. What software development methodologies and tools does your organization use for large 
development projects and to manage technical debt? Provide recent and relevant successful 
use cases. 
4. What are your current processes and methodologies for integrating with targeting software 
applications and databases (i.e. Modernized Integrated Database (MIDB), Machine-Assisted 
Analytic Rapid-Repository System (MARS)? Please provide recent and successful use cases. 
5. What is your current experience and proficiency level with Jakarta Enterprise Beans 
(formerly Enterprise JavaBeans) and Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP) Application 
Programming Interfaces (APIs)? 
6. How has your organization successfully maintained schedule and release cadences while 
addressing emerging needs? 
7. What strategies does your organization employ to transition cloud-based complex software 
development projects from an incumbent to one under your management? Identify any 
dependencies and risks. 

6 of 8 
 
8. Provide recent and relevant examples and identify risks (What experience does your 
organization have in supporting Foreign Military Sales (FMS)? Reference contract number: 
FA873022C044PX000. 
9. Please indicate if your company would be interested in participating in further market 
research activities, including Virtual One-on-One activities and Question-and-Answer

10. What questions does your company have for the Government? 
Confidentiality: Respondents may only provide unclassified RFI responses. Respondents must

5. Questions: 
Questions regarding this announcement shall be submitted in writing by e-mail to the

This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products and commercial services as prepared in accordance with the format in Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 12.212(b)(1), as supplemented in the attached Request for Quotation (RFQ). This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. A firm-fixed price purchase order is anticipated.  RFO 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services will be used. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. 

The solicitation number is 36C26026Q0852 and is attached.

This solicitation is set aside for small businesses. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. 

The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 541511, with a small business size standard of $34 Million. 

VA Puget Sound Healthcare System is seeking to purchase software maintenance and support services for MyPath tools.

Offerors are required to provide an authorization letter or other documents from OEM (Nitid Bit, LLC) at the time of offer to provide maintenance and support services for existing, proprietary equipment/system. All software licensing, warranty and service associated with the equipment/system shall be in accordance with the OEM terms and conditions.

Service Location: 

VA Puget Sound Healthcare System

1660 South Columbian Way

Seattle, WA 98108-1532

Any questions or concerns regarding this solicitation should be forwarded in writing via email to Jennifer Robles jennifer.robles1@va.gov no later than 08/03/2026. Telephone inquiries will not be responded to. No late quotations will be accepted.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

See Attached

Request for Information 

Revenue Operations Workflow, Payer Compliance and Technical Consulting

VA-26-00042471

Introduction

This Request for Information (RFI) is for planning purposes only and shall not be considered an Invitation for Bid, Request for Task Execution Plan, Request for Quotation or a Request for Proposal.  Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services described in this RFI.  Your response to this RFI will be treated only as information for the Government to consider.  You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this RFI.  This request does not constitute a solicitation for proposals or the authority to enter into negotiations to award a contract.  No funds have been authorized, appropriated or received for this effort.  Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response.  The Government does not intend to pay for the information submitted in response to this RFI.

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 541512 with a size standard of $34 million.  

2. Submittal Information:

All responsible sources may submit a response in accordance with the below information.  

There is a page limitation for this RFI of 15 pages. The Government will not review any other information or attachments included, that are in excess of the 15-page limit. NO MARKETING MATERIALS ARE ALLOWED AS PART OF THIS RFI.  Generic capability statements will not be accepted or reviewed.  Your response must address capabilities specific to the services required in the attached PWS and must include the following:

Interested Vendors shall at a minimum, provide the following information in the initial paragraph of the submission:

Name of Company

Address

Point of Contact

Phone Number

Fax Number

Email address

Company Business Size and Status

For VOSB and SDVOSBs, proof of SBA certification. SDVOSB/VOSB vendors that have not been certified by SBA should not respond to this notice.	

NAICS code(s)

Socioeconomic data

Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Number

Existing Contractual Vehicles (GWAC, FSS, or MAC)

Provide a summary of your ability to meet the requirements contained within the draft PWS for the following areas:

Provide a summary of your technical capability to meet PWS paragraphs 5.2- Revenue Operations Workflow Functionality and Cloud Computing, 5.3- Claims Scoring, Reporting, and Payment Efficacy, and 5.4- Managerial and Technical Support.  Your response shall include all software tools that will be leveraged in order to fulfill the PWS requirements.

If you were to submit a proposal, would your company be the sole provider of the complete scope of services, or is your company planning to provide any of the services sought in partnership with other entities? If it will be in partnership with another entity (or entities), identify the scope of services that will be provided by subcontractors or partners, the names of anticipated partners and the percentage(s) of the service(s) that will be provided by each of the subcontractor(s) or partner(s).Provide an overview of your company including primary services that you provide, size of the company, year established etc. 

Describe your relevant experience in providing a similar scope of services to Government agencies or commercial organizations of similar scope, size and complexity to the VA. Include the agency name, project type, scope, length, and contract number (if applicable). Your response shall address the following areas:

Describe any past or present cloud migration and implementation activities your company has managed or supported across a business enterprise. Please explain in detail the services provided in a cloud-based environment to include sustainment services for a customer base similar in size to Revenue Operations and its seven CPACs.

Please explain your experience executing revenue centric workflow management services. Workflow that generates items that are both automated and set for manual review and subsequently distributed to staff throughout a large enterprise. 

Please provide your past or present approach to providing robotic process automation services that support automation assistance to approved work processes that reduced manual staff intervention to increase business process efficiencies.

Please provide your past or present experience in providing claims scoring, reporting and payment efficacy for a large healthcare entity.

Provide your experience with building, updating and maintaining compliant modeling of insurance carrier agreements comparing actual reimbursement to expected payments while quantifying payment variances based on reimbursement methodology.

Please provide your approach to past or present enterprise-wide operational process and staffing improvement support for a large organization in support of tactical and strategic goals/metrics.

Provide your companies experience supporting a national level program in the following:

Developing, optimizing, maintaining  and assisting in the delivery of operational training and policy development, refinement.

Electronic HealthCare Record Management (EHRM) industry best practice requirements development, implementation and “go live” readiness.

Change management support on large scale initiatives and operational activities.

HIPAA / X12, NCPDP EDI subject matter expertise in a Healthcare Revenue cycle environment.

The development of executive level operations reports and business case products on both a regular and as needed (ad hoc) basis. These briefings often require a comparison of private sector Revenue Operations’ best practices, business standards or metrics.  These executive level documents and briefings may be extended to VA under-secretary, Legislative and Office of the Inspector General (IG) personnel.

For SDVOSB/VOSB vendors: Your company’s intent and ability to meet the set aside requirement in accordance with VAAR 852.219-73 (JAN 2023) (DEVIATION) VA Notice of Total Set-Aside For Certified SDVOSBs and 13 CFR §125.6, which states the contractor will not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the government to the prime for contract performance to firms that are not certified SDVOSBs listed in the SBA certification database (excluding direct costs to the extent they are not the principal purpose of the acquisition and the SDVOSB/VOSB does not provide the service, such as airline travel, cloud computing services, or mass media purchases). When a contract includes both services and supplies, the 50 percent limitation shall apply only to the service portion of the contract. 

Your response shall include information as to available personnel and financial resources; full names of proposed team members and the PWS requirements planned to be subcontracted to them, which must include the prime planned percentage or the names of the potential team members that may be used to fulfill the set aside requirement. 

Has the draft PWS provided sufficient detail to describe the technical requirements that encompass the software development and production operations support services to be performed under this effort. 

______ YES ______ NO (if No, answer question f)

If “NO”, please provide your technical comments/recommendations on elements of the draft PWS that may contribute to a more accurate proposal submission and efficient, cost effective effort.

 

Responses are due no later than 10:00am EST on February 27, 2026 via email to Gary Throckmorton, Contract Specialist at Gary.Throckmorton@va.gov and Christopher Minetti, Contracting Officer at Christopher.Minetti@va.gov.  Please note “RFI - Revenue Operations Workflow, Payer Compliance and Technical Consulting” in the subject line of your response.  Mark your response as “Proprietary Information” if the information is considered business sensitive.  The email file size shall not exceed 5 MB.

BACKGROUND

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), is one of the world’s largest health care delivery organizations. The Revenue Operations (RO) team is seeking ongoing healthcare revenue industry modeled best practice management consulting services and healthcare revenue operations business information technology tools to sustain, transform and continuously improve revenue cycle activities within the Office of Finance (OF). Revenue Operations (RO) and the seven (7) regionally aligned Consolidated Patient Account Centers (CPACs) support a vast healthcare enterprise in the service of our Nation’s Veterans. The goal of RO is to support the field in the management of the revenue cycle. As part of that effort, RO provides a variety of program services including the following: payer relations, metric-based quality / policy operational analyses, rate development, eBusiness EDI solutions and best practice modeling with a focus on process standardization to enhance revenues.

The Consolidated Patient Account Center (CPAC) uses standardized methods, tools, and processes to improve efficiency, effectiveness, and accountability in revenue operations. CPAC’s state-of-the-art business processes ensure that VA collects revenue from private health insurance carriers for nonservice-connected care provided to insured Veterans. These funds go back to the VA Medical Centers (VAMCs) to provide health care services to our Veterans. There are seven regional CPACs located around the country that provide revenue cycle management to all the  Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISNs) and their associated VAMCs. CPACs perform back-end revenue cycle processes while the VAMCs maintain ownership of key Veteran-facing revenue functions.


Transformation from the VA current state legacy system to the Oracle Health Electronic Health Record (OH EHRM) and its related health and revenue information technology tools is a critical endeavor for Revenue Operations. The RO team requires support to maintain and improve its best practice private sector revenue cycle performance while it transforms, as necessary, to the Oracle Health revenue technology tools. During preparation, deployment and stabilization of OH EHRM, RO seeks to continue its utilization of healthcare revenue business best practices and healthcare revenue business tools which provide work drivers to track and prioritize key revenue cycle activities, provide improved revenue collection services that focus on integral cash generation, improved payer management, standardization of processes, training and development of staff, along with extensive use of metrics and analytics to measure and validate performance.

These efforts are in response to Public Law 110-387, Section 406, which requires Revenue Operations and the CPACs to carry out the following functions: (1) Reengineer and integrate all business processes of the revenue cycle of the Department; (2) Standardize and coordinate all activities of the Department related to the revenue cycle for all health care services furnished to Veterans for nonservice-connected medical conditions; (3) Apply commercial industry standards for measures of access, timeliness, and performance metrics with respect to revenue enhancement of the Department; and (4) Apply other requirements with respect to such revenue cycle improvement as the Secretary may specify.  In meeting these goals, VA VHA strives to provide high quality, effective, and efficient Information Technology (IT) services to those responsible for providing care to the Veterans at the point-of-care as well as throughout all the points of the Veterans’ health care in an effective, timely and compassionate manner.  VA depends on Information Management/Information Technology (IM/IT) systems to meet mission goals.

The NAVSUP Fleet Logistics Center Norfolk, Contracting Department, Philadelphia Office is seeking information from interested sources capable of providing performance-based services to Navy Medical Readiness Logistics Command (NMRLC) Cheatham Annex (CAX) in Williamsburg, VA.  NMRLC requires contractor support to transition the prototype Warehouse Management System into a secure, operational cloud-native system. This effort is focused on the NMRLC-designated warehouses at Cheatham Annex (CAX), Williamsburg, Virginia.  The current requirement is being performed by Vana Solutions LLC under Firm, Fixed Price (FFP) type GSA task order 47QFCA23F0034.  The instant requirement will have a 12-month period of performance with no option periods.

Please see the attached draft Performance Work Statement which details the types of tasks that the contractor will be required to perform under this contract.

It is anticipated that this requirement, if solicited, will be under NAICS code 541512, with a size standard of $34M (millions of dollars), and Product/Service Code (PSC) DA10.

At this time the Government intends to negotiate a single source award to KPMG LLP.

It is requested that interested parties respond to this posting via email to helen.m.tyson.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 2:00 PM Philadelphia, PA time on Friday, 07 August 2026. Description of your recent, in the last 3 years, experience with Pre-Existing development experience RPA Script Libraries & Machine Learning Models: Respondents must possess a developer knowledgebase of pre-built RPA scripts designed to push records and synchronize data directly from Microsoft D365 into the Defense Medical Logistics Standard Support (DMLSS) system, and experience developing mature machine learning models that have been explicitly trained on Navy Medicine Readiness and Logistics Command (NMRLC) receipt and supply documentation.

If you are a large business, describe your approach to small business subcontracting. Performance Work Statement 
Naval Medical Readiness Logistics Command (NMRLC) Cheatham Annex (CAX) Warehouse 
Modernization 
 
1. Background 
 
The Naval Medical Readiness Logistics Command (NMRLC) is a vital command within the 
Bureau of Medicine and Surgery (BUMED) enterprise. NMRLC’s mission is to develop, acquire, 
produce, field, sustain, and provide enduring lifecycle support of medical materiel solutions to 
the Fleet, Fleet Marine Force, and Joint Forces in high-end competition, crisis, and combat. To 
achieve its mission, NMRLC must utilize modernized, agile, and secure systems to manage and 
distribute medical equipment, combat-support kits, and pharmaceutical inventories across both 
domestic and overseas locations. 
 
A prototype Warehouse Management System (WMS) at Cheatham Annex (CAX) in 
Williamsburg, V A, incorporating Radio Frequency Identification (RFID), Robotic Process 
Automation (RPA), and Optical Character Recognition (OCR) systems has been designed and 
deployed which successfully proved the feasibility of digitalized warehousing operations. The 
prototype is built on Microsoft D365, which serves as the core Warehouse Management 
Application (WMA) and integrates RPA, RFID, and OCR functionalities into a single, cloud-
native solution. 
 
While the initial prototype, a robust, secure, and highly scalable follow-on modernization, 
enhancement, and sustainment program is required. This follow-on effort is critical to NMRLC’s 
mission success. Consequently, this contract will not fund any new discovery, requirements 
gathering, or initial design work. 
 
2. Scope 
 
NMRLC requires contractor support to modernize, enhance, and sustain the NMRLC WMS. This 
WMS will support total asset visibility and improve financial audit readiness standards. The 
Contractor shall transition the prototype WMS into a secure, operational cloud-native system. 
This effort is focused on the NMRLC-designated warehouses at Cheatham Annex (CAX), 
Williamsburg, Virginia. 
 
The Contractor must use the existing prototype, source code, and design documents as the 
starting point for this project. This contract will not fund any "from-scratch" discovery, user 
requirements gathering, or initial design work. All activities must focus on validating the existing 
system, identifying what is needed to move it to the new network, and making technical 
improvements. The software code, database structures, interface specifications, and architectural 
diagrams developed for the prototype will be provided as Government-Furnished Information 
(GFI). 
 
Key activities within this scope include: 
• Agile Program and Delivery Management: Implement iterative project, risk, and program 
management methodologies for software delivery and reporting. 

• System Modernization and Enhancement: Update, upgrade, and secure existing WMS 
configurations through major and minor software releases to resolve bugs and deploy user-
valued functional improvements. 
• Warehouse Operations Improvement: Improve operations at Cheatham Annex (CAX) by 
optimizing system workflows and integrating mobile, automated data capture, and process 
automation technologies (RFID, OCR, and RPA). 
• Comprehensive Sustainment: Manage WMS hardware, software, licenses, and cloud 
infrastructure to minimize operational downtime. 
• Cybersecurity and ATO Certification: Resolve outstanding security conditions to transition 
the system from an Authority to Operate with Conditions (ATO-C) to a full ATO on the DHA 
Medical Community of Interest (MedCOI). 
• Documentation and Training: Develop and maintain system documentation, user manuals, 
and training materials for end-users and administrators. 
 
3. Tasks 
 
Throughout performance of this requirement, the Contractor shall manage the system updates, 
maintenance, and operational transformation of the CAX warehousing environment. 
 
3.1. System Baseline Validation & Planning.  The contractor shall 
3.1.1. Conduct a Delta Assessment of the existing WMS prototype architecture, infrastructure, 
data health, and security posture for migration to the DHA MedCOI network and submit 
a System Baseline Validation & Execution Plan within 14 days of contract award. 
3.1.2. Participate in recurring status reviews with NMRLC stakeholders to report on technical 
progress, system metrics, schedule alignment, and risk mitigation. The Contractor shall 
develop and submit a Monthly Status Report (MSR) by the 10th of each month. 
3.1.3. Utilize a modern software delivery methodology that ensures rapid, transparent, and 
continuous delivery of value. The Contractor shall facilitate regular alignment sessions 
and reviews with the NMRLC Product Owner to ensure full transparency regarding 
project capacity, delivery velocity, and backlog prioritization. 
3.1.4. Maintain a Project Management Plan (PMP) with an Integrated Master Schedule (IMS) 
and a dedicated Risk Management Plan. 
 
3.2. System Design Refinement & Security Planning.   
 
The Contractor shall provide software engineering, data integration, and cybersecurity services 
that ensure the WMS remains a highly available, secure, and fully integrated cloud-native 
solution.  The contractor shall: 
 
3.2.1. Develop a System Design Refinement and Target Operating Model by ingesting, 
validating, and updating the existing GFI design artifacts to reflect the final cloud-native 
target environment (DoDAF v2.0 compliant). 
3.2.2. Manage and mature an enterprise data strategy within the approved cloud environment 
(Azure). 
3.2.3. Deploy software enhancements and bug fixes without degrading existing system stability 
or core functionalities. Ensure the WMS environments remain secure, stable, and current 

with the latest updates via continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD). 
Provide a tiered triage of operational Help Desk to effectively resolve CAX user issues. 
3.2.4. Maintain real-time ledger accuracy within the WMS to fully support the APSR through 
periodic physical inventory cycle audits, ensuring that the WMS, RPA script 
configuration, or system data quality does not restrict, delay, or hinder audit, physical 
materiel handling, warehousing, or storage operations. 
3.2.5. Proactively and rapidly manage, apply and remediate the system’s security posture, 
verified via ACAS vulnerability scanning reports.  
  
GOVERNMENT REVIEW & CRITICAL PAUSES: The Contractor’s delivery schedules and 
performance metrics regarding ATO achievement shall account for standard Government review 
periods. In the event of a “critical pause” or delay caused exclusively by external Government 
actions or dependencies, the Contractor shall formally notify the Contracting Officer’s 
Representative (COR) and Information System Security Manager (ISSM) in writing. Time 
elapsed during these formal periods will result in a “stop-the-clock” status. 
 
3.3. System Modernization, Hardware Staging & BOM 
3.3.1. Provide end-to-end sustainment and lifecycle management for all WMS system 
components (Cloud Architecture & Software Management, Hardware Lifecycle & 
Service Contracts, Bill of Materials). 
 
3.4. Validation, Training, & UAT Preparation 
3.4.1. Maintain and update System User Manuals (SUMs), Quick Reference Guides (QRGs), 
and desk guides, and provide on-site and virtual training sessions. 
 
3.5. Final Deployment, ATO, & Transition-Out 
3.5.1. Ensure system readiness by facilitating comprehensive User Acceptance Testing (UAT) 
with local stakeholders. 
3.5.2. Execute the on-site system roll-out and provide dedicated, on-site “hyper-care” support 
until the facility achieves the Acceptable Quality Level (AQL) of zero (0) severity-1 
defects. 
3.5.3. Successfully transition the system from its current ATO-C to a full ATO. Resolve existing 
ATO-C conditions to achieve full ATO on MedCOI, and maintain RMF compliance. 
3.5.4. Detailed execution plan ensuring zero operational degradation during vendor turnover

1 | Pa ge  Autonomous Coding & Appeals and Denials Management - Request for Solution 
 
Request for Solution (RFS) 
For 
Autonomous Coding and Automated Appeals & 
Denials Management 
 
1. OVERVIEW & AUTHORITY 
The Defense Healthcare Management Systems Modernization (DHMSM) Program Management 
Office (PMO) intends to award one or more prototype Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) 
under 10 U.S.C. § 4022. This competitive process is being conducted as a Request for Solution 
(RFS). 
Under this RFS, the DHMSM PMO is seeking innovative solutions for two distinct capability 
offerings: 
• Capability 1: Autonomous Coding (AC) 
• Capability 2: Automated Appeals & Denials Management (ADM) 
These are presented as separate and distinct capability offerings to allow industry partners to 
propose targeted, highly specialized solutions for either individual capability or both combined. 
2. BACKGROUND 
The DHMSM PMO is responsible for leading the effort to modernize healthcare delivery across 
the military health system (MHS). The DHMSM PMO’s core mission is to deliver an integrated, 
interoperable health information technology solution that enables the MHS to provide high-
quality, cost-effective care to service members, veterans, and their families. This is achieved 
through the deployment and management of a comprehensive EHR, and associated technologies 
designed to improve patient care, enhance operational efficiency, and support data-driven 
decision-making throughout the MHS enterprise.  
The DHMSM PMO awarded a contract to Leidos in 2015 for the development and deployment of 
the Department of War electronic health record (DoW EHR). To that end, Leidos teamed with 
Oracle and other commercial vendors to create MHS GENESIS. Today, the DoW EHR is an 
Oracle Cerner Millennium product that supports the availability of longitudinal health records for 
more than 9.6 million DoW beneficiaries and has been deployed to over 137 parent hospitals and 
clinics with a user base of more than 190,000 Defense Health Agency (DHA) personnel. 
3. PROBLEM STATEMENT(S) 
The Government seeks primarily non-rules-based, AI/ML-enabled solutions that adapt and 
improve dynamically based on data patterns, addressing the two interrelated problem areas below. 
Additional information regarding each Capability can be found in the attached Statement of 
Objectives (SOO). 

2 | Pa ge  Autonomous Coding & Appeals and Denials Management - Request for Solution 
 
Capability 1: Autonomous Coding (AC) 
The Government seeks an autonomous coding capability that uses modern, human-like (AI/ML) 
computational processes to assign medical billing codes (ICD-10, CPT, HCPCS) from clinical 
documentation without human intervention, with full auditability and explainability. Traditional 
coding relies on human coders and is time-consuming, error-prone, and vulnerable to workforce 
shortages. The Government seeks measurable improvements in operational efficiency, coding 
accuracy, and cost-effectiveness across outpatient, inpatient, and ancillary environments, and 
measurable reductions in Discharged-Not-Final-Coded (DNFC) volume and Accounts Receivable 
(A/R) days. 
Capability 2: Automated Appeals & Denial Management (ADM) 
The Government maintains significantly backlogged aged A/R across multiple systems, creating 
risk to accurate GAAP-compliant financial reporting and limiting timely recovery of funds denied 
by Other Health Insurance (OHI) / third-party payers. Existing manual appeals and denials 
processes are labor-intensive and unable to resolve multi-year aged receivables at scale. The 
Government requires a phased, automated solution that improves first-pass claim success, 
accelerates documentation release, and enhances appeals and denials management to increase 
recoupment and reduce aged A/R.
 The solution shall not autonomously write off, adjust, or 
otherwise financially dispose of any claim; all financial dispositions shall require human 
approval; and every automated action shall carry a complete, FFMIA-aligned audit trail. 
 
4. CALL FOR WHITE PAPER SUBMISSIONS 
Interested companies may submit White Paper(s) to address either the AC capability, the ADM 
capability, or both (AC & ADM). Companies proposing both capabilities must submit two 
separate white papers, one per capability. All white paper submissions must follow the below 
guidelines. 
4.1. General Submission Guidelines (Applies to ALL submissions) 
• Submission Format: Unnecessarily elaborate brochures or proposals are not desired. Do 
not include resumes for any personnel. All submissions shall be unclassified. 
• Page Limits & Structure: White paper submission should not exceed ten (10) written 
pages for each Capability. If you are submitting for both capabilities, you must submit 
two separate and distinct white papers (up to 10 pages each). Combined submissions 
in a single file will not be accepted. The cover page, the Bill of Materials (BOM), and 
any addenda identified in this RFS do not count against the ten-page limit. Submissions 
shall be provided in PDF format and named using the convention {Company Name} 
{Capability}White Paper. 
• Specificity & Evidence: Be specific in the description of the proposed solution and, 
where specific software or the approach has been successfully leveraged, provide real-
world examples. Diagrams or figures to depict the proposed solution are encouraged and 
companies may provide links to public websites with such information. 

3 | Pa ge  Autonomous Coding & Appeals and Denials Management - Request for Solution 
 
• Cover Page: Create a cover page that identifies the capabilities being proposed against, 
the solicitation number, the name(s) of the company(ies), website(s), point(s) of contact, 
and contact information (email address, phone number and mailing address). 
• Non-Traditional Contractor: Identify whether each company listed on the cover page is 
a non-traditional defense contractor as defined in 10 U.S.C. 3014 or a non-profit research 
institution. (In short, a non-traditional defense contractor is an entity that has not received 
a full Cost Accounting Standards covered contract from the Federal Government within a 
12-month period prior to the issuance of this solicitation.) This information should not 
take more than a page to provide and will not be used to determine which solutions are 
chosen for the next step of the review process. 
• Addendum 1: Licensing Terms: Include known licensing terms (end-user licensing 
agreements) for software/technology included in the approach as well as any other terms 
and conditions (for example, for services) that the submission would rely upon. 
References to existing Federal Government contracts with appropriate terms that could be 
used to streamline negotiations are encouraged. Hyperlinks will not be accepted. 
• Addendum 2: Confidentiality: If there are any concerns about sharing information in 
your white paper with Leidos and Oracle Health, companies must include a restrictive 
marking on each relevant page identifying such limitations, as well as a paragraph 
explaining the concern. To protect business plans and technical information from FOIA 
disclosure for a period of five years, companies are required to include a legend on the 
documents identifying them as being submitted on a confidential basis.   
5. WHITE PAPER CONTENT 
The white paper will address each proposed capability and include the required details outlined 
below, as applicable.  

4 | Pa ge  Autonomous Coding & Appeals and Denials Management - Request for Solution 
 
5.1. Core Technical & Compliance Requirements (Applies to ALL submissions) 
5.1.1. EHR Architecture Experience: Describe any experience integrating your solution with 
an electronic health record (EHR). Leidos is the current system integrator for MHS 
GENESIS. The Government anticipates the successful offeror will collaborate with 
Leidos to integrate the solution into MHS GENESIS. 
5.1.2. Advanced Documentation, Automation, and Decision Support: Describe the 
solutions support capabilities that utilize modern, human-like, computational processes. 
The response should address the approach to mitigating potential bias within these 
processes to ensure fairness and accuracy in code assignment across patient populations. 
Furthermore, describe the plan for ongoing monitoring and evaluation of system 
performance to identify and correct any errors or biases. 
5.1.3. DoW EHR Data Required to Generate the Coding: Describe how long the 
company’s solution requires data to be retained to generate the coding, and whether the 
data retention time can be adjusted to suit the Government’s requirements. 
5.1.4. Security & Compliance: 
• Describe how the proposed solution complies with DODI 8510.01, Risk Management 
Framework (RMF) for DoW IT and complies with annual Federal Information 
Security Modernization Act (FISMA) security control testing. 
• Identify whether the solution has obtained or when it is anticipated to obtain 
FedRAMP authorization at the moderate level. The solution must possess, at a 
minimum, a valid DoD IL 4+ authorization (DoD IL 5 is preferred).  This can be 
attained through a FedRAMP High authorization or a FedRAMP Moderate 
authorization with additional Privacy Overlays applied. During prototype project 
performance, DHA will utilize the FedRAMP authorization to issue a mission owner 
authorization. 
• The contractor shall obtain and maintain access to the Supplier Performance Risk 
System (SPRS) via the PIEE, (available via the internet at 
https://www.sprs.csd.disa.mil/). If a group of companies is submitting a white paper, 
or any subcontractor(s) are contemplated, provide the status of the current assessment 
posted in SPRS for each. 
• Provide the status of CMMC Level 2 (self-attestation) for the company (or 
companies if a group) and any subcontractor(s) that will be managing CUI. 
• Confirm ability to comply with the incident management requirements of Chairman 
of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Manual (CJCSM) 6510.01B “Cyber Incident Handling 
Program”. 
• Confirm compliance with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act 
(HIPAA) of 1996. 
• Ability to encrypt data at rest and in transit. 
• Ability to support Common Access Card/Personal Identify Verification (CAC/PIV) 
authentication. 
• Address whether the source code is held in the United States and whether other than 
United States citizens access, maintain or upgrade the software. 

5 | Pa ge  Autonomous Coding & Appeals and Denials Management - Request for Solution 
 
• Ability to accept the terms of the DHA BAA (available online at 
https://health.mil/Reference-Center/Policies/2022/01/06/HIPAA-Compliant-
Business-Associate-Agreement). 
5.2. Solution Support Details (Applies to ALL submissions): 
• Bill of Materials (BOM): For each capability, vendors will submit a high-level BOM. 
The BOM should provide a rough, top-level summary of the major components, software 
modules, tools, data sources, licenses, hosting, AI tokens, or services required to deliver 
the proposed solution.  
• Relevant Experience: Briefly describe relevant prior experience developing, deploying 
and sustaining similar (in scope, scale, and technical complexity) solutions. Identify 
where your solution has been implemented and specify your organization's role in these 
efforts, including whether you acted as the primary vendor or a supporting partner. 
• Project Management: Explain your organization's project management expertise and 
methodology and organization's risk management capabilities and approach 
• Collaboration: Vendors should clearly indicate whether they are collaborating with any 
other organization to deliver the proposed solution. If collaboration is planned, identify 
each participating organization and briefly describe its role and contribution. 
• Data Rights, Intellectual Property, and Engine Provenance: Identify the underlying

Shiprock Service Unit 
Clearinghouse Claims Management Vendor 
Scope of Work 
 
A.   SCOPE OF WORK:   
Clearinghouse Claims Management Vendor to provide a revenue cycle process which contains at a minimum: 
automated components for Claims Submission & Management, Remittance & Payment Management , and 
Patient Billing & Payment Management.  Clearinghouse vendor is to provide an innovative automated solution 
which improves the revenue cycle process and maximizes Medicare reimbursement, from front-end eligibility 
verification to reimbursement posting.  The scope of the clearinghouse vendor  is to provide accurate and 
regulatory billing reviews and reporting notices to assure accuracy, minimize denials, and improve the quality 
of billing data submitted to third-party payers.  The clearinghouse vendor preference must incorporate a web-
based, be HIPAA-compliant, and provide billing management solutions to include a single claims management 
interface for virtually all government and commercial payers.    
 
B.  OBJECTIVES: 
 The business objective of the clearinghouse vendor is to contain a revenue cycle management solution which 
will support and maintain the continuity of critical and timely services with Shiprock Service Unit ; this in turn 
will support the I.H.S. mission of improving quality, safe and accessible healthcare services to the Alaskan 
Natives and Native Americans we serve in Indian Health Services. 
 
The interconnection will be to assist the Shiprock Service Unit Business Office in performing patient eligibility 
verification, inquire of claims status, and provide address verification on a real-time basis.  All transactions get 
routed through a communic ation server’s proprietary direct server engine and over a secure, encrypted 
connection to the vendor’s processing center that functions as the clearinghouse for claims management, 
billing, and eligibility inquiry transactions between Shiprock Service Unit and the clearinghouse.   The Shiprock 
Service Unit Business Office, seeking to improve the accuracy and efficiency of its registration and billing 
operations, will utilize the clearinghouse vendor’s eligibility system  to provide real time verification of 
eligibility, claim status, address, and other vital information. 
 
C. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE AND PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: 
 
Delivery Location:  
Northern Navajo Medical Center 
PO Box 160 
Shiprock, New Mexico 87420 
 
Four Corners Regional Health Center 
Highway 160 & Navajo Route 35 
Teec Nos Pos, Arizona 86514 
 
DZ Health Center 
6 Road 7586 
Bloomfield, NM   87413 
 
Hours of Operation: 
24/7 for Northern Navajo Medical Center 
Monday to Friday 8:00am to 4:30pm for FCRHC and DZ Health Center 
 
Period of Performance: 
Service will be provided for 12 continuous months with four Option Years 
 
 

D.   MAINTENANCE / SUPPORT PROCESS BY CONTRACTOR: 
Contractor will provide  the Shiprock Service Unit Business Office(s) on the maintenance and on -going support 
associated with vendor-related projects that may include:  
 
1.  Software Upgrades 
2. Web-based connectivity service 
3. Real-time EDI transactions including patient eligibility verification, claims status, address verification, 
denial/payment management, auto posting and others that have interface with the existing patient registration 
system so that inquiry and response dat a are electronically transferred between the RPMS registration/third 
party billing system and the clearinghouse solution program and its contracted carriers. 
4.   If required, programming fees will be a part of this maintenance and support services. Such programming 
services should include the transition process of the  applicable Medicare intermediary services and any other 
third-party requirements, such as ICD and CPT mandates.   
5. All maintenance and support services will be for the following Shiprock Service Unit locations:  
i. Northern Navajo Medical Center 
a) Ambulatory Care Center (Day Surgery Unit) 
b) Toadlena Clinic 
c) Sanostee Clinic 
ii. Four Corners Regional Health Center 
iii. Dzilth-Na-O-Dith-Hle Health Center 
 
E. SECURITY, SAFETY, AND PRIVACY: 
The Vendor/Contractor shall take appropriate security measures to ensure systems and other Government 
property is stored and installed in accordance with security guidelines and applicable regulations.  
 
The Vendor/Contractor shall comply with all Federal, State and Local Safety regulations. 
 
The Vendor/Contractor will adhere to Privacy and Patient Confidentiality laws that are consistent with the 
Privacy Act and JCAHO regulations. 
 
SSU/Vendor/Contractor shall comply with all Federal, State and Local Safety regulations. 
 
SSU will ensure security measures are in place to protect acquired equipment from disruption. 
 
F. SSU SHALL PERFORM: 
1. SSU shall provide third-party claims for the Contractor to process through the claims services. 
2. SSU will provide and comply with required electronic transactions as required by the claim master suites, 
payment management, denial & Medicare management and switching services.   Rejected claims will be 
corrected and resubmitted by SSU in a timely manner. 
3. SSU is responsible for any costs incurred in connection with modifications or enhancements to the I.H.S. 
software system that are necessary for implementing the interface with the claim master suites and 
switching services as required. 
4. SSU will initiate and process all required procurements that will obligate funds for the claim master 
suites, denial management and point of sale switching services.  SSU will also make timely payments on 
the invoices 
5. SSU will implement a performance matrix to track and monitor period of performance. 
6. SSU will initiate and coordinate with the customer service center with clearinghouse vendor on any 
issues or concerns that arise with the portal access, transmission of electronic claim files, setting up 
transaction codes, etc. 
 

G. GOVERNMENT FURNISHED PROPERTY: 
1. The Vendor/Contractor shall safeguard all Government property provided for use. 
 
2. The Vendor/Contractor shall notify the Government any time the Contractor moves Government 
furnished equipment. 
 
3. The Vendor/Contractor shall ensure that the Government facilities, equipment and materials are 
secured at the close of each work period. 
 
4. The Vendor/Contractor shall take appropriate measures to safeguard their Government Issued Security 
badges and common access cards. 
 
5. The Government shall provide access to applicable areas to complete the work requested. 
 
6. The Government will provide appropriate space, power, and network connections to complete the work 
requested. 
 
7. The Government will provide onsite support to work directly with the Vendor/Contractor as needed. 
  
 
H. Section 508 and Accessibility 
• This product must conform to the Revised Section 508 ( https://www.access-board.gov/guidelines-and-
standards/communications-and-it/about-the-ict-refresh/final-rule/text-of-the-standards-and-guidelines) 
and WCAG 2.1 Level AA standards as outlined below. 
• Solicitations for supplies and services shall require the submission of a Section 508 Product Assessment 
Template.  The template can be found at https://www.itic.org/policy/accessibility/vpat. 
  
All Information and Communication Technology (ICT) deliverables under this contract (e.g., websites, 
applications, electronic documents, and multimedia) must comply with the Revised Section 508 Standards (36 
CFR Part 1194) and the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA standards . The Contractor 
shall ensure accessibility of all ICT deliverables and provide conformance documentation in the form of a 
Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT®) / Accessibility Conformance Report (ACR), or by completing 
the HHS Section 508 Accessibility Checklists . The current VPAT 2.5 template includes fields for reporting 
conformance to WCAG 2.1 and shall be used to document accessibility. The Contractor shall remediate any 
identified accessibility issues at no additional cost. The Contracting Officer will include the applicable Health 
and Human Services Acquisition Regulation (HHSAR) clauses 352.239-73 and 352.239-74 in the solicitation and 
resulting contract.

- Technical, procurement, financial and budget approvals are routed to the right decision-makers, with transparent status, audit evidence and timely escalation.
- Procurement plans, pipelines and demand consolidation give management forward visibility of upcoming sourcing actions.

- Early industry engagement and pre-competitive activities are planned, recorded and governed in a way that supports transparency and future auditability.
- Non-competitive and pre-competitive engagement is distinguished and controlled in line with applicable policy and access rules.

- Internal reviews by procurement, technical, legal, finance and governance stakeholders occur through controlled workflows before publication.

Sources Sought Notice & Request for Information (RFI) 
Requirement: Human Performance and Student Management System (HP-SMS) 
Agency: United States Army Special Operations Command (USASOC) 
Location: Fort Bragg, NC (USAJFKSWCS) 
THIS IS NOT A NOTICE OF SOLICITATION ISSUANCE, BUT RATHER A REQUEST 
FOR INFORMATION (RFI) from industry that will allow the Government to identify 
interested sources capable of meeting the requirement. The information sought herein is for 
planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a request for quote (RFQ), request for 
proposal (RFP), invitation for bid (IFB), or as an obligation or commitment on the part of the 
Government to acquire any product or service. There shall be no basis for claims against the 
Government as a result of information submitted in response to this RFI. The Government does 
not intend to award a contract on the basis of this RFI or otherwise pay for any information 
submitted by respondents to this request. Information obtained in response to this notice may 
assist the Government in developing its acquisition strategy, determining the feasibility of a 
small business set-aside, and refining the draft Performance Work Statement (PWS). 
This notice is for market research purposes only. Please see the attached draft Performance Work 
Statement (PWS) for detailed technical requirements. The anticipated period of performance is a 
one-year base period followed by four (4) one-year option periods. 
Documentation provided must address all required elements listed herein. Providing only a 
reference to a website is unacceptable for purposes of this announcement and will not be 
considered. All proprietary or corporate data received shall be clearly identified and will be 
protected from release to sources outside the Government. 
Contractors interested in providing these services must be registered in the System for Award 
Management (www.sam.gov). Contractors responding to this RFI are asked to provide the 
following information: 
1. Company’s full name and address and Point of Contact information. 
2. Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code. 
3. Business size under the identified NAICS code (whether large, small, small-
disadvantaged, 8(a), HUBZone, women-owned, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small 
Business, etc.). 
4. A brief Statement of Capability (no more than 8 pages) that responds to the following 
questions and demonstrates the ability to meet the requirements specified in the attached 
PWS. 
 
Request for Information (RFI) Questions 
Question 1: Technical Approach & Scalability 
The PWS outlines a complex requirement involving software sustainment, modernization, 

multiple API integrations, and significant data management tasks within the SOCOM 
Information Enterprise (SIE) network environment. Please describe your high-level technical 
approach to meeting the requirements of this PWS. In your response, please address: 
• Your strategy for managing the 38 distinct legacy modules and transitioning them to the 
new baseline of 50 configured modules. 
• Your methodology for ensuring system performance, stability, and responsiveness on the 
specified government network, addressing the 24/7/365 operational requirement. 
• Your experience with the specific systems requiring API integration (Army Vantage, 
Maven, IPPS-A). 
• Describe your technical approach to scaling the system to support 110+ courses. 
Specifically, how does your platform utilize reusable templates, cloned configurations, or 
parent-child module relationships to prevent database bloat and minimize the 
administrative burden of managing 110+ unique course pipelines? 
• Explain how your platform handles concurrent user scaling as we transition from the 
current student load to a fully integrated, schoolhouse-wide population. 
Question 2: Data Management, Portability, and Open Systems 
A key objective of the PWS is to ensure the Government maintains ownership and portability of 
its data, in alignment with the Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) and DoD Data 
Decrees. Based on Sections 1.1.8 (Data Architecture), 1.1.9 (Data Transformation), 1.1.10 
(Documentation), and 1.1.11 (Data Rights): 
• Describe your approach and past experience in delivering a non-proprietary, open-
schema export of all government data as required in PWS Section 1.1.9.3. 
• Explain your process for creating and maintaining the critical documentation 
deliverables, such as the data dictionary (1.1.8.4), Interface Control Documents (1.1.3.6), 
and measurement models (1.1.10.3), to ensure they are sufficient for third-party use. 
• How do you propose to support the Government in executing the "transition-out plan" 
(1.1.10.5) to ensure a smooth migration to a successor system or provider with minimal 
disruption? 
Question 3: Staffing and On-Site Support 
The PWS requires on-site Field Support Representatives (FSRs) with a specific skill set (PWS 
Section 1.6.11.2) to provide direct support. 
• Please provide your proposed staffing plan for the on-site FSRs and the reach-back 
support team. 
• Describe your methodology for recruiting, training, and retaining personnel who meet the 
specialized experience and security clearance requirements outlined in the PWS. 

Question 4: Alternative Solution Availability 
Is your company capable of delivering an alternative, fully integrated, commercially available 
Off-The-Shelf (COTS) or Government-Off-The-Shelf (GOTS) human performance platform that 
meets or exceeds all functional requirements of the baseline 50 modules outlined in this PWS? If 
proposing an alternative solution, please describe how you would execute a complete data 
migration from the legacy system without loss of historical record or operational downtime. 
Question 5: Cybersecurity & SIE ATO Readiness 
If your company is proposing an alternative COTS or GOTS software solution (as referenced in 
Question 4), please detail your readiness to operate specifically within the USSOCOM 
environment. 
• 5a. Does your proposed solution currently possess an active Authority to Operate (ATO) 
or Interim Authority to Test (IATT) specifically on the SOCOM Information Enterprise 
(SIE) network? 
• 5b. If currently deployed on the SIE, what Impact Level (e.g., IL4, IL5, IL6/SIPR) is the 
platform authorized to support, and who is the sponsoring USSOCOM Authorizing 
Official (AO)? 
• 5c. If the platform does not currently hold an SIE ATO, but holds an ATO on another 
DoD network, describe your approach, estimated timeline, and past experience in 
establishing reciprocity or navigating the Risk Management Framework (RMF) process 
to achieve an ATO specifically on the SIE. 
Question 6: Modernization, Curriculum, and Baseline Expansion 
The Government is considering shifting the scope of this effort from a traditional, narrow 
"software licensing and configuration sustainment" model (keeping the legacy platform 
operational) to a broader, highly integrated "Assessment and Training Pipeline Support" model. 
• Please describe your capability and experience in providing deeply integrated Subject 
Matter Experts (SMEs) who do not just maintain the software, but actively manage 
templates, update modules to match evolving training curriculums, and assist in 
designing predictive measurement models. 
• How would your company proactively identify and resolve systemic software issues 
(such as network latency, database bloat, and poor connectivity) rather than treating them 
strictly as Government-owned infrastructure problems? 
• What are the primary risks and cost drivers associated with expanding the scope from 
basic software maintenance to an active, modernized pipeline support model, and how 
would you mitigate them? 
• The proposed PWS baselines the contract at 50 active, configured modules. Please 
describe your experience in rapidly deploying new, custom modules to meet evolving 
POI and curriculum requirements. 

• What is your standard timeline for designing, testing, and deploying a new performance 
module (e.g., a physical, psychological, or academic assessment form) from the moment 
the Government provides the requirement? 
• Describe the user-level administrative tools in your system. Can trained Government 
administrators (like our Technical Evaluator) build, edit, and deploy new modules and 
forms themselves, or does every modification require vendor-paid coding and software 
releases? 
Question 7: PWS Feedback & Recommendations 
The Government is interested in industry’s input. Based on your expertise, are there any 
recommended changes to the PWS's scope, tasks, or timeline that would increase efficiency or 
reduce project risk? Are there any areas that lack clarity or could present significant challenges 
to a contractor? 
Question 8: Module Unit Pricing & Growth Model 
• To support long-term scalability while controlling costs, the Government intends to 
establish a standardized, "per-module" pricing structure for any work exceeding the 
baseline 50 modules. 
• Describe how your company would structure a "menu-pricing" or "unit-pricing" catalog 
for additional module builds (e.g., Simple, Medium, and Complex modules based on the 
number of data fields, API connections, and reporting dashboards required). 
• What are the primary cost drivers (labor, licensing, database storage, testing) associated 
with building an individual custom module, and how can the Government structure its 
PWS to minimize these costs as we scale to the full 110+ course list? 
Question 9: Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) 
Please provide a non-binding Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) price for the total cost to 
complete all tasks outlined in the PWS for the base year and all four option years. This ROM is 
for market research purposes only and will not be considered a formal quote or proposal. Please 
break out the ROM by: 
• CLIN X001: Software Platform & Sustainment (FFP) 
• Software Licensing: Provision of the required software licenses for the specified 
number of users (e.g., 5,000 seats as per PWS 5.2.1). 
• Core Maintenance: Standard software maintenance, including delivery of patches, 
bug fixes, and routine software updates to ensure the platform is on the current 
release version (PWS 5.2.3, 5.2.4, 5.2.5). 
• CLIN X002: Program Management & Integrated Technical Support (FFP) 
• Program Management: Overall contract management, reporting (MSRs), and 
meetings (PWS 5.1). 

• On-Site & Reach-back Support: Provision of all Key Personnel, including the 
Program Manager, and the on-site Field Support Representatives (FSRs)/SMEs 
(PWS 1.6.11, 5.4). 
• User Training: Delivery of all standard, basic, and operational administrator 
training blocks (PWS 5.3). 
• Routine Technical Support: Base-level support such as modifying existing 
surveys and reports and adjusting configurations based on POI changes (PWS 
5.2.6). 
• CLIN X003: Modernization & Integration Support (FFP) 
• API Development & Integration: All work related to developing and maintaining 
interfaces with Army Vantage, Maven, and IPPS-A (PWS 1.1.3). 
• Data Architecture & Analytics Enablement: Design and delivery of the structured 
reporting tables, schema remediation, and dashboard enablement (PWS 1.1.8). 
• UI/UX Modernization: Execution of the user interface modernization efforts 
(PWS 1.1.6). 
• Data Transformation: The one-time effort of transforming and loading historical 
data into the new system (PWS 1.1.9.1). 
• CLIN X004: Travel (Cost - No Fee) 
• Description: This CLIN is for all pre-approved, CONUS travel required for 
contract performance, as outlined in PWS Section 1.6.13. All travel will be billed 
on a strictly cost-reimbursable basis with no fee, in accordance with the Joint 
Travel Regulation (JTR). 
• Rationale: Travel costs are variable and unpredictable. A Cost CLIN with a Not-
to-Exceed (NTE) ceiling is the standard and most appropriate method for 
managing these expenses, preventing the contractor from having to guess at travel 
costs and build them into the FFP price. 
• CLIN X005: Additional Module Build Support (Unit Price Menu - FFP) 
• Description: This CLIN is intended to capture the fixed, fully burdened unit price 
for developing, testing, and deploying additional custom modules beyond the 
baseline 50. Please provide a non-binding unit price ROM for the following 
hypothetical module categories: 
• Simple Module Unit Price: (e.g., basic digital form, up to 15 data fields, standard 
PDF export, no third-party integrations). 
• Medium Module Unit Price: (e.g., custom assessment layout, up to 50 data fields, 
automated email/dashboard alerts, standard role-based access). 

• Complex Module Unit Price: (e.g., advanced tracking, 50+ data fields, predictive 
modeling, custom analytical dashboards, and third-party data integrations). 
 
The anticipated NAICS code is 541511 – Custom Computer Programming Services, with a small 
business size standard of $34.0 million. The anticipated Product Service Code (PSC) is DA01 
(IT and Telecom - Business Application/Application Development Support Services). 
No requests for capability briefings will be honored as a result of this notice. Information 
provided will not be used as a part of any subsequent solicitation. No feedback will be provided 
regarding individual capability statements. No reimbursements will be made for any costs 
associated with providing information in response to this announcement. 
Capability Statements and responses are due no later than 2:00 PM EST, [15 days from posting, 
XX August 2026]. Please email responses to Mr. Jon Long at jonathan.long.civ@socom.mil, 
referencing “Sources Sought – HP-SMS Recompete” in the subject line. 
Failure to respond to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future associated requests 
for quotations that may be issued. Respondents will NOT be individually notified of the results. 
For information regarding this notice, please contact Jon Long at the email address listed above.

The Ballroom upgrade is engineered as a single, cohesive AV, audio, AVoIP, and lighting system. Each

audio network, NDI/AVoIP video transport, power distribution, rack layouts, DSP presets, acoustic

or compatibility impacts if possible. 
 
Compatibility & technical risk: Audio network: Clocking/PTP stability, channel mapping, and encryption 
conformance; control processor and DSP reprogramming required. (ULX‑D specific Dante/crypto 
features). AVoIP / NDI: Breakage of NDI transport profiles, multicast QoS, VLAN/IGMP settings; 
switch and endpoint tuning would need to be rebuilt. (M4250 AV profile templates for NDI/Dante). 
Acoustics & amplification: Re‑derivation of coverage plots, amplifier load, transformer selection, and 
DSP equalization; new commissioning and measurement cycles. Cost & schedule impact 
(estimates):Engineering redesign & programming: Additional AV engineering labor, acoustic design 
services, DSP/control programming, and test/commissioning cycles. Conservative estimate $50,000–
$200,000 plus 6–12 months schedule risk for review, integration, testing, and re‑validation.Procurement 
risks: Increased risk of performance shortfalls and warranty gaps when mixing unfamiliar vendors.

This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the 
Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 12, as supplemented with additional information included 
in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation that Naval Surface Warfare Center 
Carderock Division (NSWCCD) intends to issue, and is a Request for Quotes (RFQ) for the following 
Supplies and/or Services.  
 
This requirement is for the establishment of a multi award 5-year Blanket Purchase Agreement 
(BPA) ordering period to procure ACT Brand HPC Clusters on a Brand Name basis. This 
includes the associated start-up services including installation, training, and annual preventative 
maintenance.   
 
The provisions and clauses included and/or incorporated in this solicitation document are those in effect 
through the RFO effective May 6, 2026 located on https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul  and the 
Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) Change DPN 20260507 effective 
5/7/2026 located at https://www.acq.osd.mil/dpap/dars/change_notices.html. SEE ATTACHED 
SOLICITATION FOR CLAUSES AND PROVISIONS.  The NAICS code is 541519 (ITVAR) and 
the associated PSC code are 7B21 and R425, and the Small Business Standard is 150 for this 
procurement: NOTE: A Class Waiver is not applicable to a procurement unless the NAICS code, PSC, 
and NAICS Code Descriptor currently in effect, match the item(s) being procured. This procurement 
IS being set-aside for small business. 
 
Interested parties may identify their interest to this requirement by submitting a quote and/or capabilities 
statement no later than 12:00 PM on 20 August 2026.  It is anticipated that 2 or 3 one firm-fixed price 
Agreement will be issued in response to this RFQ.  
 
All responses shall include the following.  
 
1. Quote on company’s Letterhead 
2. Pricing 
3. Cage Code 
4. FOB Destination 
5. Point of contact 
6. GSA contract number (if applicable) 
7. Business Size 
8. Quote should be rounded off to the nearest whole dollar 
Offers/quotes submitted in response to this solicitation shall not contain nor be subject to the 
offeror's/vendor's standard commercial terms and conditions.  Any offer/quote submitted in 
response to this solicitation which includes the offeror's/vendor's standard commercial terms and 
conditions may be considered a material defect and may be rejected as being non-responsive to the 
solicitation. 
Responses to this notice are due on or before 12:00 PM on 20 August 2026, Eastern Daylight Time 
(EDT) to arnel.a.ngo.civ@us.navy.mil.  
 
Point of Contact for this notice is Arnel Ngo, 757-478-2013, arnel.a.ngo.civ@us.navy.mil. 
  

Section A - Solicitation/Contract Form

BPA TERMS AND CONDITIONS
"The Naval Surface Warfare Center, Carderock Division, (NSWCCD) invites vendors who are Authorized resellers/distributors of Advanced
to enter into a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) that establishes the terms and conditions applicable Clustering Technologies, Inc. (ACT) 
to ACT HPC Clusters. As a result of this solicitation, approximately 2 to 3 vendors are needed to provide the supplies and services; however, the 
Government reserves the right to award to a single vendor ".
1. The Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) holder shall provide supplies and services as described in CLIN 0001 to CLIN 0009 in Section B or as 
required on each Call, and as stated in the Minimum Requirements, if and when requested by the contracting officer for the duration of the BPA.
2. The Contracting Officers of Naval Surface Warfare Center-Carderock Division (NSWCCD) Code 02 Contracting Department are the only 
authorized individuals to order against this BPA.
3. The total of all BPA calls may not exceed the ceiling amount of $9,000,000.00.

1.0 DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES/INTRODUCTION:
The Hull Response and Protection Branch, Code 664, at the Naval Surface Warfare Center, Carderock Division 
(NSWCCD), West Bethesda, MD, requires a contract for purchase of the materials/services needed for brand new 
Advanced Cluster Technologies (ACT) - clusters and accessories to be high-performance computing (HPC) 
installed at NSWCCD's facility at Carderock MD.   
2.0 BACKGROUND: 
NSWCCD Code 664 has expertise in the area of Survivability and Weapons Effects. Code 664 relies on multiple HPC   
clusters to perform high fidelity modeling and simulation of highly dynamic weapons effect events. Code 664 requires an 
additional ACT HPC cluster to allow for more computational runs and quicker turnaround time for these critical analyses. 
3.0 OBJECTIVE:
To establish a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for the contractor shall provide and accomplish all materials/services 
required to install all ACT-brand hardware and associated software for a new HPC system in an existing unclassified and
/or classified facility using personnel trained to perform computer and software installation on closed network DoD 
systems. The scope of work includes:

of installation

3.1.1 THERMAL MANAGEMENT
The HPC system, and all of the components within, shall be air-cooled and be configured to automatically shut down in 
the event of overheating. Temperature sensors shall be incorporated into the system to detect loss of cooling (e.g. high 
ambient air temperature) within the closed space. In the event of high ambient temperature event, the HPC system shall 
perform a graceful shutdown of system components. (Note: A graceful shut down   is when a computer is turned off by 
software function and the operating system (OS) is allowed to perform its tasks of safely shutting down processes and 
closing connections.) All hardware must be TAA compliant and Country of Origin provided.

1. Introduction 
 
This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for conducting market research and planning 
purposes only. Accordingly, this RFI constitutes neither a Request for Quote, Request for 
Proposal, nor a guarantee that one will be issued by the Government in the future; 
furthermore, it does not commit the Government to contract for any services described 
herein. Additionally, this RFI does not restrict the Government as to the ultimate 
acquisition approach. In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.101(c), 
responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to 
form a binding contract. 
 
The purpose of this RFI is to identify qualified vendors who can meet Department of 
Veterans Affairs (VA) requirements for the Enterprise Data Center and 
Telecommunications Modernization (EDCTM) initiative, and to obtain industry input on the 
best approach for structuring and executing this requirement. Any contract or order that 
might be awarded based on information received or derived from this market research will 
be the outcome of the competitive process. Your response to this RFI will be treated only 
as information for the Government to consider. 
 
The Government is not responsible for any cost incurred by industry in furnishing this 
information. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested 
vendor’s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future 
solicitation if any is issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly 
voluntary. All submissions will become Government property and will not be returned. 
Interested vendors are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or 
competition sensitive information contained in their response. VA is under no obligation to 
provide feedback to the company, or to contact the company for clarification of any 
information submitted in response to this RFI. 
 
Be advised that set-aside decisions may be made based on the information provided in 
response to this RFI. Responses should be as complete and informative as possible. 
2. Background 
 
The VA, Office of Information and Technology, Infrastructure Operations, Data Center 
and Infrastructure Engineering division manages a large, geographically distributed 
portfolio of data centers, computer rooms, and telecommunications spaces. These 
environments support clinical, administrative, and mission-critical systems across the 
Veterans Health Administration, Veterans Benefits Administration, and National Cemetery 
Administration. 
 

Page 2 of 6 
 
There is no single standard configuration across VA data center facilities. Infrastructure 
varies significantly from site to site, including differences in equipment racks, cabling 
standards, power distribution, cooling systems, and facility layouts.
