VA anticipates award of a firm fixed price Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) or an 
alternative ordering-based strategy to establish a pre-priced listing of discrete, hardware-
led deliverables for data center and telecommunications modernization work. The primary 
objectives for the procurement are: 
1) Standardize legacy and non-standard telecommunications and data center 
physical infrastructure; 
2) Identify and replace end-of-life or obsolete infrastructure components;  
3) Standardize inconsistent or site-unique installation practices across facilities;  
4) Update or complete design documentation and specifications; and  
5) Eliminate infrastructure designs that increase operational risk, cost, or 
complexity. 
 
The Government is seeking industry feedback to determine vendor capabilities, 
socio-economic categories, to identify industry best practices, and identify any 
alternate contract vehicles well-suited for this requirement.  
 
Hardware-Led Deliverables with Bundled Services. The Government envisions 
ordering data center modernization work as hardware-led line items. Each line item would 
represent a major infrastructure activity (e.g., Computer Room Air Conditioner (CRAC) 
unit replacement, structured cabling refresh, rack and enclosure installation) priced on a 
firm-fixed-price basis. The price would include all ancillary services necessary to produce 
a complete, installed, and operational outcome—including but not limited to site survey, 
engineering design, procurement, installation, testing, and documentation.  
 
Standardization Across Facilities. A key objective is to move VA data centers toward

specific conditions will vary and that contractors will need to account for that variability.

STATEMENT OF WORK 
 
1. Introduction/Background: The agency needs a motion capture system to track rotor 
position and orientation in real time during spin-up testing in a low-pressure 
environment. The system must deliver continuous six-degree-of-freedom data during 
dynamic motion and under partial visibility. It also must operate reliably in non-
laboratory test environments. 
 
2. Scope of Work: The purchase request (PR) will cover the delivery, installation, and 
training for use of a Vicon Valkyrie VK6 Camera system. 
 
3. Objectives: The provision of a Vicon Valkyrie VK6 Camera system in the NASA 
Ames Planetary Aeolian Laboratory. 
 
4. Description of the Work/Contractor Tasks: The system must provide: 
 
• Real-time 6DoF tracking with latency low enough for control feedback 
• Continuous tracking when the rotor is only visible to a single camera 
• High speed capture capabilities 
• 6mp cameras for full frame resolution of over 6.1 million pixels at capture speeds 
of up to 720Hz and up to 2000Hz (with windowed FoV). 
• Lens with adjustable focal length for changing test configurations 
• Position data calculated from 256 values of greyscale from each marker-pixel, not

• Calibration that maintains accuracy during operation without stopping for manual

B.3 Statement of Work 
Vocera – ProAssure Onsite Specialist for the 
VA Northern California Healthcare System 
  
1.0  General  
1.1 Background   
VA Northern California Health Care Systems (VANCHS) recently installed a clinical 
communication system called Vocera and wants to integrate it into the hospital’s current 
Nurse Call system for improved clinical workflow and response. VANCHS is also seeking 
Vocera software licensing, support, and maintenance to ensure the high uptime and 
minimal impact to patient care.  
  
1.2 Objective  
The objective is to integrate a Vocera communication system with the hospital’s current 
ASCOM Nurse Call (Model: Telligence) system and provide continued Vocera licensing, 
support, and maintenance services.  
  
1.3 Scope of Work  
The contractor shall provide all resources necessary to accomplish the tasks and 
deliverables described in this Statement of Work (SOW). The contractor shall provide 
integration services between the Vocera communication system and the ASCOM Nurse 
Call system, provide continued Vocera software licensing, and provide support and 
maintenance services to Vocera system.  
  
1.4 Period of Performance  
The period of performance of this contract is one base year. 
  
1.5 Place of Performance  
VA Northern California Health Care System, 10535 Hospital Way, Mather Ca 95655 
  
2.0  Specific Requirements/Tasks  
  
2.1 Integrate the Vocera communication system with the ASCOM Nurse Call System 2.1.1 
Design, configure, and deploy alarm and event notifications 

 
 
Page 6 of 38 
for up to five nursing units  
 
2.1.2 Coordinate all integration services (planning, implementation, testing, etc.) with the 
Contracting Officer’s Representative and/or other designated VA staff  
  
2.1.3 Test the communication system to ensure integration services are complete and all 
devices/software are working properly  
  
2.1.4 Provide training to the VA staff on the use and proper maintenance of the Vocera 
system  
  
2.2 Provide continued support services for the Vocera system including but not limited to the 
following:  
• Software and hardware updates  
• Access to hotfixes and security patches  
• Access to Vocera support portal, knowledgebase, documentation portal, online 
community, and product feedback tool  
• Access to self-serve and self-paced training courses  
• 2-3 support contacts and 1 RMA contact  
• Emergency phone technical assistance 24x7x365 for Severity 1 issues  
• Assigned support engineer for complex escalations  
• Access to premier support webinars and distance learning training  
• Annual system health report upon request  
• Additional designated support contacts and 1 RMA contact  
  
  
3.0  Special Instructions  
3.0 Any onsite visits will be performed during the normal VANCHCS business 
hours (8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.) Monday through Friday, except Federal 
holidays, unless otherwise specified. The Contractor may work outside

provided without additional charge to the Government. Any overtime charges 
must be approved by the COR prior to the initiation of overtime work.

1.0 INTRODUCTION
 
USNO is the sole provider of Precise Time and Astrometry (hereinafter, "PTA") data products to the DoD under Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff 
Instruction (CJCSI) 4650.01H and DoD Instruction (DoDI) 4650.06. PTA data products include Precise Time (hereinafter, "PT") and time   
dissemination tools, Celestial Reference Frame (hereinafter, "CRF") data products and applications, and Earth Orientation Parameters (EOPs). These   
products are critical to navigation for any DoD system, and, most importantly, the United States Global Positioning System (hereinafter, "GPS"). The   
security and integrity of the network from which these systems disseminate data is paramount, requiring 24/7 monitoring.
 
The proposed acquisition is to strengthen USNO's network infrastructure It is intended to acquire IT PIE unique network software products to .  
continual manage network data products in which USNO is responsible for.

Utilize ITPIE software for network operations and management to ensure network stability and safety to deliver mission critical products.

06 September 2026 through 05 September 2025

The proposed acquisition is for an annual subscription of VAE, Inc. unique software product IT PIE in order to 
secure and manage network assets in which the United States Naval Observatory utilizes for disseminating

STATEMENT OF WORK 
FOR 
MODERNIZATION AND ENGINEERING 
SUPPORT FOR THE NEDU OCEAN 
SIMULATION FACILITY CONTROL 
SYSTEM 
 
1.0 SCOPE 
The Ocean Simulation Facility Control System (OSF-CS) is a life-safety critical, standalone Platform IT (PIT) 
system located at the Navy Experimental Diving Unit (NEDU). The system requires comprehensive hardware and 
software modernization to replace obsolete components, reconstitute a laboratory environment, and achieve a 
secure, Windows 11-compliant baseline. The primary goal of this effort is a one-time migration and modernization 
project. This SOW encompasses the engineering support required to reconstitute a test lab, modernize the OSF-CS 
hardware and software, and provide all necessary technical support to ensure a successful migration. The contractor 
shall provide all personnel, technical expertise, and project management to perform the phased tasks outlined below. 
 
2.0 APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS 
The following documents, of the exact issue shown, form a part of this SOW to the extent specified herein. In 
the event of conflict between the documents referenced herein and the SOW, the contents of this SOW shall take 
precedence. 
 
2.1 Military Standards: 
 List the standard here otherwise “none” 
2.2 Military Specifications: 
 List the standard here otherwise “none” 
2.3 Other Documents: 
 DoD Manual 8140.03, DoD Cyberspace Workforce Framework (DCWF) 
 
3.0 REQUIREMENTS (CDRL A001, A002, A003, A004, A005, A006, A007, A008) 
The Contractor shall execute the modernization project in a single, phased effort, providing necessary 
artifacts and deliverables in accordance with the Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL). 
 
3.0.1 The Contractor shall reconstitute the NEDU-provided laboratory environment at the Contractor's off-site 
facility. To bypass physical facility power constraints, the Contractor shall virtualize the system architecture 
using Rockwell Automation Studio 5000 Logix Emulate in place of hosting the physical Variable Speed 
Drive (VSD) hardware. To ensure compliance with stringent cybersecurity requirements, this virtualized 
environment shall be hosted and maintained on a dedicated server platform. A dedicated computer, 
provided by the Government, shall be utilized by the Contractor and integrated to host the LabVIEW and 
emulation environment The Contractor shall provide an Off-Site Lab Reconstitution & Emulation 
Validation Report (confirming successful Studio 5000 Logix, Studio 5000 Logix Emulate, Server 
Deployment, and LabVIEW configuration) (CDRL A001). 
 
3.0.2 To ensure compliance with stringent cybersecurity requirements and support additional virtualization, the 
Contractor shall procure, furnish, deploy, and configure a dedicated server platform. This dedicated server 
infrastructure will securely host the virtualized development and emulation environment. 
 
3.0.3 A dedicated computer, provided by the Government, shall be utilized by the Contractor and integrated to 
host the LabVIEW and emulation environment (CDRL A002). 

 
 
3.0.4 The Contractor shall replace obsolete operator workstations with modern Windows 11-capable hardware 
while initially retaining the current Windows 10 environment. 
 
3.0.4.1 The Contractor shall provide the following hardware/configurations: 
 
 Virtualization Server: One Dual-socket rack server, high core count, 512 GB+ RAM, redundant PSU; sized 
to securely host the virtualized OSF-CS development, emulation, and test environment. 
 
 Storage Configuration: One Enterprise NVMe/SSD array with RAID for VM datastores, snapshots, and 
lab/validation images. 
 
 UPS / Rack / PDU: One Rack-mount UPS, PDU, rails, and rack accessories for safe power and mounting. 
 
 Cabling / KVM / Network: Structured cabling, KVM access, transceivers, and miscellaneous network 
connectivity items. 
 
 Miscellaneous Infrastructure & Incidentals: Mounting hardware, labels, media, removable storage, and 
incidental infrastructure components. 
 
3.0.5 The Contractor shall perform a comprehensive analysis to identify and mitigate any interoperability issues 
with the planned upgrade to a Windows 11 environment. The Contractor shall deliver a Windows 11 
Interoperability Analysis Report, detailing all potential risks, issues, and recommended mitigation strategies. 
(CDRL A003). 
 
3.0.6 The Contractor shall execute a phased upgrade from Windows 10 to Windows 11, starting with the 
maintenance laptop, followed by the lab environment. The Contractor shall deliver a test report from the 
upgraded Windows 11 maintenance laptop and confirming successful Windows 11 lab environment upgrade. 
(CDRL A004). 
 
3.0.7 The Contractor shall upgrade main software components to the latest stable versions as the final deliverable. 
 
3.0.8 The Contractor shall perform system hardening on the final baseline by applying applicable DISA STIGs 
and SRGs. The Contractor shall deliver: 
 
o Final, modernized, and verified codebase (CDRL A005). 
 
o Technical Hardening Artifacts (STIG .ckl files and ACAS .nessus scans) to support the 
Government-led Risk Management Framework (RMF) effort CDRL (A006). 
 
o Final Project Report and Government-signed Factory Acceptance Test (FAT)[GG1.1] 
[GG2.1]Report (CDRL A007). 
 
3.0.9 The Contractor shall provide a Monthly Status Report (CDRL A008), outlining status of all tasking.

4.0 GOVERNMENT FURNISHED PROPERTY (GFP): 
4.1 The Government will provide the following GFI and GFE to the contractor: 
 
 Studio 5000 Logix Software & Licensing. 
 
 On–Site Physical Spare VSD Hardware (accessible at NEDU during validation windows). 
 
 LabVIEW Host Computer & OSF–CS Workstations (new computer hardware). 
 
 Legacy Source Code and System Documentation (unclassified OSF–CS codebase). 
 
4.2 Access to Government Facilities 
 
The Government will provide the contractor access to Government facilities to accomplish statement of work tasking. 
The Contractor shall provide a list of employees who require access to these areas, including standard security 
clearance information for each person, to the Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO) no later than three business days 
after the date of award. Access to Government buildings at Naval Support Activity Panama City (NSA PC) is from 
0600 to 1800 Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays. Normal work hours are from 0700 to 1700, Monday 
through Friday. Contractor employees shall be under Government oversight at all times. Government oversight requires 
that a Government employee be present in the same building/facility whenever Contractor employee(s) are performing 
work under this task order. Contractor personnel are not allowed to access any Government buildings at NSA PC 
outside the hours of 0600 to 1800 without the express approval of the Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO). When a 
Government facility is closed or early dismissal of Federal employees is directed due to severe weather, security threat, 
or a facility related problem that prevents personnel from working, onsite Contractor personnel regularly assigned to 
work at that facility should follow the same reporting and departure directions given to Government personnel. 
 
5.0 DATA DELIVERABLES 
 
Data shall be provided in accordance with the Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) DD Form 1423. 
 
 All source code must be delivered in its native, un-compiled, human-readable format. 
 
 The U.S. Government shall have unlimited Government Purpose Rights (GPR) to all technical data, 

 
 
computer software, source code, and documentation developed, delivered, or generated under this Statement 
of Work. 
6.0 PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE 
The items on this order shall be delivered no later than 12 months after Contract award. 
7.0 SECURITY 
 
This requirement is UNCLASSIFIED. The Contractor will not require access to nor be required to generate classified 
information to perform the requirement. 
7.1 Release of Information 
 
Release of information shall be in accordance with Section I, DFARS Clause 252.204-7000, Disclosure of 
Information. All technical data provided to the contractor by the Government shall be protected from public 
disclosure in accordance with the markings contained thereon. All other information relating to the items to be 
delivered or services to be performed under this task order may not be disclosed by any means without prior 
approval of the appropriate NSWC PCD authority. Dissemination or public disclosure includes, but is not 
limited to, permitting access to such information by foreign nationals or by any other person or entity; 
publication of technical or scientific papers; advertising; or any other proposed public release. The contractor 
shall provide adequate physical protection to such information to preclude access by any person or entity not 
authorized such access by the Government. 
 
7.2 Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) 
 
Controlled unclassified information (CUI) is official information that requires the application of controls and 
protective measures for a variety of reasons and has not been approved for public release, to include technical 
information, proprietary data, information requiring protection under the Privacy Act of 1974, and 
Government-developed privileged information involving the award of contracts. CUI is a categorical 
designation that refers to unclassified information that does not meet the standards for National Security 
Classification under Executive Order 13526, but is (a) pertinent to the national interest of the United States or 
to the important interests of entities outside the Federal Government, and (b) under law or policy requires 
protection from unauthorized disclosure, special handling safeguards, or prescribed limits on exchange or 
dissemination. 
 
7.3 Minimum Requirements for Access to Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) 
 
Access to CUI requires security clearance eligibility based on a Tier 3 Background Investigation. In addition, 
all contractor personnel performing work requiring privileged access on the OSF-CS must meet the 
requirements of the DoD Cyberspace Workforce Framework (DCWF) as outlined in DoD Manual 8140.03, 
holding valid baseline certifications (e.g., Security+, CASP+, or CISSP) and relevant OS/CE training. 
Contact for validation that employees have the required eligibility, prior to providing access to CUI. 
7.4 Minimum Protection Requirements for Controlled Unclassified Information 
 
Security classification guides and unclassified limited documents are not authorized for public release and 
cannot be posted on a publicly accessible webserver or transmitted over the Internet unless appropriately 
encrypted. 
 
7.5 CUI 
 
CUI must be marked, controlled and safeguarded in accordance with DoDI 5200.48, DoD Information 
Security Program: Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). 

 
 
7.6 Security of Unclassified DoD Information on Non-DoD Information Systems (DoDI 8582.01) 
7.6.1 DoD Policy 
Adequate security shall be provided for all unclassified DoD information on non-DoD 
information systems. 
7.6.2 Information Safeguards 
 
Unclassified DoD information that has not been cleared for public release may be 
disseminated by the Contractor, grantee, or awardee to the extent required to further the 
contract, grant, or agreement objectives, provided that the information is disseminated 
within the scope of assigned duties and with a clear expectation that confidentiality will be 
preserved. Examples include: 
 
(a) Non-public information provided to a Contractor (e.g., with a request for proposal). 
 
(b) Information developed during the course of a contract, grant, or other legal agreement (e.g., draft 
documents, reports, or briefings and deliverables). 
 
(c) Privileged information contained in transactions (e.g., privileged contract information, program 
schedules, contract-related event tracking). 
 
Note: It is recognized that adequate security will vary depending on the nature and sensitivity of the 
information on any given non-DoD information system. However, all unclassified DoD information in the 
possession or control of non-DoD entities on non-DoD information systems shall minimally be safeguarded as 
follows: 
 
(a) Do not process unclassified DoD information on publically available computers (e.g., those available 
for use by the general public in kiosks or hotel business centers). 
 
(b) Protect unclassified DoD information by at least one physical or electronic barrier (e.g., locked 
container or room, logical authentication or logon procedure) when not under direct individual 
control of an authorized user. 
 
(c) At a minimum, overwrite media that have been used to process unclassified DoD information before 
external release or disposal. 
 
(d) Encrypt all information that has been identified as CUI when it is stored on mobile computing 
devices such as laptops and personal digital assistants, compact disks, or authorized removable 
storage media such as thumb drives and compact disks, using the best encryption technology 
available to the Contractor or teaming partner. 
 
(e) Limit transfer of unclassified DoD information to subcontractors or teaming partners with a need to 
know and obtain a commitment from them to protect the information they receive to at least the same 
level of protection as that specified in the contract or other written agreement. 
 
(f) Transmit e-mail, text messages, and similar communications containing unclassified DoD 
information using technology and processes that provide the best level of privacy available, given 
facilities, conditions, and environment. Examples of recommended technologies or processes include 
closed networks, virtual private networks, public key-enabled encryption, and transport layer security 
(TLS). 

 
 
(g) Encrypt organizational wireless connection

ADAPT    Page | 1  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
U.S. Department of State (DOS) 
Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement (INL) 
 CFN  
 
 
Advanced Digital Analysis Platform and Technology 
ADAPT – Wiretapped Room 
(Digital Legal Interception System) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  


 
ADAPT    Page | 2  
 
PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT 
Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs (INL) 
Advanced Digital Analysis Platform and Technology 
FGR/UCTC ADAPT - Wiretap Room 
_____________________________________________________________________________ 
 
1.0  GENERAL 
 
The Contractor shall provide all labor, shipment services, materials, equipment, transportation, 
supervision, inventory, and all requirements necessary to accomplish the efforts described in this 
Performance Work Statement (PWS). 
2.0  BACKGROUND 
 
The Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs (INL) leads the Department 
of State’s efforts to combat international crime and counter narcotics. INL’s mission is to reduce 
the impact of transnational crime and illegal drugs on the United States, its citizens, and partner 
nations by delivering effective foreign assistance and promoting global cooperation. INL works 
closely with host nations to support stabilization efforts and strengthen their security institutions, 
infrastructure, and technological capabilities. 
 
3.0 OBJECTIVES 
Through binational collaboration, INL Mexico will provide hardware, specialized software, and 
training to enable Government of Mexico (GoM) law enforcement agencies to integrate digital 
intelligence and legally obtained communications into a unified data warehouse. This system 
will allow investigators to query, analyze, map, visualize, and report digital evidence in legally 
admissible formats to support criminal investigations and prosecutions. 
4.0  SCOPE  
The contractor shall design, supply, install, configure, and support a comprehensive Digital 
Legal Interception System for mobile communications  that complies with relevant international 
standards. The system shall enable the lawful interception, monitoring, analysis, and secure 
storage of communications data and be capable of integrating with multiple telecommunications 
providers. 
 
The contractor shall deliver all necessary hardware, software, network infrastructure, structured 
cabling (server to rack), storage solutions, software licenses, 140 workstations, current-
generation servers, and evidence recording systems. The contractor shall provide implementation 
services, comprehensive training, and a two-year warranty. The contractor shall also provide two 
years of maintenance and 24/7/365 technical support from the date of system acceptance.  
 
The system must be scalable, secure, reliable, and efficient. The system must produce output 
files in formats that are interoperable with the PLX platform used by other U.S. government 

 
ADAPT    Page | 3  
 
agencies to enable sharing digital evidence and intelligence between the Government of Mexico 
and U.S. agencies during joint criminal investigations and prosecutions. 
5.0 REQUIREMENTS  
5.1 The Contractor shall provide a Digital Legal Interception System for Mobile 
Communications, including all necessary hardware, software, and specialized labor, that meets 
the following requirements: 
5.1.1 User Capacity. The system must support at least 140 simultaneous users with 
access to the platform. 
5.1.2 Analysis and Monitoring. The system shall include a dedicated data analysis 
and exploitation software for monitoring and analysis, to be operated from a 
Monitoring Center. 
5.1.3 Legal Interception Standards. The system shall support lawful interception in 
accordance with relevant international standards and shall be capable of 
receiving digital information from multiple service providers, in compliance 
with applicable international legal standards and technical frameworks, 
including but not limited to ETSI, 3GPP, CALEA, and ATIS. 
5.1.4 Target Configuration. The system shall support configuration of up to 1,500 
targets using 3G, 4G, 5G, and future generation technologies, for voice, SMS 
text messages, MMS multimedia messages, and data communications. 
5.1.5 Concurrent Call Recording. The system shall be capable of intercepting and 
recording two hundred (200) concurrent calls.  
5.1.6 Server Requirements. The system shall operate with current-generation servers. 
5.1.7 Data Storage. The system shall provide storage for all communications and 
information processed on the platform for a period of 365 days, using a Storage 
Area Network (SAN) solution. 
5.1.8 Provider Integration. The system shall be capable of interacting and integrating 
with other telecommunications providers, including concessionaires, Mobile 
Virtual Network Operators (MVNOs), and providers of convergent services or 
other legal interception technologies, such as R2 MFC. 
5.1.9 Scalability. The system shall be scalable to accommodate future requirements. 
The platform shall support expansion of processing and storage capacity and the 
incorporation of new network elements and information sources. 
 
5.2 The contractor shall provide active network components; provision of routers, switches, and 
firewalls to support the Digital Legal Interception System, including appropriate security 
mechanisms. 
 
5.3 The contractor shall provide 140 workstations. Each workstation shall include: a desktop 
computer, latest -generation CPU, desktop computer with at least 32 GB RAM, a 512 GB solid-
state drive (SSD), and an Intel® Core™ Ultra 5 235T processor (13 TOPS NPU, 14 cores, up to 
5.0 GHz),  24-inch dual monitor, one Spanish-language keyboard, and one mouse. In addition, 
the contractor shall provide 200 high-fidelity wired headsets. 
 
5.4 The contractor shall provide structured cabling installation from servers to rack. The 
contractor shall supply and provide installation of cabling for 140 workstation connections. 

 
ADAPT    Page | 4  
 
 
5.5 The contractor shall provide evidence recording system: Provision of a system for recording 
evidence to disk (CD/DVD/BR). Contractor shall consider to include four tower units with three 
drives each, or a technically superior arrangement to meet this requirement. 
 
5.6 The contractor shall provide all required perpetual licenses for the technological platform for 
legal interception of private communications, including operating systems, storage equipment, 
telecommunications, and security.  
 
5.7 The contractor shall configure all hardware and software in accordance with the integrated 
system solution to be delivered. 
 
5.8 The contractor shall perform implementation services such as supply, installation, 
configuration, commissioning, functional testing, and operation of the Legal Interception 
Platform. The contractor shall provide continuous technical support, assistance with system 
configuration, and guidance during validation testing to ensure that the platform operates 
according to the established requirements. The contractor shall guarantee the operation of this 
platform between UCTC and various concessionaires. 
 
5.8.1 The contractor shall perform connectivity tests with the concessionaires to 
establish and verify the interconnection of the Digital Legal Interception System 
with each concessionaire. This process shall include, but not be limited to, 
configuring connection parameters, verifying interoperability, validating data 
exchange, and conducting functional tests.  
 5.8.2 The contractor shall provide technical support on infrastructure matters in 
coordination with the technical teams of each operator. This support shall 
include analyzing connectivity requirements, defining interconnection 
parameters, reviewing the available network infrastructure, and assisting in 
configuring the elements necessary to establish secure and reliable 
communication between the systems. These activities shall ensure that 
integration with each concessionaire operates correctly and in accordance with 
the established requirements. 
 
5.9 The Contractor shall acquire, ship, transport, deliver, and inventory all items to comply with 
the requirements listed in the Appendix A – Equipment and Software List with Training 
Requirements to the location provided in Section 7.2, of this document.  All items SHALL be 
new and meet or exceed the minimum specifications. 
 
5.10 As part of project acceptance, the contractor is required to provide built documentation, 
configuration baselines, and complete administrative credential handover. 
 
5.8 The Contractor shall conduct training listed in Appendix A – Equipment /Software List & 
Training Requirements. 
 
5.9 The Contractor must wait to receive INL written confirmation before delivering training. 
 
5.10 NOTE: All participants must have current and valid vetting at the time of the training. The 
program will manage the vetting process for GoM participants. The Contractor shall receive the 

 
ADAPT    Page | 5  
 
list of vetted participants prior to the start of training. Training is strictly prohibited for non-
vetted participants.  
 
5.11 Proposal Requirements: Implementation Plan and Technical Details 
 
As part of the proposal, the contractor shall provide: 
• A written Implementation and Installation Plan for the GOM-DIGITAL LEGAL 
INTERCEPTION SYSTEM. The plan shall: (1) describe the installation approach, 
sequence of activities, dependencies, and expected installation timeline; (2) include a 
detailed list of all hardware, software, and network components; (3) provide timelines for 
the supply, installation, configuration, commissioning, and functional testing of the 
system to be delivered; (4) describe how the contractor will perform all necessary 
software and hardware adjustments for commissioning; (5) include a description of the 
database engine that will be used to store the application’s information, including version 
and key technical characteristics; and (6) include a description of the router(s) and 
firewall(s) that will be used as security mechanisms for connectivity with each 
Concessionaire in the construction of the VPN, including main technical specifications 
and security capabilities. 
• A detailed cost breakdown, at a minimum disaggregated into the following categories: 
Hardware, software and training. 
• Appendix A – Equipment and Software List with Training Requirements is provided as a 
baseline for ADAPT. The contractor shall validate delivery requirements and propose 
alternatives or improvements to its proposal. 
 
6.0 WARRANTY, MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT  
 
6.1 In-Country Warranty 
  
For all Digital Legal Interception System delivered under this request, the contractor shall 
provide a two (2) year in-country warranty valid and applicable in Mexico. The warranty period 
shall commence upon delivery and acceptance of each system by the Government of Mexico. 
The contractor shall also provide maintenance and 24x7x365 mission‑critical technical support 
in Spanish for a period of two (2) years from delivery and acceptance. 
 
6.2 Maintenance and Technical Support – General 
 
The contractor shall provide maintenance and technical support in Mexico for all Digital Legal 
Interception System delivered under this request to ensure their correct operation, availability, 
and performance. 
 
6.3 Scope of Maintenance and Technical Support 
 
Maintenance and technical support shall include, but not be limited to, the following: 
 
• Continuous technical support 24 hours per day, 365 days per year (24x7x365) through a 
team of technical specialists and established support channels. 

 
ADAPT    Page | 6  
 
• Specialized technical support to address and resolve incidents or inquiries related to 
system operation. 
• Diagnosis and resolution of failures at the software level and in components associated 
with the system. 
• Software updates and patches to keep the platform secure, stable, and aligned with 
manufacturer improvements. 
• Technical advice and operational support to ensure correct system functioning. 
• Assistance with configuration activities and minor adjustments necessary to maintain 
service continuity. 
• Continuous follow‑up on reported incidents, prioritizing those that may affect system 
operation, with the goal of restoring service as quickly as possible and ensuring the 
availability and stability of the platform. 
 
6.4 Designated Technical Support Team 
 
The contractor shall provide a designated technical support team to ensure timely attention to and 
follow‑up on technical requirements, in order to maintain stable operation of the GOM-Digital 
Legal Interception Systems delivered. 
 
6.5 Proposal Requirement: Warranty, Maintenance, and Support Plan 
 
As part of its proposal, the contractor shall include: 
 
• A Warranty, Maintenance, and Support Plan that specifies at a minimum: The scope of 
the warranty, including covered items and exclusions; and specific response and 
resolution times for maintenance and technical support services. 
7.0 PLACE OF PERFORMANCE AND DELIVERY 
 
7.1 No item can be delivered at destination without previous authorization and coordination with 
INL Mexico Logistics, and/or INL Program/GTM/COR. Contractor must wait to receive INL 
confirmation before delivering equipment. Once the Contractor gets written approval, a specific 
delivery date will be established. Any action taken from contractor without writing confirmation 
will be considered under clause 9 Nonpayment for unauthorized work. 
 
7.2 All equipment/hardware under this contract shall be delivered to INL at INL warehouse in 
Brownsville as follows: 
INL Warehouse 
225 South Vermillion Rd., Brownsville, TX., 78521 
POC TBD 
 
7.3 The contractor shall ensure all items are prepared for safe transportation once confirmation is 
received. The Contractor shall replace lost or damaged items during transportation and/or 
unloading. 
 
7.4 Partial deliveries are not allowed. The contractor’s personnel must be present at the time of 
delivery to conduct the inventory of all hardware required for ADAPT project (listed in 
Appendix A), in coordination and in presence of INL Logistics or INL COR/GTM/Program.  

 
ADAPT    Page | 7  
 
 
7.5 All delivery information, including the packing list and a Technical Specifications/Data sheet 
of all equipment shall be forwarded to INL Program/COR/GTM and INL Mexico Logistics 
(MexicoCityINLLogistics@state.gov) two (2) weeks in advance of delivery to the delivery 
location detailed in section 7.2. The packing list shall include but is not limited to: Item 
Description, Name of Manufacturer, Model Number, Serial Numbers, Delivered Quantity, Unit 
Price, Extended Price, and Warranty Expiration Date for all hardware. Upon final delivery at 
Brownsville, the contractor shall provide detailed equipment specifications (including part 
numbers) wit

Notice of Intent to Sole Source 
 
The Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences (USU) is the Nation's federal health 
sciences university and is committed to excellence in military medicine and public health during 
peace and war. We provide the Nation with health professionals dedicated to career service in the 
Department of War and the United States Public Health Service and with scientists who serve the 
common good. We serve the uniformed services and the Nation as an outstanding academic 
health sciences center with a worldwide perspective for education, research, service, and 
consultation; we are unique in relating these activities to military medicine, disaster medicine, 
and military medical readiness. USU is located in Bethesda, MD on the grounds of the Naval 
Support Activity Bethesda. 
 
The mission of the USU is to provide the highest quality education programs in the health 
sciences to those selected individuals who demonstrate dedication to a health profession career in 
the Uniformed Services. 
 
Intended Recipient: Kuali Inc. (Kuali), 3300 N. Ashton Blvd Ste 230, Lehi, Utah 84048-5351 
 
Intent to Sole-Source:  
 
USU intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract with a base year and four option 
years to Kuali for Research Administration System (RAS) software licenses, data migration, and 
technical support.   
 
Sole Source Justification 
 
This requirement is a continuation of work performed to implement an enterprise-level RAS to 
manage the lifecycle of research projects from application to close-out. Kuali is currently 
working this requirement as a subcontractor via U.S. Office of Personnel Management,  USA 
Learning task order 47QACA25F0297 with Oakland Consulting Group, Inc. as the prime 
contractor. The current task order ends September 23, 2026. USUHS will award subsequent 
contracts for this requirement. Kuali is the only contractor capable of meeting agency 
requirements given the previous work accomplished for the RAS and the impracticability of 
contracting for a new RAS. This requirement will be procured in accordance with the procedures 
of FAR Part 13.106-1(b)(1)(i).  
In accordance with 5.207(c)(16)(i), all responsible sources may submit a bid, proposal, or 
quotation which shall be considered by the agency. Responses to this notice must demonstrate 
clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government, 
would not be cost or time prohibitive, and that the interested potential Offeror can meet the 
needs of the Government as stated above. Information received will be considered for the 
purposes of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The Government will 
not be responsible for any costs incurred by responding to this notice. 
Responses must be received via email to the contact listed in the notice by the closing date 
of the notice.

DESCRIPTION 
The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Officer (NCO 01) located in Brockton, MA 
intends to enter into a sole source procurement, pursuant to the authority of FAR 6.302-1, with VLOGIC 
SYSTEMS, Inc for the following requirement: 
 
STATEMENT OF WORK 
Facilities Drawing, Space Data, and Capital Asset Inventory Maintenance Services 
VA Boston Healthcare System 
1. Background 
VA Boston Healthcare System (VABHS) maintains an existing digital repository of architectural floor 
plans, room and space attributes, and Capital Asset Inventory (CAI) information for its medical centers 
and outpatient clinics. Construction projects and in-house renovations continuously change room layouts, 
doors, walls, counters, fixed equipment, departmental assignments, and other space information. The 
Government requires recurring professional and technical services to keep the authoritative drawing and 
space-data repository current and usable for facility planning, project development, space management, 
emergency planning, and capital asset reporting. 
The primary purpose of this requirement is the recurring professional and technical maintenance of VA 
facility drawings and associated room, space, and Capital Asset Inventory data. Continued access to and 
maintenance within the existing contractor-hosted repository is an integral supporting component of the 
services because completed drawing and data updates must be synchronized, revision-controlled, 
published, and made retrievable within the VA’s current production environment. The requirement does 
not include development or implementation of a new software system or acquisition of a Government-
owned stand-alone software product. 
2. Objective 
The objective is to maintain accurate, current, and retrievable facility floor plans and associated room, 
space, and CAI data for all covered VABHS locations, including incorporation of changes resulting from 
completed construction projects, maintenance alterations, and in-house renovations. 
3. Scope 
The Contractor shall provide all management, labor, professional drafting expertise, field-verification 
capability, quality control, secure hosted repository access, and other resources necessary to maintain the 
existing VABHS drawing and space-data repository. Work shall be initiated and prioritized by the 
Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) through Government-provided redlines, record drawings, 
project closeout documents, written space-data changes, or requests for field verification. 
The Contractor shall not make independent design decisions or certify design compliance. When source 
information is incomplete or contradictory, the Contractor shall identify the discrepancy and obtain 
written COR direction before finalizing the affected record. 

Special Notice 
 Special Notice 
 
Page 3 of 7 
 
4. Specific Tasks 
4.1 Repository Validation and Transition 
• Within 30 calendar days after award, review the existing drawing and data repository and provide an 
inventory identifying each covered site, building, floor, available native drawing file, current PDF, and 
associated room/space data set. 
• Confirm Government user access and establish a controlled method for the COR and designated staff to 
submit source files, redlines, and requested changes and to retrieve completed deliverables. 
• Identify missing, corrupted, duplicate, or conflicting records and provide a recommended resolution list 
to the COR. The Contractor shall not delete or supersede a Government record without COR approval. 
4.2 Architectural Floor Plan and Drawing Updates 
• Update existing architectural floor plans to incorporate changes documented by VA-approved redlines, 
record drawings, as-built drawings, project closeout documents, or written COR direction after 
completion of construction projects or in-house renovations. 
• Maintain room boundaries, room numbers, wall and opening locations, doors and door swings, columns, 
windows, fixed counters, sinks, major architectural jogs, and other elements needed for accurate space 
plans. 
• Maintain drawing layers, symbols, naming conventions, room-polylines, and file structure in accordance 
with applicable VA drawing standards and the conventions of the existing repository. 
• For each completed request, provide the updated native drawing file and a searchable PDF, update the 
hosted repository, and record the source, date, preparer, and description of the revision in a revision log. 
• Routine maintenance includes updates to existing drawings. Creation of a complete new building 
drawing set, design services, construction documents, or a full-campus re-baseline survey is outside the 
recurring scope unless expressly included by contract modification or a separately priced line item. 
4.3 Field Verification 
• When directed by the COR, perform non-destructive onsite verification to reconcile existing floor plans 
with observed conditions. 
• Field verification may include room dimensions; wall and column locations; doors and door swings; 
window locations; counters; sinks; fixed architectural elements; room numbers; room descriptions; 
organizational assignment; space function; CAI space driver; and available workstation count. Occupancy 
or patient information shall not be collected. 
• Document unresolved conditions and assumptions and obtain COR direction before final record updates. 
Field work shall not disrupt patient care or facility operations. 
• Unless a separate travel line item is established, all travel necessary to perform directed onsite work 
shall be included in the applicable fixed price. 

Special Notice 
 Special Notice 
 
Page 4 of 7 
 
4.4 Space and Capital Asset Inventory Data Maintenance 
• Update room and space attributes supplied or approved by the VA, including room number, room 
name/description, space function, service or department assignment, cost center when provided, CAI 
space driver, and available workstation count. 
• Synchronize room polygons and related database records with the current floor plan. The Contractor 
shall not infer an organizational assignment, space function, or CAI value when Government direction is 
not clear. 
• Provide standard reports or exports of room, space, and CAI records at COR request. 
4.5 Secure Web Portal and Repository Access (Ancillary to the Services) 
• Provide designated VA users with secure web-based access throughout the period of performance to 
submit source documents, review work in progress when available, and retrieve current drawings and 
approved data exports. 
• The hosted environment shall maintain a current FedRAMP authorization at Low impact or higher, or 
another authorization level accepted in writing by the VA. FedRAMP status does not, by itself, replace 
any VA authorization-to-use, security review, or contract security requirement. 
• No Contractor-owned device shall connect to the VA internal trusted network unless separately 
authorized in writing. No protected health information, patient information, or other data outside the 
approved system boundary shall be uploaded to the hosted repository. 
• Provide role-based access, user account administration, revision history, and secure transfer of files 
using Government-approved methods. 
4.6 Work Request Management and Quality Control 
• Acknowledge each COR work request within two business days. 
• Within five business days after receipt of complete source information, provide the COR an estimated 
completion date. Completion dates shall be based on the complexity and volume of the requested update 
and shall be subject to COR approval. 
• Perform an independent quality-control review before release. Quality control shall verify geometry, 
room numbering, layer use, file opening, PDF legibility, database synchronization, and consistency with 
the Government-approved source information. 
• Correct Contractor-caused errors at no additional cost within five business days after notification, or 
within another period approved by the COR based on complexity. 
4.7 Training and User Support 
• Provide remote orientation and refresher training for designated VA users on file submission, drawing 
retrieval, standard reports/exports, and user administration functions applicable to the hosted repository.

 Special Notice

questions during normal business hours.

6. Government-Furnished Information and Government Responsibilities 
• Provide available CAD files, PDFs, record drawings, redlines, project closeout documents, and written 
data changes needed to perform each request. 
• Identify the COR and designated Government users; establish request priorities; approve schedules; 
resolve discrepancies; and provide timely review and acceptance decisions. 
• Provide coordinated site access, escorts when required, and facility points of contact for approved field-
verification visits. 
• No Government-furnished equipment is anticipated. Government-furnished information remains 
Government property and shall be protected from unauthorized use or disclosure. 
7. Inspection and Acceptance 

Special Notice 
 Special Notice 
 
Page 6 of 7 
The COR will inspect deliverables for conformity with the approved source information, legibility, file 
functionality, repository synchronization, and completion of the required revision record. Acceptance will 
be documented by email or within the Government's contract administration system. Deliverables 
containing material errors or omissions may be rejected and shall be corrected at no additional cost. 
8. Data Ownership, Portability, and Records 
All VA-furnished drawings and data, and all updated drawings, metadata, room/space/CAI records, 
revision logs, and exports produced under this contract, are Government records. The Contractor shall not 
restrict Government access to or reuse of these records. 
9. Places of Performance 
Remote work may be performed from the Contractor's facilities. Onsite work, when directed, may occur 
at the following VABHS locations: 
• Brockton VA Medical Center, 940 Belmont Street, Brockton, MA 02301-5596. 
• Jamaica Plain VA Medical Center, 150 South Huntington Avenue, Boston, MA 02130-4817. 
• West Roxbury VA Medical Center, 1400 VFW Parkway, West Roxbury, MA 02132-4927. 
• Causeway VA Clinic, 251 Causeway Street, Boston, MA 02114. 
• Framingham VA Clinic, 61 Lincoln Street, Suite 112, Framingham, MA 01702-8264. 
• Lowell VA Clinic, 130 Marshall Road, Lowell, MA 01852-5130. 
• Plymouth VA Clinic, 116 Long Pond Road, Plymouth, MA 02360-2663. 
• Quincy VA Clinic, 110 West Squantum Street, Quincy, MA 02171-2122. 
10. Hours, Site Access, and Conduct 
Normal Government hours are Monday through Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time, excluding 
Federal holidays. The Contractor shall provide at least three business days advance notice for planned 
onsite visits. Work outside normal hours requires COR approval and at least five business days advance 
notice unless an emergency schedule is authorized. 
Contractor personnel shall check in as directed, wear visible identification, obtain visitor badges, park 
only in designated areas, comply with VHA smoke-free requirements, and follow all applicable Federal, 
State, local, VA safety, fire, security, and conduct requirements. Contractor personnel shall be escorted 
where required and shall not possess weapons or contraband on VA property. 
11. Security and Privacy 
The Contractor shall comply with the security, privacy, records-management, and incident-reporting 
requirements incorporated into the contract. The Contractor shall immediately report any suspected loss, 
unauthorized disclosure, or compromise of VA drawings, files, credentials, or data to the COR and 
Contracting Officer. No patient contact is anticipated, and no protected health information or personally 
identifiable patient information is required for performance. 

Special Notice 
 Special Notice 
 
Page 7 of 7 
12. Contractor Personnel and Program Management 
The Contractor shall designate a Program Manager with authority to manage daily performance and 
coordinate with the COR. Personnel performing drawing updates shall have demonstrated experience 
with CAD-based architectural floor plans, room-polygons, space-data maintenance, and quality control. 
Personnel performing onsite work shall be capable of accurate non-destructive field measurement in 
occupied healthcare facilities. 
13. Safety and Insurance 
The Contractor shall provide all necessary tools and personal protective equipment and shall protect 
personnel and property during performance. The Contractor shall report injuries and property damage 
immediately.

☐52.225-8 Duty-Free Entry (OCT 2010) 
 
(a) Definition. "Customs territory of the United States" means the States, the District of Columbia, and Puerto 
Rico. 
 
(b) Except as otherwise approved by the Contracting Officer, the Contractor shall not include in the contract 
price any amount for duties on supplies specifically identified in the Schedule to be accorded duty-free entry. 
 
(c) Except as provided in paragraph (d) of this clause or elsewhere in this contract, the following procedures 
apply to supplies not identified in the Schedule to be accorded duty-free entry: 
 
(1) The Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer in writing of any purchase of foreign supplies 
(including, without limitation, raw materials, components, and intermediate assemblies) in excess of 
$20,000 that are to be imported into the customs territory of the United States for delivery to the 
Government under this contract, either as end products or for incorporation into end products. The 
Contractor shall furnish the notice to the Contracting Officer at least 20 calendar days before the 
importation. The notice shall identify the- 
 
(i) Foreign supplies; 
(ii) Estimated amount of duty; and

(2) The Contracting Officer will determine whether any of these supplies should be accorded duty-free 
entry and will notify the Contractor within 10 calendar days after receipt of the Contractor’s notification. 
 
(3) Except as otherwise approved by the Contracting Officer, the contract price shall be reduced by (or 
the allowable cost shall not include) the amount of duty that would be payable if the supplies were not 
entered duty-free. 
 
(d) The Contractor is not required to provide the notification under paragraph (c) of this clause for purchases of 
foreign supplies if- 
 
(1) The supplies are identical in nature to items purchased by the Contractor or any subcontractor in 
connection with its commercial business; and 
 
(2) Segregation of these supplies to ensure use only on Government contracts containing duty-free entry 
provisions is not economical or feasible. 
 
(e) The Contractor shall claim duty-free entry only for supplies to be delivered to the Government under this 
contract, either as end products or incorporated into end products, and shall pay duty on supplies, or any portion 
of them, other than scrap, salvage, or competitive sale authorized by the Contracting Officer, diverted to 
nongovernmental use. 
 
(f) The Government will execute any required duty-free entry certificates for supplies to be accorded duty-free 
entry and will assist the Contractor in obtaining duty-free entry for these supplies. 
 
(g) Shipping documents for supplies to be accorded duty-free entry shall consign the shipments to the 
contracting agency in care of the Contractor and shall include the- 
 
(1) Delivery address of the Contractor (or contracting agency, if appropriate); 
 
(2) Government prime contract number; 
 
(3) Identification of carrier; 
 
(4) Notation "UNITED STATES GOVERNMENT, _____ [agency] _____, Duty-free entry to be 
claimed pursuant to Item No(s) _____ [from Tariff Schedules] _____, Harmonized Tariff Schedules of 
the United States. Upon arrival of shipment at port of entry, District Director of Customs, please release 
shipment under 19 CFR part 142 and notify [cognizant contract administration office] for execution of 
Customs Forms 7501 and 7501-A and any required duty-free entry certificates."; 
 
(5) Gross weight in pounds (if freight is based on space tonnage, state cubic feet in addition to gross 
shipping weight); and 
 
(6) Estimated value in United States dollars. 
 
(h) The Contractor shall instruct the foreign supplier to- 
 
(1) Consign the shipment as specified in paragraph (g) of this clause; 

 
6   V12 APR 2026 
 
 
(2) Mark all packages with the words "UNITED STATES GOVERNMENT" and the title of the 
contracting agency; and 
 
(3) Include with the shipment at least two copies of the bill of lading (or other shipping document) for 
use by the District Director of Customs at the port of entry. 
 
(i) The Contractor shall provide written notice to the cognizant contract administration office immediately after 
notification by the Contracting Officer that duty-free entry will be accorded foreign supplies or, for duty-free 
supplies identified in the Schedule, upon award by the Contractor to the overseas supplier. The notice shall 
identify the- 
 
(1) Foreign supplies; 
 
(2) Country of origin; 
 
(3) Contract number; and 
 
(4) Scheduled delivery date(s). 
 
(j) The Contractor shall include the substance of this clause in any subcontract if-

territory of the United States; or 
 
(2) Other foreign supplies in excess of $20,000 may be imported into the customs territory of the United

1. Contracting Activity:  Department of Veterans Affairs (VA)

2. Description of Action: The VA Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) 8, 
Miami VA Health Care System (Bruce W. Carter VA Medical Center and William 
The Miami 
VA Healthcare System is requesting a sole source firm-fixed price contract 
consisting of a 12-month base period with three(3) 12-month option periods for 
Minuteman Technology Services LLC, 100 Garden Street, Cambridge, MA 02138-
1418, to provide a unified digital wayfinding ecosystem that serves visitors, patients, 
and staff across two channels: interactive kiosks and mobile Blue Dot indoor 
meet Section 508 accessibility (Accessibility routing aligns to ADA/ABA scoping & 
technical provisions for accessible routes and signage), and avoid collection of 
Personal Healthcare Information. Blue Dot will launch with a staged/limited pilot in 
priority areas, while kiosks provide robust, text-first directions immediately. The 
contractor shall furnish all labor, materials, equipment, and project management 
necessary to develop an ADA
compliant, standardized wayfinding system that aligns 
with VA branding and environmental standards. 
 
3. Description of Supplies or Services: The requirement is for comprehensive 
wayfinding supplies and services, including the design, fabrication, and installation of 
interior and exterior signage, maps, directional markers, and related communication 
elements. These supplies and services support a standardized, ADA compliant 
wayfinding system across the facility(ies). 
 
The intended use is to improve navigation for patients, visitors, and staff, reduce 
confusion, enhance the overall customer experience, and support efficient 
movement throughout the campus. The updated wayfinding system will ensure 
clear, consistent, and accessible directions, contributing to better operational flow 
and reduced staff time spent providing directions. The total estimated value of the 
proposed action is , including all option periods. 
 
4. Statutory Authority: The statutory authority permitting other than full and open 
 Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul VA 
deviation 6.103-5(b)(1). For this action, 38 U.S.C. 8127(c), known as the Veterans 
First Contracting Program provides the authority to directly contract with a Service-
Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) or a Veteran-Owned Small 
Business (VOSB), see FAR 19.106-3 and VAAR 819.7008.   


Miami VA Wayfinding Patient Navigation System VA-26-00070397
Page 2 of 3 
5. Rationale Supporting Use of Authority Cited Above: The proposed source for this 
acquisition is, MINUTEMAN, LLC 100 Garden Street, Cambridge Massachusetts 
02138-1418. MINUTEMAN is a certified SDVOSB and is technically qualified for 
comprehensive wayfinding supplies and services, including the design, fabrication, 
and installation of interior and exterior signage, maps, directional markers, and 
related communication elements. In accordance with VAAR 819.7008(a), the 
anticipated award price of the contract (including options) will not exceed $5 million, 
the requirement will be synopsized and the required justification posted in 
accordance with FAR Part 5, the SDVOSB will be determined a responsible 
contractor with respect to performance prior to award and in the estimation of the 
Contracting Officer award can be made at a fair and reasonable price that offers 
best value to the Government.  
 
6. Efforts to Obtain Competition: Market research was conducted, details of which 
are in the market research section of this document. Consistent with the guidelines 
of the Veterans First Contracting Program, the proposed action described herein will 
be synopsized on the Contracting Opportunities Page in accordance with FAR Part 
5. 
 
7. Actions to Increase Competition: The Government will continue to conduct market 
research to ascertain if there are changes in the marketplace that would enable 
future actions to be competed. 
 
8. Market Research: Market Research was conducted in 2026 through reviews of 
leading wayfinding providers, including vendors specializing in healthcare, 
transportation and large campus navigation systems. These reviews were conducted 
through gathering available public product information, technical spec sheets and 
reviews of conducted case studies to understand functionality, durability, 
accessibility and compliance with ADA and VA requirements. While multiple 
wayfinding solutions were identified, VA identified one SDVOSB provider that can 
determination that only one SDVOSB can meet the requirement is not required.  
 
The VetCert SBA database was accessed on June 15, 2026. This search 
concluded that MINUTEMAN, LLC is registered and certified and qualifies as a 
SDVOSB in accordance with the federal small business size standard for the 
applicable North American Industry Classification System Code (cite NAICS code 
for the acquisition). It was verified on June 25, 2026 that MINUTEMAN, LLC is 
registered in the Central Contractor Registration database and is eligible to 
receive Government contracts.  
 
9. Other Facts: The Contracting Officer has determined that this proposed action 
meets all the requirements of 38 U.S.C. 8127(c). This acquisition is below the 
$5,000,000.00 threshold, MINUTEMAN, LLC is a responsible SDVOSB for 
performance of the services described herein, and the proposed contract can be 
awarded at a fair and reasonable price.

The VA Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) 8, Miami VA Health Care System (Bruce W. The Miami VA Healthcare System is requesting a sole source firm-fixed price contract consisting of a 12-month base period with three (3) 12-month option periods for Minuteman Technology Services LLC, 100 Garden Street, Cambridge, MA 02138-1418, to provide a unified digital wayfinding ecosystem that serves visitors, patients, and staff across two channels: interactive kiosks and mobile Blue Dot indoor navigation. The solution will prioritize English and Spanish for Miami’s community, meet Section 508 accessibility (Accessibility routing aligns to ADA/ABA scoping & technical provisions for accessible routes and signage), and avoid collection of Personal Healthcare Information. offered products or services to the Government in the performance of any contract, subcontract, or other

Equipment or Services—Representation, or in paragraph (v)(2)(i) of the provision at 52.212–3, Offeror 
Representations and Certifications–Commercial Products and Commercial Services. The Offeror shall not 
complete the representation in paragraph (d)(2) of this provision if the Offeror has represented that it 
‘‘does not use covered telecommunications equipment or services, or any equipment, system, or service 
that uses covered telecommunications equipment or services’’ in paragraph (c)(2) of the provision at 
52.204–26, or in paragraph (v)(2)(ii) of the provision at 52.212–3. 
  (a) Definitions. As used in this provision— 
  Backhaul, covered telecommunications equipment or services, critical technology, interconnection 
arrangements, reasonable inquiry, roaming, and substantial or essential component have the meanings 
provided in the clause 52.204–25, Prohibition on Contracting for Certain Telecommunications and Video 
Surveillance Services or Equipment. 
  (b) Prohibition. (1) Section 889(a)(1)(A) of the John S. McCain National Defense Authorization Act for 
Fiscal Year 2019 (Pub. L. 115–232) prohibits the head of an executive agency on or after August 13, 
2019, from procuring or obtaining, or extending or renewing a contract to procure or obtain, any

Statement of Objectives 
United States Army Aviation Center of Excellence (AVCOE) SIPR VTC Lifecycle Replacement 
 
1. Purpose. The United States Army Aviation Center of Excellence has identified a need to 
modernize its classified (SIPR) Video Teleconference (VTC) systems. 
2. Scope. The United States Army Aviation Center of Excellence has a requirement to upgrade 
three (3) room and three (3) desktop SIPR VTC (SVTC) systems and workspaces in Building 101 located 
on Fort Rucker, Alabama. For the room systems, in addition to providing equipment, the contractor will 
install ceiling speakers and microphones integrated with the room. 
3. Period and Place of Performance. The Period of Performance is to be determined upon selection 
of an acceptable proposal. The place of performance is 2218 6th Ave, Fort Rucker, AL 36362. 
4. Background. The existing SVTC systems were installed over 6 years ago and are past the 
recommended life cycle replacement dates. Due to age, wear and tear, and advances in technology, 
they are no longer reliable or sufficient for their intended purposes.  
5. Performance Objectives, Goals, and Outcomes. The contractor shall provide all personnel, 
equipment, supplies, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal 
services necessary to perform the technology refresh as defined in the final approved Statement of 
Work or Performance Work Statement. 
5.1 Technical Objectives: 
• All equipment must be approved for use with IL6 (SIPR) DoWIN environments. 
• All equipment must be TAA compliant, where possible. 
• Contractor will ensure end of life of equipment will not occur until 5 years after 
acceptance of task order.  
• Contractor will program a functioning system that provides ease of use and exceptional 
user experience.  
• Contractor will support the new SVTC system with a five (5) year Warranty/Service Plan. 
• All programming of control systems to be provided by the Contractor. 
• Any specific hardware called out shall be brand name or equal to that component. It’s 
up to the Government’s discretion to approve/disapprove any components that deviate 
from the proposal due to operability/use ability. 
• All cabling must be new. No existing cable will be provided or used in this project.  
• All existing equipment and existing cables must be removed and returned to the 
Government. 
• Training in basic usage and troubleshooting of all equipment and devices must be 
provided.  

 
 
• All audio speaker outputs for room systems will have sound threshold control level 
implementation. 
• All audio speaker outputs and inputs for room systems will be ceiling mounted (recessed 
if possible) and microphones have visible lighting to show when active/inactive (ex: 
Green = mic active/Red = mic inactive)  
• 5% audio startup setting required to reduce noise pollution when starting up systems 
• Information Assurance Requirements.  
• All technicians must be US citizens and able to gain access to military 
installations. 
• All configured AV equipment must meet NIST 800-53, Army Regulation 25-2 
(Army Cybersecurity) requirements, and be certified by DISA JITC for operation 
within classified environments up to Secret. 
• Real Property Modification.   
• The Contractor shall include with their pricing any additional alteration or 
modification to government facilities required for each area and piece of 
equipment. 
• Any technical solution requiring alteration of or modification to Government 
facilities or property, to include trenching, must be approved by the 
Government. The government will coordinate these actions with DPW.  
• The Contractor must also include all structural requirements in support of 
mounting display to the existing wall, cabling routes, etc. Include detail that 
describes what the added power will be for. For example: The wall monitors 
require (x each outlet 115V), Rack mounted hardware will require (x number of 
xx Volt outlets, dedicated not dedicated etc.) The electrical changes will need to 
be redlined on the building electrical drawings (Government shall provide 
drawings, Contractor shall make changes) any electrical adds or changes will 
also require technical approval by the installation DPW. The Contractor is 
expected to direct all pertinent questions to the government lead regarding 
electrical or structural support. The Contractor will also be responsible for repair 
of walls to include patching and painting for any of the following reasons: walls 
damaged during installation, removal of equipment that leaves holes or exposed 
cutouts that are no longer used. AV Integrator is also responsible for 
replacement of ceilings tiles if required but not limited to speaker and 
microphone installation.  
• The project is considered complete when all deliverables have been met, training has 
been conducted, all systems are 100% updated, functional, any required documentation 
delivered, and the government lead signs acceptance documentation provided by the 
Contractor.  

 
 
 
5.2 WARRANTY 
• Provide warranty repair or replacement for 5 Years on all products provided by the 
Contractor (including products having a manufacturer’s warranty of less than 90 days) 
and all integrator workmanship at no additional cost, except in case of obvious abuse. 
Consumable items such as lamps, batteries, tapes, etc. are not covered. 
• The warranty period will commence no sooner than the date of first beneficial use by 
the Government and no later than the date of contract closeout. 
• The Contractor shall perform all warranty work at times that are convenient to the 
Government (0800-1600 CST). 
• Any parts replaced due to warranty work must be documented with serial number swap 
and provided back to the Government.

Responses: Due by 10:00AM EDT on Wednesday, August 12th, 2026. Please submit 
any questions through the SAM portal by Monday August 10th, 2026 by 10:00AM EDT. 
 
PLEASE NOTE: This Sources Sought Notice is specifically intended to identify potential 
small business sources capable of meeting the Statement of Objectives (SOO) in its 
entirety - both the service portion and supply portion. The service portion of this 
requirement will take place at Fort Rucker, AL. 
This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes – it does not 
constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ), Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid 
(IFB) nor a promise to issue an RFQ, RFP or IFB in the future. This notice does not 
commit the U.S Government to contract for any supply or service. Further, the U.S. 
Government is not seeking quotes, bids or proposals at this time and will not accept 
unsolicited proposals in response to this SSN. The U.S. Government will not pay for any 
information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. Submittals will not 
be returned to the responder. Not responding to this SSN does not preclude 
participation in any future RFQ, RFP or IFB if any are issued. Any information submitted 
by respondents is strictly voluntary. 
Program Overview 
The United States Army Aviation Center of Excellence (USAACE), headquartered at 
Fort Rucker, Alabama, serves as the primary command staff directing all Army Aviation 
policy, doctrine, and force modernization. As the sole producer of Army aviators, 
maintainers, and air traffic controllers, USAACE is responsible for delivering 
comprehensive initial and advanced flight training across rotary-wing and fixed-wing 
aircraft, alongside unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) operators. Through its four core 
pillars—education, doctrine development, capabilities integration, and concept 
experimentation—the center actively drives organizational change and integrates future 
vertical lift capabilities to ensure the Army's aviation warfighters are prepared to 
dominate in contested multi-domain operations. 
 
Service Description 
This is a hybrid non-personal services and supply contract to provide the United States 
Army Aviation Center of Excellence (AVCOE) with Secure Video- Teleconferencing 
(SVTC) Lifecycle replacement and Technical Services in Building 101 at Fort Rucker, 

Alabama. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, 
transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services 
necessary to perform the technology refresh as defined in the Statement of Objectives 
(SOO), except for those items specified as Government- furnished property (GFP) and 
services. This requirement is highly commercial utilizing Commercial-Off-The-Shelf 
(COTS) equipment with only standard, customary modifications required to safely and 
securely operate within a Department of War (DoW) environment. 
 
Proposed NAICS code: 541519 
NAICS Description: Other Computer Related Services 
Small Business Size Standard: $34.0 million 
*If you believe this requirement would be better served under a different NAICS, include 
that NAICS in your response. 
 
Purpose of the SSN 
Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC) – Fort Eustis is conducting 
market research to: 
 
1. Provide the attached SOO to industry for early awareness and potential 
planning purposes. 
2.  Identify qualified small business concerns and SBIR opportunities with the 
capability to provide both the required services and supply. 
3.  Determine industry capability. Please submit an abbreviated capability 
statement, not to exceed 5 pages, including the following information (or N/A): 
a. Company Name 
b. Unique Entity Identification(UEI) number 
c. Cage Code 
d. Confirmation that your company qualifies as a small business under 
NAICS code 541519 –Other Computer Related Services. If you believe another 
NAICS is more fitting for this requirement, include that NAICS and your rationale. 
e. Identification of your company’s small business type (e.g., 8(a), 
HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, etc.). 
f. If you have a Small Business Innovative Research (SBIR) that 
potentially meets the needs of this requirement, please provide the topic number 
in your capabilities statement. 
 
Disclaimer 

The attached SOO is a preliminary draft for market research purposes only and is not 
intended as an actionable requirement document. There is no guarantee that a 
requirement will proceed to solicitation or award. 
 
Pages & Format 
 
Images are permitted and count towards the page limit. All submissions must be in 8.5” 
x 11” format with 1” margins. All text must be in 12-point Arial font. Any pages beyond 
the specified limits may be considered only at the Contracting Officer’s (KO) discretion. 
Marketing materials that are not specifically related to this requirement will not be 
considered. 
Responding to the SSN 
 
All responses must be submitted in the SAM portal only by 10:00AM EDT on 
Wednesday, August 12th, 2026.

SALES TAX EXEMPTION
The contractor is hereby advised that the United States Government and Agencies thereof are exempt from State and Local 
Government tax by virtue of Article 6 of the United States Constitution. No exemption certificate is required.
STATEMENT OF WORK
NAVSEA Team Submarine AV and Collaboration Equipment Upgrade for TANC Split Conference Rooms
1. INTRODUCTION
The Naval Sea Systems Command is installing AV and collaborative web conferencing systems in two new collocated conference 
rooms.
2. BACKGROUND
The Naval Sea Systems Command Washington Navy Yard HQ is upgrading Audio Visual equipment and web conferencing 
systems in two (2) new Split conference rooms by installing a combination of new CFE large screen display, rack cabinets, AV 
switching and control, web conferencing equipment and new GFE secure KVM equipment. These two conference rooms are   
formed by drawing a sound-rated security curtain through the center of a larger room. Independent AV and collaborative   
conferencing systems are to be installed in each room.
3. SCOPE
3.1 The contractor shall design, install, configure, and functionally test AV and collaborative conferencing systems using a 
combination of new Contractor Furnished display, rack cabinet, AV switch and control, Installation Hardware Package, and web 
conferencing Equipment (CFE) and new Government Furnished secure KVM Equipment (GFE) in accordance with Attachment 1 
found in Section J of this announcement.
3.1.1 The Installation Hardware Package of Attachment 1 found in Section J shall include but not be limited to: Cable, connectors, 
cable adapters, custom cable assemblies, custom interface panels, labels, video scalers and splitters, display and other equipment 
mounting devices, and miscellaneous electrical and networking devices.
3.1.2 System Cross-connects. The contractor shall provide AV cross-connects between the two independent but collocated AV   
systems to allow an AV source connected to a single system to be displayed by both systems.
3.1.3 GFE SKVM. Each GFE Secure KVM (SKVM) and its remote control shall be contained in the associated system's equipment   
rack and serve, inter alia, to isolate a single Crestron DMPS3 AV output sharing display hardware in an unrelated system.
3.1.4 All AV switching and control system, power control, SKVM, and local repeater, scaler, converter equipment shall be contained 
in a mobile, lockable 19" half-rack. Equipment half-racks shall be interchangeable across all current Team Sub AV System Upgrade   
wave (CY25 and forward) conference rooms for casualty resolution, repurposing of office space, and the move of organization to other 
locations with only minor I/O changes for type and number of input and output devices. 
3.1.5 Conference table-mounted support electronics. Due to the fluid nature of conference table placement and the rather large number   
of smaller, mobile tables in each room, conference table-mounted support electronics should be mounted on a single table in each 
room, thereafter, designated as the 'Communications Table', with the intent to position the 'Communications Table' near the central 
floor-mounted I/O's for power, network, display, and Web cam access. All these services shall be passed through the Communications   
Tables per Table 3, Attachment 2, Section J.
3.1.6. For those conference table arrangements where a 'Communications Table' cannot access I/O services, the contractor shall 
provide one side wall location in each room with stationary support electronics associated with the hard disconnect panels required in 
Table 3, Attachment 2, Section J, that allows direct power, network, HDMI, and USB connections.
3.2 Not used.
3.3 Attachment 2 found in Section J of this announcement provides the architectural floor and wall penetration groupings for both 
rooms. The contractor shall provide custom interface panels with appropriate connectors to transition signals through floors and walls   
as required in Table 3.
3.4 Damaged areas of ceiling, walls and floors rising from this installation shall be restored to original condition.
