3.5 Skill in Crestron AV control and switching system programing and setup is required to complete this installation. The contractor   
shall provide examples of previous AMX, Crestron or equal, AV control system programing and setup experience.
3.6 The contractor shall provide CAD documentation of installed systems in the As-built condition for each room, including a 
reference to any connection points in existing, unmodified systems. These drawings shall be delivered in accordance with (IAW)   
Exhibit A (CDRL A002) found in Section J of this announcement.
3.7 The contractor shall provide a digital copy of AV control system source code, annotated, generated in a recognized source code 
text editor, delivered on USB Flash Drive and on CD-R/DVD-R media or file transfer via e-mail or website download for installed 
systems, however the contractor deems appropriate.
3.8 The Contractor shall provide an Integrator's Summary Operating Instructions with Touch Panel Screen Images for reference.
3.9 The contractor shall provide independent, remotely controlled, white LED, electrically lighted "Unclassified Meeting in Progress" 
and "Classified Meeting in Progress" signage for the exterior of each room. Signage shall be readable at 45' on the perpendicular to   
22.5 to the perpendicular.
3.10 The contractor shall provide an electrician licensed in the District of Columbia to make changes in the local 120 VAC 1 Phase 20 
Amp convenience wiring, in way of removing existing equipment not to be reused, reinstalling existing equipment to be reused, and 
installing new equipment.  This will involve, non-inclusively, terminating existing wiring at removed and not to be reused equipment

PROCUREMENTS (SECTION 508) 
 
On January 18, 2017, the Access Board issued a final rule that updated accessibility 
requirements covered by Section 508 and refreshed guidelines for telecommunications 
equipment subject to Section 255 of the Communications Act.  The final rule went into 
effect on January 18, 2018.  The revisions and updates to the Section 508-based 
standards and Section 255-based guidelines are intended to ensure that information 
and communication technology (ICT) covered by the respective statutes is accessible to 
and usable by individuals with disabilities.

STANDARDS 
 
The Section 508 standards established by the Access Board are incorporated into, and 
made part of all VA orders, solicitations and purchase orders developed to procure ICT.  
These standards are found in their entirety at: Revised 508 Standards and 255 
Guidelines (access-board.gov).  A single PDF file version of the Revised Section 508 
Standards and 255 Guidelines will be supplied upon request or can be obtained from 
the Access Board website.  Federal agencies must comply with the Rehabilitation Act of 
1973, as amended.  
 
The Contractor shall comply with “508 Chapter 2: Scoping Requirements” for all 
electronic ICT and content delivered under this contract. Specifically, as appropriate for 
the technology and its functionality, the Contractor shall comply with the technical 
standards marked here:

and AA Guidelines)

2.2 COMPATABILITY WITH  ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY 
The standards do not require installation of specific accessibility-related software or 
attachment of an assistive technology device. Section 508 requires that ICT be 
compatible with such software and devices so that ICT can be accessible to and usable 
by individuals using assistive technology, including but not limited to screen readers, 
screen magnifiers, and speech recognition software. 
2.3 ACCEPTANCE AND ACCEPTANCE TESTING 
Deliverables resulting from this solicitation will be accepted based in part on satisfaction 
of the Section 508 Chapter 2: Scoping Requirements standards identified above. 
The Government reserves the right to test for Section 508 Compliance before delivery.  
The Contractor shall be able to demonstrate Section 508 Compliance upon delivery.

network connected software system or service must meet the VA Critical Security 
Controls as outlined in the VA Memorandum, “VA Security Controls”, 
https://www.voa.va.gov/DocumentView.aspx?DocumentID=5010.  VA Critical Security 
Controls identify the minimum mandatory requirements that must be implemented 
across all VA enterprise infrastructure, cloud computing environments, information 
systems, networks, and specialized devices (medical devices/systems, special-purpose 
systems, and research scientific computing devices) that process, store, and/or transmit 
VA data.  Effective July 1, 2025, the Contractor shall implement these VA Critical 
Security Controls, within any network connected software system or service prior to 
being authorized for use in the VA.  This functional requirement is not negotiable, and 
Plan of Action & Milestones (POAM) will not be accepted in the event these controls 
cannot be implemented for new systems.  Critical Security Controls are intended to 
increase VA’s security posture and provide security and privacy risk visibility into the VA 
network and is not a new requirement.  The Contractor’s failure to maintain these VA 
Critical Controls after implementation will result in VA discontinuing the use of the 
system.

1 Purpose 
The purpose of this acquisition is to procure, install, configure, and migrate a highly 
available, redundant Enterprise Storage Filer solution. The primary objective is to ensure 
resilient, high-performance data storage, tiering, archival, and disaster recovery (DR) 
capabilities while maintaining strict compliance with Air Force Network (AFNet) standards, 
Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) supply chain security, and physical workplace safety 
protocols within a Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF). 
2 Scope 
This requirement encompasses hardware delivery, logical configuration, network integration, 
disaster recovery implementation, robust system testing, and system administration training 
for a minimum 100TB storage environment distributed across three separate filers. The scope 
includes rigorous work planning, quality control, and the physical tear-down of legacy 
materials. The contractor shall un-rack and stage all legacy hardware as directed by the 
Government; however, no legacy materials, components, or e-waste are authorized to leave 
the facility. All physical installation, migration, logical configuration, and material handover 
will occur strictly within the SCIF. 
 
3 Current Equipment 
The current Storage Area Network (SAN) infrastructure supporting the 250 IS environment is 
composed of three (3) HPE MSA 2050 storage arrays and two (2) dedicated management 
servers configured as follows:

4 Technical & Operational Objectives 
The contractor shall offer and implement a solution that achieves the following operational 
capabilities, ensuring at a minimum that the offered system possesses the exact same 
capabilities, functions, and performance metrics as the legacy system, or better: 
a. System Equivalency & Capacity 
The minimum offered solution must meet or exceed all current legacy system functions, 
capabilities, and performance baselines. The architecture must deliver a minimum of 100TB 
Usable Total Storage distributed across three separate filers, featuring a minimum of 2TB 
SLC Flash Storage (or equivalent performance) and enabling full storage virtualization. 
b. Disaster Recovery & Data Management 
The contractor must integrate a comprehensive DR solution to support Continuity of 
Operations (COOP), including secure data replication, automated failover, and robust 
backup/restore processes. Data management must support automatic tiered storage, allow the 
allocation of multiple RAID levels on the same storage tier, and implement independent 
archival capabilities. 
c. High Availability & Connectivity 
The system must ensure high availability through redundant control modules, redundant 
power supply units (PSUs), redundant cooling modules, and redundant internal storage, 
alongside redundant iSCSI capability with seamless controller failover. Connectivity 
requirements mandate a minimum of four 10Gbit SFP network connections per system, 
capable of utilizing fiber adaptors. 
5 Logistics, Safety & Site Operations 
The contractor shall execute the physical deployment in strict accordance with military safety 
and SCIF security protocols: 
a. Workplace Safety & SCIF Migration 
All physical work, heavy lifting, and rack installation must comply with the US Army Corps 
of Engineers (USACE) Safety and Health Requirements Manual EM 385-1-1, as well as 
applicable OSHA standards. The contractor is responsible for physically executing and

b. Material Disposition & Training 
The contractor is responsible for the removal and off-base environmental disposition of all 
non-salvageable materials, packaging, and legacy e-waste, excluding any storage media 
governed by security mandates. Additionally, the contractor must provide comprehensive 
administrative and operational training for two designated Government personnel within the 
secure facility. 
 
6 Security & Military Installation Access 
Contractor personnel must operate within strict DoD, Air Force, and Intelligence Community 
(IC) constraints: 
a. Personnel Clearances & Base Access 
At a minimum, all contractor personnel performing on-site work must possess and maintain 
an active Secret clearance for the duration of the contract. Personnel must comply with all 
host Military Installation security directives, vehicle search protocols, and unescorted access 
procedures prior to arriving at the SCIF. 
 
For Contractors that do not require CAC but require access to a DoD Facility and/or 
Installation. Contractor and all associated sub-contractors employees shall comply with

access to information classified “Confidential/Secret/Top Secret” and requires contractors to 
comply with visitor Group Security Agreement (VGSA) when designated as a Visitor Group 
at all contractor operations located on Air Force/Air National Guard installations in 
accordance with this PWS. Contract personnel must be entered into the Defense Information

The entire system offered must be actively listed on the Air Force Approved Product List

Intelligence Agency (DIA) Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) process. To ensure 
strict data sovereignty, the system warranty must include a "Keep Your Drive" provision 
where failed drives will not be returned to the vendor. 
7 Schedule, Work Hours & Execution 
To minimize mission impact, all execution must adhere to a strict operational schedule: 
a. Work Hours & Holidays 
All on-site work must be performed during normal operational hours, defined as Monday

on observed Federal Holidays unless explicitly pre-authorized in writing by the Contracting

Support for the Industrial Wastewater Treatment Plant   
Questions from the Vendors  
Q1. Do you have access to the current Allen Bradley PLC and Ignition SCADA program files, 
and will you be able to provide the files to the contract awardee?  
A1.  Available files have been loaded to SAM.gov 
 
Q2. Is upgrading the current Allen Bradley hardware and software to the latest versions and 
creating a SCADA native to Allen Bradley an acceptable solution, or would you rather migrate 
to a different controls platform entirely?  
A2.  No, this is due to non-available local support.  We need to see a different platform 
 
Q3. 3. The issues that you are experiencing with the existing system are more to do with the 
support and implementation of the hardware and software than the hardware and software itself.  
We feel strongly that keeping your hardware and software and upgrading it to the latest versions 
as well as correcting the limitations is the cost-effective action to take.  Based on this, would it 
be allowed for the vendor to submit a proposal to replace the server hardware, computer 
hardware, upgrade the software, and properly document the system through reverse engineering? 
A3.  For HAFB, the cost-effective solution does not work long term.  This has been an issue 
since 2010 
 
Q4. To accurately prepare our quote, we require additional information on the following: Piping 
and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs), Input/Output (IO) count, Screen count, and any existing 
system notes that might be available. Will this be provided?  
A4.  Reference Q1 
 
 
Q5. Will the electrical drawings for the existing system be provided for review? (e.g., Cabinet 
Layouts, Electrical Schematics, Bill of Material / Instrument list, P&ID, Pneumatic Schematics, 
Network Diagrams)  
A5.  Reference Q1 

 
Q6. What version of Ignition is the existing HMI application developed in?  
A6.  Currently unknown 
 
Q7. Will the Ignition program for the existing system be provided for review?  
A7.  No, HAFB does not have the capability to extract information requested 
 
Q8. What version of Rockwell Studio 5000 is the existing PLC code developed in?  
A8.   Currently unknown 
 
Q9. Will the existing PLC code be provided for review?  
A9.  Reference Q7 
 
Q10. Will the tags / structure of the existing database be shared for review?  
A10.  Reference Q1 
 
Q11. How many tags are being monitored / controlled by the existing system?  
A11.  Reference Q1 
 
Q12. There were a number of older VFDs located adjacent to the PLC cabinets that we suspect 
are part of the equipment being controlled by this system. Is there manufacturer information 
available for these components?  
A12.  HAFB is planning to replace prior to project start  
 

Q13. It was mentioned during the bid walk that a single SCADA software is preferred over the 
existing Ignition / Allen Bradley system. Is there a preferred or recommended SCADA software 
for the application?  
A13.  Infoscan or equivalent in performance and capabilities 
 
Q14. Is there an operations manual available for the existing system, and will it be made 
available for review?  
A14.  Reference Q1 
 
Q15. Is there some kind of written narrative or process description of the existing control system 
available for review?  
A15.  Reference Q1 
 
Q16. Please confirm which existing system files and supporting documentation will be available 
to the successful contractor, including:  
a. current PLC program files and controller backups;  
b. HMI/SCADA project files and historian configuration;  
c. available P&IDs, control narratives, sequences of operation, I/O lists, alarm and 
setpoint lists, and loop documentation;  
d. access information needed to retrieve and migrate the existing configurations; and  
e. native editable drawing files. Please identify any of these materials that are not 
available or will not be provided.  
A16.  Reference Q1 
 
Q17. Please provide any available drawings or documentation showing:  
a. modifications made after the 31 May 2012 record drawings;  
b. the current PLC, remote-I/O and communications architecture;  

c. radio, fiber, copper, modem or serial communication links;  
d. connections extending outside Building 575; and  
e. the existing or planned interface with the base EMCS.  
A17.  Reference Q1 
 
Q18. The drawing index appears to reference sheets EI-600, EI-601, EI-602, EI-620 and EI-621 
that were not included in the released drawing set. Please provide those sheets, if they exist, or 
confirm that they were never completed.  
A18.  Reference Q1 
 
Q19. Please identify the equipment connected through any existing 1756-DHRIO or other legacy 
communication modules and state whether migration of those connected devices is included in 
the contract scope.  
A19.  Migration/replacement of all legacy control system components IS fully included in 
the contract scope. You are required to safely remove all legacy PLC hardware, obsolete 
wiring, and communication modules 
 
Q20. Please clarify what the contractor is expected to deliver for the Risk Management 
Framework process and what will constitute satisfactory completion of that work. Is the 
contractor expected to provide a securely configured and hardened system, together with the 
supporting RMF documentation and test results needed for a Government-led authorization 
process? Or is the contractor expected to prepare and maintain the full authorization package 
through Government assessment and issuance of an Authorization to Operate?  
A20.  The contractor is expected to provide securely configured and hardened system, 
together with the supporting RMF documentation and test results needed for a 
Government-led authorization process 
 
Q21. Please confirm whether issuance of an Authorization to Operate is required before final 
acceptance or contract completion. If so, please explain how the Government’s review, 
assessment and authorization activities will be coordinated within the 180-day period of 
performance.  

A21.  The contractor is not expected to obtain the final, government-signed ATO within the 
180-day PoP 
 
Q22. Please clarify how the Government and the contractor will divide responsibility for the 
Risk Management Framework process. Will this SCADA system be covered by an existing Hill 
AFB cybersecurity authorization, or will it require a separate authorization?  
A22.  A separate authorization will be required due to the new system replacing another 
system that is already have been authorize 
 
Q23. Please identify the cybersecurity requirements and any existing Government 
documentation that will apply to this project.  
A23.  DAFGM2024-32-01, a new DAFGM2026-32-01 is currently in a draft and contractor 
will follow those requirements once its publication 
 
Q24. Please confirm whether the Government will provide the responsible cybersecurity points 
of contact and access to any Government systems needed to support the review and authorization 
process.  
A24.  Information will be provided with CO approval 
 
Q25. Please identify who will perform the cybersecurity scans, review the findings, determine 
what corrections are required, approve any remaining risk, and issue the final authorization.  
A25.  ISSM, information will be provided with CO approval 
 
Q26. If the Government’s cybersecurity review continues after the system is installed and 
accepted, please clarify what support the contractor must continue to provide and for how long.  
A26.  The contractor must provide remote, administrative support for post-installation to 
answer any technical questions and resolve any discrepancies on the system. Support for 
new requirements or any ongoing operational maintenance 
 

Q27. Please clarify how users are expected to log in to and be authenticated by the SCADA 
system, including:  
a. whether the system will join an Air Force domain or operate as a standalone OT 
enclave;  
b. the Government-approved MFA method for local and administrative access;  
c. whether Government identity, certificate or directory services will be furnished; and  
d. the required method for authentication when external network connectivity is 
unavailable.  
A27.  a. The system can be joined to the COIN network or can remain standalone. 
b. If connected by COIN then users will have to go through the MFA method for local and 
administrative access. If standalone then local privileged and standard user accounts. 
c. If COIN is connected, than the identity, certificate or directory is handled by AFCEC. 
d. No external network connectivity is authorized rather its COIN network or standalone. 
 
Q28. SOW §§5.3.2 and 5.3.3 require each controller to include a touchscreen and two RS-485 
communication ports. Please clarify whether those features must be built directly into the 
controller itself, or whether the requirement may be satisfied through manufacturer-supported 
components installed as part of the controller panel. Please confirm whether this type of 
integrated controller-panel arrangement would satisfy the SOW requirements.  
A28.  The touchscreen must be a built-in, native component of the controller hardware 
itself. (MPC Controller Hardware Characteristics) explicitly requires fully interactive 
integrated digital touchscreen for IP entry, configuration, diagnostics, and setup without a 
laptop 
 
Q29. Please clarify whether the channel counts, signal types, electrical ratings and other 
limitations identified in SOW §5.4 are intended as exact mandatory module configurations, 
minimum performance requirements, or representative acceptable ranges.  
A29.  Yes 
 

Q30. Please confirm the required treatment of existing spare, unused and abandoned I/O points, 
including whether: 
1. all currently wired spare or unused channels must be recreated in the replacement system; 
2. abandoned points may be removed with Government approval; and 
3. the completed system must include a specified percentage or quantity of installed spare 
I/O capacity.  
A30.  Need to research response.  1.  Yes  2.  Yes  3.  Yes, 10% above the actual count 
 
Q31.  Please clarify how the "single supplier" requirement in SOW §1.1.3 relates to the "single, 
unified software platform" requirement in SOW §6.1.1. Does "single supplier" mean that the 
controllers, I/O, SCADA software and related components must all come from one 
manufacturer? Or may a single prime contractor or system integrator provide and take full 
responsibility for an integrated system that includes products from more than one manufacturer?  
A31.  Yes, from one supplier and the same platform 
 
Q32. Please confirm whether the PLC programming and the SCADA/HMI development may use 
their respective manufacturer-supported tools, provided that the operator graphics, alarms, 
historical data, diagnostics and other SCADA functions are brought together in one unified 
operational platform. Alternatively, does the SOW require controller programming, HMI 
graphics, alarm management, historical trending and system diagnostics to be performed within a 
single manufacturer’s software environment?  
A32.  Using separate, manufacturer-supported tools for PLC programming and 
SCADA/HMI development—even if the final operator interface is unified—is explicitly 
prohibited by the SOW. Unified Software Platform Characteristics, which mandates:  
A Single unified software environment for programming, graphics, alarming, trending, 
historian functions, and diagnostics.  The system eliminates multivendor toolchains. 
 
Q33. Please confirm whether offerors may propose a currently manufactured and supported 
server that meets or exceeds the performance, storage and redundancy requirements of the Dell 
PowerEdge T340 specified in SOW §5.1.1.  
A33.  HAFB requires specified server 
 

Q34. Please confirm whether a currently supported version of Windows Server may be 
proposed, provided that it is compatible with the approved SCADA platform and all applicable 
cybersecurity and RMF requirements.  
A34.  HAFB requires specified Windows Server 
 
Q35. Please identify the required environmental and electrical classification for each control-
panel location, including the Main and TTO panels in Building 575 and any other locations 
included in the project. Please confirm:  
a. whether any panel location is classified as a hazardous area;  
b. the required enclosure rating for each location; and  
c. whether any location is exposed to corrosive chemicals or other conditions requiring 
stainless-steel or corrosion-resistant enclosures. If the Government intends the 
replacement panels to match the ratings of the existing installed enclosures, please 
confirm those ratings.  
A35.  Existing panels meet electrical classification.  Replacement panels will match existing 
installed enclosures 
 
Q36. Please clarify which existing field devices and wiring are to be replaced and which are 
expected to remain. Should offerors assume that the existing instrumentation, analyzers, 
transmitters, switches, valve feedback devices, motor starters, variable-frequency drives, and 
field wiring will be reused and reterminated, tested during the required loop checks, and retained 
unless specifically identified for replacement?  
A36.  Existing field devices will be reutilized 
 
Q37. Please clarify how pre-existing failed, inaccurate, or nonfunctional equipment discovered 
during installation or loop testing will be addressed.  
A37.  Validate plant operations/field devices prior to project start.  Anything failed after 
that will be the contractors responsibility  
 
Q38. SOW §4.2.1 requires removal of obsolete wiring, unsecured communication adapters and 
redundant field programming ports. Please identify:  

a. whether "obsolete wiring" includes only internal panel wiring or also field cabling;  
b. the communication adapters and programming ports intended for removal;  
c. the modems referenced in SOW §5.2.4; and d. any communication equipment outside 
the IWTP building that is included in the replacement scope.  
A38.  Obsolete wiring will be in the panels.  Field wiring can remain in place if functional 
and labeled as Spare.  Remaining questions will reference available information in Q1 
 
Q39. Does the Government have any asbestos or lead-based paint survey reports for the areas 
where the work will be performed? If so, please provide those reports and identify any findings 
relevant to the proposed demolition or installation work.  
A39.  Abatement shop can provide a non-ACM/non-LBP report.  This will change if new 
wall/roof penetrations are made.  Currently, installed conduits/wiring will be reutilized 
which will preclude additional testing 
 
Q40. Please confirm whether the Government anticipates any asbestos or lead-based paint 
disturbance or abatement under this contract and, if so, whether that work should be included in 
the firm-fixed

apply to supplies not identified in the Schedule to be accorded duty-free entry:
(1) The Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer in writing of any purchase of foreign supplies
(including, without limitation, raw materials, components, and intermediate assemblies) in excess of
$20,000 that are to be imported into the customs territory of the United States for delivery to the

entry and will notify the Contractor within 10 calendar days after receipt of the Contractor’s notification.
(3) Except as otherwise approved by the Contracting Officer, the contract price shall be reduced by (or
the allowable cost shall not include) the amount of duty that would be payable if the supplies were not

foreign supplies if-
(1) The supplies are identical in nature to items purchased by the Contractor or any subcontractor in
connection with its commercial business; and

provisions is not economical or feasible.

contract, either as end products or incorporated into end products, and shall pay duty on supplies, or any portion
of them, other than scrap, salvage, or competitive sale authorized by the Contracting Officer, diverted to

entry and will assist the Contractor in obtaining duty-free entry for these supplies.

notification by the Contracting Officer that duty-free entry will be accorded foreign supplies or, for duty-free

STATEMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO) 
 
Orchestrated Transformation  
Enterprise Performance Management, Process Intelligence, Transformation Services, Data Strategy, 
Emerging Technology, and Undelivered Orders Capability 
 
1. Purpose 
The purpose of this Statement of Objectives (SOO) is to define the Government’s high-level 
objectives for acquiring Orchestrated Transformation Services to advance enterprise innovation, 
operational maturity, data-driven decision-making, and financial stewardship across the 
Department of Commerce (DOC). 
 
The DOC Orchestrated Transformation effort is intended to build on the Business Applications 
Solution (BAS) investment by improving how the Department operates across financial 
management, acquisition, property, data, reporting, and shared service delivery. The effort will 
support the implementation and optimization of Enterprise Performance Management (EPM), 
Process Intelligence, Undelivered Orders (UDO) capabilities, Data Strategy and Data Catalog 
services, Emerging Technology, and Transformation Services to support modernization, 
visibility, and operational efficiency improvements across the enterprise.  
 
This transformation supports DOC’s vision and advances strategic goals. Transformation must 
produce measurable organizational outcomes, not just completed deliverables. 
 
Vision:  
Deliver a unified resource management ecosystem that is innovative, effective, efficient, reliable, 
and compliant providing insights that enable Commerce’s mission success.  
Goals:  
• Budget: Implement standardized, automated tools that provide leadership with data-
driven decision support. 
• Data: Deliver integrated, reliable, standardized, and accessible data that supports 
automation and operational efficiency. 
• Workforce: Build a Center of Excellence to strengthen workforce capabilities through 
training, analytics, emerging technologies, and data literacy. 
• Resource Optimization: Realize resource optimization by advancing the strategic 
investment of the BAS Ecosystem across the Department. 

                                                                                                                                                         Office of Financial Systems Management 
                                                                                                                                    U.S. Department of Commerce, Office of the Secretary 
 
Statement of Objectives – Orchestrated Transformation Page 2 of 14 
 
• Shared Service Delivery: Design, implement, and a mature shared services delivery 
through a Centers of Excellence model. 
This SOO communicates the Government’s desired outcomes and enables offerors to propose 
innovative, cost-effective, and performance-based solutions. Consistent with SOO-based 
acquisition methodology, this document defines objectives and desired outcomes; it does not 
prescribe specific technical solutions, labor categories, staffing models, or detailed 
implementation approaches. Offerors are expected to propose the best approach to achieving the 
Government’s objectives. 
2. Scope / Mission 
The Government seeks a comprehensive suite of transformation services and technology 
capabilities that improve organizational performance, increase executive visibility, reduce 
manual effort, mature data governance, and support measurable operational improvements across 
the BAS ecosystem. 
The scope includes the following major capability areas: 
• Implementation and optimization of an integrated EPM capability.  
• Deployment of Process Intelligence capabilities that identify, analyze, monitor, and 
improve end-to-end processes.  
• Transformation services, including roadmap development, operating model support, 
change management, training, implementation support, adoption enablement, and 
operational governance. 
• Implementation of a UDO capability to track and monitor UDOs leveraging emerging 
technology. 
• Advancing the use of the Enterprise Data Warehouse (EDW) through a comprehensive 
Data Strategy, Data Catalog, data governance support, and analytics enablement. 
• Use of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, automation, process 
mining, intelligent workflow, natural language querying, and other innovation pilots 
where appropriate and approved by the Government. 
3. Preferred SaaS Capabilities and Equivalent Solutions 
The Government has identified preferred SaaS capabilities and technology directions that may 
support the objectives of this SOO. However, the Government remains open to equivalent or 
superior SaaS solutions that meet the Department’s functional, technical, security, data, 
integration, operational, and governance requirements. 
Offerors may propose the Government-identified preferred SaaS products, equivalent SaaS 
products, or an integrated solution architecture that best achieves the outcomes defined in this 

                                                                                                                                                         Office of Financial Systems Management 
                                                                                                                                    U.S. Department of Commerce, Office of the Secretary 
 
Statement of Objectives – Orchestrated Transformation Page 3 of 14 
 
SOO. Any proposed alternative solution must clearly demonstrate how it meets or exceeds the 
salient characteristics, integration needs, security requirements, data governance expectations, 
reporting needs, workflow capabilities, scalability requirements, auditability requirements, and 
sustainment objectives required by the Government. 
Offerors shall identify any assumptions, dependencies, licensing considerations, integration 
constraints, data migration or data access requirements, Authority to Operate considerations, 
FedRAMP status, implementation risks, transition considerations, and sustainment implications 
associated with their proposed SaaS solution. 
The Government will evaluate proposed solutions based on their ability to achieve the required 
outcomes, align with the BAS ecosystem, minimize operational disruption, protect production 
stability, support auditability and compliance, enable data portability, and provide measurable 
value to the Department. 
4. Period and Place of Performance 
Period: One (1) year plus four (4) option years 
Place: Gaithersburg, MD and/or Washington, D.C. with approved hybrid and remote support as 
authorized by the Government. 
5. Background 
DOC is completing the third and final phase of the BAS IT modernization in October 2026. The 
BAS IT modernization focused on implementing an integrated Enterprise Resource Planning 
(ERP) environment using Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS), Unison, PRISM, Sunflower, the 
Enterprise Data Warehouse, and related interfaces to support financial management, acquisition, 
property management, reporting, and enterprise data needs across DOC bureaus. 
To further realize the return on invest in BAS, DOC seeks to advance the next stage of 
modernization by improving enterprise performance management, data strategy, process 
visibility, resource optimization, and operational decision support. 
The current operational environment continues to rely on manual processes, fragmented 
reporting, inconsistent data definitions, and siloed operational insights. These conditions reduce 
agility, limit executive visibility, increase reconciliation burden, and constrain the Department’s 
ability to proactively manage performance, risk, budget execution, undelivered orders, and 
enterprise shared service outcomes. 
DOC seeks to establish a modernized performance-management and transformation ecosystem 
that provides greater automation, integrated analytics, real-time insights, improved process 
transparency, standardized processes, and measurable operational outcomes. 

                                                                                                                                                         Office of Financial Systems Management 
                                                                                                                                    U.S. Department of Commerce, Office of the Secretary 
 
Statement of Objectives – Orchestrated Transformation Page 4 of 14 
 
6. Performance Objectives 
6.1. Enterprise Performance Management (EPM) 
The desired outcome is an integrated Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) EPM capability, using the 
Government’s preferred platform or an equivalent solution, that supports planning, budgeting, 
forecasting, consolidation, reporting, controlled workflows, executive decision support, 
auditability, and integration with the BAS ecosystem. 
The EPM capability should support the Department in achieving the following outcomes: 
• Improve enterprise planning, budgeting, forecasting, consolidation, and financial 
reporting. 
• Automate the financial close by extracting, standardizing, and reconciling data from 
multiple applications. 
• Provide real-time performance dashboards and generate regulatory-compliant reports. 
• Enable controlled workflows, approval routing, version control, and auditability of 
planning and reporting activities. 
• Support labor forecasting, cost modeling, scenario planning, and resource optimization. 
• Improve leadership visibility into financial performance, budget execution, resource 
needs, and enterprise risk areas. 
• Reduce reliance on manual spreadsheets and fragmented reporting processes. 
6.2. Process Intelligence 
The desired outcome is an enterprise SaaS-based Process Intelligence capability, using the 
Government’s preferred platform or an equivalent solution, that enables DOC to ingest relevant 
BAS ecosystem data, map and monitor end-to-end processes, identify bottlenecks and control 
gaps, and provide actionable insights for process improvement, compliance, and operational 
performance management. 
The Process Intelligence capability should support the Department in achieving the following 
outcomes: 
• Establish baseline process performance and maturity assessments across selected BAS 
business processes. 
• Ingest and analyze data from core BAS solutions, including Oracle E-Business Suite, 
Unison PRISM, Sunflower, and the Enterprise Data Warehouse. 
• Use process mining and process intelligence capabilities to capture, map, model, and 
monitor end-to-end processes. 
• Identify process bottlenecks, inefficiencies, risks, control gaps, compliance concerns, and 
opportunities for standardization. 

                                                                                                                                                         Office of Financial Systems Management 
                                                                                                                                    U.S. Department of Commerce, Office of the Secretary 
 
Statement of Objectives – Orchestrated Transformation Page 5 of 14 
 
• Provide dashboards and analytics that show real-time operational performance, cycle 
times, exceptions, rework, and process variation. 
• Support continuous improvement, shared service maturity, and targeted business process 
optimization. 
• Provide actionable recommendations that can be evaluated through the appropriate BAS 
governance process. 
6.3. Transformation Services 
The desired outcome is a coordinated transformation capability that enables DOC to move from 
implementation completion to sustained modernization, shared service maturity, and measurable 
business value. 
Transformation services should support the Department in achieving the following outcomes: 
• Support the achievement of Strategic Vision, Goals and associated transformation 
Actions. 
• Develop and maintain a transformation roadmap that identifies future-state outcomes, 
milestones, dependencies, risks, governance considerations, and change-management 
strategies. 
• Build on current initiatives to support the BAS ecosystem by outlining the required level 
of effort that continues the advancement of the transformation roadmap. 
• Provide discovery, prototyping, and implementation support for approved transformation 
initiatives, including adoption enablement. 
• Design, enhance, and implement the Centers of Excellence (CoE) framework to 
centralize expertise, streamline processes, foster innovation, and cultivate talent. 
• Provide change management, stakeholder engagement, communication, and user-
readiness support aligned to customer needs and operational impacts. 
• Support the maturation of the shared services operating model, including governance, 
service delivery, performance management, and continuous improvement. 
• Promote adoption of standard processes, data-driven decision-making, and customer-
focused service delivery. 
6.4. Undelivered Orders (UDO) Capability 
The desired outcome is a UDO capability that improves enterprise visibility, accountability, 
monitoring, and resolution of undelivered orders across DOC. 
The UDO capability should support the Department in achieving the following outcomes: 
• Implement a centralized capability to track, monitor, analyze, and support resolution of 
UDO balances and related requests. 

                                                                                                                                                         Office of Financial Systems Management 
                                                                                                                                    U.S. Department of Commerce, Office of the Secretary 
 
Statement of Objectives – Orchestrated Transformation Page 6 of 14 
 
• Provide a one-stop shop for UDO-related requests, workflow, status tracking, supporting 
documentation, and management action. 
• Enable enterprise-level visibility into UDO balances, aging, ownership, resolution status, 
supporting documentation, and required follow-up actions. 
• Provide dashboards categorized by bureau, entity, fund, object class, obligation type, age, 
risk category, DOC types and other Government-approved dimensions. 
• Support aging analysis, exception reporting, audit support, and financial stewardship 
activities. 
• Enable system notifications, reminders, and escalations for applicable stakeholders, 
including finance users, program offices, acquisition users, suppliers, and other 
authorized users. 
• Provide communication materials, training, and user-readiness support.

MTS Systems Corporation is the exclusive developer, owner, and authorized provider of the specialized

validation to ensure system functionality and compliance with mission requirements. These efforts would

The BreezeReview and BreezeConnect applications developed by MGC Diagnostics 
are proprietary. Because MGC Diagnostics maintains full control over its software 
and interfaces, only MGC can provide the HL7 server required for the Kansas City 
VAMC and ensure proper integration with VISTA. MGC Diagnostics is also the sole 
vendor capable of integrating its BreezeConnect interface with Somnoware, the 
Oracle Health–approved platform. 
 
The KCVA currently operates MGC diagnostic devices using the Breeze Suite 
software, including  plethysmography box, Ultima systems, and  
spirometers. These devices, most of which were purchased within the last two years, 
depend on MGC’s proprietary software. For this reason, the facility has only 
evaluated MGC’s HL7 interface, as adopting a different vendor’s solution would 
require replacing all devices. 
 
While other brands, such as the  have been contemplated and could 
potentially be used in the future Federal EHR environment, pursuing this option

Proceeding with the BreezeReview solution avoids these significant inefficiencies. It

1. About ABMC and Purpose 
American Battle Monuments Commission is a United States federal agency responsible for 
commemorating the service and sacrifice of U.S. armed forces where they have served overseas. 
ABMC manages and maintains American military cemeteries, memorials, and monuments outside 
the continental United States and supports public access to historical and commemorative 
information. 
ABMC requires a fully managed cloud backup and recovery service for Microsoft 365, Azure, 
and identity systems. Contractor shall provide recurring licenses, software services, and data 
backup and recovery services under CLIN 0001. Contractor shall provide one-time 
implementation and deployment services under CLIN 0002. CLIN 0001 shall include one base 
year and four option years. 
 

 3 
 
 
2. Environment 
ABMC uses Microsoft 365 E5, SharePoint Online, and Azure. ABMC maintains approximately 
30 TB of SharePoint Online data, which may include duplicate data. ABMC expects the 
deduplicated data set to be less than half of that amount. ABMC expects data to grow 5 to 10 
percent per year and does not expect SharePoint Online data to exceed 45 TB during the period 
of performance. In scope Azure workloads include virtual machines, Azure SQL, infrastructure 
services, platform services, and storage. In scope identity systems include Active Directory and 
Microsoft Entra ID. 
3. Performance Requirements 
Contractor shall provide the following service characteristics, tasks, deliverables, and acceptance 
criteria for cloud backup and recovery services. 
3.1 CLIN Structure 
• CLIN 0001 Recurring Services. Contractor shall provide licenses, software services, 
storage, service capacity, and data backup and recovery services for the base year and 
each option year. 
• CLIN 0002 One Time Implementation and Deployment. Contractor shall complete 
setup, configuration, testing, documentation, and knowledge transfer needed to place the 
service into operation. 
3.2 In Scope Workloads 
1. Microsoft 365 E5 
2. SharePoint Online data, approximately 30 TB including duplicate data 
3. Azure infrastructure services, platform services, and storage 
4. Azure virtual machines 
5. Azure SQL 
6. Identity systems, including Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID 
3.3 Service Requirements 
Contractor shall provide a solution that meets the following requirements: 
1. Provide a fully managed cloud service hosted in Amazon Web Services or Microsoft 
Azure. 
2. Operate the service without requiring ABMC to deploy, maintain, or operate backup 
infrastructure. 
3. Provide a web based administrative console for authorized ABMC personnel. 

 4 
4. Support an optional local backup or recovery target without requiring local infrastructure 
for normal service operation. 
5. Include software, storage, compute, and data transfer in the subscription model. 
6. Use strong access controls for administrative and service access. 
7. Keep backup data separate from production data and protect backup data from 
unauthorized change or deletion. 
8. Monitor the service environment and detect suspicious activity. 
9. Support deduplication and maintain deduplicated cloud storage for protected data. 
10. Protect and recover in scope on premises workloads, cloud workloads, software as a 
service workloads, and endpoint data. 
11. Support planned and automated recovery using known good backup copies. 
12. Support integration with security monitoring or response tools when those integrations 
are part of the proposed solution. 
13. Protect and recover identity data across Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, and Okta

service capacity required for the systems in scope.

support contacts.

inputs, and schedule.

kickoff.

another solution.

transition out.

Artificial Intelligence Requirements

All requiring activities must adhere to the policy for all in-scope AI use-case owners to submit their AI Use-Cases through the CAIO Team Site which contains AI Use-Case Intake Form.  Please see the Intake Form site referenced for further information on AI Use-Cases, and the submission instructions.  See below for the Use-Case Categories and Examples of Use-Cases that would require submission of your effort using the AI Use-Case Intake Form.  

Use-Case Categories and Examples That Require Intake Submission:

VA AI Use-Cases required for Intake commonly fall under the following categories:

A software system that learns from data

A tool that mimics or supports human decision making

A tool exposed to new data to make predictions, decisions, or recommendations about real people, agency service delivery, or agency program execution

Some examples of AI Use-Cases at VA include:  

Machine learning or other AI tools to provide a clinical diagnosis or determine a recommended treatment; 

AI chat tools to summarize claims and contention data; 

Natural language processing to review Veteran survey comments and identify potential risks of crisis; 

AI tools to automate components of benefits and application processing. 

The answers provided within the AI Use-Case Intake Form including, but not limited to the type of AI used, the domain the AI is in, the benefit and output of the AI, will be used by CAIO to evaluate and determine if the use-case is required for Inventory, as well as if it is High-Impact, as required by M-25-21.  See also Identification and Review of High-Impact AI Use Cases.

After submitting the use-case to the CAIO office Intake process, CAIO office representatives will assist the Use-Case Owner through next steps required for their Use-Case. If High Impact Use-Case, the CAIO office will also provide information regarding required risk management practices, the AI Impact Assessment, and Risk Mitigation Plan requirements. As a result, the Requiring Activity should determine if any specific related requirements tasks are needed for their PD to support these minimum risk management requirements.  

Use-Case Owners should also indicate to CAIO whether the AI Use-Case is a pilot, which will release them from the full compliance process, but will trigger a follow-up by CAIO at six months

See Section 5.7 in the PD Template for the required information and language that will always be included in your PD, regardless of intake determination, and instructions regarding any modifications to the requirements, as necessary.  Section 5.7 also contains PD requirements to ensure Unbiased AI Principles are adhered to and incorporated into the AI System/LLM.  

Additionally, there are solicitation instructions/requirements for the Vendor to submit with its proposal, located in the Notes to the CO Section at the end of this document.

Source Code Harmonization and Reuse in Information Technology (SHARE IT) Act Requirements: 

All custom software development efforts (except for those programs/products for use in national security systems, classified code, or code whose disclosure would create an identifiable risk to individual privacy) must include software source code delivery of custom-developed code for Federal re-use requirements in accordance with the SHARE IT Act, P.L. 118-187, December 23, 2024.  (Custom-developed code means source code, or segregable portions of source code, written for a software project, module, plugin, script, middleware, or application programming interface, that is first produced in the performance of a contract, exclusively funded by the Federal Government, for which the Federal Government could obtain unlimited rights under FAR Part 27

See Section 5.8, Source Code Harmonization and Reuse in Information Technology (SHARE IT) Act, in this PD Template for the required information and language to be included in this PD if the SHARE IT Act applies.

The formal deliverable and task such as, “The Contractor shall provide a Custom-Developed Code Package including the source code or segregable portions of source code, and other key technical components of the code (including documentation, data models, schemas, metadata, architecture designs, configuration scripts, and artifacts required to develop, build, test, and deploy the code) to support reuse and transparency in accordance with the SHARE IT Act,” (or similar) must be added to the Software Development requirements at the appropriate location within the PD task in Section 1.x (to include adding the associated Custom Developed Code Package deliverable and its due date requirements in the Schedule for Deliverables table within the Notes to the CO Section (and corresponding CLIN within the Price Schedule)) to ensure delivery of the custom developed code package throughout the development process to the current VA GitHub Source Code Inventory Repository for VA/Federal re-use, as required in the SHARE IT Act. 

VA Enterprise Cloud (VAEC) Efforts, Enterprise Cloud Solutions Office (ECSO):

The VA CIO and Infrastructure Operations Director require that, if a solution cannot be provided by a SaaS solution or Infrastructure as Code, that it next be assessed for hosting on one of VA’s Enterprise Cloud Hosting Platforms including the VA Enterprise Cloud (VAEC), and VA Platform One (VAPO). VAEC is a multi-cloud hosting platform, providing both Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure government community clouds. VAPO provides a containerization strategy for migrations and new development within the VAEC clouds. Both VAEC and VAPO support the efficient migration to and utilization of cloud technology by the requiring activity.  Through VAEC and VAPO, Infrastructure Operations (IO) provides applications and systems with secure and seamless cloud functionality together with enterprise tools, standards and common services. IO adheres to the Cloud Smart Policy  (https://cloud.cio.gov/strategy/),which offers practical implementation guidance to fully realize the potential of cloud-based technologies while ensuring thoughtful execution that incorporates practical realities.  New cloud hosting requests can be directed to the IO Unified Intake Services Request here:  IO Unified Intake Services Request. To expedite a request, contact OIT IO INTAKE TRIAGE. 

To aid requiring activities that need to migrate applications or systems to the VAEC or are implementing applications or systems in the VAEC, the Office of Strategic Sourcing (OSS), Technical Acquisition Center (TAC), and the Enterprise Cloud Solutions Office (ECSO) have provided a VAEC Technical Reference Guide VAEC Technical Reference Guide 11/2022 This guide is applicable to migrations to or new development in the VAEC platforms.

Requiring Activities should also note that there is standard VAEC performance work statement (PWS) language (see below) to be used by project teams that need to migrate applications or systems to the VAEC or are implementing applications or systems in the VAEC.  This language includes cloud-specific requirements and deliverables that should be considered in your PWS/PD.  

Projects where an existing COTS or custom, legacy application or system has been deemed cloud suitable and is targeted to be migrated to and hosted in the VAEC (or is currently hosted in a VAEC) should refer to the “Standard VAEC PWS Language for Migrations” document for PWS/PD sample language considerations regarding specific VAEC requirements to be added to the Requiring Activity’s PWS/PD. 

Projects where there is a new solution implementation should refer to the “Standard VAEC PWS Language for New Implementations” document for PWS/PD sample language considerations regarding specific VAEC requirements to be added to the Requiring Activity’s PD.  

These documents can be found at the VAEC Acquisition Resources page: https://dvagov.sharepoint.com/sites/OITECSO/SitePages/VAEC-Acquisition.aspx?csf=1&e=dhnDL4.  If you require further assistance, please contact ecsoinfo@va.gov. 

SaaS EFFORTS:

In addition, Requiring Activities should note that for Software as a Service (SaaS) acquisitions, Digital Transformation Center (DTC) has developed standardized PWS/PD Language for several scenarios regarding FedRAMP, etc., to be added to your PWS/PD requirements document, as appropriate.  Please see the document “SaaS Contract Language and Price Schedule – FY24” in the “SaaS” folder for the latest language and example price schedule, located in the “OIT Acquisition Guides” folder within the “OPAL Acquisition Requirements Package (ARP) Templates” area: OIT Acquisition Guides. PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) New Jersey Healthcare System requires a comprehensive patient clinical monitoring and intervention software program that provides clinical staff immediate, real-time lists of patients, identifies those who need clinical intervention based on current best practice guidelines and facility determined criteria and provides the ability of clinical staff to monitor and protect patients from drug interactions and adverse events. The program must have the capability of targeting only those patients who need clinical interventions, resulting in increased resourcing of staff. The software program will also need to allow Pharmacy and facility to meet regulatory requirements set by Joint Commission Standards, National Patient Safety Goals as part of the Joint Commission requirements and Veterans Health Administration (VHA) directives. Additionally, the software solution needs to provide clinical staff antimicrobial stewardship which will directly assist the facility in meeting its Directive 1031, Antimicrobial Stewardship Programs (ASP) dated January 30, 2019 delineating VA Medical Center’s responsibilities with antimicrobial stewardship. The software maintenance and support program will need to include security patches and software updates, and 24/7 technical support via multiple channels, including telephone support. Software maintenance and support shall also include enhancements/changes to the proprietary interface and software via interpretation of site-specific VistA programmatic uniqueness to meet functional needs of clinical staff. The software program shall include clinical surveillance that can be customized for users within section cohorts (i.e., Pharmacy, Infection Control, ADT, Laboratory, Mico, Surgery, Impatient Pharmacy, Radiology, BCMA, and Vital Signs via alert panels stratified by clinical section, alert type, date/time range and unit/hospital/outpatient locations. 

The clinical surveillance system, with associated services must be able to interface with existing VA data resources including, but not limited to: 

Veterans Health Information Systems and Technology Architecture (VistA) 

Computerized Patient Record System (CPRS) 

Process Information Management System/Asset Information Management System (PIMS/AIMS) systems 

Bed Management 

Bar Code Medication Administration (BCMA) 

Others future systems (CERNER etc.)  

2. Scope of Work

TheraDOC surveillance and monitoring software shall be able to provide the following services: 

Meets all the needs of VANJ Healthcare System services that will utilize the surveillance program and be operational.within 90 days of award. 

Meets data, alerting and workflow needs for a broad range of healthcare users including pharmacists, infection preventionists, physicians, nurses, laboratory, and others requiring access to clinical surveillance data and information. 

The software shall be able to allow clinical pharmacists to create alerts, reports and track recommendation and interventions made by physicians during daily rounding in the areas of anticoagulation, diabetes, and cholesterol management and treatment. 

Provide a platform for inpatient and outpatient anticoagulation monitoring. 

Allow pharmacy and other services to create reports and alerts for high-risk, non-formulary, or other drug/drug evaluations. 

Allow creation of medication use evaluation reporting and provide tools for monitoring of medication adherence.

PERFORMANCE-BASED WORK STATEMENT (PBWS) 
Contract for Demographic Analysis Indian Health Service Office of Public Health Support, 
Division of Program Statistics 
PART 1: GENERAL INFORMATION 
1.1 Contract Type and Nature 
This is a Contract for the provision of expert demographic research and statistical analysis 
services to support the Indian Health Service's ongoing efforts to produce accurate, high-quality 
demographic reports and data products for American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) populations. 
Services shall be provided by qualified individual(s) who work under the general supervision of 
the Government, performing work that is integral to the Government's operations. The contractor 
shall be accountable to the Government for the quality and timeliness of all work products. 
The demographic analysis services provided under this contract are integral to IHS health service 
delivery. The adjusted vital statistics data, life expectancy calculations, and population health 
measures produced under this contract directly inform resource allocation, budget formulation, 
and health program planning for American Indian and Alaska Native populations served by IHS. 
This contract is therefore authorized under 25 U.S.C. § 1638c, which permits Contracts for 
services supporting Indian health programs, and satisfies the statutory authority requirement of 
FAR 37.104(b). 
1.2 Background and Justification 
The Indian Health Service (IHS) and Indian Tribes rely on accurate demographic data for health 
planning, policy development, resource allocation, and outcome measurement. Since 1997, the 
Division of Program Statistics (DPS) has processed county-level vital statistics data from the 
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and National Institutes of Health (NIH) to 
correct racial misclassification of American Indians and Alaska Natives on state birth and death 
certificates. 
Published research demonstrates that AI/AN race is frequently misidentified on state vital 
records. The IHS has developed and validated adjustment methodologies to correct these errors. 
However, continued application of these complex adjustment processes, analysis of vital 
statistics data, and production of demographic reports requires specialized expertise in both 
statistical analysis and public health demography using and modifying code used and owned by 
the government. 
This contract establishes a personal services arrangement whereby a qualified demographer 
works in partnership with DPS staff to ensure continuity, quality, and timeliness of demographic 
data products used for three primary publications: Trends in Indian Health and Regional 
Differences in Indian Health, the Life Expectancy Report, as well as other ad hoc demographic 
analyses as needed. 

1.3 Period of Performance 
The period of performance shall be for one (1) Base Year of 12 months plus four option years.  
1.4 Place of Performance 
Work shall be performed virtually 95% of the time, with in-person services required only for 
activities such as obtaining Personal Identification Verification (PIV) cards and other security-
related requirements. Work with confidential data must be performed exclusively on 
Government-furnished equipment in the secure Windows server environment. 
1.5 Hours of Operation 
Services shall be provided during core business hours of 8:00 AM - 4:30 PM Eastern Time, 
Monday through Friday, excluding Federal holidays and Government-directed facility closings. 
The contractor shall maintain adequate availability to ensure uninterrupted performance of all 
assigned tasks. 
 
PART 2: PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES 
2.1 Primary Performance Objectives 
The contractor shall demonstrate competency in and responsibility for achieving the following 
performance outcomes: 
2.1.1 Accurate Data Processing and Adjustment 
 Accurately apply IHS-approved adjustment methodologies to mortality, natality, and 
linked birth/infant death datasets using statistical analysis methods. 
 Produce adjusted datasets that correctly compensate for documented racial 
misclassification on state vital records. 
 Ensure all adjusted datasets match approved denominators by age group, sex, county, 
service unit, and administrative area. 
 Maintain data quality through rigorous validation and quality assurance processes. 
2.1.2 Timely Deliverable Production 
 Deliver all primary demographic reports (Regional Differences, Trends in Indian Health, 
Life Expectancy, YPLL) meeting the deadlines specified in the Deliverables Schedule 
(Technical Exhibit 1). 
 Provide periodic ad hoc demographic analyses and special reports as requested by the 
Director, Division of Program Statistics. 
 Submit monthly progress reports documenting status, milestones achieved, and any 
obstacles encountered. 

 Provide all supporting code, documentation, and data files in machine-readable format 
for Government review and future use. 
2.1.3 High-Quality Technical Products 
 Produce well-documented, efficient, and maintainable analytical code, also contributing 
successfully to the modification of existing code, following industry best practices. 
 Provide clear, comprehensive written explanations of methodologies, calculations, and 
results. 
 Ensure all demographic tables are accurate, clearly labeled, and presented in 
Government-approved Excel and PowerPoint templates. 
 Deliver code that Government staff can understand, review, modify, and execute 
independently. 
2.1.4 Technical Expertise and Problem-Solving 
 Demonstrate advanced knowledge of demographic methods including mortality analysis, 
life table construction, life expectancy calculation, YPLL analysis, and standardization 
techniques. 
 Provide technical assistance to DPS staff regarding analytical methods, algorithmic 
approaches, and interpretation of results. 
 Contribute expertise in designing approaches to correct for natality data misclassification 
in the first contract year. 
 Support DPS responses to technical questions from other Government entities and 
Congressional inquiries. 
2.1.5 Data Security and Compliance 
 Comply with all IHS information security requirements, HIPAA regulations, and data 
handling protocols. 
 Complete required ISSA and privacy training before accessing Government systems. 
 Sign and maintain appropriate Nondisclosure Agreements and Business Associate 
Agreements. 
 Safeguard all Government-furnished equipment and confidential data in accordance with 
Federal regulations. 
  

PART 3: PERFORMANCE STANDARDS AND ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA 
3.1 Standard of Performance for All Deliverables 
Each deliverable must meet the following criteria for Government acceptance: 
Accuracy: All calculations, adjustments, and presented data must be verifiable and correct. Data 
must accurately reflect the Government-approved methodologies and adjustment factors. DPS 
staff shall have the authority to request revisions until accuracy is confirmed. 
Completeness: All required components must be provided, including analytical code, 
documentation, supporting data files, and explanatory materials. Deliverables missing any 
required element shall be considered defective. 
Timeliness: Deliverables must be submitted by the date specified in Technical Exhibit 1. Late 
submissions shall be documented and may affect contractor performance ratings. 
Documentation Quality: All code must include clear comments explaining logic and 
calculations. All supporting documentation must explain methodologies in plain language 
understandable to both technical and non-technical audiences. 
Usability: All deliverable formats must follow Government-provided templates exactly. Code 
must be written in a style that Government staff can interpret, maintain, and execute 
independently after contract completion. 
3.2 Defective Service Definition 
A deliverable is considered defective and subject to revision or replacement if it: 
 Contains mathematical or computational errors. 
 Fails to apply required adjustment methodologies correctly. 
 Does not follow the Government-approved format or template. 
 Lacks required supporting documentation or code. 
 Is submitted late without Government approval for extension. 
 Cannot be executed or understood by Government staff. 
 Does not address the Government's stated analytical requirements. 
The Government reserves the right to require the contractor to revise any defective deliverable at 
no additional cost until it meets all acceptance criteria.

PART 4: CONTRACTOR QUALIFICATIONS AND KEY PERSONNEL 
4.1 Minimum Qualifications 
The contractor must be an individual or firm with personnel who collectively possess the 
following minimum qualifications. If a firm, the contractor must designate the Demographer as 
the primary point of contact and the individual responsible for overall contract performance. 
4.2 Demographer Qualifications 
The individual performing the primary demographic and statistical analysis work must have: 
Education 
 Minimum Doctoral degree in demography, possibly population studies, economics, 
quantitative sociology or a directly related field. 
 Substantial coursework in demographic methods. 
Demographic Expertise 

 Demonstrated background in demographic analysis including vital statistics (mortality, 
natality, fertility rates), life table construction, life expectancy calculations, Years of 
Potential Life Lost (YPLL) calculations. 
 Practical knowledge of direct and indirect standardization methods. 
 Understanding of population estimation and projection techniques. 
 Demonstrated expertise in population health measures and demographic processes. 
Demographic Statistical Analysis Proficiency 
 Advanced demonstrated proficiency in demographic statistical analysis. 
 Minimum 2 years of professional demographic statistical analysis experience. 
 Demonstrated ability to write efficient, well-documented code following industry best 
practices. 
 Experience with intermediate level data management and statistical analysis. 
Experience 
 Minimum 2 years of combined experience in demographic analysis. 
 Documented experience analyzing vital statistics data (mortality, natality) from NCHS or 
similar Federal sources. 
 Practical experience with indirect standardization methods for correcting racial/ethnic 
misclassification in vital records. 
 Proven ability to work with large, confidential datasets in secure environments. 
 Experience producing publications or reports using demographic data. 
Technical Knowledge 
 Strong working knowledge of demographic methods sufficient to explore and apply 
standardization techniques. 
 Understanding of HIPAA and data security requirements for health information. 
 Knowledge of Federal vital statistics data sources (CDC/NCHS, NIH/NCI). 
Communication Skills 
 Ability to explain complex demographic concepts and statistical methodologies to both 
technical and non-technical audiences. 
 Strong written and verbal communication skills. 
 Ability to participate effectively in technical discussions and collaborative problem-
solving. 
 Capability to produce clear, understandable documentation. 
4.3 Identification and Notification 
All contractor personnel must identify themselves as contractor employees when interacting with 
Government staff, attending meetings, or answering Government communications. The 

contractor shall ensure all documents and deliverables are clearly marked as contractor products 
with appropriate contractor identification. 
PART 5: GOVERNMENT-FURNISHED PROPERTY AND SERVICES 
5.1 Equipment and Software 
 Laptop computer with Government-approved statistical analysis software installed and 
configured for Government network access. 
 Access to secure Windows server environment for data processing and storage. 
 Licensed statistical analysis software (SAS) maintained on Government-furnished 
equipment. 
 R and RStudio for supplementary analytical work. 
 Virtual meeting facilities for Government-contractor collaboration. 
 PIV card and Government network access (following background check and security 
clearance). 
 ihs.gov email address. 
5.2 Data and Documentation 
 Demographic datasets from CDC/NCHS and other Federal sources. 
 IHS-approved adjustment factors and methodologies for correcting vital records data. 
 Standard Operating Procedures and Policies related to demographic data research. 
 County identifiers and additional data/information as needed.

Section I – Services 
1.0 TASK ORDER TYPE 
This is a Firm Fixed Price Task Order. This Task Order is established under General Services 
Administration (GSA) Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) 54151S – Information Technology 
Professional Services in support of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Office of 
the Chief Readiness Support Officer (OCRSO), Facilities and Operational Support (F&OS) in 
support of the Real Property Management System (RPMS). All terms and conditions of the 
vendor's GSA Schedule remain unchanged and in full force and effect, unless specifically stated 
otherwise herein. 
 
2.0 SCHEDULE B 
 
 
Section II – Statement of Work (SOW) 
 
1.0 Project title 
 
Real Property Management System (RPMS) in support of the Department of Homeland 
Security (DHS), Management Directorate (MGMT), Office of the Chief Readiness Support 
Officer (OCRSO), Facilities and Operational Support (F&OS). 
 
Background 
 
1.1 Department of Homeland Security 
 
DHS was created by enactment of H.R. 5005, the Homeland Security Act of 2002. DHS’s 
primary mission is the protection of the American people and includes: 
• Preventing terrorist attacks within the United States 
• Reducing the vulnerability of the United States to terrorism 
• Minimizing the damage and assisting in the recovery from terrorist attacks that do occur 
within the United States 
 
Within DHS’ Management Directorate, the Office of the Chief Readiness Support Officer 
(CRSO), Facilities and Operational Support (F&OS) (the “Government”) is tasked with 
overseeing portfolio elements such as rent payments, overtime utilities and security costs for 
approximately 12 million square feet of owned and leased administrative use space. 
Additionally, CRSO Real Property is tasked with ongoing efforts to consolidate Department real 
property, reducing overhead costs, and increasing operational efficiency. CRSO responds to 
Congressional and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) laws, regulations and guidance 

47QTCA22D003F / 70RDAD23FR0000117 
Real Property Management System (RPMS): 
Tririga – Maximo Application Suite (MAS) Implementation 
Page 3 of 70 
 
 
and, accordingly, DHS established a Strategic Consolidation Plan in 2019. The Plan directs 
CRSO to manage real property assets within the National Capital Region (NCR) including the 
DHS NCR Real Property Strategy established a ten-year timeframe with clear priorities through 
centralized planning and programming for proposed consolidations. 
 
 
 
To meet the goals of the OMB National Strategy for the Efficient Use of Real Property, the DHS 
NCR Real Property Strategy calls for optimizing the utilization of existing DHS real estate by 
measuring actual utilization with technology and divesting of space deemed unneeded based 
upon low utilization rates and in response to the DHS Headquarters Consolidation 
Accountability Act of 2015 (P.L. 114-150). 
1.2 The Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) 
 
OCIO is responsible for the overall management, planning, development, deployment, operation, 
maintenance, coordination, and evaluation of DHS technology programs and activities. Specific 
responsibilities include the following: 
• Acquisition and support of information technology (IT) and telecommunications 
hardware, software, and services 
• Requirements-based design and development of unique IT to support DHS mission 
objectives 
• Technology support of existing IT applications 
• Development, implementation, and evaluation of the effectiveness and efficiency of DHS 
OCIO programs including resource utilization, and service delivery 
• Integration of DHS strategic planning with automated information systems strategic 
planning activities to produce high - mission results 
• Ensuring compliance with DHS Capital Investment, IT Investment Management, 
Systems Engineering Life Cycle (SELC), DHS Information Governance and Privacy, 
DHS Records and Information management, Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act, and 
IT Security policies and procedures. 
1.3 The Office of the Chief Readiness Support Officer (OCRSO) 
 
OCRSO supports Component operational readiness by leading, governing, integrating, managing 
and capital planning for real property and assets, logistics and sustainability. 
2.0 Scope of Work 
 
OCRSO F&OS has a requirement for information technology, software, and support services to 
meet its mandated mission for real property portfolio management. The Contractor shall provide 
a Real Property Management System (RPMS) IT tool that is a single-source, scalable, cloud-
based solution to assist with overall agency services and responsibilities, such as, strategic space 
and facilities planning, project management, lease administration, and management of real 
property. OCRSO’s requirements are driven by its need for an interactive product and services 
to support its stakeholder community. OCRSO intends to procure a licensed software product. 

47QTCA22D003F / 70RDAD23FR0000117

Page 4 of 70 
 
 
The Contractor shall provide OCIO and OCRSO with solution analysis, engineering, design, 
development, and implementation support for new applications and enhancement and/or data 
migration support for applications in support of business needs. This support includes processes, 
procedures, labor, material, and information required to deliver, support, operate, and maintain 
 
 
the software aspects of the system. It also includes, as required, application troubleshooting for 
any identified issues; modifying the software system or component after delivery to correct 
faults; improving performance or other attributes; adapting to a changed environment or 
maintenance activities focused on anticipated problems; and performing preventative 
maintenance to support a continuously operating and reliable, stable, and secure application. 
The solution must be FedRAMP certified software-as-a-service (SaaS) and hosting infrastructure 
for both mission and business users throughout DHS OCRSO. DHS OCIO currently uses 
FedRAMP accredited cloud services such as Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services 
(AWS). 
 
The Contractor is expected to form a cohesive team with any DHS team members to include 
the Government and other contractors or vendors, by fostering transparency and information 
sharing for successful task execution. 
 
It is the Government’s intention to continually pursue improvements to processes and 
practices, which will result in meeting mission requirements. The Contractor is expected to 
partner with the Government to support this goal by actively studying existing processes and 
making recommendations for improvements. 
 
The Contractor shall meet the requirements detailed herein, using a tailored approach that blends 
DHS SELC, Agile/Scrum, SecDevOps methodologies as needed to meet the demands of the 
projects. The Contractor shall comply with all DHS and OCIO standards and regulations 
including those for development, performance, testing, project management, operations support, 
security, privacy, records management, and accessibility. 
 
To be responsive to its customers, the Government requires an experienced team of professionals 
with expertise in agile software development, project management, technical architecture and 
design, continuous integration and delivery, integration, testing, configuration management, 
ongoing operations and maintenance, and cloud migration. System must be physically Hosted in 
the Continental United States (CONUS). 
The Contractor shall provide support in accordance with all the services listed in this 
section. Specifically, the Contractor shall provide the below high-level activities per task 
identified: 
• Project Management 
• Business Analysis & Requirements Management
