STATEMENT OF WORK 
Hewlett Packard Multi -Jet Fusion  4200 3D Printer Maintenance Services  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 


COMFRC  CUI  Page 2 of 11 
1.0  Scope & Requirement Background  
The Fleet Readiness Centers Southeast (FRCSE) is an industrial facility that provides a wide variety of aircraft services 
including maintenance, repair and overhaul, as well as components manufacturing.  FRCSE currently utilizes two Hewlett 
Packard (HP) Multi Jet Fusion (MJF) 4200 3D printers to manufacture aircraft components.  This Statement of Work 
(SOW) defines the requirements for the Contractor to provide continuous preventive and corrective maintenance 
services to ensure these systems remain fully operational.   
 
1.1 Objectives 
The Contractor shall perform Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) certified maintenance and repair services for two 
(2) HP MJF 4200 3D printers, including build units and processing stations. 
 
2.0 Applicable Documents 
2.1 Fleet Readiness Center Southeast Work Restrictions (Enclosure 1). 
 
3.0 Requirements-   
3.1 The Contractor shall perform the following specific tasks:   
 
3.1.1     Freight and Shipping:  All items requiring shipping shall be included in the cost to maintain the systems and shall 
not be billed separately.   
 
3.1.2 Personnel Qualifications:  All services shall be performed by an OEM certified HP MJF Field Service 
Representative (FSR).   
 
3.1.3 Response Time:  All services requiring onsite support shall be accomplished within three (3) business days of 
notification unless otherwise noted in this SOW.  The Contractor shall document the date/time of notification 
and the date/time of arrival in the Maintenance Service Report (See attached CDRLs A001-AD01). 
 
3.2 Maintenance Tasks 
3.2.1 The Contractor shall provide all labor, equipment, tools, material, transportation and qualified personnel necessary 
to perform system recertification, annual comprehensive system maintenance and technical support services for the 
FRCSE HP MJF 4200 3D printers.    
 
3.2.2 Annual Comprehensive Maintenance Agreement 
3.2.3 Covered Systems: 
 
System Equipment Description Model Number (M/N) Serial Number (S/N) 
NAS System 1 HP Jet Fusion 4200 3D Printer M0P44B SG84334001 
NAS System 1 HP Jet Fusion 3D Build Unit M0P44B SG93N35008 
NAS System 1 HP Jet Fusion 3D Build Unit M0P44B SG93K35006 
NAS System 1 HP Jet Fusion 3D Processing Station M0P49C SG8BT36002 

COMFRC  CUI  Page 3 of 11 
System Equipment Description Model Number (M/N) Serial Number (S/N) 
NAS System 2 HP Jet Fusion 4200 3D Printer M0P44B SG88T34002 
NAS System 2 HP Jet Fusion 3D Build Unit M0P44B SG93N35004 
NAS System 2 HP Jet Fusion 3D Build Unit M0P44B SG91335007 
NAS System 2 HP Jet Fusion 3D Processing Station M0P49C SG86636002 
 
3.2.4 HP 3D Recertification Service (Base Year Only) The Contractor shall provide HP 3D Recertification Services for two 
(2) HP Jet Fusion 3D Build Units (Serial Numbers: SG93N35008 and SG93N35004) during the base year of the agreement. 
3.2.4.1 This recertification is required to reinstate comprehensive maintenance coverage following a lapse in 
service. 
3.2.4.2 The Contractor’s base price for this service shall include all labor, travel, and standard diagnostic testing 
required to perform a comprehensive physical inspection and system diagnostic evaluation on both build units. 
3.2.4.3 If the Contractor identifies that repairs or replacement parts are required to restore either build unit to 
OEM-certified operating standards during recertification: 
3.2.4.3.1 The Contractor shall submit a detailed quote identifying the required replacement parts to the 
Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) and Contracting Officer.   
3.2.4.3.2 The Contractor shall not proceed with any repairs, order parts, or perform work without formal 
written authorization and approval from the Contracting Officer (CLIN 0003 and CLIN 0004). 
3.2.5 The Contractor shall provide onsite hardware support for the HP MJF 4200 3D printers, build units, and processing 
stations to maintain system accuracy/reliability and minimize failures.  All onsite hardware support shall be performed 
as requested by the Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) for repairs or during scheduled kit installations. 
3.2.6 The Contractor shall provide all standard annual maintenance kits for the 3D Printer, Build Units, and Processing 
Station. These kits shall be either hand-delivered by the FSR during scheduled maintenance or shipped directly to the 
TPOC at no additional cost to the Government. 
 
3.2.7 The Contractor shall provide and install all new hardware modifications critical to the reliable and safe operation of 
the HP MJF 4200 system  at no additional cost to the Government. 
3.2.8 The Contractor shall provide all updates for the HP MJF 4200 3D-Production System controller software, Smart 
Stream software, and Control Center communications software . 
 
3.2.9 The Contractor shall ensure current and future software updates must be compatible with a version of the 
Windows® Operating System (OS) that is supported by the Microsoft Corporation Windows 10/11. 
 
3.2.10 The Contractor shall provide onsite maintenance, support, repair services within three (3) business days in the 
event of a system failure, inability to print parts, or other emergency repair at no additional cost to the government. 

COMFRC  CUI  Page 4 of 11 
 
3.2.11 The Contractor Shall replace or repair services and parts that render the machines inoperable require the 
Contractor to be onsite within three (3) business days to make repairs and replace parts.  Replacement of all damaged, 
worn, or inoperable system components shall be included.    
 
3.2.12 The Contractor shall utilize overnight shipment of replacement parts at no cost to the government to support 
next-day repair of system when the technician is onsite. 
 
3.2.13 The Contractor shall provide unlimited technical customer support via phone and email for system diagnostics, 
software issues, and application troubleshooting.  The Contractor shall respond to all inquiries within one (1) business 
day. 
 
3.2.14 The Contractor shall comply with FRCSE security protocols; the use of VPN (Virtual Private Network) remote 
access, or equivalent, is strictly prohibited for system diagnostics purposes. 
 
3.2.15 The Contractor shall provide One (1) basic operator training course for a minimum of one employee, per year. 
 
4.0 Deliverables: The Contractor shall submit the following: 
 
4.1 Maintenance Service Report (see CDRLA001): A detailed report of all work performed, parts replaced, and final 
system status. 
 
6.0 Hours of Operation 
The contractor shall perform work during core business hours of 6:00 AM (0600) to 2:30 PM (1430) Eastern Standard 
Time (EST), Monday through Friday, and shall not include after-hours, weekends, or federal holidays. 
 
6.1 Federal Government Holidays:  The Contractor shall observe the official federal holidays observed by the U.S. Office 
of Personnel Management (OPM). 
 
• New Year’s Day      (January 1) 
• Martin Luther King Jr.’s Birthday   (Third Monday in January) 
• Presidents Day      (Third Monday in February) 
• Memorial Day     (Last Monday in May) 
• Juneteenth National Independence Day   (June 19) 
• Independence Day     (July 4) 
• Labor Day      (First Monday in September) 
• Columbus Day      (Second Monday in October) 
• Veterans Day      (November 11) 
• Thanksgiving Day     (Fourth Thursday in November) 
• Christmas Day      (December 25) 
 
A.  When a designated legal holiday falls on a Sunday, the following Monday will be observed. When a 
holiday falls on a Saturday, the preceding Friday will be observed.  This list of holidays relates to 
Government duty days and is not intended to supplement or otherwise alter the provisions of any Wage 
Determination regarding applicable paid holidays 
 
B. It is understood and agreed between the Government and the Contractor that observance of such days 
by Government personnel shall not be a reason for an additional period of performance, or entitlement 
of compensation, except as set forth within the contract 
 

COMFRC  CUI  Page 5 of 11 
C. When the Department of War grants excused absence to its employees, the Contractor shall continue to 
provide sufficient personnel to perform critical tasks already in operation or scheduled and shall be 
guided by the instructions issued by the Contracting Officer (KO) or the TPOC. Changes in employee 
work schedules shall comply with the terms and conditions of the contract, to include payment 
provisions. 
 
        E.   Inclement Weather Operations:  The Contractor shall perform all scheduled maintenance/repair services 
as scheduled including during periods of inclement weather.  In accordance with FAR 52.212-4(f) if 
severe weather prevents safe performance, the Contractor shall notify the TPOC in writing to request a 
performance delay.  and Approval is at the discretion of  the TPOC The Contractor shall not request any 
additional cost for schedule changes due to inclement weather. 
7.0 Security Requirements:  The security requirements specified herein shall apply to the Contractor and all 
subcontractors.  The Contractor shall comply with applicable government security regulations and requirements. 
 
7.1. Public Release: All Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) pertaining to this contract shall not be released for 
public dissemination, including posting to any social media sites such as Facebook or Twitter, unless it has been 
approved for public release by appropriate U.S. Government authority.  Proposed public releases shall be submitted for 
approval prior to release through: Public Affairs Office, Commander, Fleet Readiness Center, 47038 McLeod Road, BLDG 
447, Patuxent River, MD 20670-1547. 
 
7.2. Non-Personal Service Statement: Contractor management will ensure that employees properly comply with the 
requirements outlined in this SOW.  Contractor employees will perform their duties independent of, and without the 
supervision of, any Government official or other Defense Contractor.  The tasks, duties, and responsibilities set forth in 
this project shall not be interpreted or implemented in any manner that results in any Contractor employee creating or 
modifying Federal policy, obligating the appropriated funds of the United States Government, overseeing the work of 
Federal employees, providing direct personal services to any Federal employee, or otherwise violating the prohibitions 
set forth in Parts 7.5 and 37.2 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR).  
 
7.3. Personnel Removal: Government rules, regulations, laws, directives, and requirements that are issued during the 
term of the contract relating to law and order, installation administration, and security shall be applicable to all 
Contractor employees and representatives who enter the installation. Violation of such rules, regulations, laws, 
directives, or requirements shall be grounds for removal (permanently or temporarily as the Government determines) 
from the work site or installation. Removal of employees does not relieve the Contractor from the responsibility for the 
work defined in this SOW. The Contractor is expected to provide support services despite personnel removal or other 
unforeseen condition(s). Should replacement become necessary, the Government reserves the right to review all 
resumes of proposed candidates. 
 
• Removal by Installation Commander: The Installation Commander may, at his/her discretion, bar an individual 
from the installation under the authority of 18 U.S.C. 1382 (1972), for conduct that is determined to be contrary 
to good order, discipline, or installation security and safety. 
 
• Removal Requested by Designated Government Representative (DGR): The DGR may require the Contractor to 
remove an employee working under this contract for reasons of misconduct or security violations. Contractor 
employees shall be subject to dismissal from the premises upon determination by the DGR that such action is 
necessary in the interest of the Government.

Attachment A – Operations Engineering and Security Services (OESS) 
 
 
HHS Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) 
Office of Operations (OPS) Engineering and Security Services (OESS) 
Statement of Objectives (SOO) / Hybrid Performance Work Statement 
 
Document Intent Defines the outcomes, required capabilities, and selected task-level 
performance requirements for the OESS task order. 
Approach 
Hybrid SOO/PWS framing. Objectives are outcome-based, but where 
precision improves performance administration, task-level requirements 
and service levels are stated explicitly. 
 
1. Background 
The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) protects the health and well-being of all 
Americans through a diverse portfolio of programs and services. The Office of the Chief Information 
Officer (OCIO) Office of Operations (OPS) provides the technological foundation that enables these 
programs to operate effectively and securely. HHS OCIO OPS maintains an enterprise infrastructure 
that spans data centers, cloud environments, collaboration tools, cybersecurity platforms, and 
supporting operational systems serving tens of thousands of users. 
Over time, operations and engineering services have been performed under multiple discrete efforts. 
That fragmentation has contributed to duplicative practices, uneven modernization, and inconsistent 
service levels. This task order consolidates OPS Engineering and Security Services (OESS) into a unified 
enterprise support construct intended to improve governance, standardize engineering and 
operations processes, strengthen cybersecurity and Zero Trust implementation, and accelerate 
migration from legacy environments to secure modern services. 
This Attachment A establishes the objectives, required capabilities, and measurable performance 
requirements for the OESS task order. The Contractor shall provide the personnel, processes, and 
technical services necessary to engineer, operate, secure, and continuously improve endpoint, 
infrastructure, network, collaboration, and related enterprise services in support of HHS OCIO 
Operations. 
The intended outcome of this task order is robust, flexible, efficient, and secure information 
technology that enables the HHS enterprise and its mission partners to meet operational 
requirements with high availability, strong cybersecurity, disciplined governance, and timely service 
delivery. 
In performing this task order, the Contractor shall support the HHS goals and CIO priorities for 
OneHHS by helping the Government operate HHS as a single, strategic, shared enterprise. The 
Contractor shall support measurable policy implementation, healthy operational patterns, 
sustainable government value, enterprise visibility, security, interoperability, portability, and reuse 

Attachment A – Operations Engineering and Security Services (OESS) 
 
 
across the full lifecycle of IT investments and operations. All work performed under this task order 
shall reinforce enterprise-aligned behaviors, measurable outcomes, and government control where 
feasible over accounts and tenancy, identity and access, logging and auditability, data portability, and 
transition and exit rights. 
• Establish and manage endpoint and infrastructure engineering processes that improve end-to-
end integration and service delivery. 
• Perform endpoint and infrastructure engineering across requirements definition, design, 
development, integration, testing, implementation, and sustainment support. 
• Perform design analysis, requirements analysis, alternatives analysis, capacity analysis, 
concept-of-operations development, and related technical documentation. 
• Manage engineering and integration projects for current and future HHS OCIO-managed 
hardware and software. 
• Develop engineering planning documentation and maintain an Engineering Test Lab, including 
government-approved procurement support as needed. 
• Evaluate, test, and document COTS and GOTS software and hardware solutions, including 
engineering and development toolsets. 
• Coordinate activities across system interface boundaries with other contractors, service 
providers, and government organizations. 
• Integrate service delivery processes with government processes to provide seamless user 
experience. 
• Provide Tier 3 support through government-furnished service management workflows and 
approved escalation procedures. 
• Promote IT innovation through research, assessments, and studies of evolving technologies 
and industry best practices. 
• Adhere to incident, problem, change, release, and configuration management requirements 
and all applicable federal and HHS security, privacy, and accessibility mandates. 
2. Scope and Scale of OESS  
The scope includes support necessary to advance enterprise requirements that improve the HHS as 
OneHHS. Accordingly, the Contractor shall perform this task order in a manner that maximizes shared 
services, enterprise visibility, control, usability, purpose alignment, security, cost efficiency, 
governance streamlining, architecture reuse, portability, interoperability, measurable value, and 
sustainable government rights across supported platforms, environments, tools, identities, and data 
flows. 

Attachment A – Operations Engineering and Security Services (OESS) 
 
 
The Contractor shall provide engineering, operational, cybersecurity, and management support 
necessary to administer, manage, and perform the duties and responsibilities described in this order. 
The Government will maintain the authoritative listing of supported sites, systems, hardware, 
software, and other in-scope assets in the applicable Section J attachments and appendices. The 
Contractor shall maintain the currency of those inventories and supporting appendices as directed by 
the Government. 
• Task 1 - Management 
• Task 2 - Infrastructure Engineering 
• Task 3 - Infrastructure Operations* 
• Task 4 - Information Assurance* 
• Task 5 - Cloud-Based Infrastructure/Identity Management Services 
3. Period and Place of Performance 
The place of performance includes Government facilities, supported HHS sites, and approved hybrid 
or remote work locations as authorized by the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR). VTC and 
Network Operations personnel shall be local to support onsite deployments and response activities in 
the Washington, DC and Maryland metropolitan areas. Other teams may support the task order 
through a hybrid or remote staffing model when approved by the Government and when 
performance requirements continue to be met. 
The Government will identify supported sites in the applicable Section J documentation. The 
Contractor shall support those sites and any approved additions, deletions, or changes directed under 
the task order. 
The Government anticipates a period of performance for a twelve (12) month base period and 
potential for four (4) twelve-month option periods. 
4. Operating Hours 
Unless otherwise directed, the Contractor shall provide support between 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. 
Eastern Time, Monday through Friday, excluding Federal holidays. The actual daily start and stop 
times shall be coordinated with and approved by the COR. All teams shall maintain an on-call roster 
to support after-hours escalation and mission needs. The Network Operations Center (NOC) and 
Security Operations Center (SOC) functions shall be operated on a continuous 24x7x365 basis. 
Work outside standard hours may be required for emergency response, maintenance, deployments, 
cutovers, testing, or other mission needs. Exceptions to the standard operating hours shall be 
approved by the Government on a case-by-case basis.

The Government anticipates a hybrid contract type, firm fixed price (FFP) for baseline effort and time-

greater specificity to manage performance, the objective includes required task-level capabilities and 
work products. The Contractor may propose efficient methods of performance but shall achieve the 
stated outcomes and comply with the performance requirements in Section 10.

6.1 Requirements for Enterprise Outcomes Supporting OneHHS Goals and CIO Priorities 
• Promote enterprise-aligned behavior, measurable outcomes, and healthy operational 
patterns that improve security, mission delivery, and long-term government value across 
HHS. 
• Increase enterprise visibility by maintaining inventory, registry linkage, logging, 
traceability, and authoritative reporting for assets, identities, environments, tools, and 
data flows within the task order scope. 
• Leverage and expand shared services and common operating models where practical so 
that solutions are reusable, measurable, portable, and positioned for enterprise-wide 
adoption. 
• Support a unified identity, connectivity, and security posture across HHS by aligning 
engineering and operations activities to common standards, shared platforms, and 
interoperable services. 
• Design and operate architecture, tools, and processes to preserve government control 
where feasible over tenancy, access, logs, data governance, portability, and transition or 
exit capability. 
• Use modular planning, phased delivery, and evidence-based performance management so 
the Government can verify outcomes, scale successful approaches, and reduce lock-in, 
duplication, and waste. 
Objective 1 - Management 
Program Management 
• Provide unified direction, planning, oversight, and delivery governance for all work under 
the task order, including cost, schedule, technical performance, quality, staffing continuity, 
and timely completion of contractual deliverables. 
• Establish and maintain the management structure, processes, and reporting mechanisms 
necessary to direct the full body of OESS work in coordination with HHS OCIO leadership, 
mission objectives, and OneHHS enterprise priorities. 
• Provide strategic direction through the Program Manager and maintain continuity of 
operations through a designated Deputy Program Manager who coordinates day-to-day 
integration among capability leads and supports continuity in the Program Manager's 
absence. 
• Maintain the Integrated Master Schedule, risk and issue logs, action tracker, staffing and 
succession data, and performance dashboards that give the Government current visibility 
into status, dependencies, resourcing, and emerging concerns. 

Attachment A – Operations Engineering and Security Services (OESS) 
 
 
• Monitor milestones, verify deliverable quality, evaluate issues affecting cost, schedule, or 
technical results, and develop recommendations and corrective actions for Government 
decision-making. 
• Support audits, reviews, data calls, invoice coordination, and performance reporting, and

• Promote collaboration among all work areas, maintain consistent documentation

PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), OI&T, IO, ICSM has an expansion hardware and software requirements for brand-name Yubico and Intercede, or equivalent to provide a token-based multi-factor authentication (MFA) and certificate management system to support privileged credential usage. The physical Universal Serial Bus (USB) connector types must be USB-A and USB-C. The MFA solution may be deployed in an on-premise, cloud-based or hybrid environment. For any proposed Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solutions, the Offeror must be Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) authorized.

  

Currently, the CyberArk tool provides privileged account security to protect data, assets and infrastructure at VA locations throughout the United States (US) and territories. The expanded MFA solution must integrate with VA’s enterprise CyberArk platform to support 180 VA locations. 

 

Additionally, VA is seeking an outsourced logistics solution to store, manage and issue tokens. This procurement shall include hardware, software licensing, maintenance, and technical support services. Initial installation services of certificate database are required for this procurement.   


The Contractor shall electronically deliver the software licenses and subscriptions upon contract award. Physical token delivery shall be phased by the Government by site location and quantity and shall be completed in accordance with the delivery requirements in Section 4.0. The Contractor shall complete any required ramp-up activities to include creating, securing, and validating online ordering website for the procurement of tokens within 45 days after award. 

The Period of Performance (PoP) shall include one 12-month base period to begin on August, 25, 2026 through August, 24, 2027 with four 12-month option periods for continued maintenance and one optional task. The total PoP shall not exceed 60 months.

NOTICE OF THE FEDERAL ACCESSIBILITY LAW AFFECTING ALL INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY (ICT) PROCUREMENTS (SECTION 508)

On January 18, 2017, the Access Board issued a final rule that updated accessibility requirements covered by Section 508 and refreshed guidelines for telecommunications equipment subject to Section 255 of the Communications Act. The final rule went into effect on January 18, 2018. The revisions and updates to the Section 508-based standards and Section 255-based guidelines are intended to ensure that information and communication technology (ICT) covered by the respective statutes is accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities.

SECTION 508 – INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY (ICT) STANDARDS

The Section 508 standards established by the Access Board are incorporated into, and made part of all VA orders, solicitations and purchase orders developed to procure ICT. These standards are found in their entirety at: Revised 508 Standards and 255 Guidelines (access-board.gov). A single PDF file version of the Revised Section 508 Standards and 255 Guidelines will be supplied upon request, or can be obtained from the Access Board website. Federal agencies must comply with the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as amended. 

The Contractor shall comply with “508 Chapter 2: Scoping Requirements” for all electronic ICT and content delivered under this contract. Specifically, as appropriate for the technology and its functionality, the Contractor shall comply with the technical standards marked here: 

	E204 Functional Performance Criteria

	E206 Hardware Requirements

	E207 Software Requirements

	E208 Support Documentation and Services Requirements

COMPATABILITY WITH ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY

The standards do not require installation of specific accessibility-related software or attachment of an assistive technology device. Section 508 requires that ICT be compatible with such software and devices so that ICT can be accessible to and usable by individuals using assistive technology, including but not limited to screen readers, screen magnifiers, and speech recognition software.

ACCEPTANCE AND ACCEPTANCE TESTING

Deliverables resulting from this solicitation will be accepted based in part on satisfaction of the Section 508 Chapter 2: Scoping Requirements standards identified above.

The Government reserves the right to test for Section 508 Compliance before delivery. The Contractor shall be able to demonstrate Section 508 Compliance upon delivery.

INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY USING SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTS

The Contractor shall comply with Sections 524 and Sections 525 of the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007; Section 104 of the Energy Policy Act of 2005; Executive Order 14148, “Initial Rescissions of Harmful Executive Orders and Actions,” dated January 20, 2025; Executive Order 13221, “Energy-Efficient Standby Power Devices,” dated August 2, 2001; and the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) to provide ENERGY STAR® certified and Federal Energy Management Program (FEMP) Designated Low Standby Power information technology products, see https://www.energy.gov/femp/search-energy-efficient-products. See http://www.energystar.gov for complete product specifications and updated lists of Energy Star certified products. FEMP low standby power product listing can be found at https://www.energy.gov/femp/low-standby-power-product-list.

The Contractor shall provide products that meet the definition of sustainable products if the products are delivered to the Government; furnished by the Contractor for use by the Government, incorporated into the construction of a public building or public work, or acquired by the Contractor for use in performing services under a Government contract where the cost of the products is a direct cost to a Government contract (versus costs which are normally applied to a contractor's general and administrative expenses or indirect costs).

Specifically, the Contractor shall provide sustainable products under this contract in accordance with RFO 52.223-23 (NOV 2025). The applicable products with their associated certification and/or designation required (e.g. Energy Star, FEMP Low Standby Power) are identified within the product requirements specifications in this PD. The Contractor shall self-certify that its proposed products meet the certification(s) and/or designation(s) specified.

For software/subscription delivery: The Contractor will deliver all software/ subscription information to VA Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) - Michael Preyer; Michael.Preyer@va.gov, upon contract award. 

For token shipment: Under a Token-as-a-service model and web-based ordering system, the Contractor will manage and distribute tokens to Government identified individual and bulk addresses. The Government may issue phased token orders by site location and quantity throughout the PoP. For each order placed by the Government, the Contractor shall deliver the ordered tokens no later than 30 days after order placement. The Government will provide the applicable shipping addresses, site locations, and quantities at the time each order is placed. 

SPECIAL SHIPPING INSTRUCTIONS

Prior to shipping, Contractor shall notify Site POCs, by phone followed by email, of all incoming deliveries including line-by-line details for review of requirements. The Contractor shall not make any changes to the delivery schedule at the request of Site POC.

Contractors shall coordinate deliveries with Site POCs before shipment of hardware to ensure sites have adequate storage space.

All shipments, either single or multiple container deliveries, shall bear the VA IFCAP Purchase Order number (if applicable) on external shipping labels and associated manifests or packing lists. In the case of multiple container deliveries, a statement readable near the VA Integrated Funds Distribution, Control Point Activity, Accounting and Procurement (IFCAP) Purchase Order (PO) or Contract number shall indicate total number of containers for the complete shipment (e.g. “Package 1 of 2”), clearly readable on manifests and external shipping labels.

Packing Slips/Labels and Lists shall also include the following:

IFCAP PO # or Contract No.: ____________ (e.g., 166-E11234 (the IFCAP PO number is located in block #20 of the Standard Form, SF 1449))

Project Description:  (e.g. Tier I Lifecycle Refresh)

Total number of Containers:  Package ___ of ___. (e.g., Package 1 of 3)

GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

VA TECHNICAL REFERENCE MODEL

The Contractor shall comply with the VA OIT Technical Reference Model (VA TRM). Compliance with the VA TRM is achieved by using only technologies and standards that are listed as approved for use in the VA TRM. The Contractor shall provide all necessary information requested by VA to ensure TRM approval is obtained prior to use on VA’s network.

ZERO TRUST – VA CRITICAL SECURITY CONTROLS

VA has established minimum mandatory security requirements and requires that any network connected software system or service must meet the VA Critical Security Controls as outlined in the VA Memorandum, “VA Security Controls”, https://www.voa.va.gov/DocumentView.aspx?DocumentID=5010. VA Critical Security Controls identify the minimum mandatory requirements that must be implemented across all VA enterprise infrastructure, cloud computing environments, information systems, networks, and specialized devices (medical devices/systems, special-purpose systems, and research scientific computing devices) that process, store, and/or transmit VA data. Effective July 1, 2025, the Contractor shall implement these VA Critical Security Controls, within any network connected software system or service prior to being authorized for use in the VA. This functional requirement is not negotiable, and Plan of Action & Milestones (POAM) will not be accepted in the event these controls cannot be implemented for new systems. Critical Security Controls are intended to increase VA’s security posture and provide security and privacy risk visibility into the VA network and is not a new requirement. The Contractor’s failure to maintain these VA Critical Controls after implementation will result in VA discontinuing the use of the system.

SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER (SSN) REDUCTION 

The Contractor solution shall support the Social Security Number (SSN) Fraud Prevention Act (FPA) of 2017 which prohibits the inclusion of SSNs on any document sent by mail. The Contractor support shall also be performed in accordance with Section 240 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act (CAA)

WHS/AD intends to issue a sole source contract to Northern Technologies Group Inc. 14413 N Nebraska Ave Tampa, FL 33613 for Special Access Program Information Technology (SAP IT) System engineering and Capabilities Support Services. The Government seeks to acquire the Special Access Program Information Technology (SAP IT) System Engineering and Capabilities Support Services, which will support Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation (RDTE) efforts for Special Access Program (SAP) Information Technology (IT) initiatives aimed at enhancing access to the current environment within all SAP programs across the Department of War (DoW).

The intended outcome is to sustain high levels of system reliability, security, and performance, thereby supporting the department’s mission-critical functions. BACKGROUND

The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is conducting market research to identify alternative sources that (a) are capable of meeting NIST’s minimum requirements for the following commercial products and commercial services and (b) would be interested in competing for that requirement:

Contractor shall be responsible for all labor, tools, material, equipment, and software required to upgrade the existing Alerton Envision Building Automaton System (BAS) to Alerton Compass 2 (or the latest stable version). See attached draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) and Attachment A. 

NIST has not yet determined its acquisition strategy for this requirement and encourages interested sources to respond to this Notice. 

If NIST’s market research indicates there are alternative sources that are capable and interested in competing to fill this requirement, separate and apart from Albireo Energy LLC (UEI Y6M1DKF55BF3) then NIST will consider conducting a competitive acquisition in accordance with law and regulation. To be clear, NIST’s identification of Albireo Energy LLC in this Notice does not constitute a binding commitment or obligation for it to conduct a sole source procurement with Albireo Energy LLC for this requirement.

Instructions for Responding to Respond to This Notice

Parties that respond to this Notice are requested to voluntarily submit the requested information via email in Microsoft Word, Adobe PDF, and/or Microsoft Excel format to the designated point(s) of contact whose name and email address appears at the bottom of this notice. Please provide only the information requested by this Notice, and do not include proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information in a response to this Notice. 

Information Requested in Response to This Notice: To help NIST with its market research, NIST is requesting that industry sources carefully review this notice and any attachments to it and voluntarily provide the following information:  

Company Summary

Notice Identification: Notice ID and Title of this posting.

Corporate Details: Company name, physical address, website address, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI).

Point of Contact (POC): Name, phone number, and email address.

Company Size Standard: Your company’s size status relative to the NAICS code provided in this Notice. (Refer to the SBA Table of Small Business Size Standards).

System for Award Management (SAM) Registration: Indicate whether your company has an active registration for procurement purposes in SAM.gov.

Feedback for Draft Requirements

Review the potential requirements/minimum specifications included with this Notice. Then, please provide suggestions to (a) improve clarity of it; (b) to make it more competitive; (c) to indicate whether there anything in it that may inadvertently exclude domestic involvement; and (d) to indicate how the requirements could potentially be revised to improve the ability for domestic (“Made in America”) end products to be considered.

Information Regarding Your Company’s Products and Services

Provide specifications, company name of the original equipment manufacturer, and the country of manufacture for products and services that your company is legally authorized to sell and that may meet NIST’s minimum requirements. 

Indicate whether, in your opinion, the product(s) meet the definition of (a) commercial product or (b) commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) item or COTS item as described at https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-2 and, if so, which definition applies ((a) or (b)).

Indicate whether, in your opinion, the service(s) meet the definition of commercial service as described at https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-2. 

Standard Commercial Pricing: Provide your company’s standard commercial pricing information for the identified products and services and explain what is included in those standard prices. 

Estimated Price Range: You may provide an estimated price or price range for the requirements, including a brief explanation of how the price estimate was developed.

Standard Commercial Terms and Conditions: Provide a copy of the standard commercial terms and conditions for the commercial products and commercial services identified in the response to this notice, including nature and duration of standard commercial warranty.

Regulatory and Supply Chain Compliance

Indicate whether your company could comply with FAR Clause 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting (OCT 2022) if this acquisition were to be set aside for small businesses. Provide a brief supporting explanation.

Existing Governmentwide Contract Vehicles

Indicate whether your company has its own GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) contract or other federal contract vehicles under which NIST could award an order and, if so, provide the contract details (contract number, Contracting Officer name/contact, SOW, terms and conditions, and price lists).

We truly appreciate your company’s willingness to provide the above-mentioned information which NIST will be valuable in helping NIST complete its market research.

Important Notes

This Notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract or otherwise pay respondents to this notice for information provided in response to this Notice. Following a review of the responses and market research, NIST may publish a solicitation on an authorized site, depending on the chosen acquisition strategy. Responses received after the closing date for this Notice may not be considered.

QUESTIONS ABOUT THIS NOTICE

For additional information, please contact the primary contact or, if named, secondary contact identified at the bottom of this notice.

THANK YOU

Thank you for taking the time to read this notice and for your interest in helping NIST with its efforts to maximize competition!

The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is a 576-acre facility consisting of thirty-six (36) mixed use (mainly office and research laboratory) buildings. II. PURPOSE

Contractor shall be responsible for all labor, tools, material, equipment, and software required to complete the specified upgrade. Contractor must maintain the systems for the first year to ensure systems are in proper operating order.  The years that follow system installed, Alerton Compass 2 server will be added to the existing Alerton Envision network and maintained accordingly.  

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

The place of performance shall be at NIST, Gaithersburg Campus. Upgrade and maintenance service shall be performed during normal business hours (7am – 5 pm Monday through Friday, excluding, weekends and Federal Holidays).

This is one year after the contract was signed.

The Contractor shall perform a comprehensive backup of the existing database to CD, DVD or flash drive to include points, trend logs, alarms, programming, graphics, and historical data.

Task 2 –   Graphics Revisions

The Contractor shall maintain all graphics at each of the applicable workstations.

Task 3 – Programing Diagnostics

The Contractor shall perform diagnostics of programs and make recommendations for change/correction to meet original control performance requirements. After consulting with NIST COR the contractor shall make changes to programming to achieve the performance requirement.

Notice of Intent to Sole Source  
Soldier Monitoring System (SMS) Life Cycle Management and Sustainment  
Oﬃce: U.S. Army Capabilities Program Executive for Simulation, Training, Testing and Threats 
(CPE ST3), Orlando, FL 32826-3276  
 Tentative Product Service Code (PSC): 5825 Radio Navigation Equipment – Except Airborne  
Tentative NAICS Code: 518210 Data Processing, Hosting, and Related Services  
General Information  
Contract Opportunity Type: Special Notice (Notice of Intent to Sole Source).  
Original Published Date: 30 July 2026  
Response Date:  07 August 2026  
Place of Performance: Multiple locations including Fort Benning, GA; West Point, NY; Fort 
Rucker, AL; Fort Sill, OK; Yuma Proving Ground, AZ; Fort Campbell, KY; Fort Bragg/Camp Mackall, 
NC.  
Description 1. Notice of Intent to Sole Source 
The U.S. Army Capabilities Program Executive for Simulation, Training, Testing and Threats (CPE 
ST3), Product Manager Combat Training Instrumentation Systems (PdM CTIS), intends to award 
a sole source, ﬁrm-ﬁxed-price contract to Black Ohm, 100 S McClintock Dr. Ste 200 Chandler, AZ 
85226, under the authority of RFO FAR 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other 
Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements.  
2. Background & Objective 
The Soldier Monitoring System (SMS) is the Army’s materiel solution for Soldier monitoring, 
safety, and training performance analysis. Military training contains signiﬁcant inherent risk, 
which is ampliﬁed during individual and isolated training such as land navigation. The SMS 
reduces these risks by providing persistent/real-time geo-tracking and automated alerts. The 
objective of this eﬀort is to ensure continuity and delivery of eﬃcient, eﬀective, and quality 
services of upgraded or new solutions to the nation’s warﬁghters.  
3. Scope of Work   
The Contractor shall provide life cycle management to ensure SMS technology and equipment 
are maintained at or above 95% Availability (Ao) and provide necessary support desk 
capabilities. This eﬀort enables PdM CTIS to perform life cycle management in support of SMS 

including Continuous Technology Refresh (CTR), technology insertion, concurrency, upgrades, 
and disposal.  
Support services required for this eﬀort include maintaining or providing the following 
components:  
• Monitoring Station (MS): Graphical tracking, device status/alerts, and After-Action 
Review (AAR) playback. The MS normally consists of a laptop and a network connection.   
• Mobile Monitoring Device (MMD): Portable dismounted devices to monitor and locate 
Soldiers in the ﬁeld. MMD normally consists of a tablet and a network connection.  
• Soldier Worn Device (SWD): Small, rugged, waterproof GPS-enabled radios utilizing an 
LTE network with Soldier-initiated SOS capability. The SWD's built-in GPS transmits precise 
location and status data over LTE for real-time monitoring.   
• Communication Network and SaaS: The SMS network connects devices via commercial 
cellular and LoRa to an AWS-hosted SaaS platform, accessible through an intuitive UI.  
• Additional Services: Help desk support, ﬁeld service, repair/replacement of damaged 
components, inventory management, training materials, and propagation studies.  
4. Period of Performance  
The anticipated Period of Performance (PoP) consists of one (1) 12-month Base Year and one (1) 
12-month Option Year.  
5. Cybersecurity & Compliance Requirements  
The Contractor must ensure solutions incorporate secure engineering principles in accordance 
with NIST SP 800-160 and meet DoD Risk Management Framework (RMF) requirements to 
maintain a FedRAMP Moderate Authority to Operate (ATO). Strict compliance with OPSEC, AT 
Level 1, and CUI handling procedures is required.  
Submission Instructions / Public Note  
THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. However, 
interested parties may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement or 
submit proposals. All responses received prior to the stated submission deadline will be 
considered by the Government.  The Government is not responsible for any costs incurred as a 
result of responding to this notice.  
A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon 
responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received 

will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a 
competitive procurement.  
Capability statements, quotes, or proposals must be submitted electronically via email to the 
Point of Contact listed below no later than 07 August 2026 at 3:00pm.   
  
Contact Information Primary Point of Contact  
Robert Verica   
Contracting Oﬃcer  
Email: robert.j.verica2.civ@army.mil   
  
Secondary Point of Contact  
Denis M. Serrano Maldonado  
Contract Specialist  
Email: denis.m.serranomaldonado.civ@army.mil

The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) as a means of conducting market research or as a market survey to determine the availability of potential qualified vendors with the technical ability to provide all management, supervision, administration and labor for the HQR (Hospital Quality Reporting) Analytics, Reporting, Business Outcomes and Research (HARBOR) application development organization (ADO) services contract within the Centers for Clinical Standards & Quality’s (CCSQ) Information Systems Group (ISG). Specifically, this requirement aims to improve patient quality of care and consumer decision-making by Medicare providers and beneficiaries across the country, by collecting, computing, and publicly reporting outcomes-based hospital quality measure data on the Medicare.gov website. This contract will serve to maintain and develop upon a human-centric reporting system known as HQR (https://hqr.cms.gov/) that allows refinement, filtering, and data comparison, as well as the ability to view supplemental information. 

This requirement will define the Hospital Quality Reporting (HQR) system maintainer scope of work related to requirement gathering, design, development, enhancement, and maintenance. All services are provided to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code to this procurement is 541512 – Computer System Design Services.

THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME.  This request for information and vendor information does not constitute a request for proposal; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary; the Government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred.

REQUIRED CAPABILITIES include but are not limited to:

Experience with HARP/IDM integrations to CMS systems and the role Okta/Saviynt play.

Experience with CMS AWS cloud environments and tooling (DynamoDB, Postgres RDS, Glue, API Gateway, Cloudwatch, Inspector, ECR, etc).

Experience with Angular as a front-end framework and Jenkins for CI/CD.

Experience with business rules management systems, such as Drools (or alternatives) for Java-centric, complex processing of measure calculations.

Experience with Medicare claims data in the IDR and experience working with measure development software packages for validation and to produce claim-based measure outputs.

Experience with Provider demographic data sources and performing ID resolution to stitch together comprehensive and accurate provider profiles for Hospitals, ASCs, IPFs, and other facility types participating in the Hospital Quality Reporting programs.

Experience with the Hospital Quality Reporting measure inventory and tracking changes to measures year over year to assess product impacts. 

QUESTIONS REQUIRING WRITTEN RESPONSES:

Does your organization possess any of the capabilities listed above? Please provide relevant examples of your experience.

Does your organization leverage AI tooling on other federal contracts? If so, what efficiencies are you seeing in software development services contracts and has your organization been able to achieve FTE reductions in contract out years OR story point/capacity increases? Please provide a few examples of the tools and a benefit statement for each that summarizes overall savings or increased capacity on contracts.

For the questions above, please limit your response to 2 pages or less.

QUESTIONS (YES/NO):

Has your organization managed a Federal IT agile software development contract with roughly 100 FTEs and/or 6 or more sprint teams as a prime vendor? 

Does your organization possess experience calculating hybrid measures (such as Claims + EHR data)?

Does your organization possess experience managing a system that receives over 40 million production files, some of which are packaged zip files between 100 - 500MB?

Does your organization have experience with Digital Quality Measures (DQMs) and developing intuitive solutions to collect DQMs from healthcare providers? 

Does your organization have experience working within a ServiceNow platform for production support?

The purpose of this announcement is to provide potential sources with the opportunity to submit information regarding their capabilities to perform work for the CMS.

All interested parties, including all categories of small businesses (small businesses, small-disadvantaged businesses, 8(a) firms, women-owned small businesses, veteran-owned small businesses, service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses, and HUBZone small businesses) are invited to submit a response.  The capabilities package submitted by a vendor should demonstrate the firm’s ability, capability, and responsibility to perform the principal components of work listed below.  The package should also include past performance/experience regarding projects of similar scope listing the project title, general description, the dollar value of the contract and the name of the company, agency, or government entity for which the work was performed.

Organizations responding to this market survey should keep in mind that only focused and pertinent information is requested.  If significant subcontracting or teaming is anticipated in order to deliver technical capability, organizations should address the administrative and management structure of such arrangements.  Submission of additional materials such as glossy brochures or videos is discouraged. 

How to Respond to this Request for Information Notice

If your organization has the capability and capacity to perform as a prime contractor, one or more of the services described in this notice, please respond to this notice and provide written responses to the following information.  Please do not include any proprietary or otherwise sensitive information in the response, and do not submit a proposal.  Proposals submitted in response to this notice will not be considered.

Organization name, address, email addresses, Website and telephone number.

What size is your organization with respect to NAICS code identified in this notice (i.e., “small” or other than “small”)? If your organization is a small business under the aforementioned NAICS code, what type of small business (i.e., small disadvantaged business, woman-owned small business, economically disadvantaged woman-owned small business, veteran-owned small business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business, 8(a) or HUBZone small business)? Specify all that apply.

Although no geographic restriction is anticipated, if responding organizations are located outside of the Baltimore area, indicate how the organization would coordinate with the CMS program office located in Baltimore, Maryland to provide the support services.

Separately and distinctly describe which of the required capabilities listed above that your organization possesses and indicate your organization’s role (prime contractor, first-tier subcontractor, and/or supplier) in related contracts.  Please also provide the contract number, contract type, customer name, address and point of contact phone number and email address, contract value, thorough description of supplies and services included in the scope of that contract, indication of how they differ from the required capabilities described in this notice, period of performance (for services) or delivery date (for products), and any other relevant information.

For Electronic and Information Technology (EIT) product offerings relevant to this requirement, provide completed Voluntary Product Accessibility templates or other documentation that addresses compliance with the applicable standards (add website link) for those products.  For any federal customers that your organization has provided information technology services within the required capabilities areas, indicate how your company complies with applicable Section 508 standards (see buyaccessible.gov).

For any federal customers that your organization has provided applicable services, indicate how your company complies with environment laws and Federal regulations.

Indicate whether your organization offers any of the required capabilities described in this notice on one or more of your company’s own federal Government contracts (i.e., GSA Federal Supply Schedule contract or Government Wide Acquisition Contracts) that CMS could order from and, if so, which services are offered.  Also, provide the contract number(s) and indicate what is currently available for ordering from each of those contract(s).

Provide a standard, non-proprietary commercial pricing information for how your company sells, as a prime contractor, required capabilities described in this notice that your organization has experience providing.  Also indicate what is included in that pricing.

Disclaimer and Notes

Any organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization’s potential capability and capacity to perform the subject work.  Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted.  After a review of the responses received, a pre-solicitation synopsis may be published in Federal Business Opportunities.  However, responses to this notice will not be considered adequate responses to a solicitation.

DMEA Complex, 4234 54th Street, McClellan, CA (Buildings 1, 2, and 600)

Contractor Facility (as authorized by the Contracting Officer's Representative)

Submission Portal: Offers shall be submitted via email directly to the Contract Specialist, Ryan Tung (ryan.c.tung.civ@mail.mil)

SAM Registration: Offerors MUST have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) at the time of quotation submission to be eligible for award. 

WOSB status: Per FAR 19.1505(d) & (e), to submit an eligible offer, the business must be certified pursuant to 13 CFR 127.300 or have a pending application in the DSBS. If the firm is not certified or pending, the proposal will be removed from consideration.

The Government intends to make award without discussions. Proposals should be submitted initially on the most accurate and favorable terms from a price and technical standpoint. Offerors should not assume they will be contacted or afforded an opportunity to clarify, discuss, or revise their proposals.

File Format: Offerors should submit all proposal files in Microsoft Office product or Adobe PDF formats.

2.0 SCOPE & STANDARDS

The Department of War (DoW) Defense Microelectronics Activity (DMEA) Directors Action Group (DAG) requires professional, technical, and systems integration services to maintain, assess, and remediate its enterprise-wide risk management (ERM) and risk management and internal control (RMIC) program.

The Contractor shall support DMEA in maintaining compliance with DoDI 5010.40 (Enterprise Risk Management and Risk Management & Internal Control Program Instruction), DoW OMB A-123 implementation guidelines, and various quality and technical compliance frameworks, specifically:

ISO 9001:2015 (Quality Management Systems)

ISO/IEC 17025:2017 (General Requirements for the Competence of Testing and Calibration Laboratories)

All services shall be performed in strict accordance with the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS) DMEA 26-6F3.

3.0 INSTRUCTIONS TO OFFERORS (ADDENDUM TO FAR 52.212-1)

This solicitation is issued as an RFQ under open-market commercial simplified procedures. The Government intends to award a single contract resulting from this solicitation without discussions. Offerors are cautioned to submit their best technical and pricing terms initially.

Quotations shall be submitted electronically via email to ryan.c.tung.civ@mail.mil. The quotation shall be structured into two (2) separate and distinct volumes. The total page limit for the entire quotation is 12 pages, excluding the cover page, table of contents, and any resumes/certifications submitted as appendices.

Volume I: Technical Quotation (No Pricing Information)

The Technical Quotation must demonstrate the offeror's capability, commercial experience, and clear understanding of the PWS requirements. It must address the following three elements:

Technical Approach:

Detail the methodology for executing systems integration, control testing/auditing, and deficiency assessment (CPAR/DARA management) across DMEA's operations.

Describe the approach to maintaining compliance with the specialized standards defined in the PWS (DoDI 5010.40, ISO 9001, and ISO 17025).

Outline the strategy for preparing the annual DMEA A-123 Statement of Assurance deliverables.

Staffing and Labor Mix:

Provide a comprehensive staffing plan identifying proposed personnel and their qualifications.

Include a Labor Category & Hours Mapping Matrix. The offeror MUST propose specific commercial labor categories and hours mapped directly to the PWS task requirements (System Integration, Control Testing, Training, and Program Management) to demonstrate realism and capability.

Relevant Experience:

Provide up to three (3) examples of recent (within the last 3 years) and relevant open-market, federal, or commercial contracts of similar scope, size, and complexity.

Clearly highlight experience with DoD Risk Management, OMB A-123, or ISO 9001/17025 compliance environments.

Volume II: Price Quotation

The Price Quotation must contain the complete business/pricing proposal, including:

Fully Burdened Commercial Rates: A detailed pricing spreadsheet detailing the proposed commercial labor categories, hours, fully burdened hourly rates, and total prices corresponding to each Period of Performance (Base and all Option Periods).

Options Pricing: Evaluated in accordance with FAR 52.212-2.

Travel Costs: If travel is required, it shall be priced in accordance with the Joint Travel Regulations (JTR) as a non-burdened, cost-reimbursable line item. Do not include travel in the firm-fixed-price labor totals.

Representations and Certifications: A statement confirming that the offeror's representations and certifications are active and updated in SAM.gov in accordance with FAR 52.212-3.

Offers are due to the Contract Specialist, Ryan Tung, by 16:30 Pacific Standard Time (PST), Friday, 14 August 2026.  Via E-mail: ryan.c.tung.civ@mail.mil 

The Government may reject any or all quotations. The Government reserves the right to cancel this solicitation at any time. The Government will not reimburse any proposal preparation costs or other expenses incurred to respond to this notice.   

4.0 EVALUATION FACTORS AND BASIS FOR AWARD (ADDENDUM TO FAR 52.212-2)

4.1 Basis for Award

This procurement is being conducted under open-market commercial procedures (FAR Part 12). Formal source selection procedures described in FAR Part 15 do not apply.

The Government intends to award a single contract to the responsible offeror whose quotation represents the Best Value to the Government, price and other factors considered.

No adjectival ratings or numerical scores will be assigned. Award will be based on a qualitative best-value assessment of the quotations received. The Government will conduct a comparative narrative evaluation of quotations, documenting specific strengths, weaknesses, risks, labor-hour realism, and price analysis to determine which quotation represents the overall best value.

4.2 Relative Importance of Factors

The evaluation factors are listed below:

Technical Approach

Staffing and Labor Mix

Relevant Experience / Past Performance (Evaluated as Performance Risk)

Price

Technical Approach and Staffing/Labor Mix, when combined, are significantly more important than Price. Relevant Experience/Past Performance will be considered primarily for assessing performance risk. Price will become more important as quotations are evaluated as becoming more technically equal.

4.3 Factor Evaluation Methodology

Factor 1: Technical Approach

The Government will qualitatively evaluate the feasibility, efficiency, and clarity of the proposed methodology to perform the tasks in PWS Section 3.3.

This includes: the integration of IT process architectures with metric systems (PWS 3.3.1); the effectiveness of the proposed control testing and auditing process, root-cause assessment, and CPAR/DARA management (PWS 3.3.2 & 3.3.3); and the training execution plan (PWS 3.3.5).

Factor 2: Staffing and Labor Mix (Labor-Hour Realism)

The Government will evaluate the proposed Staffing and Labor Mix for realism, balance, and alignment with the Technical Approach.

The Government will assess whether the proposed commercial labor categories and qualifications are appropriate for the highly technical requirements (e.g., ISO 17025 calibration lab environments and DoDI compliance).

Proposing an unrealistic labor mix, unqualified personnel, or insufficient labor hours may be assessed as demonstrating a lack of understanding of the PWS, which will be documented as a risk or weakness.

Factor 3: Relevant Experience / Past Performance

The Government will evaluate the offeror's history of successful performance on recent and relevant projects to assign a Performance Risk Assessment (e.g., High Confidence, Low Confidence). This factor is utilized to assess the risk of unsuccessful performance.

Factor 4: Price

The Government will evaluate the price quotation for completeness, mathematical accuracy, and reasonableness.

The Government will perform a labor-hour realism analysis on the price volume to ensure the pricing matches the staffing details provided in Volume I.

Options: The Government will evaluate offers for award purposes by adding the total price for all options to the total price for the basic requirement. The evaluation of options shall not obligate the Government to exercise the option(s).

BACKGROUND

The Legacy VISN 17, Heart of Texas Health Care Network, requires a new Town Hall platform service that has integrated telephone capabilities to improve Veteran engagement. Gathering regular feedback from Veterans is essential for continuous healthcare improvement, but past virtual town halls have suffered from low attendance of 60 or fewer participants. Because Veterans queried less than four times a year often feel disconnected, leadership wants to implement push/pull technology that allows for real-time crowdsourcing and two-way communication through the use of polling questions and live Question and Answer sessions. The Telephone Town Hall (TTH) Services contract will enable executives to expedite feedback, discuss Veteran patient experiences, and keep Veterans updated on new services and options. It will provide a minimum of four TTH events per facility each year (4 TTHs/year for 8 facilities is 32 TTHs total/year), ensuring Veterans remain informed and actively involved in shaping their care. Since VA is renaming Veteran Information System Network (VISN) 17, VA Heart of Texas Health Care Network, to Health Service Area (HSA) 4.3, this PD refers to Legacy VISN 17 or HSA 4.3.

Introduction

This Request for Information (RFI) is for planning purposes only and shall not be considered an Invitation for Bid, Request for Task Execution Plan, Request for Quotation or a Request for Proposal. Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services described in this RFI. Your response to this RFI will be treated only as information for the Government to consider.  You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this RFI. This request does not constitute a solicitation for proposals or the authority to enter into negotiations to award a contract. No funds have been authorized, appropriated or received for this effort. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response. The Government does not intend to pay for the information submitted in response to this RFI.

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 541512 with a size standard of $34 million.  

2. Submittal Information:

All responsible sources may submit a response in accordance with the below information.  

There is a page limitation for this RFI of 15 pages. The Government will not review any other information or attachments included, that are in excess of the 15-page limit. NO MARKETING MATERIALS ARE ALLOWED AS PART OF THIS RFI. Generic capability statements will not be accepted or reviewed. Your response must address capabilities specific to the services required in the attached PWS and must include the following:

Interested Vendors shall at a minimum, provide the following information in the initial paragraph of the submission:

Name of Company

Address

Existing Contractual Vehicles (GWAC, FSS, or MAC)

Provide a summary of your capability to meet the requirements contained within the draft PWS for the following areas:

Provide a summary of your technical capability to meet the PWS requirements. 

Describe how you will incorporate AI-generated post-interaction summaries and real-time knowledge surfacing into agent workflow, training, and coaching. Include your QA approach for identifying and correcting inaccurate or incomplete AI-generated content before it becomes part of the permanent ticket record.

Describe how you will capture reductions in wrap-up time and handle time attributable to AI/automation tooling within your staffing and scheduling model, including the timeframe in which you expect to realize measurable staffing efficiency.

Describe any AI or automation capabilities you propose to build and operate independently of the Contact Center Infrastructure platform (e.g., internal workforce forecasting/scheduling, agent coaching analytics, ticket triage or escalation routing, internal QA sampling). For each, describe the data sources required and whether those sources are available to you today.


As agentic AI and self-service resolve a growing share of standard transaction types, describe how your staffing model, agent skill mix, and training approach will evolve to reflect a contact mix increasingly concentrated on complex or exception cases.


Describe your approach to handling escalations from agentic AI or self-service to a live agent, including how you will measure and report "AI-attempted then escalated" contacts distinctly from contacts handled entirely by an agent.


Describe how your proposed pricing structure will adjust as contact volume and contact complexity shift over the period of performance in response to AI-driven deflection and self-resolution. Include any built-in review or repricing mechanisms.


Describe your staffing elasticity model and redeployment/retention approach for affected personnel as automation reduces agent-handled contact volume over time.


Provide a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM), including projected labor categories, labor hours, estimated quantities, unit pricing, and any additional anticipated costs, to meet the Government's requirements. Please include assumptions used to develop the ROM, including if commercial pricing is available for any of the services.


Corporate experience or expertise in performing these services and specific examples or references.  Specific examples or references provided must include the agency, point of contact, dollar value, and contract number.

Your response shall include information as to available personnel and financial resources; full names of proposed team members and the PWS requirements planned to be subcontracted to them, which must include the prime planned percentage or the names of the potential team members that may be used to fulfill the set aside requirement. 

Has the draft PWS provided sufficient detail to describe the technical requirements that encompass the software development and production operations support services to be performed under this effort. 

______ YES _______ NO (if No, answer question f)

If “NO”, please provide your technical comments/recommendations on elements of the draft PWS that may contribute to a more accurate proposal submission and efficient, cost effective effort.

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA or “Government”) is committed to creating an interactive experience for its technology users that is easy, pleasant, effective, and personalized. As part of this commitment, the VA is seeking to improve its efficiency and effectiveness of interactions by maintaining Tier-0 (Self-Service Services) and Tier-1 (Enterprise Service Desk (ESD) Services) via a Multi-Vendor Service Provider (MVSP) approach, inclusive of a Tier-1 (ESD) prime vendor as well as a Contract Center Infrastructure (CCI) vendor from a separate contract.

The purpose of this PWS is to establish a Task Order (TO) that enhances service delivery, reduces cost, increases business focus, and improves the quality of Information Technology (IT) Services to End Users.

The following are key business objectives the VA expects to maintain and enhance the end user experience through vendors partnering via an MVSP environment: 

Improve VA End User efficiency and effectiveness by adopting and leveraging existing knowledge databases within VA’s IT Service Management (ITSM) tool and leading IT service management practices in the areas of customer logging, tracking, reporting, and resolving of IT Tickets and service Requests.

Improve efficiency and effectiveness by, early identification and Problem Resolution of Root Causes of technical issues including working with specialized Resolver Groups, such as VA staff and designated third parties, before they become trends.

Improve IT customer service and Ticket Resolution speed through continuous Service Availability (24x7x365), self-service capabilities, and skilled personnel in the areas of industry standard IT products and services.

Each vendor shall collaborate in an environment where Incidents and Requests for all applications and related infrastructure services related to End User Tier-0 and Tier-1 Services, are received, monitored, tracked, and successfully resolved. IT service management practices used to support the delivery of Services shall be based on Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL) best practices and any subsequent version of ITIL adopted in the IT industry and approved for use by VA. This ITIL based framework is a product of VA Office of Information and Technology’s (OIT) collaboration with business partners and industry and is being adopted to identify areas of improvement within the VA’s current organizational landscape.

The Tier-1 (ESD) vendor and CCI vendor shall provide a comprehensive Managed Services solution to support VA requirements for the Services briefly described below and as further defined within Section 5.4 (Managed Services Requirements). The MVSP shall support all VA staff located in Continental United States (CONUS) or Outside of the Continental United States (OCONUS) (e.g., American Samoa, Guam, Philippines, and Germany). All Services are to be provided in the English language, with Spanish Speaking service option as outlined in Optional Task Two. 

The scope of the ESD is to provide IT support to all End Users, VA designated executives/executive assistants/ VIP End Users, on a 24x7x365 basis. The Tier-1 (ESD) vendor shall serve as the Single Point of Contact (SPOC) for all VA End Users (VA employees and VA designated third parties that use or have access to VA approved applications, hardware, software, data, and services that enable them to conduct daily business). The Contractor also shall be responsible for the end-to-end ticketing of all approved VA technologies and will work with the VA’s IT Department and appropriate third parties that provide IT support or services to ensure VA employees, and VA designated third parties are not impeded by, or prevented from, conducting daily business operations due to issues with VA applications, hardware, software, or data networks. Background:

The Veteran Experience Services (VES) portfolio within the Office of Information & Technology (OIT) is seeking information from qualified vendors in support of the Patient Advocate Tracking System – Replacement (PATSR) — an effort to sustain and modernize VA's enterprise-wide patient advocacy case management platform. The primary effort involves ongoing operations, maintenance, and continuous enhancement of PATSR, a Microsoft Dynamics 365-based solution supporting more than 28,000 Patient Advocates and clinical staff across more than 150 VA Medical Centers and Community-Based Outpatient Clinics. The effort also includes integration sustainment across multiple enterprise VA systems and support for iterative modernization using Agile and DevSecOps practices. VA is releasing a DRAFT Performance Work Statement (PWS), which is attached for reference. Respondents are strongly encouraged to review and comment on those documents as part of their response.

Submittal Information:

Respondents are asked to provide information addressing each of the following areas. VA is seeking substantive, specific feedback not marketing materials. Responses should be organized by section number as listed below. NO MARKETING MATERIALS ARE ALLOWED AS PART OF THIS RFI. Generic capability statements will not be accepted or reviewed. Your response must include the following:

Relevant Technical Experience (Briefly describe your firm’s experience with any of the following). As part of your market research response, please provide a written submission of no more than 20 pages in Times New Roman or Arial 12-point font addressing the following:

Microsoft Dynamics 365 / Power Platform
Configuring, customizing, modernizing, and sustaining enterprise scale D365 model driven applications.

Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe), DevSecOps, and Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD)
Delivering software with unified development and O&M teams, implementing CI/CD pipelines, automated testing (functional, regression, accessibility, security), and supporting UAT in federal environments.

Enterprise O&M (Tier 4), Incident Response, and Monitoring
Providing Tier 4 support, including root cause analysis, emergency incident response, application performance monitoring, telemetry dashboards, and automated SLA testing.

Enterprise Integrations & Data Management
Supporting large-scale integrations across multiple enterprise systems (e.g., identity, clinical, eligibility), maintaining integration health, and developing operational/management dashboards (e.g., Power BI).

Human Centered Design (HCD) & User Experience

BACKGROUND

The Patient Advocate Tracking System – Replacement (PATS-R) is a mission-critical Veteran Health Administration (VHA) case management and patient experience system that supports the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) in addressing, tracking, and resolving inquiries, complaints, and compliments submitted by Veterans and their families. PATS-R plays a central role in ensuring that Veterans receive timely assistance and resolution of concerns across all VA medical facilities, consistent with statutory requirements under the Patient Advocate Tracker Act (2022) and other governing public laws and VHA directives.

PROGRAM OVERVIEW

PATS-R is a Microsoft Dynamics 365–based Platform-as-a-Service / Software-as-a-Service (PaaS/SaaS) solution operated within the VA-managed cloud architecture and supported by the Office of Information & Technology (OIT), Product Delivery Service (PDS). The platform is managed and hosted by the OIT Digital Transformation Center (DTC), which provides the shared delivery infrastructure for Dynamics applications across VA.

PATS-R serves more than 28,000 Patient Advocates and clinical/service line staff across more than 150 VA Medical Centers (VAMCs) and Community-Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOCs). walkthroughs for requirements 1 through 20. Please also confirm whether the 
Enhancement Objectives and walkthroughs must be completed during the base 
period or on a schedule established after award.

Items a & c:  Must be included in the quoted firm-fixed price. 
 
Item b:   The Enhancement Objectives may be established after scheduled award 
and an amendment is possible after the walkthoughs. 
 
The walkthroughs are required to be finalized within the base period and may 
provide clarity for the Enhancement Objectives.

1. Regulatory Compliance & Audit Controls: 
• Automated Section 289 Reporting: Generate compliance exports matching U.S. 
Department of the Interior reporting formats. 
• Indian Loan Guarantee, Loan Insurance & Interest Subsidy Program Workflows: Embed 
25 CFR § 103 criteria to track eligibility, approvals, and subsidy schedules. 
 
• Immutable Audit Trail: Log every field change, user timestamp, and loan status shift, per

Financial Transaction Reporting: Format and transmit data updates automatically using

• External-Institution Loan Transfer: Build secure tools to transfer full loan portfolio data or
