institutions (CDFIs). 
 
• Subsidy & Guarantee Co-Hort Tracking: Separate standard principal/interest streams 
from federal guaranteed subsidies or interest offsets within the general ledger (LAS). 
 
• Defaulted Loans: Pay Claim for loss, Loan assigned to DCI for Collections. 
 
• Debts not referred to Department of Treasury:  TROR report  (LAS) 
 
3. Data Integration & Financial Automation 
• Core Agency APIs: Connect data directly to agency ledgers to track active inflow/outflow 
flows (LAS). 
 
• Automated ACH/Wire Processing: Support loan fee payment execution, and real-time 
settlement tracking (LAS).

• Defaulted Loans:  LAS creates a new loan:  Extract Guarantee Loan data, Extract

• Tiered Underwriter Roles: Restrict approval limits by user tier (e.g., Tier 1 up to $50k, 
Executive over $150k).  Approvals based on uploaded required documents. 
 
• Multi-Factor Authentication: Enforce hardware or app-based MFA for internal teams 
managing sensitive financial records.

C. Data Rights and Licensing 
 
7. (RFQ Sec. 3.2; Sec. 3.1, FAR 52.227-19) Please clarify how the SHARE IT Act 
language, the Creative Commons Zero commitment, the code-posting requirement, 
FAR 52.227-14, and FAR 52.227-19 apply to a solution built on a pre-existing 
commercial software platform. Specifically, please confirm the treatment of: pre-
existing proprietary platform software, tools, and documentation; configuration, 
reports, documentation, and custom code first produced under the order; 
Government approval required before incorporating software that is not free and 
open source; and code and documentation subject to public posting, including the 
repository the Government will designate. 
 
Answer:  If the contractor's proposed solution is 100% custom code the SHARE 
IT Act applies. The contract specifies that all software, data, documentation, 
configuration code, and related materials first produced under this order must 
be released to the Government with Unlimited Rights under FAR 52.227-14. This 
includes all source code and documentation created in performance of the 
contract and must be made publicly available under the Creative Commons 
Zero (CC0) Universal Deed. The contractor must post all such developed code 
to the repository or repositories designated by the Government.  
 
Pre-existing proprietary software, commercial software platforms, tools, and 
documentation that were not first produced under this contract remain subject 
to their standard commercial licenses. FAR 52.227-19 governs these 
commercial computer software items, and they are not required to be released 
under CC0 or posted publicly.  
 
If the contractor proposes to incorporate any software that is not free and open 
source into the delivered solution, the contractor must obtain prior 
Government permission. The contractor must also promptly disclose and list 
all incorporated software that carries any restriction or limitation within the 
contract documentation.  
 
Only materials first produced under this contract—including custom code, 
configurations, reports, and documentation—are subject to the CC0 public 
domain commitment and the Government’s code-posting requirements.

Commercial or proprietary pre-existing software components are not subject to 
these posting requirements.

be treated in determining compliance with the applicable limitation on subcontracting. 
Answer:  Commercial license charges, hosting fees, and other platform-related 
pass-through costs are considered non-labor, non-service expenditures and are not 
included in the subcontracting base used to assess compliance with the 
limitation-on-subcontracting requirements 
The prime Indian Economic Enterprise (IEE) must perform the required percentage of

GENERAL INFORMATION

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

THIS IS A Sources Sought Notice ONLY. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) intends to award a firm fixed price sole-source contract to AgileRank LLC., for Real Time Location System Asset Tracking Handheld Software Application on a sole source basis. However, VA is conducting market research to determine if there are other brands of software available to meet VA’s requirements.  

This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes it does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ)/Invitation for Bid (IFB)/Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFQ, IFB or RFP in the future. This notice does not commit the VA to contract for any supply or service. Further, the VA is not seeking quotes,

bids or proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals in response to this sources sought notice. The VA will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. Submittals will not be returned to the responder. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future RFQ or IFB or RFP, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the Governmentwide Point of Entry. It is the responsibility of potential offerors to monitor the Governmentwide Point of Entry for additional information pertaining to this requirement. The anticipated NAICS code is: 541519, Other Computer Related Services with a size standard of 150 employees.

VA currently uses Real Time Location System (RTLS) Asset Tracking Handheld Software Application across 69 sites throughout the enterprise, representing a significant portion of VA’s operational footprint. RTLS software licenses to support ongoing maintenance, expansion, and standardization efforts at sixty-nine VA medical facilities. These licenses are essential for ensuring that asset tracking and management processes remain consistent and efficient across all sites.

Below are the minimum requirements and salient characteristics of the required software. If interested and capable of providing an alternate solution, please provide a capabilities statement detailing the specific software and how it meets the full requirement. Please also provide a pricing estimate.  

Email Responses by: August 15, 2026

Point of contact is Mr. Juan C. Perez, contract specialist at e-mail address juan.perez5@VA.GOV; phone 512-981-4467.

MOBILE TAGGING SOFTWARE SOLUTION

Provide a solution that is compatible with Current VA Interprise Asset Management LBI and have an agreement with Current VA Interprise Asset Management that will enable the software to perform all functions identified below:

INTEGRATION SERVICES: The mobile tagging application is fully integrated with Current VA Interprise Asset Management LBI instances in to include provision of Current VA Interprise Asset Management Tagging Connector licenses for each VISN. Contractor solution shall provide PIV-D/SSOi integration as required.

LICENSING: Provide a single license per facility for an unlimited number of users at each facility. The license should allow for a minimum of 5 simultaneous users at each site.  

USER SUPPORT: Provide help desk to respond to user queries during business hours, 8AM – 5PM (EST) Monday to Friday to include:

 

User support (respond to issues and queries.)

RTLS integration support

Security compliance and continuous monitoring. (Incident response per standards in Table 1.)

HELP DESK INCIDENT RESPONSE 

Table 1: Incident Response Time Limits

SCHEDULED RELEASES: Scheduled releases shall be coordinated with and approved by COR and installed to the maximum extent possible on weekends. Contractor shall include the following in scheduled releases: 

Communicate updates to end users

Defect logging and repair

New feature additions proposed by contractor

The contractor shall comply with the RTLS Change Control Process and obtain approval from the VA RTLS Change Control Board for material changes to the system. 

ADDITONAL SITE LICENSES (OPTIONAL): Provide a single license per facility for an unlimited number of users at each facility. The license should allow for a minimum of 5 simultaneous users at each site.

Requirement Description

The RTLS Handheld solution shall be accessible via a government issued VA TRM approved  iPhone, compatible with iPhone accessibility features, and shall be available for download by authorized  user

The RTLS Handheld solution shall not allow a duplicate entry of an asset to a given facility and shall provide notification to the user that the asset is already in the system.

The RTLS Handheld solution shall allow a tag that has been decommissioned to be associated with a new asset.

The RTLS Handheld solution shall allow decommissioning of any asset under any condition.

The RTLS Handheld solution shall include permission-based access specifically for reporting features

The RTLS Handheld solution shall include permission-based system administration for user management

The RTLS Handheld solution shall be compliant with NIST Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) and shall be compatible with iOS software

The RTLS Handheld solution shall be compatible with Transport protocol: HTTPS

The Contractor shall provide a user guide for the RTLS Handheld solution in PDF format that addresses:
• Installation of software on user device
• Access instructions
• Tagging process, instructions, guidelines, and best practices
• Report generation and access
• Frequently Asked Questions (derived from Help Desk Queries) 
• Use of Help Desk to answer user questions

The RTLS Handheld solution shall be capable of scanning and commissioning CenTrak® active RFID tags in Infor® LBI using built-in phone camera with VA Technical Reference Model (TRM) approved phones

The RTLS Handheld solution shall provide a downloadable list for items to be commissioned

The RTLS Handheld solution shall be capable of scanning bar codes

The RTLS Handheld solution shall be capable of scanning and decommissioning CenTrak® active RFID tags in Infor® LBI using built-in phone camera with VA Technical Reference Model (TRM) approved phones

The RTLS Handheld solution shall be compatible with production versions of iOS on the VA Technical Reference Model (TRM)

The RTLS Handheld solution shall support Bluetooth-connected FIPS Compliant Hardware 

The RTLS Handheld solution shall include the following reporting features:  
• Tags commissioned
• Tags commissioned by user
• Tags decommissioned
• Tags decommissioned by user

The RTLS Handheld solution shall include the following query features:
• Ability to view status of tags
• Prevention of commissioning of assigned tags 

The RTLS Handheld solution shall provide the capability to transfer data to the RTLS system wirelessly, where available.

The RTLS Handheld solution shall provide the capability to read a location off of a barcode. (Barcodes typically affixed at entries to rooms and other areas).

The RTLS Handheld solution shall provide the capability to manually enter its current location.

For wirelessly enabled handheld scanners, the RTLS Handheld solution shall provide the capability to identify its current location.

The RTLS Handheld solution shall give an error when it cannot sync with Infor® LBI

The RTLS Handheld solution shall enable other RTLS mobile utility modules to include
• Battery Management (optional task)
• Wifi Accuracy Testing (optional task)
• Ability to work in offline mode (no network connectivity)
• Automatic timeout after 5 minutes for of users that are not actively utilizing the application     

The RTLS Handheld solution shall provide data encryption in transit and at rest

The RTLS Handheld solution shall allow for the commissioning and/or decommissioning a tag and asset in under 60 seconds. 

The RTLS Handheld solution must meet 508 compliance requirements on the iPhone

Transaction time between the tag up activity and when data is associated in Infor® LBI shall be less than 60 seconds

The RTLS Handheld solution shall support at least 5 concurrent users per facility. Facility is defined by a facility that has a unique site ID.

The contractor shall provide an acknowlegement within 60 minutes of receipt/notification of a Critical severity incident and take immediate action to ensure reported incident is resolved. Average resolution time shall be no longer than 8 hours.

A Critical severity incident is defined as meeting one or more of the following criteria:
• Complete loss of functionality/system
• Functionality severely degraded
• Loss of those features or functionality that may compromise: (i) medical decisions, (ii) delivery of patient care, (iii) disclosure of confidential information

The contractor shall provide an acknowledgement within 120 minutes of receipt/notification of a Medium severity incident and ensure a plan of action is put in place that defines the resolution time. Average resolution time shall be no longer than 12 hours.

A Medium severity incident is defined as meeting the following criteria:
• Disruption or a partial loss of the system, but the system is usable 

The contractor shall provide an acknowledgement within 24 hours of receipt/notification of a Low severity incident and appropriate resources are assigned within 48 hours. Average resolution time shall be no longer than 80hours.

A Low severity incident is defined as meeting the following criteria:
• Customer is experiencing issues that require technical advice or recommendation for the best solution and/or have slight impact on the operating environment

The RTLS Handheld solution shall meet or exceed the following reliability standards:  
•  Availability – 95%
• Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) – 3 months
• Mean Time to Repair (MTTR) – 3 days, 36 hours
• Accuracy – 95% commission rate   
The RTLS Handheld shall require no more than 8 hours of maintenance per month. Servicing and maintenance is expected to occur on the weekends during periods of least usage.

The RTLS Handheld solution shall be integrated  with VA PIV D/SSOi 

The RTLS Handheld solution shall comply with VA Security Compliance/Mobile Application "White Listing" process and be included on VA application White List. 

The Contractor shall ensure Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) product(s), software configuration and customization, and/or new software are Personal Identity Verification (PIV) card-enabled by accepting HSPD-12 PIV credentials using VA Enterprise Technical Architecture (ETA), https://www.ea.oit.va.gov/EAOIT/VA_EA/Enterprise_Technical_Architecture.asp, and VA Identity and Access Management (IAM) approved enterprise design and integration patterns, https://www.oit.va.gov/library/recurring/edp/index.cfm. 

The Contractor shall ensure all Contractor delivered applications and systems comply with the VA Identity, Credential, and Access Management policies and guidelines set forth in VA Handbook 6510 VA Identity and Access Management, VA Handbook 0735 Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) Program, and align with the Federal Identity, Credential, and Access Management Roadmap and Implementation Guidance v2.0.

The Contractor shall ensure all Contractor delivered applications and systems provide user authentication services compliant with the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-63-3, VA Handbook 6500 Appendix F, “VA System Security Controls”, and VA IAM enterprise requirements for direct, assertion-based authentication, and/or trust based authentication, as determined by the design and integration patterns. Direct authentication at a minimum must include Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) based authentication supportive of PIV card and/or Common Access Card (CAC), as determined by the business need.

The Contractor shall ensure all Contractor delivered applications and systems conform to the specific Identity and Access Management PIV requirements set forth in the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Memoranda M-05-24, M-19-17, and NIST Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 201-2.

OMB Memoranda  M-05-24 and M-19-17 can be found at:  https://www.whitehouse.gov/sites/whitehouse.gov/files/omb/memoranda/2005/m05-24.pdf, and https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/M-19-17.pdf respectively. 

Contractor delivered applications and systems shall be on the FIPS 201-2 Approved Product List (APL). If the Contractor delivered application and system is not on the APL, the Contractor shall be responsible for taking the application and system through the FIPS 201 Evaluation Program.

The Contractor shall ensure all Contractor delivered applications and systems support:
Automated provisioning and are able to use enterprise provisioning service.
Interfacing with VA’s Master Person Index (MPI) to provision identity attributes, if the solution relies on VA user identities. MPI is the authoritative source for VA user identity data.
The VA defined unique identity (Secure Identifier [SEC ID] / Integrated Control Number [ICN]).
Multiple authenticators for a given identity and authenticators at every Authenticator Assurance Level (AAL) appropriate for the solution.
Identity proofing for each Identity Assurance Level (IAL) appropriate for the solution.
Federation for each Federation Assurance Level (FAL) appropriate for the solution, if applicable.
Two-factor authentication (2FA) through an applicable design pattern as outlined in VA Enterprise Design Patterns.
A Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) implementation if the solution relies on assertion-based authentication. Additional assertion implementations, besides the required SAML assertion, may be provided as long as they are compliant with NIST SP 800-63-3 guidelines.
Authentication/account binding based on trusted Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) headers if the solution relies on Trust based authentication.
Role Based Access Control.
Auditing and reporting capabilities.
Compliance with VIEWS 00155984, PIV Logical Access Policy Clarification https://www.voa.va.gov/DocumentView.aspx?DocumentID=4896.

the allowable cost shall not include) the amount of duty that would be payable if the supplies were not 
entered duty-free.

foreign supplies if-

connection with its commercial business; and 
 
(2) Segregation of these supplies to ensure use only on Government contracts containing duty-free entry 
provisions is not economical or feasible.

contract, either as end products or incorporated into end products, and shall pay duty on supplies, or any portion 
of them, other than scrap, salvage, or competitive sale authorized by the Contracting Officer, diverted to 
nongovernmental use. 
 
(f) The Government will execute any required duty-free entry certificates for supplies to be accorded duty-free 
entry and will assist the Contractor in obtaining duty-free entry for these supplies. 
 
(g) Shipping documents for supplies to be accorded duty-free entry shall consign the shipments to the

STATEMENT OF WORK - SS-26-IHS-1520253 
PURPOSE 
Purpose of this procurement is for a Service Agreement to cover the support, maintenance, and supplies 
for the APC and Cooling Racks in the MDF Closet at the Cheyenne River Health Center (CRHC).  
 
BACKGROUND 
The equipment the Cheyenne River Health Center needs a Service Agreement for maintenance is the 
APC’s and Cooling Racks in the MDF of the CRHC. The equipment allows CHRC staff members to 
perform their job duties effectively to provide the best patient care. 
 
SCOPE 
The Contractor must provide only new equipment and new parts for the required products described 
herein; no used, refurbished, or remanufactured equipment or parts shall be provided under any 
circumstances. Absolutely no “Gray Market Goods” or “Counterfeit Electronic Parts” shall be provided. 
Gray Market Goods are defined as genuine branded goods intentionally or unintentionally sold outside 
of an authorized sales-territory or by non-authorized dealers in an authorized territory. All equipment 
shall be accompanied by the Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEM’s) warranty. Counterfeit 
Electronic Parts are defined as unlawful or unauthorized reproduction, substitution, or alteration that 
has been knowingly mismarked, misidentified, or otherwise misrepresented to be an authentic, 
unmodified electronic part from the original manufacturer, or a source with the express written 
authority of the original manufacturer or current design activity, including an authorized aftermarket 
manufacturer. Unlawful or unauthorized substitution includes used electronic parts represented as 
new, or the false identification of grade, serial number, lot number, date code, or performance 
characteristics. 
PLACE OF PERFORMANCE 
Cheyenne River Health Center – Eagle Butte 24276 
166TH St. 
PO Box 1012 
Eagle Butte, SD 57625 
 
HOURS OF OPERATION 
The hours of operation will be 8:00am to 5:00pm, Monday through Friday.

 Technology Operations, Maintenance and Integrator Support (Infrastructure and

Detailed descriptions of specific tasks are provided in Section 5 – Specific Tasks.
1.2  Background 
Modernization of Ginnie Mae’s proprietary systems and securitization platform includes 
the continuation and implementation of major business applications which are in 
progress, and other MBS services related to implementing new securitization products 
and application infrastructure. These major IT initiatives are critical, highly specialized, 
and necessary to support Ginnie Mae’s role in supporting the housing market and 
economic recovery.  
The vital goal of the Technology operations Program is to consolidate all technology, 
infrastructure and applications operations and maintenance under one effort. 
Consolidating technology, infrastructure and application operations and maintenance 
will achieve greater efficiency, reduce costs, improve service quality, strengthen security 
and compliance, improve consistency and strategic alignment (Simplified IT) in IT 
service delivery across the organization. This includes: 
1. Operational Efficiency 
a. Streamlined Processes: Reduces duplication of effort, eliminates 
redundant processes, and standardizes workflows. 
b. Centralized Management: Simplifies oversight and coordination, making it 
easier to manage resources, schedules, and priorities. 
2. Cost Savings 
a. Reduces Cost: Consolidates support from across many to one (unified 
support) to reduce overall costs. 
b. Reduced Administrative Overhead: Minimizes contract management 
complexity and associated administrative expenses. 
3. Improved Service Quality 

Page 7 of 112
a. Consistent Service Levels: Enables the establishment of uniform SLAs, 
performance metrics, and reporting standards across all environments. 
b. Faster Issue Resolution: Centralized support teams can address incidents 
and problems more quickly and effectively. 
4. Enhanced Security and Compliance 
a. Unified Security Posture: Standardizes security controls, monitoring, and 
compliance practices across all systems and applications. 
b. Simplified Auditing: Eases the process of compliance reporting and audit 
preparation by consolidating documentation and processes. 
5. Strategic Alignment 
a. Business-IT Alignment: Ensures technology operations are aligned with 
organizational goals and priorities across all applications and services. 
b. Agility and Innovation: Facilitates the adoption of new technologies and 
best practices across the enterprise. 
6. Resource Optimization 
a. Better Utilization: Allows for more flexible allocation of personnel and 
technical resources based on organizational needs. 
b. Knowledge Sharing: Promotes cross-training and sharing of expertise 
among teams. 
7. Improved Vendor Management 
a. Single Point of Accountability: Establishes clear ownership and 
accountability for service delivery. 
b. Simplified Communication: Reduces the complexity of managing multiple 
vendor relationships. 
1.2.1 Technical Environment Background Information: 
There are existing conditions within Ginnie Mae’s current environment which will have a 
direct impact on overall acquisition. The Ginnie Mae platform currently supported is a 
mix of modernized and legacy applications. All legacy applications are currently moving 
through modernization. This effort will provide a supporting role to those modernization 
efforts but will not perform application or infrastructure modernization. This effort will 
assume operations and maintenance of some existing applications and applications that 
have been developed or modernized under the Ginnie Mae Digital Services (Software 
Development) effort.

PERFORMANCE WORK 
STATEMENT (PWS) 
FedRAMP-Compliant Cloud Electronic Fax Solution Integrated with 
Microsoft Teams 
Indian Health Service (IHS) 
 
1.0 INTRODUCTION 
The mission of the Indian Health Service (IHS) is to raise the physical, mental, social, 
and spiritual health of American Indians and Alaska Natives to the highest level. 
To support this mission, IHS requires a secure, cloud-based electronic fax solution 
that ensures the protection of Protected Health Information (PHI), enhances clinical and 
administrative workflows, and integrates seamlessly with enterprise collaboration 
platforms. 
This PWS establishes requirements for a FedRAMP-authorized electronic faxing solution 
(Moderate or higher) that is fully integrated with Microsoft Teams, supports HIPAA 
compliance, and ensures Government ownership and portability of Direct Inward Dial 
(DID) numbers. 
2.0 OBJECTIVES 
• Provide a FedRAMP Moderate or High authorized cloud electronic fax solution 
• Ensure full integration with Microsoft Teams (native or API-based) 
• Maintain HIPAA-compliant transmission and storage of PHI 
• Ensure Government ownership and portability of all fax DIDs 
• Enable secure, auditable, and reliable fax communications across IHS 
• Eliminate on-premises fax infrastructure (cloud-only solution) 
• Provide high availability and continuity of operations 
3.0 SCOPE 
The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, software, licenses, cloud services, and 
support necessary to deliver a fully managed, cloud-native electronic fax solution. 

Consistent with the sample fax PWS, the contractor shall provide a secure web-based 
faxing capability with audit logging, encryption, and technical support. 
The work will start with approximately ¼ of the agency, starting with the Great Plains 
Area, Billings Area and Oklahoma Areas.  If the implementation is successful, this 
system will expand and add in the additional areas of Indian Health Service over a 
phased approach and be available to all of the agency.  
The full integration with Microsoft Teams and our SharePoint environment allows for the 
agency to ensure that data is stored in our Office 365 tenant and follows Indian Health 
Service aligned data retention, audit and security policies. 
3.1 Core Requirements 
• Cloud-only SaaS (no on-prem infrastructure) 
• FedRAMP Moderate or High Authorization (active ATO required) 
• Microsoft Teams integration (send/receive fax within Teams interface) 
• Exchange Online / Outlook integration (optional but preferred) 
• Web portal and API access 
• Support for enterprise identity (Azure AD / Entra ID SSO) 
3.2 DID Number Requirements 
• All fax numbers (DIDs) shall be: 
o Owned by IHS (Government retains ownership rights) 
o Fully portable to another provider at contract end 
o Not restricted by vendor lock-in or proprietary constraints 
4.0 CONTRACTOR RESPONSIBILITIES 
4.1 Solution Delivery & Configuration 
The contractor shall: 
• Provide a secure, encrypted cloud fax platform 
• Configure Microsoft Teams integration, including: 
o Send/receive fax via Teams channels, chat, or apps 
o Notification workflows within Teams 
• Provision and migrate existing fax numbers (DIDs) 
• Configure role-based access controls (RBAC) 
• Enable centralized administration 
4.2 Security & Compliance 
The contractor shall ensure: 

• FedRAMP Moderate or High authorization (mandatory) 
• End-to-end encryption: 
o Data in transit (TLS 1.2+) 
o Data at rest (FIPS 140-2/3 validated cryptography) 
• HIPAA compliance (45 CFR Part 164) 
• Audit logging for all transmissions 
• Support for Zero Trust architecture principles 
• Support VPN users authenticated on the IHS network 
• Integration with IHS identity systems (Azure AD) 
Consistent with the sample PWS, the system must provide: 
• Audit trails for all transmissions 
• Secure encrypted connections and authentication controls  
4.3 System Integration 
The contractor shall: 
• Integrate with: 
o Microsoft Teams (required) 
o Exchange Online / Outlook (preferred) 
o Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems (if applicable) 
• Provide APIs for interoperability 
• Support inbound/outbound fax routing rules 
4.4 Operations & Maintenance 
The contractor shall: 
• Provide 24/7 technical support (consistent with sample PWS expectations)  
• Maintain system uptime ≥ 99.9% 
• Perform updates, patches, and enhancements automatically 
• Provide incident response and resolution 
4.5 Data Management 
The contractor shall: 
• Ensure all data is stored within U.S.-based FedRAMP-authorized environments 
• Provide configurable retention policies 
• Allow export of all fax data and metadata 
• Ensure Government retains full ownership of all data 
4.6 Training & Documentation 

The contractor shall: 
• Provide user and administrator training 
• Deliver user guides and SOPs 
• Provide onboarding support for IHS facilities 
 
5.0 DELIVERABLES 
Deliverable Frequency Format 
Implementation Plan At project start PDF 
System Configuration Documentation Post-implementation PDF 
Training Materials Initial + updates Digital 
Monthly Usage & Audit Reports Monthly PDF/Excel 
Security Compliance Reports Quarterly PDF 
Incident Reports As required PDF 
6.0 PERFORMANCE STANDARDS (QASP SUMMARY) 
Performance Objective Standard Method 
System Availability ≥ 99.9% uptime Monitoring reports 
Fax Delivery Success Rate better 
than or equal to analog fax industry 
standard success rates 
≥ 95% Audit logs 
Support Response Time ≤ 1 hour (critical) Ticket review 
Security Compliance FedRAMP/HIPAA Audit 
Teams Integration Functionality 100% operational COR validation 
7.0 SECURITY REQUIREMENTS 
The contractor shall comply with: 
• FedRAMP Moderate or High baseline 
• HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164) 

• Privacy Act (5 U.S.C. §552a) 
• FISMA 
• NIST SP 800-53 controls 
• FIPS 140-2/3 cryptographic standards 
No system shall: 
• Restrict Government access to data 
• Prevent number portability 
• Create vendor lock-in 
8.0 PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE 
• Base Year: 12 months 
• Four (4) Option Years (12 months each) 
9.0 PLACE OF PERFORMANCE 
• Cloud-hosted (FedRAMP-authorized environment) 
• Accessible across all IHS facilities nationwide 
10.0 GOVERNMENT-FURNISHED EQUIPMENT (GFE) 
• Network access 
• Identity services  
• Existing fax numbers (for migration) 
11.0 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA 
The solution will be accepted when: 
• FedRAMP authorization is verified 
• Microsoft Teams integration is fully functional 
• Fax transmission and receipt tested successfully 
• DID ownership confirmed contractually 
• Security and compliance controls validated 
12.0 CONSTRAINTS 
• Cloud-only (no on-prem solutions permitted) 
• Must integrate with Microsoft Teams 
• Must be FedRAMP authorized (Moderate or higher) 
• Government must retain ownership of: 
o Data 
o Fax numbers (DIDs) 
o Configuration access 
13.0 QUALITY ASSURANCE SURVEILLANCE PLAN (QASP) 

Aligned with the sample PWS structure, the Government will: 
• Monitor system performance and availability 
• Validate compliance with HIPAA and FedRAMP 
• Review audit logs and reports 
• Conduct periodic security assessments 
Failure to meet performance standards may result in: 
• Service credits 
• Corrective action plans 
• Contract remedies 
14.0 EVALUATION CRITERIA (SECTION M) 
Award will be made using a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable approach. The 
Government will evaluate proposals based on the following factors: 
14.1 Technical Capability (Most Important) 
The Government will evaluate the extent to which the offeror demonstrates: 
• Compliance with all FedRAMP Moderate or High requirements 
• Depth and maturity of Microsoft Teams integration 
o Native vs API-based integration 
o User experience within Teams 
• Ability to ensure Government ownership and portability of DIDs 
• Demonstration of Past Performance with Federal agencies 
• Security architecture (encryption, access control, audit logging) 
• System scalability and performance 
• API availability and interoperability with IHS systems 
14.2 Security & Compliance 
Evaluation will include: 
• Verified FedRAMP Authorization (ATO) status 
• Alignment with: 
o NIST SP 800-53 
o HIPAA Security Rule 
o FIPS 140-2/3 cryptography 
• Zero Trust Architecture alignment (see Section 15.0) 
• Data residency and protection controls 
• Incident response and breach notification procedures 
14.3 Management Approach 
The Government will evaluate: 

• Project management methodology 
• Staffing plan and qualifications 
• Risk management strategy 
• Service delivery model and escalation procedures 
14.4 Past Performance 
Evaluation will consider: 
• Relevant experience with federal healthcare or HHS agencies 
• Past performance delivering: 
o FedRAMP-authorized SaaS solutions 
o Cloud fax or secure messaging systems 
• CPARS ratings or equivalent documentation 
14.5 Migration Approach 
The Government will evaluate: 
• Completeness and feasibility of the legacy fax migration plan 
• Ability to migrate: 
o Existing fax numbers (DIDs) 
o Historical fax data (if required) 
o User accounts and workflows 
• Minimization of operational disruption 
14.6 Price 
• Evaluated for reasonableness and realism 
• Not scored numerically but considered in tradeoff decision 
15.0 ZERO TRUST ARCHITECTURE REQUIREMENTS 
The contractor shall design and operate the solution in alignment with Federal Zero 
Trust Architecture (ZTA) principles (OMB M-22-09 and NIST SP 800-207). 
15.1 Identity-Centric Security 
• Integration with Active Directory 
• Support for: 
o Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) 
o Conditional Access Policies 
o Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) 
15.2 Device & Access Controls 
• Enforce device compliance policies where applicable 
• Restrict access based on: 
o User identity 

o Device posture 
o Location and risk signals 
15.3 Data Protection 
• Encrypt all data: 
o In transit (TLS 1.2+) 
o At rest (FIPS 140-2/3 validated) 
• Support Data Loss Prevention (DLP) integration 
• Ensure secure handling of PHI at all stages 
15.4 Continuous Monitoring 
• Provide real-time logging and monitoring 
• Integrate with Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) tools 
• Support anomaly detection and alerting 
15.5 Least Privilege & Micro-Segmentation 
• Enforce least privilege access across all roles 
• Logical isolation of tenant environments 
• No shared access to Government data across tenants 
15.6 Audit & Visibility 
• Full audit trail of: 
o Fax transmissions 
o User activity 
o Administrative actions 
• Logs must be exportable to Government systems 
16.0 MIGRATION PLAN FROM LEGACY FAX SYSTEMS 
The contractor shall provide a comprehensive migration strategy to transition IHS from 
legacy fax systems to the cloud-based solution. 
16.1 Migration Planning 
The contractor shall: 
• Conduct a current state assessment, including: 
o Existing fax numbers (DIDs) 
o Fax volumes and workflows 
o Integration points (EHR, email, etc.) 
• Develop a Migration Plan including: 
o Timeline and milestones 
o Risk mitigation strategies 
o Rollback procedures 

16.2 DID Number Porting 
• All existing fax numbers shall be: 
o Ported without service interruption 
o Verified for successful transfer 
• Contractor shall coordinate with carriers to ensure continuity 
• Ownership of DIDs remains with IHS at all times 
16.3 Data Migration (If Applicable) 
• Migrate historical fax data where required 
• Preserve: 
o Metadata 
o Audit logs 
• Ensure integrity and confidentiality of PHI during migration 
16.4 Phased Implementation 
Migration shall occur in phases: 
1. Pilot deployment (Great Plains Area, Billings Area, Oklahoma Area) 
2. Incremental rollout across IHS facilities 
3. Full enterprise deployment 
4. Decommissioning of legacy systems 
16.5 Parallel Operations 
• Maintain parallel operations (legacy + new system) during transition 
• Ensure no disruption to clinical or administrative workflows 
16.6 Testing & Validation 
The contractor shall: 
• Perform end-to-end testing of: 
o Fax send/receive functionality 
o Teams integration 
o DID routing 
• Validate: 
o Security controls 
o Audit logging 
o User access 
16.7 Training & Change Management 
• Provide targeted training for: 
o End users 
o Administrators 
• Deliver change management support, including: 

o User communications 
o Job aids 
o Help desk readiness 
16.8 Cutover & Go-Live 
• Execute a controlled cutover plan 
• Provide enhanced support during go-live period 
• Ensure immediate issue resolution capability 
16.9 Decommissioning 
• Safely decommission legacy fax systems 
• Ensure: 
o Data is archived or migrated per policy 
o No residual PHI exposure 
• Provide decommissioning report 
16.10 Post-Migration Support 
• Provide on-going support throughout the life of the contract 
• Monitor system performance and user adoption 
• Address defects and optimize workflows 
 
17.0 CONSTRAINTS 
All tasks under this contract will be conducted in accordance with Homeland Security 
Presidential Directive 12 https://www.dhs.gov/homeland-security-presidential-directive-
12, and FPS-201 http://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/FIPS/NIST.FIPS.201-3.pdf . All work 
must follow HSPD‑12/FIPS 201‑3; procure APL‑validated PACS solutions; comply with 
§889 prohibitions; never lock the Government out of any system, data, or keys; and 
observe all confidentiality/privacy requirements. 
 
Access to Government Property (on-site contractors) The COR and/or Project Manager 
will make all necessary arrangements for access by contractor personnel to the work 
site(s). While on government property, the contractor personnel shall comply with all 
rules and regulations pertaining to health and safety, not only as they apply to 
themselves, but also to other personnel and property at the site. Contractor personnel 
shall comply with all regulations restricting the disclosure of information which may 
become known during the performance of this contract 
 
In the performance of work hereunder and with the price herein, the contractor shall 
obtain and maintain in effect all necessary permits and licenses required by Federal, 
State, Tribal, or local government, or subdivisions thereof, or of any other duly 
constituted public authority. Further the contractor shall obey and abide by all applicable 
laws and ordinance. 
 

18.0 AUTHORITY 
1.   No person other than the Contracting Officer has authority to bind the Government 
with respect to this contract. 
2.   No action or omission of any government employee or representative other than the 
Contracting Officer shall increase or decrease the scope of this contract or shall 
otherwise modify the terms and conditions of this contract. 
3.   In no event shall any of the following be effective or binding on the Government or 
imputed to the Contracting Officer with respect to this contract: 
a.   An understanding or agreement between the Contractor and anyone other

1: Background 
American Battle Monuments Commission (ABMC) commemorates the service and sacrifice of 
members of the United States Armed Forces. ABMC operates 26 cemeteries and numerous 
memorials and monuments across 17 countries, with staff in Arlington, Virginia; Paris,  France; 
and overseas sites. ABMC uses ManageEngine for IT service management and requires 
professional services to deploy Freshworks products acquired under the companion Part 1 software 
license award. 
Statement of Need 
ABMC requires a Contractor to deploy, configure, migrate, integrate, secure, train, roll out, 
operate, and maintain Freshworks products at ABMC. Contractor shall perform all implementation 
and sustainment tasks. ABMC will approve changes, provide approved access and source data, 
validate deliverables, and make acceptance decisions. 
Freshworks deployment shall support ABMC’s enterprise service management (ESM) objectives, 
including IT service management, enterprise case management, Microsoft Entra ID authentication, 
public intake, shared mailbox intake, reporting, automation, audit logging, role -based access 
control, and phased expansion to ABMC departments and global sites. 
This Part 2 PWS excludes software licenses. 
Information Technology Environment 
ABMC operates a Microsoft 365 E5 hybrid enterprise environment with Microsoft Entra ID, single 
sign-on, multifactor authentication, conditional access, Microsoft Intune, role -based access 
control, centralized logging, and secure cloud integrations. Contractor shall integrate the ESM 
platform with this environment and use only ABMC-approved access methods.

license provider. 
If the Part 1 license award delays Part 2 performance, ABMC may consider schedule adjustment 
through contract modification. 
• ABMC will identify the selected platform, edition, and licensed modules before Part 2 
performance begins. 
• The Part 1 license award will include modules for workflow, asset management, reporting, 
automation, public intake, and AI capabilities.

through 0003 cover phased implementation and may overlap with ABMC approval. ABMC 
expects CLINs 0001 through 0003 to take approximately six months from Notice to Proceed. CLIN 
0004 covers one year of operations and maintenance after CLIN 0003 completion and any 
exercised option periods.  CLIN 0005 reserves contract structure for future enhancements and 
requires no task pricing at this time. 
Each CLIN starts after ABMC issues a Notice to Proceed. Offerors shall provide a schedule that 
accounts for U.S. federal holidays and ABMC staff availability. ABMC will evaluate schedule 
realism against the proposed implementation timeline. 
Standard Requirements for All CLINs 
1. Contractor shall plan, manage, perform, test, document, and transition all work required 
by this PWS. 
2. Contractor shall maintain the project schedule, milestone tracker, risk register, issue 
log, action log, decision log, and weekly status report. 
3. Contractor shall conduct kickoff, discovery, design, testing, deployment, training, and 
transition activities for each applicable CLIN. 
4. Contractor shall prepare configuration documents, test scripts, training materials, 
administrator guides, and transition materials. 
5. Contractor shall obtain ABMC approval before production changes, data migration, 
integration activation, workflow deployment, user access changes, and deliverable 
submission. 
6. ABMC will validate requirements, approve changes, provide approved access and data, 
and accept or reject deliverables. 
Security and Compliance Requirements 
1. Contractor shall configure Microsoft Entra ID single sign -on and multifactor 
authentication for authorized users. 
2. Contractor shall configure role -based access control, least privilege permissions, and 
separation of duties for administrators, agents, and requesters. 
3. Contractor shall enable audit logging for administrator activity, authentication activity, 
configuration changes, workflow changes, and available user activity. 
4. Contractor shall document data flows, integrations, public intake paths, shared mailbox 
intake, administrative roles, and security settings. 
5. Contractor shall not store, copy, export, or reuse ABMC data outside approved 
environments without written Contracting Officer approval. 
6. Contractor shall not run automated scripts, bulk permission changes, or third -party 
tools in ABMC environments without written approval. 

6 
 
7. Contractor personnel shall obtain favorable Tier 1 adjudication before receiving ABMC 
system access. 
8. Contractor personnel may begin work that does not require ABMC system access 
before access approval. 
9. Contractor personnel shall use Government -furnished equipment for ABMC system 
access and shall not access ABMC systems from contractor-owned devices. 
10. Contractor shall submit required platform and security logs to ABMC Microsoft 
Sentinel for monitoring and acceptance validation. 
11. FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001, or equivalent SaaS security evidence applies to the 
SaaS platform acquired under Part 1, not to the professional services Contractor under 
this Part 2 PWS. 
CLIN 0001: ITSM Foundation, Migration, and Initial Workflows 
CLIN 0001 establishes the production ESM platform. Contractor shall migrate approved 
ManageEngine data, configure core ITSM workflows, integrate Microsoft Entra ID, import initial 
asset data, configure initial departmental workflows, train designated users , and transition the 
platform to operational use. 
Scope 
1. Configure development, test, and production environments unless ABMC approves a 
different structure. 
2. Co-administer the tenant with ABMC during implementation. 
3. Configure production after ABMC approval, including direct production configuration 
when ABMC approves that approach. 
4. Configure platform settings, roles, permissions, groups, categories, business hours, 
notification templates, service level policies, and escalation rules. 
5. Configure incident management, service requests, service catalog, change management, 
problem management, assignments, routing, and closure workflows. 
6. Migrate approximately 15,000 ManageEngine tickets and related records from 2000 to 
present, including incidents, service requests, changes, problems, assets, users, 
attachments, comments, knowledge articles, audit history, closed records, open records, 
and recent records. 
7. Extract ManageEngine data using ABMC approved database access, API access, exports, 
or vendor support. 
8. Prepare the migration plan, define the dataset during project meetings, map fields, run a 
test migration, resolve exceptions, run the final migration, and reconcile migrated records. 
9. Import asset data through the Microsoft Intune API and document asset categories and field 
mappings. 
10. Configure Microsoft Entra ID integration using SAML unless ABMC approves another 
method.

11. Configure SCIM provisioning and just -in-time provisioning when the selected platform 
supports them. 
12. Support ABMC OCIO approval of required conditional access policies. 
13. Configure public requester access for public facing modules when required. 
14. Configure Public Affairs, Human Resources, and Historical Services workflows with 
intake forms, routing, status tracking, reporting, records retention, PII handling, and shared 
mailbox intake. 
15. Configure one public website intake integration for an ABMC public website, including 
field mapping, routing, CAPTCHA, confirmation messages, and approved file handling. 
Public websites in scope include www.abmc.gov, wwiiregistry.abmc.gov, 
weremember.abmc.gov, and wepreserve.abmc.gov.

ABMC approves a different training plan. Training shall cover applicable administrators,

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION 
Electronic Limited Technical Inspection (LTI) and System Integration Solution 
Product Manager Combat Service Support Equipment (PM CSSE) Program Manager Combat 
Support System (PM CSS) 
Gen
eral Information 
Document Type Request for Information (RFI) 
Request for Information Number M67854-26-I-5422 
Posted Date July 29, 2026 
Response Date August 26, 2026 
NAICS Code [541512 - Computer Systems Design Services] 
PSC or FSC Classification Code [DA01 - IT and Telecom - Business 
Application/Application Development Support Services] 
Description 
This Sources Sought announcement is to assist the United States Marine Corps (USMC), 
Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps (PAE-MC), Expeditionary Medical Systems 
(EMS) to identify potential vendors capable of developing, testing, and implementing an 
Electronic Limited Technical Inspection (LTI) and System Integration Solution. 
Currently, when Medical Logistics (MEDLOG) Companies issue an Authorized Medical 
Allowance List (AMAL) or Authorized Dental Allowance List (ADAL) to a using unit, they 
must conduct a manual Limited Technical Inspection (LTI). This manual process results in slow 
data input into the Defense Medical Logistics Standard Support (DMLSS) system and a critical 
lack of real-time asset visibility for higher headquarters. 
The objective of this effort is to acquire a digital warehousing solution divided into two 
interconnected parts: 
1. Electronic LTI Process: Automating the capture and transfer of asset data during
technical inspections at the MEDLOG Company level utilizing Commercial Off-the-
Shelf / Government Off-the-Shelf (COTS/GOTS) handheld scanners, tablets, or
electronic inventory devices.
2. Asset Visibility & Integration: Providing a seamless, real-time interface with DMLSS
and subsequent integration into the Maven Smart System (MSS) to ensure data integrity
and total asset visibility at the higher headquarters level.
Responses 
Interested parties are invited to submit capability statements or white papers addressing these 
requirements directly to the Marine Corps via e-mail to Contract Specialist, Ms. Ebony King at 
ebony.king@usmc.mil and the Contracting Officer, Ms. Shanna Laging at 

shanna.laging@usmc.mil no later than August 26, 2026, by 5:00 p.m. EST. The U.S. 
Government will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in response to this 
Notice. All costs associated with responding to this Notice will be solely at the expense of the 
interested party. 
(1) S
ection 1 of the white paper shall provide administrative information. Administrative
information shall include at a minimum:
• Name, mailing address, overnight delivery address (if different from mailing address),
phone number, fax number, and email of designated point of contact (POC).
• Business website.
• Business type and number of employees (large business, small business, small-
disadvantaged business, 8(a)-certified small-disadvantaged business, HUBZone small
business, woman-owned small business, very small business, veteran-owned small
business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business).
• SAM.gov Unique Entity ID (UEI) and Contractor and Government Entity (CAGE) Code
(if your company has these).
• Recommended contracting strategy (Commercial, Noncommercial, Firm Fixed price,
Cost).
• The facility security clearance of the vendor or the ability to acquire one (if available but
not required).
• Do you have a viable Federal Supply Schedule that can support this procurement? If so,
provide your GSA Schedule information to include the category of products provided.
• Do you have a current contract with other DoD Activities? If so, provide associated
information.
Section 1 of the white paper shall be limited to one page. 
(2) Section 2 of the white paper shall provide information on the products and services each
vendor can offer with respect to the Electronic LTI and System Integration Solution. Responses
should explicitly address the vendor's capability to deliver on the following core requirements:
• Hardware & Data Capture: Approach to providing intuitive COTS/GOTS handheld
scanners/tablets/devices capable of offline/local validation against AMAL/ADAL
requirements.
• System Integration: Capability to develop secure, bidirectional interfaces with DMLSS
and push real-time transaction data to MAVEN without manual data entry.
• Cybersecurity/ATO: Experience and methodology for managing the Risk Management
Framework (RMF) process to achieve and maintain a full Authority to Operate (ATO).
• Implementation & Training: Strategy for phased implementation, providing "over-the-
shoulder" support, and delivering comprehensive train-the-trainer materials to MEF
MEDLOG Companies.

Questions 
Any questions for clarification may be emailed to Contract Specialist, Ms. Ebony King at 
ebony.king@usmc.mil and the Contracting Officer, Ms. Shanna Laging at 
shanna.laging@usmc.mil no later than August 5, 2026, by 5:00 p.m. EST. Verbal questions will 
NOT be accepted. Questions shall NOT contain proprietary or classified information. An 
unattributed list of questions and answers will be published at the same web location of this 
Sources Sought Announcement. 
THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ONLY. This RFI has been issued solely for 
information and planning purposes in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 
Clause 52.215-3. It does not constitute an Invitation for Bid (IFB), a Request for Proposal (RFP), 
a Request for Quotation (RFQ), or an indication that the Government will contract for any of the 
items and/or services contained in this notice. This RFI does not commit the Government to 
contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Further, the Marine Corps is not seeking proposals 
at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. 
Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this 
RFI; all costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party’s 
expense. Responses shall not include classified material. Not responding to this RFI does not 
preclude participation in any future solicitation if one is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will 
be synopsized on the SAM.Gov (https://sam.gov/) website. It is the responsibility of the potential 
offerors to monitor SAM.gov for additional information pertaining to this requirement.

### Sheet: Sheet1
Requirement | Type | Requirement Name | Requirement Description
1.0 | BR | Intake | The business requires an application that provides the ability to intake requests.
1.1 | FR | VA Form Intake | The application shall allow the intake of appeal requests based on specific VA forms that have been filled out by appellants.
1.2 | FR | Intake Types | The application shall have the ability to intake and manage business-defined request types.
1.3 | FR | Additional Documentation | The application shall allow requests requiring additional documentation to be temporarily moved to a queue for obtaining the documentation (pre-docket).
1.4 | FR | Auto or Manual Data Entry | The application shall accept automated input or prompt users for specific information during the intake process.
1.5 | FR | Apply Topics | The application shall allow users to mark an appeal request as relating to different business-defined topics during the appeal intake process.
1.6 | FR | Multiple Intakes | The application shall allow users to intake multiple requests (appeals or other) for the same appellant.
1.7 | FR | Multiple Parties | The application shall allow a request to have multiple parties.
1.8 | FR | Manual Dockets | The application shall allow the business to define eligibility requirements for requests but still allow users to manually docket appeal issues that fail system checks of eligibility.
1.9 | FR | Work Tasks | The application shall allow a request to be assigned a work task as part of intake.
1.10 | FR | External Requests | The application shall allow the intake of requests that originate in external systems.
1.11 | FR | Power of Attorney | The application shall allow each party to have a power of attorney (POA) designated for each request.
2.0 | BR | Queue Management | The business requires an application that provides the ability to view and manage queues.
2.1 | FR | Queues | The application shall provide a variety of request queues that allow work to flow to the correct user needing to perform tasks.
2.2 | FR | Auto Distribution | The application shall be able to automatically distribute pending requests to individual user or team queues according to specific business rules.
2.3 | FR | User Queue Management | The application shall allow privileged users to request that a certain number of requests be distributed to a queue.
2.4 | FR | User Queue Management Rules | The application shall provide a way for privileged users to view and modify rules that determine how pending requests of different types are distributed to individual user or team queues.
2.5 | FR | Assigned Requests | The application shall allow users to view a queue of requests that are assigned to them for working.
2.6 | FR | Request Status | The application shall allow users to see the status of their assigned work, for example, which of their assigned requests are pending, which are on hold, and which are completed.
2.7 | FR | Request Movement | The application shall allow the user-initiated movement of requests from one queue to another.
2.8 | FR | Search | The application shall allow users to perform full or partial searches using specific criteria, and view the results in the queue.
2.9 | FR | Filter | The application shall allow users to use filter functionality such that only a targeted group of results display in a queue based on selected criteria.
2.10 | FR | Number of Documents/Pages | The application shall display the total number of documents and pages in a claims file related to a request.
2.11 | FR | Page Number Control | The application shall allow users to select how many records to display on a given page of a queue.
2.12 | FR | Special Statuses | The application shall provide the ability to automatically or manually assign a request with one or more special statuses (e.g. Advance on Docket (AOD)) based on business rules.
2.13 | FR | Application Priority | The application shall be able to order appeal requests in lists according to priority and/or docket number, e.g., Advanced on Docket and CAVC requests are priority requests.
2.14 | FR | Multiple Doc | The application shall support defining multiple request types with different workflows.
2.15 | FR | Docket Switching | The application shall allow users to switch request types for a given request.
2.16 | FR | Request View | The application shall provide the ability to display a summary of key attributes related to a request.
2.17 | FR | External Documents | The application shall allow for the upload and management of documents related to a request.
2.18 | FR | Request Status - System | The application shall automatically update item statuses in queues (e.g., opening a request changes the status from unread to read.)
2.19 | FR | Request Status - User | The application shall allow users to change an item status in queues (e.g., change read back to unread).
3.0 | BR | Request Management | The business requires an application that provides the ability to view and manage requests.
3.1 | FR | View Request Details | The application shall allow users to view details about a request.
3.2 | FR | Edit Request | The application shall allow users to edit certain aspects of a request.
3.3 | FR | Add Notes | The application shall allow users to add notes to a request.
3.4 | FR | Work Request | The application shall allow users to assign and work on tasks related to a request.
3.5 | FR | View All Requests | The application shall allow users to view all requests associated with a party.
3.6 | FR | Motion Management | The application shall support the creation, assignment, and resolution of pre‑ and post‑decisional motions.
3.7 | FR | Visual Callouts | The application shall display visual indicators for requests that reflect specific business rules, for example, contested claims.
3.8 | FR | Visual Callout Management | The application shall allow privileged users to add or remove request-specific visual indicators.
3.9 | FR | Number of Documents/Pages | The application shall display the total number of documents and pages in a claims file related to a request.
3.10 | FR | Substitution | The application shall allow parties to be substituted on an appeal request.
3.11 | FR | Automatic Task Assignment | The application shall provide the ability to automatically assign request tasks based on customized logic.
3.12 | FR | Shared Assignment | The application shall allow multiple users to be assigned to a single request task.
3.13 | FR | Task Reassignment | The application shall allow users to reassign request tasks regardless of status.
3.14 | FR | Bulk Task Assignment | The application shall allow users to assign request tasks in bulk.
3.15 | FR | Cancel Task | The application shall allow privileged users to cancel request tasks.
3.16 | FR | Multiple Users | The application shall allow multiple users to work on the same request simultaneously.
3.17 | FR | Translation Requests | The application shall visibly flag appeals that have pending or completed translation tasks.
4.0 | BR | Hearings | The business requires an application that provides the ability to manage hearings.
4.1 | FR | Hearing Types | The application shall support different types of hearing review options.
4.2 | FR | Schedule | The application shall allow users to schedule a hearing for an appellant on an allocated docket.
4.3 | FR | View Details | The application shall allow users to view hearing details, as well as appeal details and related appellant documentation, for a hearing.
4.4 | FR | Modify Details | The application shall allow users to modify details for a given appeal.
4.6 | FR | Emails | The application shall generate emails to individuals regarding an appellant's scheduled hearing, based on certain criteria.
4.7 | FR | Reschedule | The application shall allow users to re-schedule an appeal hearing.
4.8 | FR | Withdraw | The application shall allow users to withdraw an appeal hearing.
4.9 | FR | Assign | The application shall allow users to be assigned to hearings.
4.10 | FR | Create Schedule | The application shall allow users to create a hearing schedule based on provided calendar availability and blackout date information of participants involved in the hearings.
4.11 | FR | Scheduling Conflicts | The application shall prevent hearing scheduling conflicts.
4.12 | FR | View Schedule | The application shall allow users to view a hearing schedule.
4.13 | FR | View Docket | The application shall allow users to view a day's hearing docket.
4.14 | FR | Assigned Hearings | The application shall allow users to view a list of their assigned hearings, in a prioritized order.
4.15 | FR | Videoconferencing Capability | The application shall provide or integrate with a videoconferencing platform that allows users to conduct hearings.
4.16 | FR | Worksheet | The application shall allow privileged users to input and view notes and disposition information related to a hearing.
4.17 | FR | Audio Files | The application shall provide or integrate with a videoconferencing platform that allows audio files to be saved for conducted hearings.
4.18 | FR | Transcription | The application shall provide or integrate with a videoconferencing platform that allows hearings to be transcribed.
4.19 | FR | Prevent Video | The application shall provide or integrate with a videoconferencing platform that prevents video recording files from being generated.
4.20 | FR | Schedule Hearings | The application shall allow hearings to be scheduled for different locations, including a national location for virtual hearings.
4.22 | FR | Modernized Hearing Scheduler Queue | The application shall allow provide a prioritized national queue so that users can assign appeals to hearing schedulers.
4.23 | FR | Auto-Docket Creation | The application shall provide the capability to automatically create one or more hearing dockets based on specific criteria.
5.0 | BR | Decision | The business requires an application that provides the ability to draft and sign appeal decisions.
5.1 | FR | MS Word Decision | The application shall integrate with MS Word to produce a decision document
5.2 | FR | Decision Creation | The application shall allow attorney and judge users to write appeal decisions.
5.3 | FR | Decision Template | The application shall provide native boilerplate capabilities so that boilerplate content can be pulled into appeal decision documents.
5.4 | FR | Manage Content | The application shall allow users to edit, copy, and subscribe to boilerplate content.
5.5 | FR | Sign Decision | The application shall allow judge users to sign appeal decisions via digital signature.
5.6 | FR | Evaluate Attorney | The application shall provide the ability for judge users to evaluate attorneys and their work products (e.g., decision writing) based on a variety of factors.
5.7 | FR | Send Decision to Dispatch | The application shall provide the ability for signed decisions to be routed to a Dispatch service for end-product processing.
6.0 | BR | Dispatch | The business requires an application that provides the ability to dispatch decisions and request responses.
6.1 | FR | Review Decision | The application shall allow users to review signed appeal decisions and request responses for accuracy.
6.2 | FR | Print Decision | The application shall allow users to print appeal decisions and request responses, as well as cover letters, created from boilerplate content.
6.3 | FR | Print Service | The application shall allow users to upload and send the decisions and request responses to a third-party print service.
7.0 | BR | Follow On Request Work | The business requires an application that processes follow-on actions and requests that are related to an initial request.
7.1 | FR | Split Appeal | The application shall allow an appeal to be split into two separate appeals, with the same identifier, but different issues on each.
7.2 | FR | Merge Appeals | The application shall allow appeals to be merged.
7.3 | FR | Post Decision Actions | The application shall allow for appeals to be withdrawn, dismissed, and reactivated post decision.
7.4 | FR | Post Decisional Appeals | The application shall be able to intake and process new requests related to an initial request.
8.0 | BR | Quality Review | The business requires an application that allows users to evaluate completed requests for quality.
8.1 | FR | Quality Review | The application shall support the ability for users to evaluate completed requests for quality.
8.2 | FR | Review Selection Criteria | The application shall provide the ability to automatically select requests for review based on specific criteria.
8.3 | FR | Error Documentation | The application shall allow users to document errors identified during a quality review.
8.4 | FR | Corrective Notes | The application shall allow users to notate corrective actions they've taken to address documented errors in a quality review.
8.5 | FR | Edit Review | The application shall allow users to edit a submitted quality review.
8.6 | FR | Withdraw Review | The application shall allow users to withdraw a quality review.
8.7 | FR | Review Status | The application shall allow users to view the status of a quality review.
9.0 | BR | Reader | The business requires an application that allows users to view and manage documents and evidence.

9.2 | NFR | Load Time | The application shall not experience performance degradation when opening and navigating through content.

1.0  BACKGROUND 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Office of Information and Technology (OIT) 
Product Delivery Services (PDS) delivers integrated digital capabilities that support 
Veteran care nationwide.  Within PDS, the Health Services Portfolio’s Healthcare 
Environment and Logistics Management (HELM) Product Line (PL) implements, 
modernizes, sustains, standardizes, and streamlines software solutions for supply 
chain, logistics, expendables, assets, inventory, facilities, prosthetics, and 
environmental compliance HELM provides the enterprise capabilities needed to support 
a unified, efficient, and data driven supply chain and logistics environment across VA. 
VA does not currently operate with standardized, enterprise-wide supply chain business 
processes or technical systems. Numerous functional and capability gaps have been 
identified through Government Accountability Office (GAO) and Office of Inspector 
General (OIG) audits and internal assessments. VA requires accurate, reliable, and 
accessible supply chain data to improve ordering, fulfillment, and operational 
performance.  These needs align with VA’s Strategic Supply Chain (SC) Prioritization 
and Digital Modernization Strategy, which emphasize modernizing legacy systems, 
strengthening cybersecurity and resilience, improving data quality, enhancing user 
experience for logisticians, and establishing consistent, interoperable processes across 
VHA, VACO, VBA, and NCA. 
 
VA currently relies on approximately 63 disparate legacy systems across 174 sites, 
resulting in fragmented operations, limited enterprise visibility, and inefficiencies. 
Standardization and modernization are required to transform Supply Chain systems into 
integrated, enterprise-wide system of systems that supports responsive, efficient clinical 
and nonclinical supply operations. 
 
To meet mission needs, VA requires a full service, standardized, scalable healthcare 
logistics software solutions with modern supply chain management capabilities.  A 
unified digital environment shall enable lifecycle management efficiencies, data driven 
decision making, and seamless integration with major initiatives such as the Electronic 
Health Record Modernization (EHRM) and Financial Management Business 
Transformation (FMBT) programs.  HELM’s mission and modernization efforts directly 
support these enterprise requirements by advancing cloud-based logistics capabilities, 
modernizing legacy applications, and enabling consistent processes across VA’s supply 
chain functions.  In addition to modernization activities, several HELM products require 
ongoing Operation & Maintenance (O&M) support, enhancements, operation stability, 
security and Lifecyle support.

April 27, 2026 
 
 
This is a Request for Information (RFI) only.  Do not submit a quote. This RFI is for planning 
purposes only and shall not be considered a Request for Quotation.  Additionally, there is no 
obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services described in this 
RFI.  Your response to this RFI will be treated only as information for the Government to 
consider.  You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in 
responding to this RFI.  This request does not constitute a solicitation for quotes or the authority 
to enter negotiations to award a task order/contract.  No funds have been authorized, 
appropriated or received for this effort.  The information provided may be used by the 
Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) in developing its acquisition strategy.  Interested parties 
are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive 
information contained in their response.  The Government does not intend to pay for the 
information submitted in response to this RFI. 
 
Introduction:  
The Department of Veterans Affairs anticipates either a single or multiple award Indefinite 
Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) for a supply chain enterprise inventory management system 
to include procurement and receiving services contract in Fiscal Year 2027.  As such, VA is 
seeking industry feedback on the draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) to provide a 
modernized Inventory Management and ordering solution.  It is acknowledged that the VA 
Supply Chain is antiquated and complex.  As such, there may not be one single technology 
solution from a single vendor, and some desired objectives may not be readily achievable.  
Utilizing a system of systems approach is acceptable and teaming is encouraged. Additionally, it 
is acknowledged that there are several existing technology solutions already in operation 
throughout VA which could be included in potential solutions. 
 
VA is a large and complex civilian Agency within the Federal Government providing care to 
Veterans and their dependents.  VA spends billions of dollars on goods and services across 
several organizations including the Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Veterans Benefits 
Administration (VBA), National Cemeteries Administration (NCA), VA Central Office 
(VACO), and the Office of Information and Technology (OIT), each responsible for logistics and 
asset management activities and functions specific to its mission.  In support of these activities, 
and surge capabilities in response to the 4th Mission, VA requires an integrated and 
comprehensive supply chain capability that can sustain operations under all conditions, rapidly 
scale to meet emergent needs, and maintain uninterrupted delivery of critical goods and services. 
 
VHA, VBA, NCA, VACO, and OIT are each responsible for logistics and asset management 
activities and functions specific to their mission. VA requires an easy to use, integrated, 
intelligent supply chain modernization and management solution that is cloud based.  The VA 
Supply Chain manages the flow of goods, services, and information between all stakeholders, 

RFI - Inventory Management Modernization 
2 
 
including within VA, external suppliers and service providers, and the ultimate customer – the 
Veteran. This includes, but is not limited to, Prosthetics; Pharmacy and Pharmacy Bio‑response; 
Information Technology; Supplies; and Burial and Benefit supplies, as well as the administration 
of these functions. The objective of this effort is to align VA’s supply chain to enhance mission 
efficiency by reducing process and system complexity, standardizing data and business practices, 
and improving integration with other VA enterprise systems. 
 
Capability Statement 
Submit a capability statement and proposed business process flows describing your company’s 
ability to meet the objectives in the attached draft PWS. The capability statement shall be limited 
to 15 pages.  
 
The capability statement shall address the following: 
 
1. Include the following identification information 
 
a. Company Name 
b. Unique Entity ID Number under which the company is registered in 
SAM/vetbiz.va.gov/ 
c. Small Business Status and applicable NAICS code (it is intended the solicitation will 
be related to 541512). Please also indicate whether you will be able to comply with 
VAAR 852.219-10, VA Notice of Total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small 
Business Set-Aside and with subcontracting limitations in 13 CFR 125.6 in execution 
of this effort? 
d. Company Address 
e. Point of contact name 
f. Telephone number 
g. Email address 
h. Please provide any available contract vehicles the proposed solution would be 
available on (i.e. SEWP, GSA, etc.). 
i. Please provide a Rough Order of Magnitude needed in order to meet the requirements 
detailed in the PWS 
 
2. Demonstrate your expertise and capability in implementing a nationwide supply chain 
modernization/optimization for an organization of similar size, scope and complexity as VA. 
Have you done this type of work with the Federal Government? Provide supporting details to 
indicate whether you were the prime contractor or subcontractor. Please state whether you 
intend to propose on this effort as a Prime contractor or subcontractor.   
 
3. In addition, please include responses to the following questions in your capabilities statement:
 
 
a) Please provide any feedback on whether a single or multiple award IDIQ is better suited 
for this effort?  
b) Does your firm have a system compliant with the Electronic Industries Alliance Standard 
748 (EIA-748) per Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO)

Deviation Part 34.2? Does your firm have any contracts utilizing Earned Value 
Management in an Agile environment?   
c) If you are proposing cloud-based products/services/platforms and it will be hosted 
outside of VA enterprise cloud, is it currently Federal Risk and Authorization 
Management Program (FedRAMP) compliant/authorized?  If so, at what level? 
d) Does your solution have the capability to interface with, but not limited to, any of the 
following VA systems: The Integrated Financial and Acquisition Management System 
(iFAMS); the current Financial Management System (FMS), VA electronic health record 
system established under the Electronic Health Record Modernization Program; and the 
Veterans Health Information Systems and Technology Architecture (VistA) and 
Computerized Patient Record System (CPRS). 
e) Please describe your systems’ current and past use in major healthcare facilities with the 
ability to support real‑time, enterprise‑wide inventory visibility across multiple supply 
chain functional areas. Provide examples of where this capability is currently deployed.  
f) Define the scalability and performance characteristics of your solution, to include use 
during surge operations associated with VA’s 4th Mission. How would you scale the 
system for maximum volume of transactions, users, and data your system can support via 
reliability, availability (99.99%,) and maintainability (RAM). Provide examples and 
describe what you do currently to maintain adequate RAM score for other 
implementations of your system(s). 
g) Describe your system and whether it is a single solution or if it will be comprised of 
multiple systems to meet the requirements of the PWS.  
h) Describe your approach to data governance, including support for data cleansing, data 
standardization, data enrichment, data quality, interoperability, metadata/lineage tracking, 
and compliance with VA and federal data standards. 
i) Please describe how your solution supports integration with emerging technologies such 
as predictive analytics, AI/ML, demand planning tools, and inventory optimization 
engines. 
j) What is your typical deployment approach and timeline (e.g., phased rollout, pilot-first, 
big-bang, progressive wave deployment)?  
k) What is your software license schema/type (enterprise, individual, subscription, SaaS, 
monthly, annual, etc.)?  Describe the level of support that comes with the license price. 
Does your solution require any third-party licensing? 
l) Describe your Organizational Change Management (OCM) approach and support for 
business process reengineering and experience in large‑scale federal logistics or 
healthcare transformation efforts. Include training methods, end‑user adoption strategies, 
and post‑go‑live stabilization support.

n) Describe your solution’s ability to support the full medical supply chain beyond typical

special considerations for Pharmacy, Prosthetics, DME, Consignment, and Biologics. 
Provide an assessment of how significantly your workflows would need to be altered to 
meet unique federal and VA requirements—such as minimal, moderate, or extensive 
changes; include rationale across regulatory compliance, data standards and item master 
governance, integration approach, security and privacy, accessibility (Section 508), and

o) How much of your system adaptability is configuration rather than customization?
