Title: Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) Tier 1, and Tier 2 Support

Notice Type: Sources Sought Notification

PSC Code: DA10

NAICS Code: 541519

Point(s) of Contact: Nicole Tokash, nicole.tokash.civ@army.mil

BACKGROUND: The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA), a component of the Department of Defense (DoD) reporting to the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness, is responsible for operating a worldwide network of 235 commissaries across 45 states, 13 countries, and two U.S. territories. Headquartered at Fort Lee, Virginia, DeCA serves Active Duty, Reserve, and National Guard members, military retirees, service-connected disabled veterans, authorized family members, and other eligible patrons by providing quality grocery and household products at significant savings. The Agency manages annual sales exceeding $4.6 billion, employs more than 14,000 personnel, and supports approximately 3,000 checkout lanes, including self-checkout capabilities. Operational oversight is provided through five area offices—East, Central, West, Europe, and Pacific—which oversee commissary operations worldwide, supported by eight Central Distribution Centers (CDCs) and one Central Meat Processing Plant (CMPP) that provide critical logistics and supply chain support.

To support its mission and modernize enterprise operations, DeCA is advancing its digital transformation strategy by leveraging integrated SAP Retail Cloud technologies to enable near real-time, data-driven decision-making across the enterprise. DeCA envisions an operating environment with timely access to accurate, reliable, and actionable data to improve operational efficiency, increase sales, reduce costs, and maximize the value of the commissary benefit for eligible patrons. The Agency seeks industry solutions capable of sustaining and enhancing its SAP environment through innovative approaches that maintain a Clean Core architecture, support interoperability with existing systems and technologies, and enable continuous modernization. As part of this effort, DeCA is transitioning its SAP Retail Cloud program from implementation into a continuous Agile operations model supported by a Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) framework that provides Tier 2 support while delivering ongoing enhancements to meet evolving mission requirements.

PURPOSE: The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) is conducting market research to identify interested and capable businesses, stimulate industry awareness, and gain feedback to improve the acquisition strategy and planning process. 

This is not a solicitation announcement. This notice is for planning purposes only and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparation of a response to this notice. Any information submitted by respondents to this notice is strictly voluntary. The Government will not award any contract based on the information received from this notice.

The Government will utilize information received from this notice to assist in acquisition planning and identifying small businesses’ capabilities. The Government reserves the right to consider a set-aside for small businesses or one of the small business socioeconomic contracting programs (e.g., 8(a), HUBZone, service-disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB), and women-owned small business (WOSB) including economically disadvantaged women-owned small businesses (EDWOSB))

Any resultant set-aside contract or task order for services will include the applicable clause at RFO FAR 52.219-14 – Limitations on Subcontracting. Respondents (e.g., primes) intending to utilize subcontractors should provide information detailing how the prime will not pay more than 50 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities (SSEs), as defined within RFO FAR 52.219-14. A respondent (prime) utilizing a subcontracting arrangement will need to have the infrastructure and resources in place to manage the entire contract, including all task orders (if applicable).

DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT:

This requirement establishes a Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) operational support model for the SAP Retail Cloud environment, providing Tier 1 and Tier 2 support while leveraging SAP Tier 3 support for product-related issues. It transitions the program from the "Confirm" phase into a continuous, Agile-based operational state, ensuring that the "Clean Core" is maintained while addressing evolving mission requirements.

The Government anticipates this effort to be a firm fixed price (FFP) type contract. This is a new contract requirement.

North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541519 with a small business size standard of 34 Million Dollars.

SUBMISSION: Interested parties should provide a Capability Statement (no more than 10 pages). Illustrations such as tables, flowcharts, organizational charts, process charts or other similar type informational charts may be used, and they will be counted against the page count limitations. Electronic responses (i.e. email) are preferred and telephonic request for information will not be honored. Interested sources who submit data are responsible for appropriately marking information if it is proprietary in nature. No request for capability briefings will be honored as a result of this notice. Responses that do not conform to the response instructions may not be considered by the Government. Standard company brochures will not be reviewed.

Interested parties that possess the capabilities to meet the above requirements are invited to submit a Capability Statement. The Capability Statement must include the following information: 

Company Profile: 

• Company Name 

• Address 

• Point of Contact (Name, Title, Phone, Email) 

• CAGE Code and UEI Number 

• SAM Registration Expiration Date 

2. Business Size/Socioeconomic Status: Identify your business size under NAICS 541519 (e.g., Large Business, Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB). 

3. Technical Capability: Describe your company's experience providing SAP Retail Cloud support, Agile software development, DevSecOps/CI/CD pipelines, Tier 1/Tier 2 operational support, SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP), S/4HANA, and enterprise cloud environments comparable in size and complexity to DeCA. 

4. Industry Feedback: Any technical questions, clarifications, or feedback regarding the scope or logistics.

5. Existing Contracts: Provide contract numbers for any existing government-wide acquisition contracts (GWACs), GSA Multiple Award Schedules (MAS), or other contract vehicles your company currently holds that include these services.

Responses and any questions to this sources sought shall be submitted to the Contract Specialist, Nicole Tokash, nicole.tokash.civ@army.mil.

BPAs. Therefore, ordering activities are responsible to make a separate determination of fair and 
reasonable pricing for individual orders, BPAs, and orders under BPAs. The Contracting Officer 
will determine, using the procedures in FAR 15.404-1, that the prices are fair and reasonable and 
will document such determination with a level of detail commensurate with the complexity and 
circumstances of each order. By placing an order against a schedule contract, the ordering 
activity contracting officer concludes that the order represents a fair and reasonable price and 
best value to the Government. 
 
6.  Description of market research among schedule holders and the results or a statement of 
the reason market research was not conducted.   
The requiring activity and contracting activity have conducted market research among schedule 
holders. Market research confirmed that Telos Corporation is the Original Equipment 
Manufacturer (OEM) and sole developer of the Xacta suite. A review of the market indicates that 
no other vendor or third-party reseller possesses the required legal authority or access to the 
proprietary Xacta infrastructure, database, and integration technologies necessary to fulfill the 
full scope of the PWS, which mandates in-depth code development, customized workflow 
templates, and seamless architectural integration within the Naval Intelligence network. 
 
7.  Any other facts supporting the justification.  
This procurement uses a GSA Federal Supply Schedule and will be solicited and awarded in 
accordance with GSAR Subpart 538.71.  
 
8.  Actions the Agency may take to remove or overcome barriers to competition.    
For the reasons set forth in Paragraph 4, the contracting activity has no plans at this time to 
compete future contracts for the specific types of proprietary software supplies and integration 
services covered by this document. However, if another potential source emerges as a result of 
any type of synopsis or any other means, NAVSUP Fleet Logistics Center Norfolk Contracting 
Department, Fleet Directorate and the Requiring Activity will assess whether competition for 
future requirements is feasible. Regardless of whether a new potential source emerges, the 
requiring activity and contracting office will continue to perform market research to consistently 
stay aware of new cyber risk management products and services that could bring more value to 
the government or promote competition in the future.

art 1: General Information 
A. Introduction
The Red Lake Service Unit (RLSU) provides healthcare services including Emergency
Medical services, family practice, internal medicine, pediatrics, dental, optometry,
physical/occupational therapy, lab/radiology with mammography and bone density,
pharmacy, mental health services, nutrition/diabetic educator services, and contract health
services. The laboratory at Red Lake services the entire facility. The purpose of this
Statement of Work (SOW) is to establish the requirements for the procurement,
installation, implementation, maintenance, technical support, quality assurance support,
training, and ongoing operational support of the UNIPOC Point-of-Care (POC) testing
system for use within a healthcare facility environment.
5

75H70526Q00021 
UNIPOC POC 
B. Background
The healthcare facility requires a reliable and efficient point-of-care testing system to
support patient diagnosis, treatment, and monitoring in various clinical settings. The
UNIPOC POC system is intended to improve turnaround times, enhance patient care,
support clinical decision-making, and maintain compliance with applicable regulatory
and accreditation standards.
C. Scope
The Contractor shall furnish and maintain a fully operational UNIPOC POC testing
system capable of supporting clinical laboratory and patient care operations. The system
shall support rapid point-of-care diagnostic testing and include all required
instrumentation, software, interfaces, consumables, quality control support, maintenance,
technical support, and user training.
The Contractor shall provide all services necessary for:
• Delivery and installation of equipment
• Initial system setup and configuration
• Integration support with existing electronic health record (EHR) and laboratory
information systems (LIS), and scripting software.
• Initial staff training
• Preventive maintenance
• Corrective maintenance and repair
• Software upgrades and updates
• Technical and customer support
• Replacement parts and supplies
• Quality control and proficiency testing support
The Contractor shall ensure the system remains fully functional and compliant with
applicable healthcare and laboratory standards during the entire period of performance.
D. Contractor Responsibilities
a. Equipment and System Provision
Provide all equipment necessary for full operation of the UNIPOC POC system,
including but not limited to:
• Docking stations
• Data management software
• Connectivity hardware
• Required accessories and peripherals
All equipment shall be new.
b. Installation and Configuration
The Contractor shall:
• Deliver all equipment to the Government facility
• Install and configure all systems
6

75H70526Q00021 
UNIPOC POC 
• Verify operational readiness
• Perform acceptance testing
• Coordinate connectivity and interface setup
• Ensure proper system functionality prior to go-live
c. Training
The Contractor shall provide initial and ongoing training for Government
personnel.
Training shall include:
• System operation
• Quality control procedures
• Troubleshooting procedures
• Maintenance procedures
• Operator competency requirements
• Regulatory documentation requirements
Training materials shall be provided in electronic and/or hard copy format.
d. Preventive Maintenance
The Contractor shall provide all scheduled preventive maintenance in accordance
with manufacturer recommendations.
The Contractor shall coordinate maintenance scheduling with the COR.
e. Corrective Maintenance and Repair
The Contractor shall provide corrective maintenance and repair services for all
covered equipment.
Corrective maintenance shall include:
• Troubleshooting
• Diagnosis
• Repair
• Replacement parts
• Labor
• Travel
• Emergency service support
The Contractor shall provide remote technical support and on-site support as 
necessary. 
7

75H70526Q00021 
UNIPOC POC 
f. Software Updates and Upgrades
The Contractor shall provide all software updates, patches, firmware updates, and
upgrades released during the contract period at no additional cost.
Updates shall:
• Maintain cybersecurity compliance
• Improve system functionality
• Correct identified deficiencies
• Maintain interoperability
• Support regulatory compliance
g. Technical Support
The Contractor shall provide technical support services during normal business
hours, at a minimum.
Support shall include:
• Telephone support
• Remote diagnostics
• Email support
• Escalation procedures
• Service ticket tracking
The Contractor shall provide contact information for support personnel.
h. Quality Assurance and Regulatory Compliance
The Contractor shall support compliance with:
• Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA)
• The Joint Commission standards
• Applicable manufacturer requirements
The Contractor shall provide documentation supporting:
• Calibration
• Quality control
• Preventive maintenance
• Instrument performance
• Operator training
• Competency validation

The Contractor shall replace defective or nonfunctional equipment that cannot be
repaired within acceptable timeframes.

The National Institute of Health’s National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences (NCATS) 
Rare Diseases Clinical Research Network (RDCRN) intends to award a firm fixed price sole source 
contract under the authority of FAR 12.102(a) , only one source being available to meet the 
Government's needs, to: 
 
Florence Healthcare, Inc. 
600 Peachtree St. NE, Suite 920 
Atlanta, GA 30308   
 
The National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences (NCATS) RDCRN hereby submits a 
notice of intent to award a sole source firm fixed price purchase order for a renewal of the Florence 
electronic Trial Master File (eTMF) platform and associated SiteLink/eBinders services. This 
request is to renew this Software as a Service (SaaS) subscription. The required software is used in 
centralized regulatory document management across multiple RDCRN studies and participating 
research sites.
 The Florence platform supports centralized management of clinical research 
documentation and is essential to RDCRN operational continuity.  The North American Industry 
Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541511. 
 
The SaaS includes the following:  
•     Annual subscription services  
• SiteLink/eBinders access  
• Single Sign-On (SSO) integration support  
• Technical support and maintenance  
• Training services  
• Site activation and onboarding support  
• Compliance and validation support documentation 
The period of performance will be for one (1) 12-month base period. 
 
This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals, and no solicitation document exists for 
the requirement. This hereby constitutes a synopsis of the requirement.

the Government. Information received will normally be considered for the purpose of determining 
whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The Government will not be responsible for any 
costs incurred by responding to this notice. This is NOT a request for quotes or proposals.

- Source Code Access Restriction: MSC does not have access to the source code needed to

Fleet software. 
- Proprietary Modification Rights: MSC does not possess any legal right to modify or 
authorize the modification of the proprietary ABS Wavesight source code. 
- Required Vendor Authorization: Because of these source code limitations, any prospective 
vendor must demonstrate a verified partnership, authorized developer status, or direct 
licensing agreement with ABS Wavesight to legally and technically perform customization 
and sustainment services.

2. NATURE/DESCRIPTION OF ACTION(S): 
 
MOD 1: This administrative modification is executed to align the underlying authorities of 
this Class J&A with the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO).  This action ensures the 
document remains compliant with the modernized procurement framework without 
altering the mission requirement, the total estimated ceiling, or the period of performance.  
The requirement continues to be for proprietary, brand-name software support for COTS 
assets previously purchased and currently integrated into the mission partner 
infrastructure.  Per the RFO regulatory authorities this modification is strictly 
administrative and does not exceed the previously approved value, the original approval 
authority remains valid and sufficient for this action. 
 
Original J&A 
a. The nature of this action is to procure software support for previously purchased 
proprietary, commercial off-the-shelf, brand name software already integrated within 
the existing mission partner infrastructure. Scope is limited to the defined duration 
and ceiling of this J&A for software support and includes all required original 
equipment manufacturers (OEMs). This J&A does not cover the procurement of new 
software licenses or new subscriptions. Scope is restricted to software support only 
(to include subscription renewals, if appropriate). It is noted that the ordered 
software support can be, in effect, longer than the duration of this class J&A, as long 
as the contract/order is issued during the covered period. Contract/orders may also 
include option periods. 
 
b. Mission partners may be any DISA or non-DISA entities. Any DITCO contracting 
office procuring software support may use this class J&A; although, the primary 
contracting office is PS832, the IT Infrastructure Branch. Individual procurements 
will be awarded as firm-fixed-price contracts or delivery orders to an authorized 
reseller of the required OEM, utilizing the National Aeronautics and Space 
Administration (NASA) Solutions for Enterprise-Wide Procurement (SEWP) 
contracts, Army Computer Hardware Enterprise Software and Solutions (CHESS), 
General Services Administration (GSA) Federal Supply Schedules (FSS), or the 
open market via beta.SAM.gov. 
 
c. This brand name class J&A will justify software support requirements for a period of 
five years, estimated to begin on January 1, 2026, and extending through December 


Brand Name Software Support Class J&A, JA26-010 
 
 
Page 3 of 7 Pages 
 
31, 2030. When possible, competitive requests for quotes will be issued for 
individual requirements to maximize competition among authorized resellers of the 
required OEM. A redacted copy of the approved class J&A will be posted with each 
software support requirement. The total estimated cost of the proposed acquisitions 
is . This estimate is based on tracking actual usage of the predecessor 
brand name class J&A for software support, in effect from January 2021 through 
December 2025, which has a ceiling in the amount of . 
 
3. DESCRIPTION OF THE SUPPLIES OR SERVICES: 
 
The objective of the contracting efforts supported by this brand name class J&A is to renew 
annual software support for previously acquired software licenses and subscriptions that are 
installed on existing mission partner networks. The brand name software support to be acquired 
under this class J&A requires renewal to sustain existing infrastructure. The software support 
may include, but is not limited to, product updates/upgrades, new releases and versions, fixes, 
and patches for the purposes of maintaining the operability and usability of the software 
products. 
 
4. SUPPORTING RATIONALE FOR BRAND-NAME JUSTIFICATION:  
     
(a) A brand name justification was previously approved for each of the original software 
licenses or subscription procurements now requiring software support by the requisite 
OEM. Extensive market research was conducted for the initial procurements, which 
documented the technical and specific details of the only products that could meet the 
Government’s needs. It is a logical conclusion that once a brand name software product is 
procured, only the product OEM or one of its authorized resellers can provide continued 
software support, as third party support is not authorized. 
 
The required software support is essential to the Government’s requirements, as each 
OEM offers the only brand name product support to maintain the current infrastructure 
in place. Because the products are already integrated into the mission partner 
infrastructure, no other products can seamlessly integrate with the existing 
infrastructure without making changes to the baseline. Existing applications were 
specifically designed to interface and operate with specific OEM products. Other 
software brands may provide similar functionality, but without rewriting the application 
source code to integrate other OEMs’ solutions into existing OEM-centric 
environments, the competing programs would not be functional. Current operating 
systems are already implemented and require continued software support to maintain 
operations. Only the previously acquired brand name software meets the required need 
for support and compatibility with existing architecture. Introducing alternative 
products would not meet the Government’s need for interoperability. 
 
Existing OEM products are proprietary, and upgrades and support are available from only 
the existing OEM or its authorized resellers. If the currently installed software support is 
not renewed, the software would not receive the necessary updates, upgrades, and patches 
upon which the Government depends to provide continuity of operations. OEMs for 


Brand Name Software Support Class J&A, JA26-010 
 
 
Page 4 of 7 Pages 
 
applicable software support do not authorize any third party software modifications or 
patches to their software. Existing product OEMs own the copyrighted source software, 
with all legal rights, privileges, and ownership contained therein. No other source may 
legally modify or change the software, nor would they have access to the source code to 
do so, due to copyright and patent law protections. 
 
(b) After completion of market research for each software support requirement, the 
contracting officer will select the best method for accomplishing the acquisition. This 
brand name class J&A allows for the following specific authorities: 
 
1) An analysis of software orders awarded by DITCO over the past several years 
revealed that at least 90 percent of software orders were competed utilizing NASA 
SEWP Fair Opportunity and other contract vehicles utilizing FAR 16.5 procedures. 
For this reason, the primary authority for all actions authorized under this class J&A 
and competed as Fair Opportunity against NASA SEWP is FAR 16.505(a)(4). The 
particular brand name, product, or feature is essential to the Government’s 
requirements; and market research indicates other companies’ similar products, or 
products lacking the particular feature, do not meet or cannot be modified to meet, the 
Agency’s needs. The acquisitions referenced herein are conducted under the statutory 
authority of 10 U.S.C. 3406(c)(5). 
 
2) The authority for limiting sources to specific brand name product(s) when purchasing 
software support from GSA FSS or Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) orders 
established in accordance with (IAW) FAR 8.405-3 is FAR 8.405-6(b)(1). IAW FAR 
8.405-6(b)(1), the particular brand name, product, or feature is essential to the 
Government’s requirements and market research indicates other companies’ similar 
products, or products lacking the particular feature, do not meet, or cannot be 
modified to meet, the Agency’s needs. The acquisitions referenced herein are 
conducted under the statutory authority of the Multiple Award Schedule Program, 41 
U.S.C. 152(3). 
 
3) The authority for limiting sources to specific brand name product(s) when purchasing 
software support from open market sources is FAR 6.302-1/DFARS 206.302-1, only 
one responsible source or a limited number of responsible sources, and no other 
supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. The acquisitions referenced 
herein are conducted under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C.2304(c)(1). 
 
5. COST/PRICE FAIR AND REASONABLE DETERMINATION: 
 
a. Price reasonableness will be determined at the individual contract or order level. Quotes 
will be solicited from the OEM and/or authorized resellers of the required support 
through the most appropriate acquisition method, as determined by market research to 
promote competition to the maximum extent. The contracting officer will make a 
determination of fair and reasonable prices based on the comparisons of competitive 
quotes received, historical prices, commercial price lists, Governmental contract price 
lists, and the independent Government cost estimate. In addition, a determination will be 


Brand Name Software Support Class J&A, JA26-010 
 
 
Page 5 of 7 Pages 
 
made that the order represents the best value to the Government and results in the lowest 
overall price. Although NASA SEWP, Army CHESS, and GSA have already determined 
the contract or schedule prices to be fair and reasonable, the contracting officer will seek 
additional discounts for all of these actions prior to placing an order. 
 
b. All open market contracts with a lifecycle cost over  placed under this class 
J&A will be subject to cost and price analysis IAW DISA Acquisition Regulation 
Supplement (DARS) 5815.404-1(S-91), unless an exception applies. 
 
6. MARKET RESEARCH: 
 
a. Based on current market research, interoperability, and system constraints, it has been 
determined that only brand name software support can fully meet and satisfy Agency 
requirements. Only the proprietary software support, which is available through the OEM 
or their authorized resellers, will satisfy Agency needs and can support the infrastructures 
currently in place. Current market research also considered the fact that the Agency has 
been procuring brand name software support through the OEM or their authorized 
resellers for years, with publicly posted brand name J&As that have not been challenged, 
solidifying the OEM/reseller industry standard. 
 
b. This brand name class J&A supports all applicable requirements for a 5-year period, 
estimated to run from January 1, 2026, through December 31, 2030. Market research will 
be performed for each individual requirement to determine that only the previously 
awarded brand name software and support can fully meet the Government’s need. There 
is latitude within NASA SEWP, Army CHESS, GSA Schedules, and beta.SAM.gov for 
small business set-asides, and market research findings will be coordinated through the 
DISA Office of Small Business Programs IAW DFARS 219.201(c)(10) and DARS 
5819.2. 
 
7. ANY OTHER SUPPORTING FACTS: 
 
The software support products sustained by this brand name class J&A are for software licenses 
and subscriptions that were originally acquired under an individual approved brand name J&A. 
 
8. ACTIONS THE AGENCY MAY TAKE TO OVERCOME BARRIERS THAT LED TO THE 
EXCEPTION TO FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION: 
 
Individual requirements will be competed amongst the authorized resellers of the previously 
acquired software via NASA SEWP, Army CHESS, GSA Schedules, or GSA BPAs and 
beta.SAM.gov. If the OEM elects to surrender their legal ownership, copyright, and/or 
intellectual property software rights and move toward providing an open source solution for the 
products being renewed under individual procurements, then DISA will seek open competition. 
Regardless, the Government will continue to search the marketplace, and alternative software 
solutions will continually be researched to determine if alternative solutions exist. If the 
Government should determine that the previously acquired brand name products are no longer 
required, the Government will seek a competitive acquisition approach for the required 


Brand Name Software Support Class J&A, JA26-010

functionality. At that point, every effort will be made to provide for competition to the maximum 
extent practicable, based on new technologies that will support mission partner needs.

NCES Data Tool Redesign - Request for Information 
Purpose:  
The U.S. Department of Education (the Department) is conducting market research to determine if 
sufficient interest and capability exists in the marketplace for the DataLab O&M and possible re-design. 
This does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), Request for Quotations (RFQ), Invitation for 
Bids (IFB), or a commitment on the part of the Government to conduct a solicitation in the future. All 
information provided is strictly voluntary and no reimbursement will be made by the Government for 
any costs associated with providing a response to this notice or otherwise participating in market 
research activities. Further, the U.S. Department of Education offers no assurance that a solicitation will 
result from this notice. 
The Department of Education’s National Center for Education Statistics (NCES) has the need for expert 
technical support in the day-to-day operation and maintenance (O&M) of the DataLab databases and tools 
that house and are used to analyze these data. The DataLab O&M contract expires in February 2027 and 
NCES requires an experienced contractor to assume day-to-day operations and maintenance of this 
system over the next several years.   
Concurrent with that effort, NCES requires thought leadership to assess NCES’ current state data storage, 
analytics and dissemination environment and propose a modern technology solution leveraging artificial 
intelligence that provides stakeholders with an easy, intuitive, secure and accurate set of data analytics 
tools for the library of NCES data. It is expected that the ultimate awardee(s) would design, develop and 
implement a comprehensive iterative solution over an 18-month period culminating in a multi-month 
phased launch of the ultimate solution and the wind down of the various legacy products.  It is expected 
that all required functionality will remain available – either in the legacy or future state form - during the 
implementation period.   
Additional details about NCES, its mission, products and analytics tools can be found in the attached 
Statement of Objectives.   
Questions: 
1. Please describe similar experiences designing data tools, integrating tools, and maintaining data 
tools. 
a. Provide contract numbers and dollar values.  
b. Provide numbers of users or other metrics to demonstrate the size and scope of these 
previous efforts.  
2. Describe experience creating and/or using APIs.  
3. Describe experience working with secure, restricted, or confidential data. 
4. Describe experience with leveraging AI integration.  
a. Provide experiences securing confidential data with PII while using AI. 
b. Provide names of the data sources and/or customers for this work. 
5. What other innovations have you used to leverage cost reductions in data dissemination and 
analysis work? 

6. Describe experience improving user experience and functionality for audiences of different 
technical ability levels.  
7. Given the wide range of data formats, housed in different systems coupled with the interest in 
leveraging AI in improving the customer experience, what type of data formatting and 
conversion would be required to normalize data formats to fully leverage benefits of AI? 
8. Is the proposed timeline realistic? 
9. Are there other technical objectives that you foresee that could/should be included? 
10. Is your business a small business? What percentage of this work would you be able to perform, 
and what percentage would you need to subcontract in order to meet the requirements? 
11. What experience do you have with incentive contracts for this type of work? Please provide 
specific examples of incentives and how they were applied.  
12. Are the services needed offered under any GWAC or Federal Supply Schedule contracts? If so, 
please provide the contract number and SIN. 
 
Please provide responses to the questions above no later than 12pm ET, August 27, 2026 to Alyson 
Allman, Alyson.allman@ed.gov. Please include a POC with your response who can answer any follow up 
questions the Department might have.

Attachment 1 – Statement of Objectives – NCES DataLab Recompete 
 
U.S. Department of Education 
Institute of Education Sciences 
DRAFT Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
 
National Center for Education Statistics DataLab Recompete 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
1. Introduction 
 
The Institute of Education Sciences (IES) is the statistics, research, and evaluation arm 
of the U.S. Department of Education (ED). The goal of IES is to provide national 
leadership in expanding fundamental knowledge and understanding of education from 
early childhood through postsecondary study, in order to provide parents, educators, 
students, researchers, policymakers, and the general public with reliable information 
about the condition and progress of education in the United States, from early 
childhood through postsecondary education; educational practices that support 
learning and improve academic achievement and access to educational opportunities for 
all students; and the effectiveness of federal and other education programs. 
The Education Sciences Reform Act (ESRA, Title I of P.L. 107-279) established IES as an 
independent research arm of ED. Title I, Part A, of ESRA establishes IES as a research 
institute within ED, intended to provide “national leadership in expanding fundamental 
knowledge and understanding of education from early childhood through postsecondary 
study.” IES is authorized to carry out these objectives by compiling statistics, conducting 
research and evaluations, and disseminating information. 
IES executes its mission through four national education centers and an Office of the 
Director: 
• The National Center for Education Research (NCER) sponsors 
research leading to the accumulation of knowledge and understanding of 
education. 
• The National Center for Education Statistics (NCES) collects and 
analyzes education information and statistics in a manner that meets the 
highest methodological standards. 
• The National Center for Education Evaluation and Regional 
Assistance (NCEE) supports evaluation, technical assistance, development, 
and dissemination activities. 
• The National Center for Special Education Research (NCSER) 
sponsors research to expand knowledge and understanding of the needs of 
infants, toddlers, and children with disabilities. 
• The Office of the Director carries out specific duties, such as proposing 
research priorities and establishing procedures for technical and peer review. 
The Standards and Review Office (SRO) carries out rigorous peer review of all 
research, statistics, and evaluation reports conducted by, or supported 
through, the Institute and falls under the Office of the Director. 
 
2. Legislative Authority 
 
Legislative authority for the activities detailed in this work statement is granted under 
20 U. S. C. § 9543. 
 
3. Requirement Context 
 
The United States Department of Education’s (the Department) National Center for 

 
 
Education Statistics (NCES) within the Institute of Education Science (IES) has a 
requirement to provide web-based data analysis tools that allow users to search NCES 
data, create tables and graphics representing education data, examine trends over time, 
and analyze data using bi-variate and multivariate statistical tests and models. These 
data tools use data from several large and complex data collections including national 
longitudinal surveys, linked cross-sectional surveys, census data, and administrative 
record data.  
 
Existing data sets span decades and are stored in many forms (i.e. SAS, excel, html, pdf, 
etc.) across multiple systems and websites.  NCES maintains numerous antiquated and 
redundant online data analytics tools to store, manage, analyze, manipulate and report 
off-the-shelf and customer-selected data outputs.  The following is a representative 
sample of various NCES websites and corresponding data analytics tools: 
 
o DataLab https://nces.ed.gov/datalab  
o ELSi https://nces.ed.gov/ccd/elsi/   
o International Data Explorer 
https://nces.ed.gov/surveys/international/ide/   
o EDGE  
o MapED – https://nces.ed.gov/programs/mapED/Home   
o IPEDS Data Explorer 
o IPEDS Trend Generator 
o College Navigator https://nces.ed.gov/collegenavigator/   
o Bibliography Search Tool https://nces.ed.gov/bibliography/   
o NTPS State Dashboard 
https://nces.ed.gov/surveys/ntps/ntpsdashboard/map/2   
o Education Finance Statistics Center EDFIN 
https://nces.ed.gov/edfin/longitudinal/   
 
 
NCES has the need for expert technical support in the day-to-day operation and 
maintenance (O&M) of the DataLab databases and tools. The DataLab O&M contract 
expires in February 2027 and NCES requires an experienced contractor to assume day-
to-day operations and maintenance of this system over the next three years.   
 
Concurrent with that effort and under the Data Modernization contract, NCES continues 
to assess its current state data storage, analytics and dissemination environment and 
consolidate IES websites into a single, unified IES information portal.    
 
It is expected that in late 2027/early 2028, NCES will release an RFP to pursue the next 
phase of this effort to further develop a modern technology solution leveraging artificial 
intelligence that consolidates data tools and provides stakeholders with an easy, 
intuitive, secure and accurate set of data analytics tools for the library of NCES data.  As 
part of this effort, it is expected the contractor will consolidate the Data Lab and the IES 
data portal (www.ies.ed.gov). 
 
The scope of this engagement will include day-to-day management of the DataLab, and  
recommendations to eliminate functional redundancy and any functional gaps in the 
current landscape of IES data analytics tools, consolidate tools and websites and develop 
flexible, state-of-the-art technology (e.g. Artificial Intelligence) to ensure data security, 

 
 
output accuracy, and an optimal, intuitive user experience. 
 
Many of the datasets housed in these analysis systems are derived from complex 
surveys, and advanced statistical computations are needed in order to yield accurate 
estimates and standard errors from the data collected. The requirements outlined in this 
work statement necessitate close and continuing collaboration with NCES staff and 
contractors working across all Divisions in NCES. It also requires the coordination of 
staff with different sets of expertise including IT programmers, graphic designers, 
survey statisticians, educational researchers, and topical subject matter experts. 
Technical specifications for the DataLab, staging and development environments, and 
the data structures are located in Appendix A.  
 
Contractor personnel supporting this effort must possess sufficient technical 
certifications, educational degrees, and experience to support the contract's unique 
requirements. Representative software technologies implemented at the unit's include: 
Hypertext Markup and Extensible Markup Languages; Cascading Style Sheets; Active 
Server Pages; Java and JavaScript; Microsoft Visual Basic, .Net, SQL Server, ASP, PHP 
and C#. Software engineering processes and tools include: build management and 
automation tools, continuous deployment strategies, test-driven and/or behavior-driven 
development, performance testing strategies, and security testing policies. Contractors 
must also have personnel with expertise in complex surveys, especially in using replicate 
weights and Taylor Series linearization to adjust variances. 
 
Contractor personnel supporting this effort must also have extensive experience in 
leveraging technologies such as artificial intelligence to ensure data accuracy, 
consistency and security and optimize system architecture, analytics functionality, and 
customer engagement and experience. 
 
NCES reserves the right to conduct market research sessions with potential vendors in 
association with this RFI.  NCES also reserves the right to use modular contracting to 
perform discrete tasks as part of the final procurement.   
 
 
4. Performance Objectives 
 
The contractor shall meet the following core objectives: 
 
Technical objective 1: Assume day-to-day maintenance of the DataLab 
(https://nces.ed.gov/datalab) website and functionality.  See Appendix A for DataLab 
Technical Specifications. 
 
Technical objective 2: Recommendations for the design, development, 
implementation and maintenance of NCES future state online data analysis and 
dissemination environment. 
 
To accomplish these technical objectives, the bidder shall also meet all of the contract 
objectives listed below: 
Contract Objective 1: Documentation required for the COR to monitor 
deliverables and assess the validity of contractor charges on a quarterly basis. 

 
 
Contract Objective 2: Processes and systems are developed to protect 
respondent information and NCES data. All work with Department of Education 
data shall occur in approved systems with an Authority to Operate (ATO) Issued by 
the Department of Education (note whether this should be a Department of 
Education hosted system or if the bidder has access to a contractor hosted system 
with a current Department of Education ATO). All controls and policies at the 
contractor shall comply with IT and Security requirements outlined in this 
agreement and: 
• IES and NCES policies, 
• NCES Statistical Standards, 
• 20 U.S.C. § 1232g (referred to as the Family Educational Rights and Privacy 
Act [FERPA]), 
• 20 U.S.C. § 9573 (referred to as the Education Sciences Reform Act 
[ESRA]), 
• 44 U.S.C. § 3572 (referred to as the Evidence Act), 
• 5 U.S.C. § 552a (referred to as the Privacy Act), 
• 44 U.S.C. § 3551 et. seq. (referred to as the Federal Information Security 
Modernization Act of 2014), 
• the Federal regulations pertaining to these laws as well as 32 C.F.R. Part 2002 
(referred to as the NARA CUI Rule), and 
• any guidance, revision or amendment to these laws and regulations that occurs after 
the effective date of this Agreement. 
Contract Objective 3: All interim deliverables and clearances required for 
NCES and statistical agencies to release data products, including but not limited 
to: 
• Security screening documents and forms; 
• All interim documents mentioned in the NCES Statistical Standards (e.g., 
required documentation listed in Standards 3-3 and 3-4); and 
• OMB Forms Clearance Package(s). 
Contract Objective 4: An allowance for ad hoc  requests for information in 
support of inquiries needed to inform the COR, the program office, or 
management in managing risk.

Statement of Work 
Title: Daily-updated, Longitudinal, Patient-level Electronic Health Record Data 
SECTION 1 – BACKGROUND 
The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Office of Public Health Data, Surveillance, 
and Technology (OPHDST) leads efforts to modernize public health data, surveillance, and informatics 
capabilities to ensure timely, accurate, and actionable information for public health decision-making. The 
CDC routinely uses electronic healthcare data to meet its public health mission. Healthcare data are used 
to inform situational awareness, predictive modeling, and strategic, tactical, and policy decision making; 
to help track the spread and intensity of outbreaks and identify areas that are highly impacted by disease; 
to understand spectrum of illness, disease burden, risk factors for severe disease, and outcomes; and to 
understand the impact public health threats on healthcare systems and communities.  
Electronic health records (EHRs) are a critically important healthcare data source for the CDC because 
they provide timely, longitudinal, patient-level clinical information at local, state and national scale that is 
not routinely available through traditional surveillance systems. EHR data include rich clinical details 
such as granular diagnoses and procedures, lab tests and results, prescriptions, vital measurements,

clinical notes, outcomes, and demographic characteristics that may not be available in other data sources 
such as administrative claims data. Unlike administrative claims data, EHR data are not contingent on the 
insurance status of the patient and can be available on a near–real-time basis. Near-real-time EHR data 
enable the CDC to monitor disease occurrence burden, health care utilization, outcomes, and disparities 
across diverse populations and geographies, supporting both routine public health surveillance and 
emergency response. Additionally, the longitudinal structure of EHR data allows the CDC to assess risk 
factors, treatment effectiveness and safety, and short- and long-term outcomes and to conduct robust 
epidemiologic analyses. Routine, ongoing access to high-quality, analysis-ready, EHR data substantially 
enhances the CDC’s ability to detect and respond to public health threats, understand disease 
epidemiology, and generate actionable, evidence-based insights that inform public health policy and 
practice.  
The CDC Data Hub within OPHDST is a full-service enterprise resource connecting CDC staff and other 
authorized individuals with high-value healthcare data and technical and analytic support to generate 
actionable insights and inform public health action. CDC Data Hub helps ensure data security, 
governance, stewardship, and quality assurance; manages data onboarding and access permissions; and 
provides training, technical assistance, and data analysis and scientific support, including within CDC’s 
cloud-based data platforms. CDC Data Hub will manage the data and related resources obtained through 
this contract and serve as the primary liaison between the vendor and CDC staff using the data.   
SECTION 2 – PURPOSE 
 
The purpose of this contract is for CDC to obtain enterprise license and access to daily-updated, 
longitudinal, patient-level electronic health record (EHR) data that are analysis ready and immediately 
accessible to CDC staff via an integrated data and analytics platform. Specifically, CDC seeks to obtain 
access to patient-level EHR data that are very timely, daily-updated, and population-scale and capture

1.0  PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS 
 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information & Technology (OIT), 
Office of Information Security (OIS) requires a comprehensive Zero Trust Data 
Monitoring and Sensing - Structured Data Protection solution that provides a data 
protection solution to address on-premises structured data, and structured data in the 
VA Enterprise Cloud (VAEC) Cloud environments to include- Amazon Web Services 
(AWS) and Azure. Data Monitoring and Sensing is essential for enhancing cybersecurity 
measures across VA’s enterprise environments, supporting VA's Zero Trust Architecture 
Strategy in line with Executive Order 14028, Improving the Nation's Cybersecurity.  The 
Zero Trust Data Monitoring and Sensing - Structured Data Protection solution shall 
provide robust Data Loss Prevention (DLP) capabilities, including automated 
enforcement of policies to prevent unauthorized access, transfer, or exfiltration of 
sensitive structured data. In addition, the solution must support automated and 
persistent data labeling, ensuring labels are applied consistently to structured data 
assets and integrated with DLP policies for dynamic access control and compliance. 
 
DLP and labeling integration should align with VA’s Zero Trust principles and 
classification standards, enabling continuous verification, least privilege access, and 
adaptive policy enforcement across on-premises and cloud environments 
 
This solution shall be a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) product or an equivalent 
turnkey implementation that delivers end-to-end security capabilities, including 
management, threat detection, runtime policy enforcement, support, and virtual 
patching.

PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS

Several challenges exist in Enterprise, Occupational Safety, and Health (EOSH) program performance and effectiveness across United States (U.S.) Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). Facilities continue to struggle to fully integrate comprehensive Safety Management Systems (SMS) into the structure of healthcare and VA support operations beyond the local Safety Office, preventing those facilities from progressing from merely closing safety findings to proactively managing safety programs based on risk, which leads to more consistent EOSH risk reduction. Additionally, while EOSH best practices abound across the VA, there are limited standard approaches or centralized data sets/platforms that enable facilities to rapidly identify, adapt, and apply best practices to meet unique requirements and reduce program risk. The lack of an Enterprise Data platform supporting Enterprise VA-standardized management EOSH requirements, prevents facilities, Veterans Integrated Service Networks (VISNs) and Staff Offices from leveraging the data across the enterprise both to identify trends and areas of greater risks more rapidly and to gain economies in time spent developing local database systems to manage data and predictive analysis to reduce program and operational risks. 

 

The VA Center for Enterprise Human Resource Information Services (CEHRIS) has a requirement for Brand Name Cority GX2 or Equivalent Software as a Service (SaaS) application to meet the VA enterprise’s EOSH data requirements. The solution should provide an integrated SaaS platform capable of supporting safety, industrial hygiene (IH), ergonomics, workflow automation, reporting, and advanced data analytics within an integrated system. This solution should allow facilities to identify, adapt, and implement best practices to meet specific needs and mitigate risks across the VA enterprise. Additionally, the solution will adhere to VA directives 7700, 7701, 7702, and 7703, which define responsibilities for Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) programs, latex allergy prevention, Industrial Hygiene, and Safety and Health Management Systems.   


The VA CEHRIS Team successfully completed a Proof-of-Concept for Cority GX2, which confirmed that the platform met VA’s needs for managing EOSH requirements. The proof of concept included: Capability Discovery, Identification, initial business requirements documentation and configuration of a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) for Incident Reporting. Cority GX2 has received VA Authority to Operate (ATO) approval. Any offered Brand Name Cority GX2 or Equivalent SaaS solution should provide the same or greater capabilities necessary to support enterprise deployment, module configuration, integrations, and year-over-year subscription adjustments based on VA Enterprise requirements. The period of performance for this requirement shall be one 12-month base period, four 12-month option periods, and one optional task.

Because the required solution is a SaaS application that will process, store, transmit, and access VA data, the Contractor should comply with all applicable VA information, security, privacy, data handling, Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP), and ATO requirements. The requirements below apply to any offered Brand Name Cority GX2 or Equivalent solution and are intended to ensure the solution can securely support VA enterprise EOSH operations prior to full production use. 

DATA HANDLING FOR USING DEVICES:


User Consent: Users who use the product shall consent to share their data, which may include Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and Protected Health Information (PHI), directly with the SaaS provider.

Published Terms: The SaaS provider shall have published terms and conditions for user consent.

Data Ownership: All data processed by the SaaS provider shall be owned by the Veterans Affairs.

Revocation: Users shall have the ability to revoke data sharing with the SaaS provider at any point.

Data Backup & Recovery

The solution must include automated, encrypted backups with defined recovery time objectives (RTO) and recovery point objectives (RPO). The vendor must document their disaster recovery procedures and test recovery processes regularly.

Prohibited Data Practices

The vendor shall not share, analyze, mine, or repurpose VA data for commercial purposes, including analytics, AI model training, or third-party integrations, without express written consent from the VA.

Access from End-User Devices

The solution must be compatible with VA-authorized endpoints and accessible via web-based interfaces secured through encrypted channels. The vendor must not store data on local devices, cache sensitive data, or allow offline access to SPI, PII, or PHI.

Brief Description of Supplies/ Services required and the intended use/EstimatedAmount:  This is a new, sole-source requirement. Bostons VA Healthcare System islooking to acquire 12 months of continued support for the CSP2017 Pivotal POP(Percutaneous Osseointegrated Prosthesis) Study, which relies on Modus HealthsStepWatch activity monitors and their proprietary data platform to track how Veterans movethroughout their daily lives. The purchase covers the monitors and accessories, the Moduscloud where all study data is uploaded and cleaned, remote training for participating sites,mobile hotspots to keep data flowing reliably, and the specialized data-processing servicethat generates the metrics the study depends on. Total Amount for one year of service fromAugust 1, 2026  July 31, 2027, is $82,880.87.3. Unique characteristics that limit availability to only one source, with the reason noother supplies or services can be used: The CSP2017 Percutaneous OsseointegratedProsthesis (POP) Study employs StepWatch devices and Modus proprietary analytics toassess secondary endpoints of functional mobility and community ambulation. Bostons VAHealthcare System requires specific derived metrics produced within the Modus cloud, plusstrict turnaround and export capabilities. Substituting another brand device or analyticswould require protocol changes, re-validation of endpoints, and would compromiselongitudinal comparability with existing data captured under prior contract 36C24121P0844.The previous period ended on July 8, 2026, and to avoid missed follow-ups and data gaps,this action must start August 1, 2026. Only Modus Health LLC can lawfully provide therequired proprietary metrics, device compatibility (UDIs), and the project-specific cloudpipeline used by CSP Boston. Modus Health LLC is the original developer of the StepWatchdevices and the only source for the secure, project-specific cloud and algorithms already

The proprietary nature ofthe StepWatch system and its analytics pipeline prevents other vendors from providingcompatible devices or data-processing services without disrupting the study design. Internalcommunications confirm that the prior contract ended and the requirement must continuewithout interruption, with instruction from leadership to proceed with sole sourcing due totiming and the study returning to research. Synopsis – Notice to Sole Source: 
 
NOTICE OF INTENT TO ISSUE A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT FOR THE BOREALIS 
(STAKEHOLDER RELATIONSHIP MANAGEMENT TOOL) SOFTWARE, LICENSES, 
MANAGED SERVICES, CONFIGURATION SUPPORT, TRAINING, AND 
DOCUMENTATION NECESSARY TO IMPLEMENT THE STAKEHOLDER 
RELATIONSHIP MANAGEMENT (SRM) TOOL 
 
This Notice is issued in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 
Overhaul (RFO) Part 5.101, Presolicitation Notice.  The U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI), 
Office of Acquisition and Property Management, Marine Minerals Administration (MMA), 
Acquisition Operations Branch (AOB), is the contracting office for this procurement. The 
purpose of this Notice is to announce the government’s intent to issue a sole source contract 
under the authority of RFO Part 12 to Boreal – Informations Strategiques 2014 Inc. (DBA: 
Borealis + Irth Solutions), 250-107 Main Street West, Magog, QC J1X 2A6 CAN, in accordance 
with RFO Part 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will 
Satisfy Agency Requirements. 
 
MMA has determined that Borealis (Stakeholder Relationship Management Tool) is the only 
Customer Relationship Management (CRM) tool solution that provides:  
 
• Long term, multi-issue relationship tracking for stakeholders and organizations, including 
evolving affiliations; 
• Built in stakeholder mapping, allowing MMA to analyze influence, interests, linkages, 
and areas of concern—critical for NEPA and offshore energy engagements; 
• Specialized indicators and analytical structures designed for natural resource and 
regulatory engagement, not sales; 
• Immediate off the shelf use, with no need for the extensive customization;  
• Workflow capabilities tailored to engagement processes (comment tracking, issue 
association, consultation history, event participation);  
• Integration with Outlook and Microsoft Teams for automated communication tracking; 
and  
• Unique mapping capabilities. 
 
The anticipated period of performance is 12 months from date of award. 
 
PLEASE NOTE: This notice is not a request for quote (RFQ). However, any firm that believes 
itself capable of meeting the requirement described herein may submit a capability statement or 
quotation which may be considered if received by the agency by 12:00pm Eastern Time on 13 
August 2026. All submissions in response to this notice must be submitted in writing via email 
to the Contracting Officer at catherine_robertson@ios.doi.gov referencing 140M0126Q0042, on 
the subject line. A determination by the Government not to compete the Government’s 
requirements described in this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY 
 
Request for Information (RFI) on  
A New Era of Partnership: Advancing America's Computing Capabilities 
 
THIS REQUEST IS FOR INFORMATION ONLY for conducting market 
research and does not constitute a solicitation or a promise to issue a solicitation.  
Responses are voluntary.  We will use the responses to inform strategic planning, 
program design, and future funding mechanisms. 
 
AGENCY:  Office of Science, Department of Energy  
RFI Number: 892431-26-RFI-0002 
Issue Date: 27 July 2026 
Response Due: 08 September 2026 
 
Introduction  
 
America’s enduring leadership in science, technology, and national security 
critically depends on sustained innovation in computing technologies—high-performance 
computing, artificial intelligence (AI), and quantum computing.  The Genesis Mission, 
launched by the President’s Executive Order,
1 is a massive effort to harness these 
capabilities to revolutionize science innovation in this Nation, effectively doubling the 
productivity and impact of American science and engineering in a decade.  These 
advances will lead to new industries and highly skilled jobs and will solve some of our 
Nation’s most pressing challenges in energy, security, and scientific discovery.  
 
The landscape of computing technology is evolving at an unprecedented rate.    
To maintain and advance American’s leadership, American industry must play a central 
role in the Genesis Mission.  This role involves integrating world-leading commercial 
expertise and capabilities with those of the Nation’s National Laboratories and 
universities.  The Department of Energy (DOE) has a long and storied history of 
successful partnerships with the private sector, dating back to the Manhattan Project.  
More recently, public-private partnerships have catalyzed innovations ranging from high-
performance computing to beamlines at world-leading x-ray light sources and specialized 
detectors for telescopes.    
 
New models of collaboration must be formulated that are as agile and innovative 
as the technologies we seek to advance.  These new collaborations cannot simply be a 
means of procuring hardware—they must be founded on establishing a highly synergistic 
relationship in which DOE, the National Laboratories, and private sector partners work 
together to advance our shared interests in technological frontiers.  
 
 
1 Executive Order 14363, Launching the Genesis Mission, 
https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/11/28/2025-21665/launching-the-
genesis-mission 

2 
In October 2025, DOE announced two public-private partnerships.2   
The partnership of NVIDIA and Oracle with Argonne National Laboratory plans to build 
two new AI supercomputers, Equinox and Solstice.  Additionally, the partnership of 
Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. and Hewlett Packard Enterprise with Oak Ridge National 
Laboratory will deliver the new AI supercomputer Lux.  These partnerships have the 
potential to co-create our future computing platforms to yield benefits to DOE and 
industry, and most importantly, to the scientific community and the Nation. 
 
Through public-private partnerships with industry on a large or small scale, DOE 
will provide a sound investment for the American taxpayer.  Benefits will extend far 
beyond DOE, empowering the academic community and the business sector with access 
to capabilities that would not otherwise exist.  However, we recognize that a one-size-
fits-all approach will not work, and each future partnership may have a different 
structure, tailored to the unique goals of the partners and the nature of the technology.  
 
DOE seeks input from respondents with innovative ideas for public-private 
computing partnerships that can advance our national interests, economic security, and 
national security.  Respondents may also suggest criteria for evaluating proposed 
partnerships.  Together, we can build the future of computing and ensure the United 
States remains at the forefront of scientific and technological discovery. 
 
Requested Information 
 
Responses should address any or all the areas specified below. 
 
Proposed Partnership 
Describe one or more proposed partnership including: 
• Who the partners may be and what each will contribute 
• How the partnership will be financed, capitalized, and financially sustained 
• What the business model for the partnership may be, including assumptions about 
how DOE and other U.S. Government agencies will serve as customers and how 
in-kind contributions will be valued 
• What resources and capabilities will the partnership make available to DOE and 
what resources are needed from DOE to reach the goals of the partnership 
• What will the partnership add to our national capabilities 
• What the timeline for the partnership is projected to be, especially major 
milestones and decision points  
• What the largest technical and non-technical (e.g., policy, regulatory) risks or 
barriers are to timely success  
 
 
 
2 https://www.energy.gov/articles/energy-department-announces-new-partnership-
nvidia-and-oracle-build-largest-doe-ai 

3 
Partnership Structure 
Describe how DOE can most effectively structure mutually beneficial partnerships.   
In your response, consider:  
• How responsibilities for financing, risk mitigation and management, infrastructure 
support, regulatory compliance, security, business development, and other factors 
are satisfied and split between DOE and the private sector partners 
• How to balance the value to DOE and the taxpayer versus the value to the private-
sector partners 
• How to balance the risks and opportunity costs to DOE and the taxpayer versus 
the risks and opportunity costs to the private-sector partners  
 
Evaluation Criteria 
DOE is considering the criteria listed below as part of the evaluation of proposed 
partnerships.  Are these criteria sufficient?  Should DOE consider other criteria? 
• Deployment speed 
• Scale of the resources provided 
• Ability to accelerate innovation and facilitate partnership formation 
• Coupling to existing DOE resources 
• Flexibility to provide DOE with more capabilities over time 
• Alignment with the DOE mission to accelerate DOE research priorities 
• Ability to address national priorities and enhance national competitiveness 
 
Confidential Business Information 
 
Any person submitting information that he or she believes to be confidential and 
exempt by law from public disclosure should submit via email two well-marked copies:  
one copy of the document marked “confidential” that includes all the information 
believed to be confidential and one copy of the document marked “non-confidential” that 
does not include any information believed to be confidential (10 C.F.R. § 1004.11). 
 
If you do not follow these marking requirements, unmarked information could be 
disclosed under the Freedom of Information Act or otherwise.  The U.S. Government is 
not liable for disclosure or use of unmarked information and may use or disclose such 
information for any purpose.  If your response contains confidential, proprietary, or 
privileged information, you must include a cover sheet marked with the following Notice 
of Restriction on Disclosure and Use of Data identifying the specific pages containing 
confidential, proprietary, or privileged information: 
 
Notice of Restriction on Disclosure and Use of Data 
Pages [list applicable pages] of this response may contain confidential, 
proprietary, or privileged information that is exempt from public 
disclosure.  Such information shall be used or disclosed by the 
Government and its contractors (including DOE’s contractor operated 
laboratories) only for the purposes described in RFI 892431-26-RFI-0002.  
The Government may use or disclose any information that is not 
appropriately marked or otherwise restricted, regardless of source. 

4 
 
In addition: 
• The header and footer of every page that contains confidential, proprietary, or 
privileged information must be marked:  Contains Confidential, Proprietary, or 
Privileged Information Exempt from Public Disclosure 
• Every line and paragraph containing proprietary, privileged, or trade secret 
information must be clearly marked with [[double brackets]] or highlighting. 
 
DOE may make available for public inspection all other comments, in their 
entirety, submitted by organizations and businesses (except as provided above for 
proprietary information) or by individuals identifying themselves as representatives of 
organizations or businesses. 
 
Submission Instructions 
 
Responses should not exceed five pages, including attachments and cover letters.  
Please also include the organization’s name and point of contact. 
 
Submit your response electronically to ComputingPartnerships@science.doe.gov 
and include “Computing Partnerships” in the subject line of the email. 
 
Further Information   
 
You can send questions about this RFI to the DOE Office of Science at 
ComputingPartnerships@science.doe.gov.

Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 
 
1. The ability to detect and locate Bluetooth and Bluetooth low-energy (BLE) devices when they are 
paired. 
a. Justification: Bluetooth/BLE devices are rapidly growing in the market. One of the major issues 
encountered are Bluetooth/BLE devices accidentally being brought into restricted areas. 
b. Technical Discussion: Bluetooth/BLE devices advertise their availability on up to three 
advertising channels. That is where all other capabilities on the market beside Bastille Networks 
can detect Bluetooth/BLE devices. Once the device pairs it stops advertising. That makes them 
blind to detection and location by all other tools except Bastille Networks. Bastille Networks has 
patented the capability (Massive Multi-channel Demodulation (M2CD) US Patents #11,190,091 
and #11,202,216) to detect Bluetooth/BLE devices on all communication channels whether 
paired or not. Bastille Networks system is composed of parallel decoders for all channels, so 
nothing is missed. 
2. 100% Passive system 
a. Justification: The primary goal of this effort is to reduce RF within the facility. RF-enabled 
devices introduce new risks and vulnerabilities and offer the threat actors new opportunities to 
compromise systems. 
b. Technical Discussion: Bastille Networks has been certified by Federal Communication 
Corporation (FCC) as being 100% passive. The other viable competitors send our RF burst to 
generate a response from devices. 
3. Upgradeable to incorporate new technologies without having to replace sensors. 
a. Justification: New RF protocols or new versions of protocols are continually being released. 
There is a requirement to ensure the system can easily and rapidly be upgraded to handle the new 
protocols. It would be resource intensive and prohibitive to have to constantly replace the RF 
sensor when new protocols are released. The Bastille firmware upgrade process ensures that 
there will be no gaps in coverage and removed the need to replace sensors to incorporate new 
protocols into the system detection capability. 
b. Technical Discussion: One of the differentiators of the Bastille sensor array is the massive 
amount of FPGA processing power that is available. With a 480k logic element Arria 10 SoC, 
the Bastille sensor array can instantiate over 100 distinct protocol decoders in parallel that can 
simultaneously process the full 120 MHz RF bandwidth that is captured by the two SDR front-
ends in the array. This is made possible with Bastille’s proprietary software-defined radios that
