Draft Statement of Work 
 
 
TASK REQUIREMENTS 
 
Task 1.0 Project Planning and Management 
 
Subtask 1.1: Kick-Off Meeting 
 
The Contractor must meet with the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) and Project Officer 
(PO) within two (2) weeks after base and option year awards to ensure clarification of project goals, 
scope of work, routine communication standards, quality control standards, and deliverable and invoice 
submissions. The purpose of the meeting will be to discuss the objectives of the task order and to reach 
a common understanding of how the contractor will complete the work, the timelines, and the 
deliverable schedule for projects under this task order. The contractor must be prepared to discuss 
critical activities requiring immediate attention and the project execution process. The COR and PO may 
also discuss anticipated requests with the contractor. The contractor may provide COR with a list of 
questions or issues in advance of the Kick-Off meeting. After the meeting, the contractor must submit a 
memo to the COR summarizing the meeting and any decisions made.  
 
Deliverable(s): (A) Kick-Off Meeting (B) Meeting Summary Memo  
 
Subtask 1.2: Weekly COR and PO Meetings 
 
The contractor must prepare a draft project management plan for the contract that details the intended 
approach to supporting the women’s health portfolio during the period of performance. The 
management plan must be brief (up to 5 pages) and include: an overall approach to performing tasks and 
managing projects, plans for communication, processes for budget and cost estimation, and a plan for 
how to resolve any issues that present themselves over the task order period of performance (i.e., 
changes in key personnel, delays in obtaining critical data).  
 
The task order management plan must specify: the contractor’s strategy for planning and preparing 
analytic products on short, medium, or long-term projects; how appropriate or necessary analysts, 
experts (including academic or other institutions), or sub-contractors are identified, and a strategy for 
conducting any data or policy analysis that may be requested for work products, including a process for 
receiving input from the COR and/or PO during the development of each product.  
The task order management plan must also include draft elements for the monthly progress report and a 
template for the budget report (Subtask 1.4).  
 
Deliverable(s): (A) Draft Task Order Management Plan (B) Final Task Order Management Plan  
 
Subtask 1.3: Project Work Plan 
 
The COR and/or PO will submit a project request to the contractor for each specific project under this 
task order, including background information, research questions to be addressed, tasks, and a draft 
schedule of deliverables. Upon receipt of the request, the contractor may request a meeting with the 
COR and PO assigned to the project to determine the specific scope and proposed approach for each 
project. These meetings may take place via a video conferencing platform (e.g. Microsoft Teams, Zoom, 

 
 
Webex), email, conference call, or in conjunction with a weekly conference call (Subtask 1.4), and may 
occur as needed over the course of the project. Each project (See Task 2) will require a project work 
plan and a proposed subject matter team of experts.  
 
The contractor must draft a project work plan for each project request, submit it to the COR and PO for 
review and approval within two (2) weeks of receipt, and host a meeting to discuss it. The project work 
plan must detail the project's technical approach and schedule (see Task 2). Specifically, the project 
work plan must include a description of the technical approach; any anticipated challenges to 
completing the project and how the contractor will address them; staffing and management 
responsibilities; and the allocation of project resources, including projected hours per staff member. The 
project work plan shall also include a timeline that identifies the start and completion dates, as well as 
other milestones, for each deliverable specified in the plan. The project work plan must be based on the 
project request from the COR and PO, as well as discussions and other decisions made at the project 
work plan meeting. The COR and PO may modify the project work plan, including completion dates, 
after consultation with the contractor, if needed. All approved project requests must be completed by the 
end of the contract's period of performance or discontinued by mutual agreement of the contractor, the 
COR, and the PO.  
 
Draft project work plans must be submitted to the COR and PO for review and approval no later than 
two (2) weeks after the project work plan development meeting or otherwise agreed upon by the COR 
and PO. Upon incorporating comments from the COR and PO and final approval by the COR and PO, a 
final work plan shall be submitted to the COR and PO no later than one (2) weeks after final approval.  
 
Deliverable(s): (A) Draft, (B) Final Project Work Plan(s), as needed  
 
Subtask 1.4: Standing Project Management Conference Calls  
 
Standing conference calls between the contractor, the COR, and the PO must be scheduled within one 
week of the EDOC. The contractor, the COR, and the PO will decide on the periodicity of project 
management calls, which may change during the contract period to reflect HHS OWH's evolving needs, 
but should be assumed to occur weekly. During each call, the contractor shall be prepared to discuss any 
issues that have arisen since the last monthly progress report (Subtask 1.5) and to provide key updates 
on current projects, including any changes to the estimated budget or costs. The contractor must develop 
an agenda prior to the call and, within one week, distribute the meeting minutes, including key points 
and decisions, to the COR and PO.  
 
Deliverable(s): (A) Standing Call Agendas (B) Standing Call Action Items Summaries  
 
Subtask 1.5: Monthly Progress Reports  
 
The contractor must submit monthly progress reports (not to exceed four (4) pages, excluding tables or 
charts) outlining all work accomplished during the previous month. At a minimum, such reports should 
cover the following items: 
 
• Discussion of the progress in accomplishing the tasks specified in this task order. 
• Difficulties encountered and remedial action(s) taken.  
• Activities anticipated during the upcoming reporting period.  
• Personnel and other management changes.  

 
 
 
Monthly progress reports are due within the first week of each month following the Kick-Off Meeting 
(Subtask 1.1), or as otherwise agreed upon by the COR and the contractor, and must be sent by the 
Principal Investigator directly to the COR via email. Monthly progress reports should specify the use of 
funds by project, including staff hours for each project and for overall administration of the task order.  
 
Deliverable(s): (A) Monthly Progress Reports  
 
Task 2.0 Data Collection, Analysis, Research, and Reporting 
 
The Contractor will develop a 5-year Strategic Plan and an annual Work Plan that outlines an approach for 
conducting an in-depth analysis of women's and infants' morbidity and mortality data, including inpatient 
and outpatient data, as outlined in Tasks 2.0–4.0. 
 
The Contractor will provide access to up-to-date, standardized inpatient and outpatient women and infant 
deidentified health information from a nationally representative database, along with advanced artificial 
intelligence models, to better understand U.S. maternal and infant health outcomes that affect overall 
health and to identify the drivers of maternal and infant mortality and morbidity as outlined in Tasks 2.0 – 
2.3. 
 
The Contractor must develop and routinely update state and regional heat maps of de-identified women's 
and infants' health outcomes in the U.S., as outlined in Tasks 2.0 – 2.3, annually.  
 
The Contractor must access, collect, and report on de-identified, standardized inpatient and outpatient data 
for the prior calendar year (analysis to include retrospective data from 2008 through the current year, as 
available and appropriate) on women and infant health outcomes in the U.S as outlined in Tasks 2.0 – 2.3. 
 
The Contractor must ensure that all analyses and heat maps outlined in Tasks 2.0 – 2.3 include (but not be 
limited to) stratification by age, race, ethnicity, mode of delivery, chronic conditions, payer, hospital type, 
geographic location, and any other relevant factors contributing to morbidity and mortality, excluding any 
data elements defined as personally identifiable information (PII).  
 
The Contractor must provide annual statistical and quarterly trended outcome reports on all analyses 
outlined in Tasks 2.0 – 2.3. 
 
The Contractor must provide updates to the HHS women and infant dashboards as outlined in the Work 
Plan and specified in Tasks 2.0–2.3. 
 
The Contractor must provide technical assistance in developing work products, including quantitative and 
qualitative analyses and associated written documents, as outlined in Tasks 2.0–2.3. 
 
Deliverable(s): (A) Develop 5-year Strategic Plan and Annual Work Plans, (B) State and regional 
heat maps for data analysis outlined in Tasks 2.0 – 2.3. (C) Analysis of de-identified women and 
infant standardized inpatient and outpatient data. (D) Annual women and infant analysis, stratified, 
statistical, and trended outcome reports. (E) Annual and quarterly updated HHS women and infant 
dashboards as outlined in the Work Plan supporting Tasks 2.0 – 2.3.  (F) Technical Assistance 
 
Subtask 2.1: National Women and Infant Research Analysis   

 
 
 
National Women and Infant Research Analysis using a nationally representative research database to 
examine factors contributing to maternal and infant morbidity and mortality, including the role of chronic 
conditions; stratified by patient demographics and socioeconomic factors, disease severity, comorbidities, 
complications, and resource utilization data. 
 
The Contractor must analyze and measure data using advanced data technologies and biostatistics 
methods, including regression analyses and microsimulation modeling, to address requested HHS research 
topics as specified in the Work Plans, such as: 
 
• Understanding the relationship between various pre-existing conditions and other risk factors, 
complications, morbidity, and mortality. 
• Estimating the costs and benefits of women and infant policy proposals under consideration by 
HHS 
• Work with HHS on women's and infants' health innovations, market trends, and opportunities to 
identify knowledge gaps for quantitative and qualitative analysis. 
• Assessing outcomes that are the focus of HHS-wide initiatives.  
 
The Contractor must provide adjusted and unadjusted analyses from a nationally representative, 
standardized inpatient database on women's and infants’ data, including linked health outcomes, annually, 
as described in the Strategic and Work plans. 
 
The Contractor must analyze up-to-date data describing the relationships between maternal and infant 
mortality and morbidity throughout the contract and report findings on a routine basis. 
 
The Contractor must analyze data and perform cost analyses of women's and infant healthcare, including 
morbidity and mortality. 
 
The Contractor must provide technical assistance and develop work products, including various 
quantitative and qualitative analyses and associated written documents. 
 
The Contractor must routinely analyze data to evaluate the relationship between women's health across the 
continuum on maternal-infant morbidity and mortality, including contributing conditions such as diabetes, 
hypertension, and obesity. 
 
The Contractor must provide Annual statistical and trended HHS-directed measures abstracted from the 
nationally representative, standardized database on women's and infants’ data, including linked health 
outcomes, to support the HHS Interagency Maternal Health Dashboard, as described in the Strategic and 
Work plans. 
 
Task 2.1 Deliverable(s): (A) Ongoing women and infant inpatient and outpatient and linked data 
research analysis as specified in the agreed-upon Strategic and Work Plans (B) Annual and 
Quarterly women and infant analysis and outcome extract (C)Technical assistance (D) Annual 
women and infant research analysis outcome reports  (E) Analyze and measure data using 
advanced methods specified in the Work Plan (F) Analyze data describing relationships (G) Analyze 
data describing cost (H) Annual statistical and trended HHS-directed measures for the HHS 
Interagency Maternal Health Dashboard (I) Up to six (6) Ad-hoc women and infant analysis, 
focused data drills, and supporting reports as directed by HHS annually. 

 
 
 
Subtask 2.2: HHS Perinatal Improvement Collaborative (HHS PIC) 
 
The HHS PIC measures the effect of interventions on maternal and infant outcomes. This large-scale 
effort unites a cohort of more than 318 U.S. hospitals in a data-driven national maternal and infant 
perinatal quality improvement collaborative to better understand the implementation of standardized, 
evidence-based practices and processes, including nationally recognized care bundles, and their effects on

The Contractor must maintain the HHS Perinatal Improvement Collaborative (HHS PIC) (a network of

The Contractor must:

The National Institute of Health’s National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences (NCATS)

The National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences (NCATS)  hereby submits a notice of 
intent to award a sole source firm  fixed price purchase order for a Rocky Linux Subscription 
Renewal.  Rocky Linux is a free Linux- based open- source enterprise operating system, a 
downstream of Red Hat Enterprise Linux or RHEL. This request is to renew the license 
subscription and get high -level technical support for this operating system. The North American 
Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541511.

operating system, the required high -level support is to ensure availability of the NCATS HPC

scientific computing and a requirement to move forward with scientific analysis to be done using

STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 
Project Title 
JSU RPMS Replacement 
 
1. Purpose 
This Statement of Work (SOW) deﬁnes the scope, deliverables, responsibilities, and 
timeline for the procurement, installation, conﬁguration, and support of an IBM Power 
S1014 server environment, associated storage, software, and Hardware Management 
Console (HMC) for the Jicarilla Service Unit. 
The Indian Health Service (IHS), Jicarilla Service Unit, requires replacement of an end-of-
life (EOL) RPMS server currently supporting critical healthcare operations. The existing 
system is no longer supported and does not meet current security and reliability standards. 
Acquisition of a modern, supported IBM Power Systems server is required to maintain 
continuity of RPMS services, ensure compliance with federal security requirements, and 
improve system performance and resiliency. 
 
2. Scope of Work 
2.1 Hardware Implementation 
ConvergeOne will provide and coordinate delivery, installation, and validation of the 
following hardware components: 
• IBM Power S1014 Server (Power10, 8-core processor) 
• 64GB DDR5 Memory 
• NVMe and SSD storage conﬁguration 
• Tape backup solution (LTO-8 tape drive and media) 
• Multi-media storage enclosure 
• Hardware Management Console (HMC) 
• Networking components (10GbE and 1GbE adapters) 
• Power supplies, cabling, and rack integration components 
2.2 Software Installation & Conﬁguration 
Installation and conﬁguration of: 
• IBM AIX 7.3 (Base + Expansion Pack) 
• IBM PowerVM V4 (including VIOS and virtualization capabilities) 
• NovaLink integration 
• System ﬁrmware and preload conﬁgurations 
• Language and compliance conﬁgurations (US English, TAA) 

 
3. Deliverables 
• Fully installed and operational IBM Power S1014 system 
• Conﬁgured AIX 7.3 environment 
• Functional PowerVM virtualization platform 
• Operational HMC system 
• Conﬁgured backup solution 
• System documentation (conﬁguration summary) 
• Knowledge transfer session 
 
4. Support & Maintenance 
The following support services are included: 
4.1 Hardware Support 
• 3-Year Advanced Expert Care 
• 24x7 Same Day Onsite Response (6hr Call / 4hr Parts Delivery) 
4.2 Software Support 
• 3-Year Software Maintenance Agreements (SWMA) 
• 24x7 support for AIX and PowerVM 
 
5. Roles & Responsibilities 
5.1 ConvergeOne Responsibilities 
• Hardware procurement and delivery coordination 
• Installation and conﬁguration of all systems 
• System integration and validation 
• Provide documentation and knowledge transfer 
• Coordinate support activation 
5.2 Customer Responsibilities 
• Provide rack space, power, and network connectivity 
• Ensure data center readiness 
• Provide access to facilities and personnel 
• Participate in validation and acceptance testing 
6. Section 508 and Accessibility  

• This product must conform to the Revised Section 508 (https://www.access-
board.gov/guidelines-and-standards/communications-and-it/about-the-ict-
refresh/ﬁnal-rule/text-of-the-standards-and-guidelines) and WCAG 2.1 Level 
AA standards as outlined below.  
• Solicitations for supplies and services shall require the submission of a Section 
508 Product Assessment Template.  The template can be found at 
https://www.itic.org/policy/accessibility/vpat. 
 
All Information and Communication Technology (ICT) deliverables under this contract 
(e.g., websites, applications, electronic documents, and multimedia) must comply 
with the Revised Section 508 Standards (36 CFR Part 1194) and the Web Content 
Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA standards. The Contractor shall ensure 
accessibility of all ICT deliverables and provide conformance documentation in the 
form of a Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT®) / Accessibility 
Conformance Report (ACR), or by completing the HHS Section 508 Accessibility 
Checklists. The current VPAT 2.5 template includes ﬁelds for reporting conformance 
to WCAG 2.1 and shall be used to document accessibility. The Contractor shall 
remediate any identiﬁed accessibility issues at no additional cost. The Contracting 
Officer will include the applicable Health and Human Services Acquisition Regulation 
(HHSAR) clauses 352.239-73 and 352.239-74 in the solicitation and resulting contract.

Statement of Requirements 

eTesting Officer Training School/Holm Center/DE

 

 

1.0  PURPOSE. Modernize assessment capabilities across the USAF officer school training complex. The Holm Center is responsible for commissioning approximately 80 percent of all USAF officers, making a robust, reliable yet flexible testing essential. The system must support validation of learning outcomes through both paper-based and online testing—paper-based delivery when campus internet connectivity is limited or unavailable, and online testing when connectivity is reliable. The solution must also interface seamlessly with existing test bank architecture (ParTest and ParScore) to preserve historical test item performance statistics and enable long-term tracking of curriculum effectiveness.    

 

2.0  DESCRIPTION OF ITEMS. The requested requirement is for comprehensive test delivery and scoring software. The software must provide hybrid assessment delivery (both paper and online administration). Online assessments must allow test-takers to log in and complete their assessments; software must be able to receive student data in multiple formats (e.g. Excel, PDF, etc.) and export student data (test results) in multiple formats (e.g. Excel, PDF, etc.); activate lockdown and time-elapse features when test is initiated to prevent test compromise and ensure test-taker time requirements. Software must analyze test results; store tests as individual test-takers and/or across multiple class rosters for data aggregation; capture test-taker date; rescore tests when applicable test item analysis/challenges are requested; enable test-takers to retake test when required; and contain immediate test soring feature. In addition, the software must include the ability to create (build), modify, and store multiple test item banks;  provide detailed test item analysis to evaluate the effectiveness of test questions; allow questions to be imported from various sources or creation of new ones; employ testing lockdown features in alignment with emergency test stoppage (continuation feature upon emergency completion). It must also generate printed test booklets for use with Scantron forms or deliver tests online; provide test statistics and test validation features.  Software must have the capability to seamlessly provide over 5000 student assessments annually.

Brand name: Scantron Eva Exam software is the updated direct replacement for the now unsupported Scantron ParTest and ParScore software suite. It is fully backward compatible with the existing proprietary architecture, allowing us to seamlessly import test question banks from the obsolete (existing) platform into the new system. This compatibility is critical, as it preserves historical test item performance statistics and aggregated data across multiple cohorts, both past and present. In addition, the existing test banks represent thousands of labor hours. Upgrading to a compatible, modern solution is the most efficient use of time, funding, and personnel, and avoids significant costs associated with recreating assessment content.

2.1  SOFTWARE SPECIFICATIONS REQUIRED  

 

2.1.1 Software must be compatible with ParTest and ParScore allowing direct import of existing test banks and historical data from obsolete (existing) software.   

2.1.2 Must capture test item performance past to present in content transfer conversion. 

2.1.3 Have robust customizable analytics package that is customizable to organizational hierarchy used in OTS: overall class performance, squadron performance, and individual flight performance. 

2.1.4 Role-based security allowing different permissions between the test administrator, department chairs on instructional design teams, and leadership; ability to view performance across the enterprise. 

2.1.5 Operate in both paper-based and digital environments.

GENERAL INFORMATION

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

Request for Information

Customer Relationship Management (CRM) Modernization

Introduction:

This is a Request for Information (RFI) only issued for conducting market research. This request is a RFI only and shall not be considered an invitation for Bids (IFB), Request for Quotations (RFQ), or a Request for Proposal (RFP) Do not submit a proposal or quote. This market research is issued for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation nor does it restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach. Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services described in this RFI. Your response to this RFI will be treated only as information for the Government to consider. You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this RFI. The information provided may be used by the VA in developing its acquisition strategy. Any contract that might be awarded based on information received or derived from this market research will be the outcome of a competitive process. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response. The Government does not intend to pay for the information submitted in response to this RFI.

The Veteran Experience Services (VES) portfolio within the Office of Information & Technology (OIT) is seeking information from qualified vendors in support of the development of an enterprise customer relationship management application — an effort to consolidate and standardize VA contact center Customer Relationship Management (CRM)s across the entire VA enterprise. The effort will be to operate and maintain the existing Microsoft Dynamics and Salesforce based CRMs, while also designing, developing, and launching the new enterprise CRM.  

Current Understanding

The consolidated CRM will be built on the Salesforce platform. VA has identified a preliminary list of contact center CRMs likely to be included in this consolidation: 

Unified Desktop Optimization CRM (UDO) / Veterans Outreach Interaction and Communication Engine (VOICE) CRM 

VA Solid Start CRM 

Community Care CRM (CommCare) 

VET-HOME CRM 

Member Services CRM 

Education Contact Center CRM 

Women’s Veterans Call Center CRM

VA Customer Experience Service Recovery Platform (VACX SRP) CRM

VA Health Connect CRM

AskVA CRM

This list is not final and may expand as VA completes its inventory of enterprise contact center systems.

This acquisition is specific to CRM sustainment (for legacy systems) and modernization (for the consolidated system). This scope does not include the Contact Center as a System (CCaaS) (Genysys), although there is significant integration required with that system. 

Areas Requiring Further Definition

The Government is still working through several foundational decisions and is using this RFI, in part, to inform them: 

Acquisition strategy – VA has not yet determined whether this requirement will be competed full and open or set aside for a specific socio-economic category.

Consolidation and phasing approach – VA has not determined whether to migrate one CRM onto the new platform first and add others incrementally, or take a broader approach across multiple systems at once. VA has also not determined whether to consolidate into one single CRM or multiple at once, nor what a phased rollout would look like.

Scope – VA has not defined whether this scope of work will include additional features such as chatbot or live agent chat. 

Responses:

As part of your market research response, please provide a written submission of no more than 6 pages in Times New Roman or Arial 12-point font addressing the following:

1. Contractor Information
Provide your firm's name, address, phone number, email address, and Unique Entity Identification (UEI) number.

2. Existing Contracting Vehicles
VA Anticipates that this effort will fall withing North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 541512. Indicate whether your firm holds an applicable contract vehicle (e.g., GSA MAS SIN 54151S) and describe how it is within scope of this requirement.

3. Business Size and Socioeconomic Status
Confirm your firm's size status under NAICS 541512 and identify any socioeconomic certifications held (e.g. Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) status as verified in the applicable certification system of record).

4. Relevant Technical Experience
Briefly describe your firm's experience with any of the following:

Microsoft Dynamics 365 / Power Platform / Salesforce
Configuring and sustaining enterprise scale Salesforce and D365 model driven applications.

Human Centered Design (HCD) & User Experience
Conducting user research, usability testing, journey mapping, and delivering intuitive, accessible (508/WCAG) case management workflows for nationwide user populations.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) Enablement 
Evaluating Salesforce platform readiness for Agentforce and integrating AI/ML capabilities (case classification, summarization, next-best-action recommendations) into enterprise workflows using Agentforce agents, Einstein AI, and Data Cloud, including experience supporting re-platforming from D365 to Salesforce to enable native, agentic AI features.

Enterprise Change, Modernization, and Large-Scale Workflow Redesign
Executing major configuration overhauls, workflow redesigns, organizational alignment, and multiphase modernization initiatives while maintaining operational continuity.

CRM Consolidation, Re-Platforming, and Transformation
Taking a number of legacy CRM solutions into unified enterprise CRM that will support many lines of business and hundreds of call types.  

Scale of Contract and Team Management
Staffing and managing contracts of comparable scale and complexity, including team size, contract value, and number of concurrent workstreams.

5. Recommended Approach


Training & Change Management 

Describe your change management and training approach for call center CRM rollouts, including specific examples and how you measure agent adoption and address resistance.

AI Assisted Development and Test

Describe your approach to using AI tools in the CRM development process — including code generation, configuration, or testing — and how you ensure AI-assisted work meets quality and security standards prior to deployment.

Enterprise CRM Approach

Based on the call types and lines of business supported across VA's call centers, and drawing on your experience working with organizations of similar scale and scope, would it be more appropriate and cost-effective for VA to consolidate onto a single CRM or to operate multiple large CRMs? Please describe your rationale for recommending this approach.

6. Comments and questions. In your firm’s opinion, what are the most important requirements for the Government to define before a draft PWS is released? Do you have any additional comments or questions on this requirement?

Submittal Information:

Responses are requested no later than 1:00PM EST on August 4, 2026 by email to Joseph.Jeranek@va.gov. All responsible sources may submit a responses which shall be considered by the agency.

Please note “36C10B27Q0006” in the subject line of your email response.

The Government requests that submissions do not include marketing materials, boilerplate capability statements, or peripheral content. Responses should be concise and directly address the questions above.

Maintenance contract procurement is required to service Video Teleconference (VTC) equipment for Naval

cover all VTC and AV equipment in NAVIFOR VTC Rooms C100, C101, C102, C113, C186, C200, and

Option Year III: 27 September 2029-26 September 2030 
In conclusion, the requested supplies or services represent the minimum requirements of the government. 
 
Describe in detail why only this source(s) can furnish the requirements to the exclusion of other sources.  
 
Existing systems were installed and integrated by AVI-SPL LLC. The vendor has proprietary software in the 
programming of the entire system. Each device is configured to work in tandem with all the other devices. The 
specific programming for user features (Touch Panel interface) was developed and installed by AVI-SPL, the 
user interface is specific to AVI-SPL, as they own the software. AVI-SPL is aware of each device installed in 
the system and can provide one-for-one swap of malfunctioning equipment. The seamless interfacing provides 
consistency for the crucial integration and maintenance of the current systems put in place by AVI-SPL. If an 
alternative source was used other than AVI-SPL, it could result in inconsistencies and system malfunctions 
beyond repair.  
AVI-SPL Elite Support provides remote technical phone support services, facilitation of manufacturer repair or 
replacement programs, access to manufacturer published software updates and upgrades for covered assets, and

unlimited Onsite Field Technician dispatch. AVI-SPL Elite Support also includes access to an online portal for 
incident reporting and annual business reviews. Remote technical phone support services are available 
24x7x365. These services are one of a kind and are built specifically for the benefit of NAVIFOR and the 
government’s needs.  
 
Market Research was conducted against mandatory sources such as UNICOR, AbilityOne, and GSA which 
yielded negative results. AVI-SPL does not have any authorized resellers or subsidiaries and currently, there are 
no other products on the market that can satisfy the Government's minimum requirement.

AVI-SPL is the owner of the data that is programmed into the VTC system to allow each device to work 
together to conduct VTCs. This data is also what provides the Touch Screen interface for the user to control the 
system. Other vendors would need to redo all programming from scratch to bring a system back online, this 
would greatly increase the cost of the service. All property data is owned and maintained by AVI-SPL.  
  
☒ These are "direct replacement" parts/components for existing equipment. 
 
AVI-SPL will provide direct replacement parts, as needed, and will be able to transfer existing software updates 
and programming to the new device, simply and quickly.

STATEMENT OF WORK

VA Palo Alto Health Care System (VAPAHCS)

Background:  The VAPAHCS is researching the marketplace for alternative middleware software systems for Point-of-Care devices. The VA Palo Alto Ancillary Testing Department requires equipment to interface the Ancillary testing devices to the Laboratory Information System (VISTA) and the electronic health record (CPRS). This interface receives the patient POC test results and pulls the patient’s demographics from the Lab Information System (LIS). This system will apply all of the appropriate rules in adherence to all appropriate regulations to ensure quality and compliance standards and requirements are met. This system will also serve as the electronic storage of all test parameters and results.

Contract Requirements

The Contractor shall provide the following to maintain data management, support and connectivity under the following conditions:

1. Middleware support for Lab Information System (LIS) interface for the following instruments:

	a. Abbott i-STAT POC

	b. Roche AccuChek Inform II

	c. Roche CoaguChek XS Plus/Pro

	d. Oximeter AVOXimeter 1000E

      e. GEM Premier 7000

      f. GEM Premier Chemststat

2. At no additional cost provide the following to transmit laboratory results and other data between the connected diagnostic instruments (listed under sub-paragraph a.) and the LIS

	a. Licensed instrument interface (software),

	b. data/information management system

	c. server (hardware)

	d. operating system and associated server software upgrades as needed

	e. System must be available 24 hours per day/7 day

	f. Software and data management system capable of managing remote test results for all instruments listed above. This includes but is not limited to quality control and linearity, testing person identity, meter identity, patient results, critical values, flagged records, reference values, new lot reagent records and hold back results bases on pre-determined criteria.

	g. Middleware upgrades, patches and any back-end changes provided at no additional cost over the life of the contract

	h. The entire data management system must be able to interface a wide range of instrumentation; both uni-directional and bi-directional as shown in the attached desired test menu list. This will provide support for instrumentation changes at VAPAHCS over time.

Period of Performance:

	Base year:      Oct 1, 2026, to Sep 30, 2027

	Option year 1: Oct 1, 2027, to Sep 30, 2028

	Option year 2: Oct 1, 2028, to Sep 30, 2029

	Option year 3: Oct 1, 2029, to Sep 30, 2030

	Option year 4: Oct 1, 2030, to Sep 30, 2031

Location and Hours of Operation:

The primary data management system will be located at VA Palo Alto HCS, Pathology & Laboratory Medicine Service, Building 100, 4th Floor Room E4-310. The primary system administrator (Ancillary Test Coordinator) operates the system Monday through Friday 8:00 am to 5:00 pm at this location. Staff using the system are located throughout the hospital and off-site clinics and work 7 days per week, 24 hours per day.

Contractor Responsibilities and Tasks:

The Contractor shall provide qualified technicians or IT staff who shall perform in a professional manner in accordance to industry standards and VA local policies.

At the conclusion of each requested service or scheduled upgrade, the Contractor shall provide a written service report indicating the date of service, name of technician or staff that performed the work and the service performed. The reports shall be delivered to the COR and the Ancillary Test Coordinator by email.

Software or system updates: applicable regulations and manufacturers specifications, and will include, but is not limited to the following:

	a. Reviewing operating system and connections to ensure that the equipment and licensed software is operating within its specifications

	b. Replacing any worn or defective parts: inclusive of PC, cables or any other deliverables

	c. The Contractor shall furnish and replace all necessary parts for the data management system. The contractor shall use new parts only. Re-built or backward-engineered parts are not permitted.

	d. Work outside the scope of the contract shall not be performed unless authorized by VAPAHCS Biomedical Engineering Department prior to the work being performed.

Personnel Qualification

The Contractor must be qualified to work on all components of the data management system and the latest revisions of hardware and software as required by the Ancillary Testing Coordinator.

Security Consideration. All VA policies shall be followed. Based upon a review of the PWS/SOW as presented, the contractor will have access to VA sensitive information to fulfill the terms of the contract. That sensitive information will include PII/PHI.  As a result, a BAA will be required.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT DRAFT 
 
Surgical Communicator 
 
1. SCOPE OF WORK 
1.1. The contractor shall design, develop, and deploy a secure, scalable digital platform that 
provides real-time updates and engagement capabilities throughout the surgical 
journey. The contractor will work hand in hand with the VA SME to co-design the 
solution, incorporating direct feedback loops into each phase of development to ensure 
the platform reflects operational realities, fits seamlessly into existing operational 
processes and enhances rather than disrupts existing workflows. The platform shall be 
designed to integrate with VistA, VA enterprise services, DSS Livedata and future 
Oracle Health workflows, enabling automation, improving accuracy, and reducing 
manual effort over time. The developed solution will be owned and hosted by the VA 
with ongoing customer service, support and debugging during development and 
deployment provided by the vendor. 
1.2. Core capabilities of the platform: 
1.2.1. Real-Time Surgical Status Tracking A visually clean, mobile friendly, milestone-
based interface that tracks and displays the key stages of the surgical process, 
including Pre-Operative, In the Operating Room, Anesthesia induced, Procedure 
Start, Procedure Complete, Closing, and Move to Recovery. Updates are provided 
in a clear, intuitive format that is easy for patients and families to understand. 
1.2.2. Family & Caregiver Engagement Veterans can designate any number of family 
members or caregivers to receive surgical status updates. Each participant 
receives secure, permission-based access using a secure access code, sms link or 
QR code to view status updates in real time. 
1.2.3. Flexible Enrollment Workflows: 
1.2.3.1. Patients can self-enroll family members through a simple mobile friendly 
workflow during the pre-surgical process 
1.2.3.2. VA staff can enroll family members during check-in, intake, or pre-
operative workflows. 
1.2.4. Notification & Access Layer Secure links and optional notifications (e.g., SMS or 
email) ensure that families are informed of key milestones without requiring 
continuous manual outreach. 
1.3. The contractor shall use the Pilot-to-Enterprise delivery model, a phased approach (4 
phases): 
1.3.1. Phase I. Design & Discovery 
1.3.1.1. Map current workflows and identify integration points 
1.3.1.2. Design a human-centered user experience tailored to Veterans and 
families  
1.3.1.3. Engage the VA SME in working sessions to shape workflows, validate 
user experience designs, and ensure alignment with clinical and operational 
needs 

 
Page 2 of 15 
1.3.2. Phase II. Build & Integration 
1.3.2.1. Develop Minimum Viable Product (MVP) capabilities using secure, 
scalable architecture 
1.3.2.2. Align with VistA and VA enterprise services where applicable  
1.3.2.3. Ensure compliance with VA security and accessibility standards  
1.3.2.4. Iterate with continuous VA SME feedback, incorporating real-time insights 
into development sprints to refine functionality and usability 
1.3.3. Phase III. Pilot Deployment 
1.3.3.1. Launch the solution at VA Central California Health Care 
1.3.3.2. Provide training, onboarding, and white-glove support 
1.3.3.3. Monitor usage, feedback, and performance 
1.3.3.4. Partner closely with the VA SME during pilot execution to capture 
feedback, identify improvements, and guide iteration toward enterprise 
readiness 
1.3.4. Phase IV. Evaluation & Scale (LONG TERM VISION) 
1.3.4.1. Measure outcomes and refine the solution 
1.3.4.2. Expand to additional sites and capabilities 
1.3.4.3. Transition to enterprise-scale deployment support. 
1.4. Scalability 
1.4.1. The contractor shall provide a tracker that is designed as a foundational 
capability that evolves into a comprehensive surgical journey platform. This 
phased, MVP-first approach ensures that the platform delivers immediate value 
while continuously expanding in capability and impact. 
1.5. Near-Term Enhancements 
1.5.1. Pre-surgery engagement, including reminders, preparation instructions, and 
checklists 
1.5.2. Post-surgery follow-up communications, including recovery guidance and care 
instructions 
1.6. Long-Term Vision 
1.6.1. End-to-end orchestration of the surgical journey from scheduling through 
recovery  
1.6.2. AI-generated updates and summaries to provide meaningful, human-readable 
insights for families 
1.6.3. Analytics dashboards for VA leadership to monitor operational efficiency, patient 
satisfaction, and throughput 
2. CONTRACT TYPE 
2.1. Firm Fixed Price

Performance Work Statement DRAFT 
Purpose 
The Veterans Health Administration seeks to evaluate the Continuous Glucose Monitoring 
technology with an AI driven mobile application platform as a potential 
non-pharmacological intervention to support weight management and metabolic health 
among Veterans. This pilot is intended to address the needs of individuals who are not 
eligible for, have not responded to, or prefer to avoid pharmacologic treatments such as 
GLP-1 receptor agonists. The initiative will assess the feasibility and effectiveness of 
integrating Continuous Glucose Monitoring technology with an AI-driven mobile 
application to deliver real-time insights, support behavior change, and promote weight 
loss. The contractor will be responsible for full deployment, onboarding, ongoing support, 
and secure handling of Patient Generated Data in alignment with VA requirements. 
Throughout the pilot, key outcomes—including weight change, metabolic indicators, user 
engagement, and adherence—will be monitored to generate a comprehensive evaluation. 
The findings will inform the VA’s understanding of clinical impact, total cost per participant, 
and comparative value relative to GLP-1 therapies, supporting data-driven decisions 
regarding potential future adoption or expansion. 
Scope 
The purpose of this effort is to pilot and evaluate the Continuous Glucose Monitoring 
technology with an AI driven mobile application platform as a non-pharmacological 
solution for weight management and metabolic health among Veterans. The contractor 
shall provide all necessary personnel, equipment, software, and support services to deploy 
and operate a solution that combines Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) devices with 
an AI-driven mobile application. The platform must enable real-time tracking of glucose 
response to food and deliver actionable insights to support behavior change and weight 
loss. The pilot will focus on Veterans who are not eligible for, have not responded to, or 
prefer to avoid pharmacologic treatments such as GLP-1 receptor agonists. The contractor 
shall ensure full deployment, participant onboarding, ongoing support, and secure 
collection of Patient Generated Data in accordance with VA requirements. Throughout the 
period of performance, the contractor shall monitor and report on key outcomes, including 
weight change, metabolic indicators (as available), user engagement, and adherence. At 
the conclusion of the pilot, the contractor shall provide a comprehensive evaluation that 
includes clinical outcomes, total cost per participant, and a cost-benefit comparison 
against GLP-1 treatment approaches, along with clear, data-driven recommendations 
regarding scalability and potential adoption within the VA system. 

 
 
 
Data 
The Vendor shall provide participant onboarding and access to the Continuous Glucose 
Monitoring technology with an AI driven mobile application platform. During onboarding, 
the Vendor shall collect only the participant information necessary to establish user 
accounts and activate the Continuous Glucose Monitor (CGM) device. The platform shall 
collect and store participant-generated health data (PGHD), including CGM readings and 
participant-entered wellness information such as meals, exercise, sleep, and weight, for 
the purpose of providing metabolic health insights and coaching. The Vendor shall protect 
all participant information in accordance with applicable privacy, security, and contractual 
requirements. The Continuous Glucose Monitoring technology with an AI driven mobile 
application platform shall not connect to VA information systems or the VA Electronic 
Health Record (EHR), and no VA clinical data shall be transmitted to or accessed by the 
Vendor. All information collected by the platform shall be provided directly by participating 
Veterans. 
 
Based upon a review of the PWS/SOW and Appendix A as presented, the contractor will not 
have access to VA sensitive information or PII/PHI to fulfill the terms of the contract. A BAA will 
not be required.

Request for Information (RFI)

Cloud Storage Support Services for its DoD Trauma Registry (DoDTR).

General Information:

This is an RFI as defined in FAR 15.101(c) to ascertain whether a commercial item exists that provides the capabilities described herein.   

This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this RFI will be treated as business-confidential information.  Nonetheless, submitters should properly mark their responses if the information is confidential.  Response to the RFI will not be returned.  Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI.

RFI Response and due date 24 August 2026, by 12:00 P.M. EST.

Instructions to Responders:

Responses from all capable and qualified sources are encouraged to respond to this request.  

White papers should adhere to the following formatting and outline instructions:

1.   All submissions shall be made electronically and be in one of the following formats: Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF.

2. Cover Page (1page)

Title 

Organization

Responders’ technical and administrative points of contact (names, addresses, phone, fax number and email addresses)

Topic area(s) addressed

3.   Completed Attachment 1, and Attachment 2.  Please note that the response shall provide sufficient technical data to determine how you fully meet the requirements as specified in Attachment 2 below.  

Please note that responses are due no later than 24 August 2026, by 12:00 P.M. EST.  The preferred method of submission is via email.  The point of contact for this action is Jeffrey Sprecher, Contract Specialist, Email: jeffrey.b.sprecher.civ@health.mil.  Only electronic responses are requested.  No evaluation letters and/or results will be issued to the respondents.  At this time no solicitation exists; therefore, please do not request a copy of the solicitation.  NO PHONE CALLS PLEASE.  It is the responsibility of any potential offeror to monitor this site for the release of any solicitation or synopsis.

Background/Overview:  

The Defense Health Agency – Joint Trauma Systems (DHA – JTS) requires Cloud Storage Support Services for its DoD Trauma Registry (DoDTR). The contractor is responsible for the end-to-end modernization, migration, and ongoing support of the DoD Trauma Registry (DoDTR) and related systems. The requirement will include training, security, data quality, cloud enablement, analytics, and user support. 

1.1. WORKSTREAM 1 – PROGRAM MANAGEMENT & GOVERNANCE

1.1.1. Program Management & Governance: The Contractor shall provide program management for all activities associated with this PWS. The Contractor shall develop and maintain a Project Management Plan (PMP) that includes integrated scheduling, risk management, dependency tracking (including coordination with the SIMON data platform), and stakeholder engagement. The Contractor shall provide regular status reporting and ensure all workstreams are executed in a coordinated manner without disruption to clinical operations.

1.1.2. Workforce Qualification: The contractor shall provide a workforce possessing the skills, knowledge, and training to perform all services required under this contract. This includes qualified program managers, developers, and support staff, as well as epidemiologists and scientists with expertise in trauma research, biostatistics, data science, DoD data sources, and relevant analytical tools (e.g., Python, R, SAS, Stata, Tableau).

1.1.3. Data Governance & Clinical Authority: The Contractor shall support governance of registry and PI data, business rules, and clinical logic. The Contractor shall implement processes and tools that enable Government-designated authorities to define, approve, and manage data elements, coding standards, PI criteria, and business rules. All changes shall be version-controlled, documented, and auditable.

1.1.4. Collaboration and Support: The contractor shall work with JTS personnel, other Defense Health Agency (DHA) personnel, and additional vendors to maximize functionality. The contractor shall identify key stakeholders, core data elements, current state workflows, and envision future workflows. The contractor shall provide telephonic and video conferencing support for JTS automation and data management personnel.

1.1.5. Customer Support and Satisfaction: The contractor shall provide ongoing customer support to address user issues and ensure high satisfaction levels are as part of a comprehensive issue resolution strategy.

1.1.6. Non-Disclosure Statements (NDS): The contractor shall submit all Non-Disclosure Statement documents prior to performing any work.

1.1.7. Collaboration with DoD Trauma Enterprise Research Teams: The contractor shall work closely with MHS research teams to ensure the relevance and applicability of analysis and reports.

1.1.8. User Adoption & Change Management: The Contractor shall support system adoption by implementing change management practices and incorporating user feedback to ensure effective use of the system.

1.2. WORKSTREAM 2 – APPLICATION & INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT

1.2.1. Trauma Registry Application Development: The Contractor shall design, develop, and maintain a Trauma Registry application supporting full registry operations, including case lifecycle management, data abstraction, coding (ICD, AIS), validation, and completion. The system shall support 100% manual abstraction workflows while enabling pre-population from SIMON where available.

1.2.2. Performance Improvement (PI) Modality Development: The Contractor shall develop and maintain a PI modality integrated with the Trauma Registry. The system shall support PI workflows including case identification, M&M review, documentation, workflow tracking, and loop closure.

1.2.3. Configurable Registry & PI Logic: The Contractor shall provide configurable capabilities for registry and PI workflows, allowing authorized users to configure data fields, validation rules, workflows, and PI triggers without code changes. All configurations shall be auditable and version-controlled.

1.2.4. Cloud Environment: The contractor shall establish and manage an AWS Cloud One (or other service to be determined) environment, ensuring high availability, scalability, and security. The AWS Cloud One environment must meet safety, security, and transparent cybersecurity requirements.

1.2.5. Infrastructure Configuration & Performance: The Contractor shall configure and maintain the application layer infrastructure, ensuring reliable performance and connectivity to SIMON. The system must maintain functionality during surge conditions without degradation.

1.2.6. Continuity of Operations: The Contractor shall ensure continuous registry operations under degraded conditions, supporting full manual registry and PI operations during outages of SIMON or network services.

1.3. WORKSTREAM 3 – DATA MANAGEMENT & INTEGRATION

1.3.1. Data Consumption & Mapping (SIMON): The Contractor shall consume and map data from the SIMON OMOP data store into registry workflows, preserving clinical meaning and clearly distinguishing between system-populated and user-entered data.

1.3.2. Data Synchronization & Availability: The Contractor shall ensure timely and reliable availability of SIMON data, reflecting current data within defined refresh timelines.

1.3.3. Missing Data Handling: The Contractor shall support manual abstraction for incomplete or unavailable data, identifying missing fields for manual entry without interrupting workflows.

1.3.4. Data Reconciliation Services: The contractor shall provide data reconciliation services for clinical data from the Military Health System Information Platform (MHSIP) into appropriate tables for ingestion into the cloud and provide corrections during record transcription and/or abstraction in the registry front end (i.e., human-in-the-loop).

1.3.5. Multi-Facility Hospital Submission Support: The contractor shall provide multi-facility hospital submission support to include Extract Transform and Load (ETL) support as necessary to merge data into the DoDTR data, ensuring bidirectional interoperability and no loss of data.

1.3.6. Data Code Updates: The contractor shall provide regular updates for International Classification of Diseases (ICD-10), Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS), Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership (OMOP), and other ontologies (SNOMED, RxNorm, NDC, DICOM, LOINC) as required by their governing bodies and with JTS approval.

1.3.7. Data Quality Assurance: The contractor shall implement a Data Quality Management plan to ensure the integrity, accuracy, and reliability of trauma registry data. This includes data validation, error checking, consistency checks, and regular audits.

1.4. WORKSTREAM 4 – SECURITY & ACCREDITATION

1.4.1. Risk Management Framework (RMF) and Authority to Operate (ATO): The Contractor shall ensure compliance with DoD cybersecurity requirements and the Risk Management Framework (RMF) and obtain/maintain Authority to Operate (ATO) for the AWS Cloud environment.

1.4.2. Security & Access Control: The Contractor shall implement role-based access controls and data segmentation to protect sensitive data. The system shall track data origin (SIMON vs manual), user modifications, timestamps, and change history for full auditability.

1.4.3. Security Incident Response: The contractor shall implement a security incident response plan to address and mitigate security incidents promptly and develop a comprehensive disaster recovery plan.

1.5. WORKSTREAM 5 – REPORTING, ANALYTICS & USER EXPERIENCE

1.5.1. User Interface & Workflow Optimization: The Contractor shall provide intuitive, role-based user interfaces that support clinical workflows, enable efficient navigation, minimize redundant data entry, and provide actionable feedback.

1.5.2. Registry & PI Reporting: The Contractor shall provide reporting capabilities, including accurate, timely reports and dashboards to support clinical decision-making, PI analysis, and operational oversight.

1.5.3. External Reporting & Compliance: The Contractor shall support reporting to external trauma registries (e.g., NTDB, TQIP) in compliance with applicable standards.

1.5.4. Data Analysis for Trauma Research: The contractor shall perform comprehensive data analysis on trauma registry data to support research, including statistical analysis, trend analysis, and epidemiological studies as directed.

1.5.5. Reporting and Documentation: The contractor shall generate detailed reports with insights, findings, and recommendations to support trauma care improvements. All reports must have traceability to source data.

1.5.6. Data Visualization: The contractor shall utilize data visualization tools (e.g., SAS, Stata, Python, R, Tableau) to present analysis findings in a clear, actionable manner, tailored to user needs with drill-down and roll-up capabilities.

1.6. WORKSTREAM 6 – MODERNIZATION & ENHANCEMENT

1.6.1. Modernization & Capability Enhancement: The Contractor shall implement enhancements such as automation, AI-assisted abstraction, and configurable rules to improve efficiency while preserving full manual workflow capability.

1.6.2. Advanced Data Analytics: The contractor shall integrate artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms to predict trends and identify potential issues, following DoD responsible use of AI documentation. A capability development roadmap for technologies like OCR/NLP and Generative AI shall be created.

1.6.3. DoDTR Migration Proof of Concept: The contractor shall develop a proof of concept for migrating the DoDTR to a cloud-based infrastructure to evaluate and determine next steps.

1.6.4. Interoperability: The contractor shall enhance interoperability with other medical and defense data systems to streamline data sharing and integration.

1.6.5. Application Change Control & QA: The contractor shall implement an Application Change Control System to manage code changes and perform comprehensive software quality assurance (QA).

1.7. WORKSTREAM 7 – SUSTAINMENT & SERVICE MANAGEMENT

1.7.1. Sustainment & Service Management: The Contractor shall provide ongoing support and maintenance, including incident management, problem resolution, and change management to ensure system reliability and continuous improvement.

1.7.2. Release Management: The contractor shall develop a comprehensive Release Management strategy to address break fixes, security updates, software enhancements, and new upgrade requests.

1.7.3. Issue Resolution: The contractor shall provide an end-to-end Issue Resolution Process to address break fixes, user concerns, software enhancements, and workflow questions.

1.7.4. Regular Updates: The contractor shall provide regular updates to match JTS-provided requirements, update registry vendor microservices (e.g., OCR/NLP), maintain the TQIP modality, and perform routine upgrades of all modules.

1.8. WORKSTREAM 8 – TRAINING & DOCUMENTATION

1.8.1. Training & Documentation: The Contractor shall provide initial and sustainment training, role-based training scenarios, and maintain current user and technical documentation for all stakeholders, including clinical and technical personnel.

1.8.2. Update Training: The contractor shall provide training on all system updates to users via internet, telecom, video teleconference, or webinar.

1.8.3. HIPAA Compliance: The contractor shall maintain HIPAA training currency of all personnel and compliance at all times, notifying the COR within 24 hours of any violation.

MOUNTAINEER PRIDE WORLDWIDE 
DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE

MARTINSBURG WEST VIRGINIA 
24 July 2026 
MEMORANDUM FOR  POTENTIAL SUPPLIERS 
SUBJECT: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - SkySafe SaaS Drone Detection Coverage 
Subscription 
1. General Information
• Document Type: Notice of Intent to Sole Source / Special Notice
• Subject: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - SkySafe SaaS Drone Detection Coverage 
Subscription
• Posted Date: 24 July 2026
• Response Date: 7 August 2026 (email christopher.broschart@us.af.mil)
• NAICS Code: 518210 - Computing Infrastructure, Data Processing, and Hosting Services
• Product Service Code (PSC): 7A21 - IT and Telecom - Business Application Software 
(SaaS)
Contracting Office Address: 
West Virginia Air National Guard, 167th Mission Support Group, 222 Sabre Jet Blvd, 
Martinsburg, WV 25405 
2. Description of the Requirement
The West Virginia Air National Guard (WVANG) intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-
price contract to SkySafe, Inc. (San Diego, CA) for a 12-month Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) 
drone detection, tracking, and forensics coverage subscription at Shepherd Field ANG 
Base/Eastern WV Regional Airport and the surrounding Martinsburg, WV area. 
This procurement will be conducted under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented 
by FAR 6.302-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy 
agency requirements." Commercial acquisition procedures in accordance with FAR Part 12 will 
be used. 

MOUNTAINEER PRIDE WORLDWIDE 
3. Sole Source Justification
SkySafe is the only known commercial vendor capable of providing a comprehensive, hardware-
free unmanned aircraft system (UAS) detection, tracking, and forensics solution that requires 
zero deployment, maintenance, or upgrade costs for the Government. 
Key unique capabilities required by the WVANG include: 
• Infrastructure-Free Operation: Delivery of real-time and historical UAS telemetry
(including altitude, location, velocity, and pilot location) without requiring the installation,
construction, or sustainment of physical sensor hardware on base.
• FAA-Verified Performance: Independent verification by the Federal Aviation
Administration (FAA) demonstrating a detection rate of >95% for small UAS.
• Interoperability and Statewide Command Intent: Direct compatibility with the West
Virginia Adjutant General's unified state-wide security architecture for Anti-SUA detection.
4. Submission Instructions for Interested Parties
This notice of intent is NOT a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible 
sources who believe they can meet the exact requirements specified above may submit a 
capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. 
Responses must be submitted electronically to the Contracting Point of Contact no later than the 
Response Date listed above. 
Capability statements must clearly demonstrate the vendor's ability to provide a fully 
infrastructure-free, vendor-maintained SaaS drone detection capability covering the designated 
regional areas, with proven FAA-verified performance rates equivalent to or exceeding those of 
SkySafe. 
A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses 
to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. 
2
d Lt CHRISTOPHER P. BROSCHART, Jr., USAF 
Base Contracting Officer, 167th AW

SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE (SSN) 
AUDIO/VISUAL IMPROVEMENTS  
SS-2026031418 
Date of Issuance: 07/24/26 
Response Deadline: 08/21/26 at 5:00pm, MDT 
 
1.0 Introduction and Purpose 
 
The National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) is the U.S. Department of 
Energy’s (DOE) primary national laboratory for energy systems research and development. As 
the energy systems laboratory, NLR’s unique strength lies in developing and integrating a broad 
array of energy technologies into robust, resilient systems - bridging foundational research with 
practical applications to lower energy costs, drive economic growth, bolster national security, 
and deliver abundant and reliable energy. 
 
This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) issued by the Alliance for Energy Innovation, LLC 
(Alliance). The purpose of this SSN is to conduct market research and gather information on the 
current capabilities of potential sources to provide audio-visual (AV) professional services 
including design, sales, fabrication, installation, maintenance, engineering, and project 
management of enterprise scale AV systems. AV systems may include conference room audio 
and visual systems, video walls, 2D and 3D projection and display systems, audio reinforcement, 
digital signage, and Public Address (PA) technologies. 
 
The information received will be used for planning purposes and to inform the potential 
development of a future solicitation. 
2.0 Scope of Need 
The project objective, at a high level, is to provide dynamic, modern, and secure AV technology 
systems for use at all five (5) of the NLR campuses.  
 
2.1 Required Capabilities: 
 
a. Audio-Visual firms with a Colorado office, local presence, and ability to support task 
orders with onsite requirements including 24-hours’ prior notice.  
b. Ability to travel as required to the five (5) NLR campuses 

 
 South Table Mountain (STM) Campus:  
15013 Denver West Parkway 
Golden, CO 80401-3305 
 
 Flatirons Campus (FC):  
19001 W. 119th Avenue 
Arvada, CO 80007 
 
 Denver West (DW) Building 16  
1607 Cole Boulevard 
Golden, CO 80401 
 
 Washington DC Office (WDC) 
901 D Street, S. W., Suite 930 
Washington, DC 20024-2157 
 
 Applied Research for Communities in Extreme Environments 
(ARCEE):  
955 Draanjik Drive 
Fairbanks, AK 99775 
 
c. Staffing ability to handle multiple concurrent AV projects in various stages of 
implementation and provide maintenance service 
 
2.2 Preferred Capabilities: 
 
a. Certified Crestron Master Programmer able to be dedicated to NLR Projects 
b. Certified Project Management Professional able to be dedicated to NLR Projects 
c. Certified QSC Programmer able to be dedicated to NLR Projects  
d.  Subcontractor may be required to maintain DOE Q Access Authorization security 
clearance for some av installations.  
e. If subcontractor has experience working in classified AV spaces and performing 
installations, please provide relevant details  
 
2.3 Technical or Safety Requirements: 
 
a. Conference room AV equipment installations shall meet or exceed compliance with 
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Sections 204, 205, 307 and 309, standards for 
keeping access clear, audibility, usability and access to operable parts.  
b. Installation of AV specific low-voltage Category (CAT) cabling and associated 
infrastructure shall follow industry best practices outlined in the current revision of 
the Telecommunications Industry Association and Electronic Industry Alliance 
(TIA/EIA) 568 standards for wiring of commercial buildings. 
c. Ability to maintain an Experience Modification Rate (EMR) of 1.0 or less when 
averaged over 3-years  

 
 
3.0 Information Requested from Respondents 
Please structure your response to address the following areas. This information will help us 
understand your ability to meet our potential needs. 
3.1. Company Information 
 
• Company Name, Address, and Website URL. 
• Point of Contact (Name, Title, Email, and Phone Number). 
• Company Overview (briefly describe your company, its size, and core competencies). 
• Socio-Economic Status (e.g., Small Business, Woman-Owned, Veteran-Owned, 8(a), 
HUBZone, etc.) under the specified NAICS code. 
3.2. Capabilities and Relevant Experience 
 
• Provide a narrative of your company's experience with AV projects within an 
Enterprise or Government environment with similar scope, size, and complexity. 
• Specifically describe any experience providing AV solutions to government agencies 
(Federal, State, or Local). 
• Provide up to three (3) examples of past projects, including a brief description, the 
client, and the outcome. 
• Describe any experience with classified related AV projects (SCIFF, Classified, 
Multi-Class conference rooms).  
3.3. Technical/Solution Approach 
 
Based on the "Scope of Need" in Section 2.0, describe your company capabilities and 
approach to new AV design and installation projects. Include a typical timeline from 
design through completion including commissioning and standard support and warrantee.   
3.4. Pricing Labor Support 
 
Describe the labor categories for AV System Design, Installation, Project 
Management, Engineering, exc with Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) price 
estimates for each category.  
3.5. Key Questions  
 
1. Provide your experience sourcing, installing, and certifying video-wall displays and 
direct-view video walls 
2.  Describe any lower-tier subcontractors your organization might use to complete a 
complex audio-visual system design, installation, project management, 
commissioning, warranty and service agreement  
 

 
4.0 Submission and Administration Instructions 
 
• Response Deadline: All responses must be received by 08/21/2026 at 5:00 PM 
MDT. Late responses may not be considered. 
• Format: Responses should be submitted in PDF format. Please limit your response to 
10 pages or less not including a cover page. 
• Method of Submission: Responses must be submitted electronically to the following 
email address: ASP.Responses@nlr.gov.  
• The subject line should read: SS-2026031418: [Your Company Name] 
• Small Business Requirements: The NAICS code anticipated for any potential future 
requirement is 541512 Computer Systems Design Services. Responses may be used 
to determine if a small business set-aside is appropriate for a resultant solicitation. 
 
Disclaimer: Responding to this request identifies your company as an interested candidate only. 
Your submittal is not in response to a Request for Proposals (RFP). This is an SSN, not a

Representative (COR)/Program Official has provided sufficient justification and the Contracting Officer 
has determined that the circumstances warrant such action. The content for a justification must contain 
detailed facts and rationale to justify the sole source acquisition. Soliciting from a single source must be 
done in accordance with FAR 13.106-1(b) or 8.405-6. At a minimum, the following information must be

D. Justification: 
 
1. The justification for this non-competitive action is:   
 
☒  In accordance with FAR 13.106-1(b)(1), “only one source [is] reasonably available” which 
states that, “For purchases not exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold. (i) 
Contracting officers may solicit from one source if the contracting officer determines that 
the circumstances of the contract action deem only one source reasonably available 
(e.g., urgency, exclusive licensing agreements, brand-name or industrial mobilization). (ii) 
Where a single source is identified to provide a portion of a purchase because that 
portion of the purchase specifies a particular brand-name item, the documentation in 
paragraph (b)(1)(i) of this section only applies to the portion of the purchase requiring 
brand-name item.  The documentation should state it is covering only the portion of the 
acquisition which is brand- name.”  
☐ Urgency

☐  In accordance with FAR 8.405-6 “Limiting Sources” which states that, “the only 
circumstances that may justify the action are – (A) An urgent and compelling need exists, 
and following the procedures would result in unacceptable delays; (B) Only one source is 
capable of providing the supplies or services required at the level of quality required 
because the supplies or services are unique or highly specialized; or (C) In the interest of 
economy and efficiency, the new work is a logical follow-up to an original Federal Supply 
Schedule order provided that the original order was placed in accordance with the 
applicable Federal Supply Schedule ordering procedures.  The original BPA must not 
have been previously issued under sole-source or limited-sources procedures.” 
☐ Urgency

2. Other facts supporting sole source procurement: 
 
a. What can this product/service do that other products/services cannot do? 
The mobile application for CDC’s STI Treatment Guidelines (“app”) was built and is 
maintained by Mobomo, LLC. They are currently the only vendor who has worked on 
this app and it’s backend panel. After exhausting all option years the program office 
had planned to in-source to CDC’s Office of Communications. However in April of 
2025 the relevant CDC branch was eliminated, leaving the program without this 
option for keeping the app live. The program is therefore seeking an urgent extension 
of Mobomo’s app maintainance work to ensure the app remains live with 
uninterrupted access to healthcare providers while the government seeks to clear the 
contents of the new guidelines and define the requirements for a recompete. 
Transferring management of the app to CDC is no longer an option, and transferring 
to another vendor would create a disruption in app availability, which would 
potentially negatively affect patients seeking treatment for STIs.

Market research was not conducted for this contract. This is considered a one year

Statement of Objective Consulting Service for Palo Alto Prisma Access and Autonomous Digital Experience Management (ADEM) Deployment 1.0.GENERAL1.1. Background.  FDIC has been piloting Palo Alto’s Prisma Access and its associated ADEM service.  FDIC plans to fine tune the setup and deploy into production. 1.2. Scope of Work.  The contractor shall review the FDIC’s current pilot design and configurations of Prisma Access and ADEM and recommend improvement as needed. For ADEM, additional tests should be setup if needed.  For production deployment, the Contractor shall understand FDIC’s requirements, plan the architecture and design, help the FDIC with the required configurations, and support testing and operational troubleshooting. The work will also cover the integration with other FDIC systems and services to ensure the ecosystem works end to end.  It includes but is not limited to the following: o Discuss and understand FDIC Requirements o Review current FDIC pilot configurations and performance o Recommend improvement to current FDIC configurations as needed o Plan and design the production deployment of Prisma Access  o Plan and design panorama layout and configuration hierarchies for multi-tenant Prisma production deployment o Plan and support Prisma Access Multi-tenant environment o Configure, comply with and support FDIC’s Secure Baseline Configuration Guide (SBCG) o Support FDIC in Change Control Board, Security Impact Assessment, and other board approvals as needed o Integrate with other FDIC systems and services to ensure Prisma Access works end to end o Troubleshoot and support Prisma Access and related system operational needs o Troubleshoot and support performance related issues and concerns o Troubleshoot and support operational and business needs and requirements o Evaluate current FDIC ADEM deployment setup in the pilot o Recommend ADEM configuration improvement as needed o Setup common application testing and custom application testing in ADEM o Support other issues that may come up during the Prisma Access or ADEM deployment  2.0. GENERAL INFORMATION

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office 17  Regional Procurement Office West 124 E Hwy 67 Suite 100 Duncanville TX intends to solely negotiate withFUJIFILM Healthcare Americas Corporation, located at 81 Hartwell Avenue, Suite 100, Lexington, MA 02421 for the procurement of Synchronicity POCUS Software Implementation services. 

Scope of work

The Dallas VA Medical Center Emergency Department requires implementation of the Synchronicity POCUS software to centralize ultrasound image management, enhance documentation accuracy, and support quality assurance. The software will streamline workflow and improve interoperability with VA clinical systems.




The purpose of this procurement is to obtain, install, configure, and validate Synchronicity POCUS software to ensure seamless integration with VA health information systems while improving efficiency and accuracy in ultrasound-related workflows.

The contractor shall provide all software licenses, HL7 interface configuration, professional services, training, and technical support required to deploy Synchronicity POCUS software within the Emergency Department.

The contractor shall deliver the Synchronicity software, configure HL7 ADT, orders, results, and billing interfaces, establish a test environment, complete workflow validation, provide staff training, documentation, and post-deployment support.

This procurement is being conducted in accordance with RFO FAR 12.102 (a), Soliciting from a Single Source.

THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. However, Contractors may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation which shall be considered by the contracting officer whether to continue with the sole source procurement or to provide for competition.  Such responses MUST be received no later than Wednesday July 29, 2026, at 11:00 AM CST.  Forward responses by e-mail to Francisco.Mendoza@va.gov .  Due to technical issues, please allow additional time if you’re using electronic means.  

Responses received will be evaluated; however, a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement based upon responses received to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

The Department of Veterans Affairs, NCO 17 will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by interested parties in responding to this notice of intent. Only written responses will be considered. All responses from responsible sources will be fully considered. As a result of analyzing responses to this notice of intent, the Government shall determine if a solicitation will be issued. Any prospective contractor must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) in order to be eligible for award. All interested parties shall submit clear and convincing documentation demonstrating their capabilities to satisfy the requirement. 

DISCLAIMER:  This notice is issued informational purposes pursuant to FAR 5.201.  Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Department of Veterans Affairs to form a binding contract.
