Page 1 of 4 
 
DRAFT - Statement of Work (SOW) – SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ATTACHMENT   
MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSE ONLY  
2.1 DRAFT - STATEMENT OF WORK 
To achieve the purpose stated above, the Contractor shall perform the tasks below but 
is not limited to the following: 
Task 1 - Project Initiation, Requirements, and Regulatory Traceability 
• Conduct kickoff with & Testing Division and other Office of Standards, Certification, 
and Analysis (OSCA) staff and contracting stakeholders as appropriate. 
• Develop a requirements traceability matrix mapping 45 CFR 170.404(b)(2), § 
170.215(a), § 170.315(g)(10), § 170.556, § 170.580, and secondary documentation 
requirements to pipeline tests and evidence artifacts. 
• Define the initial monitoring universe, including all active CHPL listings certified to § 
170.315(g)(10), unless the Government identifies a specific subset of products 
certified to (g)(10) for initial prioritization. The Government recognizes that changes 
to the initial cohort list may require additional time and funding to be provided to the 
contractor. 
• Define issue taxonomy, severity model, human review checkpoints, and decision 
rights for suspected non-conformities and compliance concerns. 
• Deliver project management plan, integrated schedule, and stakeholder engagement 
plan. Specific Point of Contacts will be provided by ONC and then explicitly listed in 
the stakeholder plan. 
Task 2 – Administrative Task  
A monthly status report will be provided to show the progress of the contracted work.  
This report shall include: 
• Progress of each task including timeline of events. 
• Report any blockers that are prohibiting or delaying progress. 
• Expected completion dates for remaining work to be done. 
Task 3 - Data Source Discovery and Ingestion 
• Inventory public data sources, including CHPL product and certification data, Service 
Base URL List attributes, developer-published FHIR Bundles, Lantern data or APIs, 
CMS National Plan and Provider Enumeration System (NPPES) or other public 
organization reference data as approved, and relevant ONC Certification Program 
resources. 

   
 
Page 2 of 4 
 
• Build ingestion connectors for authoritative public sources and preserve raw source 
artifacts, timestamps, request metadata, response headers, and hashes for 
reproducibility. 
• Normalize developer, product, version, certification criterion, CHPL ID, service base 
URL list, organization, endpoint, and validation result records into a common data 
model. 
• Implement data lineage and source-of-truth precedence rules, including how the 
system resolves conflicts between CHPL metadata, developer-published artifacts, 
and endpoint observations. 
• Produce an ingestion data dictionary and source inventory. 
Task 4 - Agentic Pipeline Architecture and Governance 
• Design the end-to-end pipeline architecture, which may include ingestion agents, 
validation agents, endpoint observation agents, evidence assembly agents, triage 
agents, reporting services, and human review work queues. 
• Use deterministic validators for legal or standards-based pass/fail determinations 
wherever possible. Artificial Intelligence (AI)/agentic components may summarize, 
classify, reconcile, and draft, but shall not make final compliance determinations 
without human review. 
• Develop production ready AI agent tools capable of completing required tasks.  
Software development should include commercial best practices, including elements 
like prompts, tool policies, guardrails, retry logic, rate limits, error handling, and audit 
logs for agentic components. 
• Document model selection, evaluation methods, known limitations, fallback 
procedures, and version control for prompts, models, validators, and rules. 
• Implement a secure deployment pattern aligned with Government hosting and 
security requirements. 
Task 5 - 45 CFR 170.404(b)(2) Publication and Conformance Testing 
• Detect whether each applicable CHPL listing includes a publicly accessible service 
base URL list or Bundle link. 
• Fetch developer-published endpoint lists and classify common availability failures, 
including URL not found, timeout, redirects that obscure the published location, 
malformed responses, inaccessible content, or non-machine-readable content. 
• Validate that service base URLs are represented as FHIR R4 Endpoint resources 
and related organization details as FHIR R4 Organization resources. 
• Validate that Endpoint and Organization resources are collected into a FHIR Bundle 
and that Organization resources include name, location, facility identifier, and 
references to applicable endpoint resources. 

   
 
Page 3 of 4 
 
• Capture evidence of quarterly review or update status where discoverable from 
metadata, version history, timestamps, published content, or other Government-
approved signals. 
• Create test cases for centrally managed and locally deployed API Information 
Source scenarios. 
Task 6 - Real-World Endpoint Observation 
• Move from list publication checks to observation of deployed endpoints by 
attempting safe, non-authenticated endpoint discovery where appropriate, including 
metadata and capability statement retrieval. 
• Assess whether endpoints respond with FHIR capability information sufficient to 
support monitoring of availability and standardization. 
• Monitor endpoint drift over time, including added, removed, moved, unreachable, or 
materially changed endpoints and organization mappings. 
• Compare observed endpoint behavior with developer-published artifacts and CHPL 
metadata to flag implementation gaps. 
• Avoid collection, request, storage, or use of patient data or protected health 
information unless separately authorized in writing by the Government. 
Task 7 - Evidence Case Generation and Triage 
• Build an evidence case package for each suspected issue, including source 
metadata, raw and normalized artifacts, validation outputs, screenshots where 
necessary, request/response logs, timestamps, hashes, severity, and rule 
traceability. 
• Generate a plain-language issue narrative explaining what was tested, what failed or 
appeared inconsistent, why it matters, and what evidence supports the conclusion. 
• Implement deduplication and issue clustering by developer, product, listing, 
customer organization, endpoint, and root cause. 
• Support export of evidence packages to Government-designated systems in 
machine-readable and human-readable formats. 
Task 8 - Corrective Action Workflow Support 
• Design workflows that support, but do not replace, ONC or ONC-ACB discretion 
under applicable surveillance and direct review authorities. 
• For confirmed issues, generate draft corrective action materials consistent with 45 
CFR 170.556 and 170.580, including description of the issue, scope and affected 
customers, notification expectations, remediation steps, expected evidence of 
resolution, timetable, and prevention of recurrence. 
• Provide a controlled mechanism to re-test affected artifacts after remediation and to 
compare before-and-after evidence. 

   
 
Page 4 of 4 
 
Task 9 - Argos Authority to Operate (ATO): Manage the process and support the 
Certification and Testing team to achieve an HHS Authority to Operate (ATO) for the 
Argos 
● System Categorization and Scoping (Months 4 through 6): The contractor will 
work with the HHS Office of Information Security (OIS) to categorize Argos based 
on FIPS 199 standards and define the authorization boundary. 
● Documentation and Control Implementation (Month 6+): The contractor will 
develop all necessary security documentation, including the System Security 
Plan (SSP), and work with Argos to ensure all required security controls are 
implemented and documented. 
● Assessment and Authorization (Month 6+): The contractor will facilitate the 
security control assessment with a third-party assessor (3PAO) and prepare the 
final authorization package for review by the HHS Authorizing Official, with the 
goal of receiving an ATO. 
Task 10 – PPC Release Package  
• Deliver a final production-ready package that could be deployed through a HHS 
system including deployed code, documentation, runbooks, rollback and operations 
guide. 
• Deliver a final PPC evaluation report describing architecture, test coverage, results, 
limitations, operational costs, staffing requirements, and lessons learned. 
Task 11 - Public Artifact Assessment and Strategy  
• Assess how the PPC can extend to EHI export documentation under 45 CFR 
170.315(b)(10), including whether export format documentation is publicly available, 
linked with export files, and kept up to date. 
• Assess how the PPC can evaluate API documentation under 45 CFR 170.315(g)(10) 
and 45 CFR 170.404, including whether documentation is publicly accessible without 
preconditions and includes syntax, parameters, response structures, exception 
handling, configuration, and application registration requirements 
• Prototype documentation-quality scoring for a limited set of developers or products if 
directed by the Government. 
• Deliver recommendations for expanding the Argos public-artifact layer. 
• Develop an Argos FY 2027 strategy that recommends expansion to additional 
observable artifacts, synthetic patient/test data, real-world interoperability checks, 
policy changes, and oversight efficiencies.

SOFTWARE, INCLUDING GDAL, PDAL, PROJ, QGIS, ETC FOR THE NATIONAL OCEAN SERVICE

THE NORTH AMERICAN INDUSTRY CLASSIFICATION CODE (NAICS) FOR THIS ACQUISITION IS 
541519, OTHER COMPUTER RELATED SERVICES, WITH A BUSINESS SIZE STANDARD OF $34 
MILLION.  
 
***THE SOLE SOURCE DETERMINATION IS BASED ON NOAA’S REQUIREMENT THAT HOBU IS 
THE ONLY SOURCE CAPABLE OF PROVIDING THE SERVICES REQUIRED AT THE LEVEL OF 
QUALITY REQUIRED BECAUSE THE TECHNICAL SERVICES ARE HIGHLY SPECIALIZED. 
HOBU INC. IS THE ONLY COMPANY WITH THE KNOWLEDGE, EXPERTISE, AND STANDING TO 
PROVIDE THE DEVELOPMENT SUPPORT NEEDED BY THE OCS NATIONAL BATHYMETRIC 
SOURCE PROGRAM IN THE UNITED STATES. OCS DEPENDS ON GDAL TO CONTINUE 
OPTIMIZATION OF OCS BATHYMETRY WORKFLOW. OCS REQUIRES FURTHER 
DEVELOPMENT OF MANY LIBRARIES, INCLUDING GDAL, BUT ALSO PDAL, LIBLAS, SHAPELY,

HOBU INC. HAS NO AUTHORIZED PARTNERS OR RESELLERS WHO CAN PROVIDE THESE 
SERVICES.

DETERMINING WHETHER OR NOT TO CONDUCT THIS PROCUREMENT ON A COMPETITIVE 
BASIS. A DETERMINATION BY THE GOVERNMENT NOT TO CONDUCT A COMPETITIVE 
PROCUREMENT, BASED UPON RESPONSES TO THIS NOTICE, IS SOLELY WITHIN THE 
DISCRETION OF THE GOVERNMENT. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS ARE NOT ACCEPTABLE IN 
RESPONSE TO THIS NOTICE.

(a) The Contractor agrees to give preference in employment opportunities under this contract to Indians who

affiliation. To the extent feasible and consistent with the efficient performance of this contract, the Contractor 
further agrees to give preference in employment and training opportunities under this contract to Indians who are not 
fully qualified to perform regardless of age (subject to existing laws and regulations), sex, religion, or tribal 
affiliation. The Contractor also agrees to give preference to Indian organizations and Indian-owned economic 
enterprises in the awarding of any subcontracts to the extent feasible and consistent with the efficient performance 
of this contract. The Contractor shall maintain the necessary statistical records to demonstrate compliance with this 
paragraph.

provide reasonable opportunities for training, incident to such employment. Such training shall include on-the-job,

conditions, including price, for awarding of subcontracts in connection with the work performed under this contract, 
the Contractor agrees to comply with the provisions of this contract involving utilization of small businesses;

by such governing body in accordance with the Indian Financing Act of 1974 (88 Stat. 77; 25 U.S.C. 1451).

established or organized for the purpose of profit, provided that such Indian ownership shall constitute not less than 
51 percent of the enterprise, and that ownership shall encompass active operation and control of the enterprise.

PARATUS AOI 1 Q&A 
23 July 2026 
 
1. Phase 1 logistics. Will Phase 1 demonstrations (1.a through 1.c) be conducted virtually, in person in the 
National Capital Region, or at the offeror's election? How much total presentation time will each offeror 
or team be allotted, and approximately when within the Days 8 to 28 window should offerors expect 
scheduling notices after NOI submission? 
Phase 1 will be conducted virtually.  Demonstration time is still being finalized but plan for roughly 
60 minutes (subject to change).  The Government will provide further details regarding 
demonstration time during scheduling.  The Government will begin scheduling July 28-31, with 
demonstrations being completed within the following 3 weeks.  You will be notified via email 
address provided in Notice of Intent to Demonstrate. 
 
2. Phase 1.b demonstration environment. Section 4.5.1 states no Government-hosted environment is 
required to pass Phase 2, and Section 5.0 treats IL5 hosting as the production target rather than a Phase 1 
condition. Please confirm that Phase 1.b may be satisfied by a live, working, end-to-end demonstration of 
the Parts A through C2 capability running in the offeror's own commercial cloud environment using 
synthetic data, with IL5/IL6 posture addressed narratively under Phase 1.c. 
Confirmed 
 
3. Contract Data Package timing. Section 4.5.1 states the CDP is furnished "in connection with the Phase 
2 down-select gate." Will the target schema, data dictionary, and FHIR R4 profile constraints be released 
to all offerors who pass Phase 1 on a common date, and will the Government consider releasing the 
schema and data dictionary portions earlier so offerors can maximize use of the roughly two-week Phase 
2 window for conformance engineering rather than document review? 
The Government will provide the CDP as early as possible to vendors that pass Phase 1. 
 
4. Teaming after NOI submission. Section 8 requires the NOI to identify any teaming arrangement, while 
Section 4.6 permits team composition to evolve between phases with advance notice. Please confirm an 
offeror may submit its NOI as a single entity and subsequently add a teaming partner (for example, a 
clinical workflow or connectivity partner) with advance notice to the Government, provided the addition 
is not a material substitution of previously evaluated capability. 
Teaming arrangements can evolve during the down select process. 
 
5. Provisional pricing mechanics. For an offeror or team that passes Phase 2, at what point will the 
Government request the provisional not-to-exceed pricing contemplated by Section 4.9.5: with Phase 2 
demonstration materials, or during the Days 43 to 50 OT award decision window? Is there a preferred 
format or cost-element breakdown for that submission? 
The Government will provide a Not To Exceed amount on the OT award during the Days 43 to 50 
OT award decision window.  Format has not been decided. 
 
6. The below excerpt from the CSO’s problem statement seems disassociated from the focus and scoping 
of PARATUS and the three AOIs outlined.  
The Government is also interested in identifying innovative commercial technologies and approaches that 
enhance operational medical planning, analysis, modeling, simulation, and decision support across the 
continuum of military operations. Solutions should improve planning efficiency, interoperability, data-
driven decision making, and adaptability to support joint, combined, and coalition operations. 
Can you please confirm the language is associated properly to PARATUS? 
Yes, the information below was added to the PARATUS CSO as a possibility for future, potential, 
Areas of Interest.  AOI 1 does not focus on medical planning, modeling, or simulation at this time; 

however, there is potential in the future.  IF this work comes to fruition, it will be a separate AOI 
linked to CSO HT0038SC004. 
 
7. Could you please confirm if the submission due date is Jul 27, 2026, 03:00 pm EDT is correct and if 
there have been any updates or amendments that may not have been posted yet? 
That is the correct date and time for the Notice of Intent to Demonstrate submission. 
 
8. Is there any incumbent/recompete or is this a brand-new project? 
This is a new requirement for JOMIS. 
 
9. Could you please clarify whether this AOI includes a small business set-aside, small-business 
participation goal, or minimum subcontracting or workshare requirement for small-business teaming 
partners? 
There is no SB set-aside or participation goal on this requirement. 
 
10. Could you confirm whether questions or pre-submission dialogue are still being accepted ahead of the 
July 27, 3:00 PM ET closing, and whether a specific solution brief template applies to this AOI? 
Questions can be submitted up to 27 July.  The questions & answers will be posted to SAM.gov. 
There is no solution brief template.

DEFENSE COMMERCIAL SOLUTIONS OPENING (CSO) 
AREA OF INTEREST (AOI) 
Periodic Health Assessment (PHA) Modernization Capability  
In Support of the Profiling and Readiness Action Tracking Unified System (PARATUS)  
 
1. Authority and Purpose 
This Area of Interest (AOI) solicits innovative commercial solutions, or new applications of 
existing commercial technology, to close a defined capability gap in the Periodic Health 
Assessment (PHA) process governed by DOWI 6200.06 (Periodic Health Assessment Program) 
and DOWI 6025.19 (Individual Medical Readiness). 
This AOI does not constitute a Statement of Work or Performance Work Statement. It describes 
the Government's area of interest and the technical data and evaluation factors that will govern 
proposal selection. Offerors retain latitude to propose the technical approach, architecture, and 
implementation method that best satisfies the stated capability need, including proposing as part 
of a team consistent with Section 4.6. 
Following successful completion of Phase 2 (CDP Conformance Gate), the Government may, in 
its discretion, award a prototype Other Transaction agreement under 10 U.S.C. § 4022 to one or 
more offerors or teams who have passed Phase 2, using the competitive procedures conducted 
under this CSO through Phase 2 to satisfy the competitive-procedures prerequisite of 10 U.S.C. 
§ 4022. Award of an OT agreement under this provision does not constitute completion of this 
AOI's technical evaluation; Phases 3 through 6 continue as post-award milestones under that 
agreement, administered per Section 4.9.Upon an offeror's or team's successful completion of 
Phase 6, whether reached through the standard AOI down-select described at Sections 4.7 and 
4.8 or through post-award milestones under a prototype OT agreement awarded under Section 
4.9, the Government may, in its discretion, either (a) extend or convert that offeror's or team's 
prototype OT agreement to a follow-on production agreement which may include a sole-source 
follow-on production contract under 10 U.S.C. § 4022 Nothing in this section commits the 
Government to any award, or alters the Government's discretion described at Section 6. 
2. Background and Capability Gap 
The PHA is the annual, comprehensive medical readiness assessment required of Active and 
Reserve Component Service members across the Military Services, documented on DD Form 
3024. The current PHA is completed in four sequential parts: Part A (Service Member self-
assessment), Part B (Record Review, completed by a designated Record Reviewer), Part C1 
(Mental Health Assessment, completed by an MHA Provider), and Part C2 (PHA Health Care 
Provider review, recommendations, referrals, and certification). There are current policy-focused 
efforts to reform the PHA, by shortening unnecessary questions and aligning the timing to 
replace other joint health assessments. 
No automated, AI-enabled, or risk-prioritized capability currently exists to support completion of 
the PHA utilizing a common data framework and hosting architecture. The present-day process 
— spanning Military Service Readiness Systems and Service-specific PHA portals — is manual 
and forms-driven: Service members complete static web-based questionnaires; Record 

2 
Reviewers manually cross-check immunization, laboratory, and deployment documentation; 
MHA Providers and PHA Health Care Providers (collectively Clinical Readiness Staff, along with 
Record Reviewers) manually review structured and free-text responses without machine-
assisted triage; and unit commanders receive completion and readiness status through static, 
periodically generated reports rather than real-time notification. Service members in remote or 
geographically dispersed locations — including a significant share of Reserve Component 
personnel — face additional access barriers because existing tools are largely desktop/web-
only and not designed for mobile completion.
 
Closing this gap also requires that PHA data be curated, governed, and made available within 
the common data backbone supporting PARATUS — not just modernized at the point of 
capture. This AOI accordingly addresses the following capability gap: a streamlined, AI-enabled, 
risk-prioritized, multi-platform PHA capability. Every capability described in Sections 4.2 and 4.3 
represents a gap to be closed through commercial competition, not an existing system to be 
extended, and is intended to inform the broader PARATUS consolidation of Military Service 
medical readiness systems.
 
3. Statement of Government Interest 
The Government is interested in commercial solutions — software, software-as-a-service, or a 
new application of an existing commercial product — that modernize completion of the PHA (DD 
Form 3024, Parts A, B, C1, and C2) through raw data to decision-ready data, agentic AI, 
machine learning (ML)-based risk scoring, automated notifications, and visualization 
dashboards, accessible via both web and native or responsive mobile platforms, suitable for 
operation within a DOW IL5 environment, capable of DOW IL6 cross domain solution (CDS) 
connection and capable of integrating with Military Health System data sources (e.g., MHS 
GENESIS, FHIR R4, HL7, structured and unstructured). 
Solutions of interest should demonstrate, at minimum: 
• Agentic AI that guides Service members through Part A self-assessment via adaptive, 
conversational interaction rather than static questionnaire logic, while preserving the full 
DD Form 3024 data set required for Individual Medical Readiness (IMR) determination. 
• AI- or ML-based risk scoring that triages completed assessments for Clinical Readiness 
Staff attention, prioritizing review queues by clinical and readiness risk rather than strict 
first-in-first-out order. 
• Automated notification and reminder capability spanning Service members, Clinical 
Readiness Staff, and unit commanders, tied to PHA due dates, overdue status, risk 
changes and IMR category changes. 
• Visualization dashboards providing real-time, part-level PHA completion and risk status 
at the individual, unit, and command level. 
• Native and/or responsive mobile accessibility, in addition to full web access, with 
CAC/PKI or equivalent DOW-approved authentication. 
• Demonstrated or readily achievable integration with authoritative Military Health System 
data sources. IL5 hosting/data governance constraints, and IL6 CDS. 

3 
• Conformance with the Government-furnished Contract Data Package described at 
Section 4.5, sufficient to ingest, transform, and govern PHA-domain data within the 
common joint-service medical readiness data backbone, without dependence on access 
to a Government-hosted environment. 
• Demonstrated ability to connect to, and exchange data with, the Government-
provisioned test environment described at Section 4.5.4, using either native deployment 
within that environment or a secure remote connection, consistent with the offeror's 
proposed hosting approach at Section 4.9. 
• Human-in-the-loop safeguards ensuring AI- and ML-generated outputs function strictly 
as clinical and administrative decision and process support, with all diagnostic, referral, 
and readiness determinations retained by a licensed Health Care Provider or other 
designated official.
 
4. PHA Capability Requirements — Down-Select Discriminators 
The PHA capability described in Section 4.2 and the data validation described in Section 4.5 are 
the primary technical discriminators for down-select under this CSO. Proposals will not advance 
from phase to phase, as described in Section 4.7, on the basis of price, narrative quality, 
general technical merit, or prior corporate experience with DOW/DHA-specific data 
environments alone.  
4.1 Intent 
The PHA capability requirement reflects the Government's intent to replace a disconnected, 
data-deficient, static, manual, forms-driven assessment process with a streamlined, AI-enabled, 
risk-prioritized capability spanning all four parts of DD Form 3024. The data validation 
requirement reflects the Government's parallel intent to establish, within the program's 8-month 
credibility window described at Section 6, a working integration of PHA data into the common 
joint-service data backbone that subsequent Areas of Interest under this CSO will build upon. 
The capability is intended to reduce administrative burden on Service members and Clinical 
Readiness Staff, accelerate identification and routing of elevated-risk cases, and provide 
commanders and program offices with real-time, decision-ready medical readiness status — 
consistent with the Defense Health Agency's medical readiness modernization objectives and 
the broader PARATUS effort to unify joint-service medical readiness data.
 
The Government's intent in defining the validation requirement at Section 4.5 is to evaluate an 
offeror's or team's ability to conform to a Government-defined data and to connect that 
conformant data into a Government-provisioned environment, not to require that an offeror have 
independently built an enterprise-scale orchestration backbone prior to competing. This 
distinction is deliberate: it is intended to keep this AOI open to offerors with mature PHA 
capability who may not have prior experience specifically within the DOW or DHA data 
environment, whether competing individually or as part of a team under Section 4.6. 
This AOI's data validation requirement comprises two distinct, sequentially gated elements: 
conformance to the published Contract Data Package (Section 4.5.1), and live connectivity to 
the Government-provisioned test environment (Section 4.5.4). These are evaluated as separate 
gates because they test materially different capabilities — interface conformance versus 

4 
operational connectivity — and because collapsing them into a single gate risks a failure in one 
being masked by success in the other.

Statement of Requirements 

eTesting Officer Training School/Holm Center/DE

 

 

1.0  PURPOSE. Modernize assessment capabilities across the USAF officer school training complex. The Holm Center is responsible for commissioning approximately 80 percent of all USAF officers, making a robust, reliable yet flexible testing essential. The system must support validation of learning outcomes through both paper-based and online testing—paper-based delivery when campus internet connectivity is limited or unavailable, and online testing when connectivity is reliable. The solution must also interface seamlessly with existing test bank architecture (ParTest and ParScore) to preserve historical test item performance statistics and enable long-term tracking of curriculum effectiveness.    

 

2.0  DESCRIPTION OF ITEMS. The requested requirement is for comprehensive test delivery and scoring software. The software must provide hybrid assessment delivery (both paper and online administration). Online assessments must allow test-takers to log in and complete their assessments; software must be able to receive student data in multiple formats (e.g. Excel, PDF, etc.) and export student data (test results) in multiple formats (e.g. Excel, PDF, etc.); activate lockdown and time-elapse features when test is initiated to prevent test compromise and ensure test-taker time requirements. Software must analyze test results; store tests as individual test-takers and/or across multiple class rosters for data aggregation; capture test-taker date; rescore tests when applicable test item analysis/challenges are requested; enable test-takers to retake test when required; and contain immediate test soring feature. In addition, the software must include the ability to create (build), modify, and store multiple test item banks;  provide detailed test item analysis to evaluate the effectiveness of test questions; allow questions to be imported from various sources or creation of new ones; employ testing lockdown features in alignment with emergency test stoppage (continuation feature upon emergency completion). It must also generate printed test booklets for use with Scantron forms or deliver tests online; provide test statistics and test validation features.  Software must have the capability to seamlessly provide over 5000 student assessments annually.

Brand name: Scantron Eva Exam software is the updated direct replacement for the now unsupported Scantron ParTest and ParScore software suite. It is fully backward compatible with the existing proprietary architecture, allowing us to seamlessly import test question banks from the obsolete (existing) platform into the new system. This compatibility is critical, as it preserves historical test item performance statistics and aggregated data across multiple cohorts, both past and present. In addition, the existing test banks represent thousands of labor hours. Upgrading to a compatible, modern solution is the most efficient use of time, funding, and personnel, and avoids significant costs associated with recreating assessment content.

2.1  SOFTWARE SPECIFICATIONS REQUIRED  

 

2.1.1 Software must be compatible with ParTest and ParScore allowing direct import of existing test banks and historical data from obsolete (existing) software.   

2.1.2 Must capture test item performance past to present in content transfer conversion. 

2.1.3 Have robust customizable analytics package that is customizable to organizational hierarchy used in OTS: overall class performance, squadron performance, and individual flight performance. 

2.1.4 Role-based security allowing different permissions between the test administrator, department chairs on instructional design teams, and leadership; ability to view performance across the enterprise. 

2.1.5 Operate in both paper-based and digital environments. 

2.1.6 Ability to import student data with customized student IDs used to onboard students in OTS environment. 

2.1.7 Provide browser lockdown capability to preclude test compromise in a digital environment.   

2.1.8 Platform agnostic for end-users (laptop and tablet with different operating systems (Windows and Apple device compatibility)

2.1.9 Test Administrator must operate in Windows 11 or higher environment (with software upgrades coinciding with any Windows upgrades)

2.2.0 Software compatible with relevant plug-ins to ensure test security

2.2.1 Software “sandbox” experience for 30 days to ensure compatibility with current system using current test items 

2.2.2 Supported by multiple browsers for online exam participants (Microsoft Edge, Chrome, Firefox, etc.)

2.2.3 Ability to export test result data in multiple formats and reports.

 

        2.2.  EQUIPMENT AND OTHER PERIPHERALS REQUIRED 

 

      2.2.1 Software (Scan Station License) downloads to stand-alone computer (nonNIPR). 

2.2.2 Tech support (US-based) Monday – Friday. 

2.2.3 Software updates completed outside testing timeframes. 

2.2.4 WCAG 2.0 Level AA compliant

2.2.5 iNSIGHT ES4 scanner (document feeder; duplex capability; B/W with 200 dpi resolution; twain driver; multipage TIFF files with group IV compression)

2.2.6 24-pound scantron paper or equivalent

2.3 PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE

2.3.1	For CLINs 0002, 1002, 2002, 3002, & 4002 –

	Base Year: 30 August 2026 – 29 August 2027

	Option Year 1: 30 August 2027 – 29 August 2028

	Option Year 2: 30 August 2028 – 29 August 2029

	Option Year 3: 30 August 2029 – 29 August 2030

	Option Year 4: 30 August 2030 – 29 August 2031

 3.0  DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS:   

 

3.1 Cloud-based software that downloads operational program and subsequent software updates.

  

3.2 OTS: 550 E. Maxwell Blvd, Bldg. 1487, Room C106, Maxwell AFB AL 36112

3.3	Delivery of software licenses and deliverables on or before 30 August 2026

 

4.0  INSTALLATION REQUIREMENTS: Concise software installation instructions.

 

5.0 TRAINING REQUIREMENTS: Provide initial software training to test administrators and instructional design department chairs. Provide a digital User’s Guide that clearly explains how to configure the software. Technical Support: The contractor shall provide hands-on user training and comprehensive technical support, including unlimited US-based technical telephone support.

  

6.0 STANDARD WARRANTY: The contractor shall provide any Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) standard commercial warranty applicable to the products being purchased at no additional cost to the Government.  

 

 6.1 Prior to project acceptance, the contractor shall provide the customer with all manufacturer warranties as needed for any component incorporated into this project such as equipment manuals, literature, CDs and DVDs and other documentation on all equipment and software. 

 

6.2 Prior to project acceptance, the contractor shall provide written procedures, points of contact within company, and required information for all warranty services prior to project acceptance. This information shall include written confirmation of the warranty period, phone numbers and contact information/procedures for technical support, troubleshooting assistance, and replacement of faulty equipment and software. 

 

7.0   GENERAL INFORMATION: Items must be brand new.  Refurbished items are not authorized. The design of Eva Exam is such that it will allow downward compatibility with ParTest and ParScore currently in use by the Holm Center.  Scantron created both software products and the proprietary architecture is compatible between these software products.  The upgrade (Eva Exam) will streamline the upgrade conversion and support both paper-based and online testing. Additionally, this supports AFAC line of effort to recruit the Airmen and Guardians the Nation needs to win any future fight.

Chief Program Office 
AmeriCorps NCCC and AmeriCorps VISTA 
Digital Recruitment Platform for College-aged Individuals 
Performance Work Statement 
July 21, 2026 

Page 2 of 16 
 
PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
Digital Recruitment Platform for College-aged Individuals. 
 
PART 1: GENERAL INFORMATION 
1.1 STATEMENT OF NEED 
The purpose of this Performance Work Statement (PWS) is to use a college recruitment platform 
to improve recruitment of AmeriCorps members in support of the Corporation for National and 
Community Service (AmeriCorps).  
1.2 BACKGROUND 
For nearly three decades, The Corporation for National and Community Service (AmeriCorps) 
has tapped the ingenuity and courage of the American people to meet our toughest challenges. 
Working with nonprofit and community organizations, state and local agencies, Tribal nations, 
and other partners, AmeriCorps programs improve lives, strengthen communities, and foster 
civic engagement through service and volunteering. Each year, AmeriCorps engages Americans 
of all ages and backgrounds in sustained, results-driven service at thousands of locations across 
the country, meeting a wide range of community needs in education, health, economic 
opportunity, disaster services, environmental stewardship, and supporting veterans and military 
families. 
The Domestic Volunteer Service Act, VISTA’s legislating authority, requires that the program 
establishes and maintains a Volunteer placement office and is responsible for all functions 
related to the recruitment and placement of Volunteers.   
Under the national service program component of the National Civilian Community Corps 
Program authorized by section 152(a), eligible young people shall work in teams on National 
Civilian Community Corps projects. The Corporation shall disseminate information regarding 
available approved national service positions through cooperation with secondary schools, 
institutions of higher education, etc. 
1.3 OBJECTIVES 
Use of this tool will allow AmeriCorps to meet its strategic plan objectives of maximizing 
impact and achieving results for the American people and promoting volunteer service and 
community participation nationwide.  
 
Since a large amount of AmeriCorps Volunteers across the network are 18-28 years old, 
reaching a high volume of current and recently graduated college students is critical to 
this objective. Through the use of this platform, AmeriCorps will be able to seamlessly 
communicate with college-aged individuals and promote service opportunities and virtual 
events through individual and automated messaging campaigns. 

Page 3 of 16 
 
 
The objectives of this project are to: 
 
• Build and manage a Volunteer pipeline  
• Raise campus awareness of AmeriCorps programs 
• Decrease time to connect with college students and graduates 
• Expand the number of universities that can be reached 
• Increase impact and efficiency 
 
1.4 SCOPE 
AmeriCorps requires a college recruitment platform to promote opportunities, engage with 
events, cultivate partnerships, and track key metrics that can interface with universities that 
utilize the platform as their software system supporting the Career Services Center. The system 
must provide AmeriCorps the ability to message students directly about AmeriCorps 
opportunities through targeted campaigns, post positions, connect with schools, segment schools 
and students by key characteristics such as geographic location and Veteran status. Additionally, 
the system must give AmeriCorps the ability to attend and host career events for prospective 
applicants and connect students with program staff who can provide more detail about their 
specific programs. The tool must be fully functional in its two-way communication and provide 
access to a high volume of schools (1,600+) and students (20 million+). 
The essential features of the system are as follows:
 
Talent Engagement Suite – full access to engagement features with five recruiter seats 
included. 
Advocate Seats – up to five lower-level access seats for agency representatives to use on an as-
needed basis.  
Additional Recruiter Seats – As needed option, full access for relevant agency staff who are 
directly involved in recruitment of AmeriCorps members and interns. 
Insights & Analytics – ability to track events attended, campaigns sent, engagement rates, and 
demographics of schools and students. 
School Explorer – access to directly communicate with colleges and universities to cultivate 
partnerships.
 
Event Manager – ability to both attend career events hosted by universities as well as host 
events at the agency level. 
Expert Assist – As needed option, consistent, timely, and technically adept customer support, 
including consultation utilization strategy. 
1.5 TERM/TYPE OF CONTRACT 
The Government will award a 60-month, Firm-Fixed-Price contract. 
1.6 PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE 

Page 4 of 16 
 
The period of performance for this PWS is one 12-month base period and 4 one-year options.  
1.7 QUALITY CONTROL 
The Contractor shall develop and maintain an effective quality control program to ensure the 
Contractor performs services in accordance with this PWS. The Contractor shall develop and 
implement procedures to identify, prevent, and ensure non-recurrence of defective services. The 
Contractor’s quality control program is the means by which the Contractor assures that the work 
complies with the requirement of the contract. After acceptance of the quality control plan, any 
proposed changes to Contractor Quality Control (QC) system shall require Contracting Officer’s 
acceptance (Deliverable 7). 
1.8 RECOGNIZED HOLIDAYS 
The Contractor is not required to perform services during federal holidays. Federal law (5 U.S.C. 
6103) establishes public holidays for federal employees. Please note that most federal employees 
work on a Monday through Friday schedule. For these employees, when a holiday falls on a non-
workday – Saturday or Sunday – the holiday usually is observed on Monday (if the holiday falls 
on Sunday) or Friday (if the holiday falls on Saturday). Direct billing/invoicing shall not be 
allowed for any Federal Government Holidays. Federal holidays are listed at the Office of 
Personnel and Management at https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/federal-
holidays. 
1.9 HOURS OF OPERATION 
The Contractor is responsible for conducting business, between the hours of 8:00 am and 5:00 
pm (Eastern time zone) Monday thru Friday except Federal holidays or when the Government 
has closed its facilities due to local or national emergencies, administrative closings, or similar 
Government directed facility closings. The Contractor must at all times maintain an adequate 
workforce for the uninterrupted performance of all tasks defined within this PWS when the 
Government facility is operating. When hiring personnel, the Contractor shall keep in mind that 
stability and continuity of the workforce are essential. AmeriCorps observes all Federal 
Holidays, and the Contractor may not conduct business on such Holidays, unless mutually 
agreeable at the standard rate.  
1.10 PLACE OF PERFORMANCE 
The Contractor shall perform work remotely from any location within the United States of 
America and its territories. The Government will not provide on-site space to perform the work. 
1.11 TRAVEL  
Travel is not required to perform the work, so no payment of travel expenses will be paid to the 
Contractor for routine travel to and from the Agency’s location. If mission needs require travel, 
travel must be pre-approved by the COR. All travel will be reimbursed in accordance with the 
Federal Travel Regulations (FTR).  

Page 5 of 16 
 
1.12 CONTRACTING OFFICER REPRESENTIATIVE (COR) 
The Contracting Officer (CO) will identify the Contracting Officer Representative (COR) by 
separate designation letter, which states the responsibilities and limitations of the COR, 
especially with regard to changes in cost or price, estimates or changes in delivery dates. The 
COR monitors all technical aspects of the contract and assists in contract administration. The 
COR is authorized to perform the following functions: assure that the Contractor performs the 
technical requirements of the contract; perform inspections necessary in connection with contract 
performance; maintain written and oral communications with the Contractor concerning 
technical aspects of the contract; issue written interpretations of technical requirements, 
including Government drawings, designs, specifications; monitor Contractor's performance and 
notifies both the O and Contractor of any deficiencies; coordinate availability of Government 
furnished property; and provide site entry of Contractor personnel. The CO has not authorized 
the COR to change any of the terms and conditions of the resulting contract.  
1.13 IDENTIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR EMPLOYEES 
All contract personnel attending meetings, answering Government telephones, and working in 
other situations where their contractor status is not obvious to third parties are required to 
identify themselves as such to avoid creating an impression in the minds of members of the 
public that they are Government officials. Contractor personnel shall identify themselves and/or 
obtain and wear badges. The Contractor shall also suitably mark Contractor products, documents 
or reports as produced by Contractor personnel, or that contractor participation was involved. 
1.14 DATA RIGHTS 
The Government has unlimited rights to all documents/material produced under this contract 
including but not limited to reports, native files, data, media, photography, and video, etc. For 
intellectual property developed under contract to AmeriCorps, the Government retains a non-
exclusive, paid-up, royalty-free, irrevocable license throughout the world, allowing the 
Government to (a) use, disclose and reproduce the work in any medium of expression now 
known or subsequently developed, or (b) use the invention for Government purposes. The 
definition of “unlimited rights” is contained in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 27.401, 
“Definitions.” FAR clause 52.227-14, “Rights in Data-General” is hereby incorporated by 
reference and made a part of this BPA call. The Contractor shall return to the Government at the 
end of the performance period or when specified in this contract, all documentation and 
electronic data and information collected by the Contractor and generated in support of this 
contract. 
The Contractor shall guarantee strict confidentiality of the information/data that it is provided by 
the Government during the performance of the task order. The Government has determined that 
the information/data that the Contractor shall be provided during the performance of the task 
order is of a sensitive nature. 

Page 6 of 16 
 
The Contractor shall not release any information/data, in whole or in part, without the written 
consent of the COR. Any request for information relating to the award that is presented to the 
Contractor shall be submitted to the COR for approval. Personnel working on any of the 
described tasks may, at the Government’s request, be required to sign formal non-disclosure 
and/or conflict of interest agreements to guarantee the protection and integrity of Government 
information and documents. 
The Contractor shall not release, publish, or disclose sensitive information to unauthorized 
personnel, and shall protect such information in accordance with provisions of the following 
laws and any other pertinent laws and regulations governing the confidentiality of sensitive 
information: 18 U.S.C. 641 (Criminal Code: Public Money, Property or Records) 
1.15 ORGANIZATIONAL CONFLICT OF INTEREST 
Contractor and subcontractor personnel performing work under this contract may receive, have 
access to or participate in the development of proprietary or source selection information (e.g., 
cost or pricing information, budget information or analyses, specifications or work statements, 
etc.) or perform evaluation services which may create a current or subsequent Organizational 
Conflict of Interests (OCI) as defined in FAR Subpart 9.5.  The Contractor shall notify the 
Contracting Officer immediately whenever it becomes aware that such access or participation 
may result in any actual or potential OCI and shall promptly submit a plan to the Contracting 
Officer to avoid or mitigate any such OCI.  The Contractor’s mitigation plan will be determined 
to be acceptable solely at the discretion of the Contracting Officer and in the event the 
Contracting Officer unilaterally determines that any such OCI cannot be satisfactorily avoided or 
mitigated, the Contracting Officer may affect other remedies as he or she deems necessary, 
including prohibiting the Contractor from participation in subsequent contracted requirements 
which may be affected by the OCI. 
1.16 FEDERAL INFORMATION SECURITY PROTOCOLS 
As a federal agency, AmeriCorps is subject to and complies with the security and privacy 
requirements of the Federal Information Security and Modernization Act (FISMA) of 2014 and 
the Privacy Act of 1974. The Contractor must ensure that services and products provided under a 
contract or task order resulting from this solicitation comply with FISMA, the Privacy Act of 
1974, AmeriCorps IT policies, and the Contractor security and privacy requirements. The 
Contractor must immediately report any condition that may indicate a breach of these policies 
and procedures to the COR. Failure to adhere to federal and AmeriCorps policies may result in 
adverse contractual actions. 
Contractors are responsible for the security, integrity, and appropriate authorized use of their 
systems interfacing with the government and/or used for the transaction of any and all 
government business. The Government, through the Contracting Officer or COR, may require 
the use or modification of security and/or secure communications technologies related to 
AmeriCorps systems access and use. AmeriCorps requires that security procedures be monitored, 
verified, and validated by designated AmeriCorps personnel. 

Page 7 of 16 
 
Access must be provided to the extent required to carry out a program of IT inspection, 
investigation, and audit to safeguard against threats and hazards to the integrity, availability, and 
confidentiality of customer AmeriCorps data and/or to the function of computer systems 
operated on behalf of customer agencies, and to preserve evidence of computer crime. 
AmeriCorps, at its discretion, may suspend or terminate user’s access and/or use of any

1. Title: Data Processing and Related Services for NIMHD DIR’s Chronic Disease Prevention

2. Background Information: The National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities 
(NIMHD) conducts and supports research and training programs to advance knowledge and 
understanding of health disparities, identify mechanisms to improve minority health and 
reduce health disparities, and develop effective interventions in community and clinical 
settings. 
 
NIMHD is the lead organization at NIH for planning, reviewing, coordinating, and evaluating 
minority health and health disparities research activities. NIMHD also promotes workforce 
development, supports research capacity at less-resourced institutions that train students in 
research careers, serves populations experiencing health disparities, supports participation in 
clinical research, and promotes information dissemination through regular communications, 
public education outreach, and scientific presentations. 
 
The President’s Executive Order (EO) 14212 Establishing the President’s Make America 
Healthy Again Commission aims to improve the health of Americans. As described in the EO, 
escalating burden of chronic diseases poses significant challenges in the United States. These 
conditions contribute to rising health costs, reduced workforce productivity, and stagnant life 
expectancies across the country, both in adults and children. Engaging with communities 
experiencing high prevalence of chronic diseases to develop and implement gold-standard 
interventions is a key approach to reduce this burden.

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Center for Data and Computational Sciences (C-DACS) has a requirement for the procurement of security and information management equipment for the Veterans Health Administration (VHA). The purpose of this procurement is to enhance the security posture for the research data and analysis systems for the VA Office of Research and Development (ORD).  The program features several big data applications and databases which connect to a high-performance computing and storage environment.  

The contractor shall provide a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) solution for deployment in multiple data centers.

NOTICE OF THE FEDERAL ACCESSIBILITY LAW AFFECTING ALL INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY (ICT) PROCUREMENTS (SECTION 508)

On January 18, 2017, the Architectural and Transportation Barriers Compliance Board (Access Board) revised and updated, in a single rulemaking, standards for electronic and information technology developed, procured, maintained, or used by Federal agencies covered by Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as well as our guidelines for telecommunications equipment and customer premises equipment covered by Section 255 of the Communications Act of 1934. The revisions and updates to the Section 508-based standards and Section 255-based guidelines are intended to ensure that information and communication technology (ICT) covered by the respective statutes is accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities.

SECTION 508 – INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY (ICT) STANDARDS

The Section 508 standards established by the Access Board are incorporated into, and made part of all VA orders, solicitations and purchase orders developed to procure ICT.  These standards are found in their entirety at: https://www.access-board.gov/guidelines-and-standards/communications-and-it/about-the-ict-refresh/final-rule/text-of-the-standards-and-guidelines.  A printed copy of the standards will be supplied upon request. 

Federal agencies must comply with the updated Section 508 Standards beginning on January 18, 2018. The Final Rule as published in the Federal Register is available from the Access Board: https://www.access-board.gov/guidelines-and-standards/communications-and-it/about-the-ict-refresh/final-rule. 

The Contractor shall comply with “508 Chapter 2: Scoping Requirements” for all electronic ICT and content delivered under this contract. Specifically, as appropriate for the technology and its functionality, the Contractor shall comply with the technical standards marked here: 

	E205 Electronic Content – (Accessibility Standard -WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA Guidelines)

	E204 Functional Performance Criteria

	E206 Hardware Requirements

	E207 Software Requirements

	E208 Support Documentation and Services Requirements

COMPATABILITY WITH ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY

The standards do not require installation of specific accessibility-related software or attachment of an assistive technology device. Section 508 requires that ICT be compatible with such software and devices so that ICT can be accessible to and usable by individuals using assistive technology, including but not limited to screen readers, screen magnifiers, and speech recognition software.

ACCEPTANCE AND ACCEPTANCE TESTING

Deliverables resulting from this solicitation will be accepted based in part on satisfaction of the Section 508 Chapter 2: Scoping Requirements standards identified above.

The Government reserves the right to test for Section 508 Compliance before delivery.  The Contractor shall be able to demonstrate Section 508 Compliance upon delivery.

The Contractor shall deliver and furnish to the Government, or use in the performance of work by Contractor employees at a Federally controlled facility, only servers that at the time of submission of proposals and at the time of award, are EPEAT® bronze registered or higher. For information about EPEAT®, see www.EPEAT.net.)

For information about ENERGY STAR, see http://www.energystar.gov for complete product specifications and updated lists of qualifying products.

GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

VA TECHNICAL REFERENCE MODEL

The Contractor shall support the VA enterprise management framework.  In association with the framework, the Contractor shall comply with OIT Technical Reference Model (VA TRM).  The VA TRM is one component within the overall Enterprise Architecture (EA) that establishes a common vocabulary and structure for describing the information technology used to develop, operate, and maintain enterprise applications.  Moreover, the VA TRM, which includes the Standards Profile and Product List, serves as a technology roadmap and tool for supporting OIT.  Architecture & Engineering Services (AES) has overall responsibility for the VA TRM.

SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER (SSN) REDUCTION 

The Contractor solution shall support the Social Security Number (SSN) Fraud Prevention Act (FPA) of 2017 which prohibits the inclusion of SSNs on any document sent by mail.  The Contractor support shall also be performed in accordance with Section 240 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act (CAA) 2018, enacted March 23, 2018, which mandates VA to discontinue using SSNs to identify individuals in all VA information systems as the Primary Identifier.  The Contractor shall ensure that any new IT solution discontinues the use of SSN as the Primary Identifier to replace the SSN with the Integrated Control Number (ICN) in all VA information systems for all individuals.  The Contractor shall ensure that all Contractor delivered applications and systems integrate with the VA Master Person Index (MPI) for identity traits to include the use of the ICN as the Primary Identifier. The Contractor solution may only use a Social Security Number to identify an individual in an information system if and only if the use of such number is required to obtain information VA requires from an information system that is not under the jurisdiction of VA.

INTERNET PROTOCOL VERSION 6 (IPV6)

The Contractor solution shall support Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6) based upon the memo issued by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) on November 19, 2020 (https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/M-21-07.pdf).  IPv6 technology, in accordance with the USGv6 Program (https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/usgv6-program/usgv6-revision-1), NIST Special Publication (SP) 500-267B Revision 1 “USGv6 Profile” (https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.500-267Br1), and NIST SP 800-119 “Guidelines for the Secure Deployment of IPv6” (https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-119), compliance shall be included in all IT infrastructures, application designs, application development, operational systems and sub-systems, and their integration.  In addition to the above requirements, all devices shall support native IPv6 and dual stack (IPv6 / IPv4) connectivity without additional memory or other resources being provided by the Government, so that they can function in a mixed environment.  All public/external facing servers and services (e.g. web, email, DNS, ISP services, etc.) shall support native IPv6 and dual stack (IPv6 / IPv4) users and all internal infrastructure and applications shall communicate using native IPv6 and dual stack (IPv6 / IPv4) operations.

The Assessment and Authorization (A&A) requirements do not apply and a Security Accreditation Package is not required.

All VA sensitive information shall be protected at all times in accordance with local security field office System Security Plans (SSP’s) and Authority to Operate (ATO)’s for all systems/LAN’s accessed while performing the tasks detailed in this Product Description.

Description 
The US Air Force Academy (USAFA), Department of Physics and Meteorology, intends to award a sole 
source firm-fixed-price purchase order to Lunt Solar Systems, located at 2520 N Coyote Dr Ste 111, 
Tucson, Arizona 85745. Lunt Solar Systems is a small business and the sole authorized US distributor for 
the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), Astro Systeme Austria (ASA). 
Requirement 
The requirement is for 200 hours of remote IT support and custom software upgrades for the USAFA 
One-Meter Telescope. The services involve specialized remote engineering labor to integrate a new 
main telescope control computer and perform custom software upgrades to the telescope system. This 
specifically includes upgrading the dome control motor/motion logic, tracking, pointing, and camera 
compatibility to ensure efficient low-earth orbit satellite tracking. 
Sole Source Justification 
The telescope hardware and control architecture utilize proprietary software and hardware interfaces 
unique to the OEM, Astro Systeme Austria (ASA). Third-party vendors lack the necessary access to the 
proprietary source code required to integrate the new control computer or reprogram the dome’s

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) - Intelligent Coding Assistance Tool  

Agency/Office:

Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)

Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)

Centers for Consumer Information and Insurance Oversight (CCIIO)

Payment Policy & Financial Management Group (PPFMG)

Project Title: HHS-Operated Risk Adjustment Data Validation Program (HHS-RADV) Intelligent Coding Assistance Tool (ICAT) RFI #2

Response Date: August 20, 2026 

BACKGROUND: The purpose of HHS-RADV is to promote confidence in the risk adjustment program set forth in Section 1343 of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (ACA) by validating the integrity and quality of data provided by issuers via External Data Gathering Environment (EDGE) servers for the purpose of operating the risk adjustment program in state market risk pools where HHS operates the risk adjustment program. The HHS-RADV audit for a benefit year begins almost immediately following the data submission deadline for that benefit year. For example, the risk adjustment data submission deadline for the 2024 benefit year was April 30, 2025. HHS-RADV samples for the 2024 benefit year audit were generated in May 2025. The 2024 benefit year HHS-RADV results will be reported in June 2026 and HHS-RADV adjustments to the 2024 benefit year risk adjustment transfers will be reported in July 2026. 

SUMMARY: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is issuing a second Request for Information (RFI) as a means of conducting market research to determine the availability and potential technical ability to procure an AI tool that is compatible with or integrated within Salesforce that consolidates from various sources discrete medical chart/record values for diagnosis abstraction. 

CMS issued an RFI on November 17, 2025 , and this is a follow-up to that original RFI. Please see the previous RFI for background information including technical flows and regulatory citations and a full discussion.   

To support clear and concise submissions, we divided this RFI into three; technical feasibility, operations and maintenance, and acquisition strategy.  

CMS is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) as a means of conducting market research to determine the availability and potential technical ability to procure a tool that is compatible with or integrated within Salesforce that consolidates from various sources discrete medical chart/record values for diagnosis abstraction.  We are seeking a tool that can be deployed initially within 6 months of award and then maintained and enhanced going forward.  We are considering a FY 27 procurement meaning CMS is seeking to procure a developed product that requires limited customization and integration with Salesforce. 

This tool should be able to populate the initial review template after accounting for HHS-operated risk adjustment and medical chart/record review requirements. Specifically, this tool will facilitate SVA primary coders and HCC validation.  CMS intends to use this tool to facilitate enhanced and more accurate first-level medical chart/record review and diagnosis abstraction for the HHS-RADV program, specifically as part of the second validation audit (SVA) (see 45 CFR 153.630). CMS is evaluating the appropriate ICAT from a wide range of commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) products, open-source solutions, and artificial intelligence (AI) options from various vendors and research institutions.  Our primary goals are:

Reduce the time for medical coders to reach accurate conclusions for SVA decisions. 

Facilitate the review of medical charts/records more quickly than and as accurately as a human medical coder, notating and synthesizing relevant diagnostic information within the medical chart/record, and identifying relevant sections of medical chart/record and diagnosis codes with the same accuracy as or better than a human medical coder;

Reduce burden and CMS costs associated with hiring medical coders to complete HHS-RADV, specifically the SVA portion of HHS-RADV;

Improve efficiency and performance through progressive use and correction; and

Demonstrable and achievable financial and functional return on investment (ROI) within a reasonable timeframe. 

Under 45 CFR § 153.630, a senior reviewer must confirm any enrollee risk adjustment error discovered during the initial validation audit (IVA). For purposes of this section, a “senior reviewer” is a human reviewer certified as a medical coder accredited by a nationally recognized accrediting agency who possesses at least 5 years of experience in medical coding. CMS therefore will likely restrict this tool to first-level review, but we welcome discussion (pros and cons) regarding potential use cases during “senior review” in later sections of this RFI.  

Technical Feasibility: This RFI is seeking solutions to be deployed in—or interact seamlessly with—our Salesforce, for instance, called the CCIIO Customer Service Response Management System (CCRMS).   We are seeking solutions that can be deployed within 6 months (at least in pilot form) and do not require significant custom coding.  Our preference is to leverage AI tools native capabilities to the greatest extent practicable, avoiding significant custom coding that could increase implementation risk.   In addition, we are seeking information regarding:

The potential offeror’s proposed architectural solution

Implementation roadmap and timetable

Security and related FEDRAMP certifications

Interfaces with Salesforce

Historical interactions with CMS systems 

Operations and Maintenance: This RFI is also seeking information on the ongoing costs (licensure, tokens, etc.), updates, and other requirements for ongoing maintenance.  CMS wants to ensure that we achieve a return on investment (savings in labor) and can deploy additional funding for continuous improvement to this solution over the lifecycle, providing doing so will result in continual measurable ROI.  In addition, we are seeking information regarding:

The potential offeror’s plan for operations and maintenance

Annual updates or continuous improvements

Workflows

Return on investment metrics

Dependencies 

Acquisition Strategy: Finally, this RFI is seeking information on contract strategy, requirements definition  (Performance Work Statement or Statement of Objectives) and preferred teaming arrangements for optimal delivery. CMS wishes to ensure that there are no sourcing constraints between the RADV professional services acquisition vehicle and the ICAT acquisition vehicle. We request information on best methods to procure discrete aspects (or modular parts) of the proposed ICAT solution. 

Conflict of Interest:  In RFI #1, CMS stated that any ICAT solution must follow the requirements are satisfied and discussed the regulatory citation 45 CFR § 153.630(b)(3):

RESPONDING TO THIS REQUEST: 

 

THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ONLY. This RFI is issued solely for CMS’ information and planning purposes. This RFI does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service. At this time, CMS is not soliciting quotes/proposals. Respondents are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI; all costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the respondent’s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future procurement. It is the responsibility of the interested vendors to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this requirement. Information provided in the RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. HHS, CMS, or OAGM have not made a commitment to procure any of the items discussed, and release of this RFI is not a commitment or an authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be allowed or sought.  

 

Proprietary information and trade secrets, if any, must be clearly marked on all materials. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked “Proprietary” will be handled accordingly. Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be returned, nor will the receipt be confirmed. Respondents will not receive feedback on their submission. No basis for claims against the United States Government shall arise as a result of a response to this RFI or from the United States Government’s use of such information. 

Responses to this RFI shall be submitted no later than 10:00 AM local prevailing time on August 20, 2026 to Andrew Mummert, Contracting Officer, at andrew.mummert@cms.hhs.gov, in a format that is readable in Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF document with page size 8.5 by 11 inches, with a minimum of 1” margins. Calibri Font Size 11 with no less than single spacing between lines is required.  Please note that a response to every question is not required.  Responses will be no more than 3,000 characters per question.  CMS will accept up to 10 additional Appendix pages to accommodate blueprints or other technical documentation.  CMS will not accept hard-copy responses or other formats. All responses to the RFI shall contain ‘HHS-RADV- ICAT RFI – Company Name’ in the response email's subject-line. 

Section I. – General Vendor Information: General Vendor Information to include the following: 

Organization Name 

Mailing address 

Name, phone number, and e-mail address of designated point of contact 

Business type (large business, small business, small disadvantaged business, 8(a)-certified small disadvantaged business, HUBZone small business, woman-owned small business, very small business, veteran-owned small business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business). 

Any current or previous federal contracts in the GSA, Governmentwide Acquisition Contracts (GWAC), or any other relevant federal contracts held by your organization. 

Section II. The name and contact information of the organization whose views are represented in the submission, if different from the information provided in Section I. 

Section III. Respondents are encouraged to provide complete but concise responses to the questions listed below. Please note that a response to every question is not required. 

QUESTIONS: 	 

This RFI seeks responses from industry regarding technological tools that may improve HHS-RADV accuracy and efficiency and promote continued confidence in the program. The feedback from this RFI may be used to develop future RFPs. 

CMS asks that respondents address the questions that are germane to your experience and expertise. Respondents are not required to answer all questions.   CMS may request demonstrations following review of responses. 

Technical Feasibility:

What functionality can be delivered within 6 months of award that accomplishes some resource reduction, then in later phases, scaled upward, achieving greater resource efficiency?

What is the offeror’s timeline for these deployment phases?

Please provide a reference architectural diagram of the offeror’s proposed ICAT solution.    

Please describe interfaces with our Salesforce instance, called the CCIIO Customer Service Response Management System (CCRMS) proposed with ICAT.  Please describe any other CMS system needs or dependencies.  

Please provide the ICAT solution FEDRAMP authorization (High, Medium, or Low) including the hosting platform, software platform, or other 3rd party dependencies.  

Operations and Maintenance:

What adoption, staffing and other factors permit for a positive CMS ROI over your proposed timeline?

What training should be included in this scope for effective user adaption?

Please provide a cost projection and a one- to five-year ROI estimate that identifies expected costs, expected savings, cost avoidance, payback period, and break-even point using proposed ICAT costs as the benchmark.  Do not include CMS SVA costs in this analysis.   Include one-time implementation costs, recurring license/subscription costs, Salesforce/CCRMS integration costs, cloud or compute costs, OCR/NLP/LLM/API costs, O&M costs, training costs, security and support costs, and help desk or user support costs.

Acquisition Strategy:

Describe your organization’s interest and ability to support an acquisition strategy in which CMS may award separate contracts for products, and services, and require all contractors to collaborate under Government-defined coordination and processes.

Should CMS consider using a multiple-contract structure rather than a single IDIQ or BPA approach?

For a multiple-contract structure, what layers/roles would you recommend CMS consider?

Describe your willingness to participate in a CMS-defined demonstration using synthetic or de-identified RADV-like records. Identify what functionality can be demonstrated live, what requires a sandbox, and what evidence CMS should request to compare solutions fairly.  CMS may schedule demonstrations during the summer and fall of 2026.

Conflict of Interest:

In RFI #1, CMS stated any ICAT solution must meet be free of conflicts of interest as discussed, the regulatory citation 45 CFR § 153.630(b)(3):	

Upon conducting market research, we are concerned the application of this standard may limit the availability of commercial products thereby undermining the ICAT goal of a 6-month initial deployment.   We solicit comment on this question.  Question 13 is not subject to the 3,000 limit to provide opportunity for a robust discussion.
