NEXT GENERATION COMMAND AND CONTROL (NGC2) 
CALL FOR SOLUTIONS (CFS)  
 FOR 
SCALABLE SOFTWARE APPLICATIONS 
W9128Z-26-R-A004 
ISSUED UNDER W15P7T-25-S-0001 
 
 
 
 
Program Manager Command and Control (PM C2) Applications 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 


2 
 
SECTION 1 – INTRODUCTION  
1.1 BACKGROUND  
The U.S. Army is transforming command and control (C2) for the current and future fight 
through the Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) effort. The U.S. Army is replacing 
fragmented, vertical warfighting systems with a unified technology stack architecture of 
heterogenous software and hardware components. This transformation ensures data from any 
sensor, shooter, or warfighting system is accessible from a common data layer, and any 
application, user dashboard, algorithm, or AI agent accesses the same data source to support 
Warfighter operations. The architecture eliminates silo-ed data. To dominate on the modern 
battlefield, commanders and the algorithms that assist them with data synthesis must have access 
to data on demand, enabling faster and superior decision-making over our adversaries. 
The United States Army Contracting Command, Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), on 
behalf of CPE C2IN, and PM C2 Applications, is publishing this call under the current 
Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) W15P7T-25-S-0001, utilizing the authority of 10 U.S.C. 
§ 3458 and DFARS 212.70, for scalable software applications in support of NGC2. The 
information provided herein is intended to ensure that to the maximum extent practicable, 
competitive procedures are used to identify the best solutions received in response to this call. 
1.2 CFS Procedures  
This CFS is a competitive solicitation seeking innovative, commercially available software 
applications capable of scaling in the NGC2 ecosystem. This CFS may result in one or more 
solutions determined to be “awardable”; and subsequently one or more FAR Part 12 commercial 
contracts based on operational application needs.   
The Call for Solutions is solicitating white papers (WPs) until the call expiration date of 1300 
ET on 6 August 2026.  WPs submitted in response to the call will be governed by this call and 
3.1 General Guidelines in CSO W15P7T-25-S-0001, unless otherwise noted herein. 
The Government reserves the right not to fully evaluate any WPs submitted that are not relevant 
to this call. WPs received will be evaluated according to instruction, submission, and evaluation 
details described herein.  
1.3 Call Approach, Submission and Evaluations of WPs and Proposals  
Two- Phase Approach: This call will use a two-phase process to solicit WPs and select offeror(s) 
eligible for a potential award. Phase I, Step 1 of the process will allow potential offerors to 
submit descriptive WPs in lieu of full proposals. If necessary, the Government may request a 
solution demonstration of the white paper proposal which shall be at no cost to the Government 
under Phase I, Step 2. Based on the Phase I evaluation criteria defined in this call, the 
Government will select offeror(s) for Phase II.  
 
At Phase II of the process, the Government may request favorable offeror(s) to submit full 

3 
 
proposals. Due to available resources, all Phase II eligible (“awardable”) offeror(s) may not 
receive a proposal request, and not all requested proposals will result in an award.  
 
Submission of a WP does not guarantee advancement to Phase II (Request for Proposal), and the 
Government is under no obligation to make any award for solutions determined to be 
“awardable”. The Government reserves the right not to provide clarifications, or significant 
individual feedback, for submissions that do not advance. The Government will not include a 
comparison of submissions against a common statement of work (SOW) as the CFS provides no 
common SOW that constrain how interested parties must respond; instead, the WP represents a 
submission opportunity for a variety of innovative commercial items, technologies, and/or 
services that represent meaningful NGC2 modular capabilities of diverse scope and price. 
 
SECTION 2 – Problem Statement 
The NGC2 program is transitioning from prototyping at two operational units to the product 
delivery phase. While previous application efforts focused on experimentation, proof-of-concept 
development, and iterative development of application functionality, the next phase will 
emphasize the fielding of scalable, mission-ready applications that comply with established 
architectural, cybersecurity, data, and interface standards.  
 
NGC2 applications cannot be standalone products; instead, they are productive interfaces for 
Warfighters to interact, visualize, and synthesize data in support of dynamic operations. 
Applications are not an end state for data. NGC2 applications provide a means to add context to 
data about the battlefield for rapid consumption by other users, algorithms, and/or AI agents. 
Data transformed by a user in an application must be published to the data layer, ensuring that it 
is discoverable and able to be consumed by any other applicable NGC2 component.  
As the NGC2 ecosystem matures, the Government requires applications that can integrate into 
the newly established converged data layer (Common Data Baseline Link) using open APIs and 
SDKs. Solutions must demonstrate modularity, including required integrations with common 
services (such as maps, weather, ICAM), required compliance with data registry for how data is 
consumed or published from and to the data layer, and required compliance with an AI services 
registry for how AI models are trained, monitored, and deployed. Each application accesses data 
in compliance with authentication and role-based access controls provided as a common service 
in the technology stack. 
NGC2 architecture leverages modern practices aligned with the open container initiative. 
Applications will rely on common NGC2 tools for CI/CD that ensure rapid delivery of updates to 
the deployed operational compute environments, whether in an environment with cloud access or 
limited to local installs. NGC2 applications must be deployed as containers within the OCI-
compliant environment selected by the Government and provided in the converged data layer. 
NGC2 applications will not provide their own runtime environment or application platform. 

4 
 
Applications must account for functionality across a range of compute infrastructure and range 
of network transport bandwidth. The NGC2 ecosystem includes a family of compute 
infrastructure, ranging from robust enterprise cloud infrastructure, multi-GPU or CPU edge 
hardware, limited mounted compute in platforms such as Abrams, Bradley, Stryker, and down to 
austere, limited edge compute infrastructure. Consequently, NGC2 software design accounts for 
configurability for diverse compute form factors, including parameterizing the size of software 
updates to account for limited compute or time windows for delivery. NGC2 applications must 
also be designed for dynamic data shaping, accounting for when Warfighters only have access to 
network transport with limited bandwidth to synchronize data, but flexible to adjust to more 
expansive data elements when bandwidth is not limited. 
The NGC2 ecosystem is designed around a common data layer, providing opportunity for 
commanders to have some flexibility in what application interfaces are preferred to interact with 
battlefield data (i.e. data is the same since all applications consume from the same data layer 
source); however, common applications used across the Army are advantageous for minimizing 
training as Warfighters transition among operational units every few years. As the NGC2 product 
delivery progresses, the Government will explore opportunities to find a balance between 
diversity and commonality in how applications are purchased and available to some or all of the 
Army. Consequently, the price for applications will account for purchasing for singular Army 
units (Division, Corps, Reserve) and purchasing for consumption-based usage (using application 
telemetry data to track how many users).  
The Government seeks to identify commercial solutions ready for operational product delivery 
and capable of supporting both current and emerging mission requirements. Solutions that 
successfully demonstrate technical merit, scalability, and affordability may be designated as 
awardable solutions, signifying that they can satisfy one or more anticipated Government 
capability needs. Once determined to be awardable, solutions are eligible for consideration for 
future acquisitions without requiring repeated technical evaluations, speeding up the acquisition 
timeline to meet emerging operational needs at pace. The objective is to reduce acquisition lead 
times, ensure applications are modular components with the data layer and accelerate the 
delivery of commercial capability to the warfighter. 
SECTION 3 –  Phase I  
3.1 Phase I- WP Submission 
(i) Format: WPs shall be electronically submitted, shall not exceed 5 pages in length 
(single sided, single spaced, 12-size font, 1 inch margins). The 5-page limitation does 
not include the completed questionnaire. 
a. WP Structure and Contents: A complete WP will consist of four sections with the 
required information listed in the subparagraphs:  
Section 1 - Cover Sheet; 
Section 2 - Software Application Description 

5 
 
Section 3 - Scalability Overview; and  
Section 4 - Price / Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM). 
b. Questionnaire: Responses in the questionnaire can be explicitly substantiated with 
supporting details in the submitted white paper. No additional material may be 
amended to the questionnaire. 
(ii) WPs and the Questionnaire shall be submitted via e-mail to 
usarmy.apg.acc.mbx.army-c2-solutions@army.mil. It is the offeror’s responsibility to 
ensure submission is received. 
 
3.2 Phase I - WP Contents 
3.2.1 Section 1- Cover Sheet: 
White Papers shall include a cover sheet that includes: 
(1) The name, CAGE Code, Unique Entity ID of the offeror. Business Size Classification under 
North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 541715; 
(2) Primary point of contact, including name, address, phone and e-mail contact information; and 
(3) Date of submission. 
 
3.2.2 Section 2 – Software Application Description: 
Provide an overview of the software application, identify the warfighting function(s) it supports, 
and summarize its unique value to the NGC2 ecosystem. Describe the application’s he current 
technical maturity, capability gaps, use cases, and any known dependencies required to fully 
capitalize on its use. Specify top differentiators, such as unique technology, specific expertise, 
and agile processes your solution provides. Describe Cloud to Edge deployment approach, 
including the ability to adapt between usage on cloud infrastructure and usage onTactical Edge 
Compute (TECs), including timeframes on edge infrastructure with Disconnected, Degraded, 
Intermittent, and Low-bandwidth (DDIL) network transport capabilities which may require 
dynamic data shaping to maintain application performance. 
 
3.2.3 Section 3- Scalability Overview: 
The narrative in this section should directly align with, expand upon, and substantiate the  
responses provided Attachment 0001- Phase I Offeror Questionnaire. Detail the current software 
application(s) adherence to NGC2 architecture principles described in the problem statement 
section. Address deployment as containers to a Government-specified, OCI-compliant 
environment using provided CI/CD tools. Describe security accreditation and posture based on 
any existing or expired cybersecurity Authority to Operate (ATO) on any military network, and 
whether for cloud or edge compute environments. 
 
3.2.4 Section 4 – Price (ROM) 

6 
 
This section shall include the ROM price and narrative associated with license costs and services 
required to scale the application’s use. ROM submissions shall provide enough fidelity for the 
Government to understand the alignment to the Offerors current commercial offerings.  
 
The ROM narrative shall include, at a minimum, details on the following categories for the 
ROM:  
License price for a period of twelve (12) months based on the following scale, for unlimited 
users, within the following potential deployment tiers: 
(i) Test/Developer license for non-production environments, sandbox environments, 
and/or testing capabilities. 
(ii) One (1) Active Army Division 
(iii) One (1) CORPS and downtrace divisions/brigades/commands 
(iv) COMPO 1 Active Army Divisions 
(v) Unlimited use within the Army 
 
The ROM pricing shall be assumed to be the license costs, minimal services to maintain 
adherence to architecture standards as detailed in the questionnaire, and cybersecurity updates 
per Service Level Agreements. Potential costs including training, travel or user test events shall 
be excluded from the above price points; however, these costs will be requested at a later time.  
3.2.5 Section 5 - Completed Questionnaire 
A completed version of Attachment 0001- Phase I Offeror Questionnaire for the software 
application being proposed. Offerors shall complete and submit this questionnaire in its entirety. 
Instructions for completing the questionnaire are provided as a worksheet in the document. 
 
3.3 Phase I- Step 1 WP Evaluation 
Phase I Step 1 Evaluation Process: Responses will be evaluated by a panel of subject-matter 
experts (SMEs) using the criteria specified in this call. Individual WP evaluations will be based 
on acceptability or unacceptability without regard to other WPs and proposals submitted under 
this call.  
Phase I Evaluation Criteria: The evaluation factors of the white paper include Technical Merit 
and Scalability as described below. The factors are listed in the descending order of importance. 
1) Technical Merit 
2) Scalability 
 
The Government will also evaluate the ROM for affordability. A ROM that is deemed excessive 
or unrealistic for the proposed solution may result in an “unawardable” rating, regardless of the 
evaluation of the other factors.  

7 
 
 
 
3.3.1 Technical Merit: 
 
The Government will evaluate the offeror’s proposed software applications(s) for its technical 
merit in satisfying the technical challenges and objectives outlined in this call. Additionally, the 
Government will evaluate how eligibly and effectively the WP narrative substantiates, expands 
upon, and proves the baseline capabilities affirmed by the offeror in Attachment 0001 - Phase I 
Offeror Questionnaire. The evaluation will be based on a comprehensive review of the offeror’s 
WP.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)
Microsoft Unified Support for PAESSP
1.0 Background & Objective
The Government requires Microsoft Unified Enterprise Support to maintain the operational availability and cybersecurity compliance of Portfolio 
Acquisition Executive Strategic Systems Program's (PAE SSP) Unclassified and Secret Excepted networks. Due to the highly technical and mission-
critical nature of these systems, the Government requires specialized, proprietary Microsoft professional support. This includes direct OEM (Original 
Equipment Manufacturer) reach-back to Microsoft product developers and Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) to tailor proprietary code to the PAESSP 
environment and resolve critical system outages.
2.0 Scope of Work (CLIN 0001)
The Contractor shall provide non-personnel services for Microsoft Unified Enterprise for Federal Base coverage with Secured Delivery Management, 
and associated support hours being performed exclusively by US citizens.
3.0 Specific Performance Requirement
The Contractor shall provide comprehensive support services, leveraging proprietary tools, knowledge bases, and direct developer access. Core 
requirements include:
Proprietary direct OEM Support & Reach-Back: Provide real-time access to Microsoft software 
developers and product teams who possess source code access. The Contractor must provide architectural 
planning, problem resolution, and outage escalation that cannot be fulfilled by third-party vendors.
Customer Success Account Manager (CSAM): Provide a cleared CSAM to oversee solution health, 
proactive resilience, disaster preparedness, and technology optimization. The CSAM will act as the single 
point of contact for service delivery, management planning, and escalation management.
Reactive Problem Resolution & Incident Response: Provide 24/7 break-fix support with rapid escalation 
paths. The Contractor must adhere to strict initial response Service Level Agreements (SLAs), including:
Severity 1 (Critical System Down): 15-minute response for Azure components; 1-hour response for 
all other products, with continuous 24/7 effort and critical situation resources assigned.
Severity A-C: Scaled response times ranging from 1 to 4 hours based on business impact.
US Citizen Support: Guarantee that all initial Problem Resolution Support (PRS) and Advisory Support 
for qualified products is handled exclusively by US Citizens physically located within the United States. 
All support data must be stored in US-based data centers.
Proactive & Educational Services: Provide access to On-demand Assessments (automated log analysis), 
On-demand Education (online training/labs), and Advisory Support for architecture and configuration best 
practices.
4.0 Security & Certifications
Clearance: The Contractor must possess a SECRET clearance based on a Single Scope Background 
Investigation (SSBI) on the first day of the period of performance.
Cybersecurity Workforce (CSWF): Contractor personnel with privileged access must meet DOD 8140 
CSWF Specialty Area 451 (System Administration) certification and proficiency requirements.
Operations Security: All work shall be performed in accordance with DOD and Navy OPSEC and Risk 
Management Framework (RMF) requirements.
5.0 Period and Place of Performance
Period of Performance: 15 September 2026 through 14 September 2027 (12 Months).
Place of Performance: Work shall be performed remotely whenever viable, or on-site at the following 
locations as required:
Washington Navy Yard, DC
Silverdale, WA

Kings Bay, GA
6.0 Government Furnished Property (GFP)
The Government will provide all required Microsoft software licenses and software assurance.
7.0 Deliverables & Quality Control
Quality Control Plan (QCP): Due 30 days after award.
Status Reporting: The CSAM shall conduct regular status meetings and provide standardized reporting on 
service delivery, support activities, and system health.
Critical Escalation: Overarching Microsoft environment support with documented critical escalation paths.

Sources Sought Synopsis 
 
The Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) is issuing this sources sought 
synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and 
the resources to support this requirement for the Knowledge Management System and Services 
(KMSS). The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of 
procurement. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 
assigned to this procurement is 541511, Custom Computer Programming Services. The Product 
Service Code assigned to this procurement is DA01, Business Application/Application 
Development Support Services. 
 
There is no solicitation at this time. This request for capability information does not constitute a 
request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely 
voluntary; the government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred.   
 
If your organization has the potential capacity to perform these contract services, please provide 
the following information: 1) organization name, address, email address, website address, 
telephone number, and size and type of ownership for the organization; and 2) tailored capability 
statements addressing the particulars of this effort, with appropriate documentation supporting 
claims of organizational and staff capability. If significant subcontracting or teaming is 
anticipated in order to deliver technical capability, organizations should address the 
administrative and management structure of such arrangements.  
 
The government will evaluate market information to ascertain potential market capacity to 1) 
provide services consistent in scope and scale with those described in this notice and otherwise 
anticipated; 2) secure and apply the full range of corporate financial, human capital, and 
technical resources required to successfully perform similar requirements; 3) implement a 
successful project management plan that includes: compliance with program schedules; cost 
containment; meeting and tracking performance; hiring and retention of personnel and risk 
mitigation; and 4) provide services under a performance based service acquisition contract.  
 
Based on the responses to this sources sought notice/market research, this requirement may be 
set-aside for small businesses or procured through full and open competition, and multiple 
awards may be made. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no 
feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions. 
 
Submission Instructions: Interested parties who consider themselves qualified to perform the 
above-listed services are invited to submit  a response to this Sources Sought Notice by Friday,

rigorous research; evaluates HUD policies and programs; supports innovation in building

B.3 PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT

SCOPE

The Contractor shall provide maintenance, clinical and technical support, project management, and ongoing sustainment for the existing (or upgraded systems) as part of the Veteran Integrated Services Network (VISN) 21 Philips Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) Enterprise.  The support shall include furnishing all necessary hardware, software, licensing, professional and installation services, and upgrades required to maintain the VISN 21 PACS at a 99.99% uptime. The PACS system covers all facilities in VISN 21: San Francisco, Palo Alto, Mather, Reno, Fresno, Honolulu, Sacramento, Las Vegas, and Manila (see item 22 for locations and addresses).  VISN 21 has over 6.5 million PACS studies with an annual volume of over 600,000 studies.

The Contractor shall provide an Enterprise-wide viewer that is a browser-based medical image and information management system that provides one (1) click to offer full resolution, diagnostic-quality images on demand, directly to the point of patient care to all standard Personal Computers (PCs) anywhere across the VA enterprise.  The Contractor must provide unlimited viewing licenses for enterprise-wide viewer application.  The Contractor must work with the Veteran Affairs (VA) to keep the software approved for use with Office of Information and Technology (OI&T) baselined computers and systems via the Technical Reference Model.

The Contractor shall provide a Diagnostic Radiology Client that is an advanced radiology diagnostic application that provides a comprehensive, full-resolution diagnostic presentation of current and prior procedures and associated clinical information.  The radiology client shall include functionality, including but not limited to multi-planar, maximum intensity projection and basic three-dimensional rendering capabilities. The Contractor must provide unlimited viewing licenses for Diagnostic Radiology Client application.

The Contractor shall also provide a single database and PACS storage for all sites (except Manila which will have its own separate system) that is an always-online digital medical image storage system that supports millions of studies per year and thousands of concurrent Enterprise-wide viewers and Diagnostic Radiology clients across multiple sites.  In addition, the Contractor shall provide database and PACS storage provides a common storage/archive for VISN 21 Cardiology PACS images.  The Contractor must provide an unlimited number of modality connections to the Contractor provided PACS solution.  The PACS system shall have a local cache for processing exams and an additional backup solution (PICS) if main repository is offline (for all locations listed in section 22).  Both the local cache, and disaster recovery system shall each hold one (1) years’ worth of studies (minimum per site), and the system shall not use near-line (optical storage) or off-line storage.

ESR – Contractor Engineering Service Report.  Documentation of the services rendered for each incidence of work performance under the terms and conditions of the contract.

External Downtime – all time that the server cannot be accessed by all authorized users beyond the Single Point of Demarcation (SPOD) due to causes beyond the Contractor’s reasonable control and occurring without its fault or negligence, including, without limitation, war, strikes, fires, floods, governmental restrictions, power failures or surges, disruptions in telephone service or manual shutdowns by Customer.

FSE – Field Service Engineer is a person who is authorized by the contractor to perform maintenance (corrective and/or preventive) services.

OEM – Original Equipment Manufacturer.

PM – Preventive Maintenance Inspection.  Services which are periodic in nature and are required to maintain the equipment in such condition that it may be operated in accordance with its intended design and functional capacity with minimal incidence of malfunction or operative conditions.  

Scheduled Downtime – all time that the server cannot be accessed by all authorized users beyond the SPOD due to scheduled maintenance including, but not limited to, preventative maintenance, updates, upgrades, scheduled reboots, and restarts.  The Contractor will work with the Customer to determine a mutually agreeable time for Scheduled Downtime; however, the Contractor as the sole discretion in determining the final timing of Scheduled Downtime. The Contractor shall provide at least twenty-four (24) hours advance notice of Scheduled Downtime.

SPOD – Standard Point of Demarcation meaning the network connection interface installed at the server computer hardware.

Unscheduled Downtime – all time that the server cannot be accessed by all authorized users beyond the SPOD that is not Scheduled Downtime or External Downtime, the cause of which originates on the Contractor’s side of the SPOD.  Measurement of Unscheduled Downtime begins when Customer’s authorized representative notifies a Contractor Customer Service Representative of the existence of Unscheduled Downtime and the Contractor Customer Service Representative issues and logs a trouble ticket.

The Contractor must provide VA with all inventory documentation for equipment and network configuration for any hardware additions or subtractions.  The Contractor must provide a hardware assessment at the request of the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) annually if requested.

Section C - Description/Specifications/Statement of Work
Statement of Work for:
GlobalScape Software Maintenance FY 26
 
 
(S)  Background
The Atlantic Test Range, Telemetry Branch is procuring GlobalScape Software Maintenance in support of Atlantic Test Range (ATR).
-         Scope
The Telemetry Systems Branch, Data Engineering and Analysis (DEA) Section's Data Lab distributes processed telemetry and onboard data post-
flight and provides an environment for flight test engineers to share analyzed data. ATR DataPoint File Transfer Web Server (FTWS), the system   
providing this capability, utilizes the GlobalScape EFT Server Enterprise software to perform this functionality on unclassified and classified 
environments. The classified ATR DataPoint FTWS system provides a parallel capability on the classified environment; allowing data to be shared   
on the classified NMCI and RDTE networks. Software maintenance is required to support our unclassified and classified systems.  
(S)  Objectives/Task
The unclassified FTWS system has been in production since 2011, and has proven to successfully support the NAVAIR Flight Test Community data 
distribution and access requirements including access for Contractors (e.g. NGC, LMCO, and Boeing) with DISA approved certificates; meet large 
file transfer requirements (e.g. 10+ GB); and meet Cybersecurity requirements.

BACKGROUND

The Department of Veteran’s Affairs (VA) uses a variety of clinical information systems (CIS) to document clinical care provided to veterans across a spectrum of clinical services and specialties. These CIS are computer-based systems used to gather, store, and integrate clinical data on patients to the VA’s electronic health record (EHR).  These systems may be implemented and used at single VA Medical Center (VAMC) locations, or across entire health care systems at the Veteran Integrated Service Network (VISN) or national levels. 

The VA is in the process of transitioning to new CIS for specific clinical solutions as part of national standardization efforts, which introduces a need to retain or migrate the legacy CIS data for a particular endoscopy information system (EIS) in alignment with VA policies. The VA is interested in procuring services to help consolidate legacy SQL databases from disparate VAMC throughout the country into a single SQL server management platform and build customized reporting tools that will allow clinical stakeholders to review this historical data to aid in clinical decision making and optimizing future care. This specific procurement will include several VAMC across VHA as outlined in Addendum C.

STATEMENT OF WORK   
AUDIO/VISUAL SYSTEM
 RECRUIT TRAINING COMMAND, GREAT LAKES, ILLINOIS
 
1.       Description of Services: Recruit Training Command (RTC) orchestrates the presentation of 48 yearly Navy Boot Camp 
Graduations, 3 New Student Indoctrinations, 2 Sea Cadet events, and other command functions necessitating projection in the 
Midway Ceremonial Drill Hall. This procurement request aims to provide the essential visual equipment to enhance spectator 
visualization and support the mission needs of RTC.
Due to storm damage on existing audio/visual equipment in the Midway Ceremonial Drill Hall, an urgent requirement for repair is 
needed to restore mission capabilities for RTC Graduation ceremonies.
2.       Scope: The Contractor shall provide the following items that must be compatible with or superior to Crestron system:

Additional services required include:
 
-         Operational Test and training on procedures and troubleshooting for RTC N6 Staff, PAO personnel, and Midway 
Ceremonial Drill Hall Staff will be provided after installation.
-         The Contractor shall procure, transport, and set up all equipment listed in table 1, above.  
-         The Contractor shall also replace switchers and conditioners in accordance with the specifications outlined in the 
statement of work. 
-         The Contractor shall procure and utilize an aerial lift as it will be required for repairs and installation. 
-         The Contractor shall remove and dispose all packaging materials, ensuring their proper disposal outside of the 
installation area. 
-         Maintaining adherence to the standards outlined within the contract, as well as compliance with all relevant Federal, 
State, and local government laws/regulations and industrial standards, is expected from the Contractor. 
-         By completion of the scope the Contractor shall confirm that all equipment listed in table 1, above, is fully capable of 
broadcasting in the drill hall and enable broadcasting streaming capabilities outside of the drill hall.
 
Under unforeseen circumstances, additional repairs identified while performing the required tasks of this contract could be required 
from the Contractor. The Contractor shall provide a written estimate of the cost (labor & materials) of the additional work identified to 
the Contracting Officer prior to the commencement of work. The quote shall include the following as a minimum: Materials Cost, 
Labor Cost, Additional Cost and Total Cost. Providing a quote does not authorize the Contractor to proceed with the additional work. 
The Contracting Officer will review the quote and make a determination regarding how to proceed.
 
3.       Contractor Furnished Items:     The Contractor shall provide all materials, personnel; supervision and equipment needed to        
provide and deliver the items listed in table 1, above. Additionally, the Contractor shall provide equipment operation manuals.
 
The Contractor shall contact the Technical Point of Contact to arrange an acceptable date of delivery and installation within the 
required period of performance. After installation, the Contractor shall conduct an operations test and provide Standard Operating 
Procedures and Troubleshooting training for RTC N6, Midway Ceremonial Drill Hall, and PAO staff members.
 
4.       Audio Booth Specifications: see table 1, above.
 
5.       Warranty Coverage: Warranty coverage shall be manufactures standard warranty included in the purchase of the 
equipment.
    
6.       Key Personnel and Specific Skill Sets Required: Recruit Training Command personnel will oversee the delivery process 
to ensure compliance with operational instructions. Designated staff members will be assigned to accompany the delivery 
personnel throughout the entire duration of the delivery. At the conclusion of install, training on Standard Operating Procedures 
and troubleshooting will be provided to RTC N6, PAO, and Midway Ceremonial Drill Hall staff members.

7.       Personnel Security Requirements: Prior approval is required for base access. Contractor personnel performing under this 
contract must be US Citizens with no history of felonies and able to pass a background clearance to have access to the base. They 
will be required to fill out a SECNAV 5512 and must have two valid forms of identification. Work under this task is Unclassified.
 
8.       Security and Personnel Conduct: All contractor equipment, personnel, and vehicles shall be subject to inspection and 
search by Government security officials (or designated representatives) upon entry to any Government owned and/or operated 
installations and facilities. The Contractor shall comply with all local base/installation security procedures required to gain access 
to US Government ships, facilities, and other assets. If directed by Government security officials (or designated representatives), 
the contractor shall remove any equipment or personnel considered a security risk. The Government reserves the right to inspect 
contractor equipment and personnel; to visit and inspect work sites; and/or to travel with the contractor while the contractor is 
within the limits of Government owned and/or operated installations and facilities. Due to security measures, delays may occur 
during vehicle inspections to obtain base entry. The Government is not responsible for delays due to security measures; due to 
vehicle inspections; or due to the failure of the contractor and/or contractor personnel to obtain proper base access in advance. The 
Government has the right to decline and not utilize contractor personnel who fail to meet the safety and security standards of the 
US Navy. The determination of whether contractor provided personnel meet the safety and security standards of the US Navy 
shall be at the sole discretion of the Government. If and when contractor personnel are identified by the Government as not 
meeting these standards, the contractor shall remove those personnel from the performance of any work under this contract and 
replace them with an individual who meets the US Navy's safety and security standards at no additional cost to the Government.
 
9.       Other Requirements: To prevent any last-minute issues, the designated representative from the Recruit Training 
Command must ensure that all contractors are cleared for access at least one week before their scheduled arrival. Considering a 3-
working-day clearance process, it is imperative that all SECNAV 5512 forms be submitted to the Security Pass and ID office no 
later than 10 days before the planned delivery date.
 
10.    Hours of Operations: The customer's hours for accepting this service is between the hours of 0800-1500 none can be on a 
weekend or a holiday.
  
11.    Government Furnished Property Material and Services: Not Applicable. 
 
12.    Place of Performance/Delivery: 
 
Recruit Training Command, Building 7220 USS MIDWAY RTC 3131 INDIANA ST Great Lakes, IL 60088), on the drill 
deck.  For Building 7220, an exterior garage door will access the drill hall directly. The Contractors delivery truck must have a lift 
gate or ramp.
 
**Wage Determination 2015-4935 Rev. 30 Dated 5/13/2026 is incorporated into this contract**
 
13.    Period of Performance: The Contractor shall complete the full scope of this statement of work no later than August 12, 
2026.
     
14.    Acceptance of Services Rendered: The RTC staff must be present to verify that the products meet all requirements of this 
request before the contract representative deems the job complete.

GENERAL INFORMATION

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

Notice of intent to award a sole source, firm fixed price contract to PROAIM Americas, LLC.

SOL: 36C24226Q0823

DUE: 07/28/2026, 1600 EST.

SET ASIDE: N/A 

NAICS: 541519 – Information Technology Value Added Resellers.

POP STATE: 30 Days ARO

AGENCY: Department of Veterans Affairs; Margaret Cochran Corbin VA Medical Center, 423 East 23rd Street, New York, NY 10010.

Email: Jonatan.rondon@va.gov 

 

The Department of Veterans Affairs, Margaret Cochran Corbin VA Campus, intends to award a sole source, firm fixed price contract to PROAIM Americas, LLC. under the authority of RFO FAR 13.101(b) to PROAIM Americas, LLC., 16024 Manchester Road, Suite 200, Saint Louis, MO 63011 for their authorization to perform services and repairs on Carl Zeiss products.

This project covers the upgrade of four (4) Zeiss Humphrey Field Analyzer 3 (HFA3) and five (5) Zeiss Cirrus Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) diagnostic systems across the New York Harbor VA Medical Center campuses—including Manhattan, Brooklyn, St. Albans and Staten Island—from their current Windows operating system to Windows 10 IoT Enterprise 2021 LTSC. These upgrades will utilize the OEM-supported Zeiss Windows 10 IoT LTSC license kits.

The scope includes on-site installation of Windows 10 IoT LTSC upgrade kits, validation of software functionality post-upgrade, and coordination with clinical engineering and IT personnel to ensure full compatibility with existing Zeiss imaging software. All work must adhere to VA OIT and Biomedical Engineering standards, ensuring minimal downtime of ophthalmic diagnostic services.

The objective of this procurement is to obtain all necessary Windows 10 IoT Enterprise 2021 LTSC license kits, installation services, and technical support required to upgrade all Zeiss HFA3 and Zeiss Cirrus OCT units to a VA‑compliant operating system. The included upgrade kits—specified per serial number for Brooklyn, Jamaica Plains, Staten Island, and New York campuses—provide OEM‑validated compatibility for HFA3 units with serial numbers 860‑15001 and above, and Cirrus OCT units with serial numbers 5000‑4994 and above.

This project also ensures full VA cybersecurity compliance, including:

• Migration from unsupported Windows versions to a federally approved OS baseline

• Alignment with VA TIC, FISMA, and NIST 800‑53 security controls

• Verification of device hardening, patching status, and Windows 10 IoT LTSC security configuration

• Maintenance of secure network integration, consistent with VA network security policies

The upgraded platform will enhance system security, standardize OS versions across all campuses, ensure ongoing OEM software support, and reduce cybersecurity vulnerabilities associated with legacy.

Carl Zeiss Meditec USA, Inc. products are authorized to be only sold through Small Dis-advantaged Owned government distributor PROAIM America’s LLC or Sub Distributors of PROAIM America’s LLC. Only Carl Zeiss Meditec USA Inc. Employed Certified Field Service Engineers and certified ZEISS and authorized ZEISS trained personnel are approved to perform “service” “repair” services on Zeiss products/ equipment.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT 
 
Utility Monitoring and Control Systems (UMCS) Sixth Generation (VI) 
 
(Revision Date: 18 June 2026) 
 
PART 1 
GENERAL INFORMATION 
 
1.1 Description of Services.  The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment tools, materials supervision, and 
other items and non-personal services necessary to provide the Procurement and Installation (P&I) of and/or the 
Maintenance and Service (M&S) of Facility Related Control Systems (FRCS) including but not limited to: Utility 
Monitoring and Control Systems (UMCS), Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems  to include 
chiller/boiler systems installation and/or integration, Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Systems, 
Fire Alarm Systems (FAS), life safety systems, other automated control systems including chemical / biological / 
radiological contaminant detection / filtration / response, utilities (electric/ gas/ water/ steam) metering, 
power/electrical distribution/power generation systems (include but not limited to photovoltaic, backup generator, 
microgrid, uninterruptible power supplies), other utility systems (central plant, water distribution, electrical 
distribution, sewer systems) and Electronic Security Systems (ESS), and security and/or force protection measures 
such as, but not limited to, barriers, fencing, gates, window treatments, hardening, and lighting.   
 
1.2 Background.  The U. S. Army Corps of Engineers Engineering & Support Center, Huntsville (CEHNC) 
maintains Centers of Expertise in UMCS and ESS.  As Centers of Expertise, CEHNC provides direct support to 
Government agencies for the P&I and M&S of UMCS and related systems as described above.  
 
1.3 Objectives.  The Contractor shall provide technical support, procurement, installation, monitoring, and M&S for 
UMCS, ESS and related systems.  These services include those actions required to preserve and maintain the 
systems in such a condition that they may be effectively used for their designated functional purpose.   
 
1.4 Scope.  This contract will require the Contractor to have the capability to respond to multiple requests 
simultaneously and to work at diverse locations.  The Contractor shall provide all engineering and services 
necessary for the P&I of new and/or upgrades to Direct Digital Control (DDC) systems, existing HVAC systems, 
SCADA systems, or other automated control systems on Government facilities.  This contract will require 
monitoring and control and M&S of control systems at Government facilities, munici palities and educational 
institutions to meet specific installation requirements.  The Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) will 
predominantly be services contracts, but some task orders may have construction and supply elements.  The task 
orders will include the necessary clauses, terms, conditions, instructions, and references for each of these work 
elements as applicable (services, construction, and supply). 
 
1.4.1  These services also include Preventive Maintenance (PM), Corrective Maintenance (CM), repair/ 
replacement/modernization, equipment inventories, condition assessments, identification and/or validation of 
problems and deficiencies, preparation of work plans describing method of correction/repair, actual execution of 
work plan to repair failed or failing systems and associated equipment, facility management support, project 
management, central monitoring services, minor construction work within or exter ior to a facility, development of 
PM plans, development of recommended spare parts lists, and other activities associated with operation, 
maintenance, and repair.  Facility maintenance/repair/renovation shall conform to the requirements of the Unified 
Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS) and Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) as per the Performance Work 
Statement (PWS) issued with each Task Order (TO) award, and/or other applicable codes and standards.  
 
1.4.2  Services will include, but are not limited to, developing of equipment installation engineering plans, providing 
hardware and software, providing system cybersecurity engineering and implementation, system testing and check-
out, performing facility modification and minor construction required to support equipment installation, providing 
technical solutions that incorporate applicable force protection measures, interfacing with and installing new data 
transmission equipment, determining compatibility of new equipment with existing systems and integrating them, 
preparing system and component documentation, providing operation and maintenance manuals, providing training, 
warranting systems, maintaining and servicing systems, retro-commissioning systems, operating and monitoring 

systems, preparing after action and other reports, providing as-built installation drawings, system evaluations, 
configuring/programming systems, system administration systems, provide inspections/functional 
tests/recommendations on control systems, and other technical and programmatic support services. 
 
1.5 Ordering Period.  This effort will be accomplished via individual TOs awarded under multiple Indefinite 
Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (ID/IQ) contracts that have an ordering period of seven years (36 month base period 
and two, 24 months option periods).  The Period of Performance (PoP) will be specified in each TO award.   
 
1.6 Service Contract Labor Standards. TOs from this contract may be issued which are subject to Service Contract 
Labor Standards (see Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 52.222-41). In the event that individual service task 
orders contain minor incidental work subject to the Construction Wage Rate Requirement (formerly known as the 
Davis-Bacon Act), Construction Wage Rate Requirements (RFO 52.222-6) will apply. The latest version of the 
wage determinations for the geographical areas in which the work is to be performed will be incorporated with the 
issuance of the TO solicitation. Wage determinations may also be found at www.wdol.gov .  TOs with performance 
in foreign countries will not be subject to either Service Contract Labor Standards or Construction Wage Rate 
Requirements. For work overseas not subject to Service Contract Labor Standards and Construction Wage Rate 
Requirements, the contractor shall comply with local labor laws in accordance with Defense Federal Acquisition 
Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 252.222-7002, Compliance with Local Labor Laws (Overseas) (DEVIATION 
2026-O0040). Additionally, Defense Base Act (DBA) insurance requirements will be included in TOs performed 
overseas, when required.   
 
1.7 General Requirements 
 
1.7.1 Quality Control Program (QCP).  The Contractor shall develop and maintain an effective quality control 
program to ensure services are performed in accordance with this PWS.  The Contractor shall develop and 
implement procedures to identify, prevent, and ensure non-recurrence of defective services.  The Contractor’s QCP 
is how he assures himself that his work complies with the requirements of the contract.  At a minimum, the 
contractor shall develop quality control procedures that address the areas identified in Appendix A, Performance 
Requirements Summary (PRS).   
 
1.7.1.1 Corporate Quality Control and Surveillance Plan.  Contractor shall develop, document, and implement an 
effective quality control and surveillance program for this contract and document in a plan.  The QC Plan shall be 
submitted within 30 calendar days after MATOC award and shall include at a minimum the following documents: 
Corporate QC Manager appointment letter, QC organizational structure (organization chart), inspection procedures, 
recordkeeping procedures, report templates, and any other information as required to describe the QC program.  At a 
minimum, the Contractor shall follow an inspection process (e.g. three phase inspection process (preparatory, initial, 
and follow-up) or other Government approved inspection methodology) and include sample forms to be filled out 
for each definable feature at the TO level.  After acceptance of the QC Plan, the Contractor shall submit any 
proposed changes to the Government, tracked through CMP/Quality Control System (QCS) for approval by the 
UMCS Program Manager or COR on the MATOC.   
 
1.7.1.2 Site Specific Quality Control Plan and Surveillance Plan.  A task/site specific quality control plan shall be 
developed/adapted to the services specified in individual TOs and submitted as required per TO.  The site-specific 
QC Plan shall include the following documents at a minimum: The QC Manager appointment letter (include duties 
and authorities at a minimum), summary of inspection procedures to be followed, sample inspection forms 
(preparatory, initial, follow-up) or other Government approved inspection methodology forms, and the list of 
definable features of work that the inspections will be based off.  The Government shall be provided a minimum of 
48-hour notification (based on workdays), unless otherwise specified at the TO level, of any inspection meetings.  
The Government is not required to be present but must be notified and given the opportunity to attend. It is the 
responsibility of the Contractor to maintain the inspection reports and to submit them to the Government via email 
within 5 days of completion.  Additional details may be included at the TO level. After acceptance of the QC Plan, 
the Contractor shall submit any proposed changes to the Government, tracked through CMP /QCS for approval by 
the COR on the TO.   
 
1.7.2 Quality Assurance (QA).  The Government will evaluate the contractor’s performance under this contract in 
accordance with the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) and will include an evaluation of the Contractor’s 

performance.  This plan is primarily focused on what the Government must do to ensure that the Contractor has 
performed in accordance with the performance standards.  It defines how the performance standards will be applied, 
the frequency of surveillance, and the minimum acceptable defect rate(s).  The Government may conduct QA 
inspections at any time on all phases and types of work performed.  If any Government QA review identifies a 
process/work product failure or identifies noncompliance with safety prac tices, the Contractor will be issued a 
Corrective Action Request (CAR).  Each CAR will be annotated as a critical nonconformance, major 
nonconformance, or minor nonconformance.  Definitions and required contractor response times are:   
 
* Critical Nonconformance:  a nonconformance that is likely to result in hazardous or unsafe conditions for 
individuals using, maintaining, or depending upon the supplies or services, or is likely to prevent performance of a 
vital agency mission.  Contractor is provided 24 hours (one business day) to provide written response to the CAR.  
 
* Major Nonconformance:  a nonconformance, other than critical, that is likely to result in failure of the supplies or 
services, or to materially reduce the usability of the supplies or services for their intended purpose. Contractor is 
provided 72 hours (three business days) to provide written response to the CAR. 
 
* Minor Nonconformance:  a nonconformance that is not likely to materially reduce the usability of the supplies or 
services for their intended purpose or is a departure from established standards having little bearing on the effective 
use or operation of the supplies or services.  Contractor is provided up to 15 business days to provide written 
response to the CAR. 
 
1.7.3 Government Remedies.  The KO shall follow 52.246-4, “Inspection of Services-Fixed Price” for contractor’s 
failure to perform satisfactory services or failure to correct non-conforming services. 
 
1.7.4 Place of Performance.  The Contractor is responsible for performing the services required under this contract at 
the location as specified in the individual TOs.  These UMCS services are required to support Department of 
Defense (DoD) installations or other Government facilities throughout the Continental United States, Alaska, 
Hawaii, and Outlying areas, as well as outside the Contiguous United States to include: Bahrain, Belgium, Brazil, 
Costa Rica, Ecuador, Gabon, Germany, Georgia, Greece, Haiti, India, Indonesia, Italy, Iraq, Jamaica, Japan, 
Kazakhstan, Kuwait, Malaysia, Mali, Montenegro, Norway, Poland, Republic of Korea, Romania, Saudi Arabia, 
Serbia, Suriname, Tanzania, United Arab Emirates,  and United Kingdom where controls systems are installed.  
Other foreign jurisdictions may be added to the geographic scope of the base MATOC contracts after preparing a 
Justification and Approval for an out-of-scope modification to add a country in accordance with RFO Part 6, 
Competition Requirements, for approval by the appropriate approving authority. This will include verification that 
all contractors within the MATOC award pool can comply with the applicable requirements for the country to be 
added. 
 
Work performed by the Contractor may be subject to other requirements or restrictions such as those issued by a 
U.S. Department of Defense theater-level Unified Combatant Commander (COCOM), e.g., U.S. Central Command 
(CENTCOM) requirements, which are provided under this contract. . 
 
Entry and exit requirements to countries within the CENTCOM AOR, including Iraq, are contained within DFARS  
252.225-7995, Contractor Personnel Performing in the United States Central Command Area of Responsibility 
(DEVIATION 2017-O0004), available at https://www.acq.osd.mil/dpap/policy/policyvault/Class_Deviation_2017-
O0004.pdf .   
 
Predeployment training requirements for Contractor personnel deploying to Iraq (and other countries as applicable)  
will be specified at the task order level.  
 
Access to bases and installations within Iraq (and other countries as applicable) will be subject to varying 
operational, security, and force protection conditions.  The Contractor shall coordinate with the CENTCOM (or 
other COCOM as applicable) Liaison Officer (LNO) for the status of such conditions for the bases and installations 
of interest.  Granting access to bases and installations within Iraq may take up to 30 calendar days following request 
or notification of intent to enter. 
 
1.7.5 Type of Contract.  TOs will be firm-fixed price. 

 
1.7.6 Security Requirements.  This contract may require the handling and generation of classified information.  
Security requirements appropriate for each TO will be delineated in the individual TOs.  Some TOs issued may 
require a security level of SECRET and some may require a higher level than SECRET.  The Contractor shall meet 
the Industrial Security requirements of the National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM) for

Performance Work Statement 
Strategic Quality Support System (SQSS) 
 
Background 
Fort Yuma Health Care Center (FYHCC) requires a comprehensive, web-based Strategic 
Quality Support System (SQSS) to support Accreditation Association for Ambulatory 
Health Care (AAAHC) accreditation readiness and ongoing healthcare quality management 
activities. 
The contractor shall provide a system capable of tracking, documenting, monitoring, and 
reporting accreditation and compliance-related activities across all required healthcare 
quality functions. The system shall support FYHCC’s operational need to manage 
accreditation tasks efficiently while reducing administrative burden on healthcare 
personnel. 
The contractor shall provide all software, system configuration, implementation support, 
maintenance, reporting, training, technical support, and related services necessary for 
successful operation of SQSS throughout the period of performance. 
 
Scope and Performance Requirements 
The contractor shall provide a secure, fully web-based Strategic Quality Support System 
(SQSS) that enables FYHCC personnel to manage accreditation, compliance, quality 
assurance, risk management, and performance improvement activities. 
The system shall: 
• Track and document up to 4,000–5,000 accreditation and compliance-related 
tasks; 
• Provide automated reminders, alerts, and notifications for due, overdue, and non-
compliant tasks; 
• Generate compliance, accreditation readiness, and performance reports; 
• Allow assignment and reassignment of tasks by department, role, and responsible 
staff member; 
• Support monitoring and trending of deficiencies and corrective actions; 

• Provide centralized access to policies, procedures, and supporting accreditation 
documentation; 
• Support all 16 major healthcare quality functions identified by FYHCC; 
• Be accessible to authorized staff through a secure web-based platform without 
requiring local installation; and 
• Maintain system availability, security, and technical support in accordance with this 
Performance Work Statement. 
The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, supervision, equipment, software, 
hosting, maintenance, and technical support necessary to perform the requirements of 
this contract. 
 
System Requirements 
Functional and Performance Requirements 
The contractor shall provide a Strategic Quality Support System (SQSS) that shall: 
1. Be designed to function within healthcare systems and manage activities across all 
sixteen (16) major quality functions in a typical healthcare organization, including: 
• Infection Control 
• Safety 
• Corporate Compliance 
• Utilization Management 
• Patient Clinical Management 
• Credentialing and Privileging 
• Peer Review 
• Performance Evaluation 
• Orientation 
• Continuing Education 
• Patient Complaint Management 
• HIPAA Compliance 
• Pharmacy and Therapeutics 
• Service Recovery 
• Patient Satisfaction 
• Patient Advocacy 
2. Track between 4,000 and 5,000 accreditation and compliance-related tasks. 

3. Provide daily task or “to-do” lists for staff to identify required activities, due dates, 
and pending actions. 
4. Send automated messages, reminders, and alerts for tasks that are due, overdue, 
incomplete, or non-compliant. 
5. Provide task instruction fields detailing procedures necessary to complete tasks in 
accordance with accreditation and regulatory standards. 
6. Be accessible to authorized staff members across all departments. 
7. Be fully web-based and contractor-hosted, eliminating the need for local 
installation or routine technical support by the Service Unit IT department. 
8. Allow real-time uploading and documentation of task completion activities and 
generation of compliance reports. 
9. Create and assign tasks to individual staff members, groups, departments, or 
functional areas. 
10. Support assignment of primary and secondary responsible individuals and allow 
reassignment or transfer of tasks when staff are absent or leave the Service Unit. 
11. Allow flexibility in scheduling tasks by frequency, interval, department, shift, 
recurring cycle, or rotating staff assignment. 
12. Enable transfer of task completion, validation, and oversight responsibilities 
without loss of historical documentation. 
13. Provide readily retrievable compliance reports sortable by individual, department, 
task, accreditation function, or reporting category. 
14. Display trends, dashboards, graphs, metrics, and outlier analyses for identification 
of deficiencies and targeting of corrective actions. 
15. Provide readily accessible and knowledgeable technical support. 
Required System Features 
The system shall: 
1. Upload documents and supporting materials to provide a centralized location for 
accreditation-related records and activities. 
2. Upload links to training resources, policies, procedures, websites, and reference 
materials necessary for task completion. 
3. Graph data and visually display trends, metrics, dashboards, and other 
performance activities. 

4. Encrypt patient-specific and sensitive information in accordance with HIPAA, HHS, 
and Federal cybersecurity requirements. 
5. Create spontaneous or ad hoc quality improvement initiatives related to existing 
tasks or as stand-alone projects. 
Reporting Requirements 
The contractor shall provide monthly compliance and accreditation readiness reports 
summarizing: 
• Task completion rates; 
• Overdue items; 
• Compliance trends and identified deficiencies; 
• Corrective actions taken or pending; 
• Department-level performance metrics; and 
• Performance and compliance status by responsible staff member. 
Reports shall be exportable in PDF and Microsoft Excel formats and shall be available to 
authorized Government personnel upon request. 
 
Service Level Requirements 
1. System uptime shall be at least 99% excluding scheduled maintenance periods. 
2. Contractor shall provide at least seventy-two (72) hours advance notice to the 
Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) for any scheduled system outages or 
maintenance activities expected to impact system availability. 
3. Contractor shall maintain technical support processes sufficient to address system 
outages, user access issues, and critical functionality failures in a timely manner. 
 
Data Ownership and Security Requirements 
1. All data entered into the Strategic Quality Support System (SQSS) shall remain the 
sole property of the Government. 
2. Contractor shall comply with all applicable Health Insurance Portability and 
Accountability Act (HIPAA), Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), 
Indian Health Service (IHS), and Federal cybersecurity and privacy requirements. 
3. Contractor shall implement appropriate administrative, technical, and physical 
safeguards to protect Government information and prevent unauthorized access, 
disclosure, alteration, or destruction of data. 

4. Contractor shall notify the COR within twenty-four (24) hours of discovery of any 
suspected or confirmed data breach, cybersecurity incident, or unauthorized 
access involving Government data. 
5. Contractor shall not use, disclose, distribute, or retain Government data except as 
required for performance of this contract. 
 
Period of Performance 
The period of performance shall consist of: 
• One (1) twelve-month base year; and 
• Four (4) twelve-month option years. 
The contract shall include: 
1. An implementation and configuration period beginning at contract award and 
continuing through successful system deployment and validation. 
2. A recurring services period for ongoing system access, technical support, 
maintenance, updates, reporting, and training support throughout the duration of 
the contract.

Transition and Offboarding Requirements 
Upon expiration, termination, or non-renewal of the contract, the contractor shall: 
1. Provide all Government-owned data in a mutually agreed-upon electronic format 
within thirty (30) calendar days. 
2. Assist with transition activities necessary to support migration of data to the 
Government or a successor contractor. 
3. Ensure all Government data remaining in contractor-controlled systems is securely 
removed or destroyed in accordance with applicable Federal records management 
and cybersecurity requirements after written Government confirmation of 
successful transfer. 
4. Provide documentation necessary to support continuity of operations and system 
transition activities. 
 
 
System Acceptance 
Final system acceptance shall occur after: 
• Successful implementation and configuration of required functionality; 
• Validation by the COR that all required quality functions are operational; 
• Completion of user training; 
• Demonstration of required reporting capabilities; and 
• Resolution of critical system deficiencies identified during testing. 

The Government reserves the right to require correction of deficiencies prior to final 
acceptance.

Solicitation Notice 
Solicitation No. PHX-SS-26-010 
Strategic Quality Support System (SQSS) 
Indian Health Service 
Fort Yuma Health Care Center 
Winterhaven, California 92283
Commercial Acquisition – RFO Part 12 
The Indian Health Service (IHS), Phoenix Area Office, intends to award a commercial 
purchase order to D.D. Bainbridge & Associates, Inc. for the Strategic Quality Support 
System (SQSS) in support of Accreditation Association for Ambulatory Health Care 
(AAAHC) accreditation activities at Fort Yuma Health Care Center. 
This acquisition is conducted in accordance with RFO 12.102(a), Restricting 
Competition, based on the Government's determination that only one responsible source 
is available to satisfy the Government's requirement. 
This notice is not intended to re-open market research. Rather, it provides one final 
opportunity for any responsible source capable of furnishing the proprietary Strategic 
Quality Support System (SQSS) to identify itself prior to award. 
Description of Requirement 
The contractor shall provide the proprietary Strategic Quality Support System (SQSS), 
including software licensing, implementation support, system configuration, training, 
maintenance, technical support, software updates, and related services in accordance 
with the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS). 
The anticipated period of performance consists of: 
• One (1) 12-month Base Period
• Four (4) 12-month Option Periods
NAICS: 541512 – Computer Systems Design Services 
PSC: DA10 – IT and Telecom – Business Application/Application Development Software as 
a Service 
Restriction of Competition 

The Government conducted market research, including the issuance of Sources Sought 
Notice SS-26-PHX-025, and evaluated all responses received. Based on the market 
research conducted, the Government determined that D.D. Bainbridge & Associates, Inc. 
is the only responsible source capable of providing the proprietary Strategic Quality 
Support System (SQSS). 
Competition is restricted because no other source demonstrated the authority to furnish, 
license, implement, maintain, or support the proprietary SQSS platform. 
Response Instructions 
All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, quotation, or other information 
demonstrating their ability to satisfy the Government's requirement. 
Responses shall specifically demonstrate: 
• Authority to provide the proprietary Strategic Quality Support System (SQSS);
• Authorization to license, implement, maintain, and support SQSS if the respondent
is not the software owner;
• Capability to satisfy the requirements identified in the attached Performance Work
Statement.
Responses proposing alternative software products or equivalent solutions will be 
evaluated solely to determine whether the Government's decision to restrict competition 
should be reconsidered. 
Responses shall be submitted electronically to: 
Dekovan Cook 
Contract Specialist 
Indian Health Service 
Phoenix Area Office of Acquisition Management 
Email: dekovan.cook@ihs.gov 
Response Due Date: July 24, 2026 
Time: 2:00 PM Arizona Time

COMFRC Mission

Scope & Requirement Background

The Commander, Fleet Readiness Centers (COMFRC), Digital Group, Aviation Product Lifecycle Management (AvPLM) program requires software maintenance and engineering support for a set of Anark Core Server (ACS) and Anark Core Workstation (ACW) software applications, for use in the AvPLM environment

This Statement of Work (SOW) defines the procurement of maintenance and support for software products used in the AvPLM capability to generate 3D Portable Document Format (PDF) files from Computer Aided Drawing (CAD) models and associated data files.  This SOW also includes an option to procure professional service hours to support AvPLM integration activities related to Anark tools.  This effort is part of the Additive Manufacturing/Digital Thread (AM/DT) software environment project, which comprises a set of tools used to develop, validate, configure, and manage 3D Computer-Aided-Design (CAD) models and associated data for additive manufacturing projects.
