Performance Work Statement (PWS) for PMA-273 / CNATRA

Predictive Business and Technical Decision Analysis Services for

Naval Undergraduate Flight Training Systems Total Lifecycle Management


Date: 21 July 2026

1.0 INTRODUCTION AND SCOPE

1.1 Introduction

The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) PMA-273, in partnership with the Chief of Naval Air Training (CNATRA), requires Contractor support for the development, integration, sustainment, and modernization of data-driven readiness tools. These tools will enhance training, resource management, and operational decision-making across CNATRA and Navy Fleet Replacement Squadrons (FRS). This PWS defines the requirements for technical, programmatic, and security support to ensure the effective delivery and ongoing support of these tools and associated systems.

1.2 Scope

This PWS covers all activities necessary to design, develop, integrate, test, deploy, and sustain data-driven readiness tools and support infrastructure for PMA-273 and CNATRA, specifically for readiness tools including Lone Star TruNavigator® MAX platform tools; Platform Utilization and Logistics Status Enterprise (PULSE), Lifecycle Enhanced Asset Decision Software (LEADS), CNATRA Enterprise Model (CEM), Property Management module, Manning Model and modules that will integrate with these systems. The Contractor shall provide technical expertise, program management, cybersecurity, training, and documentation to ensure the effective delivery and ongoing support of these tools. The scope includes, but is not limited to, software development, data integration, cloud migration, system modernization, user support, configuration management, and compliance with all applicable DoD and Navy standards.

2.0 APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS

The following documents, in their latest versions, are applicable to this PWS and are incorporated by reference:

Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS)

Department of Defense (DoD) Directives and Instructions (e.g., DoDI 8500.01, DoDI 8140)

Department of War (DoW) Cloud Computing Security Requirements Guides (SRG)

DoD CSP SRG v1r1 – Security requirements for CSPs providing cloud services to DoD mission owners.

DoD Mission Owner (MO) SRG – Technical requirements for the organization using the CSP’s service.

NIST Special Publications (SP) 800-53, 800-171

3.0 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall conduct all general requirements with each of the individual Task Orders (TOs).

3.1 Data Integration and Interoperability within the War Data Platform (WDP)

The Contractor shall ensure seamless integration of all relevant data sources into the WDP, enabling interoperability between CNATRA, FRS, and other Navy systems. This includes developing and maintaining data pipelines and data transformation processes to support real-time and batch data exchange. The Contractor will ensure data consistency, accuracy, and availability across all platforms.

3.2 Cloud-Based Systems

The Contractor shall design, implement, and maintain cloud-based solutions for hosting, processing, and analyzing readiness data. All cloud services must comply with Department of War (DoW) Cloud Computing Security Requirements Guides (SRG) and be hosted in authorized environments (e.g., AWS GovCloud, Azure Government). The Contractor will support cloud migration, scalability, and disaster recovery planning.

3.3 Configuration Management

The Contractor shall establish and maintain configuration management processes for all software, hardware, and documentation. This includes tracking changes, maintaining baselines, and ensuring traceability throughout the system lifecycle. The Contractor shall have documentation available for Government audit summarizing configuration items, change requests, version control activity, audit results, and recommendations.

3.3.1 Data Repository Management

The Contractor shall maintain data repositories for all systems (e.g., LEADS, CEM, WDP) to ensure data integrity and security. Routine backups will be implemented to avoid data loss.

3.3.2 Version Control

The Contractor shall adhere to strict version control protocols to prevent conflicts during software updates or system enhancements.

3.4 Program Management

The Contractor shall provide comprehensive program management support, including project planning, scheduling, risk management, resource allocation, and regular Program Status Reports (CDRL A001). The Contractor will coordinate with government stakeholders to ensure timely delivery of all requirements and deliverables. The Contractor shall attend an annual PMR at the Program Office to review all task orders and path forward. 

3.5 Government Furnished Property (GFP)

The Contractor shall manage any assigned Government Furnished Property in accordance with FAR 52.245-1 and DFARS 252.245-7005. This includes tracking, safeguarding, and returning all GFP at contract completion or as directed by the Government.

3.6 Quality Assurance and Acceptance

The Contractor shall implement a robust quality assurance program to ensure all deliverables meet or exceed contract requirements. The Government will review and accept deliverables based on predefined acceptance criteria. Specific acceptable quality levels (AQLs) and performance metrics will be defined in a Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) attached to each individual Task Order. Payment under Firm Fixed Price Task Orders is contingent upon meeting these established AQLs.

3.7 Compliance with Standards

The Contractor shall ensure all work complies with applicable federal, DoD, and Navy standards, including software development, cybersecurity, and data management best practices.

3.8 Security and Data Protection

The Contractor shall implement and maintain a comprehensive security program to ensure the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of all data, software, models, and systems managed under this contract. All security measures shall comply with DoW directives, Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS), and Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Level 2 (Self-Assessment).

3.8.1 Security Management

The Contractor shall maintain secure facilities and physical access controls in accordance with DoD standards. All personnel with access to CUI or classified information shall have appropriate clearances and complete DoW-mandated security training. The Contractor shall appoint a Facility Security Officer (FSO) to oversee compliance, training, and serve as liaison to the Government.

3.8.2 Risk, Vulnerability, and Incident Management

The Contractor shall establish and maintain a Risk Management Plan, conduct regular risk assessments, and address emerging threats. Continuous vulnerability management, including regular audits, scans, and prompt remediation, is required. The Contractor shall implement and maintain an Incident Response Plan (IRP) in accordance with NIST SP 800-171 and DoD requirements. The IRP must include immediate containment and mitigation of incidents, notification to the Government within 72 hours per DFARS 252.204-7012, and support for forensic analysis, root cause determination, and lessons learned.

3.9 Travel

Local and long-distance travel in performance of an individual task order. Costs associated with travel and lodging shall be reimbursed in accordance with the Joint Travel Regulation (JTR) and with NAVAIR clause 5252.232-9509 Reimbursement of Travel, Per Diem, and Special Material Costs.

3.10 Material

The Contractor shall provide material in accordance with individual task orders. The contractor shall provide all support data, and cost estimates necessary to justify a fair and reasonable price per item procured. The Contractor shall have adequate accounting and inventory systems to track all items and the acquisition status per task order and per item. Prior to material procurement, the contractor shall include a detailed list of all equipment and/or material needed for each task order. All material associated with this contract that is provided by the contractor shall become the property of the Federal Government.

4.0 PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS

4.1 Performance Requirements Summary

The Contractor shall conduct only the performance requirements specified in individual TOs. A summary of the performance requirement will be provided in each individual TO.

4.2 Support and Maintenance

4.2.1 Licensing

The Contractor shall procure, manage, and maintain all necessary software licenses required for the operation and support of readiness tools and systems. All licenses must be compliant with DoW and Navy policies and be available for government audit upon request. The Contractor shall provide a License Management Report (CDRL A002).

4.2.2 Seat Maintenance

The Contractor shall provide ongoing maintenance and support for all user seats, including provisioning, deprovisioning, and troubleshooting user access issues. The Contractor will ensure that all users have uninterrupted access to required systems and tools.

4.2.3 System Maintenance, Updates, Patches and Inspections

The Contractor shall perform regular system maintenance, including applying software updates, security patches, and conducting routine inspections to ensure optimal performance and security. Maintenance activities shall be scheduled to minimize operational disruptions. The Contractor shall deliver a maintenance and update schedule as a part of the Program Status Reports (CDRL A001).

4.2.4 Enhancements and Modifications

The Contractor shall implement system enhancements and modifications as directed by the Government. This includes developing new features, improving existing functionality, and adapting systems to evolving requirements.

4.2.5 User Support

The Contractor shall deliver user manuals and change documentation (CDRL A003). 

The Contractor shall provide Tier 1 and Tier 2 Help Desk support. Individual Task Orders will specify the volume of users, required hours of coverage, and required ticket resolution times (e.g., 90% of critical tickets resolved within 4 hours).  Support shall be available during normal business hours, with procedures in place for handling urgent issues outside of standard hours.

4.3 Development and Delivery of Future Simulations, Models, and Modules

4.3.1 Predictive Models and Simulations Development

The Contractor shall design and produce advanced predictive tools capable of analyzing, simulating, and forecasting mission readiness, resource allocation, and training optimization metrics to support CNATRA and FRS operations.

4.3.2 Scenario-Based Simulations

The Contractor shall develop situation and scenario-driven models that simulate training schedules, resource constraints, fleet readiness, and operational risks. These models shall be flexible for analyzing "what-if" scenarios critical for decision-making.

4.3.3 Business Case and Cost/ Benefit Modeling 

The Contactor shall provide task, project and program level modeling of complex business case analysis with the capability to deliver outcomes and supporting rationale for probable cost and return, sensitivity, risk and other critical decision Key Performance Parameters (KPPs). 

4.3.4 Total Ownership Cost Modeling

The Contactor shall model the Total Ownership Cost (TOC) of individual products/assets, systems, system of systems, tasks, projects and programs to deliver insight into the multi- organizational impact of the TOC as well as the impact on, and requirement for, different financial allocations

4.3.5 Manning Models

The Contractor shall produce customized manning models to forecast workforce and personnel requirements. The Contractor shall optimize operational or maintenance personnel deployment across CNATRA and FRS operations.

4.3.6 Performance and Gaming Simulations

The Contractor shall develop interactive and performance-oriented gaming simulations aimed at improving operational readiness, testing new strategies, and supporting decision-making under practical constraints.

4.3.7 Interoperability and Modernization

The Contractor shall ensure all new tools are fully interoperable with existing systems (e.g. CEM, Manning Model, LEADS, PULSE, and others). The Contractor shall utilize advanced technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) for enhanced automation, analytical capabilities, and scalability. The Contractor shall design all systems with cloud-based compatibility and emphasize modularity for future growth and upgrades. 

4.3.8 Development of Data Modules

The Contractor shall produce data modules to support new PMA-273, CNATRA, and FRS requirements. Data modules refer to, but are not limited to, technical manuals/publications, logistics data, and engineering data.

4.3.9 Data Analytics and Reporting

The Contractor shall develop and implement advanced data analytics and reporting capabilities to support decision-making at all organizational levels. This includes creating dashboards, automated reports, and data visualization tools tailored to CNATRA and FRS operational needs. The Contractor shall ensure that analytics solutions are user-friendly, secure, and capable of integrating with existing and future systems.

4.3.10 Primary Data Collection

The Contractor shall provide primary and secondary data collection capabilities, including surveys, benchmarking, interviews, focus groups, and third-party data reviews, as required to develop and validate the business and technical analysis, modeling, or simulation requirements.

4.4 Training and Knowledge Transfer

The Contractor shall provide comprehensive training and knowledge transfer to government personnel and end users. This includes developing and delivering training materials (CDRL A004), conducting instructor-led and virtual training sessions, and providing ongoing support to ensure users are proficient in all delivered tools and systems. Additionally, the Contractor shall deliver a Data Accession List (DAL) (CDRL A005).

4.5 Cybersecurity Plan

For Cybersecurity requirements see the Cybersecurity Plan (CSP), Attachment X. Specific mentioned policies in the CS Plan can be accessed via the Cybersecurity Policy Chart at the following link: https://www.dtic.mil/document;accessionNumber=AD1128710;type=IAC;searchText=policy%20chart

The Contractor shall be required to deliver a Program Cybersecurity Implementation Plan (CSIP) or Annex CSIP to address each of the sections of the Cybersecurity Plan (CSP). The contractor shall demonstrate its understanding of the CSP and describe how the requirement of each of the sections of the CSP will be achieved by the contractor. Sections of the CSP that are NOT applicable are required to be addressed.

The contractor shall describe why a particular section is not applicable. The final Program CSIP shall be in Adobe Acrobat format w

SECTION C: PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT 
 
C.1 BACKGROUND 
 
The U.S. Census Bureau (USCB) serves as the leading source of quality data about the nation’s 
people and economy. It is the largest statistical agency in the United States. The USCB’s mission 
is built around large-scale surveys and censuses. It collects, tabulates, and disseminates a large 
volume and wide variety of statistics about the people, housing, and economy of the U.S. These 
statistics provide basic yardsticks needed to measure, understand, anticipate, and respond to 
changes to the U.S. economy and American society. 
 
The Census Bureau conducts research and production work using administrative records data to 
enhance numerous Census Bureau programs and products, as well as to facilitate surveys the 
Census Bureau conducts on behalf of other agencies on a reimbursable basis.  The Census 
Bureau enters into agreements with data providers, including federal, state, and private entities, 
to acquire data files.  These data are used to support the Census Bureau’s work authorized by 
Title 13 of the United States Code, which includes planning and conducting future decennial 
censuses, current surveys such as the American Community Survey (ACS), other Census Bureau 
demographic and economic research and production work.  These data are also used to support 
the reimbursable surveys the Census Bureau conducts for other federal agencies.  Such surveys 
are authorized by other parts of the U.S. Code, including Titles 12, 20, 34 and 42.   The Census 
Bureau will use the data acquired in the contract to continue to carry out the aforementioned 
production work that is underway as well as continue research to find new uses for the data 
obtained.   
 
In support of the USCB’s mission, the Commercial Data Acquisition Team (CDAT) is 
responsible for acquiring and maintaining a broad range of administrative records datasets, with 
the express purpose of enhancing the value of data from household surveys and censuses, 
resulting in reduction of respondent burden, validation and data collection costs.  In addition, the 
USCB is assessing the capability of these data products to accurately predict, and potentially 
correct for, nonresponse in our demographic surveys and censuses.    
 
C.2 PURPOSE AND SCOPE 
 
The purpose of this contract is to acquire commercial data file(s) for all 50 U.S. States and 
Washington, D.C.  The submitted data file(s) shall include the following core data elements: 
Address, Resident Information, and Contact Information.

vintage information for each commercial data file delivered to the Census Bureau.  All 
commercial data files shall be delivered in ACSII format.  The contractor shall deliver to 
the Census Bureau via secure file transfer protocol on an agreed-to schedule.

Statement of Work 
Implementation of Q-Flow Customer Journey Management System 
Crownpoint Service Unit, Indian Health Service 
1. Purpose 
This Statement of Work (SOW) outlines the implementation of a patient flow and queue 
management system across the Crownpoint Healthcare Facility Pharmacy Department and 
associated service areas. The implementation aims to improve operational efficiency, 
patient access, service coordination, and patient experience through virtual queuing, 
appointment management, and real-time communication technologies. 
 
The contractor shall furnish all labor, software, hardware, licenses, project management, 
technical documentation, installation services, configuration services, testing, training, and 
warranty support necessary to deliver a fully operational patient flow management 
solution. 
 
The contractor shall demonstrate that the proposed patient flow and queue management 
system has been successfully implemented within other Indian Health Service (IHS) 
facilities. The contractor shall provide evidence of prior implementation, operational 
performance, and customer references. 
 
The proposed solution shall provide reliable real-time queue management, digital signage, 
patient notifications, reporting, audit logging, role-based access control, and secure 
administration. The solution shall operate as a standalone application within the 
Crownpoint Healthcare Facility network and shall not require interfaces with the Electronic 
Health Record (EHR), pharmacy information systems, or other clinical applications unless 
authorized by the Government through a future contract modification. 
 
Additionally, the system shall comply with applicable federal cybersecurity requirements 
and be capable of operating within an environment requiring an Authorization to Operate 
(ATO). 
2. System Configuration and Connectivity 
The contractor shall configure the system to support virtual queuing, appointment 
management, patient notifications, reporting, administrative dashboards, audit logging, and 
role-based user access. The contractor shall configure all kiosks, digital signage, queue 
definitions, notification templates, service categories, and administrative settings. 
 
The contractor shall coordinate with IHS Information Technology personnel to ensure 
compliance with applicable network security requirements, including firewall policies, 
VLAN configuration, user authentication, and encrypted communications. Any required 

network ports or IP addresses shall be documented prior to implementation. The solution 
shall not require connectivity to external clinical systems to perform its intended functions. 
3. Services Provided 
The contractor shall provide project management, system design, workflow configuration, 
equipment delivery, installation, software configuration, functional testing, user acceptance 
testing (UAT), staff training, technical documentation, warranty support, and post-
implementation technical assistance. The contractor shall validate that all hardware and 
software components are functioning according to manufacturer specifications prior to 
Government acceptance. 
4 Standalone System Deployment 
The contractor shall deploy the patient flow and queue management system as a standalone 
application operating within the Crownpoint Healthcare Facility network. The system shall 
support patient check-in, virtual queuing, appointment scheduling, queue monitoring, 
digital signage, patient notifications, reporting, and administrative functions without 
requiring interfaces to Electronic Health Record (EHR), pharmacy management systems, or 
other clinical applications. 
 
The contractor shall perform installation verification, operational testing, failover testing 
where applicable, and user acceptance testing before production deployment. All identified 
deficiencies shall be corrected by the contractor prior to Government acceptance. The 
deployed solution shall maintain data integrity, system security, and a minimum 
operational availability of 99.5% during normal business hours, excluding approved 
maintenance windows. 
5. Vendor Selection: 
The Government requires a patient flow and customer journey management solution that 
has been successfully implemented in healthcare environments comparable to Indian 
Health Service facilities. The proposed solution shall have a demonstrated history of 
supporting pharmacy operations, including patient check-in, virtual queuing, queue 
management, patient notifications, and reporting capabilities. 
Offerors shall provide evidence of successful deployments in healthcare organizations of 
similar size and complexity, including references that demonstrate successful 
implementation, operational performance, and user adoption. Preference may be given to 
solutions with demonstrated experience within Indian Health Service due to the reduced 
implementation risk and familiarity with federal operational requirements.

Solicitation Number:  9594OIT260064 
Title:  Specialized Cybersecurity, Privacy Engineering, and Continuous Authorization  
 Support Services 
 
1. General Information. 
• Document Type: Special Notice (Notice of Intent to Sole Source) 
• NAICS Code: 541519 – Other Computer Related Services 
• Product Service Code (PSC): DJ01 – IT And Telecom - Security And Compliance 
Support Services 
 
2. Description of the Requirement. 
 
 a. The Court Services and Offender Supervision Agency (CSOSA) intends to award a sole-
source, purchase order to Business Operational Concepts, LLC, a certified Women-Owned Small 
Business (WOSB). The Contractor will provide expert, multi-disciplinary cybersecurity, privacy 
engineering, and program management services. 
 
 b. The scope of work requires the immediate deployment of qualified personnel to support a 
portfolio of forty-five (45) enterprise information systems transitioning to a continuous 
authorization model. Key technical drivers of this requirement include: 
 
• Engineering, configuration, and operational deployment of continuous monitoring 
workflows utilizing the agency’s mandatory Caveonix Governance, Risk, and 
Compliance (GRC) platform. 
 
• The development and execution of an enterprise migration strategy for full compliance 
with NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0 standards. 
 
• Authoring and implementing an agency-wide AI Threat Strategic Plan and Playbook in 
strict alignment with Executive Order 14110.  
 
• The ongoing execution of complex Privacy Threshold Analyses (PTAs), Privacy Impact 
Assessments (PIAs), and annual FISMA audit preparation activities. 
 
3. Statutory Authority. The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition 
for this acquisition is Section 8(m) of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 637(m)), as 
implemented by FAR 6.302-5(b)(7) ("Sole source awards under the Women-Owned Small 
Business (WOSB) Program") and FAR 19.1506. The applicable NAICS code is 541519, which 
is formally designated by the Small Business Administration (SBA) as an industry substantially 
underrepresented by WOSB concerns. 
 
4. Justification for Sole Source. Business Operational Concepts, LLC is uniquely qualified to 
execute this highly technical scope of work without introducing unacceptable operational gaps, 
data vulnerabilities, or transition delays to the agency’s 45 systems. The Contractor possesses 
specialized, proven corporate past  performance transitioning organizations from the Static 3-

year ATO model to Continuous ATO model using Governance, Risk and Compliance tools such 
as Cavenoix, etc. within federal environments and maintains an immediate pipeline of certified 
Key Personnel holding required combinations of PMP, PMI-ACP, and advanced security/agile 
certifications. 
 
5. Response Instructions.  
 
 a. This notice is not a request for competitive proposals. However, interested, SBA-certified 
WOSB concerns that believe they can fully meet the specialized technical requirements 
described above may submit the following: 
 
  (1) Active SBA certification as a WOSB in SAM.gov under NAICS 541519 
 
  (2) At least one project demonstrating corporate experience engineering and managing the 
following: 
 
   (a) Security authorizations via tools such as Caveonix GRC platform. 
 
   (b) Authoring federal enterprise strategies for NIST CSF 2.0 migration and AI framework 
implementation. 
 
   (c) Delivery of ATO packages for multiple systems (minimum 15) within a 12 month 
period. 
 
   (d) Immediate corporate capacity to staff qualified personnel meeting the following 
education, experience, and certifications (provide resumes showing capability): 
 
    (i) Program Manager with the following certifications and qualifications: 
 
• ITIL v4 Foundations; 
• Project Management Professional (PMP); 
• PMI-ACP Certified; 
• SAFe Product Owner/Product Manager; 
• Certified SAFe Scrum Master; and 
• Certified SAFe Agilist. 
• Minimum of seven (7) years of progressive project/program management 
experience supporting federal cybersecurity or IT modernization efforts; 
• Demonstrated experience managing multi-disciplinary teams in a federal 
environment, preferably supporting ISSO/RMF/ATO activities; and  
• Strong knowledge of FISMA, NIST RMF, NIST SP 800-53, CSF 2.0, and 
federal compliance reporting. 
 

     (ii) At least four Information System Security Officers (ISSOs) with the following 
certifications and qualifications: 
 
• (ISC)² CISSP; 
• Certified Information Security Manager (CISM); and 
• Certified Information Security Auditor (CISA). 
• Minimum of five (5) years of hands-on experience performing ISSO or 
equivalent functions in a federal environment;  
• Demonstrated experience developing and maintaining SSPs, SARs, POA&Ms, 
SIAs, and supporting ATOs under the NIST RMF; and 
• Experience with continuous monitoring, vulnerability management, risk 
assessments, and privacy compliance (PTA/PIA). 
 
  (3) The submitted project must include the following information: 
 
• Title; 
• Description how the submitted projected aligns with all elements identified in 
5.a(2) above; 
• Period of performance; 
• Value; 
• Client reference information. 
 
 b. The above information must be submitted electronically via email to 
catherine.collins@csosa.gov no later than August 5, 2026. All responses must be in writing. 
Telephone requests/information will not be considered. 
 
 c. This notice is not a request for competitive proposals; however, the Government will 
consider all responses received by the response date stated above. A determination by the 
Government not to compete this acquisition is solely within the discretion of the Government.

20002-4260.

SPECIAL NOTICE 
 
Subject: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT 
 
NAICS Code: 518210 Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, and Web Hosting. 
PSC: 7C20 it and telecom - data center products (hardware and perpetual license software). 
Solicitation: N00244-26-Q-0057 
 
This action is being conducted in accordance with FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial 
Products and Commercial Services. Pursuant to FAR 12.102(a), the Government has 
documented its decision that only one responsible source is available to satisfy the agency's 
requirements and that no other supplies or services will suffice. 
 
Description: 
 
NAVSUP Fleet Logistics Center San Diego (FLCSD) intends to award a commercial Sole 
Source contract to Quartermaster AI, Inc. (CAGE Code: 9K6Q6, UEI: HCFJASF32YV3).  
 
This requirement is for the procurement of a 12-month commercial subscription-based Data-as-
a-Service (DaaS) model for the SmartMast Maritime Sensor system, to be installed onboard the 
Medium Unmanned Surface Vessel (MUSV) "Sea Hunter" in support of Unmanned Surface 
Vessel Squadron One (USVRON-1) and Carrier Strike Group One (CSG-1) pre-deployment 
work-ups, training, and operational missions. The requirement also includes a 5-month optional 
subscription extension and custom software engineering services to integrate the proprietary 
SmartMast sensor data streams directly into the Navy's Minotaur C2 architecture. 
 
The contractor shall provide all hardware installation, satellite data transmission, secure web 
portal access, programmatic API delivery, training, and subsequent hardware retrieval as defined 
in the Requirements Statement. 
 
The Quartermaster AI SmartMast is a highly specialized, proprietary sensor platform that fuses 
EO/IR cameras, AIS, and RF detection with onboard edge-AI processing (Automated Target 
Recognition). Due to its proprietary software code, API architecture and existing pre-approved 
integration with the Minotaur ecosystem, Quartermaster AI, Inc. is the sole developer and 
intellectual property owner of this technology. It represents the only source capable of 
completing the mandatory installation and integration by the critical threshold date of August 10, 
2026, to support scheduled fleet operations. 
 
 
This Notice of Intent is not a request for competitive quotes or proposals. However, responsible 
sources may identify their interest and submit a capability statement in response to this notice. 
Capability statements must be submitted by July 27, 2026, 08:00 a.m. PST via email to 
yesica.l.burrill.civ@us.navy.mil, and will be considered by the agency. Information received will 
be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive 
procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based 
upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

The requested software license is a direct replacement and renewal of the LowTrack software currentlyin use at eleven Naval Nuclear Propulsion Program (NNPP) sites. LowTrack provides essentialfunctionality for inventory management, generation, and electronic transfer of the Nuclear RegulatoryCommission Uniform Low - Level Radioactive Waste Manifest, and is exclusively licensed by the Departmentof Energy to execute shipments of mixed waste and low - level radioactive waste for off - site treatmentand disposal. Continued use of LowTrack is required to maintain continuity of operations across allNNPP sites, ensure compatibility with existing NNPP equipment, and meet regulatory deadlines,environmental laws, and state permit requirements. Market research has shown that LowTrack is the onlyvendor that can provide the required software at a reasonable rate; while other vendors offerlogistics software, their pricing is approximately ten times higher and does not align with NNPP’soperational or regulatory requirements. Performance Work Statement (PWS): Enterprise Skills Assessment Platform:

1.  Introduction and Background. 

     a.  Mission Objective: The United States Army Special Operations Command (USASOC), hereafter referred to as "the Government," requires an existing, commercially available, subscription-based Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution to systematically assess, measure, and guide the upskilling of its technical workforce. The primary objective is to enhance mission readiness by identifying and closing skill gaps in critical domains such as coding, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Data Engineering, Cybersecurity, and Software Development. This PWS defines the performance outcomes required to achieve this objective.

     b.  Scope: The Contractor shall provide the platform, including all necessary licenses, technical support, and reporting to meet the performance standards outlined herein. The scope includes platform provisioning, user onboarding, role-based skills assessment, data analytics, and ongoing technical support for 500 users.

     c.  Period of Performance (PoP): The PoP shall be for one Base Year of 12 months.

          (1)  Base Period: 15 July 2026 to 14 July 2027

2.  Definitions and Acronyms.  A complete list of definitions and acronyms will be included in Appendix 1.

     a.  AQL: Acceptable Quality Level

     b.  COR: Contracting Officer's Representative

     c.  DoW: Department of War

     d.  PII: Personally Identifiable Information

      e.  PRS: Performance Requirements Summary

     f.  PWS: Performance Work Statement

     g.  QASP: Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan

     h.  Skill Circuit: A tailored assessment path for a specific job role or technical domain within the platform.

3.  Government Furnished Property, Material, Equipment and Services

     a.  Government Furnished Services: The Government will provide access to necessary points of contact (POCs) for technical coordination and subject matter experts (SMEs) for the Skill Circuit customization task. 

     b.  Government Furnished Equipment: No Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) will be provided.

4. Contractor Requirements.  Tasks and Performance Objectives: 

     a.  Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) and Performance Requirements Summary (PRS).  The Contractor is responsible for delivering the outcomes defined in the table below. The Government will measure performance against these standards in accordance with the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP).

     b.  Specific Tasks

          (1)  Task 1: Platform Provisioning and Onboarding. The Contractor shall initialize the Government's enterprise tenant, configure it with 500 licenses, and provide administrative accounts to designated Government POCs. The Contractor shall also deliver user onboarding guides and training materials.

          (2)  Task 2: Skill Circuit Customization. The Contractor shall collaborate with Government SMEs to review and calibrate the following initial Skill Circuits to meet mission requirements:

Coding (a variety of commonly-used coding languages)

Artificial Intelligence (AI) / Machine Learning (ML) Engineer

Data Engineer (Python, SQL, MSL, R)

Cybersecurity Analyst

Software Engineer (Python/C++)

Cloud Architect

Data Analyst (Python, SQL, MSL, R)

          (3)  Task 3: Reporting and Analytics. The Contractor shall provide the COR with a Quarterly Skills Gap Analysis Report and a Final Performance and Usage Summary as specified in the Deliverables section.

	(4) Task 4: Contractor shall be interoperable with Digital University (DU). Upon completion of a coding assessment and identification of any weak skill areas, Contractor’s interface with DU will identify courses available in DU to improve those weak skill areas and will recommend those courses to the student.

	(5) Task 5: Contractor Licenses will be used for skill assessment only and not as a job interview aid.

	(6) Task 6: Contractor will provide a subscription management plan to ensure maximum use of subscriptions. B.1  GOVERNING LAW

Federal law and regulations, including the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR), shall govern this Contract/Order.  Commercial license agreements may be made a part of this Contract/Order but only if both parties expressly make them an addendum hereto.  If the commercial license agreement is not made an addendum, it shall not apply, govern, be a part of or have any effect whatsoever on the Contract/Order; this includes, but is not limited to, any agreement embedded in the computer software (clickwrap), any agreement that is otherwise delivered with or provided to the Government with the commercial computer software or documentation (shrinkwrap), or any other license agreement otherwise referred to in any document.  If a commercial license agreement is made an addendum, only those provisions addressing data rights regarding the Government’s use, duplication and disclosure of data (e.g., restricted computer software) are included and made a part of this Contract/Order, and only to the extent that those provisions are not duplicative or inconsistent with Federal law, Federal regulation, the incorporated FAR clauses and the provisions of this Contract/Order; those provisions in the commercial license agreement that do not address data rights regarding the Government’s use, duplication and disclosure of data shall not be included or made a part of the Contract/Order.  Federal law and regulation including, without limitation, the Contract Disputes Act (41 U.S.C. § 7101 et seq.), the Anti-Deficiency Act (31 U.S.C. § 1341 et seq.), the Competition in Contracting Act (41 U.S.C. § 3301 et seq.), the Prompt Payment Act (31 U.S.C. §3901 et seq.), Contracts for Data Processing or Maintenance (38 USC § 5725), and FAR clauses 52.212-4, 52.227-14, 52.227-19 shall supersede, control, and render ineffective any inconsistent, conflicting, or duplicative provision in any commercial license agreement.  In the event of conflict between this Clause and any provision in the Contract/Order or the commercial license agreement or elsewhere, the terms of this Clause shall prevail.  Claims of patent or copyright infringement brought against the Government as a party shall be defended by the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ).  28 U.S.C. § 516.  At the discretion of DOJ, the Contractor may be allowed reasonable participation in the defense of the litigation.  Any additional changes to the Contract/Order must be made by contract/order modification (Standard Form 30) and shall only be affected by a warranted Contracting Officer.  Nothing in this Contract/Order or any commercial license agreement shall be construed as a waiver of sovereign immunity.

B.2 SOFTWARE LICENSE, MAINTENANCE AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT SOFTWARE LICENSE, MAINTENANCE AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT:

Definitions.

       Licensee.  The term “licensee” shall mean the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (“VA”) and is synonymous with “Government.”

       Licensor.  The term “licensor” shall mean the contractor having the necessary license or ownership rights to deliver license, software maintenance and support of the computer software being acquired.  The term “contractor” is the party identified in Block 17a on the SF1449.  If the contractor is a reseller and not the Licensor, the contractor remains responsible for performance under this order.

       Software.  The term “software” shall mean the licensed computer software product(s) cited in the Schedule of Supplies/Services.

       Maintenance.  The term “maintenance” is the process of enhancing and optimizing software, as well as remedying defects.  It shall include all new fixes, patches, releases, updates, versions and upgrades, as further defined below.

       Technical Support.  The term “technical support” refers to the range of services providing assistance for the software via the telephone, email, a website or otherwise.  

       Release or Update.  The term “release” or “update” are terms that refer to a revision of software that contains defect corrections, minor enhancements or improvements of the software’s functionality.  This is usually designated by a change in the number to the right of the decimal point (e.g., from Version 5.3 to 5.4).  An example of an update is the addition of new hardware.

      Version or Upgrade.  The term “version” or “upgrade” are terms that refer to a revision of software that contains new or improved functionality.  This is usually designated by a change in the number to the left of the decimal point (e.g., from Version 5.4 to 6).

Software License

The Government may use the software in a networked environment. 

Any dispute regarding the license grant or usage limitations shall be resolved in accordance with the Disputes Clause incorporated in FAR 52.212-4(d).

All limitations of software usage are expressly stated in the Schedule of Supplies/Services and the Performance Work Statement/Product Description.  

Software Maintenance and Technical Support

(a)	      If the Government desires to continue software maintenance and support beyond the period of performance identified in this contract or order, the Government will issue a separate contract or order for maintenance and support.  Conversely, if a contract or order for continuing software maintenance and technical support is not received the contractor is neither authorized nor permitted to renew any of the previously furnished services.

(b)	      The contractor shall provide software support services, which includes periodic updates, enhancements and corrections to the software, and reasonable technical support, all of which are customarily provided by the contractor to its commercial customers so as to cause the software to perform according to its specifications, documentation or demonstrated claims.  

(c)	      Any telephone support provided by contractor shall be at no additional cost.

(d)	      The contractor shall provide all maintenance services in a timely manner in accordance with the contractor’s customary practice or as defined in the Performance Work Statement/Product Description.  However, prolonged delay (exceeding 2 business days) in resolving software problems will be noted in the Government’s various past performance records on the contractor (e.g., www.ppirs.gov).

(e)	      If the Government allows the maintenance and support to lapse and subsequently wishes to reinstate it, any reinstatement fee charged shall not exceed the amounts that would have been charged if the Government had not allowed the subscription to lapse. 

Disabling Software Code.  The Government requires delivery of computer software that does not contain any code that will, upon the occurrence or the nonoccurrence of any event, disable the software.  Such code includes but is not limited to a computer virus, restrictive key, node lock, time-out or other function, whether implemented by electronic, mechanical, or other means, which limits or hinders the use or access to any computer software based on residency on a specific hardware configuration, frequency of duration of use, or other limiting criteria.  If any such disabling code is present, the contractor agrees to indemnify the Government for all damages suffered as a result of a disabling caused by such code, and the contractor agrees to remove such code upon the Government’s request at no extra cost to the Government.  Inability of the contractor to remove the disabling software code will be considered an inexcusable delay and a material breach of contract, and the Government may exercise its right to terminate for cause.

B.5 PRODUCT DESCRIPTION

STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW)

Discharge Care Plan

Overton Brooks VAMC

510 E. Stoner Avenue

Shreveport, LA. 71101

1. PURPOSE 

The purpose of this Statement of Work (SOW) is to procure access to a subscription-based, patient-centered discharge care planning platform, specifically the Engineered Care Patient Care Plan (or equal), for use at Overton Brooks VA Medical Center (OBVAMC), 510 E. Stoner Avenue, Shreveport LA 71101. 

This procurement supports the implementation and sustainment of Project Greenlight, a facility-led quality improvement initiative designed to enhance discharge communication, improve patient understanding of post-hospital care instructions, and reduce avoidable readmissions. The Engineered Care platform provides a standardized, evidence-based, and patient-friendly discharge care plan that translates complex clinical information into clear, actionable guidance tailored to a health literacy level appropriate for the Veteran population. 

The system will replace or augment existing discharge documentation processes by delivering individualized, easy-to-understand care plans that improve care transitions from inpatient to outpatient settings. This solution is expected to improve key performance metrics, including patient experience, care coordination, medication understanding, and overall patient safety. 

This acquisition will be conducted as a brand name or equal procurement for a base year with four option years, ensuring continuity, scalability, and sustained impact on discharge processes across the facility. 

2. SCOPE

The successful vendor will license the use of the Discharge Care Plan software to the Overton Brooks VAMC and support the installation, implementation, and customization of the Discharge Care Plan software. 

The license grant includes, at no additional charge, the right to make and use a reasonable number of copies of the Software for testing, back-up, archival and disaster recovery purposes, and of the Documentation for internal training, support and deployment. 

The successful vendor will provide the following solution: 

Creation of Discharge Care Plans with health literacy appropriate patient discharge instructions for patients. 

Report functionality to enable continual quality improvement and performance tracking. 

Administrative interface to perform user management, application configuration and auditing. 

Integrate the DCP software with the hospital-based Vista software used for evidence-based, Vista-Integrated Discharge Instructions. Care Transition Portal replaces a site`s existing CPRS discharge note with a patient-friendly discharge instruction booklet that: * Has been shown to reduce unnecessary readmissions * Is customized for the VA environment to help educate veterans about their care and additional VA programs * Improves the discharge process at a VA site while providing leadership opportunities for clinical staff. This is new software that will interface with CPRS to improve the discharge process. It allows the care givers to have one source to print Care Plans, discharge medication list, the patients schedule appointments, etc. End-users will access via CPRS Tools. Engineered Care grants to the Customer a license for the Customer and its Users to use the Product, during the Term. Term of license is 5 years. 

Allow care givers to have one source to print Care Plans, the patients schedule appointments, etc., through access via CPRS Tools. 

Clear discharge instructions compiled in a booklet to keep instructions in one place and be easier for veteran patients to review and understand and follow their Care Plans, in one easy booklet. 

Technology that is table integrated application intended to improve the patient discharge process by providing education regarding patient diagnosis, documentation follow-up appointment and discharge services, confirms the medication plan, reviews steps on what to do if a problem arises, assesses the patient’s understanding of the plan, gives the patient a written discharge plan to take home review and follow. 

3. SPECIFICATIONS 

The successful vendor will work with designated clinical and IT representatives of the Overton Brooks VAMC to deploy the Vista integrated Discharge Care Plan. This work will include installation, configuration and customization as required. 

3.1 

The proposed software will include the following features: 

Discharge planning software for providers 

Creation of health literacy appropriate patient discharge instructions configured for optimal access by Overton Brooks VAMC staff 

Reporting functionality to enable continual quality improvement and performance tracking 

IT Professional interface to perform user management, application configuration and auditing 

User accounts will be created for all users 

Customized to match Overton Brooks VAMC branding requirements including logo placement 

Addition of Overton Brooks VAMC is related Congestive Heart Failure (CHF) discharge instructions 

Vendor will create and print a Care Plan booklet for every veteran discharged from the Overton Brooks VAMC site. The Care Plan will include the following data to the extent that they are available within the system: 

Branded Site Logo 

Patient Aligned Care Team details 

Patient Demographics 

Medications 

Appointment Information 

Instructions on care and management of primary discharge diagnosis 

Diet and Activity Instructions 

Additional Instructions 

My HealtheVet information 

3.2 Discharge Care Plan Software Installation and Configuration 

DCP Software setup. Install the software on the designated server system and create initial user accounts for testing. 

3.3 Implementation and Customization of Discharge Care Plan 

Vendor will customize the Discharge Care Plan for the Overton Brooks VAMC concerning specific medicines and procedures at Overton Brooks VA Medical Center. The DCP booklet will be customized to address/improve care delivery. 

4. PERFORMANCE MONITORING 

The successful vendor will provide periodic performance reporting during the course of DCP software installation and deployment. Overton Brooks VAMC will have real-time access to the DCP software during this time and may conduct periodic product sampling to verify compliance with requirements.

1.0  BACKGROUND 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Office 
of Mental Health and Suicide Prevention (OMHSP), in coordination with the Office of 
Information & Technology (OIT) Health Data Management portfolio is pursuing 
enhanced capabilities to support care coordination and suicide prevention efforts for 
Veterans receiving care in community settings.  This effort aligns with legislative 
priorities including Elizabeth Dole 21st Century Veterans Healthcare and Benefits 
Improvement Act, which emphasizes improved care coordination, timely access to 
information, and enhanced support for Veterans at risk.   
 
VHA has identified a gap in timely visibility into care events occurring outside of VA 
facilities, particularly for Veterans receiving treatment in community hospitals, 
emergency departments, and post-acute care settings.  Without timely notification of 
these events, VA care teams may be delayed in coordinating follow-up care, which is 
especially critical for Veterans identified as high-risk.  Improving awareness of these 
events is essential to enabling proactive outreach and prevention. 
 
To address this gap, VA is exploring the use of electronic notification (eNotification) 
services that provide near real-time alerts for Admission, Discharge, and Transfer (ADT) 
events occurring in community settings.  Market research conducted by VA indicates 
that no single vendor provides sufficient national coverage across all relevant care 
settings.  As a result, a solution that leverages multiple notification networks is 
necessary to achieve targeted/adequate coverage and ensure comprehensive visibility 
into Veteran care events. 
 
This pilot will support up to six (6) VA Medical Centers (VAMCs) and a defined 
population of Veterans identified as high-risk.  VA will provide a Veteran attribution list, 
that will be updated periodically, to enable targeted notification delivery.  Notifications 
will be transmitted via Direct Secure Messaging (DSM) infrastructure, through the 
Oracle Health’s Health Information Service Provider (HISP), into VA Direct Secure 
Messaging (DSM) inboxes, leveraging existing infrastructure without requiring direct 
integration with VA clinical systems.  The objective of the pilot is to assess the 
effectiveness, timeliness, and operational impact of eNotification services in improving 
care coordination and supporting suicide prevention efforts.

3.0  SCOPE OF WORK 
The Contractor shall provide and implement an Admissions, Discharge, and Transfer 
(ADT) eNotifications Software as a Service (SaaS) utilizing multiple existing provider 
networks already in place to support a VA-defined population of Veterans identified as 
at-risk across up to six (6) VA Medical Center (VAMCs).  The Contractor shall support a 
VA-defined population of up to approximately 82,000 patients, with attribution data 
provided and maintained by VA and updated on a quarterly basis.  The Contractor shall 
provide implementation support including configuration, testing, and deployment of the 
SaaS solution and enable filtering of notifications based on VA-defined criteria, including 
Veteran/patient association with a home VAMC.

eNotifications associated with the VA-defined patient population and relevant treatment-
related events.  The Contractor shall support the secure transmission of eNotifications,

1.0  BACKGROUND 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information & Technology (OIT), 
Infrastructure Operations (IO), Data Center and Cloud Engineering (DCCE) division 
strives to provide high quality, effective, and efficient Information Technology (IT) 
services to those responsible for providing care to the Veterans at the point-of-care as 
well as throughout all the points of the Veterans' health care in an effective, timely and 
compassionate manner.  VA depends on Information Management/Information 
Technology (IM/IT) systems to meet mission goals.  
VA currently operates a complex hybrid enterprise environment spanning on-premises 
data centers, private cloud infrastructure, and public cloud environments through the VA 
Enterprise Cloud (VAEC). Over the past decade, infrastructure teams across the 

Infrastructure Automation Technical Debt Reduction (IATDR) Program 
VA-26-00026979 
 
 
Page 4 of 91 
enterprise have independently developed thousands of ad-hoc automation scripts, 
adopted inconsistent infrastructure-as-code and configuration management automation 
usage patterns, relied on manual execution paths for infrastructure changes, and 
created duplicative automation logic across organizational boundaries. These conditions 
represent accumulated infrastructure automation technical debt that increases outage 
risk, security exposure, labor cost, and time-to-delivery for critical Veteran-facing 
services. 
The Infrastructure Automation Technical Debt Reduction (IATDR) Program will establish 
an on-premises, enterprise automation control plane that standardizes, governs, and 
operationalizes infrastructure automation. This capability will enable repeatable, 
auditable, and policy-governed provisioning and configuration of infrastructure platforms 
across VA's hybrid environment, reducing configuration drift, improving compliance 
posture, and accelerating infrastructure delivery in support of VA's mission to serve 
Veterans.  
The IATDR Program directly supports VA's ongoing enterprise infrastructure 
modernization initiatives, including enterprise virtualization modernization, enterprise 
storage consolidation, and data center transformation efforts. Establishing a centralized 
automation control plane is a foundational prerequisite for executing these programs at 
enterprise scale with consistency, auditability, and governance. This effort is conducted 
under the authority of the Clinger Cohen Act (40 U.S.C. Section 11101 and Section 
11103) and is subject to oversight under the Federal Information Technology Acquisition 
Reform Act (FITARA).

NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT 
 
Notice Type: Special Notice – Notice of Intent to Sole Source 
 
Solicitation Number: 140R4026Q0099 
 
Title: CADSWES RiverWare Support Services IDIQ 
 
Description 
The Department of the Interior, Bureau of Reclamation (BOR), intends to negotiate and award a 
sole-source Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to: 
 
The Regents of the University of Colorado 
Center for Advanced Decision Support for Water and Environmental Systems (CADSWES) 
 
The proposed contract will provide RiverWare software support services, including software 
maintenance, technical support, enhancements, updates, and related professional services in support 
of Bureau of Reclamation water operations and planning activities. 
 
The anticipated contract will be a Firm-Fixed-Price IDIQ with a performance period of up to ten 
(10) years. 
 
Authority 
This acquisition is being conducted using the authority of FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible 
Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements, and applicable 
simplified acquisition/commercial procedures, as appropriate. 
 
Sole Source Rationale 
RiverWare is proprietary software developed, owned, and maintained exclusively by the Center for 
Advanced Decision Support for Water and Environmental Systems (CADSWES) at the University 
of Colorado. CADSWES retains exclusive ownership of the RiverWare source code and intellectual 
property rights. 
 
The Bureau of Reclamation relies on RiverWare to perform critical reservoir operations, water 
management modeling, planning studies, and implementation of Records of Decision supporting 
statutory water management responsibilities. Only CADSWES possesses the proprietary source 
code, technical expertise, and legal authority necessary to provide software maintenance, 
enhancements, bug fixes, upgrades, and technical support for RiverWare. 
 
Market research conducted by the Government confirmed that no other source is capable of 
providing these services without violating proprietary rights or intellectual property protections. 
Accordingly, no other responsible source can satisfy the Government's requirements. 

2

submit all questions and comments in response to this notice, with final

participation, feedback, and questions submitted in response to the notice.  
In response to the feedback received, the USCB intends to host a Virtual Industry Day. The 
purpose of this event is to address notable themes from the feedback, clarify the 
acquisition strategy, refine the technical requirements, and outline the upcoming 
procurement process to assist vendors in preparing high-quality quotations.

providing a formal response to each individual vendor’s question.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO)  
AI-Enabled Aircraft Maintenance Data Standardization & Troubleshooting – Pilot 
1. Purpose. To evaluate the feasibility, performance, and operational integration of a commercial 
AI capability that cleanses and standardizes historical USAF aircraft maintenance data and 
provides prescriptive troubleshooting to maintainers, to inform an aircraft repair decision. 
2. Background. The Department of the Air Force's reliance on the Integrated Maintenance Data 
System (IMDS) and the Reliability and Maintainability Information System (REMIS) is severely 
constrained by unstructured data. These databases house millions of records, critical qualitative 
details that are trapped in free-text "narrative" fields written by maintainers. 
Because these entries lack standardization, suffer from rampant typos, and use non-standardized 
acronyms, advanced analytical tools cannot easily parse the data. This "dark data" prevents 
aircraft maintenance technicians, analysts, and engineers from conducting targeted automated 
data cleansing and analysis in a timely manner to aid in diagnosing an aircraft problem and 
comparing to historical effective and non-effective repairs. 
Aircraft maintenance technicians and analysts require the ability to automatically ingest, clean, 
and analyze this unstructured text. Without this capability the technicians are left with a massive 
"blind spot" to quickly troubleshooting and repair aircraft.   
Maintenance analysts are forced to manually review thousands of logs to identify "bad actor" 
parts or recurring failure modes—a process that is incredibly labor-intensive and slow. 
Consequently, aircraft technicians and analyst teams miss historical repair data that increases 
aircraft downtime during troubleshooting and repair, delaying supply chain demands, and 
degraded mission-capable rates across the fleet.  
Aircrew use of historical aircraft reported discrepancies and effective repairs will enable aircrew 
to precisely describe an identified problem.  Providing aircraft maintenance technicians, a 
focused and detailed description of a problem with the aircraft enables efficient troubleshooting 
and diagnosis with a faster aircraft repair and return to service. 
The combined AI capability to assist in aircrew debriefing actions leads to aircraft technicians 
completing troubleshooting and aircraft repairs faster and with greater precision. Culminating in 
greater aircraft availability.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)

DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS (VA)

Office of Procurement

VA Enterprise Contract Management System (CMS)

Date: July 16, 2026

 VA-26-00066426

PWS Version Number: 1.0

 

1.0 BACKGROUND 

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Acquisition, Logistics, and Construction strives to provide high quality, effective, and efficient Information Technology (IT) services to those responsible for providing care to the Veterans at the point-of-care as well as throughout all the points of the Veterans’ health care in an effective, timely and compassionate manner. VA depends on Information Technology (IT) systems to meet mission goals. 

VA is one of the largest consumers of commercially acquired goods and services in the Federal Government. The VA operates from many locations throughout the United States supporting Veterans and their families. The Office of Procurement under the leadership of the Senior Procurement Executive (SPE) is responsible for Department-wide Acquisition Management and oversight for policy development, workforce development, supply chain management and Acquisition Business Systems management.

 

The program office, Procurement Systems Management (PSM), is responsible for configuration management, change management, communication management, understanding technical and functional capabilities required by the VA Acquisition Workforce (AWF) and aligning with the VA Strategic Objectives related to modernization and transformation. This work is vital to improving, modernizing, and transforming acquisition management across the enterprise along with intentional timely deployment of emerging technology to integrate enterprise acquisition standards for the four cornerstones:

 

Acquisition Policy – Builds on federal mandates and regulatory guidance, develops and manages the direction of acquisition policy for the Department. Ensures compliance when making acquisition decisions. Requires the latest technology in acquisition business systems to properly align electronic processes with frequently changing acquisition regulatory and VA internal guidance.

 

Workforce Development - Builds, enables, and sustains a knowledgeable workforce that can execute on the acquisition business needs of the Department of Veterans Affairs.

 

Acquisition Business Strategy - Provides support and monitors the performance of VA acquisition activities related to various federal initiatives. Assures the VA business systems include the required technology-based tools and templates required to limit manual processes, reduce non-value-added processes, and drive output that adds value.

 

Acquisition Systems Capabilities – Manages the collection and exchange of acquisition data using technology to create transparency, accountability, and acquisition lifecycle reform, leading to supportable data-based decisions and improvements in the exchange of information between the government and the public. 

 

The current portfolio of applications, called “eCMS”, are an integration of proprietary Commercial-off-the-Shelf (COTS) products, existing Government off-the-Shelf (GOTS) software, and custom integration and software designed to meet VA specific needs. The system infrastructure is comprised of Microsoft .NET platform, ASP.NET Model-View-Controller (MVC), Core.NET, WebAPI, Web Forms, AngularJS JBoss, Java 2 Platform Enterprise Edition (J2EE), Microsoft SQL Server, and Microsoft Internet Information Server (IIS), access by end-users to a web-based system -- single sign-on via Microsoft Integrated Windows Authentication (IWA).  System Architecture is available and formally describes the various components, technologies and interfaces in an organized way that defines structural properties of the applications that make up the systems referred to as the eCMS portfolio.

   

By adhering to these guidelines and providing the specified support services, the Contractor shall support the program office, PSM, in achieving its objectives of modernizing acquisition management, improving efficiency, and integrating emerging technologies within the VA’s acquisition systems.

This portfolio, its associated applications/components, and applicable system definitions are fully outlined within the below referenced technical attachments.

7.6.4-01 - Inspection and Acceptance - July 2008
(a) All goods and services shall be subject to inspection and test by the FDIC Oversight Manager, to the extent
practicable, at all times and places during the term of the award.  All inspections by the FDIC shall be made in such
a manner as not to unduly delay the work.
 
(b) The FDIC shall have 15 (fifteen) business days from the date of Contractor''s delivery to determine if such goods
and services are in compliance with the requirements of the contract.  If any services performed or goods delivered
hereunder are not in conformity with the requirements of this Award, the FDIC shall have the right to require
Contractor to reperform the services or redeliver the goods in conformity with the requirements of the Award, at no
additional increase in total contract amount.  When the services to be performed are of such a nature that the defect
cannot be corrected by reperformance of the services, the FDIC shall have the right to (1) require Contractor
immediately to take all necessary steps to ensure future performance of the services in conformity with the
requirements of the contract; and (2) reduce the contract price to reflect the reduced value of the services
performed.  In the event Contractor fails promptly to reperform the services or redeliver the goods, or to take
necessary steps to ensure future performance of the services or delivery of the goods in conformity with the
requirements of the Award, the FDIC shall have the right to either (1) by contract or otherwise, have the services
performed or the goods delivered in conformity with the contract requirements and charge to Contractor any cost
occasioned to the FDIC that is directly related to the performance of such services or the delivery of such goods; or
(2) terminate this Award for default as provided in 7.6.6-02, Termination for Default.
 
(c) Contractor shall provide and maintain an inspection system acceptable to the FDIC covering the goods or
services to be delivered or performed hereunder.  Records of all inspection work by Contractor shall be kept
complete and available to the FDIC during the term of this Award and for such longer period as may be specified
elsewhere in this Award.

7.3.2-41 - FDIC Personnel - July 2008
(a)  FDIC Oversight Manager.  The Oversight Manager is the person designated in writing by the Contracting
Officer to represent the FDIC for the purpose of monitoring technical performance and accepting goods or services.
The Oversight Manager is not authorized to issue any instructions or directions which affect any substantive change
in this contract, including, but not limited to, an increase or decrease in the price of this contract, or a change in the
delivery date(s) or Period of Performance.  Specific areas of delegated authority are more particularly defined in the
Oversight Manager Appointment Memorandum.  The Oversight Manager is Hoang-Yen Luu who can be reached at
hluu@fdic.gov.
 
(b)  FDIC Contracting Officer.  The Contracting Officer is the person with FDIC-delegated authority to enter into,
modify, administer, and terminate contracts and orders.  The Contracting Officer is Christina V. Brooks who can be
reached at chrbrooks@fdic.gov.
 
7.5.13-01 - Method of Payment - Electronic Fund Transfer (EFT) - March 2014
(a) Payment methods.  Payments by the FDIC may be made by check or electronic funds transfer (EFT), or by a
third party in lieu of payment directly from the FDIC, at the option of the FDIC. If the FDIC makes payment by EFT,
the FDIC may, at its option, also forward the associated payment information by electronic transfer.  Any third party
payments will be made by the FDIC''s commercial purchase card issuer.  In the event Contractor certifies in writing
to the payment office that Contractor does not have an account with a financial institution or an authorized payment
agent, the FDIC would make payments by other than EFT.
 
(b) Contractor Payment Requests.  If the FDIC elects for third party payments to be made, Contractor shall make
payment requests through a charge to the FDIC purchase card with the third party, at the time and for the amount
due in accordance with the terms of this contract.  Contractor and the third party shall agree that payments due
under this contract shall be made upon submittal of payment requests to the third party in accordance with the
terms and conditions of an agreement between Contractor, the Contractor''s financial agent (if any), and the third
party and its agents (if any).  No payment shall be due the Contractor until such agreement is made.   Payments
made or due by the third party are not subject to the Prompt Payment Act or any implementation thereof in this
contract.  Documentation of each charge against the FDIC''s purchase card shall be provided to the Contracting
Officer upon request.
 
Contractor is required, as a condition to any payment, to maintain current information in the System for Award

(a) NAVSEA may use a file room management support contractor, hereinafter referred to as "the support contractor", to manage  its 
file room, in which all official contract files, including the official file supporting this procurement, are retained. These  official files 
may contain information that is considered a trade secret, proprietary, business sensitive or otherwise protected pursuant to law or

secretarial or clerical support; data entry; document reproduction, scanning, imaging, or destruction; operation,  management, or

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT

Title: Alerton Building Automation System Maintenance and Emergency Repair 

Date: 07/15/2026

I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION 

The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is a 576-acre facility consisting of thirty-six (36) mixed use (mainly office and research laboratory) buildings. There are currently four (4) proprietary building automation systems used to control various mechanical equipment that maintain the required environmental conditions on campus.  The Alerton Envision for BACtalk Control Systems pertains to this performance work statement (PWS).

II. PURPOSE

Contractor is to provide all labor, supervision, tools, material, and equipment to provide preventative maintenance and emergency services for the Alerton Envision for BACtalk Control systems specified. Contractor must maintain systems to ensure systems are in proper operating order.

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

Maintenance service must be provided twice a month, and the place of performance shall be at NIST, Gaithersburg Campus. Maintenance service shall be performed during normal business hours (7am – 5 pm Monday through Thursday, excluding, weekends and Federal Holidays).

PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE 

This is a 1-year Base Period contract with four (4) 1-year Option Periods.

Base - 9/1/2026 – 8/31/2027

Opt.1 – 9/1/2027 – 7/31/2028

Opt.2 – 9/1/2028 – 7/31/2029

Opt.3 – 9/1/2029 – 7/31/2030

Opt.4 – 9/1/2030 – 7/31/2031

Six-Month EXT – 08/01/2023 – 01/31/2032. 

 

 SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS

The maintenance service shall cover:

Alerton Envision for BACtalk application 6ea. Locations. 2ea.Servers and 4ea. Clients. This includes replacement and/or updating of servers, client PCs.

Global Controllers (BTI’s and BCM’s) 16 ea. BTI’s and 9ea. BCM’s or interfacing of automation to unitary devices related to mechanical operation of points to be controlled by automation system that are maintained in DDC Cabinets.

TASKS

Maintenance services shall include the following:

Task 1 –   Data Backup

Complete data backup to CD, DVD or flash drive to include trend logs, programming, graphics, and control software must be conducted whenever software or programming changes is made but no less frequently than monthly.

Task 2 –   Graphics Revisions

The contractor shall maintain all graphics at each of the applicable workstations.

Task 3 – Programing Diagnostics

The contractor shall perform diagnostics of programs and make recommendations for change/correction to meet original control performance requirements. After consulting with NIST COR the contractor shall make changes to programming to achieve the performance requirement.

Task 4 – Field Panel Diagnostics 

The contractor shall perform diagnostics of all field panels. The contractor shall analyze the results of diagnostics and make recommendations for changes to optimize the building control performance within the functional capabilities for the system any changes required to hardware will be the responsibility of NIST. Changes required to software to resolve issues shall be the responsibility of the contractor.

Task 5 - Control Loop Evaluation and Tuning

The contractor shall evaluate and tune critical control loops to maintain peak efficiency of equipment as the building mechanical systems’ performance changes over time. NIST DDC personnel shall work with the Contactor to identify the critical control loops on each system.

Task 6 – Consultation

The Contractor shall consult with NIST DDC personnel to identify and resolve problems with hardware and/or software in the applicable automation system. Any changes required to hardware will be the reasonability of NIST. Changes required to software to resolve issues shall be the reasonability of the contractor.

Task 7 – Emergency Service 

This shall Include time for Contractor to diagnose and resolve problems identified by NIST. This shall include normal or out of normal hours past 7am – 5pm Monday through Thursday to include Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays and Federal holidays. If necessary, the Contractor shall respond to the site in 24 hours of contact by NIST. Pricing shall be based upon 40 hours of emergency service.

Task 8 – IT Security Requirements

Security Hardening & Configuration

The Contractor shall ensure that all software components including the operating system, firmware, and database management systems utilized in the management and operation of the BAS systems are maintained on versions currently supported by the manufacturer.  

All non-essential services, ports, and protocols must be disabled or removed.

Before and after any maintenance or repair activity, a full system configuration backup shall be performed.

Access Management 

Access shall be granted only to the level required for the specific maintenance or repair task.  

The use of shared administrative accounts is strictly prohibited. The Contractor must use unique, named credentials for all installation and configuration tasks.

All default passwords (e.g., system administrator, admin, operator, guest) must be changed to unique passwords prior to system handover.

Device Control

Personal laptops, USB drives, smartphones or any wireless-capable devices are prohibited from connecting to the BAS environment.

The Contractor personnel shall not attempt to bridge the BAS systems to a cellular hotspot or any other network-connected device.

Auditing & Logging

The Contractor shall configure the system to provide an audit trail of all administrative and operator actions.  The system shall log administrative actions, successful and failed login attempts, account lockouts, and configuration changes.  Logs must include a timestamp and the specific user ID.

Audit logs and event histories shall be retained within the active production database for a minimum of 12 months before archiving.  Archived logs shall be maintained for an additional period of 18 months in a format that allows for restoration if requested by the COR or during an audit.  

Task 9 Homeland Security Presidential Directive (HSPD)-12 

 

Contractor personnel (including subcontractors) who require physical access to NIST facilities or logical access to NIST IT networks or systems must comply with Homeland Security Presidential Directive (HSPD)-12, Policy for a Common Identification Standard for Federal Employees and Contractors; OMB M-05-24; OMB M-19-17; FIPS 201, Personal Identity Verification (PIV) of Federal Employees and Contractors; NIST HSPD-12 policy; and Executive Order 13467, Part 1 §1.2. 

Roster 

 

The Contractor must submit a roster by name, position, e-mail address, phone number and responsibility, of all personnel (including subcontractor personnel) working under this acquisition where the Contractor will develop, have the ability to access, or host and/or maintain a government information system(s). 

 

The Contractor must submit the roster to the COR and/or CO within 14 days of the effective date of this contract. Any revisions to the roster because of staffing changes must be submitted within 14 days of the change. The COR will notify the Contractor of the appropriate level of investigation required for each staff member. If the employee is filling a new position, the Contractor must provide a position description, and the Government will determine the appropriate suitability level. 

 

Position Sensitivity Designations Requirement

All Contractor (and/or any subcontractor) personnel must obtain a background investigation commensurate with their position sensitivity designation that complies with Parts 1400 and 731 of Title 5, Code of Federal Regulations
