3. DRAFT STATEMENT OF WORK 
3.1 Project Title 
Novel High-Density Optical Data Storage Pilot 
3.2 Background 
The Library of Congress, hereinafter referred to as the “Library” or “LOC”,” is exploring innovative 
preservation methods for its digital collections. The LOC is seeking to determine the feasibility of 
utilizing ultra-high density optical data storage designed for the long-term preservation of a subset of 
the Library’s digital collections. Currently, the Library manages over 1 billion unique objects of digital 
preservation data (~33 petabytes) via traditional storage methods. For longevity and reduced migration 
intervals, it may be reasonable for this portion of data to be permanently stored on a novel medium. 
The focus would be on a solution that exhibits high areal density, a long lifespan, reduced 
maintenance/migration cycles, is immutable, and displays a high level of durability. The Library aims to 
demonstrate the feasibility of an innovative optical data storage solution as a high-density, scalable, and 
durable medium for storing its preservation collection. 
The Library wishes to examine the feasibility of this method on a small subset of its digital collections. To 
be successful, a variety of data formats—including video, audio, text, and images— must be encoded 
onto the media, errors must be detected/recorded, preservation techniques must be validated and 
select data must be recalled/read with high fidelity. This work will contribute to the boundary pushing 
field of high-density optical data storage while pushing the boundaries of access and preservation. 
The desired outcomes of this requirement are as follows: 
 The successful writing of 1TB of the Library’s digital data in various formats (video, audio, images, 
text) onto a robust high-density optical media designed to outlast legacy storage solutions at a 
higher areal density. 
 The determination of the accuracy of the writing process by demonstrating early-stage error 
detection and ultimate 100% recovery of data. 
 The documentation of successful processes, shortcomings, error rates, timelines, potential solutions 
to issues, risks, trends, and technological improvements throughout the period of performance as 
they pertain to the media of choice. 
 Proof of concept for the potential indefinite storage approach of the Library’s data on a novel optical 
storage medium. 
 The successful recall and reading of all Library-furnished digital files that have been encoded on the 
media of choice.

 The isolation of a subset of the data will be carefully curated and stored for the purposes of an 
educational and artistic display. This will used for educational and display purposes for Library 
visitors. 
3.3 Scope 
The contractor shall develop a comprehensive plan and implement a process to transfer a designated 
selection of the Library’s digital collection onto/into a novel high-density optical media to determine the 
feasibility of the Library utilizing this method as a long- term storage solution. The contractor shall 
employ techniques for long-term storage of encoded the media, accurately identify specific data 
selected by the Library from the storage solution, accurately read items selected by the Library, display 
the scalability of their processes, and employ validation methods to determine the accuracy of every 
critical stage (encoding, writing, storing, decoding, and data recovery). 
3.4 Task Objectives 
3.4.1 Project Management 
 
3.4.1.1 Kickoff Meeting 
The Contractor shall hold a project kickoff meeting within 5 days after period of performance 
start date to include: 
a. Introduction to the project team and discussion of roles. 
b. Review the contract and functional requirements. 
c. Review of the draft project management plan submitted with the proposal. 
d. Discussion of Communications Plan/ coordination of meetings. 
e. Initiation of immediate tasks (first 30 days). 
f. Quality and acceptance criteria for deliverables. 
3.4.1.2 Project Management Plan 
The Contractor shall develop and implement a Project Management Plan (PMP). The PMP 
must detail milestones, activities, subcontracting plan, communications plan, organizational 
chart, personnel roles, and timelines for the deliverables and milestones of the data storage 
services. The PMP shall also include known risks and corresponding risk mitigation 
techniques. 
 
The LOC shall provide any notes or request for updates for the Project Management Plan at 
the contract kickoff meeting. A final Project Management Plan with agreed upon changes 
and updates discussed/provided at kickoff meeting incorporated shall be provided within 10 
business days after the kickoff meeting.

a. The Contractor shall maintain clear government visibility into the program schedule, 
technical performance, and risks via bi-weekly reporting though the contractor may 
propose more frequent reporting). Reporting and analytics must be meaningful and 
inform the Library of up-to-date and comprehensive information regarding technical 
performance. 
 
b. The Contractor must maintain regular communication with the COR regarding 
roadblocks, schedule risks, and changes in technical landscape. This includes scheduled 
meetings and presentations with relevant LOC staff regarding project updates. 
 
c. After each relevant project phase outlined in Section 3.4.2, the Contractor must 
provide a formal report as listed in Section C.4.2 detailing the processes, lessons 
learned and results of the applicable project phase. 
3.4.2 Novel High-Density Optical Data Storage 
3.4.2.1 General 
The contractor shall: 
a. Provide historical error rates in addition to error rates for any work competed 
while working with the Library. 
b. Deliver the entire 1TB dataset, preserved onto the medium of choice and 
contained within the permanent storage solution, to the Library. The 
contractor must validate that the media delivered to the Library data actually 
contains the Library’s data The LOC staff must be able to confirm validation for 
acceptance purposes. 
c. Document processes, to include shortcomings, for reporting to the Library 
Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR). 
3.4.2.2 Encoding/Writing 
The contractor shall: 
a. Receive and process 1TB of digital data in a variety of formats, to include 
video, audio, images, and text files. The transfer of government furnished 
information (GFI) will be facilitated by the Library via file transfer software 
and will be presented in the BagIt file packaging format. No GFI will be 
classified, personally identifiable information (PII), controlled unclassified 
information (CUI), or restricted access information.

b. Partition the data in the most space conscious manner. The fundamental 
purpose of this project is to determine the current feasibility/advantages of 
this technology. Therefore, the Library wants  the data partitioned to 
ultimately be stored in a manner that occupies the smallest physical 
footprint, accounting for necessary redundancy, while still maintaining 
recoverability and random access. 
c. Convert the data (4.2.3.1) into a usable format for encoding data to the high-
density optical media of choice. 
d. Utilize a robust encoding protocol for representing diverse data formats 
(video, audio, text, and images) on a the medium. The encoding process will 
aim to maintain the ability to faithfully and efficiently reconstruct the original 
data. 
e. Ensure that the encoding process preserves the integrity of the original data 
with minimal loss or distortion. This includes the development of redundancy 
protocols to mitigate the risk of potential errors during encoding, writing, and 
ultimately data retrieval. While the Library will not define the extent of the 
redundancy the contractor chooses to implement, the contractor should plan 
for sufficient redundancy to ensure 100% data recovery. It is of interest to the 
Library to determine the number of copies required to ensure recovery in the 
future, and the Library wishes to consider this while analyzing the feasibility 
of this novel data storage solution. 
f. Ensure the media containing the data can be validated for accuracy 
throughout the writing process, minimizing potential corruption during 
storage or ultimate retrieval. 
g. A formal report detailing the error rates from validation testing and 
corrective actions required to remediate any known errors shall be provided 
after validation of the encoding and writing processes are completed. 
h. Manufacture a data storage medium that has written an accurate 
representation of the data provided by the Library. 
 
3.4.2.3 Storage Mechanisms 
The contractor shall: 
a. Store the media in secure and stable conditions to prevent degradation over 
time, ensuring long-term data preservation. The storage mechanism shall 
ensure the integrity of the chosen media for a minimum of 50 years on the

Q1.	Please confirm that the VBA receives 41,000 packets per day on average but the ask of the contractor for this TO is to process up to 5-7,000 after the third month.  The potential is more as the contractor proves its value.  This 5-7,000 is all USPS mail and mail that is being shipped to contractor by VBA RO's.

A1.	The Government confirms that VBA estimates receiving approximately 41,000 mail packets per day across all centralized mail operations; however, this figure represents the total mail volume processed through the full centralized mail pipeline and is not the contractor's Task 5.14 obligation. Task 5.14 Mail Packet Processing Services is a distinct function separate from mail receipt, scanning, and conversion.  It represents human-assisted claims processing actions, analogous to work a claims assistant would perform, on mail packets that automated processing was unable to complete, ensuring mail is actioned the same day it enters a work queue. The contractor's Task 5.14 obligation is to process 5,000–7,000 packets per day following the Month 3 ramp-up period as outlined in Table 5 of PWS Section 5.14.  The Government notes that this volume has trended downward over time as mail automation capabilities have matured, though temporary spikes may occur due to automation issues or special projects.

1.0 INTRODUCTION 

THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) for Mail Management Services. This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes only. There is no obligation for the Government to acquire any products or services described in this RFI. In accordance with the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 15.101(c), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. No funds have been authorized, appropriated, or received for this effort. The information provided may be used by VBA in developing its acquisition strategy and informing, refining, and finalizing a Performance Work Statement (PWS). Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response. Only electronic responses to this RFI will be accepted. The Government will not pay for any time expended or information submitted in response to this RFI. Eligibility in participating in a future acquisition does not depend upon a response to this RFI. 

2.0 BACKGROUND 

Through its three (3) administrations, Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA), National Cemetery Administration (NCA), and Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Veterans Affairs (VA) administers vital services to America's Veterans. VA provides health care services, benefits programs, and access to national cemeteries for former military personnel and their dependents.

The fundamental mission of the Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA) is to provide Veterans, service members, and their families the benefits they have earned through their military service to the United States. VBA accomplishes its mission by delivering client-centered, personalized services that help Veterans readjust to civilian life and enhance their well-being.

To continuously improve benefits processing efficiency and cycle-time, VBA expanded its mail receipt and processing services to include Centralized Mail (CM) processing. The CM activities require vendors to receive mail directly from Veterans, claimants, Veterans / claimants representatives and third parties providing evidence in support of a claim. Physical materials are received via paper mail (bulk mail, US Postal Service pickup and delivery, other external mail delivery services) and digital formats (CD/DVD, Flash drives, Microfilm, Microfiche, Other alternate media). Non-physical information is received via various digital formats (direct upload service by Veterans, external Veteran Service Organization user or other third party; through an application program interface (API); secure file transfer; email; and fax). The materials and information received by the contractor are converted into digital files in the searchable Portable Document Format (PDFs) and are then made available to VA end users for review within an interactive centralized mail portal; routed for additional processing; or accessed for unattended mail automation operations. Upon completion of mail processing, images, with associated data, are uploaded to VBA’s image repository, the Veterans Benefits Management System (VBMS). If the CM materials were received in physical formats (e.g., paper), they are prepared for shipment to a government contracted long-term storage facility, awaiting disposition.

This Request for Information (RFI) describes VBAs requirements for contractor support related to mail management services. In addition, the purpose of the RFI is to engage industry vendors with expert knowledge and extensive experience as well as with credibility in addressing and mitigating risks. The Government seeks innovative solutions from industry on mail management services. 

3.0 INFORMATION SOUGHT 

The Government is seeking the following information to be provided by vendors when responding to the RFI:

RFI respondents shall provide a capability statement with an overview of the company’s capabilities to fulfill the requirements of the attached PWS. Overview should include but not be limited to: 

Details regarding proposed joint ventures, teaming arrangements, strategic alliances, or other business arrangements to satisfy requirements of the entire PWS.

3.3 Answers to Questions 

RFI respondents shall provide answers to the questions provided in Section 5.0 of this RFI. RFI respondents are requested to address each question. Questions that do not apply to RFI respondents or if RFI respondents cannot provide answers shall be addressed by marking these questions with “N/A”.

The Department of Veterans Affairs has developed detailed Business Requirements Documents (BRDs) that further describe the technical and operational requirements for Mail Management Services. These BRDs are not included with this RFI.

Respondents should base their feedback on the high-level requirements and objectives outlined in this RFI.

The Government anticipates providing the full BRDs and other supporting documentation during the subsequent solicitation phase (e.g., Request for Proposal or Request for Quotation).

If you require clarification on any requirement or would like to comment on the anticipated level of detail, please indicate this in your response.

 4.0 SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS 

Response submissions to this RFI are due no later than July 21, 2026, 3:00 pm Eastern Time and shall be submitted to gregory.stevens@va.gov  The email subject line must contain the following: “Company Name, Response to RFI 36C10D26Q0139.” VBA reserves the right to not reply to any emails, responses, questions, and materials submitted in response to the RFI. Mark your response as “Proprietary Information” if the information included is considered to be business sensitive and/or includes trade secrets. RFI responses shall not exceed 15 pages total. Responses shall be prepared in Microsoft Word with standard 8.5 x 11-inch page format (charts may be landscaped but must be on 8.5 x 11-inch page format) and shall be in Times New Roman, font size (12), with 1” margins. All page format of the response shall be appropriately numbered and identified with the RFI number. The email file size limitation shall be no more than 40MB.

5.0 LIST OF QUESTIONS 

1) Please describe your company’s strategy to address the full scope of work, to include risk management, solution management, incident and event management, and education and outreach and communication support services as outlined in the PWS. Please describe any relevant experience within the Government or Industry that demonstrates your capabilities in each service area. How would you address any gaps in your service offerings?  

2) Please describe innovations you have employed on other projects and how those innovations differentiate your company from others in regard to the types of services outlined in the PWS. 

3) Please outline the experience your company has in scaling, making recommendations, and incorporating continuous improvement principles to enable service delivery and achieving objectives in the PWS. 

4) Please describe your company’s approach to quality assurance, employing performance metrics, and your success in meeting Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) performance objectives on similar efforts.   

5) What is your company’s approach for proposing and implementing evolving technologies such as machine learning, natural language processing, robotic processing (“bots”) or full artificial intelligence to drive automation for solutions?  How do you ensure these technologies remain current and effective? Can you provide any examples of successful integrations in similar projects?

  

6) Please describe your company’s experience with protecting Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and Protected Health Information (PHI) when utilizing large databases and processing transactional activities associated with tracking source materials locally and remotely in a secure environment. B.3 STATEMENT OF WORK 


1.0 INTRODUCTION / BACKGROUND
The Harry S. Truman Veterans’ Memorial Hospital requires the implementation of a modern inventory control software system to replace the existing ConnectRx platform used within Inpatient Pharmacy. ConnectRx will no longer be supported after December 2027, and new interfaces are no longer being developed. This discontinuation was announced after the facility committed to the purchase of SwissLog Allegro carousels, creating an operational need to identify and implement a replacement solution.

The Pyxis Logistics (PLX) solution and its associated HL7 interfaces are required to maintain communication between the Pyxis ES system and the Allegro carousels. The replacement system must ensure continued support for automated dispensing cabinet refill workflows, first-dose medication requests, inventory tracking, and wholesaler order communication. Implementation of a supported, integrated platform is essential to sustaining safe, efficient, and uninterrupted inpatient pharmacy operations.

2.0 SCOPE OF WORK
The contractor must provide all labor, equipment, software, licenses, interfaces, materials, training, and support necessary to deliver a fully operational inventory management solution that replaces ConnectRx and integrates seamlessly with SwissLog Allegro carousels.

The contractor must:

Install and configure all required software, hardware, and interfaces.

Establish HL7 communication between Pyxis ES and Allegro systems.

Provide inventory management capabilities for medications stored both inside and outside carousel systems.

Enable cabinet refill data transmission, first-dose request handling, and wholesaler order communication.

Conduct all required testing, validation, and quality assurance activities.

Provide staff training, technical documentation, and go-live support.

Deliver ongoing maintenance and support during the base year and through each option year.

The contractor must ensure the final solution is stable, fully supported, and compliant with all applicable VA, VHA, and federal regulations and policies.

3.0 REQUIREMENTS / DELIVERABLES

Kit-Install, Pharmogistics/Carousel, Network – Qty 2

Kit ZQ630 Printer US with 6 Label Rolls – Qty 1

Cradle Charge 5-Slot TC5X White US – Qty 2

Additional Interface Without Database – Qty 1

3.2 Service Deliverables – Base Year and Four (4) Option Years
The contractor must provide monthly support for the following:

Pharmogistics Enterprise System (ES) Software Hospital

Pyxis Check Software Hospital

Kit DS3678 Scanner US/OUS Wireless

Printer ZT411 Thermal Barcode, Stand-Alone

Handset Staged TC52X-HC FIPS A13

Pyxis Check Scanner Kit

Kit ZQ630 Printer US

Additional Interface Without Database

Support services must include technical assistance, software updates, interface maintenance, troubleshooting, and patch management necessary to maintain continuous operational capability.

4.0 PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE
The period of performance includes a Base Year of 12 months and four (4) 12-month Option Years. 

5.0 PLACE OF PERFORMANCE
Harry S. Truman Veterans’ Memorial Hospital
800 Hospital Drive
Columbia, Missouri 65201
Inpatient Pharmacy

6.0 GOVERNMENT RESPONSIBILITIES
The Government will provide access to all necessary clinical and technical environments, coordinate scheduling with pharmacy staff, and make available IT personnel as required for installation and interface testing.

7.0 CONTRACTOR RESPONSIBILITIES
The contractor must comply with all VA security, privacy, and confidentiality requirements, including applicable provisions of VA Handbook 6500. All on-site contractor personnel must adhere to VA policies, obtain required badges, and follow facility procedures.

8.0 PERFORMANCE STANDARDS
The contractor must ensure:

All interfaces are fully functional and validated before go-live.

System uptime meets or exceeds vendor-published reliability standards.

Training is completed prior to operational use.

All deliverables meet VA requirements for quality and functionality.

9.0 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
The Government will accept deliverables upon:

Successful completion of installation and configuration.

Verified and documented interface functionality.

Completion of staff training and submission of training records.

Confirmation of stable system performance during initial operational use.

Draft Statement of Work 
 
HHS Fertility Data and Analysis Initiative Contract 
 
TASK REQUIREMENTS 
 
Task 1.0 Project Planning and Management 
 
Subtask 1.1: Kick-Off Meeting 
 
The Contractor shall meet with the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) and Project 
Officer (PO) within two (2) weeks after base and option year awards to ensure clariﬁcation 
of project goals, scope of work, routine communication standards, quality control 
standards, and deliverable and invoice submissions. The purpose of the meeting will be to 
discuss the objectives of the task order and to reach a common understanding of how the 
contractor will complete the work, the timelines, and the deliverable schedule for projects 
under this task order. The contractor shall be prepared to discuss critical activities 
requiring immediate attention and the project execution process. The COR and PO may 
also discuss anticipated requests with the contractor. The contractor may provide COR 
with a list of questions or issues in advance of the Kick-Off meeting. After the meeting, the 
contractor shall submit a memo to the COR summarizing the meeting and any decisions 
made.  
 
Deliverable(s): (A) Kick-Off Meeting (B) Meeting Summary Memo  
 
Subtask 1.2: Weekly COR and PO Meetings 
 
The contractor shall prepare a draft project management plan for the contract that details 
the intended approach to supporting the women’s health portfolio during the period of 
performance. The management plan shall be brief (up to 5 pages) and include: an overall 
approach to performing tasks and managing projects, plans for communication, processes 
for budget and cost estimation, and a plan for how to resolve any issues that present 
themselves over the task order period of performance (i.e., changes in key personnel, 
delays in obtaining critical data).  
 
The task order management plan shall specify: the contractor’s strategy for planning and 
preparing analytic products on short, medium, or long-term projects; how appropriate or 
necessary analysts, experts (including academic or other institutions), or sub-contractors 
are identiﬁed, and a strategy for conducting any data or policy analysis that may be 
requested for work products, including a process for receiving input from the COR and/or 
PO during the development of each product.  
 
The task order management plan shall also include draft elements for the monthly progress 
report and a template for the budget report (Subtask 1.4).  

 
Deliverable(s): (A) Draft Task Order Management Plan (B) Final Task Order Management 
Plan  
 
Subtask 1.3: Project Work Plan 
 
The COR and/or PO will submit a project request to the contractor for each speciﬁc project 
under this task order, including background information, research questions to be 
addressed, tasks, and a draft schedule of deliverables. Upon receipt of the request, the 
contractor may request a meeting with the COR and PO assigned to the project to 
determine the speciﬁc scope and proposed approach for each project. These meetings 
may take place via a video conferencing platform (e.g. Microsoft Teams, Zoom, Webex), 
email, conference call, or in conjunction with a weekly conference call (Subtask 1.4), and 
may occur as needed over the course of the project. Each project (See Task 2) will require a 
project work plan and a proposed subject matter team of experts.  
 
The contractor shall draft a project work plan for each project request, submit it to the COR 
and PO for review and approval within two (2) weeks of receipt, and host a meeting to 
discuss it. The project work plan shall detail the project's technical approach and schedule 
(see Task 2). Speciﬁcally, the project work plan shall include a description of the technical 
approach; any anticipated challenges to completing the project and how the contractor will 
address them; staffing and management responsibilities; and the allocation of project 
resources, including projected hours per staff member. The project work plan shall also 
include a timeline that identiﬁes the start and completion dates, as well as other 
milestones, for each deliverable speciﬁed in the plan. The project work plan shall be based 
on the project request from the COR and PO, as well as discussions and other decisions 
made at the project work plan meeting. The COR and PO may modify the project work plan, 
including completion dates, after consultation with the contractor, if needed. All approved 
project requests must be completed by the end of the contract's period of performance or 
discontinued by mutual agreement of the contractor, the COR, and the PO.  
 
Draft project work plans shall be submitted to the COR and PO for review and approval no 
later than two (2) weeks after the project work plan development meeting or otherwise 
agreed upon by the COR and PO. Upon incorporating comments from the COR and PO and 
ﬁnal approval by the COR and PO, a ﬁnal work plan shall be submitted to the COR and PO 
no later than one (2) weeks after ﬁnal approval.  
 
Deliverable(s): (A) Draft, (B) Final Project Work Plan(s), as needed  
 
Subtask 1.4: Standing Project Management Conference Calls  
 
Standing conference calls between the contractor, the COR, and the PO shall be 
scheduled within one week of the EDOC. The contractor, the COR, and the PO will decide 
on the periodicity of project management calls, which may change during the contract 
period to reﬂect HHS’s evolving needs, but should be assumed to occur weekly. During 

 
each call, the contractor shall be prepared to discuss any issues that have arisen since the 
last monthly progress report (Subtask 1.5) and to provide key updates on current projects, 
including any changes to the estimated budget or costs. The contractor shall develop an 
agenda prior to the call and, within one week, distribute the meeting minutes, including key 
points and decisions, to the COR and PO.  
 
Deliverable(s): (A) Standing Call Agendas (B) Standing Call Action Items Summaries  
 
Subtask 1.5: Monthly Progress Reports  
 
The contractor shall submit monthly progress reports (not to exceed four (4) pages, 
excluding tables or charts) outlining all work accomplished during the previous month. At a 
minimum, such reports should cover the following items: 
 
• Discussion of the progress in accomplishing the tasks speciﬁed in this task order. 
• Difficulties encountered and remedial action(s) taken.  
• Activities anticipated during the upcoming reporting period.  
• Personnel and other management changes.  
Monthly progress reports are due within the ﬁrst week of each month following the Kick-Off 
Meeting (Subtask 1.1), or as otherwise agreed upon by the COR and the contractor and 
shall be sent by the Principal Investigator directly to the COR via email. Monthly progress 
reports should specify the use of funds by project, including staff hours for each project 
and for overall administration of the task order.  
 
Deliverable(s): (A) Monthly Progress Reports  
 
Task 2.0 Data Collection, Analysis, Research, and Reporting 
 
The Contractor will develop a 5-year Strategic Plan and an annual Work Plan that outlines 
an approach for conducting an in-depth analysis of women’s and men’s fertility, infertility 
treatment, and linked infant health outcomes, including inpatient and outpatient data, as 
outlined in Tasks 2.0–4.0. 
 
The Contractor shall conduct nationally representative analyses of women’s and men’s 
fertility, infertility treatment, and linked infant health outcomes in support of HHS research 
priorities identiﬁed in the approved Strategic and Work Plans. 
 
Using standardized inpatient, outpatient, and linked research databases, the Contractor 
shall analyze factors associated with fertility and related health outcomes, including 
chronic conditions, disease severity, comorbidities, and complications, stratiﬁed by 
patient demographics (geographic location, socioeconomic status, race, and ethnicity), 
treatment patterns, environmental factors, and costs. 
 

 
The Contractor shall apply advanced analytic methods, including biostatistics, regression, 
microsimulation, and cost analyses, to assess fertility-related outcomes; estimate the 
costs, beneﬁts, and impacts of HHS policy proposals; identify innovations, market trends, 
opportunities, and knowledge gaps; evaluate HHS-wide initiatives; and provide adjusted, 
unadjusted, and routine analyses throughout the contract period. 
 
The Contractor shall provide technical assistance and related work products, including 
quantitative and qualitative analyses, written reports, data extracts, and routine brieﬁngs 
 
Deliverables: A. Access to ongoing fertility-related inpatient, outpatient, and linked data 
analyses, as speciﬁed in the approved Strategic and Work Plans; B. Annual and quarterly 
fertility analysis and outcome extracts; C. Technical assistance; D. Annual fertility data 
research and outcome reports; E. Advanced analytic methods speciﬁed in the Work Plan; 
F . Analyses of fertility-related health outcome relationships; and G. Fertility-related cost 
analyses. H. Develop 5-year Strategic Plan and Annual Work Plans 
 
Subtask 2.1: National HHS Fertility Data and Research Analysis   
 
Implement HHS Fertility Data and Analysis using a nationally representative research 
database to examine factors contributing to U.S. fertility, including the role of chronic 
conditions, stratiﬁed by patient demographics (geographic, race, ethnic, and 
socioeconomic factors), disease severity, comorbidities, complications, and resource 
utilization. 
 
The Contractor shall analyze and measure data using advanced data technologies and 
biostatistics methods, including regression analyses and microsimulation modeling, to 
address requested HHS research topics as speciﬁed in the Work Plan, such as: 
• Understanding the relationship between various pre-existing conditions and other 
risk factors, complications, fertility, and fertility treatment outcomes. 
• Estimating the costs and beneﬁts of women, men, and infant policy proposals 
under consideration by HHS 
• Work with HHS on women's and men's health innovations, market trends, and 
opportunities to identify knowledge gaps for quantitative and qualitative analysis. 
• Assessing outcomes that are the focus of HHS-wide initiatives.  
• The Contractor shall conduct ongoing comprehensive analyses of men, women, 
and infants addressing, at a minimum, the following domains: 
o Physical health and chronic conditions, including infertility, diabetes, endocrine 
disorders, cardiovascular disease, obesity, pregnancy complications, and long-term 
health outcomes. 
o Mental health conditions, including anxiety, depression, chronic stress, and 
associated pregnancy and long-term health outcomes. 
o Nutrition, including its relationship to men’s and women’s fertility, pregnancy 
outcomes, infant health, and chronic conditions. 

 
o Medication and Substance use and lifestyle factors, including exercise, tobacco, 
alcohol, and drug use before and during fertility treatment and pregnancy. 
o Access to care, including fertility care utilization, routine screenings, and ongoing 
management of chronic and reproductive health conditions. 
o Demographic factors, including healthcare access, environmental conditions, and 
socioeconomic factors affecting fertility and health outcomes. 
 
The Contractor shall provide adjusted and unadjusted analyses from a nationally 
representative, standardized inpatient database on women's and men’s fertility data, 
including linked infant health outcomes, annually, as described in the Strategic and Work 
plans. 
 
The Contractor shall analyze up-to-date data describing the relationships between 
women's and men’s fertility and associated health outcomes throughout the contract, and 
report ﬁndings on a routine basis. 
 
The Contractor shall analyze data and perform cost analyses of women's and men’s fertility 
healthcare, including fertility treatment and management, with respect to health 
outcomes. 
 
The Contractor shall provide technical assistance and develop work products, including 
various quantitative and qualitative analyses and associated written documents. 
 
The Contractor shall routinely analyze data to evaluate the relationship between women's 
and men’s fertility health across the continuum, including contributing factors such as 
treatment, management, environmental impact, and chronic conditions.  
 
The Contractor shall, in addition to the above analysis, conduct four focused drills and 
provide adjusted and unadjusted analyses of fertility data for women and men, along with 
supporting reports, briefs, or manuscripts, as directed by HHS. 
 
The Contractor shall develop an outcome dashboard to display annual rates of identiﬁed 
outcomes as identiﬁed in the Work Plan and provide all analysis tables, graphs, and 
visualizations associated.  
 
Task 2.1 Deliverable(s): A. Access to ongoing women's and men’s fertility inpatient and 
outpatient and infant linked data research analysis as speciﬁed in the agreed-upon 
Strategic and Work Plans B. Annual and Quarterly women's and men’s fertility analysis and 
outcome extract C. Technical assistance D. Annual women's and men’s fertility data 
research analysis outcome reports  E. Analyze and measure data using advanced methods 
speciﬁed in the Work Plan F . Analyze data describing relationships G. Analyze data 
describing cost H. Four (4) annual ad-hoc adjusted and unadjusted analyses on women's 
and men’s fertility annually. I. Provide Outcome Dashboard, updated annually, along with 
all analysis, tables, graphs, and visualizations.  

 
Subtask 2.2: HHS Fertility Impact Collaborative 
 
The Contractor shall establish and maintain the HHS Fertility Impact Collaborative (HHS 
FIC), a national learning network comprising at least 75 inpatient and outpatient healthcare 
sites, systems, clinics, and providers to implement and evaluate targeted strategies to 
address the root causes of infertility. The HHS FIC shall implement, support, and evaluate 
evidence-based fertility practices and interventions designed to address factors 
associated with infertility and improve fertility-related outcomes for women and men.  
 
The Contractor will provide a nationally representative sample and prioritize HHS FIC 
recruitment in diverse, underserved, rural, and tribal communities. 
 
The Contractor shall use the HHS FIC to collect, analyze, and report data on fertility-related 
outcomes; implementation of evidence-based practices; resource utilization; costs; 
medication use; screening, prevention, treatment; complications; and contributing chronic 
conditions.

Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought Notice 
 
Subject to FAR clause 52.215-3 entitled “Request for Information or Solicitation for Planning Purposes,” this 
announcement constitutes a Sources Sought Notice for information and planning purposes for qualified and 
experienced sources to provide a Billing Data Analysis and Reporting business intelligence to 
in support of Naval Computer and Telecommunications Area Master Station Atlantic (NCTAMSLANT) Financial 
Management Department. This is not a solicitation announcement for proposals and no contract will be awarded  
from this announcement. It is not to be construed in any way as a commitment by the Government for any 
purpose other than to gain the information requested, nor will the Government pay for the information  
submitted in response. The Government has determined the these supplies and services are commercial items as 
defined in FAR 2.101. Interested parties are encouraged to respond to this RFI/Sources Sought Notice.  
Scope 
The primary objective of this requirement is to provide NCTAMSLANT FM Department with a six (6) month 
subscription supply to a web-based billing analysis commercial off the shelf (COTS) product and associated web -
based product training and helpdesk technical support that are designed to allow NCTAMSLANT FM Department 
to continue to meet the Department of Defense (DOD) and Department of the Navy (DON) Financial Improvement 
and Audit Readiness (FIAR) requirements, as well as those internal requirements as outlined in COMNAVIDFOR 
M-2066.1. 
 
This requirement is necessary to ensure NCTAMSLANT N00FM BCO Billing Branch has an automated and 
systematic method of processing external and internal data related to telecommunications billing for the purpose of 
reporting and analytical capabilities via a SQL compliant database to aggregate data from disparate data sources to a 
configurable business intelligence software platform that users interact with via their web browser.  
NCTAMSLANT Billing Branch personnel imports multiple different data sources into the current platform, which is 
then processed via specifications identified by the agency. A multi-user, highly scalable software solution will 
compile numerous billing inputs received from various vendors and then sort, categorize, and distribute data as 
needed by any approved NCTAMSLANT command/unit and/or user. 
 
Any potential contract resulting from this RFI/Sources Sought Notice is anticipated to be a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) 
contract. See the draft list of specifications posted with this notice for additional details.  
 
NAICS Code 
The anticipated NAICS code for this requirement is anticipated to be 541511 – Custom Computer Programming, 
The anticipated product supply code (PSC) 7A21, It & Telecom – Business Application Software. 
 
This is a follow on requirement. 
 
Required Delivery Date 
The anticipated delivery date for this 28 September 2026. This will be a s-x-month base subscription contract. PoP: 
28 Sep 2026 - 27 Mar 2027. 
Capabilities Statement 
 
This is a market research tool. The input provided will help the Navy ascertain the interest, capability, and capacity 
of potential businesses. If you are an interested business, FLCN appreciates your assistance in providing a  
capabilities statement addressing the items below. Standard company brochures will not be reviewed. Submissions 

are not to exceed four standard typewritten pages. All technical questions and inquiries may be submitted within the 
response. 
 
1. Full business name, address, point of contact, telephone number, and e-mail address 
2. Contractor and Government Entity (CAGE) code 
3. Size of business: Large Business, Small Business, Small Disadvantaged, 8(a), HubZone, Woman-owned, 
Service Disabled Veteran-Owned, or other category 
4. If the items can be obtained from a GSA or SeaPort-e contract vehicle, provide the applicable contract number. If 
only some items can be obtained, verify which items can/cannot be obtained from GSA contract.  
 
5. Describe your ability to support the scope of the requirement listed in this notice and in the provided draft list of 
specifications. Documentation of technical qualifications and authorized reseller letters must be presented in

NCTAMSLANT N00FM BCO BUSINESS INTELLIGENCE TOOL;  
   SUBSCRIPTION AND SUPPORT SERVICES 
PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
 
1.0 INTRODUCTION:  Naval Computer and Telecommunications Area Master Station Atlantic 
(NCTAMSLANT) Financial Management Department, BCO Billing Branch, requires a 6-
month subscription to a web-based Enhanced Billing Data Analysis and Reporting 
business intelligence tool required to conduct aggregation, analysis, and reporting of 
telecommunications billing data in order to improve reimbursable customer funding 
recapture rates, track expenditure rates, maximize buying power, provide on-time 
command service usage reports, and sustain auditable financial conditions.   
 
2.0 BACKGROUND:  The mission of NCTAMSLANT Base Communications Office (BCO) is to 
provide day-to-day management, administration, operations, maintenance and 
reporting of the existing Base C2 communications services, whether leased or 
government-owned, to all command activities within our area of responsibility. In 
accordance with COMNAVIDFOR M-2066.1 and all other applicable regulations and 
directives, the BCO requires reimbursement from non-mission customers for 
incremental communication services, including tolls, Centrex, Local Exchange Carrier 
(LEC) and other unique customer service requirements.   
Currently, NCTAMSLANT N00FM utilizes a commercial off the shelf (COTS) web-based 
platform to conduct data aggregation, analysis, and reporting via CAC-enabled access.  
An automated processing and reporting suite includes dashboards, drilldowns, and 
historical and predictive analysis functions and capabilities; ensuring all reporting 
requirements as identified by the agency are met. The current COTS product has the 
capability to effectively and efficiently merge, process, and manage all necessary and 
pertinent agency and vendor data sources into one single source.  It is provided utilizing 
a subscription service and hosted in a DFAR 252.204-7012 (Safeguarding of Covered 
Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting) compliant environment.  
 

3.0 REQUIREMENT:  NCTAMSLANT FM Department intends to acquire a 6-month 
subscription service to a web-based billing analysis commercial off the shelf (COTS) 
product and associated web-based product training and helpdesk technical support 
services that are designed to allow NCTAMSLANT FM Department to continue to meet 
the Department of Defense (DOD) and Department of the Navy (DON) Financial 
Improvement and Audit Readiness (FIAR) requirements, as well as those internal 
requirements as outlined in COMNAVIDFOR M-2066.1. 
 
This requirement is necessary to ensure NCTAMSLANT N00FM BCO Billing Branch has an 
automated and systematic method of processing external and internal data related to 
telecommunications billing for the purpose of reporting and analytical capabilities via a 
SQL compliant database to aggregate data from disparate data sources to a configurable 
business intelligence software platform that users interact with via their web browser. 
NCTAMSLANT Billing Branch personnel imports multiple unique data sources into the 
current platform, which is then processed via specifications identified by the agency.  A 
multi-user, highly scalable software solution will compile numerous billing inputs 
received from various vendors and then sort, categorize, and distribute data as needed 
by any approved NCTAMSLANT command/unit and/or user.   
3.1 Configuration and implementation in accordance with the agency’s 
specifications to include: 
3.1.1 SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS 
 
 Management of all data repositories including Lines & Circuits 
inventory, Job Order Numbers, Bases and Commands supported, 
and all other supporting data repositories 
 Management and tracking of Telephone Control Officers (TCOs) 
and financial POCs 
 Importing and tracking status of multiple data sources including 
commercial services, government owned switch services, and toll 
usage data via a universal import template 
 Tracking of successfully processed files 
 Capability of providing real-time ad-hoc and summary reports  
 View of fallout records prior to finalizing monthly reports 
 Viewing and managing command customer accounts and 
reporting products 
 Validation capability of command usage reports 
 Data and cost adjustments capability 
 Year to Date expense reporting  
 Audit tracking capability on changes made by users 

 Mass update capability  
 Capability of mass distributing emails, with or without 
attachments, to all POCs 
 Capability of providing Funds Status view 
 Providing email notifications of released billing usage reports, as 
well as undeliverable email notifications  
 Capability of assigning multiple levels of user access 
 CAC-enabled access via NMCI web browser ensuring security 
controls are being maintained 
 Access to archived files 
 Data back up to occur on a continuous basis 
 
3.1.2 SUPPORT REQUIREMENTS 
 
 Web-based product training 
 Training for super-users as necessary 
 Unlimited access to vendor trouble help desk including system 
access issues 
 User Desk Top Guides and Manuals for all processes 
 
NCTAMSLANT Billing Branch will provide Government Furnished Information (GFI) 
legacy data as the initial source of data input for this requirement.

Introduction 
 
The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) hereby notifies the following 
Procurement O pportunity in accordance wit h the Procedure for NATO Competitive 
Procurement ( link). This notification is issued to foster open and fair competition among 
eligible vendors from participating nations. This notification does not constitute a commitment 
to award a contract. 
 
Vendors are invited to review the requirements described herein and to prepare for bid 
compilation in accordance with the instructions provided in this notification and subsequent 
solicitation documentation. All interested vendors are reminded that timely registration and 
compliance with eligibility requirements are essential, as deadlines for submission may not be 
extended. Vendors are advised to regularly check for updates to this notification. 
 
This opportunity reflects NATO’s commitment to transparency, equal treatment of suppliers, 
and the efficient delivery of goods, works, and services in support of NATO missions and 
participating nations. 
 
All eligible and responsible sources may submit a quotation, bid, or proposal, which shall be 
considered by the NCIA. 
 
1. Title of Procurement Opportunity 
 
“Provision of Global Seamless Vector Basemap Data” 
 
2. Description of Requirement 
 
This procurement opportunity will have as delivery a Global Seamless Vector Basemap Data 
Package compliant with STANAG 2592
 NATO Geospatial Information Framework (NGIF) and 
its relevant data schema to serve as a foundation base for any additional authoritative national 
geospatial data and directly support NATO Operations, Missions or other Activities. 
 
The data is expected to support NATO in stated geospatial use cases of web mapping, rapid 
mapping, geospatial analysis, routing and geolocation services. 
 
The Package will consist of several products: 
 
 The actual vector data using purchaser furnished and open sources, namely current 
Overture Maps conflated with vendor furnished data adding value specifically to the 
stated geospatial use cases will form the centrepiece. The vector data shall consist of 
all relevant geospatial layers and attributes to act as a global seamless basemap and 
support stated geospatial use cases relevant to NATO’s mission.It shall reflect NATO’s 
geopolitical view  in roman script and be compatible with NATO’s Esri technology-
based enterprise GIS solution, CoreGIS.  
 P rofessional symbolization will coherently style  the dataset at specified scales ready 
for use in CoreGIS.  
 Derived products in form of raster and vector caches to defined styles, routable 
networks and geolocator files will be produced from and coherent to the vector data.  
 Metadata describing source and resulting data, processes, quality assurance and 
translation to NGIF will complete the package. 
The data license is required to cover NATO and Non-NATO Entities (NNEs) in support of any 
North Atlantic Council ( NAC) approved activity. Licensing for National use will be added as 
options.

a. Participation in this Procurement Opportunity is restricted to vendors from

b. This restriction applies to the eligibility of the vendors only and does not require

within participating nations.

for this Procurement Opportunity as of the Anticipated Solicitation Release Date 
as follows: 
 
i. Indicating your interest by emailing the Point of Contact listed above to 
request being added to the bidder’s list and receive the solicitation. 
ii. no Declaration of Eligibility (DoE) required.

The purpose of this synopsis is to announce the Health and Human Services (HHS) intent 
to negotiate a Firm Fixed Price sole source contract with Webﬁrst, Inc. located at 9200 
Corporate Boulevard Suite 375, Rockville, MD 20850-3886, to continue providing the HHS 
with Digital Communications Support for a six (6) month period. 
Only one (1) source, Webﬁrst, Inc, is available to fulﬁll the Government’s requirement for 
these services in an interim period to provide the needed digital communications support. 
This action will support a short-term, six (6) month bridge to allow for adequate time to re-
complete the existing order HHSN316201200189W/75N98122F00001 with a current 
expiration date of September 28
th, 2026, maximize future competition, and prevent a lapse 
in critical services. 
ASPA Digital manages HHS digital communications operations and public-facing digital 
services. The current SOW requires the contractor to support high-tempo, mission-facing 
services including Service Desk operations, Drupal enterprise content publishing, website 
and application modernization, analytics, accessibility, security, and program 
management. The current Service Desk supports more than 250 content owners across all 
ASPA Digital-managed websites, manages approximately 120 requests per week, 
processes approximately 300 operations and maintenance tickets per month, and 
supports approximately 10 to 15 projects per month. Some requests must be completed 
within half an hour. Disrupting these services during a six-month bridge would create 
avoidable operational risk. 
The incumbent contractor has current knowledge of ASPA’s workﬂows, systems, 
governance documents, service queues, ongoing projects, content publishing processes, 
Drupal environment, AWS environment, analytics toolchain, security requirements, and 
stakeholder operating tempo. A new contractor would need to complete transition 
activities, onboarding, suitability and access processes, system familiarization, knowledge 
transfer, documentation review, and coordination with incumbent staff. The SOW itself 
contemplates transition and phase-in activities, including coordination with the 
incumbent, uninterrupted service delivery, knowledge transfer, access conﬁrmation, and 
full performance no later than 60 days after the phase-in start date. For a six-month bridge, 
a 60-day phase-in followed by transition-out activities would consume a material portion of 
the performance period and would duplicate costs without a commensurate beneﬁt to the 
Government. 
The work also involves sensitive operational and security responsibilities. Contractor 
personnel require appropriate background investigations, HSPD-12/PIV compliance, roster 
management, and access to HHS information systems. The contractor must support 
security, privacy, FISMA, ATO, FedRAMP , NIST, encryption, incident response, audit logging, 

and related controls. Onboarding a different contractor for a six-month interval would 
increase transition risk, delay productive performance, and require duplicative system 
access and security coordination that would not improve the Government’s long-term 
competitive posture. 
The bridge is a short-term continuity action while the Government completes the 
competitive BPA. The Government will compete for the follow-on BPA and use the bridge 
period to complete requirements validation, market engagement, solicitation, evaluation, 
award, and transition planning. 
The Government considered whether a new contractor could reasonably assume the 
requirement for the six-month bridge. Although multiple ﬁrms may be capable of 
performing these services under a full competitive acquisition with adequate transition 
time, the short bridge period and continuity needs make award to a new contractor 
inefficient and operationally risky. The future BPA will be competed to allow adequate time 
for meaningful industry participation and transition. 
For the reasons stated above, awarding the bridge contract to the proposed vendor is in the 
best interests of the Government for this intermediary period. 
The total estimated cost of this service is $4,721,667.00 for a six (6) month period. 
THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS, however, interested 
ﬁrms may submit a capability statement in response to the above requirement with pricing 
information by August 3, 2026 @ 2:00 PM Eastern Time to Thien Nguyen, Contracting 
Officer, Email: thien.nguyen@hhs.gov . A determination not to open competition based 
responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

Requirements Document

Renewal of Splunk Cloud Platform and Enterprise Security Subscription Services for Indian Health Service

1. Purpose

This Requirements Document is prepared in support of an acquisition package for the Indian Health Service (IHS) to obtain continued subscription access to the existing Splunk cloud environment used for cybersecurity monitoring, log management, analytics, and related security operations. This document defines the Government's minimum requirements for use in solicitation development, evaluation, and award documentation.

2. Requirement Overview

IHS requires renewal of the current Splunk subscription environment to maintain continuity of cybersecurity operations and avoid interruption to enterprise monitoring and analysis capabilities. The requirement consists of cloud platform subscription capacity, security functionality, storage capacity, archive capacity, and associated support entitlements necessary to continue operations in the existing environment.

This is a renewal requirement for an existing operational environment. The acquisition is intended to preserve the current deployed capability and maintain uninterrupted access throughout the performance period.

3. Background

IHS uses a Splunk-based cloud environment to support enterprise cybersecurity and security operations activities. The current environment includes hosted platform capabilities, Enterprise Security functionality, cloud data storage, dynamic data archive capacity, and support features associated with the subscribed services.

The current environment is hosted in GovCloud (US East). The platform subscription reflects federal compliance impact level controls and encryption at rest, and the platform environment is provisioned in a FedRAMP Moderate environment.

4. Acquisition Objective

The objective of this acquisition is to secure a one-year renewal of the existing Splunk cloud subscription environment and associated support services so that IHS can continue ongoing cybersecurity operations without disruption.

5. Period of Performance

The required period of performance is July 22, 2026 through July 21, 2027.

6. Place of Performance

Performance shall be primarily remote as an electronically delivered cloud subscription service. The required hosting environment shall be GovCloud (US East).

7. Minimum Requirements

The contractor shall provide a renewal solution that satisfies all of the following minimum requirements:

Splunk Cloud Platform subscription with federal compliance impact level controls, encryption at rest, and Premium Success Plan.

Provisioning in GovCloud (US East).

FedRAMP Moderate environment provisioning for the applicable platform subscription.

Platform capacity of 404 SVC.

Splunk Enterprise Security Essentials with Premium Success Plan.

Enterprise Security capacity of 404 SVC.

Splunk Cloud data storage capacity in 500 GB increments totaling 11,680 units.

Splunk Cloud dynamic data archive capacity in 500 GB increments totaling 5,300 units.

Support entitlements associated with the required subscriptions.

Continuity of the current operational environment with no lapse in subscription coverage.

For this requirement, SVC refers to a unit of cloud capability that includes compute, memory, and I/O resources.

8. Required Contractor Capabilities

The contractor shall:

Be authorized to provide the required subscriptions and renewals for U.S. Federal customers.

Provide only genuine and fully supported subscriptions.

Renew the identified subscriptions for the full period of performance.

Maintain the required hosting, compliance, encryption, and support characteristics of the existing environment.

Coordinate all administrative actions necessary to activate the renewal and prevent service interruption.

Provide all documentation necessary to confirm successful renewal and continued support coverage.

9. Functional Requirements

The offered solution shall:

Support continuation of enterprise cybersecurity monitoring and log analysis functions.

Maintain access to the existing hosted platform environment.

Maintain access to Enterprise Security capabilities associated with the subscribed platform.

Maintain the required data storage and archive capacities.

Maintain applicable support and success plan entitlements included with the subscriptions.

10. Deliverables

The successful contractor shall provide the following deliverables:

Active subscription renewal for all required components.

Confirmation of subscription activation and effective coverage dates.

Documentation identifying renewed products, quantities, capacities, and support entitlements.

Access to included support and any associated subscription-based service entitlements.

11. Acceptance Criteria

The Government will consider the requirement successfully fulfilled when:

All required subscription components have been renewed.

Coverage is active for the entire period of performance.

The renewed environment matches the required hosting environment, capacity levels, and support features.

There is no lapse or interruption in operational service.

Any variance from the required environment, capacity, support, or performance period shall be resolved prior to Government acceptance.

12. Security Requirements

The contractor shall provide subscriptions that preserve the federal compliance impact level controls and encryption-at-rest capabilities associated with the current environment. The platform subscription shall remain provisioned in the required government cloud environment and support continued IHS cybersecurity operations.

13. Compatibility and Continuity Requirements

This acquisition is for renewal of an existing environment. The offered solution shall be fully compatible with the current IHS Splunk deployment and shall preserve continuity of service, existing subscribed capacities, and associated support coverage for the full performance period.

14. Quotation Submission Requirements

Offerors responding to the solicitation should provide sufficient detail to demonstrate compliance with this Requirements Document. At a minimum, quotations should:

Identify the offered subscriptions and associated product descriptions.

Confirm the offered solution is a renewal of the existing environment.

Confirm compliance with all hosting, capacity, security, and support requirements.

Identify any assumptions or Government information needed to process the renewal.

Demonstrate authorization to provide the required subscriptions for Federal use.

15. Evaluation Considerations

For solicitation purposes, quotations may be evaluated for technical acceptability based on the extent to which the quotation demonstrates compliance with the requirements in this document, including:

Ability to provide the required renewal subscriptions.

Ability to meet hosting and security environment requirements.

Ability to provide the required capacities and support entitlements.

Ability to ensure continuity of service throughout the renewal term.

16. Non-Personal Services

This requirement is for non-personal services. Contractor personnel performing under any resulting order shall not be considered Government employees for any purpose.

17. Government Points of Contact

The Contracting Officer will be identified in the solicitation. A Contracting Officer's Representative may be designated after award, if required.

BACKGROUND

The Veterans Canteen Service (VCS) was statutorily established on August 7, 1946, under 38 U.S.C. Ch. 78 to provide America’s Veterans enrolled in VA’s healthcare system, their families, survivors, caregivers, and VA employees with reasonably priced merchandise and services essential to their comfort, health, and wellbeing. With our many retail stores, cafés and coffee shops across the country, we serve those who have served our country. Our Canteens are whole health spaces for Veterans to connect, relax, share and care for themselves in an environment that is their benefit. We are proud to Serve America’s Veterans and those who provide for their care.

Our Mission

To provide America’s Veterans, enrolled in VA’s Health Care System, their families, caregivers, VA employees, volunteers, and visitors reasonably priced merchandise and services essential to their comfort, health and well-being.

Our Vision

As an integral part of the VA community, be an efficient, innovative, customer-driven, environmentally friendly organization consistently delivering merchandise and services of exceptional quality and value by a knowledgeable, friendly and enthusiastic team that takes pride in our mission.

Giving Back

VCS is proud to be part of the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. We are a self-sustaining entity providing merchandise and services to Veterans enrolled in VA’s healthcare system, their families, caregivers, VA employees, volunteers and visitors. We are honored to give back to the VA community through many programs established for the health and well-being of our nation’s heroes. Revenues generated from VCS are used to support a variety of programs, such as VA’s Rehabilitation Games, Fisher Houses, Poly-Trauma Centers for Operation Iraqi Freedom(OIF)/ Operation Enduring Freedom (OEF)/Operation New Dawn(OIF/OEF/OND) Veterans, disaster relief efforts, Substance Abuse Cessation, VA’s Homelessness initiatives, Women Veterans, Veteran Suicide Prevention and other activities. 

VCS currently operates nationwide on Oracle Retail Merchandising System (RMS) v13, and Store Inventory Management (SIM) hosted on legacy on-premises application servers that do not meet the current Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Office of Information and Technology (OIT) Security requirements. To achieve compliance, VCS must implement a modernized replacement system under an accelerated implementation timeline. 

This Performance Work Statement (PWS) outlines the requirements, tasks, deliverables, and performance standards to transition from the current on-premises Oracle Retail RMS and SIM systems to Oracle Retail Merchandising Foundation Cloud Services (MFCS) and Oracle Retail Store Inventory and Operations Cloud Services (SIOCS) . FedRAMP compliance and associated FedRAMP authorization activities shall not be required under this contract.

Introduction

This Request for Information (RFI) is for planning purposes only and shall not be considered an Invitation for Bid, Request for Task Execution Plan, Request for Quotation or a Request for Proposal. Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services described in this RFI. Your response to this RFI will be treated only as information for the Government to consider.  You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this RFI. This request does not constitute a solicitation for proposals or the authority to enter into negotiations to award a contract. No funds have been authorized, appropriated or received for this effort. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response. The Government does not intend to pay for the information submitted in response to this RFI The information provided may be used by VA in developing its acquisition strategy and Product Description (PD).

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 541519 with a size standard of 150 employees.

The VA Technology Acquisition Center (TAC) is seeking response to develop its acquisition strategy for a proposed Firm Fixed Priced Order for NTP Rhapsody Maintenance, Support and Ongoing Sustainment Services. Please see attached draft Product Description.

 Submittal Information:

All responsible sources may submit a response in accordance with the information below.

There is a page limitation for this RFI of five pages. The Government will not review any other information or attachments included, that are in excess of the five-page limit. NO MARKETING MATERIALS ARE ALLOWED AS PART OF THIS RFI. Generic capability statements will not be accepted or reviewed. Your response must address capabilities specific to the services required in the attached PD and must include the following:

Name of Company

Existing Contractual Vehicles (NASA SEWP or other GWAC, GSA FSS or MAC)

Provide a summary of your capability to meet the requirements identified in the entirety of section 1.0 and all subsections contained within the draft PD:

Written evidence of authorized resellers status. Specifically, a letter from the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) Rhapsody Corepoint. Any responses without such evidence from the OEM will not be considered.

For SDVOSB status consideration :Your company’s intent and ability to meet the set aside requirement in accordance with VAAR 852.219-73 (JAN 2023) (DEVIATION) VA Notice of Total Set-Aside For Certified SDVOSBs and 13 CFR §125.6, which states the contractor will not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the government to the prime for contract performance to firms that are not certified SDVOSBs listed in the SBA certification database (excluding direct costs to the extent they are not the principal purpose of the acquisition and the SDVOSB/VOSB does not provide the service, such as airline travel, cloud computing services, or mass media purchases). When a contract includes both services and supplies, the 50 percent limitation shall apply only to the service portion of the contract. 

Has the draft PD provided sufficient detail to describe the technical requirements that encompass the software development and production operations support services to be performed under this effort. 

______ YES _______ NO (if No, answer question f)

If “NO”, please provide your technical comments/recommendations on elements of the draft PD that may contribute to a more accurate proposal submission and efficient, cost-effective effort.

Please submit the below requested information by 11:00 AM Eastern Time on July 23, 2026, via email to Christine Keen-Deputy, Contract Specialist, at Christine.Keen-Deputy@va.gov. VA reserves the right not to respond to any, all, or select responses or materials submitted. All current VA requirements identified herein or in the attached draft PD are subject to change at any time.

 PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) National Teleradiology Program (NTP) strives to provide high quality, effective, and efficient Radiology Services for our Nation’s Veterans. In support of that mission, NTP requires software licensing that includes maintenance and support services for the previously procured, NTP Health Level 7 (HL7) Integration System.

The Contractor shall provide software licensing that includes maintenance, support and ongoing sustainment for the existing NTP Rhapsody Corepoint system. This requirement includes both the Production and Pre-Production environment. Rhapsody Corepoint, also known as the Corepoint Integration Engine (CIE), is a modular platform that enables healthcare organizations to efficiently exchange and integrate clinical data across disparate systems. NTP requires Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Rhapsody Corepoint licenses and support. The required Rhapsody Corepoint shall include software, software updates/patches, and technical support services required to maintain the system and all associated components to guarantee 99.9% uptime. The Contractor shall provide access to the latest version of Rhapsody Corepoint software to include latest updates, patches, upgrades, and or revisions as they are released. The Contractor shall ensure that all Rhapsody Corepoint licenses procured under this contract shall not expire during the duration of the contract.

Contractor shall be responsible for supporting all components of the system, whether they are the OEM or utilizing the system as a component to the comprehensive NTP PACS solution. This includes any integration components into the complete NTP PACS solution.  

In this requirement we are also requiring professional service hours for configuration of both Pre-Production and Production environment for changes needed to allow for additional Telemammography, Federal Electronic Health Record (FEHR) go lives, and HL7 version upgrades happening VA wide. The professional service hours are covering for the configuration work, testing and go live events for these changes that will be needed in the environment.  

Components of the system that shall be included for the maintenance and support mentioned above includes the following: 

 

HELP DESK AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT

The Contractor shall provide a level 1 and a level 2 technical support desk. Level 1 support staff shall be available via phone 24x7x365. Level 2 support shall be available within a half hour 24x7x365. Level 1 shall be capable of resolving 90% of typical service requests and Level 2 shall be able to handle 99% of requests and manage system configuration changes and site setup.  

A failure is deemed critical if it prevents the timely provision of teleradiology service.  

The Contractor shall provide preventive maintenance by monitoring and managing system patching on all Corepoint servers. The Contractor shall proactively monitor system health with real-time server status monitoring and shall take corrective/preventive action when system performance is outside of normal operating limits. The Contractor shall be responsible for ongoing monitoring of system health and proactively optimize functioning of the system. Any expected downtime for PMs, patching, upgrades shall be coordinated with NTP staff in advance with at least 48-hour notice and shall not exceed 15 minutes. Any extended downtime longer than 15 minutes, shall be coordinated with the Contracting Officer’s Representative and NTP leadership at least 7 days in advance. Critical system messages shall also be sent to vhantpsupport@va.gov to ensure that NTP is advised of an issue.

Software updates for security vulnerability remediations shall be provided at no charge for the duration of this contract in compliance with Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Binding Operational Directives. 

HL7 Support

The Contractor shall provide ongoing HL7 support for link/message troubleshooting/resolution, configuration support for HL7 version changes across all NTP sites, HL7 activations for new facilities, Veterans Health Information System and Technology Architecture (VistA) and Oracle Health interface specification changes, and site-specific mapping for NTP configuration.

The Contractor shall ensure that the system functions in conformance with the latest requirements of National Fire Protection Association (NFPA)-99, The Joint Commission, National Electric Code, Federal and VA information security specifications and requirements as applicable. The system shall be maintained such that it meets the performance specifications as established in the OEM’s technical specifications.

CONTRACTOR QUALITY CONTROL PROGRAM (QCP)

The Contractor shall establish and maintain quality control to ensure all contract requirements are met. The contractor's QCP shall include the following or have incorporated into during performance of contract:

The contractor shall provide a monthly downtime report identifying any facilities where the performance benchmark was not met (99.9% uptime). This is to be provided as a component of monthly invoicing.

The contractor shall provide an on-line web portal for tracking work orders generated by NTP and provide access to NTP to submit tickets.  

The contractor shall have an on-line 24x7 proactive monitoring tool that identifies issues with critical system processes. There are existing monitoring and alerts in Dynatrace and email notification that must be kept and maintained.  Corrective action shall be taken as a result of a process triggering an alert.  The issue that resulted in the alert must be fixed. 

The Contractor shall have methods of identifying and preventing communication breakdowns and provide alternative communications in the event of a breakdown of the communication system.

PERSONNEL

"Fully Qualified" is based upon authorized OEM training and on experience in the field. For training, the Field Service Engineer(FSE(s)) shall successfully complete a formalized training program with the OEM and shall be currently approved by OEM to work on the system and have full rights to software code.

The FSEs shall be authorized by the Contractor to perform the services. All work shall be performed by "Fully Qualified" competent FSEs. The Contractor shall provide written assurance of the competency of their personnel and a list of credentials of approved FSEs. 

ONBOARDING SUPPORT

The Contractor shall assist with the on-boarding process for VA access and for individual system/environment access for all Contractor staff supporting NTP Rhapsody. 

The Contractor shall: 

Provide a Resource Management Report spreadsheet for all personnel currently and formerly assigned that lists:

Personnel Identity Verification (PIV) Expiration

U.S. Geological Survey
