  S tatement of Work 
Coastal Change Mapping Utilizing SpatioTemporal Asset Catalogs (STAC) 
I. General Information 
A. Introduction 
Coastal change hazards from erosion and flooding pose threats to infrastructure and natural 
resources throughout the Nation. A primary goal of the U.S. Geological Survey (U SGS), Pacific 
Coastal and Marine Science Center (PCMSC) is to provide critical information regarding coastal 
change hazards to support preparedness, emergency response, and the protection of people and 
resources in coastal and ocean environments. 
USGS PCMSC currently utilizes CoastSeg, a machine-learning- based shoreline mapping tool 
operating within the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform. Enabling CoastSeg to incorporate 
satellite imagery available through publicly accessible SpatioTemporal Asset Catalogs (STAC), 
including Landsat and Sentinel -2 datasets, will provide increased flexibility and potential cost 
efficiencies. 
The Contractor shall develop, validate, document, and deliver a STAC -based shoreline change 
measurement capability for the CoastSeg workflow. Initial development and validation shall focus 
on selected sites along the western and northern Alaskan coast to support hazard assessments in 
that region. 
B. Background 
Coastal changes resulting from shoreline erosion and flooding are pervasive hazards, particularly 
in low -lying coastal regions subject to storms. Documenting rates and spatial distribution of 
erosion and flooding supports natural resource management, infra structure risk assessments, and 
development planning. 
Although existing satellite-based techniques, including CoastSat and CoastSeg, provide tools for 
mapping coastal change, the current CoastSeg workflow does not utilize publicly available STAC-
hosted imagery. Incorporating STAC resources into a newly forked Git repository of CoastSeg on 
a USGS -approved Git hosting platform for scientific software releases will allow PCMSC to 
evaluate coastal change using publicly accessible datasets without reliance on proprietary 
processing environments, thereby adding flexibility and potential cost efficiencies  to shoreline 
change analyses. 
Upon successful development and validation, PCMSC will publish and use the STAC -enabled 
workflows developed and published on a USGS -approved Git hosting platform for scientific 
software releases to evaluate coastal change patterns and rates throughout Alaska. 
DOI, USGS RFQ# 140G0326Q0165  Software Development Services for Coastal Remote Sensing
Page 5 of 44

C. Applicable Model and Data Resources 
The model identified for use in this work is CoastSeg, which is described in 
[https://joss.theoj.org/papers/10.21105/joss.06683] and available at 
[https://github.com/SatelliteShorelines/CoastSeg]. This model relies on deep learning principles, 
satellite imagery analyses, coastal oceanographic theory, and cartographic sciences to 
characterize shoreline positions and coastal change. 
Satellite imagery data will be sourced from the STAC developed by the USGS EROS Data 
Center [https://www.usgs.gov/landsat-missions/spatiotemporal-asset-catalog-stac].  
II. Scope of Work 
The purpose of this work is to develop a workflow to incorporate satellite imagery available from 
the STAC data catalogs to provide cost -effective and time-efficient data processing of shoreline 
position information. The workflow will be developed within a forked copy of CoastSeg a USGS-
approved Git hosting platform for scientific software. This extension of the model will require 
code development, validation and optimization, and detailed understanding of data architectures 
and cartographic sciences. PCMSC will oversee these developments, and the satellite imagery will 
be accessed through both Google Earth Engine and the USGS STAC to test and compare CoastSeg 
workflows. PCMSC will provide all lidar, photogrammetry and satellite -derived shoreline 
positions for comparisons and model validation. The remaining development of the STAC -based 
tool, its application and optimization, and the final reporting to PCMSC will be the responsibility 
of the contractor. 
The Contractor shall extend the CoastSeg workflow to incorporate satellite imagery available 
through STAC data catalogs. 
This effort shall include: 
a. Developing code, tools and training data to enhance CoastSeg workflows 
available on a USGS-approved Git hosting platform for scientific software for use 
with STAC-derived imagery 
b. Developing and implementing model validation analyses and comparisons with 
GEE workflows. 
c. Applying the optimized model to ten Alaska test sites to highlight model result 
characteristics and limitations (sites listed in Table 1 below). 
d. Review and publication of code consistent with USGS Survey Manual IM OSQI 
2019-01 (https://www.usgs.gov/survey-manual/im-osqi-2019-01-review-and-
approval-scientific-software-release). 
e. Providing documentation of methods, inputs, code, and results in formats and 
styles suitable for routine use by PCMSC in the future and for the academic 
publication of the results. 
DOI, USGS RFQ# 140G0326Q0165  Software Development Services for Coastal Remote Sensing
Page 6 of 44

The Government will provide lidar, photogrammetry, and satellite -derived shoreline datasets for 
validation purposes and will provide technical oversight. The Contractor is responsible for all 
development, validation analysis, documentation, and final deliverables. 
III. Technical Requirements 
The Contractor shall: 
1. Conduct the extension of the CoastSeg workflows to incorporate STAC-derived imagery and 
use selected Alaska coastline segments for comparison and validation by:

review-and-approval-scientific-software-release). 
e. Providing documentation of methods, inputs, code, and results in formats and

AI-Enabled Manpower Modeling and Readiness Optimization Solution 
 
Issuing Organization: United States Marine Corps Forces Reserve (MARFORRES)  
 
Requiring Activities: MFR G-1 (Manpower) and Marine Corps Individual Reserve Support 
Activity (MCIRSA)  
 
Document Type: Request for Information / Sources Sought (Market Research)  
Classiﬁcation: Controlled Unclassiﬁed Information (CUI)  
Date: 07/16/2026  
Response Due: 07/30/2026 
Point of Contact: jordyn.edwards@usmc.mil and parren.tatum.civ@usmc.mil 
 
Introduction/Purpose 
 
The Government is conducting market research to identify qualiﬁed sources capable of 
designing, developing, and delivering an AI-enabled software solution for manpower 
modeling, readiness analytics, and personnel allocation optimization in support of Marine 
Corps Reserve mobilization operations. Responses will help the Government understand 
available commercial and custom solutions, reﬁne requirements, estimate cost and 
schedule, and shape a future acquisition strategy. 
 
Background 
 
The Marine Corps Reserve must rapidly assess unit readiness and allocate individual 
Reserve Marines, including the Individual Ready Reserve (IRR) and Selected Marine Corps 
Reserve (SMCR), against validated requirements during mobilization. Today, these 
processes rely heavily on manual data pulls from multiple legacy personnel systems, are 
labor-intensive, and provide limited real-time visibility. Decision-makers lack a single, 
integrated tool that can aggregate data across systems and produce timely, explainable 
recommendations. 
 
The Government seeks a modern, data-driven software capability that consolidates two 
related mission needs into a single solution: 
 
• Unit/Aggregate Readiness Analytics: Understanding, diagnosing, and forecasting the 
readiness of Reserve units. 
 
• Individual Allocation Optimization: Tracking available personnel inventory and 
matching the best-qualiﬁed Marine to the correct billet. 
 
Scope of Anticipated Work 
 

1. Data Integration 
 
Establish secure, read-capable data connections (APIs or approved data pipelines) to 
Government authoritative personnel and readiness systems (legacy mainframe and 
modern systems). 
 
Ingest and normalize both structured data (personnel records, billet structure, readiness 
status) and unstructured data (e.g., awards, training history, civilian employment 
information). 
 
Deliver a data dictionary and maintain data quality/validation controls. 
 
2. Analytics and Artiﬁcial Intelligence Capability  
 
The solution should support a progression of analytic maturity: 
 
Descriptive: Present current inventory, ﬁll rates, and readiness status. 
 
Diagnostic: Identify root causes of readiness shortfalls and ﬂag disqualifying factors (e.g., 
medical, administrative, legal). 
 
Predictive: Forecast future readiness, end strength, and personnel availability. 
 
Prescriptive: Recommend optimized personnel-to-billet matches and readiness actions. 
All AI-generated outputs must be explainable (the solution must show the rationale behind 
each recommendation) and must function in a decision-support capacity only, keeping a 
human in the loop for all ﬁnal decisions. 
 
3. User Interface and Reporting 
 
An intuitive, web-based dashboard designed for non-technical users. 
 
Guided search and ﬁltering (e.g., military occupational specialty, grade, location, 
readiness, availability, clearance). 
 
Sortable results with export to standard Office formats (Excel/PowerPoint). 
Visual readiness/risk indicators (e.g., green/amber/red status). 
 
Role-based access controls tailored to different user echelons. 
 
Commander-level dashboards, coverage/gap reports, and early-warning alerts. 
 
4. Scenario Modeling 
 

"What-if" and scenario-based modeling to support mobilization planning. 
 
Anticipated/Phased Approach 
 
Phase Objective 
Phase 1 – Foundation Secure read-only data integration; data 
dictionary; descriptive dashboards; basic 
search and manual candidate lists 
Phase 2 – Diagnostic Anomaly detection, disqualiﬁer logic, and 
readiness early-warning capability. 
Phase 3 – Predictive/Prescriptive AI-driven scoring, ranking, explainable 
recommendations, and allocation 
optimization. 
Phase 4 – Advanced Skill/talent analysis of unstructured data 
and expanded modeling capabilities 
 
Security, Compliance, Hosting 
 
Experience/Approach regarding: 
 
• Operating within Government-authorized cloud or hosting environments. 
 
• Obtaining and maintaining an Authority to Operate (ATO) or leveraging existing 
enterprise authorizations. 
 
• Compliance with DoD and Department of the Navy cybersecurity requirements 
(e.g., RMF), Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certiﬁcation (CMMC) as applicable, and 
handling of CUI and Personally Identiﬁable Information (PII). 
 
• Support for classiﬁed data handling where required. 
 
• Delivery of audit trails and access logging.

GENERAL INFORMATION

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

The Department of Veterans Affairs, Technology Acquisition Center (TAC), 

intends to award a sole source contract under the authority of FAR 6.103-1 Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements, to DOXIMITY INC. to provide Amion software subscription and technical support.

Amion software is a healthcare scheduling platform designed for hospitals and healthcare systems to manage and share on-call and shift schedules for physicians and other medical staff. It provides real-time updates so changes to the schedules are immediately reflected and accessible to relevant staff. It indirectly helps to align scheduling with Veteran-centered care priorities such as specialty, urgent or mental health coverage enabling VA hospitals to mobilize providers specifically in urgent care scenarios such as stroke, heart attack, or urgent surgeries.  

The contractor shall provide technical support for all subscriptions purchased. All technical support shall be provided 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, and 365 days a year. All technical support shall include but not be limited to major product and technology releases, technical support, updates, fixes, security alerts, data fixes, and critical patch updates, upgrade scripts, tax, legal, and regulatory updates and certification with most existing third-party products/versions. Decision Support Center IT Upgrade Projects 
25 June 2026 
1.1 DESCRIPTION OF REQUIRING ORGANIZATION.  The United States Special Operations 
Command (USSOCOM) Decision Support Center (DSC) conducts senior leader seminars, and other 
Special Operations Forces (SOF) Operational Planning Events to directly support the USSCOM 
Commander in achieving operational and planning priorities for SOF. These events require visualizing, 
displaying, synchronizing, and rehearsing operational and mission concepts in terms of time, space and 
prioritization during multiple Commander’s directed leadership events. To meet this requirement, the 
Government has transformed the DSC into a Decision Support Theater with a Virtual Planning 
Workplace (VPW) capable of supporting many different types of events supporting various mission 
planning activities. The entire DSC facility is made up of 4 rooms; the main theater (110), an overflow 
room (222), an alternate main room (115) and a conference room (114). Room #110 operates as the main 
operating control center with rooms #110, #222 and #115 operating as part of the synchronized control 
infrastructure (i.e. displays and audio/visual for each room can be controlled from room #110). These 
rooms are also able to be controlled independent of room #110 with operator stations in each room.  
1.2 TASK PURPOSE/SCOPE 
The purpose of this task is to incorporate room #114 into the synchronized control infrastructure, as well 
as provide upgrades to the existing DSC computer and audio-visual systems.  The required tasks are:  
 Contractor shall remove existing DVLED video wall processor and install an upgraded one. (See
Section 3.0.1 for details.)
 Contractor shall install a DVLED video wall processor for the DVLED video floor that currently
does not utilize one.  (See Section 3.0.1 for details.)
 Contractor shall upgrade DSC audio station and completely re-wire all 3 DSC control stations so
that they are all identical in control functionality.  (See Section 3.0.1 for details.)
 Contractor shall install ThinkLogical ICT18 computers and consolidate Room #114s computers
to Room #136. (See Section 3.0.2 for details.)

government furnished equipment (GFE) Silicone Core LED panels. (See Section 3.0.3 for
details.)

comply with all federal, state, and local environmental requirements and laws.

warranties.

3.0.1.1 Modify the current audio desk architecture to function like the other two VPW workstations,

the carpet on the floor in room #110) where required.  
 
3.0.4 Room #136 Requirements: 
 
3.0.4.1 Install three (3) complete ThinkLogical ICT Chassis. 
 
3.0.4.2 Assist the DSC personnel in identifying which traditional computer chassis will be removed from 
service and replaced by the ICT solution. 
 
3.0.4.3 Cable the new ICT system into the DSC video distribution system.  
 
3.0.4.4 Update and provide a complete system diagram for all equipment in the system (existing and 
newly added).  
 

 
4  
3.0.4.5 Update the Crestron control code to support all new functionality added by the above 
modifications, and provide the complete, uncompiled code upon successful project completion. 
 
 
3.0.6 Painting. The Contractor shall be required to re-paint any affected areas that may get damaged from 
these projects due to the large scale of equipment installation and movement (chips, scratches, etc) to 
match current wall coverings. 
 
3.1 LOCATION AND HOURS OF WORK 
Place of performance shall be at the Decision Support Center for HQ USSOCOM located at MacDill 
AFB, FL. Work to be performed shall be coordinated with the staff at the Decision Support Center. 
Normal core hours are 0700-1600; however, work to be performed may have to be accomplished during 
non-traditional hours 1700-0700 for event preparation. Contractor may be required to perform 
maintenance during non-traditional hours (1700-0700) and potentially on weekends in order not to 
impede scheduled events that occur during the hours of 0700-1700 Monday through Friday.  
 
4.0 SECURITY REQUIREMENTS.  Security will be in accordance with the attached DD254. 
Contractor team individual(s) performing tasks in support of the DSC network and audio-visual system 
shall be cleared at the Top Secret level at the start of the task.  Contractors will require access to SCI, 
Non-SCI National Intelligence Information, NATO, Foreign Government Information and ACCM in 
performance of this effort.  Contractor will require access to NIPRNET, SIPRNET and JWICS computer 
systems at US Government facilities.  Contractor will be authorized to courier classified information up to 
Top Secret/SCI in performance of official duties upon approval of and designation by the COR. 
Contractor team individual(s) only performing ancillary tasks (i.e. carpet installation) do not require Top 
Secret clearance.  Identification of required individual clearances shall be provided upon contract award. 
 
4.1 The contractor shall ensure requirements for safeguarding classified information and classified 
materials, for obtaining and verifying personnel security clearances, for verifying security clearances and 
indoctrination of visitors, for controlling access to restricted areas, for protecting government property, 
and for the security of automated and non-automated management information systems and data are 
fulfilled.  The contractor's management system shall prevent unauthorized disclosure of classified and 
sensitive unclassified information.  The government shall be immediately notified if any security incident 
or any indication of a potential unauthorized disclosure or compromise of classified or sensitive 
unclassified information.    
 
4.2 The contractor shall provide security management support. Typical efforts include, but are not limited 
to, performing classified document control functions, classified materials inventories, program access 
requests, preparing and monitoring personnel indoctrination and debriefing agreements, and maintaining 
and using security-related databases.  
 
4.3 When no government employee or military member is available, the contractor  may be required to 
conduct security related functions (traditionally considered inherently governmental functions) such as 
end-of-day checks for the safeguarding classified information/material and arming/de-arming USSOCOM 
Buildings, Secure Rooms, and/or SCIFs/SAPFs.  If the contractor fails to properly conduct these 
responsibilities, and a security violation/incident occurs, the government will have the option to take 
action against the company IAW U.S. law. In addition, the company shall be responsible for reviewing 
preliminary inquiry reports for any security violation/incident for which an employee is found culpable 
and provide a written response to the GCA and Organizational Security Manager for actions taken against

GENERAL INFORMATION

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

DIGITAL GI BILL AND EDUCATION SERVICES

 DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS (VA) VETERANS BENEFITS ADMINISTRATION (VBA)

Digital GI Bill and Education Services Automation & Modernization 

Date: July 16, 2026

Request for Information (RFI)

Request for Information

 Digital GI Bill and Education Services Automation and Modernization

Introduction: 

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is seeking industry input on solutions to complete the remaining development and modernization of the Digital GI Bill (DGIB) platform, transition the platform from its current Managed Service Vendor to VA-owned/managed infrastructure, and continue advancing automation across DGIB's claims processing capabilities. The Government aims to transform the DGIB ecosystem into a secure, scalable, cloud-based enterprise platform. This platform will facilitate comprehensive claims processing, optimize automation where feasible, lessen dependence on outdated systems, improve the experiences of both Veterans and employees, and offer the adaptability needed for future legislative, policy, and technological shifts. Through this Request for Information (RFI), the VA is seeking insights from industry on the most effective technical and acquisition strategies to reach this goal. This includes suggestions on solution architecture, implementation plans, and contract frameworks.

This is an RFI issued for conducting market research and for eliciting industry input as to the Government’s requirement for DGIB and Education Services Automation and Modernization. This RFI constitutes neither a Request for Proposal/Quote (RFP/RFQ) nor a guarantee that one will ever be issued by the Government; furthermore, it does not commit the Government to contract for any services described herein. Please do not include a price or proposal in your response.  

The VA is not, at this time, seeking proposals or quotes, and therefore will not accept, review, or evaluate unsolicited proposals or quotes received in response hereto. This notice is not to be construed as a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract/order, nor does the Government intend to pay for any information submitted because of this request. The Government does not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the submission of the information being requested, or reimburse expenses incurred for responses to this RFI. Please do not include pricing information in your response.  

The information provided may be used by VA in developing its acquisition strategy and Performance Work Statement (PWS).  Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP/RFQ, if issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary; however, any information received shall become the property of the Government and will not be returned to the respondent. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or competition sensitive information contained in their response. This is a request for information and does not obligate the Government in any way, nor does it commit the Government to any specific course of action. RFI responses will not be evaluated for technical merit and will not provide any competitive advantage in any potential future procurements.

NAICS Code: VA is considering NAICS 541512 (Computer Systems Design Services). Industry feedback on NAICS capability is welcome.

Background:

The DGIB program administers education benefits under Chapters 30, 33, 35, and 1606 of Title 38, U.S. Code, serving Veterans, servicemembers, and their dependents annually. The program processes more than $12 billion in education benefits each year and represents one of VA's most mission-critical technology platforms.

What is a ‘claim’?

In the DGIB context, a claim is a request submitted by a Veteran, servicemember, or eligible dependent for determination and/or payment of education benefits under Title 38, U.S. Code. There are two types of claims:

Original Claim The initial application or request for benefits — the first entry point into education benefits. Based on the specific benefit being applied for, eligibility rules are run to validate service history, eligibility, and entitlement. This results in one of two decisions:

Certificate of Eligibility (COE), or 

a denial

Supplemental Claim Every action that occurs after an Original Claim has been established. Supplemental claims can include additional eligibility information, enrollment certification from a school or training provider, or any other type of follow-on request. These result in a determination of eligibility (benefit level, payment rates, etc.) award, and/or disbursement of payment.

Claim Cycle (for DGIB purposes) A claim cycle begins at the entry point of an application or supplemental action item using either My Education Benefits (MEB) or Enrollment Manager (EM) for enrollment certifications and ends at successful delivery of payment information to VA's payment processing system, eMPWR.

All claims received, via MEB or EM, are processed through one of two systems: the Digital GI Bill Ch33 Processing System for Chapter 33 claims or Benefits Manager (BM) for all non-Chapter 33 claims. Regardless of which system processes the claim, each benefit chapter has its own distinct rules governing eligibility and payment determinations. Claims may be resolved through full end-to-end (E2E) automation, partial automation, or manual adjudication by a Veteran Claims Examiner (VCE). 
Automation levels for claims are defined as:

Automated Claim: A claim received, processed and authorized by automated adjudication without any human intervention.

Partially Automated Claim: A claim where automation initiates the claim, applies processing rules, but must be authorized manually (by a human).

Manual Claim: A claim received or generated outside of DGIB (EM or MEB) and created and authorized by manual adjudication.

The current DGIB operating environment relies on a Managed Service Vendor (MSV) responsible for application development, infrastructure hosting, and operations and maintenance across a complex, mature platform that includes 700+ repositories, 50+ databases (Oracle 19C, PostgreSQL 14, Amazon Redshift, DynamoDB), and extensive CI/CD infrastructure. Other current systems configuration includes: 76 EC2 compute instances (Windows Server and Red Hat Enterprise Linux), 590+ compiled software artifacts , 30+ S3 object storage buckets and 90+ vendor, open-source, and hardware licenses. The system currently holds an active Authority to Operate (ATO) in a vendor-managed AWS GovCloud environment.

VBA is conducting market research to modernize, migrate, and enhance the DGIB platform in alignment with VA's cloud-first strategy and broader enterprise modernization goals. VBA is exploring five primary capability areas, described in the Requirement section below, and is seeking industry input to inform its evaluation of potential approaches.

Current Systems

The DGIB ecosystem consists of legacy systems slated for replacement and modern systems built to replace them but not yet at full operational capability. DGIB processes more than $12 billion in education benefits annually. Automation rates vary by chapter and have improved meaningfully year-over-year, with an overall automation rate of approximately 60% across all benefit chapters. Automated claims are resolved in approximately one day across all chapters, compared to 9.5–18.7 days for manually adjudicated claims, depending on chapter. Quality across both pathways have an overall automation quality rate of 95+%.

Systems Being Replaced (Legacy)

The Image Management System (TIMS) Legacy claims processing queue and work-assignment tool. Used by Veteran Claims Examiners to receive, prioritize, and work claims. Function to be replaced by Workload Manager.

Web Enabled Approval Management System (WEAMS) Legacy system supporting school and training program approval — i.e., determining and tracking which institutions and programs are approved for GI Bill benefit use. Function to be replaced by Approval Manager.

eForce Legacy system also supporting school/program approval case management, operating alongside WEAMS. Function to be replaced by Approval Manager.

Systems Being Built/Matured (Current MVP State)

My Education Benefits (MEB) MEB is VA's enterprise digital platform that modernizes the delivery of education benefits by providing a secure, user-friendly application experience for Veterans, service members, and eligible beneficiaries. MEB leverages automated decisioning to process claims in real time, allowing applicants to receive an immediate eligibility decision and Certificate of Eligibility (COE) when all required information is available and no additional review is needed. The goal is to continue modernizing the platform so that the majority of all submissions result in an immediate decision.

Enrollment Manager (EM) EM is an Education Service web-based system used by schools and training facilities to certify enrollments and report changes for Veterans and other eligible beneficiaries receiving VA education benefits. EM streamlines communication between educational institutions and VA by enabling electronic submission of enrollment certifications for all EDU benefits and timely delivery of education benefits.

Workload Manager System (WLMS) WLMS will be a modernized replacement for TIMS that goes beyond simple work-queue replacement. In addition to virtual evidence storage and queue management, Workload Manager takes on Regional Processing Office (RPO) workload assignment, management, and reporting — using a competency-based framework to automatically match in-progress work products to qualified adjudicators, and producing reporting and monitoring mechanisms at the individual, team, and RPO level. 

Approval Manager(AM) AM will be a modernized replacement for both WEAMS and eForce, assuming their full school and program approval case management functionality. Approval Manager will also be enhanced to support claim automation by ensuring submissions are aligned with school and program approval and will include compliance and risk measures to proactively identify potentially at-risk schools and instances of fraud, waste, and abuse.   

Data Mart Analytics Platform (DMAP) A separate analytics layer that serves as the back-end for all data-based applications within the DGIB environment. DMAP stores, processes, and retrieves adjudication, workload (including WLMS), user, and automation data, along with broader education (EDU) benefits data such as outcome measures and beneficiary data, to create and continually enhance reporting products that enable intelligent, data-driven decision-making

Claims Processing Platforms (Consolidation Target)

VBA currently uses two platforms to process claims received via MEB and EM. VBA is exploring consolidating these two into a single unified processing platform.

Digital GI Bill Ch33 Processing System Handles automated and manual processing specifically for Chapter 33 (Post-9/11 GI Bill) and VET TEC claims.

Benefits Manager (BM) Handles processing for all non-Chapter 33 claims (Chapters 30, 35, 1606).

Requirement: 

VBA seeks to maximize innovation and automation solutions supporting Digital GI Bill Automation and Modernization. VBA is seeking industry input on the viability of solutions that would deliver rapid implementation and aggressive automation, while preserving Government oversight and accountability of the processes to ensure that our Veterans and their beneficiaries receive world class services in the most efficient manner possible. 

VA Cloud Migration 

In addition to continued development of a world-class claims automation and management platform, VA anticipates a transition of all Digital GI Bill components from the managed service vendor to a VA owned/managed infrastructure, which can be executed as an option to improve efficiency, eliminate single vendor lock-in solutions,  align with VA's cloud-first strategy and reduce costs to the American taxpayer. Any proposed solution would have to reside on the VA owned/managed infrastructure and maintain a valid ATO.

Workload Manager 

VA is exploring continued development and enhancement of the Workload Manager beyond its planned Minimum Viable Product (MVP) state to achieve full operational capability, enabling the replacement and decommissioning of TIMS (The Image Management System) and work assignment tool used by veteran claims examiners (VCEs).

Approval Manager 

VA is exploring continued development and enhancement of  Approval Manager beyond its planned MVP state to achieve full operational capability, enabling the replacement and decommissioning of both WEAMS (Web Enabled Approval Management System) and eForce.


Data Mart Analytics Platform (DMAP)

VA is exploring continued development and enhancement of DMAP beyond its planned Minimum Viable Product (MVP) state to achieve full operational capability, enabling enhanced reporting metrics.

Claims Processing System Consolidation

VA is exploring the consolidation of the Digital GI Ch33 processing system and Benefits manager (benefits processing system for all non-33 claims) into a unified processing platform, reducing operational complexity and system redundancy.


Claims Automation Advancement

VA is exploring continued enhancement of automated claims adjudication capabilities to progressively increase and maintain automation rate and quality accuracy of E2E processing across all GI Bill benefits. This includes expansion of original and supplemental automation, offramp refinement, and ongoing improvement to automation logic as legislative and policy changes occur.

Streamlined Manual Claims Processing

VA is exploring ongoing human-centered design research and iterative improvement manual claims processing for VCEs. With the goal of reducing processing time, improving accuracy, enhancing the examiner experience and potential automation capability.

This RFI is being issued to solicit industry input on the viability of a DGIB and Education Services Automation and Modernization process requirement and to obtain associated data that will help inform and shape a potential acquisition. The requirements described above reflect the current DGIB operational landscape but do not constitute final requirements. VA encourages responses from qualified vendors capable of operating, modernizing, or migrating systems of comparable scale and mission-criticality.

Please submit the below requested information NLT 5:00 pm EST August 28, 2026, via email only to Stephen.Winkler@va.gov. PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)

DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS (VA)

VETERANS HEALTH ADMINISTRATION (VHA)

STRATEGIC INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT (SIM)

BUSINESS ARCHITECTURE SERVICES (BA) 

HEALTH ARCHITECTURE SERVICES AND STANDARDIZATION

Date: TBD

PWS Version Number: x.x

BACKGROUND

Business Architecture (BA) is part of the Strategic Investment Management (SIM) Office within the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA). Other services within SIM are Investment Governance Services (IGS), and Requirements Development and Management (RDM). SIM was established to support the business’ health information technology (IT) needs by providing the information that leaders need to make sound decisions. SIM supports the vision of informing the transformation of VHA health care through the timely provision of structured information that enables leadership to make knowledgeable decisions on health and health IT investments. SIM’s mission is to facilitate sound decision making for the development, acquisition, and maintenance of health-focused IT investments by providing leadership with a comprehensive understanding of needed VHA business capabilities including business requirements, processes, information needs, IT strategy and priorities, and investment analysis. The focus of this Performance Work Statement (PWS) is on business architecture, work that is foundational to the IT acquisition process. 

Business Architecture (BA) is an integral part of SIM. As its name suggests, BA develops and manages the VHA’s business architecture which structures and communicates VHA's healthcare business, including descriptions of business behaviors, functionality, processes, and the flow of information that is required to achieve VHA’s mission. The VHA business architecture supports and integrates with VA and other federal enterprise architectures. Key functional component areas of BA that are relevant to this PWS are as follows:

Director’s Office 

Data Analytics and Design

Tooling Operations and Quality Assurance 

Referential Architecture

Process Architecture

Information Architecture

SIM provides leadership and staff resources for several integrated governance bodies of which BA plays a key role. Likewise, BA staff support SIM with analyses of IT requests, to inform the Capability Management Boards (CMBs) who prioritize business cases submitted by program offices for IT solutions. SIM’s overarching mission is executed through functional services focused on functional requirements, business architecture, and investment management provided to the Information Technology Committee (ITC), which is charged with providing IT investment priorities and strategic considerations for VHA decision-making.

As VHA moves forward with its mission to honor America’s Veterans by providing exceptional health care that improves their health and well-being, it is imperative that Business Architecture obtains the support services, skill sets, and subject matter expertise available to ensure continuity of already established business architecture efforts.

FSS SOLE SOURCE JUSTIFICATION 
Logical Follow-On - RFO/GSAR 538.7104-3(b)(1)(iii)
      
Workspace Reservation System 
  Tango AgilQuest 
   GS-35F-470BA 
N/A 
   
   base award year; 6/2026-6/2027;option year 1; 
6/2027-6/2028;option year 2; 6/2028-6/2029;option 
year 3; 6/2029-6/2030
 
  CST1 
  General Services Administration (GSA) 
Public Buildings Service (PBS), 
Office of Acquisition Management (OAM) 
Project Delivery Contracting Division - DC
 
   47PM0923F0077 
      
This justification supports the proposed award of a sole-source Contract by Project Delivery Contracting- 
Central on behalf of Office of Administrative Services (OAS). The proposed order will be issued to Tango 
AgilQuest under Contract No. TBD, for workspace reservation system services in support of swing space 
for the relocation of GSA Headquarters (1800 F Street) staff into the Theodore Roosevelt Building (TRB). 
The system is required to support the stand-up and management of workspace reservations for personnel 
relocating to the Theodore Roosevelt Building swing space, including reservation functionality, user 
access, location/asset configuration, reporting, and integration with GSA's existing technical and security 
environment. 
      
The Government requires a workspace reservation system capable of supporting the timely deployment 
and operational management of reservation functionality for the Theodore Roosevelt Building swing space. 
The requirement includes, but is not limited to: 
● workspace reservation functionality;
● user profile and access management;
● location, room, desk, or asset configuration;
● administrative reporting;
● support for system deployment and configuration;
● integration with GSA's existing access/security environment;
● compliance with applicable federal security and accessibility requirements.


The proposed action is a new sole contract order to Tango AgilQuest  for continuation and deployment of 
reservation system services that are a logical follow-on to a prior competitively awarded FSS order. 
 
The authority for this sole-source FSS order is RFO/GSAR 538.7104-3(b)(1)(iii).
The ordering activity may place an FSS order exceeding the SAT on a sole-source basis when the order is 
in the interest of economy and efficiency because it is a logical follow-on to an FSS order already issued 
on a competitive basis. RFO/GSAR 538.7104-3 requires the justification to be in writing and to include 
sufficient detail and supporting rationale for the exception used. 
     
GSA previously competed and awarded FSS Order No.47PM0923F0077 to Tango for workspace 
reservation system services. The prior order was awarded on 09/27/2023 under GS-35F-470BA following 
competition among 3 FSS contractors, Agilquest (TANGO),  
The prior competed order resulted in the implementation and/or configuration of a GSA workspace 
reservation system environment using the Tango AgilQuest platform. The system has been used or 
configured to support GSA workspace reservation needs and has established technical, operational, 
security, and integration elements that are directly relevant to the current requirement. 
The prior order has expired; however, the current requirement represents a continuation and natural 
extension of the prior competed effort. The current requirement is not a new, unrelated requirement. 
Rather, it requires continuation of the same or substantially similar reservation system capability within the 
existing GSA environment to support the Theodore Roosevelt Building swing space requirement. 
       
Award to Tango  is in the interest of economy and efficiency because the current requirement is a logical 
follow-on to the previously competed FSS order.The contractor has already implemented, configured, or 
supported a GSA reservation system environment, and GSA has already invested time and resources in 
technical review, configuration, security review, accessibility review, and system integration activities 
associated with this platform. 
Awarding the follow-on order to another vendor at this stage would require the Government to duplicate 
substantial implementation and transition activities, including: 
● onboarding a new vendor;
● configuring a new reservation system environment;
● establishing user roles, permissions, and workflows;
● uploading or recreating user, asset, and location data;
● completing additional security review and authorization activities;
● completing accessibility/Section 508 review;
● integrating the system with GSA's single sign-on environment;
● conducting user experience and functionality testing;
● training users and administrators;
● managing transition risk and potential operational disruption.
These activities would increase cost, duplicate prior effort, and create schedule risk. In contrast, award to 
Tango allows the Government to leverage the existing GSA environment, prior configuration work, prior 
technical familiarity, and established system capabilities. 


     
  
An instance of the Tango AgilQuest system has already been developed and is currently operational or 
configured for GSA use. This existing instance demonstrates the vendor's understanding of GSA's 
workspace reservation requirements and provides a platform that can be used, modified, or expanded to 
support the Theodore Roosevelt Building swing space requirement. Because the system environment 
already exists, award to Tango AgilQuest  avoids the time and cost associated with standing up a 
completely new reservation platform. 
     
The existing Tango AgilQuest environment has undergone GSA security review activities, including ATO 
status, 03/04/2026. A new vendor or new platform would require additional security review, documentation, 
testing, and authorization activities. Repeating these activities would create duplicative effort and schedule 
risk, particularly given the Government's need to have the reservation system operational by July 31, 2026. 
   
The existing platform has been reviewed or verified for Section 508 compliance. This reduces the need for 
the Government to initiate a new accessibility review process for an entirely different reservation system. A 
new system would require separate accessibility review and validation, which would add time and risk to 
the deployment schedule. 
  
The existing Tango AgilQuest  platform is already integrated, or is substantially positioned for integration, 
with GSA's single sign-on environment. This allows for secure and seamless access by GSA personnel. 
Integrating a new reservation system with GSA's SSO environment would require additional technical 
development, coordination, testing, and validation. This would duplicate prior effort and further delay 
deployment. 
   
The Tango AgilQuest platform allows for the configuration of users, assets, locations, and workspace 
reservation rules. This functionality is critical for rapidly configuring the Theodore Roosevelt Building swing 
space. Because the vendor has already supported GSA's reservation system requirements, the contractor 
is positioned to configure the required workspace reservation environment more efficiently than a new 
vendor. 
    
GSA has existing familiarity with the Tango AgilQuest platform, including its administrative functions, user 
interface, and operational capabilities. Use of the incumbent platform reduces the level of new user testing, 
training, change management, and administrative onboarding required for deployment. A new system 
would require additional review to ensure it meets GSA's functional, operational, security, and accessibility 
requirements. 
  
GSA has a critical operational need to stand up the workspace reservation system by July 31, 2026, to 
support the relocation of headquarters staff into the Theodore Roosevelt Building swing space. 

The deadline is not the sole basis for this justification; rather, it reinforces the need for economy, efficiency, 
and continuity. Conducting a new competition and transitioning to a different platform would require the 
Government to repeat significant configuration, security, accessibility, integration, testing, and deployment 
activities that have already been completed or substantially mitigated through the existing Tango AgilQuest 
environment. 
Based on the Government's required schedule, transitioning to a new vendor would create substantial risk 
that the reservation system would not be operational in time to support the relocation and effective 
management of the swing space. 
 
The Government considered whether other FSS contractors could meet the workspace reservation system 
requirement. Market research indicates that other vendors may offer reservation system or workplace 
management capabilities under FSS contracts. However, the existence of other reservation system 
providers does not eliminate the economy and efficiency rationale for this logical follow-on. 
The Government's need is not merely for any reservation system. The Government requires timely 
continuation and deployment of a reservation system capability that leverages the existing GSA 
environment, prior configuration, security review, accessibility review, SSO integration, and operational 
familiarity. 
Award to another vendor would require duplicative implementation and transition activities that would 
increase cost, increase schedule risk, and jeopardize the Government's ability to meet the July 31, 2026 
operational deadline. 
Therefore, award to Tango AgilQuest is justified as a logical follow-on in the interest of economy and 
efficiency. 
       
The proposed order will be placed under Tango AgilQuest’sFSS contract. FSS contract pricing has been 
determined fair and reasonable at the Schedule contract level. 
The ordering activity contracting officer will evaluate the contractor's proposed pricing for this order, 
including any discounts, concessions, labor categories, subscription pricing, implementation charges, 
travel, or order-level materials, as applicable. The contracting officer will document the order file to support 
the determination that the proposed order represents the best value to the Government. 
The best value determination will consider price, continuity of service, reduced transition risk, avoidance of 
duplicative implementation costs, schedule requirements, and the Government's need to have the 
reservation system operational by July 31, 2026. 
    
This sole-source logical follow-on is not intended to avoid competition for future recurring requirements.
For any longer-term or future requirement beyond this immediate operational need, the Government will 
consider competing a new FSS order or establishing a competitively awarded FSS BPA to support ongoing 
workspace reservation system requirements. The Government will also consider whether future 
requirements can be structured to reduce transition barriers, including documentation of system 
requirements, data export needs, integration requirements, and migration planning. 

The proposed sole-source award to Tango AgilQuest is justified under RFO/GSAR 538.7104-3(b)(1)(iii) 
because the requirement is a logical follow-on to a previously competed FSS order. 
Award to Tango AgilQuest is in the interest of economy and efficiency because the contractor has already 
implemented or configured the GSA reservation system environment, and award to another vendor would 
require duplicative configuration, security review, accessibility review, SSO integration, testing, training, 
and deployment activities. 
The July 31, 2026 deadline further supports the need for continuity and timely deployment. Award to Tango 
AgilQuest reduces transition risk, avoids unnecessary duplication of effort, and supports the Government's 
ability to meet its operational requirement. 
I certify that this justification is accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief.
